abu-dhabi/khalifa-city.tutorsIntro: Profiles are filtered by the kind of gap a marked script actually shows rather than by subject alone, because a technique gap, a content gap and a habit gap need different teaching and cost different amounts to close.

intro.heading: What the school covers, what it cannot, and what closing the difference costs
paragraphs: Khalifa City is a large mainland community of villa plots and low-rise housing between the airport road and the city, with Khalifa City A and B and the newer edges running towards Al Raha and Mohammed Bin Zayed City. It has one of the densest school clusters in the emirate, across British, American and IB continuum routes, and households here tend to be settled rather than transient. Many have been in the same school for years.

That produces an unusually well-informed parent and an unusually specific question. The enquiries from this community are rarely about what the IB Diploma is or how IGCSE works. They are about value: how many hours, at what rate, for what outcome, and whether the thing being sold is the thing that is needed. Nobody in this market publishes the answers, which is the gap this page tries to close.

Start with the structure of the problem. A school week has a fixed number of taught periods per subject and those periods carry new content. Consolidation is set as homework and checked rather than taught. Everything after that — rehearsal, timed practice, drafting an assessed piece, reviewing a marked script for patterns — belongs to the student alone. That third category is substantial, and in an examined programme it is where the grade is largely decided.

There are three different gaps that live inside that third category, and conflating them is the most expensive mistake available to a parent. A technique gap means the student knows the content and loses marks in the writing of answers. A content gap means specific topics were never learned. A habit gap means the independent hours do not happen at all. They look identical on a report card and cost very different amounts to close.

The cheapest is the technique gap, which often moves within six to eight sessions because the fix is behavioural. The most expensive is the content gap across a two-year syllabus, which needs a term or more of teaching. The habit gap is the odd one out: it is cheap to diagnose, cheap to fix structurally, and almost impossible to fix with money alone, because the thing required is a protected window and a reviewed output rather than another paid hour.

What follows prices each of those honestly, compares six provider models on more than rate, lists the extras that quietly change a quoted figure, sets out how many hours different goals actually take, and says what no budget buys. Market rates are presented as the market's with each publisher named; they are not an IB Gram price list. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, and IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in the UAE — visiting tutors are a service we run only in India.

abu-dhabi/khalifa-city.programmesIntro: Khalifa City households sit across the IB continuum, British and American routes, and the cost question looks different in each. Each note below is about where money is well spent in that programme.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across Higher and Standard Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internally assessed component against published criteria, submitted and moderated before external papers sat in one window. More of the result depends on self-managed work than in any other route, and the second year concentrates deadlines into an eight-week autumn.
programmes.countryNote: This is the programme where households overspend most reliably, because six subjects and three core components create six or nine places to buy help. The spending that works is narrow: one or two components where the marks are most recoverable, usually a Higher Level paper and one internally assessed piece. The spending that does not work is a tutor per subject, which costs several times as much and dilutes the student's attention across the week.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year externally examined courses, with Cambridge codes such as 0580 Mathematics and 0620 Chemistry and Pearson International GCSE codes such as 4MA1 and 4CH1. Cambridge mathematics and the separate sciences are tiered into Core and Extended, which fixes the available grade range before papers are sat. Eight to ten subjects are usually taken together.
programmes.countryNote: With eight or more subjects running at once, the question in Khalifa City is almost always which one gets the hour. The answer is the subject where a grade change alters a sixth-form entry decision, not the subject with the lowest mark. A low mark in a subject the student will drop at sixteen is a poor place to spend, however uncomfortable it looks on a report.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, labelled A to D and scored 0 to 8 against task-specific rubrics, combining to a total out of 32 that converts to a grade from 1 to 7. The final year carries the Personal Project, an extended independent piece with its own criteria and interim deadlines set by the school.
programmes.countryNote: Middle Years tutoring is the cheapest useful tutoring available in this community, because the purchase can be precise. Identify the criterion letter that is low across several subjects, buy six to eight sessions on that one skill, and several grades move together. A standing weekly subject lesson at this stage usually costs more and achieves less than a targeted block.

programmes.name: American curriculum and Advanced Placement
programmes.description: Continuous assessment across a grade point average, with Advanced Placement courses taken individually and examined separately on a 1 to 5 scale. Risk is distributed across a year, which rewards steady submission and does not build examination stamina. Standardised tests sit alongside the transcript and carry their own preparation.
programmes.countryNote: On this route the spending question is unusual: the transcript responds to consistency rather than to intensive intervention, so money spent on a crisis block near the end of a year buys very little. Where it does buy something is standardised test preparation and examination stamina, both of which are specific, measurable and separable from the school course.

abu-dhabi/khalifa-city.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Khalifa City households ask about most. Each description names what is actually being bought when a family pays for that subject, because the answer differs more than the subject names suggest.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 and 4MA1)
subjects.levels: IGCSE Core and Extended · Pearson Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The most requested subject in the community and the one where the gap type matters most. A student losing method marks needs script marking, which is cheap and fast. A student missing two years of algebraic fluency needs teaching, which is not. A marked script separates the two in twenty minutes.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Calculus, algebra and proof, with an optional-topic paper at Higher Level. The expensive version of this purchase is a weekly lesson for two years. The efficient version is a specialist for a defined block on the specific paper where marks are lost, plus a protected independent window the rest of the time.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and calculator technique. What is usually being bought here is the interpretation sentence rather than the mathematics, and that is a short, teachable skill. Families who buy general tuition in this subject frequently pay for content the student already has.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE Core and Extended
subjects.description: Mechanics, electricity, waves and, at Higher Level, fields and quantum topics. Experimental-design questions are the reliable loss and the cheapest to fix, because they are a small, well-defined set of question types. Formula provision differs between Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE Core and Extended
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms. Mole arithmetic is rehearsal, not teaching, and paying a specialist rate for rehearsal is poor value. Paying a specialist for mechanism work and internally assessed investigation design is good value.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE Core and Extended
subjects.description: Physiology, genetics, ecology and data analysis, with the heaviest command-term load of the sciences. Most of what families buy here is command-term technique, which transfers across the whole subject and often across other subjects as well, making it one of the better-value purchases available.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.levels: IB Language A HL and SL · IGCSE First Language
subjects.description: Analysis, comparative writing, the individual oral and the higher level essay. The purchase that works is marked written work with feedback on structure and argument. The purchase that does not is content coverage, because the student has usually read the texts and cannot yet write about them under time.

subjects.name: Economics and Business
subjects.levels: IGCSE 0455 and 0450 · IB HL and SL
subjects.description: Markets, macroeconomics, marketing, operations and finance, assessed largely through essays and case studies. Diagram accuracy, application to an unfamiliar business and the evaluation paragraph are the three things worth paying for, and all three are short blocks rather than year-long arrangements.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Mandatory in UAE private schools whatever the licensed curriculum. The spending pattern here is backwards in most households: it gets the smallest budget and the worst slot, and it appears on the report every term. Short frequent sessions cost less per week than one long one and work better.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Points that are cheap to earn relative to lifting a Higher Level grade, and almost always under-bought. A small number of well-timed sessions on reading a prescribed title and structuring an argument around knowledge claims competes well with any other use of the same money.

subjects.name: Standardised tests
subjects.description: Separable from the school course and measurable, which makes them the easiest purchase to judge. The Ministry of Education's American-track equivalency requirements include specified minimum scores, so for some families this is a requirement rather than an enhancement.

sections.heading: Three different gaps, three different prices
paragraphs: Before any rate is discussed, work out which gap you have. They present identically — a mark lower than expected — and they cost very different amounts to close, so buying the wrong remedy is the main way money is wasted in this market. A marked script with the teacher's annotations still on it tells you which in about twenty minutes.

A technique gap shows as marks lost in the writing rather than the knowing. Working not shown, so method marks go. An 'explain' answered as a 'describe'. Units omitted, axes mislabelled, an answer abandoned because the timing collapsed. The student knows the material and cannot convert it. This is the cheapest gap to close, because the fix is behavioural and transfers across every topic at once.

A content gap shows as blank or badly wrong answers in specific topics, consistently. Something was taught while the student was absent, or taught in a different school, or taught and never understood. This is the expensive gap: content has to be taught and then practised, and across a two-year syllabus that is a term or more of sessions. There is no shortcut and anyone selling one is selling something else.

A habit gap shows as a student who understands everything in a lesson and cannot reproduce it a fortnight later. Nothing is wrong with the teaching or the technique. The independent hours are not happening, so nothing consolidates. This gap is cheap to diagnose, cheap to fix structurally and almost impossible to fix by buying more teaching, which is why a household that responds to it with three weekly lessons gets poorer value than one that responds with a protected window and a fortnightly review.

sections.heading: Six provider models compared on more than rate
paragraphs: Comparing tutors by hourly rate is like comparing cars by fuel capacity. The rate is one variable among several that determine what a household actually receives, and the others are rarely published. The table below compares models rather than brands, with every quoted rate attributed to the provider that published it and dated.

The variables that matter beyond rate are these. Whether marking of work set between sessions is included. Whether a replacement is offered if the match is wrong, and how quickly. Whether a trial exists and what condition attaches to it. Whether the person teaching holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit. And whether delivery is actually what was implied — several providers in this market route UAE enquiries to numbers outside the country without saying so.

On the permit specifically: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories from registered school teachers to university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing with a two-working-day completion time. Because it is free and quick, a provider who cannot answer the question has told you something.

We have not put an IB Gram rate in the table, and that is deliberate rather than evasive. Publishing a single hourly figure would be less useful than telling you what sits inside the hour, which varies by level and format. Ask for the trial and the consultation and you will get both numbers and inclusions in writing before anything is booked.

sections.heading: The extras that quietly change the real hourly figure
paragraphs: A quoted rate is a headline, and the number a household actually pays per hour of teaching is often different. None of the items below is dishonest in itself; they become a problem only when they are not disclosed, and in this market they frequently are not. Ask about each one in writing before a first session and the comparison between providers becomes real.

The commonest adjustment is marking. If work is set between sessions and marked in the next session, that is teaching time consumed by administration, which effectively raises the price of the teaching. If marking is billed separately, the headline rate understates the cost. If no work is set between sessions at all, the rate is lower and so is the value, because consolidation is the point.

The second is session length versus the hour. A rate quoted per session where sessions run fifty minutes is a higher hourly rate than it appears. The third is cancellation policy, which determines what a missed session costs and in a household with travel can be a meaningful annual figure. The fourth is exam-term repricing, where demand peaks and some providers raise rates or restrict availability exactly when a family needs it.

Then there are the smaller items that add up: materials fees, platform fees, charges for written reports, minimum terms that prevent stopping after a poor match, and package structures that expire unused sessions. The table sets out what to ask about each. A provider who answers all of them in writing is usually a safe choice; one who treats the questions as unreasonable has answered them differently.

sections.heading: How many hours does a result actually take?
paragraphs: Nobody can honestly promise a grade, and anybody who does is telling you something about themselves rather than about your child. What can be said, with ranges rather than certainties, is roughly how many hours different goals have taken for students in similar positions, and what else has to be true for the hours to work. That is the information families in this community actually want and nobody publishes.

The ranges below assume a student who attends, does the work set between sessions, and has a protected independent window. Remove any of those three and the hours stop predicting anything, which is the honest reason tutoring sometimes fails. The variable that most changes the number is not the tutor's quality but whether the independent work happens.

Read the right-hand column as carefully as the hours column. It names the condition that has to hold, and in several rows that condition is the whole intervention. A student whose problem is timing does not need more content hours; they need timed practice and somebody marking it. A student who will not open a book between lessons needs a structure, and buying them a third weekly session is the most expensive way to discover that.

The last row is the one most worth reading. Some targets are not reachable in the time remaining, and the honest response is to revise the target or the plan rather than to sell more hours into it. We will say that when the evidence says it, because the alternative is a household spending a term on the lowest-return hour in its week.

sections.heading: Tutoring set against the cost of the school year
paragraphs: The comparison most households make is between one tutor's rate and another's. The more useful comparison is between a year of tutoring and a year of school fees, because that is the proportion that tells you whether a purchase is sensible. School fees are the dominant educational cost in every household in this community, and tutoring at one session a week in one subject typically sits at a small fraction of them.

That framing changes two decisions. First, it makes a steady year-long arrangement look more reasonable than it does in isolation, and a crisis block in the spring look worse: the same money spread across the year buys more hours and far more improvement. Second, it stops a household treating tutoring as an emergency expense, which is the mindset that produces the three-lessons-a-week panic in March.

It also raises a question worth asking directly. If a school's fees are substantial and a child still needs tutoring in a core subject across two years, that is information about the fit between the child and the provision, and it belongs in a conversation with the school rather than being quietly solved with money. Schools in this corridor generally respond well to specific, evidenced questions from parents.

Abu Dhabi's regulator, the Department of Education and Knowledge, supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes inspection outcomes, and fee arrangements for private schools sit within the regulator's remit rather than being set freely. For current fee rules and for any school's published inspection outcome, go to ADEK's own channels rather than to a tutoring website, including this one.

sections.heading: If the budget is one hour a week, which subject gets it?
paragraphs: This is the most common real question in Khalifa City and it has a clear answer, which is not the one most families reach. The hour should go to the subject where a grade change alters a decision, not to the subject with the lowest mark. Those are frequently different subjects, and the difference is worth a great deal.

Work through it in order. First, which grades are load-bearing: a sixth-form entry requirement, a university offer condition, a subject that must be passed for a progression rule. Second, within those, where is the gap closest to closeable — a technique gap in a load-bearing subject beats a content gap in one, because the same hours buy more. Third, only then consider how uncomfortable the mark looks.

A worked example. A Year 11 student has a 4 in a subject they will drop at sixteen and a 6 in a subject where the sixth form requires a 7. The 4 is the uncomfortable number and the 6 is the one that decides the next two years. The hour belongs to the second subject, and explaining that to a teenager is part of the job.

There is one exception worth naming. Where a subject is at risk of failing in a way that affects progression or an equivalency requirement, it takes priority regardless of comfort, because a failure has consequences that a middling grade does not. On the British track, Ministry of Education equivalency requires five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five, so the count is worth checking before any subject is written off.

sections.heading: The cheap end: what it can do and what it cannot
paragraphs: Published budget rates in this market run from AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing AED 45-65 and Tutopiya AED 33-52. Those are real prices for real teaching and they are the right purchase for some jobs. Pretending otherwise would be dishonest, and most providers at the specialist end do pretend otherwise.

What the cheap end does well: routine homework support in lower secondary, keeping a younger student moving through set work, conversational language practice, and basic rehearsal where the task is repetition rather than instruction. For a Year 7 student who needs somebody to sit with them while they finish the week's mathematics, a budget rate is appropriate and a specialist rate is waste.

What it generally does not do: mark written work against a board mark scheme with the authority of someone who knows how marks are awarded, diagnose a gap from a script, supervise an internally assessed component within the honesty rules, or prepare a Higher Level candidate for a paper the tutor has never taught. At this end the hour is usually teaching time alone, with no marking between sessions, and marking is the mechanism that makes consolidation visible.

One thing applies at every price point. Anyone providing private tutoring in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free and valid for two years, and individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here. Ask the question at every band; a low rate is not a reason for the answer to be vague.

sections.heading: Group classes, tuition centres and one-to-one compared
paragraphs: Khalifa City has tuition centres within reach and group classes are the cheapest paid option per head, which makes them worth considering honestly rather than dismissing. A group class works when the group is genuinely at the same point in the same syllabus and the teaching is content delivery. It stops working the moment the need becomes individual.

The structural limitation is simple arithmetic. In a group of eight, a ninety-minute class gives each student a little over ten minutes of individual attention if it is distributed evenly, which it never is. For content delivery that is fine, because the delivery is shared. For script marking, gap diagnosis or assessed-component supervision it is not, because those are individual by nature.

A tuition centre adds premises, which brings travel back into the arrangement and, in this community, a drive at the worst time of day. It also brings a regulatory dimension: a centre operating with premises and staff needs the relevant educational services permit from the emirate's authority, with annual renewal, which is a different thing from an individual's tutoring permit. Ask for the permit and the licensing authority.

The honest conclusion is that these are complements rather than competitors. A student with a genuine content gap across a topic area can be well served by a group class at a lower price, and then needs a small number of individual sessions to convert that content into marks. A household that buys only one-to-one for a content gap is overpaying; a household that buys only group classes for a technique gap is paying for the wrong thing.

sections.heading: What no amount of money buys
paragraphs: This section exists because the rest of this page is about spending, and a page about spending that never names the limits is a sales document. There are things a household in this community cannot buy from us or from anybody else, and knowing them is worth as much as knowing the rates.

You cannot buy a grade. No tutor, however experienced with a particular paper, can guarantee an outcome, and a provider who promises a specific grade, a specific number of marks, or a refund tied to a result is making a claim about a process they do not control. You cannot buy assessed work: internal assessments, Extended Essays, Theory of Knowledge essays, Personal Projects and coursework are assessed as the student's own, a breach is treated as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student. At least one operation in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price.

You cannot buy board materials from us. Past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and syllabus documents belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well as a copyright one. We cite and link the official source; schools hold what their students are entitled to use and will usually release past papers on request.

You cannot buy regulatory standing, and you should be suspicious of anyone selling it. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of Abu Dhabi's private schools; MoHRE issues the private tuition work permit to individuals. Neither accredits a tutoring platform, and IB Gram holds nothing from either, nor from any examination board. Finally, you cannot buy the independent hours. Those are the student's, they are where the grade is decided, and the most a paid arrangement can do is make them visible.

sections.heading: Spending a Khalifa City budget in the right order
paragraphs: If a household has a fixed amount to spend across a year, the order matters more than the total. The first spend is nothing: establish the protected independent window and decide what it produces. That is free, it is the condition on which every later hour depends, and skipping it is how families spend a term on teaching that does not consolidate.

The second spend is a diagnosis. One session with a marked script, which tells you whether the gap is technique, content or habit. That single hour determines whether the right purchase is a six-session block, a term of weekly teaching, or a fortnightly review, and those differ by a factor of several across a year. Buying a year of weekly lessons without it is the commonest overspend in this community.

The third spend is the defined block against the named target, with a diagnostic at each end so it can be judged. Only after that block has been judged does a standing arrangement make sense, and only in the cases where the diagnosis said content. The fourth spend, if anything is left, goes to the cheap points: Theory of Knowledge, a criterion that is low across subjects, or Arabic in short frequent sessions.

What should come last, and usually comes first, is a tutor per subject. Six subjects with six tutors costs several times a targeted plan, dilutes the student's week, and produces six people each believing their subject deserves more of the independent hours. Where a household genuinely needs breadth, it is better to rotate blocks through the year than to run everything at once.
bullets: First: the protected window and its output, which costs nothing
Second: one diagnostic session with a marked script
Third: a defined block against a named target, judged at both ends
Last, if ever: a tutor per subject, which dilutes the week and multiplies the cost

process.title: Establish the free part first
process.description: A protected independent window with a defined output, in a fixed place at a fixed time. It costs nothing and every paid hour afterwards depends on it. Households that skip this step frequently pay for teaching that never consolidates.

process.title: Buy one diagnostic session
process.description: One session with a marked script and a short written task tells you whether the gap is technique, content or habit. Those three need different remedies that differ several-fold in cost, and guessing between them is the main source of waste in this market.

process.title: Name the target in writing
process.description: Not 'improve in chemistry' but 'secure method marks on Paper 2 structured questions'. A named target can be tested at the end of a block. A vague one renews indefinitely because nobody can tell whether it was met.

process.title: Confirm the inclusions before the first lesson
process.description: Rate per hour or per session, marking included or billed, cancellation notice, exam-term repricing, minimum term and package expiry. Seven questions, answered in writing, make a comparison between providers real rather than rhetorical.

process.title: Ask about the permit
process.description: The MoHRE private tuition work permit is free and valid for two years and takes two working days to issue, so a vague answer is itself informative. Ask at every price band, including the lowest.

process.title: Judge the block, then decide again
process.description: A diagnostic at the end, comparable with the one at the start. If the target was met, stop or move to the next target. If it was not, change the method or the tutor, and consider that the target itself may need revising.

whyPoints.title: We price the diagnosis, not the panic
whyPoints.description: One session with a marked script tells you whether you need six sessions, a term, or a structure and no teaching at all. Selling a year of weekly lessons before that diagnosis is the standard practice in this market and it is the main source of waste.

whyPoints.title: Market figures, attributed and dated
whyPoints.description: Every AED number on this page is a rate a provider published, named and dated October 2026. We do not present the market's numbers as ours, and we give our own figures with the inclusions in writing at the consultation rather than as a headline.

whyPoints.title: Models compared on more than rate
whyPoints.description: Permit position, replacement route, trial conditions, marking inclusion, minimum terms and whether delivery is really what was implied. Those decide what a household receives, and almost none of them appear on a competitor's page.

whyPoints.title: We recommend less where less works
whyPoints.description: A habit gap needs a fortnightly review rather than three weekly lessons, and we will say so even though it halves the invoice. Group classes are the better buy for a shared content gap, and we will say that too.

whyPoints.title: The limits published alongside the prices
whyPoints.description: No promises about a specific grade, no assessed work at any price, no board papers supplied, no accreditation claimed from ADEK, MoHRE or any examination board. A page about spending that never names its limits is a sales document.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the hours nobody sells
whyPoints.description: The independent hours decide the grade and cannot be bought. The most a paid arrangement does is make them visible by reviewing what they produced, which is why our cheapest recommendation is often the most effective one.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child needs technique help or actual teaching?
faqs.answer: Read a marked script with the teacher's annotations still on it. A technique gap shows as marks lost in the writing: working not shown, an 'explain' answered as a 'describe', units omitted, a final question abandoned on timing. A content gap shows as consistent blanks or serious errors in specific topics. A habit gap shows as a student who understands everything in the lesson and cannot reproduce it a fortnight later. Those three cost very different amounts to close, and twenty minutes with a script usually settles which you have.

faqs.question: What should I ask a provider before the first paid session?
faqs.answer: Seven questions, in writing. Is the rate per hour or per session? Is marking of work set between sessions included or billed? What cancellation notice avoids a charge? Does the rate change in the exam term? Do I receive notes after each session? Is there a minimum term, and do package sessions expire? And does the tutor hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? A provider who answers all seven plainly is usually a safe choice; one who treats them as unreasonable has answered them differently.

faqs.question: Why does this page not publish IB Gram's hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Because a single figure would be less useful than the inclusions, which vary by level and format. An hour that includes marking of work set between sessions is a different product from an hour that does not, and quoting one number invites a comparison with providers whose number excludes it. Ask for the trial and the consultation and you get both the figure and what sits inside it in writing before anything is booked. Every other number on this page is a market rate with its publisher named.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class worth considering in Khalifa City?
faqs.answer: For the right job, genuinely yes. A group class is the cheapest paid option per head and works when the group is at the same point in the same syllabus and the teaching is content delivery. It stops working for script marking, gap diagnosis or assessed-component supervision, which are individual by nature: in a ninety-minute class of eight, each student gets a little over ten minutes of individual attention at best. Centres also bring travel back, and premises need an educational services permit worth asking about.

faqs.question: Do tutors visit homes in Khalifa City?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We deliver tutoring in the UAE as one-to-one lessons online, over live video, and we do not send anyone to a residential address in the Emirates; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Published market rates for visiting tutors run AED 180-500 an hour with travel inside the figure, and independent tutors in this corridor commonly do offer visits. What we offer instead is a tutor matched to the exact board and component, with no travel priced into the hour.

faqs.question: How many hours does it take to move a grade?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which gap you have, and ranges are the only honest form of answer. Fixing method presentation in a quantitative subject typically runs six to ten hours. Command-term technique in a written subject runs six to twelve. Closing two or three genuine topic gaps runs ten to twenty. Building examination stamina from scratch runs eight to fifteen. All of those assume the student does the set work and has a protected independent window; remove either condition and the hours stop predicting anything.

faqs.question: We can afford one hour a week. Which subject should get it?
faqs.answer: The subject where a grade change alters a decision, not the subject with the lowest mark. Those are often different. Work through it in order: which grades are load-bearing for a sixth-form place, a university offer condition or a progression rule; then, within those, where the gap is closest to closeable, since a technique gap buys more per hour than a content gap; then comfort. The exception is a subject at risk of failing in a way that affects progression or an equivalency requirement, which takes priority.

faqs.question: Is cheap online tutoring ever a sensible purchase?
faqs.answer: Yes, for specific jobs. Published budget rates run AED 45-150 an hour, with EdFlik listing AED 45-65 and Tutopiya AED 33-52, and that band suits routine homework support in lower secondary, keeping a younger student moving through set work, conversational language practice and basic rehearsal. What it rarely includes is marking against a board mark scheme, gap diagnosis from a script, or assessed-component supervision within the honesty rules. Paying less for an hour without marking is not always a saving.

faqs.question: What extras tend to be left out of a quoted rate?
faqs.answer: Marking of work set between sessions is the big one: included, billed separately, or not offered at all, and it changes the effective cost materially. Then session length against the hour, since a fifty-minute session raises the hourly rate by a fifth. Then cancellation notice, exam-term repricing, charges for written reports, minimum terms that prevent stopping after a poor match, and package structures where unused sessions expire. Ask about each in writing; the answers differ more than the headline rates do.

faqs.question: Should I compare tutoring cost against other tutors or against school fees?
faqs.answer: Against the school year, because that is the proportion that tells you whether a purchase is sensible. School fees are the dominant educational cost in any household here, and one weekly session in one subject typically sits at a small fraction of them. That framing makes a steady year-long arrangement look reasonable and a spring crisis block look poor, which matches the evidence. It also raises a fair question: persistent need in a core subject is worth discussing with the school.

faqs.question: Can a tutor guarantee an improvement if we commit to a term?
faqs.answer: No, and an offer to do so is a reason to look elsewhere. No tutor controls attendance, sleep, the independent hours, the quality of the school's teaching or what appears on a paper, so a guarantee is a claim about a process the provider does not control. The same applies to refunds tied to an outcome. What a provider can reasonably offer is a named target, a diagnostic at each end of a block so the target can be tested, and an honest conversation when it was not met.

faqs.question: Do tutors in Abu Dhabi need a permit, and does it cost anything?
faqs.answer: They need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. The published eligibility list includes registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing with a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Can we buy help with an internal assessment to save time?
faqs.answer: You can buy teaching, scope testing and feedback on a draft the student has written. You cannot buy the piece itself, at any price, from anyone. Internal assessments, Extended Essays, Theory of Knowledge essays, Personal Projects and coursework are assessed as the student's own work, a breach is treated as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on whoever helped. At least one operation in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price; what it is selling is a declaration the student has to sign.

faqs.question: What is the single most common way families here waste money on tutoring?
faqs.answer: Buying a tutor per subject. Six subjects with six tutors costs several times a targeted plan, dilutes the student's week, and produces six people each believing their subject deserves more of the independent hours. The second most common is buying a year of weekly lessons without a diagnosis first, which frequently funds teaching for a problem that was behavioural. The third is a spring crisis block, which costs more per hour of benefit than the same money spread across the year.

faqs.question: Will you tell us if we do not need to buy anything?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we do it often. Where the content and the technique are sound and the independent hours are simply not happening, the effective purchase is a fortnightly review that marks what was produced and sets the next fortnight's work, which costs about half a weekly arrangement. Where a marked script shows marks consistent with effort and prior attainment, the honest answer may be that the target needs revising rather than that more hours are needed, and we would rather say that in week one.

abu-dhabi/khalifa-city.closingHeading: Diagnose first, then spend in order
abu-dhabi/khalifa-city.closingBody: Send us a marked script with the teacher's annotations still on it, the board and syllabus codes, and an honest account of what happens in the independent hours. One session will tell you whether the gap is technique, content or habit, and those three differ several-fold in what they cost to close. You will get a named target, a stated number of sessions and a way to judge whether it worked. Where the right answer is a structure rather than a weekly lesson, we will say so. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video.

abu-dhabi/madinat-zayed.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are matched on three things at once: the subject and level, a slot that fits a central-district week, and a rate that makes sense for the number of hours actually needed. A specialist who only suits an impossible hour is not a match.

intro.heading: A short school run, a crowded flat and a fixed monthly figure
paragraphs: Madinat Zayed is central Abu Dhabi: the shopping centre and the gold souk at its core, mid and high-rise apartment blocks around them, Hamdan and Al Falah Streets running through the grid, and the city's main bus interchange within easy reach. It is one of the most densely populated parts of the emirate and one of the most mixed, and the households here face a combination of constraints that villa communities and the islands do not.

The first constraint is space rather than time. Many children in this district walk to school or take a ten-minute bus, which means they are home early and the clock is generous. What is not generous is the flat. A two or three-bedroom apartment with siblings sharing a room and a living area that is also the dining area has exactly one quiet surface, and a teenager who needs ninety uninterrupted minutes with a laptop is competing with the whole household for it. Arrangements here fail over noise and interruption far more often than over scheduling.

The second constraint is budget, and it deserves to be discussed honestly rather than tactfully. Many families in this district are funding tuition out of a fixed monthly figure that also covers rent and school fees. That changes what good advice looks like. A provider recommending three subjects of weekly tuition to such a household is not giving advice; it is selling. The right recommendation is usually one subject, properly, in the order that produces the most grade movement per dirham, and an honest statement of what the cheap end of the market can and cannot do.

The third is verification. This district has the greatest density of informal tutoring in the emirate: noticeboards, group chats, word of mouth, a neighbour who teaches at a school nearby. Some of that is excellent and some of it is unlawful, and parents have almost no way to tell them apart. So this page publishes the permit rules in full, including who is eligible, what the permit costs and how a parent can ask about it without awkwardness.

There is a fourth thing, and it is the one that separates good value from bad in this district. Families here are offered teaching when what they need is diagnosis. A household paying for three hours a week of general lessons in a subject whose real problem is a mark-tariff habit has bought the wrong thing competently. One hour spent reading the last marked script against the official scheme would have identified it, and the set work that follows is free. We would rather sell that hour and lose the term.

What we offer is one-to-one tuition over live video. In a crowded flat that has a specific advantage beyond the obvious: no visitor occupies the only shared room for ninety minutes, the session can happen with headphones in a bedroom corner, and nothing in the arrangement depends on a stranger's travel. It also means the hourly rate carries no travel premium, which matters when the budget is the binding constraint rather than an afterthought.

abu-dhabi/madinat-zayed.programmesIntro: This district spans international and national-board schooling, and the programme notes below are framed around cost and hours rather than around curriculum philosophy.

programmes.name: IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year externally examined courses from Cambridge International or Pearson Edexcel. Cambridge tiers several subjects into Core and Extended with different papers, and Core caps at grade C, which makes the tier decision the single most consequential and least discussed moment of Year 10.
programmes.countryNote: For a household budgeting carefully, Year 10 is the cheap year and almost nobody uses it. Establishing timed-practice habits then means Year 11 needs supervision rather than rescue, and the total number of paid hours across the two years ends up considerably lower.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. In the current science guides the internal assessment carries 20% of the subject grade, and the Mathematics exploration the same, so a fifth of each grade is coursework produced at home.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students from this district usually travel to Al Mushrif, Al Bateen or further, since central-district Diploma provision is limited. Coursework supervision timed to three specific points in each component is the highest-value purchase available to these families, and it is also the cheapest.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups marked against four lettered criteria out of eight each, assessing process alongside content. Criterion marking confuses parents more than any other reporting system, because a 5 describes performance against one named skill rather than a general standard.
programmes.countryNote: A single session decoding a returned MYP task against its rubric often changes a student's marks more than a term of subject lessons, and it costs one hour. For a budget-conscious household this is the clearest example of buying diagnosis before buying teaching.

programmes.name: A Level
programmes.description: Linear qualifications assessed entirely at the end, with little coursework in most subjects. Narrower and deeper than the Diploma, and more exposed: there is no internally assessed component to absorb a weak paper.
programmes.countryNote: On the Ministry of Education's British track, candidates need one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that five.

abu-dhabi/madinat-zayed.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects central-district families ask about most, with a note on how many hours each realistically needs, because that is the number a budget has to accommodate.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE)
subjects.description: The tier decision comes first and sets the ceiling, with Cambridge Core capped at grade C. After that, most of the available improvement comes from timed past papers and self-marking, which means fewer paid hours than families expect.

subjects.name: Physics (IGCSE)
subjects.description: Electricity and waves are the predictable weak strands. The alternative-to-practical paper rewards experimental conventions that are rarely drilled and are learnable in a handful of hours, which makes it the best value in the subject.

subjects.name: Chemistry (IGCSE)
subjects.description: Moles and electrolysis separate the top grades, and each student misunderstands a different step, so this is diagnosis work rather than teaching work. Four focused sessions usually resolve what a term of general lessons does not.

subjects.name: Biology (IGCSE)
subjects.description: Content-heavy and deceptively safe, which is why students over-rely on recall and lose the application marks. Correcting the describe-instead-of-explain habit is a technique job measured in weeks, not terms.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Standard Level sits two papers at 40% each with a 20% exploration; Higher Level adds Paper 3 at 20%. Higher Level is the one subject on this list that genuinely needs a sustained weekly hour across two years, because the content compounds.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with the graphic display calculator throughout. More modular than Analysis and Approaches, so a short session can complete a whole topic, which suits a tighter budget.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Register control and accurate structure matter more than vocabulary range. For households where English is not the home language this is frequently where the fastest grade movement is available per hour spent.

subjects.name: First Language English
subjects.description: Directed writing and reading response papers rewarding structure and precise textual reference. The work that moves marks is a timed response written then dissected, which needs a longer session rather than more of them.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diploma Standard Level is Paper 1 at 30%, Paper 2 at 40% and the portfolio at 30%, with Paper 3 at Higher Level. The three-commentary portfolio needs blocks at three points rather than continuous weekly attention.

subjects.name: Accounting and Business
subjects.description: Structured, rule-based subjects where marks are lost on presentation conventions as much as on understanding. That makes them unusually responsive to a small number of corrective sessions.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first and additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the international programme under the federal rules, with different expectations and separate provision for Arab and non-Arab students. Frequent short sessions suit script and fluency work better than long weekly ones.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into fewer papers, so one weak strand drags the award. Diagnosing by strand first stops a family paying for three subjects when the problem sits in one, which on a fixed budget is the difference between affordable and not.

regions.name: Al Danah
regions.note: The district immediately around Madinat Zayed, dense and commercial at street level with apartments above. Children here often walk or take a short bus, which is why the early afternoon is genuinely usable in a way it is not elsewhere in the emirate.

regions.name: Al Markaziyah

regions.name: Al Wahda

sections.heading: Four windows in a central-district week, and what each can carry
paragraphs: A Madinat Zayed household has more usable hours than almost anywhere else in the emirate and less usable quiet. That inversion is worth taking seriously, because it changes which window to choose and what to attempt inside it.

The early afternoon window, from about half past two to half past four, is the best one in the city and the most wasted. A child who walked home or took a ten-minute bus is at a desk before three, the flat is often at its emptiest, and the student is not yet tired. It is the right window for anything demanding: a timed paper, an essay, a coursework stretch. Families leave it empty because it feels like the middle of the day.

The early evening window, from about six to eight, is the one everybody chooses and the worst of the four. The flat is full, dinner is happening, siblings are home, and the student has already been working for ten hours. It is usable for short, defined, low-friction work and it is a poor place to attempt anything requiring sustained concentration.

The late evening window after about half past eight is quieter and suits an older student who genuinely functions late, which some do and most do not. And the weekend morning window is the only block in the week that is both long and uncontested, which makes it the home for the single heaviest piece of work in the week. The table below sets the four out with what each realistically supports.

sections.heading: Where a student works when the flat has no study
paragraphs: This is the practical problem nobody writes about, and it decides more outcomes in this district than any choice of tutor. A student needs a surface, a chair at the right height, light, a charged device, headphones and a door or a corner that signals do not interrupt. In a three-bedroom apartment housing five or six people, assembling those six things reliably at the same time each day is genuinely hard.

What works, from families who have solved it: a fixed corner rather than a fixed room, since a corner can be claimed and a room usually cannot. Headphones that the whole household recognises as a signal. An agreement with siblings rather than an instruction, which survives considerably longer. And the session time agreed with everyone in the flat, not just with the student, so nobody is surprised at four o'clock on a Tuesday.

What does not work: the living room during the hours anyone else is awake, a bed as a desk, a phone as the device, or an arrangement that depends on a younger sibling being quiet because they were asked once. Those four account for most of the sessions that degrade over a term until the family concludes tutoring does not work for them.

There are also free alternatives worth knowing. A school library or a supervised homework club, if the school runs one, solves the problem entirely and costs nothing, and it is always worth asking about before buying anything. Public library space exists in the city. And for a student with an older sibling, a shared agreement about which hours each one gets the quiet corner is more effective than either of them negotiating alone.

Agree the hour with the whole flat, not only with the student

sections.heading: Six provider models compared, with the rates attributed
paragraphs: This market is opaque about price, which hurts budget-conscious families most. Three of the six competitor pages examined for this project publish no figure at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars rather than dirhams. So the table below compares the models themselves, with every rate attributed to whoever published it and the month it was read.

The pattern in it matters more than any single number. The cheap end of the market, AED 45 to 150 an hour, is university students and non-specialist generalists, and it is genuinely useful for primary-level support, homework supervision and basic consolidation. It is not useful for a Higher Level Diploma subject or for coursework supervision, because the person at that price point has usually not taught the syllabus. Paying specialist rates for homework supervision is equally wasteful in the other direction.

Tuition centres and group classes occupy a real middle ground. Per student they are cheaper, and for shared revision of a common syllabus they work well. What they cannot address is an individual error pattern, which is by definition different for each student in the room, and individual error patterns are what cost capable students their grades. A sensible split on a tight budget is a group for revision plus a small number of individual sessions for diagnosis.

Independent freelance tutors are often the best value in this district and carry the most variance. Some are outstanding; some are unpermitted; some teach a different board from the one your child sits. The next section covers how to check the first and the last of those without awkwardness.

sections.heading: Is the person teaching your child legally permitted to do it?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and in a district with this much informal tutoring that is worth knowing in detail rather than vaguely. Individuals providing private lessons need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits.

Three facts make the conversation easy. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, so nobody has a financial reason to avoid it. Eligibility is broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. And the application route is public, through the Ministry's own smart app, website and e-services system, with the service listed as the issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing and a completion time of two working days.

The consequence of not holding one is also published, and the limits of what is published matter. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from the Ministry are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any specific amount circulating in a group chat is unverified and should be treated as such. We do not quote one.

There is a separate point specific to this emirate. Press reporting indicates that the Department of Education and Knowledge sets professional-ethics rules prohibiting private and charter school staff from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that the permit's own code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's school. Treat that as reported rather than quoted, and verify it against the current policy document if it matters to your situation. The practical implication is clear enough: your child's own class teacher is not the right person to hire privately, however convenient it seems.

How to ask is simpler than parents fear. Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition permit, and which board and syllabus code do you teach. Those two questions are routine, they cost nothing, and a tutor who is irritated by them has answered a third question you did not ask.

sections.heading: Prayer times, Ramadan and the rhythm of a central district
paragraphs: Central Abu Dhabi runs on a rhythm that a tutoring schedule should accommodate rather than ignore. Prayer times move through the year and the afternoon and sunset prayers both fall inside the hours families most want to use. A session that butts up against one of them ends badly for everybody, and the fix is simply to ask at the first conversation rather than to discover it in week three.

The sensible approach is to set the slot with a buffer in both directions and to accept that the slot will shift across the year as the times move. A fixed time that is wrong for four months of the year is worse than a slot reviewed twice a year. Families who state their preference up front get a workable arrangement; families who feel awkward raising it tend to lose sessions instead.

Ramadan reshapes the whole day. Schools across the emirate run shortened hours, which puts children home much earlier and opens an early afternoon window that the rest of the year does not have. Many older students in this district prefer a post-Iftar session, which tends to be calmer and considerably more productive than a rushed term-time evening in a full flat. Either arrangement is better than letting the month lapse and restarting late, which costs three or four weeks of momentum right before the mock season.

The long summer break matters too, particularly for budget-conscious families. It is the only period in which a real foundation rebuild is possible, because nothing competes with it, and intensive work concentrated into July and August is usually cheaper in total hours than spreading the same rebuild across a term while new material arrives.
bullets: State prayer-time preferences at the first conversation, not in week three
Expect the slot to shift across the year as the times move
Shortened Ramadan days open an early window; post-Iftar suits older students

sections.heading: Spending a tight tutoring budget in the right order
paragraphs: If the budget is fixed, the order of spending matters more than the rate. The sequence below is what we would advise a family in this district to follow, and the first two items cost nothing.

First, ask the school what free support exists: a homework club, a library hour, subject support sessions, a revision class. Many schools run these and many parents never ask. Second, get the examination board and full syllabus code for every examined subject in writing, so that no paid hour is ever spent on the wrong board's past papers. Third, buy a diagnostic: one or two hours built around the most recent marked script, producing a written assessment. For a meaningful number of families the diagnosis is a technique habit the student can correct with set work, and the spending stops there.

Fourth, if teaching is genuinely needed, buy one subject with continuity rather than several thinly. Choose it by which grade is most at risk rather than which subject feels weakest, because those are often different: a Higher Level grade that decides a university offer matters more than a Standard Level subject that is merely uncomfortable. Fifth, add coursework blocks against the school's own deadline list, because those are small, defined purchases with a disproportionate effect on a grade that is a fifth coursework.

What not to buy, on any budget: an open-ended weekly arrangement across four subjects, a package bought before a diagnosis, a specialist rate for homework supervision, a budget rate for a Higher Level subject, and anything at all from a provider offering to produce coursework. That last item is covered in its own section below, because it is sold hardest to exactly the families who can least afford the consequence.
bullets: Free school support and the syllabus codes first, because both cost nothing
Then a diagnostic; for many families the spending ends there
Then one subject with continuity, chosen by which grade is most at risk
Then coursework blocks placed against the school's own deadlines

sections.heading: The home tutor question in a central apartment block
paragraphs: Parents here search for a home tutor, and in a dense apartment district the honest answer is more complicated than the rate difference suggests. A visiting tutor and a sixteen-year-old working through a mock script occupy the only shared surface in the flat for ninety minutes. In a household of five that displaces everybody else, and it happens weekly.

The money runs against it too. Market in-home one-to-one visits are AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel inside the figure, on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table and comparable listings, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a comparably qualified tutor working online. For a family on a fixed monthly figure, that difference is a session a month, which over a year is a full term of extra support for the same money.

IB Gram does not make home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons for Abu Dhabi families run one-to-one over live video. In a flat that means a corner, headphones and a closed door rather than a cleared living room, and it means the rate carries no travel premium.

The honest limitation is attention supervision for younger children. A nine-year-old who needs an adult physically present to stay on task is harder to hold on screen, and for that age we recommend shorter sessions, more often, with a parent within earshot. That is a real constraint rather than a sales caveat, and it is better stated than discovered.
bullets: A visiting tutor occupies the only shared surface in the flat, weekly

sections.heading: Coursework, and the offers a parent should refuse
paragraphs: Every programme in this district carries work produced away from the examination hall: a Diploma internal assessment in each subject, the Extended Essay at 4,000 words, the Theory of Knowledge essay at 1,600, the MYP Personal Project, coursework in some IGCSE subjects. That work must be the student's own, and a breach is recorded against the student. It can cost a diploma.

The offers to refuse are circulating in this district, in group chats and on noticeboards as well as online. One operation in this market sells completed Diploma internal assessments outright, at a price that looks almost reasonable next to a term of tuition. It is marketed as a shortcut for a busy student and it is an integrity breach that the student alone carries. No legitimate tutor supplies text, rewrites a section into something the student could not have produced, edits a draft to completion, or hands over a topic, structure or data set ready-made.

What a legitimate tutor does with coursework is substantial and considerably cheaper than the alternative. Interrogating the research question until it can be answered inside the word limit. Pointing out that a planned method will not generate usable data, before any data exists. Reading a draft against the published criteria and naming the criterion that is unevidenced. Teaching the missing skill, then returning the work. Asking the student to justify a paragraph out loud.

We also do not supply or reproduce subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables from the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Those belong to the boards and your child's school holds them legitimately. A provider advertising a library of board documents is telling you how it treats rules in general, which is useful information before you hand over any money.
bullets: Completed coursework is sold in this market; the student carries the breach
Questions, methods and criteria coaching, placed early, cost far less
No supplied text, no rewriting to completion, no ready-made topics or data
Board materials are referenced and linked, never redistributed

sections.heading: Starting from Madinat Zayed
paragraphs: Four things before the first paid hour, and two of them are free. The examination board and full syllabus code for every examined subject, in writing from the school. Whatever free support the school already offers, which many families never ask about. The most recent marked script in the subject that worries you. And an honest answer about where in the flat the student will actually sit, and at what time the whole household can live with.

Then a diagnostic session rather than an introduction. The tutor marks the script with your child against the official scheme and names what is actually happening: a content gap, tariff discipline, command-term misreading, pacing, or a tier that does not fit. That written assessment is yours whether or not you continue, and it is also the document that makes a conversation with the school about a set or tier change productive rather than awkward.

After that, the narrowest plan that addresses the finding. One subject, one slot, a defined target and a date to measure it on a real paper. If the finding is a technique habit, the plan is six weeks of drilling and a re-measurement, not an open arrangement. We would rather finish and be recommended than renew quietly for a year.

Two honest limits stated up front. Coverage for the rarer Diploma languages and some Higher Level combinations is thin in this time zone, and when there is no real match we say so rather than substituting a generalist. And whoever you engage, from us or anyone else, ask about the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition permit. It is free, it lasts two years, the eligibility list is broad, and the question takes five seconds.
bullets: Syllabus codes and free school support first; both cost nothing
The diagnostic produces a written assessment you keep either way
The narrowest plan that addresses the actual finding, with a measurement date

whyPoints.description: The constraint here is quiet rather than time, so the advice is about corners, headphones, household agreements and the empty early-afternoon window that almost nobody uses. faqs.question: Which hour of the day is actually best for studying in a central Abu Dhabi flat?
faqs.answer: The early afternoon, from about half past two to half past four, and almost nobody uses it. A child who walked home or took a short bus is at a desk before three, the flat is at its emptiest, and the student is not yet tired. That window will carry a timed paper or an essay. The six to eight o'clock slot that most families choose is the worst of the four: the flat is full, dinner is happening, and the student has already been working for ten hours.

faqs.question: My child has nowhere quiet to work. What do other families here do?
faqs.answer: They claim a corner rather than a room, because corners can actually be held. Headphones become a recognised signal rather than a request. The arrangement is made with siblings rather than imposed on them, which survives much longer. And the session time is agreed with the whole flat so nobody is surprised on a Tuesday afternoon. Before buying anything, ask the school whether it runs a homework club or an open library hour, because that solves the problem completely and costs nothing at all.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Abu Dhabi need a permit, and what does it cost?
faqs.answer: Yes, and nothing. Individuals providing private lessons need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the Ministry's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system. Because it costs nothing, there is no financial reason for a legitimate tutor not to hold one, which makes the question easy to ask.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for the private tuition permit?
faqs.answer: The published eligibility is broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. That breadth is useful for parents to know, because it means a tutor at the budget end of the market, typically a university student, can perfectly well be permitted. The absence of a permit is therefore a choice rather than an obstacle, and it tells you something worth knowing before the first session.

faqs.question: What is the fine for tutoring without a permit in the UAE?
faqs.answer: No amount has been published, and we will not repeat one. The official position is that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from the Ministry are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, with no schedule specified. Figures circulating in group chats and on some tutoring websites are unverified. The practical point for a parent is not the penalty but the signal: a tutor operating outside a free, broadly available permit scheme has made a decision about rules in general.

faqs.question: Can I hire my child's own class teacher for private lessons?
faqs.answer: It is reported that the Department of Education and Knowledge prohibits private and charter school staff from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's school. Treat that as press-reported rather than as a quotation and verify it against the current policy if it matters to you. Either way the practical answer is clear: however convenient it looks, your child's own teacher is not the right person to engage privately.

faqs.question: Is a budget tutor at AED 60 an hour ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the right job. The AED 45 to 150 band, generally university students and non-specialist generalists, is genuinely useful for primary support, homework supervision and basic consolidation, and paying specialist rates for that work is wasteful. What it cannot do is a Higher Level Diploma subject or coursework supervision, because a person at that price point has usually not taught the syllabus. Matching the rate to the job in both directions is how a fixed budget goes furthest.

faqs.question: Group class or individual tutor on a tight budget?
faqs.answer: Both, in the right proportion. A group is cheaper per student and works well for shared revision of a common syllabus, since the content is identical for everyone in the room. It cannot address an individual error pattern, and individual error patterns are what cost capable students their grades. The split that works is a group for revision plus a small number of individual sessions for diagnosis and script marking, which costs less than a weekly individual arrangement and does more than a group alone.

faqs.question: What should I spend the first hundred dirhams of a tutoring budget on?
faqs.answer: Nothing, until two free things are done. Ask the school what support it already provides, because homework clubs and library hours solve a surprising share of problems. And get the examination board and full syllabus code for every examined subject in writing, so no paid hour is ever spent on the wrong board's papers. After that, the first paid purchase should be a diagnostic built around the most recent marked script, because for many families the finding makes further spending unnecessary.

faqs.question: Do tutors visit apartments in Madinat Zayed?
faqs.answer: Not through us. IB Gram does not make home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India, and Abu Dhabi lessons run one-to-one over live video. Independent in-home tutors do work in this district at market rates of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel inside the figure, against AED 150 to AED 300 online. In a flat there is also a space cost nobody prices: a weekly visitor occupies the only shared surface in the home for ninety minutes.

faqs.question: How do I ask a tutor about their permit without being rude?
faqs.answer: Make it one of two routine questions asked together: do you hold the MoHRE private tuition permit, and which board and syllabus code do you teach. Framed as logistics rather than as suspicion, it is unremarkable, and most tutors answer both in a sentence. A tutor who is irritated by the first question has told you something useful, and a tutor who cannot answer the second is about to practise the wrong papers with your child, which is the more expensive problem of the two.

faqs.question: Can sessions avoid prayer times?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is better raised at the first conversation than discovered in week three. Prayer times move through the year, and the afternoon and sunset prayers both fall inside the hours families most want to use. The sensible arrangement is a slot with a buffer either side and a review twice a year as the times shift, rather than a fixed hour that is wrong for four months. Families who state the preference up front get a workable arrangement; those who hesitate tend to lose sessions instead.

faqs.question: Someone offered to prepare my child's internal assessment. Should I consider it?
faqs.answer: No. That work must be the student's own, and a malpractice finding is recorded against your child rather than against whoever supplied it, with the diploma itself at risk. One operation in this market sells completed Diploma internal assessments at a price that looks almost reasonable next to a term of tuition, which is exactly why it is dangerous. Legitimate help is cheaper anyway: coaching the research question, checking the method before data is collected, and naming the criterion a draft fails to evidence.

faqs.question: How many weeks before we know whether tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: About twelve, measured on something external. A full paper under genuine timing, marked against the official scheme, compared with the script we started from. Sessions feeling productive is not evidence, and on a fixed budget that distinction matters more than anywhere. If the marks have moved, continue or finish. If they have not after twelve weeks of kept sessions and completed set work, the plan changes or the tutor does, and we will say so first.

faqs.question: Should we stop tutoring during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Move it rather than stop it. Schools run shortened days, children are home much earlier, and an early afternoon window opens that exists at no other point in the year. Many older students in this district prefer a post-Iftar session, which is calmer and more productive than a rushed evening in a full flat. Letting the month lapse and restarting late costs three or four weeks of momentum immediately before the mock season, which is the worst moment in the year to lose it.

abu-dhabi/madinat-zayed.closingBody: Ask your child's school two questions this week. What support does it already provide free, and what is the examination board and full syllabus code for every examined subject. The first often solves a quiet-space problem that looked like an academic one. The second prevents the most expensive mistake in this market, which is practising the wrong board's papers for a term. Then send us the most recent marked script and buy one diagnostic hour, not a package. For a fair number of Madinat Zayed families that is where the spending sensibly stops, and where it does not, the plan that follows is one subject, one slot and one measurement date, delivered one-to-one over live video.
