sections.heading: What the timetable delivers, and what your child is left holding
paragraphs: Before buying anything, it is worth separating what a school can do from what it cannot. Taught periods are finite and they have to carry new content. Consolidation is set as homework, which is collected and checked rather than taught again. Beyond those two categories sits a third that belongs to the student alone, and in an examined programme it is large.

The third category includes consolidation that was never set, past-paper practice, the first draft of an assessed piece, the memorisation that makes a paper possible, and the reading that makes the next lesson comprehensible. None of it appears on a timetable. None of it is marked. Nobody is responsible for noticing when it does not happen, and that is exactly why a report can say the child is attending and engaged while the marks drift.

Parents on Yas frequently reach a different conclusion, which is that the school is at fault. Occasionally it is. More often the school is doing what schools do and the gap is structural. Testing which it is takes one exercise: ask the student to produce, under time and without notes, something they were taught six weeks ago. If they can, the teaching landed and the problem is elsewhere. If they cannot, the content was covered but never consolidated, which is a different purchase.

Use the table as a diagnostic rather than a description. Work down the component column for your child's subject and ask honestly which of the last three columns each row belongs in. The rows that fall into the unsupervised column, with nobody noticing, are where the tutoring hours should go.

sections.heading: An independent-study week, written down
paragraphs: The fix for an unsupervised half-week is not more hours; it is defined outputs. 'Revise biology' produces the appearance of study. 'This past-paper section, timed, marked against the scheme, with the three biggest losses listed' produces a document, and a document can be reviewed. The difference in results between those two instructions is larger than the difference between a good tutor and an average one.

The week below is a template rather than a prescription, built for a Year 11 or Diploma student on a Yas school run. It assumes five short weekday windows and one longer weekend slot, because that is what the commutes here leave. Adjust the subjects; keep the structure, and keep the rule that every slot ends with something written that someone will look at.

Two rules make it hold. Fix the place and the time, so the student stops deciding when and where each day, and let someone see the output in the next tutoring session. The second rule is the one that does the work: an hour whose product is reviewed by another person stops being optional. That is the real function of a weekly slot, and it is almost never how tutoring is sold.

The weekend slot is where timed work belongs. A student used to continuous assessment needs to build examination stamina deliberately, and that means sitting full sections without notes, at full length, repeatedly. Nothing in a continuous-assessment school week asks for that, which is why it has to be scheduled rather than assumed.

sections.heading: Advanced Placement, the Diploma and A Levels compared
paragraphs: Yas families reach this decision more often than most Abu Dhabi households, because the island's school mix puts an American route alongside British and IB options within a short drive. The three are genuinely different products and the choice should follow the student rather than the brand.

Advanced Placement is modular in the most useful sense: courses are taken individually, a strong student can take several and a cautious one can take one, and each is examined separately on a 1 to 5 scale in a window set by the College Board. It fits a student who performs steadily across a year and wants to demonstrate depth in selected subjects without committing to a fixed programme shape. It does not build the examination stamina that a terminal system demands.

The Diploma is a fixed shape: six subjects, three core components, and a points total. It spreads risk, so one weak subject does not sink a result, and it demands sustained independent project work. A Levels concentrate risk in three named grades and reward examination technique above everything else, with the most predictable workload of the three and the least room to absorb a poor result.

Decide on marked timed work rather than on reputation. Sit a timed written piece and a timed problem paper in the student's two strongest subjects and have them marked honestly. Where the evidence is balanced, choose the school and the department rather than the qualification; a well-staffed cohort in any of the three beats a thin one in the other two.

sections.heading: The American track and what the Ministry actually publishes
paragraphs: Families on an American route who intend to study in the UAE will meet the Ministry of Education's equivalency process, and the published requirements for this track are specific and testable rather than vague. They also differ in kind from the British-track requirements, which are expressed in subject counts and grades.

For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test, and the published source states this applies before applying rather than afterwards. The same source does not mention EmSAT, so no EmSAT requirement is stated here.

The practical implication for a Yas household on an American route is that two of those requirements are standardised tests with their own preparation and their own sittings, and they need to be planned into Grade 11 and Grade 12 rather than discovered in the spring of the final year. A student whose transcript is strong and whose SAT Math sits below the stated threshold has a problem that is entirely solvable with notice and awkward without it.

Two cautions apply. Equivalency is run by the authority; it is not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or accelerates, and we point families to the Ministry's own channels for current rules. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency or for a university place — any page suggesting otherwise is manufacturing urgency about an administrative process, which is a reason to treat the rest of its claims with caution.

sections.heading: Where marks leave the page in a timed examination
paragraphs: A student moving from continuous assessment into terminal examinations loses marks in a pattern that has very little to do with knowledge, and recognising the pattern is most of the repair. The first and largest loss is pacing. A student who has always worked to a deadline measured in days writes the first two questions beautifully and abandons the last one, which in most papers is where the heaviest marks sit.

The second loss is the absence of notes. Continuous assessment usually permits reference material, and a student whose understanding is sound but whose recall was never rehearsed finds the examination asks for memory rather than comprehension. Definitions, equations, named studies and command-term conventions have to be in the head, and that is rehearsal rather than learning.

The third loss is command-term mismatch, which costs marks in every written subject. 'Explain' requires a causal chain, 'describe' does not, and 'evaluate' needs a judgement with support. A student who writes the same quality of answer to all three earns the marks for only one of them. It is a vocabulary problem and it takes a handful of sessions to fix.

The fourth is mechanical: units dropped, significant figures ignored, axes mislabelled, working not shown, an answer written outside the space. These are the cheapest marks in the building and they are lost by strong students more often than weak ones, because strong students work quickly. A marked script shows all four patterns in twenty minutes, which is why we ask for one before suggesting a plan.

sections.heading: Past papers done properly, and what we will not supply
paragraphs: Most students use past papers badly: they read a question, decide they could answer it, and move on. That produces familiarity rather than capability. Used properly, a past paper is a measuring instrument. Sat under time, without notes, then marked against the official scheme by someone who knows how the marks are awarded, it gives a number and a list. Both are necessary.

The method that works is short and rarely followed. Choose one section rather than a whole paper. Time it exactly. Put the notes away. Mark it immediately against the official mark scheme, line by line, awarding marks the way a marker would rather than the way a sympathetic parent would. Then write down the three largest losses and treat that list as the next fortnight's work. Repeat with a different section, and compare.

There is one thing we will not do, and it is worth saying plainly because competitors in this market do otherwise. We do not reproduce, host or supply board papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or syllabus documents. They are the copyright of Cambridge International, Pearson, the IB and the College Board, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure on top of the copyright problem. We reference them, cite the official source and link out to it.

The practical route for a parent is simpler than it looks. Schools hold the materials their students are entitled to use and will usually release past papers for revision on request. The boards publish specimen and past material through their own channels. Ask the school first; it costs nothing and it keeps everyone on the right side of a rule that at least some providers in this market ignore.

sections.heading: What support costs on Yas, and which band fits which job
paragraphs: Published rates in this market span a wide range and most of the best-ranking pages give no figure at all. The table sets out the market's own numbers in AED with the provider that published each. They describe the market rather than an IB Gram rate card; ask us for the trial and the consultation if you want our figures and what sits inside the hour.

The useful question is not which band is best but which band fits the job. A supervised practice slot whose purpose is to look at work the student produced does not need the top of the market; it needs someone who marks accurately and tells the truth. A Higher Level subject that a university offer turns on may genuinely justify a specialist. Buying the specialist for the practice slot is the commonest overspend here.

At the bottom of the market the hour is usually teaching time alone, with no marking of work set between sessions. For the independent-study problem this page is about, that is the least useful possible purchase: the entire mechanism depends on someone reading what the student produced. Paying less for an hour that excludes the marking is not a saving.

Three questions settle most comparisons. Is the rate per hour or per session? Is marking of work set between sessions included or billed separately? Does the rate change in the exam term? Those answers vary far more between providers than the headline numbers do.

sections.heading: Event weeks, weekends and a Yas Island timetable
paragraphs: Yas is built around leisure, and that shapes the academic year in ways no revision timetable accounts for. Event weekends bring heavy traffic onto and off the island, the mall and the parks are a short walk or drive from most of the residential phases, and houseguests arrive in the cooler months. A plan that assumes a quiet Friday and Saturday will survive about three weeks.

The sensible response is to plan around it rather than pretend otherwise. Identify the weekends that will not be available and move the long timed session rather than skipping it: a Thursday evening or a Sunday morning is better than a lost week. Treat the cooler months as the period when the household is busiest socially, which is the opposite of the assumption most revision plans make.

Ramadan has a separate effect and is worth planning a fortnight ahead. Schools run shortened days, so the afternoon returns earlier and the usual late slot often stops working because the household's rhythm has shifted. Many families move to a later evening session after Iftar or to a mid-morning weekend slot. Because lessons are online, the change is one line in a calendar rather than a renegotiation of anyone's driving route.

The long summer break is the other structural feature of the UAE year. For a Yas household it is the cheapest period to buy improvement in, because the commute disappears and the day has room in it. Holiday work is best bought as a defined block with a written target and a diagnostic at each end, rather than as general sessions to keep a student ticking over.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with assessed work
paragraphs: Every programme on this island carries work that is assessed as the student's own: internal assessments and the core in the Diploma, coursework in several IGCSE subjects, research tasks and projects on the American route. Academic-honesty rules treat a breach as malpractice and the consequences land on the student, not on whoever helped.

The line stated plainly. A tutor may teach the assessment criteria letter by letter with the marks attached to each. A tutor may test a proposed research question and say honestly whether it is narrow enough to generate usable data. A tutor may read a draft the student has produced and give feedback on structure, reasoning, evidence and clarity. A tutor may teach the underlying skills — referencing, uncertainty treatment, graph conventions, evaluation language — on a different example.

A tutor may not author any sentence that appears in a submission, provide text for the student to adapt, build the student's data set, or supply a model answer to the student's own question. Where a school's rules are tighter than the board's, the school's rules apply, and some schools limit external feedback on an assessed draft to one round. Ask about that at the start of a task rather than at the end.

For standardised tests the rule is simpler and absolute: a tutor teaches technique and supervises timed practice, and has no involvement of any kind during a live assessment. Any provider whose offer blurs that boundary is selling a risk that falls entirely on the student, and at least one operation in this market already sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price.

sections.heading: Starting from Yas Island
paragraphs: Send three things and the first conversation is useful: the school with board and syllabus codes, the most recent marked script with the teacher's annotations still on it, and an honest account of what the student actually does in the unsupervised hours. The third item is the one families hesitate over and the one that decides the plan, because the whole question on this page is what happens outside taught periods.

The trial is taught rather than sold. The tutor sets a short diagnostic, works it through live, and writes afterwards naming the specific losses found and what the first six weeks would target. For most Yas enquiries that plan is a supervised practice arrangement rather than content teaching, which is usually cheaper than the family expected and less dramatic than they feared.

Where the honest answer is that tutoring is not the right purchase, we say so. A student who is attending, engaged and simply not consolidating needs a structure and someone to look at the output, which can sometimes be built without a weekly paid lesson at all. We would rather tell you that and keep the fortnightly review than sell a term of teaching into a problem that is not a teaching problem.

On availability: the post-five weekday window is the most requested in Abu Dhabi and the first to fill, with January the tightest month. For a few niche Higher Level subjects the specialist may be based outside the UAE and teaching into a UAE evening; we say where a tutor is based whenever you ask. We claim no approval or accreditation from ADEK, the Ministry of Education or any examination board, because we hold none.

process.title: Test whether the teaching landed
process.description: Ask the student to produce, under time and without notes, something taught six weeks ago. If they can, the problem is not class coverage. If they cannot, the content was covered and never consolidated, which is a different and usually cheaper thing to fix.

process.title: Send a marked script
process.description: A script with annotations shows all four loss patterns in twenty minutes: pacing, recall, command-term mismatch and mechanical errors. Percentages show how much was lost; only the script shows where, and the where determines what kind of tutor is needed.

process.title: Write the independent week down
process.description: Five short weekday windows and one longer weekend slot, each with an output rather than a subject. Fixed place, fixed time. The template on this page is a starting point; the structure matters more than the particular subjects in it.

process.title: Make the output visible
process.description: Every independent slot ends with something written that someone will look at in the next session. That single mechanism is what converts optional hours into real ones, and it is the main function of a weekly or fortnightly slot.

process.title: Use past papers as instruments
process.description: One section, exactly timed, no notes, marked immediately against the official scheme, three largest losses written down. Ask the school for the materials your child is entitled to use; we link official sources and do not supply papers ourselves.

process.title: Compare at six weeks
process.description: A second timed section, marked the same way, set against the first. If the marks and the pacing have not moved we change the method or the tutor, and we say when the honest answer is that the structure rather than the teaching needs fixing.

whyPoints.title: Aimed at the unsupervised half
whyPoints.description: Most enquiries from this island are about a gap that sits outside taught periods. We name it component by component, write the independent week down with an output per slot, and make that output visible, which is the mechanism that actually changes results.

whyPoints.title: Supervised practice as a product
whyPoints.description: A session whose purpose is to mark what the student produced alone is a different purchase from content teaching, and usually a cheaper and more effective one. We sell it as what it is rather than bundling it into a general weekly lesson.

whyPoints.title: Built for a continuous-assessment background
whyPoints.description: Students from American routes arrive at terminal examinations with sound understanding and no pacing. Timed full sections, spaced out and marked immediately, build the stamina that no continuous-assessment week asks for.

whyPoints.title: We do not hand out board material
whyPoints.description: Past papers, mark schemes, grade boundaries and syllabus documents are the boards' copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well. We cite and link the official source and tell you to ask the school, which is where the entitlement sits.

whyPoints.title: Figures attributed, claims absent
whyPoints.description: Every AED rate here is a market figure with the publisher named, and none is ours. There are no satisfaction percentages, tutor headcounts or ratings on this page, because we cannot produce the data behind them and an unverifiable number helps nobody.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line, including for standardised tests
whyPoints.description: Criteria taught, questions tested for scope, feedback on the student's own drafts, and no involvement of any kind during a live assessment. Where a school's rule on external feedback is tighter than the board's, the school's rule applies.

faqs.question: My child attends every lesson and hands in all the homework. Why are the marks still falling?
faqs.answer: Because attendance and homework cover two of the three parts of learning, and the third is large. Taught periods carry new content, homework covers some consolidation, and everything else — memorisation, past-paper practice, first drafts, reviewing marked work for patterns — is genuinely unsupervised and nobody notices when it does not happen. Test it directly: ask your child to produce something taught six weeks ago, under time and without notes. If they cannot, the content was covered but never consolidated.

faqs.question: How much independent work does a Diploma student actually have to do alone?
faqs.answer: More than any other route available in Abu Dhabi. Six internally assessed components, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are all produced outside taught periods on school-set deadlines, and the school cannot supervise the drafting. On top of that sits consolidation and past-paper practice in six subjects. The practical consequence is that in the second year a weekly slot spent on project supervision is often worth more than the same hour spent teaching content.

faqs.question: What should a revision session produce, rather than just cover?
faqs.answer: Something written that another person will look at. 'Revise biology' produces the appearance of study; 'this past-paper section, timed, marked against the official scheme, with the three biggest losses listed' produces a document. Fixed place, fixed time, defined output. The mechanism that makes it stick is review: when a tutor opens the next session with what was produced, those hours stop being optional, and that shift matters more than the choice of tutor.

faqs.question: Do tutors travel to Yas Island in the evenings?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We deliver tutoring in the UAE as one-to-one lessons online, over live video, and we do not send anyone to a residential address in the Emirates; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Published market rates for visiting tutors run AED 180-500 an hour with travel inside the figure. For the kind of work this page describes, the online format also has a practical edge: the marked script is shared, annotated live and still available next week.

faqs.question: Should my son take Advanced Placement courses or move to the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Decide on marked timed work rather than reputation. Advanced Placement suits a student who performs steadily across a year and wants depth in selected subjects without a fixed programme shape, with each course examined separately on a 1 to 5 scale. The Diploma suits a student who manages long independent projects and needs breadth, and it spreads risk across six subjects plus the core. The Diploma demands considerably more examination stamina and considerably more self-managed project work.

faqs.question: How do we build exam stamina for a child who has only ever had continuous assessment?
faqs.answer: Deliberately, because nothing in a continuous-assessment week asks for it. Sit full paper sections under exact timing, without notes, repeatedly, starting well before the examination term and spacing them out. Mark each one immediately and record pacing as well as accuracy, because the characteristic loss is a strong first half and an abandoned final question where the heaviest marks often sit. Ninety minutes at the weekend is the right slot; a weekday evening after school is not.

faqs.question: Can you send us past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason matters. Past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and syllabus documents are the copyright of Cambridge International, Pearson, the IB and the College Board, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well as a copyright one. We reference them and link the official source. The practical route is to ask the school, which holds the materials its students are entitled to use and will usually release past papers for revision on request.

faqs.question: What are the American-track requirements for Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test, and the published source states this applies before applying. The source does not mention EmSAT, so no EmSAT requirement is stated here. Verify current rules with the Ministry directly; equivalency is run by the authority and not something a tutoring provider performs or accelerates.

faqs.question: How many tutoring sessions does a supervised-practice arrangement need?
faqs.answer: Often fewer than families expect. Once the independent week is written down and the habit is established, fortnightly is frequently enough: the session exists to mark what was produced, classify the losses and set the next fortnight's work. Weekly makes sense while the habit is being built, in an examination term, or when an assessed component is in progress. We review the frequency at six weeks and we will suggest reducing it when the evidence supports that.

faqs.question: Which subjects on Yas Island get asked about most?
faqs.answer: Mathematics first, across every route, followed by Chemistry and Physics where the losses are usually mechanical and diagnosable. After those come the written subjects, where the request is nearly always about turning understanding into answers rather than about content, and Theory of Knowledge, which families discover late. On American routes the requests skew towards examination technique and standardised tests rather than subject content, which reflects the structural gap rather than the teaching.

faqs.question: How do event weekends and traffic on the island affect a study plan?
faqs.answer: More than most plans allow for. Yas is organised around leisure, so event weekends bring heavy traffic and houseguests arrive in the cooler months, which is exactly when revision plans assume quiet weekends. Identify the unavailable weekends in advance and move the long timed session to a Thursday evening or Sunday morning rather than losing it. Because lessons are online, moving a slot is a calendar change rather than a renegotiation of anyone's route.

faqs.question: Does the Ramadan timetable on Yas Island mean moving our lesson slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth arranging a fortnight ahead rather than week by week. Schools run shortened days during Ramadan, so the afternoon return comes earlier and the usual late-afternoon slot often stops working because the household rhythm has shifted. Families commonly move to a later evening session after Iftar or to a mid-morning slot at the weekend. Tell us in advance and the slot is held in the new pattern for the whole period.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an Extended Essay or an internal assessment draft?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can teach the criteria letter by letter with their mark allocations, test whether a research question is narrow enough to produce usable data, read a draft the student has produced and give feedback on structure, reasoning and use of evidence, and teach the required skills on a different example. A tutor cannot author text appearing in the submission or build the data set. Where a school limits external feedback to one round, that limit applies.

faqs.question: Is the summer break a good time to buy tutoring?
faqs.answer: It is often the cheapest improvement available to a Yas household, because the school commute disappears and the day has room in it. Buy it as a defined block with a written target rather than as general sessions: closing specific gaps identified from marked scripts, bridging from IGCSE into the Diploma, or building the examination stamina a continuous-assessment year did not. A diagnostic at the start and a repeat at the end gives you something to judge the block by.

faqs.question: What happens if the specialist we want has no slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you and offer the real alternatives: a different weekday or weekend time, a different tutor with the same component experience, or waiting. The post-five weekday window is the most requested in Abu Dhabi and January is the tightest month of the year. For a few niche Higher Level subjects the person who knows the paper may be based outside the UAE and teaching into a UAE evening, and we say where a tutor is based whenever you ask rather than leaving it to be discovered.

Send us the board and syllabus codes, the most recent marked script, and an honest account of what happens in the hours nobody watches. We will set a diagnostic in the trial, name the losses we find, and in most cases propose supervised practice rather than more teaching. Where a structure would do the job without a weekly paid lesson, we will say that too. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video.

intro.heading: Ajman sits under a different regulator, and that changes what you can learn about a school
paragraphs: Four emirates run their own school regulator. Dubai has KHDA. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have ADEK. Sharjah has SPEA. Ajman has none of them. Private schools here are licensed and inspected federally, by the Ministry of Education, along with those in Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain. The practical consequence for a parent is simple and rarely stated: the published record of your child's school in Ajman is thinner, and organised differently, than the report a neighbour in Jumeirah can pull up in two clicks. Choosing academic support here starts with knowing exactly what a Ministry of Education school inspection covers and what it leaves for you to ask about yourself.

A UAE inspection, under any of the regulators, judges a school on attainment and progress in a fixed set of subjects, phase by phase: Islamic Education, Arabic as a first language, Arabic as an additional language, English, mathematics and science, split across foundation, primary, middle and secondary. It also judges teaching, assessment, curriculum, protection and safeguarding, and leadership. Each judgement is drawn from the same six-band scale, from Outstanding down to Very Weak, with Acceptable set as the minimum the country expects. That is genuinely useful information. What it is not is a verdict on how well Chemistry is taught at Higher Level to a class of nine Year 13 students, because no inspection framework in the UAE reports at that resolution.

That gap matters more in Ajman than in Dubai, because the cohorts are smaller. A Diploma year group of thirty or forty students cannot run every option block. Higher Level sets fill with four or five students or they do not run at all, and a subject that was offered when your child chose it in Year 11 can quietly become a self-study arrangement by the middle of Year 12. One teacher leaving mid-course moves the whole set. None of this shows up in a whole-school band, and none of it is a criticism of the school: it is arithmetic. It is also the single most common reason an Ajman family starts looking for a subject specialist.

IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform, not a school and not an agency with a van. Tuition for families in Ajman is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in Ajman; home visits are a service we run only in India, and saying so plainly is more useful than pretending otherwise. The trade is deliberate. A family in Al Mowaihat gets a tutor who has taught Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level and marked its exploration against criterion E, instead of whoever is willing to drive out from Sharjah at seven in the evening.

The rest of this page is built in that order. First the regulator and how to read an inspection band without over-reading it. Then what tuition actually costs in this market, in AED, with the source of every figure named. Then the exam calendar counted backwards from the session your child sits, the Internal Assessment criteria by letter with their marks attached, the academic-honesty line a tutor may not cross, the Arabic and Islamic Education requirements that run alongside an international curriculum, and what Ministry of Education equivalency asks for when a school leaver applies to a UAE university. Nothing on this page is a promise about a grade. All of it is information you can check.

ajman.programmesIntro: Ajman carries a full IB continuum school alongside a large British and Indian sector, so a family here may be dealing with PYP report descriptors in one year group and Cambridge tier decisions in another. These are the four programme frames tuition is usually requested against, with what each one means for a student sitting in Ajman.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external exams. Progress is reported against learner-profile attributes and transdisciplinary units, which is why PYP reports read so differently from the marks-based reports a parent may expect. Support at this stage is mostly about securing number fluency, reading stamina and the habit of writing to a prompt, so that the move into MYP criteria is not the first time a child meets a rubric.
programmes.countryNote: In Ajman the PYP cohort is concentrated in a single continuum school, so there is no second PYP intake to move to if a year group does not suit. Primary requests here are usually for English reading age and for maths number work, and they come from parents comparing a PYP report with a cousin's CBSE marksheet and finding no common scale between them.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks every subject against four criteria, A to D, each out of 8, and converts the total to a 1-7 grade through published boundaries. MYP 5 can end in on-screen eAssessment and the IB MYP Certificate. The criteria are where marks are won and lost: a student who can do the science but cannot write a criterion D evaluation loses a quarter of the available marks without ever getting a question wrong.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to Diploma transition is the pressure point for Ajman families, because the local Diploma cohort is small and option blocks are decided early. A student aiming at Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level needs the MYP extended maths route, and that decision is often made in Year 9, two years before anyone in the family is thinking about a Diploma at all.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, scored 1-7, plus up to three core points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, for a maximum of 45 and a minimum pass of 24 with conditions attached. Higher Level is not the same course with more homework: Mathematics AA HL adds Paper 3, worth 20% of the grade and sat as an extended problem-solving paper with no equivalent at Standard Level.
programmes.countryNote: An Ajman Diploma student is often one of a handful taking a given Higher Level subject, which means less in-class differentiation and a timetable built around what the school can staff. That is where an online IB tutor in Ajman does most good: a weekly hour on the specific Higher Level content the set is thin on, run alongside school rather than repeating it.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Graded 9-1 in most subjects, with tiering decisions that cap the grade before the exam is sat. Cambridge splits many subjects into Core and Extended, so 0580 Core candidates take Papers 1 and 3 and cannot be awarded above grade 5 equivalence, while Extended candidates take Paper 2 non-calculator and Paper 4 with a calculator, each worth 50%. Edexcel International GCSE Maths A, 4MA1, tiers as Foundation and Higher instead.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman's British-curriculum schools do not all use the same board, and some mix boards by subject, so the first question for any IGCSE tutor in Ajman is which syllabus code the school entered. Cambridge IGCSE 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1 cover similar mathematics but set it out in different papers with different formula provision, and revising from the wrong board's past papers wastes a term.

ajman.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma and Middle Years subjects Ajman families request most, with what each one is actually assessed on. Weightings are taken from the current subject guides; your school's coordinator will confirm which guide a cohort is working to, because the IB revises them on a rolling cycle.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Higher Level, Paper 1 and Paper 2 carry 30% each and Paper 3 adds 20% as a two-question extended investigation. At Standard Level, Papers 1 and 2 are 40% each. Marks go missing in proof, calculus technique and the unstructured reasoning Paper 3 demands, which almost no school has time to practise properly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-active throughout, with statistics, modelling and, at Higher Level, graph theory and complex numbers. Higher Level also carries a Paper 3. The common failure is treating AI as the easier route and then meeting a modelling question that requires choosing the function, justifying it and criticising the fit.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Paper 1 splits into multiple choice and a data-based section for 36%, Paper 2 is 44%, and the scientific investigation is 20%. Organic mechanisms and energetics are where IB Chemistry HL students lose the most, usually because they can recall a reaction but cannot explain it with curly arrows and a named reagent.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Same assessment shape as Chemistry: Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44%, investigation at 20%. The Higher Level extension in fields, induction and quantum physics is where a thin set shows. Students who can manipulate the algebra still drop marks on the explanation command terms, where a formula earns nothing on its own.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy, with Paper 1 at 36% and Paper 2 at 44%, and a scientific investigation worth 20%. The marks are in precision of language: an answer that says a membrane is permeable where the mark scheme wants partially permeable scores zero, and that pattern repeats across the whole paper.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis of unseen non-literary texts is 35% at both levels. Higher Level adds the HL essay at 20%, written on a text studied, in 1,200 to 1,500 words. The Individual Oral is where most students under-prepare, because it is assessed on a global issue they chose themselves.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Productive writing, reading and listening papers plus an individual oral. A strong speaker can still score poorly, because the oral is marked on language, message and interactive skills against descriptors rather than on fluency. Ajman's multilingual cohorts often sit English B when English A would actually suit them better.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three 800-word commentaries form the portfolio, worth 30% at Standard Level and 20% at Higher Level, with Higher Level adding Paper 3 quantitative questions. Diagrams are the fastest marks on the paper and the most commonly wasted, because a diagram that is drawn but never referred to in the text earns almost nothing.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with a pre-released case for Paper 1 and an internal assessment worth 30% at Standard Level and 25% at Higher Level. Students lose marks by describing a tool rather than applying it to the organisation in front of them, and by leaving the evaluation command terms until the last paragraph.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Productive writing, a receptive paper covering listening and reading, and an individual oral. For students who speak Arabic at home but have been schooled in English, the written register is the obstacle rather than the vocabulary, and the fix is structured practice against the text-type conventions the paper expects.

ajman.igcseSubjectsIntro: Ajman's British-curriculum sector runs both Cambridge and Edexcel, sometimes within one school. The syllabus code is the thing to establish before any revision plan is written, because papers, tiering and formula provision differ between boards even where the content looks identical.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge IGCSE 0580 Extended now sets Paper 2 without a calculator and Paper 4 with one, 50% each, which has caught out cohorts drilled on older past papers. Edexcel 4MA1 Higher provides a different formula sheet. Tier choice caps the grade, so it is a decision worth revisiting in Year 11.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge runs multiple choice at 30%, theory at 50% and either the practical test or the alternative to practical at 20%. Electricity circuits and moments are the reliable losers. Students sitting the alternative to practical need taught exam technique, not more laboratory time, because it tests how experiments are described.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and the qualitative analysis tables are where Extended candidates separate from Core candidates. The analysis tables can be learned outright for straightforward marks, and most students never do. Edexcel's single-tier paper assumes the full content, with no Core safety net underneath it.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Long-answer questions reward recall expressed in the syllabus's own words. Genetics, transport in plants and the control of blood glucose produce the widest mark spread. Practice should be marked against the published scheme every time, because self-marking consistently flatters a student by a grade.

igcseSubjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / Edexcel 4EA1)
igcseSubjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response carry most of the marks, and both are assessed on reading as much as on writing. Students with strong spoken English routinely under-score because they answer the text rather than analysing the writer's method, which is what the mark scheme pays for.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
igcseSubjects.description: Two papers, with structured data response carrying the heavier weight. Definitions earn marks outright and are often skipped. Diagram accuracy, especially shifting the right curve in the right direction, is the difference between a 6 and an 8 for most candidates in this subject.

igcseSubjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (Cambridge 0508)
igcseSubjects.description: Reading comprehension and composition in formal Arabic. Ajman students who speak dialect at home and English at school often meet Modern Standard Arabic only in this exam, which makes the register, not the content, the thing to work on across Years 10 and 11.

ajman.regionsTitle: Ajman district by district, and what each one does to a session time
ajman.regionsIntro: Ajman is compact at the coast and then suddenly is not: the emirate includes two inland exclaves that sit a long drive from the city. Where a family lives changes the earliest realistic start time and, in the exclaves, whether a local specialist exists at all.

regions.name: Al Nuaimiya
regions.note: The densest part of Ajman city and home to several of the emirate's long-established private schools. Most children here are within fifteen minutes of the school gate, so the constraint on IGCSE tuition in Al Nuaimiya is the shape of the evening rather than travel time.

regions.name: Al Rashidiya
regions.note: Mixed apartment and villa blocks running back from the Corniche. A short school run means a 4.30pm start is realistic here, which is early by UAE standards and worth using, because a tired 8pm session is a wasted hour however good the tutor is.

regions.name: Al Jurf
regions.note: The industrial and school belt along Sheikh Ammar Road, with some of Ajman's largest Indian-curriculum intakes. Bus routes out of Al Jurf are long, so families here often find 5.30pm the first honest slot once a child has eaten.

regions.name: Al Mowaihat
regions.note: Villa districts whose working parents commute to Dubai over Emirates Road. Sessions that need a parent in the room do not start before 7pm on a weekday, which is exactly why a fixed weekly slot booked in advance works better here than an ad hoc arrangement.

regions.name: Al Zahya and Al Tallah
regions.note: Newer development close to Emirates Road and to Ajman's IB continuum provision. This is where the emirate's PYP, MYP and Diploma families are concentrated, and where requests for Higher Level sciences and Mathematics AA cluster.

regions.name: Al Helio and Al Rawda
regions.note: Residential expansion inland from the city, with children bussed in several directions to different curricula. A household here can be running a Cambridge Year 11 and an MYP Year 8 on the same evening, which makes back-to-back online slots far easier than two visits.

regions.name: Ajman Corniche and Al Rumailah
regions.note: Older apartment stock near the waterfront. A noticeable share of these children attend schools across the Sharjah border, so their term dates and mock timetables follow SPEA-regulated schools rather than Ajman ones, and revision has to be planned against the school's calendar.

regions.name: Masfout
regions.note: Ajman's inland exclave, roughly a hundred kilometres from the city and close to the Hatta road. There is no meaningful local market for a Diploma subject specialist, so online tuition in Masfout is not a compromise here; it is the only route to a Higher Level subject teacher.

regions.name: Manama
regions.note: The emirate's second exclave, inland beyond Al Dhaid. Families here face the same arithmetic as Masfout: a two-hour round trip to reach the coastal tutoring market, against a scheduled video session that starts when the school bus gets back.

regions.name: Emirates City and Al Alia
regions.note: Tower developments beside Emirates Road with a largely commuter population. Weekend sessions are popular here, and Friday or Saturday morning slots are easier to hold through exam term than a weekday evening that competes with a parent's drive home.

schoolClusters.city: Ajman city: Al Nuaimiya, Al Rashidiya and Al Jurf
schoolClusters.note: The established sector, weighted towards Indian and British curricula with large year groups at primary and a narrowing at Year 12. Tuition requests from this cluster are dominated by IGCSE maths and sciences in Years 10 and 11.

sections.heading: Who inspects a private school in Ajman, and what the report actually contains
paragraphs: Ajman's private schools are licensed and inspected by the federal Ministry of Education. There is no emirate-level authority here the way KHDA exists for Dubai, ADEK for Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, and SPEA for Sharjah. The same federal arrangement covers Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain, which between them get almost no coverage from tutoring companies at all. If you have moved from Dubai, the first thing you will notice is that the familiar annual report with its colour-coded subject grid is not where you expect to find it.

What an inspection does contain is a judgement on attainment and progress in a defined subject set, phase by phase, plus judgements on teaching, assessment, curriculum, the protection and safeguarding of students, and leadership. Those judgements use one six-band scale across the country. A school rated Good in secondary English has been judged above the minimum expected standard for that phase in that subject. That is a real finding and worth reading.

What it does not contain is anything about the set your child actually sits in. No UAE framework reports on a named Higher Level class, on which option blocks ran this year, or on how long the person teaching Mathematics AA Paper 3 has taught that syllabus. Those are the three questions that determine whether a Diploma student needs outside support, and all three are answered by the school rather than by the regulator. Ask them in writing, ask them before the option deadline, and ask again in September when staffing is settled.

This is why the honest starting point for support in Ajman is not a league table. It is a short, specific conversation with the school about staffing and sets, followed by a decision about which single subject is worth an hour a week. A parent who does that usually spends less than one who buys three subjects of general tuition on the strength of a whole-school band.

sections.heading: Reading an inspection band from Outstanding down to Very Weak
paragraphs: The six bands are Outstanding, Very Good, Good, Acceptable, Weak and Very Weak, and Acceptable is defined as the minimum standard expected of a private school in the UAE. That definition is the part most parents miss. Acceptable does not mean adequate in the casual sense; it means the school has met the floor and nothing above it. A large number of private schools nationally sit at Good or Acceptable, which means the band on its own rarely separates two schools a family is choosing between.

Read the band as a filter, not a verdict. A Weak or Very Weak judgement is a reason to read the whole report, because the weakness is usually concentrated in particular phases or departments rather than spread evenly, and the phase your child is in may not be the affected one. The reverse also holds: an Outstanding school can have a department that lost two teachers in July, and the inspection that produced the band may predate that.

The most useful lines in any report are the ones about progress rather than attainment. Attainment tells you where a cohort arrived; progress tells you what the school added. A cohort with high attainment and acceptable progress is a cohort being carried by its intake, and a student in the middle of that distribution can drift for a full year without a single report flagging it. That is the student who most often turns out to need one hour a week on one subject.
Then stop reading and start asking. The table below is how to translate each band into a question for the school office, because the question is where the useful answer lives.

sections.heading: Why a good school judgement can still leave a Diploma subject uncovered
paragraphs: Cohort size is the mechanism. A Diploma year group of forty students choosing six subjects each generates a timetable with hard constraints: subjects are grouped into option blocks, and a block runs only if enough students pick it. In a large Dubai school, Chemistry at Higher Level, Economics at Higher Level and Visual Arts can all run in parallel. In a small Ajman cohort, two of those three will share a block, and a student who wanted both is told to choose. No inspection band captures that, because the school is not doing anything wrong.

The second mechanism is staffing depth. A school with one chemist can teach Chemistry at both levels competently until that chemist leaves in July, at which point an entire Year 13 set is taught by someone meeting the syllabus for the first time. Most schools handle this well. Some handle it by asking students to self-study a Higher Level option, which is a legitimate response to a staffing gap and a very poor arrangement for a sixteen-year-old carrying three other Higher Levels.

The third is the quiet one: assessment literacy. Diploma marks are awarded against command terms and mark schemes, not against general competence. A student can understand electromagnetic induction and still score four out of eight on it, because the question said explain and the answer gave an equation. In a set of five, with a teacher covering content at speed, nobody is marking enough practice for that pattern to be noticed, let alone fixed. It is the single most common thing an IB Diploma tutor in Ajman is actually asked to repair.

None of this argues against the school. It argues for diagnosing at the level of the subject and the paper. Ask which blocks ran. Ask who teaches the Higher Level set. Ask to see a marked past-paper script. Three answers tell you more than any band.

sections.heading: What IB and IGCSE tuition costs in Ajman and the northern emirates
paragraphs: Almost nobody in this market publishes a number. Of the competitor pages reviewed for this page, three gave no price at all, and two quoted in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. So here are the AED bands as the market actually advertises them, with the source of each figure named, and with one thing stated plainly: these are market rates, not an IB Gram price list.

The spread is wide because the tiers are genuinely different products. At the bottom, a budget online tutor is frequently a university student supervising homework. In the middle sits a qualified subject teacher who has taught the paper. At the top is someone with examiner familiarity, who can tell a student what a mark scheme pays for in a question they have not seen. A family in Ajman buying at the bottom of the range for a Higher Level subject usually ends up buying twice.

Travel is the hidden variable. An in-home rate quoted locally carries the tutor's journey inside it, and an Ajman address sits outside the dense Dubai tutor belt where that journey is short. The same hour costs more here than in Jumeirah for reasons that have nothing to do with teaching. Monthly packages advertised in the market show the same pattern: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, against roughly AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits.

Bestimate's 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session land at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Use those as a planning figure for a full academic year rather than a quote. IB Gram's own arrangement is discussed on a free consultation, after a trial session, because the honest answer depends on the subject, the level and how many weeks remain before the paper.

sections.heading: One-to-one online against the in-home market, for an Ajman address
paragraphs: Home tuition is what parents in this market search for, and the question deserves a straight answer rather than a redirection. In-home tuition sold locally works like this: you pay the hourly rate plus the journey, the pool of available people is whoever will drive to your district on a weekday evening, and the earliest start is set by that person's own commute. For a family in Al Nuaimiya, that pool is workable. For a family in Masfout or Manama, it is close to empty.

IB Gram delivers tuition for UAE families as one-to-one online lessons over live video. We do not send anyone to an address in Ajman, and the in-home service we run exists only in India. The case for online here is not that it is cheaper, although it usually is once travel is stripped out. The case is the size of the pool. A Higher Level Chemistry specialist who has marked the scientific investigation does not have to live within a twenty-minute drive of Al Jurf to teach your child, and in this emirate they almost certainly do not.

There is a real trade-off, and pretending otherwise is how tutoring companies lose trust. A younger child who needs someone physically turning the page benefits from presence in a way video cannot replicate. A student who will not sit still for an hour unsupervised needs a parent in the room for the first few sessions. For Years 10 to 13, working on papers, mark schemes and coursework criteria, the screen-shared document is often the better tool, because the mark scheme, the script and the annotation are all visible to both people at once.

sections.heading: The exam calendar counted backwards from an Ajman school year
paragraphs: Not one competitor page reviewed for this set names an exam session, a registration deadline or a results date. That is a strange omission, because the calendar is the only part of this process with hard dates in it, and every useful decision about tuition is a function of how many weeks remain. The IB runs two sessions a year, May and November. Cambridge runs June and November series. Edexcel International GCSE adds a January series, which matters for schools that enter modular units.

Registration is done by the school, not by the family, through the Diploma coordinator or the exams officer. The IB's final registration point for a May session falls in the middle of the preceding November, and for a November session in the middle of the preceding May. Cambridge and Edexcel entry deadlines sit earlier than parents expect, and tier decisions, Core against Extended or Foundation against Higher, are locked at entry. A tier chosen in February caps the grade available in June, and that is the deadline most worth knowing about.

Counted backwards, a Diploma year looks like this. Twelve months out, the Extended Essay topic is agreed and Internal Assessments are being planned. Six months out, drafts exist and first marking has happened, while the final Higher Level content is still being taught. Three months out is the point at which content work should be giving way to timed papers. Six weeks out, new topics are a poor investment and paper technique is the only thing still moving a grade.

Confirm every date in the table with the school, because entry deadlines are set by the centre and results publication dates shift by a day or two between years. The shape, though, is stable, and the shape is what you plan against.

sections.heading: Internal Assessment criteria by letter, with the marks attached
paragraphs: Every page in this market says its tutors help with the Internal Assessment. Not one of the pages reviewed names a single criterion. That is the difference between marketing and teaching, because the criteria are the assessment: an exploration is not marked on how interesting it is, it is marked on five lettered criteria with a fixed mark each, and a student who has never read them is guessing at a fifth of their grade.

The Mathematics exploration, for both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, carries twenty marks: criterion A presentation, four; criterion B mathematical communication, four; criterion C personal engagement, three; criterion D reflection, three; criterion E use of mathematics, six. Criterion E is the heavyweight and the one most often lost, because it asks for mathematics commensurate with the level of the course. An IB Maths AA exploration built on content a Year 10 student could handle cannot score well on E however neatly it is written.

The sciences now assess one scientific investigation across four criteria of six marks each, twenty-four in total: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Research design is where most marks go missing, through a method that never states the range of the independent variable or how the controlled variables were held. The Theory of Knowledge essay is different again, marked as a single global impression out of ten against the prescribed title the student chose.

Read these numbers as a diagnostic tool. If a student's exploration is losing marks, the question is which letter, and the fix for each letter is different. That is a two-session conversation, not a term of general tuition.

sections.heading: Word and time limits by component, and what the limit is for
paragraphs: Limits are published, enforced and widely misread. A limit is a ceiling, not a target, and examiners stop reading at it. A Theory of Knowledge essay that runs to two thousand words is not a longer essay; it is an essay whose final four hundred words were not marked. Students who understand this write to about ninety per cent of the ceiling and spend the saved effort on structure.

The Extended Essay is four thousand words and is graded A to E alongside Theory of Knowledge, with the two together contributing up to three points to the diploma total. Those three points decide university offers more often than families expect, because an offer pitched at 36 points is lost by a student who scored 35 subject points and nothing from the core. The Extended Essay rubric most current cohorts work to awards marks across five criteria, with critical thinking carrying the largest single allocation.

Elsewhere the limits are tighter than students assume. The scientific investigation runs to three thousand words and is twenty per cent of the subject grade at both levels. Each Economics commentary is eight hundred words, three of them, worth thirty per cent at Standard Level and twenty at Higher. The Language and Literature Higher Level essay is twelve hundred to fifteen hundred words for twenty per cent of the Higher Level grade, which means a text chosen because it is short will not sustain the essay.

Check the current guide with the school's coordinator before planning around any of these, since the IB revises subject guides on a rolling cycle and a cohort two years apart can be working to different documents.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a tutor may and may not do with coursework
paragraphs: One competitor page found during research for this set sells completed Internal Assessments outright, at a published price. That is not tutoring. It is an academic-integrity breach, it is a malpractice trigger under IB rules, and the consequence lands on the student, not on the seller: a malpractice finding can cost the diploma. Any service offering to supply a finished exploration, essay or commentary should be treated as a risk to your child's qualification.

The legitimate line is clear and it is worth having in writing before a coursework session starts. A tutor teaches the criteria, explains what a mark scheme pays for, marks practice work, and gives feedback on a student's draft in the same way a school supervisor does. A tutor does not choose the topic, supply the data, draft a paragraph or restructure a submission. The student signs a declaration that the work is their own, and the supervisor records what the student did independently. Both statements have to be true.

Feedback itself is permitted and expected. The IB builds supervision into the Extended Essay through recorded reflection sessions, and schools mark Internal Assessment drafts. What is not permitted is work that is no longer the student's own after the help has been given. The practical test is whether the student could explain every choice in the document to an examiner, in their own words, without notes.
Everything in the table below applies to a tutor working through IB Gram, and it is the standard a session is run to.
