sections.heading: What an exam-term intensive costs in AED
paragraphs: Intensives are where families in this district spend most, and the figures are worth seeing as weekly patterns rather than as hourly rates. The market's published numbers, read in October 2026: Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200; TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist support; Bestimate's Dubai rate table gives AED 200 to 450 and above for specialist exam-year work and AED 180 to 350 for in-home visits; EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at the budget end.

Converted into monthly commitments, Bestimate's own estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Packages circulating in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, with travel inside the second figure.

The table puts the patterns side by side so the arithmetic is visible before February rather than after it. Two observations that save money. First, the budget band is appropriate for supervising practice and inappropriate for marking a Higher Level component, and buying it for the second job is a false economy that shows up in a mock. Second, an in-home intensive carries two journeys per session inside the rate, which from February at twice weekly is a substantial amount of somebody's time being paid for.

IB Gram publishes no rate card here. There is a free trial lesson with the tutor who would teach the course and a consultation that prices the actual plan, because the answer depends on the level, on how scarce the specialist is, and on how many weeks are left on the calendar this page is built around.

sections.heading: From Al Mowaihat: online against driving to a tuition centre
paragraphs: This page targets a home-tutor search and the honest answer has two halves. Visiting tutors work in Ajman and charge roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the rate, and for a young child or a household without a quiet room they are often the better product. IB Gram does not offer that service anywhere in the UAE; home visiting runs in India only. The more interesting comparison for Al Mowaihat, though, is not online against in-home. It is online against the thing families here actually do, which is drive to a tuition centre.

The centre option is genuinely attractive on price. A group class costs less per student hour than any one-to-one arrangement, the timetable is fixed, and the teaching is often good. What it cannot do is move the specific marks a mock script identified, because a class of eight proceeds at the group's pace on the syllabus rather than on your child's two weak question types. For broad content revision that is fine. For a targeted exam term it is the wrong instrument.

Then there is the arithmetic the price hides. Twenty to thirty minutes each way from Al Mowaihat, twice per session, out of an evening block that is three and a half hours long. At one session a week in the autumn that is tolerable. From February at twice weekly it is two hours a week in a car, taken from the hours in which independent practice has to happen, and independent practice is what actually converts teaching into marks.

The table applies what we have called the February test to each row: does this arrangement still work when the pattern doubles? That is the question worth asking in October, because by February the pattern has doubled and changing it is another disruption in the worst possible month.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when a deadline and a holiday collide
paragraphs: Calendar pressure is what pushes coursework across the academic-honesty line, and the collisions are predictable. An internal deadline a few days after a holiday. A Theory of Knowledge essay due in the same fortnight as two subject mocks. An Extended Essay draft expected in a week when the family is travelling. Nobody plans to break a rule; a week disappears and somebody helpful fills the gap.

The rule itself does not move with the calendar. Submitted work must be the student's own, a school supervisor must see drafts, and the submission is authenticated. What a tutor, a parent or an older sibling may legitimately do is teach the content, read the criteria aloud and explain what each one rewards with the marks named, press on whether a question is answerable with available evidence, and give feedback on work the student has already written. What none of them may do is supply sentences, reorganise a draft on the student's behalf, provide a dataset, or return a document with new material in it.

The protection is scheduling rather than willpower. Put the coursework decisions in DP1 and the drafting before the holiday rather than after it, and keep the reflections in a weekly five-minute habit rather than a DP2 weekend. A student who has a draft three weeks early does not need rescuing, and a family that has planned the collisions does not meet them.

Two market notes for a family buying support in an exam term. There are providers selling completed Internal Assessments to UAE families at fixed prices, and buying one is malpractice under IB rules with the consequence falling on the student. And board materials - syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes - belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, so they are cited and linked rather than distributed in bundles.

process.title: Send the entry letter and the mock script
process.description: Two documents answer most questions. The exam-entry letter gives the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the series. The most recent marked script gives the question types that lose marks. Together they produce a plan in one session rather than in three weeks of getting to know the student.

process.title: Free trial at the slot the calendar allows
process.description: For an eastern-route household that is about 5.30pm, for a Sharjah-route household about 6pm, and for a DP2 student often a Saturday. The trial runs with the tutor who would take the course, at that hour, because a slot that works only in theory fails in week five.

process.title: Build the year's calendar in week one
process.description: Entry deadline, zone-specific timetable, coursework internal dates, mock windows and the series itself, taken from the exams officer and the boards' own pages. The weekly plan is then derived from that calendar rather than from whatever feels urgent in a given week.

process.title: Review three weeks after each mock
process.description: The review point is set by the calendar rather than by a billing cycle. Three weeks after a script comes back, a second timed component shows whether the two targeted losses moved. If they did not, the subject, the tutor or the approach changes, and that decision is yours with the evidence in front of you.

whyPoints.title: The year written down before the hours are sold
whyPoints.description: Entry deadlines, mock windows, Ramadan, the series and the summer block, with what each window is already too late for. Most of the money wasted on tutoring in this district is wasted on timing rather than on teaching, and a calendar is cheap.

whyPoints.title: Mock scripts read for question types
whyPoints.description: A grade is a verdict and a script is a plan. We ask for the script with the mark scheme, list the losses by question type with marks attached, and work only on the two heaviest for three weeks. Then a second component checks it.

whyPoints.title: Session shapes set by the student
whyPoints.description: Half-hours for primary, four-session blocks in the middle years, ninety minutes fortnightly in DP2 so a component and its correction both happen. The familiar weekly hour is a billing convention, not a pedagogical one, and it is wrong at both ends.

whyPoints.title: The driving cost made explicit
whyPoints.description: A tuition centre is cheaper per hour and costs twenty to thirty minutes each way from Al Mowaihat, which from February at twice weekly is two hours a week taken out of the block where independent practice has to happen.

whyPoints.title: Board dates from the boards, and no IB dates at all
whyPoints.description: Cambridge's and Pearson's published key dates are quoted with the board named. No IB session or results date appears here, because the IB's own site could not be read for this project and a guessed date is worse than an absent one.

faqs.question: Do tutors travel to homes in Al Mowaihat, Ajman?
faqs.answer: Some local providers do, at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the rate. IB Gram does not: lessons for Al Mowaihat families run one-to-one over live video, and home visiting is a service we offer in India only. The district-specific reason is the evening block. A bus back at 4.15pm and a usable window to about 9pm leaves three and a half hours for homework, coursework and tuition, and an arrangement that adds somebody's drive at both ends takes more of it than the lesson does.

faqs.question: When is the right month to start tutoring for a June series?
faqs.answer: October, if the issue is content, and February if the issue is technique. Those are different problems with different windows. Content taught in October can still be practised and consolidated before the papers; content taught in April is not retained well enough to be worth the hours. Technique work - pacing, question types, extended answers - responds quickly and is best done against marked components from February. The one month to avoid starting from scratch in is the last six weeks, when the only sensible activity is timed practice and correction.

faqs.question: What should we actually do with my daughter's mock script?
faqs.answer: Get it back from the school with the mark scheme, which they will usually provide if asked, and read it for question types rather than topics. List every loss with the marks attached. You will typically find two recurring question types account for most of it, which is a structural problem rather than five knowledge gaps. Then work those two twice a week for three weeks and sit a second timed component to check. After about three weeks the script stops being useful, because the term has moved and the specifics have faded.

faqs.question: Can we still change my son's entry tier in February?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not for a series the centre has already entered him for. Tiers are fixed at entry, and entries close months before the papers: for the June series Cambridge's final entry date falls in the spring, and it is the centre that holds it. The practical conclusion is that the tier conversation belongs in the autumn term, supported by a timed paper at the higher tier marked against the published scheme, so the evidence exists before the entry is drafted. If a Core entry for June is already filed, the realistic plan is a secure Core grade in June and, if a higher grade is genuinely needed, an Extended entry in the November series. Ask the school in writing which tier your son is entered for, and ask in the autumn.

faqs.question: How do we plan revision around Ramadan in an Ajman school year?
faqs.answer: Rewrite the timetable for those weeks rather than suspending it. Shorter sessions more often - thirty to forty minutes three times a week instead of ninety minutes once - because concentration while fasting is a real constraint. Move the heavier analytical work to whatever part of the day your household actually has energy in. Treat Eid as a holiday and agree the post-Eid plan before it starts, since the gap to a May or June series is short. The shortened school day is also the one period when an afternoon slot genuinely works here.

faqs.question: Are Friday and Saturday sessions better for an Al Mowaihat family?
faqs.answer: For some kinds of work, clearly yes. The weekend is when a working parent is reliably present and unhurried, which makes it right for anything that needs a decision rather than practice: choosing an Extended Essay question, reviewing a mock script together, agreeing whether to argue a tier. It is also the only window long enough for a full timed component. Keep the weekday evenings for drilling, retrieval sets and short feedback, and split a component and its correction across a Saturday and the following Tuesday.

faqs.question: Why would a ninety-minute fortnightly slot beat a weekly hour in DP2?
faqs.answer: Because a full component and the conversation that makes it useful do not fit in an hour. A weekly sixty-minute slot in DP2 usually holds the sitting or the correction and postpones the other, and the postponed half is the one where marks move. Ninety minutes every fortnight per subject holds both, and two subjects then fill alternate weeks without taking more from the evening block than a weekly pattern would. For a commuting student that arithmetic matters more than the total number of hours bought.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre on the Emirates Road belt cheaper than online tutoring?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes, because the rate is shared across the group. Per mark moved, often not. A class of eight follows the syllabus at the group's pace, which cannot chase the two question types a mock script identified for your child. Add twenty to thirty minutes each way from Al Mowaihat, twice per session, out of a three-and-a-half-hour evening block, and from February at twice weekly that is two hours a week in a car taken from the time independent practice needs. Try the school's own support sessions first; they are already paid for.

faqs.question: How much does an exam-term intensive cost per month in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Using the market's own published figures read in October 2026: Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Packages in this market include about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions with travel inside the figure. Hourly, specialist support runs AED 200 to 450 and above. IB Gram prices after a free trial and a consultation.

faqs.question: Which direction does the school bus go, and does it change the slot?
faqs.answer: It changes it by about half an hour, which is enough to matter. Al Mowaihat households send children east to the Emirates Road belt, south into central Ajman, and across to Muwaileh or University City in Sharjah. Eastern routes return around 4.15pm, so 5.30pm works once food and a decompression gap are allowed for. Sharjah routes return after 4.45pm, which puts the earliest workable slot at about 6pm. Book against the actual return time rather than a nominal school finish, and add the twenty minutes.

faqs.question: Does my child need tutoring in the summer holidays?
faqs.answer: If there is a content gap heading into the next year, the summer is the cheapest and most effective time to close it, and that is the strongest case for holiday work. Six to ten weeks of targeted teaching before a course needs the content costs less and achieves more than the same material taught in November against a moving syllabus. What is not worth buying is general revision over the summer with no specific gap identified, which consumes a holiday and produces very little that survives to September.

faqs.question: What are the November and June series results dates, and does it matter which we sit?
faqs.answer: It matters if a grade is needed for an application. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge follows the same rhythm from its own two series: a June entry produces a grade in the summer, and a November entry produces one in the new year. A November grade therefore lands after several application deadlines, which is the real cost of treating November as a free second attempt. The series is chosen at entry, months before revision begins, which is why it belongs on the autumn calendar rather than the exam-season one.

faqs.question: Where should an Al Mowaihat family get the IB session dates from?
faqs.answer: Because we could not read them from the IB itself for this project, and a date taken from a secondary source and published on a tutoring page is exactly how incorrect dates spread. Cambridge and Pearson both publish their own key dates, so those appear here with the board named. For IB sessions, ask the school's diploma coordinator or read ibo.org directly, then build the family calendar around that. Treat any provider quoting IB dates without naming its source as a provider that guessed.

faqs.question: A coursework deadline falls the week after our holiday. What do we do now?
faqs.answer: Move the work, not the rule. Submitted work must be the student's own, a supervisor must see drafts, and the submission is authenticated, and none of that relaxes because a week disappeared. The fix is scheduling: get a draft written before the holiday rather than after it, and book the feedback session for the week you return. Legitimate help is explaining criteria, questioning the research question, and giving feedback on what the student has already written. It is not supplying sentences or reorganising the draft on their behalf.

ajman/al-mowaihat.closingBody: The cheapest thing an Al Mowaihat family can do this term is build one calendar: the entry deadline, the zone timetable, the coursework internal dates, the mock windows, the Ramadan weeks and the series. Then ask for the last marked script with its mark scheme. Those two pieces of paper decide what to buy, in what shape and in which month, and they usually show that less is needed than feared but sooner. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, in slots built around the bus rather than against it.

Each one teaches a named syllabus, not a subject in general.

intro.heading: Al Nuaimiya is an apartment district, and that changes what tutoring has to solve
paragraphs: Al Nuaimiya is one of the oldest and densest residential districts in Ajman: mid-rise towers and walk-up blocks along Sheikh Khalifa Bin Zayed Street, with Ajman City Centre and the hospital at the centre of daily life. Almost nobody here lives in a villa. The typical household is a flat with two or three bedrooms holding four to six people, often with one parent driving to Sharjah or Dubai before seven in the morning and returning after seven at night. That single fact shapes every tutoring decision a family here makes, and it is the thing nobody writing about tutoring in Ajman ever mentions.

The children in those flats are spread across more curricula than the district's size suggests. Indian-curriculum schools inside Ajman take the largest share, and a steady number of those students move onto Cambridge International GCSE in Year 9 or Year 10 because the parents want a qualification a UK or Canadian university reads without translation. A smaller group travels to Ajman Academy on the Emirates Road belt for the IB Middle Years Programme, and the Diploma students almost all commute to Sharjah or Dubai. Three different assessment systems, three different vocabularies, and one shared kitchen table.

The academic pressure points cluster tightly. In the primary and lower secondary years it is English: a child who reads comfortably in one language and is assessed in another loses marks in Science and Humanities long before anyone calls it a language problem. In Years 9 and 10 it is the subject-option decision, and specifically whether a school has entered a child for Core or Extended papers, because Core caps the grade at C and most families discover this after the entry is made. In Years 12 and 13 it is Higher Level content taught to a class of six by a teacher who also teaches three other year groups.

The second pressure point is physical. A one-to-one lesson needs a door that closes, a table, and a connection that holds a video call for an hour. In an Al Nuaimiya flat with three children and two working parents, none of those three things is automatic, and a tutor who ignores the room will spend half the hour competing with a television. Working that out in advance is part of the setup, not an afterthought, and it is one of the few variables a family can fix in a single afternoon.

IB Gram does not send a tutor to an Al Nuaimiya address. Home visits are a service offered only in India; everything delivered to UAE families is one-to-one over live video. That is a deliberate position rather than a limitation. A district of this size cannot support a resident Chemistry Higher Level specialist, an Arabic first-language teacher and a Pearson Edexcel Further Maths examiner all within a fifteen-minute drive. Over video, the pool stops being geographic and the match is made on syllabus rather than postcode.

ajman/al-nuaimiya.programmesIntro: Three programme families account for nearly every Al Nuaimiya enquiry. The notes below describe what each one assesses and what it means for a household in this district specifically, rather than in general terms.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years of linear courses ending in written papers, usually eight or nine subjects. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel does not tier in the same way but offers modular entry in some subjects. Grades are reported 9-1 or A*-G depending on the subject and board. The written papers carry almost all of the marks, with practical science assessed through an alternative-to-practical paper in most UAE centres.
programmes.countryNote: This is the dominant route for Al Nuaimiya families moving out of an Indian-curriculum school. The transfer usually happens at the end of Year 9, which leaves one year to close a gap in written-answer technique that the previous curriculum never asked for. Ajman's private schools sit under federal Ministry of Education supervision, and the exam entry itself is made by the school as a Cambridge or Pearson centre.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years across eight subject groups, assessed against four criteria per subject lettered A to D, each marked out of eight. Criterion scores are summed and converted to a 1-7 grade using published boundaries, which is why a student can feel strong in a subject and still see a 4 reported. MYP 5 ends with the Personal Project, a self-directed piece assessed on process rather than product.
programmes.countryNote: Al Nuaimiya MYP students almost all travel to Ajman Academy or across the border into Sharjah, which puts them home late. The common request here is criterion-specific: a child losing marks on Criterion D in Sciences is being marked on reflection and evaluation, not on content, and no amount of extra content revision moves that number.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internally assessed component worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of the grade. The written examinations are sat in a single session at the end of the second year, so the internal components are the only marks banked before then.
programmes.countryNote: There is no IB Diploma campus inside Al Nuaimiya itself. Students here commute to Sharjah or Dubai, and a 90-minute round trip is normal. That makes the internally assessed components the pressure point: they fall due in the same weeks as mock examinations, and a student on a long commute has fewer free evenings to absorb a bad draft.

ajman/al-nuaimiya.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Al Nuaimiya households ask for most often, with a note on what each one actually assesses and where the marks tend to go missing. Boards and levels are confirmed against the school's entry before a tutor is matched.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Extended and Higher tier papers reward method marks on multi-step questions. Most lost marks here are not conceptual: they are unshown working, premature rounding, and answers given without units. A Core entry caps the grade, so the tier a school has entered a child for is the first thing to check.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and waves account for a disproportionate share of lost marks, usually because circuit reasoning is memorised rather than derived. The alternative-to-practical paper asks students to describe a method and identify a control variable, which is a writing skill as much as a Physics one.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations and organic reaction pathways separate grades at the top. Students who can define a term and still cannot explain a trend are being caught by command words: 'state' and 'explain' carry different mark allocations and different expectations.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The content volume is the problem rather than the difficulty. Transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance reward precise terminology, and a vague answer in biology loses marks that a vague answer in maths would not.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language and First Language English
subjects.description: Two different qualifications that Al Nuaimiya families often confuse. First Language English assesses directed writing and reading comprehension on unseen texts; English as a Second Language assesses functional accuracy. The wrong entry costs a grade and is hard to change after the deadline.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language
subjects.description: Taught to Arab students as a full language and literature subject with its own grammar and comprehension demands. KHDA's published guidance requires Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for this stream, and Ajman schools follow the same federal subject requirement.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: A separate subject with separate expectations, compulsory for non-Arab students in UAE private schools. The usual request from Al Nuaimiya parents is a tutor who can get a child to a pass without the child falling behind in the subjects that carry their university offer.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches / Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Analysis and Approaches is the algebra and calculus route; Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics with a graphical calculator throughout. Engineering and most physics degrees expect Analysis and Approaches, and switching after the first term of Year 12 is painful.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The Higher Level extension topics in organic chemistry and energetics carry the grade. The scientific investigation is assessed against published criteria, and a strong student with a weak method section loses more marks there than in any single examination topic.

subjects.name: Business Management and Economics
subjects.levels: IB DP HL and SL, IGCSE
subjects.description: Both reward application to a named context rather than definition recall. Al Nuaimiya students frequently write accurate theory with no reference to the case material, which is the single most common reason a competent answer sits at a 4.

sections.heading: What an Al Nuaimiya search for a tutor is actually asking
paragraphs: A parent typing a search for IB and IGCSE tutors in Al Nuaimiya is usually asking three questions at once, and only one of them is about teaching. The first is whether anyone qualified in the right subject is reachable from this district at all. The second is what it costs. The third, rarely typed but always present, is whether a lesson can physically happen in the evening in a flat where other people are also living. A page that answers only the first question has answered the easy part.

On reachability, the honest answer is that Al Nuaimiya has good access to general tuition and poor access to specialists. There are tuition centres and freelance tutors within a short drive who will teach IGCSE Maths or Science competently at a general level. What there is not, within any sensible travel distance, is a resident teacher for IB Chemistry at Higher Level, for Pearson Edexcel Further Pure Mathematics, or for Arabic as a first language taught to literature standard. Those people exist; they are not in Ajman.

That gap is the whole argument for one-to-one over live video. The lesson arrives in the flat without anyone driving, and the tutor is selected from a pool that is not limited to a twenty-minute radius. It is a trade: a family gives up a person physically in the room and gets a specialist in the actual syllabus the child sits. For a Year 7 struggling with reading, the trade is arguable. For a Year 13 on three Higher Levels, it is not close.

Everything below is built for this district in particular. The timings assume an Ajman school run and a commute to Sharjah or Dubai. The costs are quoted in dirhams and attributed to whoever published them. The subject detail names syllabus codes, because 'Maths tutor' and '0580 Extended tier' are not the same request.

sections.heading: Who lives in Al Nuaimiya, household by household
paragraphs: Five household shapes account for most enquiries from this district, and each one needs a different answer about timing rather than about teaching. The pattern matters because the single most common reason tutoring fails here is not a bad match: it is a slot nobody can actually keep. A lesson booked at 16:00 because that is when the tutor was free will be missed three times in a month, and the family will conclude that tutoring does not work.

The two-income flat with both parents commuting out of the emirate is the most common. Nobody is home before 18:30, the children arrive back from school around 15:30 and are unsupervised until then, and a lesson placed in that window happens with a sibling watching television in the next room. These households do better with a 19:30 start and a shorter, sharper session than with a longer afternoon one.

The single-income household with three or four children is the second shape, and the question there is almost always which child to prioritise. The honest answer is the one whose next examination is closest, which usually means the eldest. The third shape is the Emirati household running the Ministry of Education curriculum at school and buying IGCSE Maths and Science privately, where two separate tutors on two separate nights is the normal arrangement rather than one tutor covering both. The fourth shape is the household with a single Diploma candidate commuting out of the emirate, and the fifth is the teacher household, where the parent knows exactly what good teaching looks like and specifically wants someone with no connection to their own school.

sections.heading: Studying in an Al Nuaimiya flat: the room, the noise and the line
paragraphs: A one-to-one video lesson needs three physical things, and in a dense apartment district none of them can be assumed. It needs a surface the student can write on with the screen at eye level. It needs forty-five minutes during which nobody else needs that space. And it needs a connection that holds a two-way video call without the tutor losing the student mid-explanation. Sorting this out before the first lesson is worth more than any amount of discussion about teaching method.

The commonest setup failure is the laptop balanced on a bed. A student lying down cannot write, and a tutor who cannot see the working cannot diagnose the error. The second commonest is a shared living room with a television on. The third is a phone used as the lesson device, which works for talking and fails completely the moment a diagram or a past paper needs to be on screen alongside the tutor.

None of this requires spending money. A folding table in a bedroom, a pair of cheap wired headphones, and a household rule that the door stays closed for the hour will solve most of it. The connection question is worth testing once: run a video call at the time of day the lesson will happen, not at ten in the morning when the towers are empty. Evening contention in older blocks is real, and it is better discovered in a test than in a lesson about mole calculations.

sections.heading: The cross-emirate school run, and why a 16:00 lesson rarely survives it
paragraphs: Al Nuaimiya sits roughly twenty-five minutes from Sharjah's university corridor and about forty-five from the Dubai border in afternoon traffic, and both figures stretch in term time. For a family whose child attends a campus on the Emirates Road belt or over the Sharjah line, the useful number is not the distance but the time the child is genuinely available with a book open. That is usually at least ninety minutes after the school bell, and in the worst corridors closer to two hours.

This is why booking the first slot a tutor offers is a mistake. An afternoon lesson at 16:00 looks convenient on a calendar and collides with the moment the bus arrives, the uniform comes off and the kitchen is busiest. By 18:00 the household has settled, and by 19:30 both parents are usually home, which matters because a thirteen-year-old left to join a lesson unsupervised frequently does not.

The counter-argument is tiredness, and it is a fair one. A student who starts at 20:00 after a long commute will not do their best thinking. The compromise most Al Nuaimiya families reach is two shorter evening sessions rather than one long one, plus a Saturday morning slot for the subject that needs the most sustained work. Saturday at ten in the morning is consistently the most productive hour available to a commuting household in this emirate, and families who put their heaviest subject there tend to keep the slot through the whole year rather than quietly abandoning it in week six. The other useful habit is to protect exam-leave and study days, which for a commuting student are the only weekday mornings available all year.

sections.heading: English as an additional language inside an English-medium programme
paragraphs: A large share of Al Nuaimiya students are assessed in a language that is not the one spoken at home. In the primary years this shows up as a reading-speed problem. By Year 9 it shows up somewhere less obvious: in Science and Humanities marks, where the content is understood and the answer does not earn the mark because it is imprecise, unstructured, or uses an everyday word where the syllabus wants a technical one.

The diagnostic is simple and most parents can run it themselves. Take a marked paper and separate the lost marks into two piles: answers that were wrong, and answers that were roughly right but did not say the thing the mark scheme wanted. If the second pile is larger, the problem is expression rather than content, and more Science revision will not move the grade. What moves it is practice in writing to a command term, which is a language exercise conducted inside the subject.

This also matters for the entry decision. Cambridge offers both First Language English and English as a Second Language, and they are different qualifications with different ceilings and different value to a university admissions office. Some Al Nuaimiya families find out which one their child was entered for only when the statement of entry arrives. It is worth asking the school directly, in Year 9, and it is worth asking what evidence the decision was based on. A child capable of First Language English who was placed in the second-language route because of a home-language form will carry that ceiling into a university application three years later.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside an international timetable
paragraphs: Every private school in the UAE teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies alongside whichever international curriculum it is licensed to deliver. The federal rule is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must follow the Ministry's general regulations. Ajman's private schools sit under the Ministry of Education directly, rather than under an emirate-level authority as Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah do.

The most detailed public account of how these subjects are organised is KHDA's mandatory-subjects guidance for Dubai schools, and it is useful reading for an Ajman parent even though Ajman is not KHDA territory. It sets out that schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and that combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. It also states that instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes.

For a family in this district the practical consequence is that these are real subjects with real marks, not a formality to be absorbed. A non-Arab child doing Arabic as an additional language needs that subject taught as a language, with vocabulary and grammar built deliberately. An Arab child doing Arabic as a first language is sitting a literature-standard course in Standard Arabic. Treating both as the same request is the mistake, and it is the reason a family sometimes books three terms of the wrong lessons.

sections.heading: What one-to-one support costs an Al Nuaimiya family, in dirhams
paragraphs: Most tutoring pages in this market publish no price at all, and the few that do quote in dollars. The table below sets out the dirham bands that providers in the UAE market actually publish, with the provider named, so that a parent in Al Nuaimiya can judge a quote against something. These are market rates read in October 2026, not IB Gram's rates; our own figure comes with the consultation and the free trial lesson, which carries no card requirement and no obligation to continue.

Three things move the number more than anything else. Level is the first: Diploma Higher Level and Pearson Edexcel International A Level work commands more than lower secondary, because the pool of people who can teach it is smaller. Format is the second, and the in-home premium is largely the tutor's travel time being paid for. Scarcity is the third, and it is the one Ajman families feel most: a common subject at a common level has many available teachers, and a rare Higher Level subject has few at any price.

Published monthly packages give a second reference point. Online packages around AED 799 a month for eight sessions appear in this market, and in-home monthly packages of roughly AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Bestimate's 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session land at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support.

sections.heading: Who may legally teach your child in Ajman, and how a parent checks
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. The official route is MoHRE's own service, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, with a two-working-day completion time stated on the service page.

The eligible categories are wider than most parents expect. They include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. That last category explains a great deal of the informal tutoring market in a district like Al Nuaimiya, where an older sibling's friend teaching mathematics for pocket money is common. It can be entirely legitimate, and the permit is the thing that makes it so.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts has been published, so any figure quoted to you as the fine is not something either you or the person quoting it can verify. The other rule worth knowing is a conduct one: the permit's code of conduct, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules in Abu Dhabi, bar a teacher from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Asking a child's own class teacher for evening lessons puts that teacher at risk, and IB Gram will not match a student to a tutor at their own school.

sections.heading: Where feedback stops and authorship begins
paragraphs: Every IB internally assessed component, and every piece of IGCSE coursework, carries the same condition: the work submitted must be the student's own. The IB requires the supervisor to authenticate it. Breaching that is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on whoever helped. In a market where at least one visible operator sells finished Internal Assessments outright, a parent is owed a clear statement of where the line sits.

A tutor may legitimately do a great deal. They can teach the published assessment criteria and what each one rewards. They can discuss whether a research question is answerable in the word count. They can read a draft and say that the method section does not let a reader repeat the experiment, or that the evaluation identifies a limitation without explaining its effect on the result. They can teach referencing, and they can work through the analysis the student has already carried out.

What a tutor must never be is the author. Not a paragraph, not a rewritten conclusion, not a reworded research question typed by someone else. The practical test we use is simple: after a session, every sentence in the document should still be one the student typed. Feedback in the margin, discussion on a call, and teaching on the criteria all pass that test. Anything that puts a tutor's words into the submitted file does not, and we decline that work when it is asked for.

sections.heading: Starting from Al Nuaimiya, and what we say when nobody covers the subject
paragraphs: The first conversation is a diagnostic rather than a sales call. We ask which school, which board, which syllabus code, and which tier or level the student is entered for, and we ask for a recent marked paper or report if there is one. Those four facts decide the match. A request for 'a maths tutor in Ajman' cannot be matched well; a request for Cambridge 0580 Extended tier, Year 10, losing marks on multi-step algebra, can be matched in a day or two.

Then there is a free trial lesson. The condition attached is worth stating plainly: it is one lesson, in the subject you asked for, with the tutor you would continue with, and it requires no card details and no commitment afterwards. If the match is wrong, say so and we change it rather than persuading you. Most mismatches are visible inside one lesson, and almost all of them are about manner rather than knowledge.

Sometimes the honest answer is that no specialist is free. This happens most with rare Higher Level combinations and with Arabic first-language work at literature standard, and it happens more in the weeks before a session than at the start of a term. When it does, we say so, give an expected date, and suggest what the student should do in the meantime rather than placing them with a tutor who teaches the subject but not the level. A family in Al Nuaimiya has usually already been promised availability that did not exist; we would rather be the ones who did not.

process.title: Tell us the four facts that matter
process.description: School, board, syllabus code and tier or level. If you have a recent marked paper or school report, send it. Those four facts plus one piece of evidence are what lets us match a subject specialist rather than a generalist, and they take two minutes to supply.

process.title: We match on syllabus, not on postcode
process.description: Because lessons are delivered over live video, the shortlist is not limited to tutors who could drive to Al Nuaimiya. We name the tutor, their subject and the level they teach, and we confirm they have no connection to your child's school before anything is booked.

process.title: Take the trial lesson
process.description: One full lesson in the subject you asked about, with the tutor you would continue with. No card details, no obligation. At the end you get a short written note on what the tutor found, which is useful even if you decide not to continue.

process.title: Fix a slot that survives the school run
process.description: We book around the Ajman school run and a Sharjah or Dubai commute rather than around tutor convenience. For most households in this district that means an 18:30 or 19:30 start and a Saturday morning for the heaviest subject.

process.title: Review against marks, not impressions
process.description: Every four to six weeks we look at what has actually changed on marked work. If the pattern of lost marks has not moved, we change the approach or the tutor rather than adding hours.

whyPoints.title: A specialist instead of a neighbour
whyPoints.description: Al Nuaimiya has competent general tutors within a short drive and no resident Higher Level Chemistry teacher. Online delivery lets a family here pick from the second group, which is the entire point of giving up a person in the room.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes confirmed first
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers with different structures, and Core and Extended have different grade ceilings. We check the entry details against the school's own paperwork before a tutor is matched.

whyPoints.title: Timings built for a commuting household
whyPoints.description: Slots are offered from 18:00 to 21:00 Gulf Standard Time and on Saturday mornings, because a 16:00 lesson in this district is a lesson that gets missed. The slot is held for the term unless you move it.

whyPoints.title: Prices quoted against published market bands
whyPoints.description: Every dirham figure on this page is attributed to the provider that published it and dated. You can judge any quote, ours included, against something rather than against a feeling.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: We teach the criteria, read drafts and give feedback. We are never the author of an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or a piece of coursework, and we decline that request when it is made.

whyPoints.title: No tutor from your child's own school
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE permit's code of conduct and ADEK's ethics rules both bar a teacher from paid tutoring of students at their own school. We check for that connection rather than leaving the family to discover it.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to an Al Nuaimiya apartment?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Everything delivered to Al Nuaimiya families is one-to-one over live video, with the student and tutor on camera and shared material on screen. The trade is deliberate: instead of choosing from the teachers who happen to live within a twenty-minute drive of Ajman, you choose from a pool selected on the syllabus your child actually sits. For a Year 13 taking three Higher Levels, that difference is larger than the difference between a screen and a chair.

faqs.question: My three children share one bedroom in Al Nuaimiya. Where should the lesson happen?
faqs.answer: Wherever there is a door and a table for the hour, which in most flats here means a bedroom at a time the other children are out, or a cleared kitchen table once dinner is finished. What matters is a writing surface and a screen at eye level, because a tutor who cannot see the working cannot diagnose the error. Wired headphones solve most of the noise problem cheaply. If the only possible hour is one when the flat is busy, say so when booking and we will place the slot where the household is quietest rather than where the tutor is free.

faqs.question: Which schools do most Al Nuaimiya children actually attend?
faqs.answer: The nearest campuses are Indian-curriculum and British-curriculum schools within a short drive of Sheikh Khalifa Bin Zayed Street, including GEMS Our Own English High School Ajman, Ibn Seena English High School, Habitat School Ajman, Ajman Modern School, Al Ameer English School and Scholars Indian School. Families who want an IB programme usually travel inland to Ajman Academy or across the border to Sharjah campuses such as Victoria International School of Sharjah. Diploma students most often commute out of the emirate entirely. We support students from all of these; none of them is affiliated with IB Gram in any way.

faqs.question: What internet speed does a live lesson need in an older Al Nuaimiya tower?
faqs.answer: A stable connection matters more than a fast one. A two-way video call with a shared screen will run comfortably on a few megabits each way, and the usual problem in older blocks is not headline speed but evening contention when every flat is online at once. Test it at the hour the lesson will actually happen rather than in the morning. If the connection drops repeatedly, moving the slot by an hour fixes it more often than changing provider does, and a wired connection to the router beats wireless from a far bedroom.

faqs.question: My son's English is holding back his Science marks. Is that a Science problem or a language one?
faqs.answer: You can test this yourself on a marked paper. Separate the lost marks into answers that were factually wrong and answers that were roughly right but did not say what the mark scheme wanted. If the second pile is bigger, it is expression rather than content, and more Science revision will not move the grade. What moves it is practising answers against command terms, so that 'state', 'describe' and 'explain' produce visibly different responses. That work happens inside the Science lesson rather than in a separate English one, which is why we match the subject tutor rather than adding a language tutor.

faqs.question: Does my daughter still take Arabic if she sits Cambridge IGCSEs in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are required in UAE private schools alongside whichever international curriculum the school is licensed to deliver, and Ajman's private schools sit under federal Ministry of Education supervision. Arabic as a first language and Arabic as an additional language are separate subjects with separate expectations, and KHDA's published guidance for Dubai requires schools to teach the two groups in separate classes. For a non-Arab student the subject should be taught as a second language, built from vocabulary and structure rather than treated as a lighter version of the first-language course.

faqs.question: Who inspects private schools in Ajman, and where are the reports published?
faqs.answer: Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than by an emirate-level regulator. Dubai has KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have ADEK, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge. That matters when comparing schools, because the published inspection formats and the amount of detail released differ between authorities. Check the Ministry's own channels for an Ajman school rather than assuming a KHDA-style rating exists for it, and ask the school directly for its most recent report.

faqs.question: What does an hour of one-to-one tuition cost around Al Nuaimiya in 2026?
faqs.answer: Published UAE market rates read in October 2026 run from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tuition, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit including the tutor's travel, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialist. Those are other providers' published figures, named and dated, not ours. Level and scarcity move the number most: a common subject at Year 9 sits near the bottom of those bands, and a rare Higher Level subject sits near the top.

faqs.question: Both of us commute to Dubai. What is the latest a lesson can start?
faqs.answer: Slots run to 21:00 Gulf Standard Time, and 19:30 is the most-booked start for commuting households in this district. Later than 20:00 the return on a session drops because the student is tired, so two shorter evening lessons usually beat one long late one. Saturday at 10:00 is the single most productive hour available to an Ajman household with parents working out of the emirate, and families who put their heaviest subject there tend to keep the slot. Tell us the real constraint and we will build around it rather than offering whatever is free.

faqs.question: Can two of my children take the same session to split the cost?
faqs.answer: Yes, when they are genuinely on the same work: same board, same tier, same examination series, and a small gap in attainment. Two children both sitting Cambridge 0580 Extended in the same year can share a slot productively. One on Core and one on Extended cannot, because the papers differ and one of them will spend the hour watching. Both students need their own paper and their own camera. If the gap widens mid-term, we split them back into separate slots rather than letting the weaker one coast.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre near Ajman City Centre cheaper than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Per hour, usually yes, because the cost is divided across a group. What you give up is specificity: a centre teaches to the middle of the room and to a general syllabus rather than to the exact paper your child is entered for, and the questions your child personally gets wrong may never come up. A centre with premises and staff also needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit in Dubai, and comparable approvals elsewhere, which is worth asking about. Group teaching suits content coverage; one-to-one suits a specific diagnosed pattern of lost marks.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with an Al Nuaimiya family need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered schoolteachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no schedule of amounts has been published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted with scepticism. Applications go through MoHRE's own smart app, website or e-services system.

faqs.question: How much feedback can a tutor give on my daughter's Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: A great deal, as long as the tutor never becomes the author. A tutor can teach the published assessment criteria, discuss whether a research question is answerable in the word count, read a draft and say that the method cannot be repeated by a reader, point out that an evaluation names a limitation without explaining its effect, and teach referencing. What must not happen is a tutor's sentences appearing in the submitted file. The IB requires the supervisor to authenticate the work as the student's own, and the consequence of a breach falls on the student.

faqs.question: We are moving from CBSE into Year 10 IGCSE. How far behind will my son be?
faqs.answer: Rarely behind on content, often behind on answer technique. CBSE students arriving in a Cambridge or Pearson Year 10 usually know the mathematics and the science, and lose marks because the papers reward shown method, precise terminology and answers written to a command term rather than a correct final figure. Six to ten weeks of focused work on past-paper technique closes most of that gap. The thing to settle first is the tier: ask the school whether he has been entered for Core or Extended, because Core caps the grade and changing it later is difficult.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor covers my child's Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: We tell you, give an expected date, and suggest what the student should do in the meantime. This happens most often with rare Higher Level combinations and with Arabic first-language work at literature standard, and most often in the weeks just before an examination session when specialists are already committed. The alternative, which some providers take, is to place a student with someone who teaches the subject but not the level. That costs a term and usually ends with the family concluding tutoring does not work, so we would rather state the gap.

ajman/al-nuaimiya.closingHeading: Start with one marked paper and one honest conversation
ajman/al-nuaimiya.closingBody: If your child is in a flat in Al Nuaimiya losing marks in a pattern you can see but cannot name, the useful first step is not booking hours. It is sending one recent marked paper and telling us the school, the board and the tier. We will tell you what the pattern looks like, which subject specialist fits it, and what an evening slot would realistically look like around your commute. Then there is one free trial lesson, with no card required and no obligation to continue, and a short written note afterwards that is worth having either way.

intro.heading: Al Rashidiya is where a child's school file usually has two curricula in it
paragraphs: Al Rashidiya is one of Ajman's older residential districts, and the housing tells you who lives there. Low-rise apartment blocks along Sheikh Humaid Bin Rashid Al Nuaimi Street sit a few streets from older villa compounds, and the two household types send their children in different directions. Apartment families tend to start in an Indian-curriculum primary close to home, because the fee is affordable and the bus route is short. Villa families more often start British and stay British. By Year 10 both groups end up in the same examination hall sitting Cambridge or Pearson International GCSE papers, and that is where the trouble shows up.

A switch of curriculum mid-school is not a transfer of marks. A child who has spent six years on an Indian-curriculum syllabus has been taught to reproduce a method accurately and at speed. An IGCSE paper asks for the method and then asks what the answer means, in a command-term vocabulary nobody has taught them: describe, explain, suggest, evaluate. The content gap is usually small and closes in a term. The command-term gap is what costs grades, and it is invisible on a report card that still says the child is working hard.

The second pressure point in Al Rashidiya arrives two years later. Ajman has fewer Diploma Programme places than Dubai, so a family choosing the IB at sixteen is often choosing a school in Sharjah or Dubai and a commute with it. Families who stay local take A-Levels or a second year of the British system instead. Either route needs a decision about mathematics that most parents make on the wrong information, and the decision is close to irreversible once the first term of DP1 is under way.

This page is written around those switch points rather than around Al Rashidiya's position on a map. It covers which board your child's school actually enters them for, what the two mathematics routes commit them to, what tuition costs in AED across the northern emirates, what an IGCSE grade converts to on paper, and what the Ministry of Education asks for when the certificates are finished. The teaching itself runs online, one-to-one, on a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time.

One thing worth saying plainly at the start: IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in Ajman. Home visiting is a service we run in India only. For a family in Al Rashidiya the practical effect is that the pool a child is matched from is not limited to the handful of specialists who happen to live within a twenty-minute drive, which matters far more here than it would in Jumeirah. The lesson happens wherever the child already works, on a fixed weekly slot, with the annotated document left behind afterwards for whichever parent gets home first to read.

ajman/al-rashidiya-ajman.programmesIntro: Three routes matter to an Al Rashidiya family, and only one of them is widely available inside Ajman without a commute. The notes below say what each one assesses and what it does to a weekly tuition plan. The Diploma entry is written for families who have already accepted a drive to Sharjah or Dubai for DP1 and DP2.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years, two boards, and most Al Rashidiya children sit one without knowing which. Cambridge grades 9 to 1 on syllabuses such as 0580 Mathematics and 0625 Physics; Pearson uses 4MA1 and 4PH1 and offers an entry pattern Cambridge does not. The papers differ in length, in calculator rules and in whether a tiered entry exists. A tutor who prepares a child for the wrong one still teaches good physics and still loses marks on question style.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman's private schools are inspected by the federal Ministry of Education rather than KHDA, which means the inspection report you can read about an Al Rashidiya school is a different document from the one a Dubai parent reads. The board a school enters is a school-level decision, published in its exam-entry letter rather than in any regulator file, so that letter is the first thing to find.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and reported as a 1 to 7 level. A child moving into MYP from an Indian-curriculum primary meets criterion language for the first time: inquiring and analysing, knowing and understanding, communicating. Marks come from the criteria rather than from a percentage, so a child who answers correctly but ignores the criterion wording scores lower than a weaker answer that addresses it.
programmes.countryNote: Very few Ajman schools run the MYP, so an Al Rashidiya family in it has usually chosen a campus on the Emirates Road belt or over the Sharjah border. The practical consequence is a long bus day, which pushes any tuition slot past 6pm and makes a fixed weekly online time easier to hold than a visiting arrangement that depends on traffic on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal assessment carries about a fifth of most subject grades and is marked against named criteria by the teacher, then moderated. The written papers are sat in a single May session for almost every UAE school. Two years of content and three coursework pieces land in the same twelve months, which is why DP1 drift is harder to recover from than Year 10 drift.
programmes.countryNote: A Diploma decision taken in Al Rashidiya usually comes with a school change and a commute, because Diploma places in Ajman are limited. Families who make that move arrive at a campus where their child is new, the teaching language is the same but the assessment grammar is not, and the first internal assessment deadline is six months away. That is the window where one-to-one support pays for itself.

ajman/al-rashidiya-ajman.subjectsIntro: Eight subjects account for most of what Al Rashidiya families ask about, and they are not the eight a Dubai Marina page would list. Mathematics dominates, the three sciences follow, and English B appears more often than English A because many households here use Malayalam, Urdu, Arabic or Tagalog at home.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route for engineering, physics and most economics degrees. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which exposes any algebra a student has been getting away with on a graphic display calculator. Marks go missing in proof by induction, in complex numbers at Higher Level, and in the exploration, where the mathematics is often correct and the personal engagement criterion scores two out of four.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-permitted throughout and heavier on statistics, regression and modelling. It suits business, psychology and design routes. The trap is the assumption that this is the easy option: Higher Level carries a demanding statistics and matrices load, and some engineering admissions still ask for Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics are where Al Rashidiya students most often ask for help. Paper 1 carries the multiple-choice section, Paper 2 carries the extended response, and the internal assessment is a single scientific investigation marked on personal engagement, exploration, analysis, evaluation and communication.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The subject where command terms do the most damage. A student who can calculate the answer still loses the mark for explain, because the explanation needs a named physical principle rather than a repeat of the arithmetic. Circular motion, fields and the Higher Level extension topics are the recurring gaps.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of recall plus a demanding data-analysis strand. Students arriving from an Indian-curriculum primary usually have strong factual recall and weaker experimental reasoning, which is the opposite of the profile a British primary produces. Sessions start with past-paper data questions rather than with content revision.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: For students who use English at school and another language at home. Assessment covers two written papers and an individual oral built on a visual stimulus linked to a course theme. The oral is where preparation shows: a student who has rehearsed speaks for the full time and addresses the theme, rather than describing the picture.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: The Extended tier reaches grade 9; Core cannot be awarded above grade 5 or C. Choosing Core to feel safe is one of the most expensive decisions a Year 10 family makes, because it closes the Higher Level mathematics door two years early. A timed diagnostic paper in the first term of Year 10 answers the question properly.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three papers at Higher Level, two at Standard, plus internal assessment commentaries built on real news articles. Diagram accuracy carries marks that students routinely give away: an unlabelled axis or a missing new-equilibrium point loses the same mark whether the written analysis is good or poor.

sections.heading: Who lives in Al Rashidiya, and what that does to a school file
paragraphs: Ajman is the smallest emirate by area and Al Rashidiya sits close to its centre, which means almost nothing is far away and almost everything is shared. The same stretch of Sheikh Humaid Bin Rashid Al Nuaimi Street serves apartment households where both parents commute to Dubai or Sharjah and villa households where one parent works locally. The two patterns produce different academic problems and ask for different tuition timetables, and treating them as one audience is how a generic page gets written.

The commuting household's problem is time, not money. A parent who leaves Al Rashidiya at 6.40am for a Dubai office and returns at 7.30pm is not supervising homework at 5pm, and the child does three hours of unsupervised study between the school bus and dinner. What that child needs is a fixed appointment with someone who checks the work, not more worksheets. A 7pm or 8pm slot in Gulf Standard Time is the realistic one, and it is a slot a visiting tutor would charge travel for.

The locally employed household's problem is more often subject coverage. Ajman's private-school set is small, and a school that teaches IGCSE Physics well may have one teacher covering Higher Level chemistry as a second subject. The child is not failing and the school is not negligent; there is simply no specialist in the building. That gap does not close by hiring someone who lives nearby, because the nearby pool has the same shape as the school's.

Both groups share one thing: the child's school file usually records more than one curriculum. A transfer in Year 5 from an Indian-curriculum primary, a stream change in Year 9, an IGCSE entry in Year 10 that the parent did not choose. Each of those is a point where the assessment grammar changed and nobody retaught it. The rest of this page is organised around those points rather than around a list of subjects.

sections.heading: The curriculum switch, subject by subject
paragraphs: A curriculum change is described to parents as a transfer and experienced by the child as a new subject. The content overlap between an Indian-curriculum Class 9 and a Cambridge IGCSE Year 10 is large in mathematics and smaller in the sciences, but the assessment overlap is small in all of them. A child who scored 85 in a Class 9 mathematics examination can sit an Extended 0580 paper and come out at grade 5, not because the mathematics is weaker but because a third of the marks are for interpretation, for units, and for showing a method the marker can follow.

The same applies in the other direction. A British Year 11 student moving into DP1 has been trained to answer in exam-board language and meets criterion language for the first time. Internal assessment marks come from named criteria with letters attached, and a student who writes a strong report without addressing criterion D leaves four marks on the table. Nobody tells them that in the first term, because the first term is about content.

The table below sets out the switches that actually happen in Al Rashidiya, with the gap each one leaves and roughly how long it takes to close with weekly one-to-one work. The week counts are planning figures to argue with rather than promises, and they assume a student who does the practice between sessions.

Two practical notes sit under the table. Timing matters more than intensity: a gap identified in the first month of a transfer closes in half the sessions it needs six months later, once the wrong habits have been practised. sections.heading: Which exam board your child's school actually entered them for
paragraphs: This is one of the most useful questions a parent in Al Rashidiya can ask the school office, and most do not know it is a question. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both award an International GCSE, both are accepted by UAE and overseas universities, and both are taught in Ajman. They are not the same examination. The syllabus codes differ, the number of papers differs, the tiering rules differ, and in mathematics the calculator rules differ too.

Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones. Cambridge's own exams officers' guide states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Pearson offers International GCSE in May or June and in November, and publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series that can still be revised.

What that means for a tuition plan is simple enough: the plan is written against the code on the entry letter, not against the subject name. A student preparing for 4MA1 who practises 0580 past papers is practising a slightly different examination, and the difference shows up in timing and in question tariffs rather than in content. The table gives the pairs that come up most often in Ajman schools.

Dates and timetables in that table come from the boards' own published pages, which are the only versions worth planning against. The school's exams officer holds the zone-specific copy. Ask for it in September rather than in April, when the deadlines that matter have already passed.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE grade converts to, and what it does not
paragraphs: Al Rashidiya parents comparing a child's progress across two curricula hit a translation problem. An Indian-curriculum report gives a percentage. A Cambridge IGCSE gives a number from 9 to 1 on most syllabuses and a letter from A* to G on others, and the two Cambridge scales are not two names for the same thing in a child's head even though they map cleanly on paper. A Diploma subject gives a 1 to 7. None of these convert to a percentage, because grade boundaries move every series.

That last point is the one worth holding on to. Boundaries are set after the papers are marked, against that cohort's performance. A student who needs seventy per cent for an A has been given a rule of thumb rather than a fact, and planning revision against a percentage target produces false confidence in a generous series and panic in a hard one. The useful target is marks on specific question types, which is diagnosable from a past paper and is what a tuition plan should be written against.

The table sets the scales side by side with what each band signals for a next step, which is the question parents are actually asking. Note the two ceilings in it: a Cambridge Core entry cannot be awarded above grade 5 or C, and a Foundation tier entry at Pearson caps in a comparable way. That ceiling is set in Year 10 by an entry decision, long before anyone revises for anything.

Where an internal assessment is involved the arithmetic changes again. A Diploma internal assessment is marked against criteria out of a stated total, combined with the written papers at the subject's published weighting, and the whole thing is then converted to a 1 to 7 against that session's boundaries. A student who hears eighteen out of twenty-four has no idea yet what it is worth, and neither does the teacher until the session is graded.

sections.heading: The Ministry of Education equivalency file an Ajman leaver needs
paragraphs: A certificate earned in Ajman is recognised abroad on its own terms. Inside the UAE it usually needs an equivalency certificate from the Ministry of Education before a university will process the application, and the requirements are published rather than negotiable. For the British track - the one most Al Rashidiya leavers are on - Gulf Today's reporting of the ministry's clarification sets out five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

One detail in that rule changes subject choices in Year 9, and almost nobody mentions it: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. A child who counts them is a subject short. At least one competing tutoring site currently tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects, which is the wrong count. Reading the rule properly in Year 9 costs nothing; discovering it in Year 13 costs a year.

For the American track the same clarification requires English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and at least 450 in SAT Mathematics before applying. For the IB there is no points threshold we are willing to publish, because the figure is not in that source and we have not read it on moe.gov.ae. Anyone quoting an IB points number for equivalency should be asked which page it came from and when.

IB Gram does not perform equivalency, submit attestations or guarantee any outcome in that process. It is a Ministry of Education process and it belongs with the ministry and the school. What tuition can do is make sure the five subjects a child is counting on are the five that count, and that the grades in them clear the line with room to spare - including Arabic and Islamic education, which remain compulsory school subjects under federal rules even though they sit outside that count of five.
