sections.heading: Academic honesty: the boundary a tutor works inside
paragraphs: Internal assessment is where tutoring in this market goes wrong. One site ranking for UAE IB queries sells finished Internal Assessments at a fixed price. That is not tutoring and it is not a grey area: submitted work that is not the student's own is malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence lands on the student rather than on the seller. A family in Al Rashidiya paying for exam-year support should know exactly where the line sits before the first session is booked.

Here is the working version of that line. A tutor may teach the subject content an assessment draws on, explain the published criteria and what each one is actually asking for, discuss a research question until it is narrow enough to answer, read a draft the student has already written and say which criterion is under-served, and model an unrelated worked example. A tutor may not supply sentences, restructure a student's draft on their behalf, hand over a data set, or return a document with new content added to it.

Two practical consequences follow for a tuition plan. Sessions on coursework are front-loaded: the useful work happens before the student starts writing, in narrowing the question and understanding the criteria, not in polishing afterwards. And everything is kept in a form a school supervisor could read without concern - because a supervisor is required to see drafts and to authenticate the work, and because a student who cannot explain their own method in a conversation has a bigger problem than a mark.

The same applies to past papers and mark schemes. Board materials are copyright and belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. Tutors reference them and link to the official pages; they do not hand out libraries of them, and any provider offering a pack of unreleased material is offering a problem rather than an advantage.

sections.heading: Starting mid-term, and what happens when no specialist is free
paragraphs: Most enquiries from Al Rashidiya arrive in the wrong week. A mock result in November, a parents' evening in February, a Year 11 who has just worked out how many weeks are left. Starting late is worse than starting early and much better than not starting, and the plan for a late start is a different plan: fewer topics, chosen by marks available, and no attempt to cover the syllabus for its own sake.

The first session for a late start is a timed past paper on the school's own syllabus code, marked against the published scheme. That produces a list of question types rather than a list of topics, and the list is nearly always shorter than the parent feared and differently shaped than the child described. Six weeks of twice-weekly work on four recurring question types moves more marks than twelve weeks of chapter revision.

On availability, the honest version. Subject scarcity is real at Higher Level and in the smaller Diploma subjects. If nobody who teaches your child's exact syllabus and level is free in the window you need, we say so rather than putting a generalist in the slot. Where a UAE-based specialist is not available, the match may be a specialist based elsewhere working on Gulf Standard Time, and that is stated before anything is booked rather than after.

What that means in practice for an Al Rashidiya family is three questions to ask before paying anyone. Which syllabus code will you teach to. What level have you taught at, and when. What happens if the match is wrong after two sessions. A provider who cannot answer the first question has not read the entry letter.

faqs.question: Can we get an IB or IGCSE home tutor in Al Rashidiya, Ajman?
faqs.answer: Home tutors exist in this market and local providers charge roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour for a visit, with travel inside the rate. IB Gram works differently: lessons for Al Rashidiya families are one-to-one online over live video, and home visiting is a service we run only in India. The practical gain is the size of the pool. A Higher Level chemistry specialist does not have to live within a twenty-minute drive of Sheikh Humaid Bin Rashid Al Nuaimi Street to teach your child twice a week, which matters in an emirate with a small private-school set.

faqs.question: Which authority inspects private schools in Al Rashidiya, Ajman?
faqs.answer: The federal Ministry of Education. The u.ae government portal states that the ministry supervises private schools in the emirates of Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, while Dubai sits with KHDA, Abu Dhabi with ADEK, Sharjah with its Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge. That matters when you go looking for a report: there is no KHDA inspection file for an Ajman school, so a page telling you to look one up was written for Dubai and copied across. Ask the school directly for its most recent inspection outcome.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child sits Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE papers?
faqs.answer: Ask the school office for the exam-entry letter or the candidate statement of entry. It carries the board, the syllabus code and the tier. Cambridge codes look like 0580 for mathematics and 0625 for physics; Pearson Edexcel codes look like 4MA1 and 4PH1. The subject name on a report card does not tell you, and the two boards set different papers with different mark tariffs. A tutor preparing a child for the wrong code teaches good content and loses marks on question style, which is the most avoidable problem described on this page.

faqs.question: My son moved from an Indian-curriculum school into IGCSE in Year 10. What usually goes wrong?
faqs.answer: Content is rarely the issue; the mathematics overlaps heavily. What catches these students is command-term vocabulary and interpretation marks. An IGCSE paper asks them to describe, explain, suggest and evaluate, and each verb carries a mark tariff behind it. A student who calculates correctly and then writes two sentences of restated arithmetic has earned the method marks and lost the rest. Eight to twelve weeks of weekly work on question types, with a timed paper at the start, closes most of that gap when it begins in the transfer term rather than in Year 11.

faqs.question: Is it a mistake to let the school enter my daughter for IGCSE Core rather than Extended?
faqs.answer: It is a decision with a ceiling attached, and ceilings are worth understanding before they are accepted. A Cambridge Core entry cannot be awarded above grade 5 or C, and that closes Higher Level mathematics at Diploma and some sixth-form routes two years before anyone revises. Core is the right call for some students and the safe-feeling call for many more. The way to answer it properly is a timed Extended past paper in the first term of Year 10, marked against the published scheme, rather than a conversation about confidence.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tutors charge per hour around Ajman?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online work, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel included, and AED 200 to 450 and above for IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialist support. IB Gram offers a free trial lesson and a consultation rather than a published price list.

faqs.question: Why would an online lesson beat a tutor sitting at the same table in Al Rashidiya?
faqs.answer: For some children it would not, and a young child who needs a hand physically guided through long division is better served in the room. For an IGCSE or Diploma student the arithmetic changes. The specialist pool stops being everyone within a drivable radius of Ajman and becomes everyone who teaches that syllabus at that level. Screen-shared work leaves the family an annotated document a commuting parent can read at 8pm. And the slot survives a bad evening on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, which a travelling arrangement does not.

faqs.question: How many Advanced Level subjects does the Ministry of Education equivalency need?
faqs.answer: On the British track, the ministry's published clarification requires one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five. Verify the current wording at moe.gov.ae before locking a Year 9 or Year 12 subject choice, because this is the ministry's own process and not something a tutoring provider performs or guarantees.

faqs.question: Does an IB points figure exist for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Not one we are prepared to publish. The ministry clarification covering the British and American tracks states subject counts and minimum grades for those routes, and sets out English and mathematics test scores for the American track, but it does not state an IB points threshold, and we have not read one on moe.gov.ae. Several tutoring sites quote a number anyway. If you are given one, ask which page it was read on and on what date. For an IB leaver the reliable route is the school's diploma coordinator and the ministry's own attestation channel.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my daughter's mathematics exploration without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary worth stating in advance. A tutor can teach the mathematics the exploration relies on, explain each assessment criterion and the marks attached to it, help narrow a topic until it is answerable, and read a draft she has already written and say which criterion is under-served. A tutor cannot supply sentences, restructure the work on her behalf or add content to the document. Everything done in a session should be the sort of thing her school supervisor could see without concern, because the supervisor is required to see drafts and authenticate the work.

faqs.question: How late is too late to start before the June IGCSE series?
faqs.answer: Twelve weeks is comfortable, six weeks is workable, and three weeks changes the job from teaching to triage. A late plan is built from marks available rather than from the syllabus: a timed paper first, then four or five recurring question types worked twice a week until they are reliable. Covering everything is not the aim and attempting it wastes the weeks that remain. One scheduling note for Al Rashidiya families: Cambridge allocates centres to administrative zones with different timetables, so plan against the copy your school's exams officer holds.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in the UAE need a permit, and how would I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring is permitted work under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and MoHRE issues a private tuition work permit which is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app and e-services, and the service page lists a two-working-day completion time.

faqs.question: Two children in one Al Rashidiya flat, two different boards. Does that work?
faqs.answer: It works, but not as one booking. A Year 11 on Pearson 4MA1 and a Year 9 on Cambridge 0580 need different papers, different tiering decisions and usually different tutors, and putting them in one session helps neither. What can be shared is the timetable: consecutive slots on the same evening, one quiet room used twice, and a single review point at six weeks so you are reading one plan rather than two. Households with one usable desk should book the harder subject into the earlier, quieter slot.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for my son's Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: You are told before you pay. Scarcity is real in the smaller Diploma subjects and at Higher Level generally, and it is sharper in the northern emirates than in Dubai. If nobody who teaches that syllabus at that level is available in the window you need, we say so rather than filling the slot with a generalist. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the alternative offered may be a specialist working from elsewhere on Gulf Standard Time, and that is disclosed before booking. No page in this market publishes a coverage limit; this one does.

intro.heading: Al Rawda's real question is which three subjects go at Higher Level
paragraphs: Al Rawda 1, 2 and 3 are inland villa streets, newer than central Ajman and quieter, with the kind of housing that gives a teenager a desk and a door. Families here tend to be settled rather than transient: a five-year tenancy, two or three children, and a plan that assumes the youngest will finish school in the same emirate the eldest started in. That stability changes the questions parents ask. Nobody in Al Rawda is asking how to survive a mid-year transfer. They are asking what to choose at sixteen.

The choice is narrower than it looks and more consequential than it feels. A full Diploma means six subjects, three of them at Higher Level, and the Higher Level three are not simply the same courses with extra homework. They carry additional content, an extra paper in several subjects, and a different internal assessment expectation. A student who takes three Higher Levels that all demand long written answers has built a timetable where every deadline arrives in the same fortnight.

Then there is mathematics, which is a two-door decision made once. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic, proof-oriented route; Applications and Interpretation is the statistical, modelling-oriented route. Both exist at Standard and Higher Level. They are not ranked, they are different, and some degree routes expect one specifically. The decision is taken in the spring of Year 11 by a sixteen-year-old with incomplete information, and it is effectively final by the end of the first DP1 term.

Al Rawda's other structural feature is distance from a Diploma classroom. Ajman's Diploma provision is limited, so most students here travel to a campus on the Emirates Road belt or into Sharjah. A 7am departure and a 5pm return is a long day, and it rules out afternoon tuition entirely. The only workable shape is a fixed evening slot, which is one reason online delivery suits this district rather than being a compromise in it.

That is what this page covers: how the Higher Level load actually distributes across papers and coursework, how to choose between the two mathematics routes against a degree rather than against a reputation, what the prerequisites are and where to verify them, what two years of support costs in AED, and where marks are lost in each Higher Level science. Tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists in India only.

A note on what this page does not do. It publishes no IB exam dates, because the IB's own site could not be read directly for this project and a date taken from a secondary source is not a date. Cambridge and Pearson dates appear where the boards themselves published them. Ask your child's diploma coordinator for the session calendar, and plan against that rather than against anything written here.

ajman/al-rawda.programmesIntro: Four blocks matter to an Al Rawda family in sequence: the International GCSE years that set the entry grades, the Middle Years Programme where criterion marking is learnt, the Diploma itself, and the Diploma core that sits alongside the six subjects and is underestimated by almost everybody.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, with final written papers in a single session. Each subject carries an internal assessment marked against named criteria by the teacher and then moderated. Points run to 45 including the core, and the award conditions are set by the IB rather than by the school. The programme rewards students who can hold several long-running pieces of work at once, which is a scheduling skill before it is an academic one.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma places near Al Rawda are few, so families in the programme have usually accepted a daily journey to the Emirates Road belt or into Sharjah. The consequence for planning is specific: a student leaving at 7am and home at 5pm has one usable study block, between about 6pm and 9pm, and that block has to hold homework, coursework and any tuition. Sessions that sit inside it work; sessions that compete with it do not.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: The core runs for two years in parallel with everything else. Theory of Knowledge has an exhibition and an essay; the Extended Essay is an independent 4,000-word research piece supervised by a teacher; CAS is a portfolio of creativity, activity and service with reflective requirements. The core carries up to three bonus points and, more importantly, carries conditions that can affect the award of the diploma itself.
programmes.countryNote: The core is where Al Rawda students most often ask for help, and it is where the academic-honesty rules are tightest. A supervisor must see drafts and authenticate the work, so tuition here is feedback on writing the student has already done, criterion by criterion. The useful sessions happen before the writing: narrowing a research question until 4,000 words can actually answer it is worth more than any amount of editing afterwards.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, converted to a 1 to 7 level against published grade boundaries. The programme teaches the habit the Diploma then assumes: answering against a criterion rather than against a question. Students who arrive in DP1 from MYP 5 generally handle internal assessment better than students arriving from IGCSE, and generally handle Paper 1 timing worse.
programmes.countryNote: Few Ajman schools run the MYP, so an Al Rawda student in it is already commuting and already used to it. The transition worth preparing for is the content jump: MYP depth is lower than IGCSE depth in the sciences and in mathematics, so a student moving into Higher Level chemistry or Higher Level Analysis and Approaches from MYP 5 has a content gap that six to ten weeks of targeted work closes if it starts in the summer rather than in November.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years ending in a June or November series, graded 9 to 1 or A* to G depending on the syllabus. For an Al Rawda family the International GCSE matters mostly as the gatekeeper: the grades decide which Higher Levels a sixth form will allow, and a grade 5 in mathematics is a common line for Higher Level entry. Extended or Higher tier entry is therefore a Diploma decision taken two years early.
programmes.countryNote: Because Ajman schools fall under the federal Ministry of Education, there is no emirate inspection portal to compare local schools' entry practice. Ask the school which tier it enters by default. A student intending to take Higher Level mathematics in two years' time needs the Extended or Higher tier now, and that is a conversation for the first term of Year 10 rather than for the end of it.

ajman/al-rawda.subjectsIntro: What Al Rawda families book is almost entirely Higher Level work, and the requests cluster where the mark allocations are harshest. The descriptions below name the component and where the marks actually go, because a student who knows a paper is worth a third of the grade revises differently from one who does not.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic route, with proof, calculus and complex numbers at Higher Level and a non-calculator paper that nothing else in the Diploma resembles. Students who survived IGCSE on a calculator meet the consequences here in the first term. The optional topic depth and the timing of Paper 3 are the two places where otherwise strong candidates lose marks they could keep.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling, matrices and graph theory, with technology permitted throughout. Higher Level is demanding rather than gentle, and the common error is choosing it as the lighter option and then meeting hypothesis testing and regression at depth. Marks are lost in presentation: an unstated assumption or an unlabelled model costs the same as an arithmetic error.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields carry most of the Higher Level extension, and the examination rewards explanation in the language of named principles. A candidate who calculates a correct value and then restates the calculation in words has answered a describe question when the paper asked to explain. Uncertainty treatment in the internal assessment is the other recurring loss.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium are the Higher Level pressure points. The internal assessment is a single investigation scored against criteria covering engagement, exploration, analysis, evaluation and communication, and the evaluation criterion is the one students treat as a conclusion rather than as a critique of their own method.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The largest recall load in the group and an examination that keeps asking students to apply it to unfamiliar material. Higher Level extension in metabolism and plant biology is where the content volume defeats memorisation. Work here is built on unseen data and graph interpretation rather than on re-reading, which is also what the internal assessment rewards.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level adds a third paper and a quantitative demand that surprises students who chose the subject for the essays. Diagrams carry marks that are given away rather than lost: axes unlabelled, the new equilibrium unmarked, the shift drawn in the wrong direction. The internal assessment commentaries need genuinely recent articles, which is a sourcing problem before it is a writing one.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two written papers, an individual oral and, at Higher Level, an essay on a studied work. The paper that catches students is unseen analysis: they summarise the text instead of analysing how it produces its effect. Higher Level candidates also need a defensible global issue for the oral, chosen early enough to gather extracts that actually support it.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies, methods and ethical considerations, with Higher Level extensions and an experimental internal assessment that must replicate a published study simply enough to be ethical. Students lose marks by describing studies rather than using them as evidence for a claim, and by writing a report that reads as a narrative rather than as a structured analysis.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source work, essay writing and, at Higher Level, a regional depth study across an extra paper. The internal assessment is a historical investigation with a strict word allocation across its sections, and students routinely over-write the first section and leave the evaluation of sources thin, which is where the marks sit.

ajman/al-rawda.regionsIntro: The journey to a Diploma classroom is the thing that shapes an Al Rawda week, so these neighbourhood notes are about roads and timings rather than about character. Each one changes when a session can realistically start.

regions.note: Inland villa streets with space for a desk and a closed door, which is a real advantage for video lessons. Most secondary students here are bussed out of the district, so the usable study block runs from about 6pm.

regions.note: Directly adjacent and similar in housing, sharing the same bus routes and the same small pool of local subject specialists. Families in the two districts often compare notes and discover they have been offered the same tutor.

regions.name: Al Zahya and Al Tallah
regions.note: Newer development along the Emirates Road corridor, where several of the British and IB campuses Al Rawda students attend are located. Pick-up here is early and the return leg carries the full evening peak.

regions.note: Over the border and the destination for a good share of Al Rawda's Diploma students. Twenty-five minutes on a clear road and considerably more at 7.15am, which is why the school day starts before most households are awake.

regions.note: Where the emirate's examination centres and older schools sit. Worth knowing for a private-candidate entry or a resit, since the centre rather than the home district determines the timetable zone that applies.

modes.description: Weekly sessions through the first Diploma year, aimed at the two things that decide DP2. The first is the Higher Level content gap left by MYP 5 or IGCSE, which is specific and closable. The second is learning to answer against a criterion, which is a habit rather than a topic and takes a term of corrected practice to build.

sections.heading: Who lives in Al Rawda, and what their sixth-form decision looks like
paragraphs: Al Rawda is a settled district. The villa streets of Al Rawda 1, 2 and 3 hold families who have been in the same house for years, often with two or three children spread across primary and secondary. The academic consequence is that parents here are making decisions for the second or third time, which makes them better informed and also more likely to assume that what worked for the eldest will work for the next one. Subject choice is the place where that assumption costs most.

The decision in front of these families is not whether to take the Diploma. It is which three subjects to take at Higher Level and which mathematics route to follow, and those two choices interact. Three Higher Levels that all require extended written answers put four long deadlines in the same fortnight of DP2. Two sciences and Higher Level mathematics put the heaviest content load in the same year. There is no arrangement without a cost, and the useful work is choosing which cost to carry.

The second thing that shapes the week here is the commute. Ajman has limited Diploma provision, so most Al Rawda students are at a campus on the Emirates Road belt or over the Sharjah border. Leaving at 7am and arriving home at 5pm leaves one study block in the evening, and everything - homework, coursework, reading, tuition - has to fit inside it. A visiting tutor consumes part of that block in logistics; a video call at a fixed time does not.

What a tutor is actually useful for in this district is narrower and more valuable than general support. Closing a specific Higher Level content gap. Teaching criterion-based writing before DP2 makes it urgent. Marking timed components against the published scheme so a student knows what their work is worth. None of that requires proximity, and all of it requires somebody who teaches that subject at that level routinely.

sections.heading: Three Higher Levels: how the load is actually distributed
paragraphs: Higher Level is described to students as more depth, which is true and unhelpful. What changes is the structure: additional syllabus content, an extra written paper in several subjects, a longer or more demanding internal assessment in some, and a different expectation of independent reading in the humanities. A student choosing three Higher Levels is choosing a timetable, and timetables can be well or badly designed.

The badly designed version is familiar. Two essay-based Higher Levels plus Higher Level history gives a student three extended pieces of coursework with similar deadlines and a reading load that cannot be compressed. Two sciences plus Higher Level Analysis and Approaches gives the heaviest content volume available and three internal assessments requiring laboratory or computational work. Neither is wrong. Both need the deadline map drawn in DP1 rather than discovered in DP2.

The table sets out what changes between Standard and Higher Level across the things that affect planning. The precise weightings for your child's subjects sit in the current subject guide, which the school's diploma coordinator holds; the pattern below is the shape of the difference rather than a substitute for that document. Read it with a calendar open.

One practical rule that falls out of it. Put the subject with the earliest internal assessment deadline into the earliest tuition block of DP1, not the subject the student finds hardest. The hardest subject is a two-year problem. A deadline is a six-week problem, and a missed one costs marks no amount of later work recovers.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: This is the only Diploma choice that regularly closes a university door by accident. Analysis and Approaches is the algebra-and-proof route: calculus, functions, trigonometric identities, complex numbers at Higher Level, and a paper sat without a calculator. Applications and Interpretation is the statistics-and-modelling route: regression, hypothesis testing, matrices, graph theory, with technology permitted throughout. Both run at Standard and Higher Level. Neither is the easy one.

The myth worth dismantling is that Applications and Interpretation is the soft option. Higher Level Applications includes a demanding statistical and matrix load, and students who chose it to avoid algebra find the modelling questions require exactly the algebraic fluency they were avoiding. Equally, a student who genuinely thinks in patterns and data and is pushed into Analysis and Approaches for prestige spends two years translating rather than thinking.

The decision should be made against the degree, and then verified with the university. Engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics programmes commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level. Business, psychology, design and many social science routes accept either and sometimes prefer Applications. That is the general pattern, and the general pattern is not an admissions requirement. The only authority on what a specific programme wants is that programme's own admissions page, and it is worth reading in Year 11 rather than Year 13.

A diagnostic helps more than a conversation. Give the student a short set of questions from each route and watch which one they argue with productively. A student who enjoys proving a statement and a student who enjoys interpreting a dataset are visible within half an hour, and that observation is more reliable than either their stated preference or their current grade.

sections.heading: Prerequisites, and the only place worth checking them
paragraphs: Subject choice at sixteen is a bet on a degree a student has not applied to yet, which is why prerequisites get treated as folklore. Someone's cousin got into engineering with Standard Level mathematics; a school counsellor said medicine needs three sciences; a tutoring website published a table. All three may be true somewhere and none of them is a requirement anywhere in particular.

The reliable method is unglamorous. List three or four plausible destinations, open each one's own admissions page for the specific programme, and write down what it says about subjects and levels. Do it in Year 11 while the choice is still open, repeat it in DP1 because requirements change, and keep the printed page. A requirement read on the university's own site in a dated screenshot beats any summary, including this one.

The table below is a map of where to look and what the common expectation tends to be, not a statement of any institution's rules. It exists because families ask for the shape of the landscape before they start reading admissions pages, and because the shape is genuinely useful: it tells you which choices are likely to be constraining and therefore which pages to read first.

One structural point about UAE destinations specifically. A student leaving school in Ajman and applying to a UAE university will usually also need a Ministry of Education equivalency certificate for the school certificate itself, which is a separate process from the university's subject requirements. Both have to be satisfied, and the equivalency rules for the British track count five accredited subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education. IB Gram neither performs nor guarantees equivalency; it is the ministry's process.

sections.heading: What two Diploma years of support cost in Al Rawda
paragraphs: A Diploma is a two-year commitment and families here plan it as one, so the useful figure is not an hourly rate but an annual shape. The hourly bands are the market's and they are published by the providers named: a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300, specialist IB support at AED 200 to 450 and above, in-home visits at AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate, and budget online work from AED 33 to 65 at the low end. All read in October 2026.

Converted into a year, the arithmetic looks different. One weekly hour of mid-market support across a term is a few thousand dirhams; two weekly hours in DP2 for two Higher Level subjects is a materially larger commitment, and most families in Al Rawda end up buying intensity in the second year rather than coverage across both. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work.

The pattern that wastes the least money is front-loaded and then narrow. Buy support in DP1 for the specific Higher Level content gap and for criterion writing, which are cheap to fix early. Stop. Resume in DP2 for marked timed components in the two subjects that need them. Continuous weekly tuition in all six subjects for two years is the most expensive plan available and rarely the most effective one.

One piece of local context. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's economic incentives package. That freeze is a Dubai measure and does not cover Ajman schools, so an Al Rawda family budgeting for the two Diploma years should not assume it. IB Gram publishes no price list on this page: the free trial lesson and the consultation that follows it price the actual plan.

sections.heading: Where marks are lost in each Higher Level science
paragraphs: Diagnostics are more useful than reassurance, so this section is specific. In Higher Level physics the recurring loss is command-term failure: a candidate computes the right number and then writes a sentence restating the computation, which answers a describe question rather than an explain one. The fix is mechanical and fast. Practise answering explain prompts by naming the principle first, then applying it, and the marks return within a few weeks.

In Higher Level chemistry the loss concentrates in two places. Organic mechanisms are drawn rather than reasoned, so a student who has memorised arrow patterns cannot handle an unfamiliar substrate. And in the internal assessment, the evaluation criterion is written as a conclusion. Evaluation means critiquing your own method with specific reference to what the data shows about its limits, and students who understand that distinction gain marks without changing their experiment.

In Higher Level biology the loss is strategic rather than technical. The content volume rewards memorisation, the examination rewards application to unseen material, and a student who revises by re-reading is optimising for the wrong thing. Sessions built around unseen data questions and graph interpretation produce more movement than any amount of content revision, and they also prepare the internal assessment analysis.

Across all three, the internal assessment is where the quickest gains sit, because the criteria are published and most students have never read them properly. A tutor can explain exactly what each criterion rewards and read a draft the student has written to say which one is under-served. A tutor cannot supply text or restructure the student's work on their behalf, and that boundary is covered in its own section below.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against the alternatives, from an Al Rawda villa
paragraphs: The home-tutor question deserves a direct answer on a page that targets the phrase. An Al Rawda villa is a good environment for a visiting tutor: there is space, there is a door, and the household is settled enough to hold a regular appointment. If that is the arrangement you want, the local market sells it at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the figure, and for a younger child it is often the better product.

IB Gram does not provide it. Tuition for Al Rawda families is one-to-one online over live video, and home visiting is a service we run only in India. For a Diploma student the reasoning is straightforward. The person who can tell a Higher Level chemistry candidate what the evaluation criterion actually rewards is a subject specialist, and the number of those within driving distance of an inland Ajman villa is small. Matching on geography means matching on availability.

The comparison below is built on the things that differ in practice rather than on a sales argument. Note the row about the evening study block, which is the constraint that matters most here: a commuting Diploma student has roughly three usable hours, and travel logistics eat into them whether the travel is the tutor's or the family's.

One alternative worth taking seriously before paying for anything. Most schools run subject support sessions, and a student who has not attended them has an unused resource that is already inside the fees. Where the school has a specialist in the subject, that is often the first and cheapest fix, and a tutor's honest advice is to try it.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with an exploration, an essay and a Theory of Knowledge piece
paragraphs: Al Rawda families buying two years of support will spend some of it on coursework, so the boundary needs stating before the first session rather than after a problem. The IB's position is that submitted work must be the student's own, a supervisor must see drafts, and the submission must be authenticated. Those three facts define what support can be, and they define it the same way for a tutor, a teacher and a parent.

Inside the boundary there is a great deal a tutor can usefully do. Teach the subject content the task draws on. Read each assessment criterion aloud with the student and explain what it actually rewards, with the marks named. Argue about whether a research question can be answered with the evidence available and the words allowed. Read a draft the student has written and say which criterion is under-served and why. Model an unrelated worked example so the student can see the standard.

Outside the boundary the list is equally clear. No supplied sentences. No restructuring somebody else's work for them. No handing over a dataset. No returning a document with new material added. The test a family can apply at home is whether the student could explain, without prompting, why each decision in the piece was taken. If they cannot, the work has drifted away from them, and the consequence of that falls on the student rather than on whoever helped.

The same principle governs materials. Syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes are the property of the IB, Cambridge and Pearson. They are cited and linked rather than reproduced, and any provider offering a downloadable library of them, or material from an unreleased session, is offering a risk dressed as a resource.

sections.heading: A Diploma plan counted in terms rather than weeks
paragraphs: Families in this district plan in years, so here is the two-year shape that wastes the least. DP1 term one: close the Higher Level content gap left by MYP or IGCSE, and start criterion-based writing practice. DP1 term two: internal assessment research questions narrowed and agreed with the school supervisor, before any data is gathered. DP1 term three: first drafts written by the student, feedback mapped to criteria, and the Extended Essay question fixed.

DP2 term one is the heaviest and the one most commonly mismanaged. Coursework deadlines, mock examinations and the beginning of serious paper practice all land here. The plan that works narrows sharply: two subjects receiving real attention rather than six receiving a little. DP2 term two is timed components, marked against published schemes, with correction sessions aimed at whatever the marking exposed. Nothing new is introduced in the last six weeks.

Dates are deliberately absent from that outline. The IB's own site could not be read directly for this project, so no IB session or results date appears anywhere on these pages, and any date you see elsewhere should be checked against ibo.org or your school's diploma coordinator. Where Cambridge or Pearson dates are quoted on this site they come from the boards' own published pages, and for a UAE family the useful worked example is Pearson rather than Cambridge: the final Pearson Edexcel International GCSE timetable for the November 2026 series runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and those results reach students in January, exactly as the November 2025 grades did on 22 January 2026. Cambridge candidates in Ajman sit the June series or the November series, never the February-March one, which Cambridge offers to India only. Entries for any of them close months ahead of the first paper, and the date that governs your child is the one printed on their statement of entry from the school.

On availability, the position stated plainly. Higher Level specialists in the smaller subjects are scarce, and scarcer in the northern emirates than in Dubai. If nobody teaching that subject at that level has a slot in the window you need, you are told before any booking is made, and where no UAE-based specialist is free the alternative may be a specialist working from elsewhere on Gulf Standard Time. That is disclosed at the point of matching.

process.title: Start from the subject and level, with the guide to hand
process.description: Tell us the subject, whether it is Higher or Standard Level, and which internal assessment is next. The school's diploma coordinator holds the current subject guide with the component weightings in it. A tutor planning from that document plans accurately; one planning from a subject name guesses.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the Higher Level specialist
process.description: The trial is taught by the person who would take the course, on the topic the student is actually in. For a Diploma subject that matters more than at IGCSE, because Higher Level extension content is where a generalist becomes visible within twenty minutes.

process.title: A timed component, marked against the published scheme
process.description: In the first two sessions the student sits one real component under timing and it is marked properly. The output is a breakdown by question type with marks attached, which tells you where the grade actually sits rather than where the last report said it was.

process.title: Two-year plan, reviewed each term
process.description: The plan names what happens in each remaining term, which subjects get intensity and when support stops as well as when it starts. It is reviewed at the end of each term against the marked work rather than against impressions, and the review can conclude that tuition should pause.

whyPoints.title: Weightings quoted, not described
whyPoints.description: A page that says an assessment is important has told you nothing. This one names components, mark allocations and where candidates lose marks, and points you at the current subject guide for your child's actual numbers. That is the difference between advice and atmosphere.

whyPoints.title: The mathematics decision handled properly
whyPoints.description: Analysis and Approaches against Applications and Interpretation, compared on content and on loss type, with a diagnostic rather than a reputation to decide it. And the prerequisite checked on the university's own admissions page, which is the only source that binds anybody.

whyPoints.title: No IB dates we could not verify
whyPoints.description: The IB's site returned no readable response for this project, so no IB session or results date appears on these pages. Cambridge and Pearson dates are quoted with the board's own publication behind them. A date without a source is worse than no date.

whyPoints.title: A plan that tells you when to stop
whyPoints.description: Continuous tuition in six subjects for two years is the most expensive option available and rarely the most effective. The plan here is front-loaded on content gaps and criterion writing, then narrow and intense in DP2, with explicit pauses in between.

whyPoints.title: The cheapest fix recommended first
whyPoints.description: Where a school runs subject support sessions with a specialist in the subject, that is already paid for and is the first thing to try. A tutor who never mentions it is selling hours rather than solving a problem, and families in Al Rawda can tell the difference.

faqs.question: Can we book an IB home tutor for an Al Rawda villa in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Local providers do offer visits and charge roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the rate, so the product exists. IB Gram is not it: tuition for Al Rawda families is one-to-one online over live video, and home visiting is a service we run in India only. For a Diploma student the trade is favourable. The specialist who can explain what the Higher Level chemistry evaluation criterion rewards is rarely within driving distance of an inland Ajman villa, and matching on geography means matching on who happens to be free.

faqs.question: How do we choose which three subjects my son takes at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Start with the degree routes that are plausible and read their actual admissions pages, then look at load distribution rather than only at interest. Three Higher Levels that each need extended written coursework put several long deadlines in the same fortnight of DP2. Two sciences plus Higher Level mathematics gives the heaviest content volume available. Neither arrangement is wrong; both need a deadline map drawn in DP1. Where a student is genuinely undecided, a short diagnostic in the candidate subjects is more informative than another conversation about preference.

faqs.question: Is Applications and Interpretation the easier mathematics route?
faqs.answer: No, and treating it that way is how students end up in the wrong course. Higher Level Applications and Interpretation carries a demanding statistics and matrices load, and its modelling questions need the algebraic fluency some students chose the route to avoid. Analysis and Approaches is harder in proof and in non-calculator work; Applications is harder in interpretation and in presenting assumptions. The useful question is which type of thinking your child argues with productively, which a half-hour diagnostic across both routes will show more reliably than a predicted grade.

faqs.question: Which mathematics route does an engineering degree usually want?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, is the common expectation for engineering, physics and mathematics programmes, and several economics departments ask for it too. That is a pattern rather than a rule. The only binding statement is on the admissions page of the specific programme your child intends to apply to, so open it, read it, note the date, and keep it. Requirements change between cycles. Checking in Year 11 while the choice is still reversible costs an afternoon; discovering it in DP2 costs considerably more.

faqs.question: My daughter is moving from MYP 5 into Higher Level chemistry. What is the gap?
faqs.answer: Content depth rather than skill. MYP students generally handle criterion-based assessment better than IGCSE students do, because they have been marked that way for years, and generally handle the content volume and paper timing worse. The practical gap in Higher Level chemistry is quantitative: moles, energetics and equilibrium at a depth MYP does not reach. Six to ten weeks of targeted work closes it, and the cheapest time to do that is the summer before DP1 rather than November, once the course has moved on without her.

faqs.question: What does two years of Diploma tutoring cost for an Al Rawda family?
faqs.answer: It depends on how it is bought, and the pattern matters more than the hourly rate. Market rates read in October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150 to 300 an hour and specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 and above; Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour are AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist work. The least wasteful shape is front-loaded in DP1 on content gaps, paused, then intensive in DP2 on two subjects. IB Gram prices after a free trial and a consultation.

faqs.question: Why does this page not give the IB exam dates?
faqs.answer: Because we could not read them from the IB itself. The IB's site returned no usable response to the checks done for this project, and a date taken from a secondary source and published on a tutoring page is how wrong dates spread. Cambridge and Pearson dates appear on these pages because both boards publish their own key dates, and those are quoted with the board named. For IB sessions, ask your child's diploma coordinator or read ibo.org directly, and plan the revision calendar against that.

faqs.question: Where do Higher Level physics candidates usually lose marks?
faqs.answer: On command terms, more than on physics. A candidate computes the correct value and then writes a sentence restating the computation, which answers a describe prompt when the paper asked to explain. An explanation needs a named physical principle stated first and then applied. The second recurring loss is uncertainty treatment in the internal assessment, where students report a result without a defensible uncertainty or propagate it incorrectly. Both are mechanical problems with mechanical fixes, and both respond within a few weeks of corrected practice rather than needing a term.

faqs.question: What exactly can a tutor do with my child's Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the subject content the essay draws on, explain the assessment criteria with the marks attached to each, press hard on whether the research question can be answered in 4,000 words with the evidence available, and read a draft the student has written to say which criterion is under-served. A tutor cannot supply sentences, reorganise the work on the student's behalf, or add material to the document. The school supervisor must see drafts and authenticate the submission, so every session should produce something the supervisor could read without concern.

faqs.question: Does my child need a UAE equivalency certificate as well as the Diploma?
faqs.answer: For a UAE university application, usually yes, and it is separate from the university's own subject requirements. Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process. For the British track the published rule counts five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at E. No IB points threshold appears here because we have not read one on moe.gov.ae. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency; verify the current requirement with the ministry and the school.

faqs.question: Should we book tuition in all six Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Almost never, and it is the most expensive plan available. Continuous weekly support across six subjects for two years consumes the evening study block that a commuting Al Rawda student only has three hours of, and spreads attention so thin that nothing moves decisively. The pattern that works is front-loaded and narrow: DP1 support for the specific Higher Level content gap and for criterion writing, a pause, then intensive marked practice in DP2 for the two subjects that need it. The plan should name when support stops.

faqs.question: Our commute to a Sharjah campus is long. When can a session realistically start?
faqs.answer: About 6pm, and that is being optimistic in the first weeks of term. A Diploma student leaving Al Rawda at 7am and getting home around 5pm needs food and twenty minutes before anything cognitive happens. The usable block runs to roughly 9pm, and it has to hold homework and coursework as well. A one-hour online slot takes an hour from that block and nothing more, which is the practical argument against adding a visiting tutor's arrival, setup and doorstep conversation on top of it.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Higher Level maths and Higher Level physics?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth checking rather than assuming. The overlap in content is real, and a tutor who teaches both routinely can save a family a scheduling slot. What matters is whether they teach both at Higher Level now, not whether they studied both years ago. Higher Level extension content and the internal assessment criteria differ enough between the two that competence in one does not transfer. Ask which components they have marked recently and what the last internal assessment they gave feedback on was.

faqs.question: What if no Higher Level specialist is free when we need one?
faqs.answer: You are told before you pay anything. Scarcity is genuine in the smaller Diploma subjects and at Higher Level generally, and it is sharper in Ajman and the northern emirates than in Dubai. If nobody teaching that subject at that level has a slot in your window, we say so rather than putting a generalist in the chair and hoping. Where no UAE-based specialist is available, the alternative offered may be a specialist working from outside the UAE on Gulf Standard Time, disclosed at matching rather than discovered in the third week.

ajman/al-rawda.closingHeading: Decide the levels first, then buy the hours
ajman/al-rawda.closingBody: The expensive mistakes in an Al Rawda Diploma are made before any tuition is booked: three Higher Levels whose deadlines collide, a mathematics route chosen for its reputation rather than for the degree, an entry tier at IGCSE that quietly closed Higher Level two years earlier. Fix those with a subject guide, a university admissions page and one timed diagnostic. Then buy a narrow, front-loaded plan rather than six subjects for two years. Lessons for Al Rawda families run one-to-one over live video on a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot inside the evening study block.

The point of a continuum tutor is knowing what the next stage will assume, not just what the current one assesses.

intro.heading: Al Yasmeen's question is not the grade, it is the join
paragraphs: Al Yasmeen is one of Ajman's newer villa communities, inland and towards the Emirates Road, with the kind of housing families buy when they intend to stay. The households here tend to have two or three children spread across primary and secondary, a settled school choice, and a plan that runs ten years rather than one. That changes the questions completely. Nobody in these streets is in crisis. They are trying to work out whether a seven-year-old's reading is on track and whether a fifteen-year-old is ready for what comes next.

A good share of them are inside an IB continuum, with children in the Primary Years Programme, the Middle Years Programme and the Diploma at different stages of the same school or the same group of schools. A continuum is a genuinely coherent thing and it is also three different assessment systems in a row, and parents are handed each one without being told how it relates to the last.

The result is a specific pattern of worry. In the primary years, reporting is descriptive and carries no percentage, so a parent cannot tell whether a child is comfortable or coping. In the middle years, work comes back as criterion levels out of eight converted into a 1 to 7, and a parent who does not know which criterion dragged the grade cannot help. Then DP1 arrives and assumes a depth of content the middle years deliberately did not reach, and a student who was strong in MYP 5 has a hard autumn for reasons nobody has explained.

None of those are failures of the school. They are joins, and joins are where support is cheap and effective if it arrives on time. Four sessions in MYP 3 on how to read a criterion descriptor change two years of work. Six to ten weeks of mathematics content over the summer before DP1 removes a problem that otherwise persists to the mock examinations. The same work bought in DP2 costs more and achieves less.

So this page maps the continuum rather than selling hours. How achievement is reported at each stage and what to ask for instead. What each MYP criterion becomes in the Diploma. The content gap from MYP 5 to DP1, subject by subject, with the weeks it takes to close. What is worth buying at each stage and what is a waste. And how a household with three children at three stages arranges one evening, which is the practical problem in Al Yasmeen more often than any academic one.

On delivery: tuition here is one-to-one online over live video, on booked slots in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in the UAE, and home visiting is a service we run in India only. For a family with children at three stages, that matters arithmetically - four short sessions across a week cost four hours of screen time and no travel, where a visiting arrangement would cost four journeys.

ajman/al-yasmeen.programmesIntro: Four routes appear in Al Yasmeen households, and the first three are usually the same school. The notes below are written as a sequence rather than as a menu, because the useful thing to know about any stage is what the next one will assume.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units rather than subject chapters, with children explaining their reasoning aloud from an early age. The strength is real: PYP students arrive in the middle years able to discuss a problem rather than only answer it. The gap that shows up later is arithmetic fluency and written method, because deliberate practice volume is lower than in a traditional British or Indian-curriculum primary.
programmes.countryNote: An Al Yasmeen family with a child in PYP has the easiest scheduling in the district, and should use it. Two half-hour sessions a week on number facts and written method, taken at the dining table straight after the bus, are worth more than a weekly hour and far more than the same work bought in Year 7. Short and frequent is not a compromise at this age; it is the correct dose.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, converted to a 1 to 7 against published boundaries. The criteria are the whole assessment system: a technically correct answer that ignores the criterion wording scores below a weaker one that addresses it. MYP 5 ends with the personal project, the first substantial piece of work a student plans, executes and documents independently.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman has few MYP schools, so families here have chosen deliberately and usually commute. The highest-value intervention in these years is not subject tutoring. It is four sessions on reading a criterion descriptor and planning an answer against it, taken in MYP 3 while the habit still forms quickly, which pays back through MYP 5 and into the Diploma internal assessments.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, each with an internal assessment marked against named criteria, plus the core of Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The programme builds on MYP habits and raises the content ceiling sharply, which is why a strong MYP 5 student can have a difficult DP1 without anything having gone wrong.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma places near Al Yasmeen mean a commute towards the Emirates Road belt or into Sharjah, and a 6.45am departure with a 4.15pm return. That leaves one evening block for homework, coursework and any tuition, so plans here are finite by design: close the content gap, coach the coursework process before the writing, then mark timed components in DP2 and stop.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: The alternative to MYP 4 and 5 for the same age group, and the route many Al Yasmeen siblings take at a different school. Graded 9 to 1 or A* to G, with tiered entry in several subjects. Students arriving in the Diploma from IGCSE typically have more content depth and less criterion literacy than MYP students, which is the mirror image of the gap described above.
programmes.countryNote: Where one child is in MYP and another in IGCSE - a common arrangement in these streets - the two need genuinely different support, and a household that buys the same thing for both wastes half of it. The IGCSE child needs the entry tier checked and timed papers marked; the MYP child needs criterion literacy. Same house, same evening, different products.

ajman/al-yasmeen.subjectsIntro: Because the requests here span the continuum, this grid runs by stage rather than by level. The descriptions say what the stage assesses and what the next one will assume, which is the information an Al Yasmeen parent is usually missing.

subjects.name: PYP numeracy and written method
subjects.description: Number facts to automaticity, column method, fractions as quantities rather than as rules. The aim is fluency, which is what the middle years quietly assume and what descriptive reporting does not measure. Two half-hour sessions a week beat one hour, because the binding constraint at this age is attention rather than teaching time.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics
subjects.description: Marked against knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is where strong arithmetic students lose levels: finding a rule is not enough, it has to be justified. That justification habit becomes the Diploma exploration, so it is worth building early.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.description: Inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, knowing and understanding, and reflecting on impacts. The design and evaluation criteria are the direct ancestors of the Diploma individual investigation, and students who learn to critique their own method in MYP 4 start DP1 ahead on the criterion most candidates mishandle.

subjects.name: MYP Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text and using language, each marked out of eight. The analysing criterion asks how a text produces an effect, not what it says, and that distinction is the single most transferable skill in the continuum: it is the same demand the Diploma unseen paper makes under timing.

subjects.name: MYP Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Students collect case studies and describe them; the critical-thinking criterion asks them to weigh and judge. That is the gap between an MYP 5 level 6 and a Diploma History or Economics essay, and it closes with practice on marked questions rather than with more content.

subjects.name: IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route that exposes any algebraic gap left by the middle years, because Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and the content assumes fluency from day one. Radians, function transformations and introductory calculus arrive in the first DP1 term, which is why the summer before is the right time to close the gap.

subjects.name: IB Chemistry
subjects.description: Where the MYP-to-Diploma content jump is largest. MYP sciences cover reactions qualitatively; DP1 opens with the mole concept at depth, then energetics and equilibrium. The individual investigation then asks for exactly the evaluation habit MYP sciences taught, which is the one piece of good news in the transition.

subjects.name: IB English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two written papers, an individual oral and, at Higher Level, an essay on a studied work. The unseen paper rewards the MYP analysing criterion performed at speed and without support. Students who were strong in MYP Language and Literature usually have the skill and not the timing, which is a practice problem rather than a teaching one.

subjects.name: Arabic, as a first and as an additional language
subjects.description: Compulsory in UAE private schools under federal rules whatever international curriculum a school teaches, and the subject with the least home support in non-Arabic-speaking households. KHDA's guidance for Dubai requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, which indicates how differently the two streams are pitched.

modes.description: Short sessions on number facts, written method and reading fluency, placed straight after the bus while an adult is nearby. The dose matters more than the content at this age: half an hour of focused practice three times a week builds automaticity that one weekly hour does not, because the gaps between sessions are where forgetting happens.

sections.heading: Who lives in Al Yasmeen, and why the continuum question comes up here
paragraphs: The households in these villa streets are planners. They bought or took long leases in a newer community, they have more than one child, and they chose a school on the basis of what it offers across a decade rather than a year. That is a different customer from the one most tutoring pages are written for, and it asks better questions.

The questions sound like this. My daughter's primary report says she is meeting expectations, but what does that mean in numbers? My son's MYP grade went from a 6 to a 5 and the comment says he needs to develop his analysis, which I do not know how to help with. My eldest was excellent in MYP 5 and is finding DP1 chemistry difficult, and nobody can tell me whether that is normal. All three are reasonable questions and none of them is about finding a tutor.

What makes them hard to answer is that each stage of a continuum uses a different measuring instrument, and the school explains each one in isolation. Descriptive reporting in the primary years is pedagogically sound and tells a parent nothing about fluency. Criterion levels in the middle years are precise and arrive without the breakdown that makes them actionable. Diploma predictions blend coursework and papers into one number. Each is defensible; the sequence is opaque.

The practical effect in Al Yasmeen is that support gets bought late and in the wrong shape. A family that would have benefited from four sessions on criterion reading in MYP 3 buys weekly subject tutoring in MYP 5. A family that needed six weeks of algebra before DP1 buys a Higher Level chemistry tutor in February of DP2. The teaching in both cases is fine. The timing costs several times what it needed to.

sections.heading: How work is reported at each stage, and what to ask for instead
paragraphs: The single most useful habit for a continuum parent is to stop reading the headline and ask for the layer underneath it. Every stage produces more information than the report shows, and the underlying layer is where an action sits. A descriptive comment hides whether a child is fluent or merely accurate. A 1 to 7 hides which of four criteria is weak. A predicted grade hides whether the risk is in the coursework or in the papers.

The requests that get useful answers are specific. In the primary years, ask for evidence of number-fact fluency and written method rather than for effort grades: can she recall multiplication facts without counting, and does her column method survive a carry? In the middle years, ask for the criterion breakdown behind the 1 to 7 and for a piece of marked work next to the descriptor that produced the level. In the Diploma, ask for the internal assessment mark and the paper marks separately.

The table below sets those out stage by stage. It is written to be taken to a parents' evening, and the third column is the one worth reading first: it names what each reporting format conceals. A parent who knows what is missing asks a better question in the eight minutes a teacher has, and gets something actionable rather than reassurance.

One addition that applies at every stage. Ask for the script back after a mock or an internal test, with the mark scheme. A grade tells you where a student is; a script tells you which question types returned no marks at all, which is the only information a plan can be built from. Schools will usually provide it if asked, and almost nobody asks.

sections.heading: What each MYP criterion becomes in the Diploma
paragraphs: This mapping is the thing continuum parents most consistently say nobody has shown them, and it is not complicated. The middle years assess four criteria per subject. The Diploma assesses components with their own criteria. The two are related by design: the MYP criteria are the Diploma's demands, taught at a lower content ceiling and with more support. Seeing the relationship changes what a parent does with an MYP report.

Take the sciences as the clearest case. MYP inquiring and designing asks a student to frame a question and plan a method. The Diploma individual investigation's exploration criterion asks the same thing with higher stakes and no scaffolding. MYP processing and evaluating asks a student to handle data and evaluate; the Diploma analysis and evaluation criteria ask the same, and the single most common Diploma error - writing the evaluation as a conclusion - is a habit that forms in MYP 4 and is correctable there in a fortnight.

Mathematics follows the same line. MYP investigating patterns rewards finding and describing a general rule; the Diploma exploration rewards justification and, at the top end, proof. A student who gets used to spotting a pattern and stopping has learnt half the skill. Pushing for justification in MYP 3 is a small intervention that pays off four years later in a component worth a fifth of the subject grade.

The practical use of the table is this. Look at your child's weakest MYP criterion, find the Diploma component it becomes, and buy four sessions on that criterion now rather than a term of subject tutoring later. That is a different purchase from the one most families make, it costs considerably less, and it is the clearest argument this page has for why timing beats intensity.

sections.heading: The MYP 5 personal project as a Diploma rehearsal
paragraphs: The personal project at the end of MYP 5 is the most informative assessment in the middle years and the most under-used by parents. A student chooses a goal, plans it, carries it out, and documents the process against criteria. Nobody tells them what to do. It is, in miniature, exactly what the Extended Essay and the internal assessments will demand two years later, and how a student handles it predicts the Diploma better than any subject grade.

The failure modes are also the same ones. A goal too broad to achieve, which becomes a research question too broad for 4,000 words. Process documentation written at the end from memory, which becomes a CAS portfolio compiled in a weekend. A product that is finished and a reflection that is thin, which becomes an investigation with good data and a weak evaluation. Each is visible in MYP 5 and fixable there at low cost.

What useful support looks like is narrow. Help the student narrow the goal until it is achievable in the time available. Set up a process journal that gets written as the work happens rather than afterwards. Read the criteria with them before they start and again at the halfway point. Then step back, because the project has to be theirs and the school supervises and authenticates it exactly as the Diploma will.

For an Al Yasmeen parent the diagnostic value is the point. If a child manages the personal project with reminders but without rescue, DP1 coursework will probably be fine with the same light touch. If the project only completed because an adult took it over in the last fortnight, that is information worth having two years early, and it changes what the family should buy in DP1 from subject tutoring to process coaching.

sections.heading: The content gap from MYP 5 into DP1, subject by subject
paragraphs: This is the transition that catches good students, and it catches them for a structural reason rather than an academic one. The middle years are deliberately broad and conceptual; the Diploma raises the content ceiling sharply in the first term. A student who finished MYP 5 with level 7s has the skills the Diploma wants and not yet the content it assumes, and the autumn of DP1 moves too fast to go back and fill in.

The gaps are specific enough to list, which is what the table does. In mathematics it is algebraic fluency, radians and the early calculus that DP1 opens with. In chemistry it is the mole concept at depth, then energetics and equilibrium, none of which MYP sciences treat quantitatively at that level. In physics it is vector treatment, uncertainty handling and algebraic derivation. In the humanities it is technique rather than content: diagram discipline in economics, source evaluation in history, unseen analysis under timing in language.

The timing matters more than the amount. Six to ten weeks of targeted work in the summer before DP1 closes most of these gaps, and it is cheap because nothing else is competing for the student's time and no deadline is pressing. The same work in November costs more sessions, because the course has moved on and the student is now carrying both the gap and the current content. By February of DP2 it is remediation rather than preparation.

One piece of advice that saves families the most money on this page: ask the receiving school in MYP 5 which content it assumes in the first term of each Diploma subject your child intends to take. Some schools publish a bridging list. Where they do not, the subject teacher will usually say in two minutes, and that two minutes tells you exactly what to buy and for how long.

sections.heading: What is worth buying at each stage, and what is not
paragraphs: A continuum lasts a decade and a family cannot buy tutoring across all of it, so the question is where the money does most work. The answer is counter-intuitive: the highest-return purchases are small, early and skill-based, and the most common purchases are large, late and subject-based. Market rates make the arithmetic worse, because the late purchases are also the expensive ones.

Those rates, for reference, read in October 2026 from providers' own pages: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at the budget end; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist support; Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to 450 and above and in-home visits at AED 180 to 350. None of those is IB Gram's price, which follows a free trial lesson and a consultation.

Read the table's middle column as carefully as the first. Four sessions on criterion literacy in MYP 3, at the qualified-tutor band, cost a fraction of a term of Higher Level support in DP2 and prevent part of the need for it. A primary child's half-hours sit in the budget band and are the right use of it, because the task is practice supervision rather than specialist teaching. Specialist rates belong where specialist judgement is needed: coursework criteria and marked components.

What is a waste is just as worth naming. Hour-long weekly sessions for an eight-year-old, because attention runs out at about half that. Subject tutoring for a child who is simply young in the year group. General revision with no criterion or mark scheme attached. And weekly tuition in all six Diploma subjects, which consumes the evening block that independent work needs and spreads attention so thin that nothing moves.

sections.heading: Three children, three stages, one evening
paragraphs: The scheduling problem in Al Yasmeen is not finding an hour, it is finding three or four and placing them where they do not collide. A household with a child in PYP, one in MYP and one in DP1 has three different dose requirements, three different attention windows and one set of adults. Most families solve it by accident and end up over-serving the youngest and under-serving the eldest.

The arrangement that works puts each child where their attention actually is. The primary child takes half an hour straight after the bus, while an adult is in the kitchen within earshot and the house is not yet loud. The middle-years child takes an hour in the early evening, before the household peaks. The Diploma student takes the later slot, after the commute and after food, when the apartment or villa is quietest and the work needs concentration rather than supervision.

The weekend carries a different kind of session. Friday afternoons and Saturdays are when a decision can be made rather than a skill practised, which makes them the right slots for a personal project plan, a research question, or a marked paper reviewed with a parent present. Keeping those out of the weekday evening removes most of the collision.

This is also where the delivery question stops being philosophical. Four sessions across a week delivered online cost four hours of screen time and no travel at all. The same four sessions from visiting tutors cost four journeys, four arrivals and four doorstep conversations, and in practice one of them is always late. IB Gram does not offer home visiting in the UAE in any case - that service runs in India only - but for a multi-stage household the arithmetic is the honest reason rather than the policy.
