sections.heading: Trialling properly, and the limits of what any tutor can do
paragraphs: A trial lesson is usually treated as a sample and is better used as a test. The useful trial has the student's most recent marked paper or current draft in front of the tutor, not a generic worksheet, because what you are evaluating is diagnosis rather than charm. A tutor who can look at a marked script and name three specific recurring losses in forty minutes has demonstrated the thing you are buying.

Four things are worth watching. Whether the tutor asks for the evidence before offering a plan. Whether the student talks, or is talked at for an hour. Whether anything is written down and sent afterwards. And whether the tutor says anything inconvenient, because a provider who never disagrees with a parent in a first conversation is managing a sale rather than a student.

Then there are the honest limits. No tutor can promise a grade, because the examination is marked by the board and the work is the student's. No tutor can recover marks already locked into a submitted internal assessment. No tutor can produce the work that must be the student's own, and any offer to do so puts the qualification at risk rather than helping it. No tutor can fix in six weeks what two years produced, though paper discipline in six weeks is worth real marks near a threshold.

And there is availability, which almost nobody in this market discloses. For a narrow Higher Level combination, a minority language or coursework supervision in a short window, there may be no suitable specialist free when a family needs one. The honest options are a different slot, a wait, or a recommendation to look elsewhere. We will say which applies rather than putting a generalist into a specialist seat, which is the failure a family discovers too late to fix.

process.title: Shortlist by what is already visible
process.description: Remove any provider showing a rating with no dated reviews, a promise about a final grade, a claimed regulator approval, a statistic with no sample size, or a non-UAE contact number on a UAE page. That usually halves the list before you speak to anybody.

process.title: Ask the eight questions
process.description: Subjects and levels taught, where marks are lost, what they will not do with assessed work, what you receive in writing, what happens when they cannot cover something, the permit, a relevant reference, and how to end the arrangement. Twenty minutes, and the answers sort themselves.

process.title: Trial on the real material
process.description: One free session, with no card details taken, using your child's most recent marked paper or current draft rather than a generic exercise. You are testing whether the tutor can diagnose from evidence, which is the whole of what you are buying.

process.title: Commit to a small block, in writing
process.description: A defined number of sessions with an agreed end point and a stated way out. Nothing about a good arrangement requires a long minimum commitment, and a provider confident in the work does not need one.

process.title: Review against the evidence, not the relationship
process.description: At the end of the block, compare the agreed end point with the starting position. Continue, change focus, change tutor or stop. A provider who has made the exit easy from the start makes this a decision rather than a confrontation.

whyPoints.title: We publish no rating
whyPoints.description: There is no countable, dated, attributable review set behind a number we could honestly print, so we print none. If that changes, the figure will appear with its sample size and date, which is the only form in which a rating means anything.

whyPoints.title: We claim no accreditation
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no licence, accreditation or partnership from the IB, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or Cambridge. Those bodies regulate schools and qualifications. A provider implying otherwise is making a claim worth testing.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits stated, not hidden
whyPoints.description: For a narrow Higher Level combination or a minority language there may be nobody suitable free in the window you want. We will say so and suggest where else to look rather than placing a generalist and letting the term reveal it.

whyPoints.title: A line on assessed work we will not move
whyPoints.description: The student chooses the question, does the work and writes every sentence. We teach skills on other examples, read what exists and ask questions. We decline requests to supply text for an internal assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay.

whyPoints.title: Specialists reachable from a small emirate
whyPoints.description: Because teaching is online, the pool for a specific subject and level is national rather than limited to who will travel into Ajman on a weekday evening. In a thin local market that is the difference between a specialist and a substitute.

whyPoints.title: An exit stated before you commit
whyPoints.description: A defined block, an agreed end point and a way out without penalty. Making it easy to leave is the clearest signal a provider can give about its confidence in the work, which is why it is worth asking every provider for it.

faqs.question: Is there an official ranking of IB tutors anywhere in the UAE?
faqs.answer: No. No authority assesses or ranks individual tutors, no register of tutor quality exists, and no published comparison is based on measured student outcomes. Regulators oversee schools and qualifications rather than private tutors, and the permit regime covers the right to tutor rather than the standard of teaching. So any page answering a superlative search directly is advertising. The practical substitute is a short set of checkable questions plus a trial session using your child's own marked work, which produces better information than any ranking could.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor in the first five minutes?
faqs.answer: Two things. Which subjects have you taught, at which level, and in which years. Then: where do students most often lose marks in that subject. The first answer should be specific rather than a list of curricula; the second cannot be improvised by anyone who has not marked student work, because a real answer names question types and mark allocations rather than recommending more past papers. If both answers are strong, the rest of the vetting is worth doing. If either is vague, you have saved yourself an hour.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor has genuinely taught at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Ask for the subject, the level and the years, then ask a level-specific question and listen to the answer. For Analysis and Approaches, ask what separates Higher Level from Standard Level in the papers. For a science, ask what the internally assessed investigation needs that a Standard Level student finds hardest. Then ask for one reference from a parent whose child took that subject at that level. A general testimonial is not evidence about your subject, and a provider claiming a specialism should be able to produce one relevant name.

faqs.question: Does calling a tutor an examiner mean anything I can verify?
faqs.answer: Rarely. Current examiner status is a contractual relationship with a board, it changes year to year, and a parent usually cannot check it independently. A collective claim that a provider's tutors are examiners, with nobody named and no year given, cannot be tested at all. Examining also confers no access to unreleased papers, marking in progress or grade boundaries, which are set after papers are marked. Ask instead how many years they have taught the subject at that level and whether they have marked work against that mark scheme.

faqs.question: A provider shows a high star rating with many reviews. Should I trust it?
faqs.answer: Treat it as decoration unless the reviews are dated, named and countable. There is no independent review platform for UAE tutoring with verified transactions behind it, so most figures are self-published by the party they flatter. In this market, rating figures have appeared that contradict another figure on the same page, and review counts that do not reconcile with claimed student numbers. A rating that differs between the visible page and the structured data behind it can also be discounted by search engines. Ask for one relevant reference instead.

faqs.question: An advert promises a specific final score. What does that tell me?
faqs.answer: That the provider is promising something it does not control. The examination is marked by the board, internal work is moderated externally, and the work itself is the student's. A promise about a final grade, about a fixed improvement, or a refund tied to a result is a commitment nobody in this position can honour, and the fact that it was made tells you how the provider handles claims in general. Our pages say what tuition can realistically move and over what period, which is a less exciting statement and a true one.

faqs.question: Is an agency better than an independent tutor for IB subjects?
faqs.answer: Neither is better in general; they fail differently. An agency gives you a pool, which matters for an unusual subject and level, plus some process, and it risks tutor rotation and a gap between the profile and the person who turns up. An independent tutor can be the strongest relationship available and carries no institutional backup, so the permit question, the record-keeping question and the reference question matter more. Decide by the failure you would least tolerate, and get the replacement or notice arrangement in writing either way.

faqs.question: What does it mean if a UAE tutoring page lists a foreign phone number?
faqs.answer: Usually that the support, and sometimes the teaching, is not where the page implies. Two providers ranking for these searches route UAE parents to numbers outside the country, and one shows a Dubai address on a page aimed at another emirate. Neither is automatically disqualifying, but both are things to ask about directly: where are the tutors based, where is the support team, and what hours do they work in Gulf Standard Time. A provider that is straightforward about it has nothing to hide; one that is evasive has answered the question.

faqs.question: How many trial sessions should we take before committing?
faqs.answer: One properly run trial is usually enough to judge diagnosis, and two sessions is enough to judge whether the student engages. Use the real material: the most recent marked paper or the current draft, not a generic worksheet. Watch four things. Does the tutor ask for the evidence before proposing a plan. Does the student talk. Does anything arrive in writing afterwards. And does the tutor say anything inconvenient, because a first conversation with no disagreement in it is a sales conversation.

faqs.question: Should I ask whether a tutor holds a private tutoring permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the reaction matters as much as the answer. The private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible categories including school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule of amounts. Since the permit costs nothing, dismissing the question tells you about attitude rather than about cost.

faqs.question: Can I ask for a reference from another parent?
faqs.answer: Yes, and ask for a specific one: a parent whose child took the same subject at the same level with the same tutor. Three questions are enough. Did the same person teach throughout. What did you receive in writing after each session. Would you book again. A provider claiming depth in a subject should be able to produce one relevant name, and a testimonial page with no subjects or levels attached is not a substitute. If no relevant reference exists, that is itself information about the claimed specialism.

faqs.question: Is the most expensive tutor usually the strongest?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, in a market with no independent quality signal. Published rates in this country run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget end to AED 650 at the top, with qualified online tuition around AED 150 to 300 and specialist work from AED 200 to 450 and above. That span reflects business models and positioning as much as capability. Price does correlate with scarcity: a genuine specialist in a narrow Higher Level subject costs more because few people can do it. Pay for the scarcity, having tested it, rather than for the position on a rate card.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram claim to be accredited by the IB or by KHDA?
faqs.answer: No, and it is worth being explicit. IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence, registration or partnership from the IB, from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE as an organisation, Cambridge or Pearson. Those bodies regulate schools, qualifications and, in the case of a Dubai training institute with premises, a specific educational services permit. None of that is a general endorsement of a tutoring provider, and no tutoring provider can hold one. Any page implying otherwise is making a claim a parent should ask it to evidence.

faqs.question: Would the strongest IB tutor for our child be someone based in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Possibly for a mainstream subject, and much less likely for a specific Higher Level combination. Ajman is a small emirate, few of its schools run the full Diploma, and the local pool of people who have taught a named subject at Higher Level is thin. Insisting on proximity in that situation means choosing availability over expertise without necessarily realising it. Our teaching is delivered one-to-one over live video, so the match is made nationally on subject and level. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India.

faqs.question: What should make us end an arrangement rather than persevere?
faqs.answer: Four things. Nothing arrives in writing, so the hours cannot be audited. The same person is not teaching each week without that having been agreed. A second marked attempt at the same question type shows no movement although the between-session work was done. Or the tutor offers, at any point, to produce part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay. The last one is immediate and non-negotiable, because the risk falls on your child's qualification rather than on the provider's reputation.

ajman/best-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Replace the ranking with a test you can run yourself
ajman/best-ib-tutor.closingBody: There is no best IB tutor in Ajman in any measurable sense, and a page claiming the title has told you about its advertising rather than its teaching. What there is, is a short test: eight questions that a specialist answers specifically and a generalist cannot, a handful of warning signs visible before you make contact, and one trial session judged on diagnosis rather than on manner. Run it on us and on everyone else you are considering. Send your child's most recent marked paper, take the free trial with no card details taken, and judge the written note that follows against anything else you receive.

ajman/best-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are IGCSE subject specialists who teach to a named syllabus code rather than to a general idea of maths or science. Each works one-to-one over live video, and each will mark a baseline past paper before the first full lesson is planned.

intro.heading: The word "best" is doing a lot of work in that search
paragraphs: An IGCSE tutor is only good relative to a specific syllabus, a specific paper and a specific gap. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 cover similar ground, but they are tiered differently, structured differently and marked to different schemes. A tutor who is excellent on one and guessing at the other is not the right match, however impressive the degree. The first question worth asking any tutor is which code they teach to, and the second is what they do in week one.

Ajman adds a practical constraint. Private schools here sit under the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level regulator, the private-school set is small, and a large share of households work in Dubai or Sharjah. That combination produces two effects a tutoring plan has to respect. Specialist subject teachers for the harder Extended papers are thin on the ground locally, and a weekday session realistically starts after 6.30pm once a parent has cleared Emirates Road.

The honest answer to scarcity is not to pretend otherwise. IB Gram matches Ajman families to subject specialists who teach over live video, one-to-one. That removes the radius problem entirely: a child in Al Mowaihat taking Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 Extended gets a physics specialist rather than the nearest generalist who can drive over. Home visits are a service IB Gram offers only in India, and this page makes that explicit rather than burying it.

What follows is the detail a parent needs to run the decision themselves. Which tier your child is entered for and what it caps their grade at. Which papers they sit and how long each one is. Where the marks actually leak in each subject, named by topic. What the market charges in AED per hour across the provider models in this part of the UAE. The exam calendar read backwards from the paper to the entry deadline, because the deadline is months earlier than most families expect. And the five-subject rule the Ministry of Education applies when it looks at an IGCSE certificate for equivalency.

There is one more thing worth saying before the detail starts. The pages competing for this search average about 2,300 words and most publish no price, no exam date and no syllabus code at all. That is not a reason to trust this page instead; it is a reason to check it. Every regulatory statement here is attributable to u.ae, KHDA, MoHRE or the exam board that published it, every AED figure is attributed to the provider or rate table it came from, and anything unverified is marked as unverified rather than smoothed over. IB exam-session dates in particular are not published here, because the IB's own site could not be confirmed directly and a date a family plans around has to come from the school's IB coordinator.

None of it needs a tutor to be useful. If you read the tier table and the mark-loss section and conclude your child needs six focused weeks on one paper rather than a year of weekly sessions, that is a better outcome than a subscription. The page is written so you can tell the difference.

ajman/best-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: IGCSE is one stage in a longer sequence, and Ajman families arrive at it from several directions — a British primary, an Indian-curriculum school that switched boards, or an IB Middle Years Programme. What comes after it matters just as much, because subject choices made in Year 10 close doors in Year 12.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The two-year Cambridge course most British-curriculum schools in the northern emirates run. Subjects are identified by a four-digit code — 0580 Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, 0610 Biology, 0500 English First Language — and each code has its own paper structure and tiering rules. Most subjects are examined entirely by written paper, with coursework an option that few UAE schools take up. Grades are reported on the 9-1 scale in most subjects, with legacy A*-G still appearing on some.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman schools entering candidates through Cambridge are allocated to one of six administrative zones, and the zone determines which version of the timetable applies. Cambridge is explicit that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses a paper because the wrong zone timetable was used, so the exams officer's copy is the only one worth planning against.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The alternative international GCSE, taken by a sizeable minority of schools across the UAE. Codes run 4MA1 for Mathematics A, 4PH1 for Physics, 4CH1 for Chemistry, 4BI1 for Biology. Pearson's modular structure lets some subjects be sat across two series rather than one, which changes revision planning considerably. Assessment is by written paper, with a practical-skills paper replacing laboratory assessment in the sciences.
programmes.countryNote: A family moving between Ajman schools can find a child halfway through a Pearson course arriving at a Cambridge centre, or the reverse. The topic overlap is high and the paper conventions are not. A term of targeted work on command terms and mark-scheme phrasing usually closes more of that gap than fresh content teaching does.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The IB's middle-school framework, assessed against four criteria per subject on a 1-8 scale rather than by terminal examination. Students at an IB continuum school in or near Ajman reach the end of MYP Year 5 at the same age their British-curriculum neighbours finish IGCSE, and families comparing the two routes often ask which is better preparation for the Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students in the northern emirates sometimes transfer into an IGCSE cohort mid-course. The criterion-based habit of mind travels well into coursework, less well into a timed written paper. The usual gap is examination technique rather than content: pacing a 90-minute paper, reading a command term precisely, showing method for method marks.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two-year programme many strong IGCSE candidates in Ajman move into, locally or at a school in Sharjah or Dubai. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Higher Level sciences and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches assume a confident Extended-tier IGCSE background, which is why tier choice at 14 matters more than it looks.
programmes.countryNote: An Ajman student planning a Diploma needs Extended-tier mathematics and at least two Extended sciences to keep Higher Level options open. A Core entry is not fatal, but it means a bridging summer. Flagging that in Year 10 rather than Year 11 is one of the more useful things a tutor does.

ajman/best-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Ajman families ask about most often, with the syllabus code and the specific place marks tend to go. Codes are given for Cambridge; the Pearson equivalent is named where the structure differs enough to matter.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two papers at each tier. Extended Paper 2 and Paper 4 reach into functions, vectors, differentiation and histograms with unequal class widths, none of which appears on Core. The repeated mark loss is method marks thrown away by not writing the working, and the unit error in volume and surface-area questions.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for Higher Level maths. Introduces calculus, logarithms, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities a year before most curricula do. Students who coped with 0580 by pattern-matching questions tend to stall here, because 0606 asks for a method chosen rather than recalled.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetic induction account for a disproportionate share of lost marks, followed by the practical-skills paper. Graph questions where a gradient has to be interpreted as a physical quantity with units are the single most reliable predictor of grade on the Extended tier.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations, electrolysis half-equations and organic reaction pathways carry the Extended grade. The common failure is not understanding electrolysis but losing state symbols and balancing on half-equations, which is a drill problem rather than a comprehension one.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: A content-heavy syllabus where the marks are lost in extended-response questions on transport, homeostasis and inheritance. Examiners want precise terminology — diffusion against active transport, osmosis described with water potential — and award nothing for a near-miss synonym.

subjects.name: English First Language (0500)
subjects.description: Reading paper 1 and writing paper 2, with directed writing and a composition. Marks go on structure and register rather than vocabulary. Students with strong spoken English routinely underperform because they answer the question they expected rather than the one printed in the task.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Listening, reading and writing components, with the speaking endorsement separately reported. The Extended tier asks for summary writing under a word limit, which rewards editing discipline. Many Ajman candidates sit this alongside Arabic as a first language.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Two papers, both case-study driven. The grade is decided by evaluation marks, not knowledge marks: a candidate who defines working capital correctly and never judges whether a decision was sound caps out in the middle bands. Application to the named business in the case study is non-negotiable.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Multiple choice plus structured data response. Diagram accuracy carries real marks — axes labelled, curves shifted in the right direction, the new equilibrium marked. UAE students often have good contextual knowledge of trade and oil markets and lose marks on the mechanics of a supply shift.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Paper 1 theory and Paper 2 algorithms and programming. Pseudocode conventions are assessed, so a student who codes fluently in Python can still lose marks writing pseudocode. Data representation, especially hexadecimal and two's complement, is a predictable weak point.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508)
subjects.description: Runs alongside the international curriculum as a federally mandated subject in UAE private schools. Standard Arabic is the language of instruction and assessment. Grammar and classical comprehension are where non-native-household Arab students lose marks, rather than vocabulary.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Three papers including a geographical skills paper and an alternative-to-coursework option. Case-study recall is where the grade sits: examiners reward specific named places with figures, not generic examples. Map and cross-section skills are trainable in a handful of sessions.

ajman/best-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Ajman is compact, which makes the geography less about distance and more about when a session can realistically start. These notes reflect what families in each area tell us about school runs, commutes and the realistic weekday window.

regions.note: Dense, long-established and close to the Sharjah boundary. Families here often have one parent commuting to Sharjah industrial areas, so the practical session window is 6pm to 9pm on weekdays and mid-morning on Saturdays.

regions.note: Central Ajman with a mix of towers and villas near the Corniche. Short school runs, so afternoon sessions at 4.30pm are genuinely available here in a way they are not for Dubai-commuting households.

regions.note: Villa communities spread across Al Mowaihat 1, 2 and 3, popular with families at the larger Ajman private schools. Expect Extended-tier science and maths requests concentrated in Years 10 and 11.

regions.note: Residential and quiet, with a high proportion of Indian and Pakistani curriculum families who have switched a child to IGCSE mid-stage. Board-transition work is the most common request from this area.

regions.note: High-rise towers with a largely expatriate population and frequent mid-year school moves. Students arriving in Year 11 from another board are the recurring case, and they need paper technique before content.

Schools here are overseen by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority, which is why inspection reporting looks different from KHDA's Dubai model.

schoolClusters.note: A large number of Ajman families drive a child into Sharjah for school, which means the school day finishes later and the realistic tutoring window shifts back by an hour. These schools come up repeatedly in conversations with Ajman households.

ajman/best-igcse-tutor.modesIntro: Three shapes of support cover almost every IGCSE request we take from Ajman. The difference between them is not price per hour but how the hours are distributed, and that distribution is what decides whether a grade moves.

modes.description: One or two sessions a week on a single subject, running alongside school. The tutor works from the school's scheme of work and the student's returned class assessments, so the session targets what was actually taught that fortnight rather than a generic syllabus order. This is the default for Year 10 and the first half of Year 11.

Ends with a marked section of a real past paper

sections.heading: How to test whether a tutor is actually good at IGCSE
paragraphs: A good IGCSE tutor can tell you, in the first conversation, which syllabus code your child is entered for, which papers that code involves, and what the tier caps the grade at. If that exchange turns vague, the rest of the conversation does not matter. Everything else — the university they attended, the years of experience, the testimonials — is weaker evidence than a precise answer about 0620 Paper 4 or 4MA1 Paper 2H.

The second test is the first lesson. A tutor who opens by teaching is guessing. A tutor who opens by having the student attempt a section of a real past paper, then marks it against the published scheme and shows the parent where the marks went, has evidence. That distinction matters most in Ajman, where the local specialist pool is small and families are sometimes choosing between a general science graduate and nobody.

The third test is what happens to assessed work. IGCSE has far less coursework than it once did, but where it exists, the boundary is absolute: the work is the student's. A tutor may teach the skill, discuss a plan, and give feedback on a draft the student produced. Any offer that goes further than feedback is a malpractice risk for the student, not a service.

Finally, ask what the tutor does when progress stalls. The useful answer names a diagnostic step — re-marking an earlier paper, changing the question type, moving from content to technique. An answer that amounts to more hours is a billing strategy.
bullets: Ask for the syllabus code before you ask for a rate
Expect a marked baseline paper in week one, not a lecture
Check the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit
Agree what a six-week review will measure before you start

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the tier that sets your child's grade ceiling
paragraphs: Several Cambridge IGCSE subjects are tiered, and the tier decides the highest grade available. Core papers cap at grade C on the legacy scale or 5 on the 9-1 scale. Extended papers reach A* or 9. Schools make the entry decision, usually in Year 10, and parents are frequently unaware it has been made at all until a report arrives with a grade that looks capped because it is.

The decision is not only about ability. A student entered for Core in mathematics has a lighter content load, sits different papers, and is examined on a syllabus that stops short of calculus-adjacent material. That can be the right call for a student taking nine subjects who needs a solid pass. It is the wrong call for a student who intends to take Higher Level Mathematics in an IB Diploma or A-Level Mathematics afterwards, because the entry assumptions for those courses are Extended-tier.

Moving tiers is possible but time-bound. The entry is made by the centre ahead of the final entry deadline for the series, which sits months before the paper. A student who wants to move from Core to Extended for a June series needs the conversation with the school in the autumn term, not in March. That calendar reality is the single most useful thing a parent can take from this page.

Where a tier change is agreed, the content gap is real but narrower than it looks. In mathematics it is typically a defined list of topics rather than a different subject. Six to ten focused sessions on that list, plus timed practice on the Extended paper format, is the usual shape of the work.

sections.heading: The papers your child actually sits, and how long each one is
paragraphs: Most Ajman families can name their child's subjects and almost none can name the papers. That is a problem, because revision planned against a subject is vague and revision planned against a paper is specific. A student revising Chemistry is doing something unmeasurable. A student revising for 0620 Paper 4 — the Extended theory paper, the one carrying the moles calculations and the organic pathways — is doing something that can be practised and marked.

Paper structures differ between boards in ways that change technique more than content. Cambridge science Extended candidates sit a multiple-choice paper, a structured theory paper and a practical-skills paper. Pearson's International GCSE sciences fold the practical assessment into the written papers differently. A student who has practised on the wrong board's past papers for a term has practised the wrong question stems, and question stems are where command terms live.

The practical question comes up constantly from families considering online tuition. For most private candidates and online learners in the UAE, laboratory practical work is assessed by a written practical-skills paper rather than by a supervised experiment. That paper rewards experimental reasoning, graph plotting and error analysis — all of which can be taught properly over a shared screen, and all of which are routinely under-practised in school because laboratory time goes on the experiment itself.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Mark loss at IGCSE is rarely about not knowing the content. It concentrates in a small number of repeatable behaviours, and that is good news, because repeatable behaviours respond to practice far faster than missing knowledge does. A student who drops eleven marks across a mathematics paper by not writing working is not a weak mathematician; they are losing method marks a mark scheme would have given them.

Command terms are the second recurring leak. State, describe, explain, compare, evaluate and justify ask for structurally different answers, and mark schemes allocate accordingly. A student who explains when asked to describe is wasting time; one who describes when asked to explain is leaving marks on the table. Twenty minutes with a mark scheme and a highlighter usually produces more improvement than a month of content revision.

The third is data and graph work, across every science and both social sciences. Plotting accurately, drawing a line of best fit rather than joining the dots, reading a gradient, converting the gradient into a physical quantity with the correct unit — these are assessed explicitly and taught quickly. They also transfer: the same skill set earns marks in Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Geography and Economics.

The fourth is timing. Candidates who have never sat a full paper under timed conditions discover in the hall that the last extended-response question, worth six or eight marks, gets four minutes. The fix is uncomfortable and simple: full papers, timed, marked, with the timing failure discussed as a tactical problem rather than a personal one.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tutoring costs in Ajman — the AED market, not our price list
paragraphs: Most pages ranking for tutoring queries in the UAE publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no family here transacts in. The figures below are market rates gathered from competitors' own published pages and from Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table for 2026. They are the market. IB Gram's own position is a free trial lesson first and a quote after the diagnostic, because a Year 11 Extended Chemistry rescue and a Year 10 weekly maths slot are not the same piece of work.

Ajman sits below Dubai on rate, and the gap is real but smaller than families expect — perhaps ten to fifteen per cent at the qualified-tutor end. What differs more is availability. The budget end of the market in Ajman is dominated by university students and recent graduates, and the specialist end is thin, so a household that wants an Extended Physics specialist is often choosing between a long drive and a video call regardless of price.

The in-home premium is the figure worth examining. Market rates for an in-home visit run roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. Some of that gap is travel time priced in. The rest is scarcity: the pool of tutors willing to drive to Al Helio for a 7pm session is a fraction of the pool available over video, and a smaller pool prices higher for the same quality.

Monthly packages are common across the market. Figures seen include AED 799 per month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 per month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against a tutor at the door in Ajman
paragraphs: IB Gram does not provide in-person tutoring in Ajman or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Saying so plainly is more useful than hedging, because it lets the comparison be made on merits rather than on sales pressure. For an Ajman family the comparison usually resolves in one of two directions, and which one depends almost entirely on how specialised the subject is.

For a general Year 10 subject where many competent tutors exist within a fifteen-minute drive, an in-home tutor has genuine advantages: no technology to manage, a parent in the next room, and a younger student who stays on task more easily. Families of students in Years 7 to 9 often prefer it, and that preference is reasonable.

For Extended-tier sciences, 0606 Additional Mathematics, or a student eight weeks from a series, the calculation inverts. The specialist who has marked three hundred 0625 practical-skills papers is probably not living in Al Jurf. Over video, geography stops being a filter. A shared screen also does things a kitchen table does not: an annotated past paper saved and revisited, a mark scheme side by side with the student's answer, a recorded explanation of the one calculation they keep failing.

The honest weakness of online delivery is engagement with younger or less self-directed students, and it is managed rather than denied — shorter sessions, a visible plan, written parent updates, and a trial lesson before any money changes hands so the family can judge the format on their own child rather than on a claim.

sections.heading: The exam calendar read backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Nearly every tutoring page in this market talks about exam preparation and none of them names a session, a registration deadline or a results date. That omission matters, because the deadline that constrains a family's options is almost always the entry deadline, and it falls months before the paper. A tier change, a subject addition or a private-candidate entry all have to clear it.

Cambridge offers IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in two series a candidate sitting in Ajman can actually enter: June and November. The February and early-March sitting that turns up in a lot of search results is an India-only arrangement and is not available here, and the Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests that run in March, May and October are a different qualification altogether rather than an extra IGCSE window. Read the June series backwards and the shape families get caught by appears immediately. The final entry deadline sits in the spring, months ahead of the first paper. The mock window sits before that again. The exact deadline is held by the school rather than published for parents, which is why the useful thing a family can do in the autumn term is ask the exams officer for it in writing: a tier change, a subject addition or a private-candidate entry all have to clear it, and after it closes the options narrow to the November series.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official PDF is the only version worth planning against.

One Cambridge detail catches UAE centres specifically. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the exams officer which zone the school sits in, and plan from that document.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, and the subject-count rule competitors get wrong
paragraphs: An IGCSE certificate earned in Ajman has to be recognised by the UAE Ministry of Education before it is usable for a UAE university application, and the rule for the British track is published and specific. Students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade.

Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That detail matters because at least one page currently ranking for UAE equivalency queries tells parents that candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. Publishing the correct rule is not a marketing claim; it is the difference between a family planning a subject load correctly and planning it wrong.

For the American track the requirements are different again: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the academic IELTS, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics through at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test. No IB Diploma points threshold is published in the same source, so any figure you see quoted for IB equivalency should be checked directly against moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation channel before you rely on it.

Equivalency is a process the ministry runs, not something a tutoring service performs or can expedite. Nobody should suggest that tutoring is required for it. What a tutor can reasonably do is make sure the five subjects a family is counting on are the five that count, and that the grades clear the floor with room to spare.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, past papers, and the limits of what a tutor may do
paragraphs: This SERP contains at least one operator selling finished Internal Assessments. It is worth naming the boundary clearly, because a family that does not know where the line sits can cross it by accident. Assessed work must be the student's own. A tutor teaches the skill, discusses an outline the student has produced, asks questions about a draft, and gives feedback the student then acts on. A tutor does not author any part of the submitted work, and no legitimate service offers to.

The same principle governs the material a tutor uses. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. They can be referenced, discussed and linked from their official sources. Reproducing them as a downloadable pack is copyright infringement, and for unreleased material it is a malpractice exposure for the student as well as the provider. If a tutor offers to send you a folder of mark schemes, that is a signal about the operation, not a benefit.

There is a staffing boundary too. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. The federal permit applies in Ajman, so a parent asking a current class teacher for paid lessons is asking for something the teacher should decline.

None of this reduces what a tutor can usefully do. Teaching a student to read a mark scheme, to recognise a command term, to show working, to plot a graph that earns its marks — that is the entire job, and it is more than enough to move a grade.
bullets: Feedback on the student's own draft is legitimate; authorship of any part is not

sections.heading: Who oversees schools in Ajman, and what a parent should do about it
paragraphs: Ajman's private schools sit under the federal Ministry of Education, which supervises private schools in the emirates of Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. That is a different arrangement from Dubai, where the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education, and from Abu Dhabi, where the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah has its own body, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ras Al Khaimah has the Department of Knowledge.

The practical consequence for an Ajman family is that inspection reporting and fee approval do not follow the Dubai pattern a lot of UAE tutoring content assumes. A parent moving from Dubai to Ajman should not expect to find a KHDA-style inspection report with the same cadence and framing, and should ask the school directly what its current oversight position is rather than searching for a document that may not exist in that form.

Federal rules do reach into the timetable. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the ministry's general regulations. In practice that means your child is carrying mandatory UAE subjects alongside the IGCSE load, and those subjects compete for the same evening hours as revision. Any tutoring plan that ignores them will be abandoned by November.

Private tutoring itself is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you see quoted with suspicion.

sections.heading: Starting, and what happens when the specialist you need is not free
paragraphs: The first step is a short conversation about the actual problem: subject, syllabus code, tier, what the last assessment showed, and what date the family is working towards. That takes ten minutes and it determines everything else. A Year 10 student drifting in mathematics and a Year 11 student twelve weeks from a June series need different plans, different session lengths and different numbers of hours.

Next comes a free trial lesson. It exists to test the match on your own child rather than on a description. A trial that consists of a tutor talking for an hour has told you very little. A trial where the student attempts real questions and the tutor identifies two specific things to fix has told you most of what you need to know.

Scarcity deserves a straight answer. For some combinations — Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 at the algorithms end, Arabic as a first language at the higher grades — the pool of genuinely specialist tutors available in UAE evening hours is small. When that happens we say so and give a realistic match time rather than filling the slot with a generalist. Where a specialist is only available at a different hour, or where the match takes a week, that is the information a family needs to decide.

After six weeks the plan gets reviewed against evidence: a re-marked paper, the topics that moved, the ones that did not. If the answer is that the student needs fewer sessions, or a different subject, or nothing at all because the problem was timing rather than content, that is the answer we give.
bullets: A ten-minute diagnostic call before anything is scheduled
A free trial lesson, with the condition stated up front: one lesson, one subject
A written plan naming the syllabus code, the tier and the two priority topics
A six-week review against a re-marked paper, not against a feeling

process.title: Tell us the code, not just the subject
process.description: Share the syllabus code, the tier, the school and the date you are working towards. If you do not know the code, the school's exams officer does, and it is worth the email. Everything downstream — tutor match, past-paper selection, revision order — depends on getting this right at the start.

process.title: Baseline a real past paper
process.description: Before teaching begins, the student attempts a section of a genuine past paper for their tier. The tutor marks it against the published scheme and reports where the marks went, by question and by reason. This is the only reliable way to separate a content gap from a technique gap.

process.title: Free trial lesson, one subject
process.description: A full one-to-one lesson over live video at no cost, on the subject you actually need. The condition is simple and stated up front: one lesson, one subject, no card details required. If the match is wrong, say so and we try a different tutor rather than persuading you.

process.title: A weekly plan with two priorities
process.description: The plan names two priority topics rather than eight, sets the session length and slot, and schedules the timed papers. Two topics fixed properly moves a grade; eight topics touched lightly does not. The plan is written down so a parent can check it against what actually happens.

process.title: Six-week review against evidence
process.description: At six weeks the student re-sits a comparable paper and it is marked the same way. The conversation that follows uses the two mark breakdowns, not impressions. Sessions go up, down or stop depending on what the papers show, and stopping is a legitimate outcome.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes, not subject labels
whyPoints.description: Every plan names the board and code — 0580, 0625, 4MA1, 4CH1 — because the paper structure, tiering and mark-scheme conventions differ, and practice material drawn from the wrong board teaches the wrong question stems. A tutor who cannot name the code is not matched to the course.

whyPoints.title: Specialists reachable from Ajman
whyPoints.description: Ajman's local pool for Extended-tier sciences and Additional Mathematics is small. Live video removes the radius constraint, so the match is made on who knows the paper rather than on who can reach Al Mowaihat before 7pm. That is the whole argument for the format.

whyPoints.title: Evening slots built around a Dubai commute
whyPoints.description: Sessions are scheduled in Gulf Standard Time with late-evening slots available, because a large share of Ajman households have a parent returning from Dubai or Sharjah at 6.30pm. A plan that assumes a 4pm start is a plan that gets cancelled twice a month.

whyPoints.title: Marked work, returned with reasons
whyPoints.description: Past-paper work comes back annotated against the published mark scheme, with the loss attributed by question and by cause. Parents get a written note every fourth session. The point is that progress can be checked by someone who is not the tutor.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Coursework and assessed tasks are the student's own. Tutors teach the skill, question a draft and give feedback. Nothing is authored on a student's behalf, and no past papers or mark schemes are redistributed. This is a boundary, not a limitation, and it protects the candidate.

whyPoints.title: Honest answers about availability
whyPoints.description: Where a specialism is thin, we give a realistic match time rather than filling the slot with a generalist. Where the answer is that your child needs six sessions rather than a year, that is what we say. A smaller engagement that works is better business than a larger one that does not.

faqs.question: What actually makes one IGCSE tutor better than another for a student in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Specificity. A tutor who can name the syllabus code, the papers that code involves and the tier ceiling has engaged with your child's actual course. One who talks in general terms about maths or science has not. The second marker is what happens in lesson one: a marked section of a real past paper, with the lost marks attributed by question, beats an hour of teaching aimed at nothing in particular. The third is the plan when progress stalls — a diagnostic change rather than more hours. Qualifications matter less than these three things, and in Ajman, where the local specialist pool is small, they matter more than proximity.

faqs.question: Is my child entered for IGCSE Core or Extended, and how do I find out?
faqs.answer: The school makes the entry, usually during Year 10, and it is not always communicated clearly to parents. Ask the exams officer or head of department directly which tier your child is entered for, by subject. The distinction is consequential: Core caps at grade C, or 5 on the 9-1 scale, while Extended reaches A* or 9. If a report shows a ceiling that looks suspiciously low, a Core entry is the most likely explanation. Tier changes are possible but must clear the final entry deadline, which falls months before the paper, so the conversation belongs in the autumn term.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE grades does an Ajman student need for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E, or grade 3 on the numerical scale, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. Equivalency is a process the ministry runs, not something a tutoring provider performs or can accelerate, and you should confirm current requirements on moe.gov.ae before relying on any third-party summary, including this one.

faqs.question: Do private schools in Ajman follow Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Both appear across the northern emirates, and some schools use different boards for different subjects. The only reliable answer is the one your school gives, because it determines which past papers are useful. Cambridge subjects carry four-digit codes such as 0580 or 0625; Pearson International GCSE codes look like 4MA1 or 4PH1. The structures differ enough to matter — tiering rules, practical assessment, modular entry options — so a term spent practising the wrong board's papers trains the wrong question stems. Ask the exams officer for the code list in writing and keep it.

faqs.question: My daughter is in Year 11 in Al Nuaimiya and sits mocks in January. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: With a marked paper, not with teaching. Have her attempt a full past paper for her tier under timed conditions, then get it marked against the published scheme with the loss attributed question by question. That single exercise usually reveals that the problem is narrower than it felt — two topics and a timing failure rather than a whole syllabus. From there, a six to ten week block built backwards from the mock date, running two priority topics and a timed paper every second week, is the shape that works. Mocks are also useful data rather than a verdict.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects should we put tutoring behind at once?
faqs.answer: One, in most cases, and two at a stretch. A student taking nine subjects already has a full week; adding three tutored subjects produces a timetable nobody keeps and homework nobody completes. Pick the subject where the grade matters most for the next stage, or where the gap is widest, and fix it properly. A subject moved two grades is worth more than three subjects nudged. The exception is a student eight weeks from a series with two specific failing papers, where a short, finite block on each can be justified because it ends.

faqs.question: Does my child's IGCSE certificate use the 9-1 scale or A*-G?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject and the board, and both scales still appear on UAE certificates. Cambridge has moved most subjects to 9-1 reporting while some continue to report A*-G, and the two are not a clean mapping. What matters practically is the tier ceiling rather than the scale label: a Core entry caps at C or 5, an Extended entry reaches A* or 9. For equivalency purposes the ministry's published floor is stated as no less than E or grade 3, which covers both conventions. Check the subject statement the school issues for the precise reporting scale.

faqs.question: How are IGCSE science practical marks assessed if the tutoring is online?
faqs.answer: For most private candidates and online learners in the UAE, laboratory work is assessed by a written practical-skills paper rather than by a supervised experiment. That paper tests experimental design, variable control, graph plotting, error analysis and evaluation of method — all of which teach well over a shared screen, with the student's own graph on the display and the mark scheme beside it. These are also the skills school laboratory time tends to squeeze, because the lesson goes on running the experiment. Confirm with the school which route your child's entry uses, since it varies by board and centre.

faqs.question: How late in the evening can an Ajman session start if we commute back from Dubai?
faqs.answer: Late enough to be realistic. Sessions run in Gulf Standard Time and slots at 7pm, 7.30pm and 8pm are routinely used by Ajman households, because a parent clearing Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road at 6.15pm cannot make a 5pm start. Over live video there is no tutor travel to accommodate either, which is precisely why the late window exists at all. Shorter 45-minute sessions twice a week often survive a commuting schedule better than a single 90-minute block, and weekend mid-mornings are the least cancelled slot of the week.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor cost per hour in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Market rates across the northern emirates run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for a university-student tutor, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel priced in, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an exam-board specialist. Those figures come from competitors' own published pages and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table, not from us. IB Gram's approach is a free trial lesson first and a quote after the diagnostic, because a Year 10 weekly slot and a twelve-week Extended Chemistry rescue are different pieces of work.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my child's IGCSE past papers against the official mark scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the most valuable things a tutor does. Published mark schemes for past series are available from the board's own site, and marking against them shows exactly where credit was available and not taken. The output a parent should expect is not a percentage but an attribution: three marks lost to unwritten method, four to a command-term mismatch, two to units. That breakdown converts into a lesson plan. A score on its own does not, which is why a tutor who returns only a grade is leaving the useful work undone.

faqs.question: Will the tutor send us Cambridge past papers and mark schemes to keep?
faqs.answer: No, and an offer to do so should make you cautious. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the property of Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. They are referenced in lessons and linked from their official sources, which is where you should download them from directly. Redistributing them as a pack is copyright infringement, and for any unreleased material it is also a malpractice exposure that attaches to the candidate. A provider willing to hand over a folder of restricted material is telling you something about how it operates generally.

faqs.question: Who regulates private schools in Ajman, and does that change anything for tutoring?
faqs.answer: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, unlike Dubai where KHDA oversees private education quality, or Abu Dhabi where ADEK handles licensing and accreditation. For a tutoring plan the practical effects are two. Inspection reporting does not follow the Dubai pattern much UAE tutoring content assumes, so ask your school directly about its oversight position. And federal rules require Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the international curriculum, which means those subjects compete for the same evening hours as IGCSE revision and must be planned around.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE tutor working with my child in Ajman need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: An individual providing private tuition in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Those offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so discount any specific amount you see quoted. Asking a prospective tutor whether they hold the permit is a fair and easy question.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody covers IGCSE Additional Maths 0606 when we ask?
faqs.answer: You get told that, with a realistic match time, rather than being given a generalist and finding out in week three. Additional Mathematics is one of the genuinely thin specialisms in UAE evening hours, along with the algorithms end of Computer Science 0478 and higher-grade Arabic as a first language. Where a specialist exists but only at a different hour, we say so and let you decide whether the slot works. Where the wait is a week, we say that too. Disclosing a coverage limit costs a booking occasionally and costs far less than a mismatch discovered late in Year 11.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education counted in the five IGCSE subjects the ministry requires?
faqs.answer: No. The published British-track rule requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. This is worth knowing because at least one page currently ranking for UAE equivalency queries states that candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is not what the requirement says. Your child may still be required to study Arabic and Islamic education under federal school rules — those are separate obligations. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae before building a subject plan around it.

faqs.question: Can IGCSE sessions carry on through Ramadan in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the timing changed rather than the plan abandoned. School hours shorten during Ramadan and household rhythms shift, so sessions commonly move to the early afternoon or to a post-Iftar slot in the evening. Shorter, more frequent sessions work better than long blocks in that period. It matters for Year 11 because the Cambridge and Pearson series do not move, so a month of lost momentum has to be recovered somewhere. Plan the Ramadan schedule a fortnight ahead rather than week by week, and agree which sessions are being paused deliberately.

ajman/best-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the code, the tier and one marked paper
ajman/best-igcse-tutor.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, take the sequence. Find out the syllabus code and the tier your child is entered for. Get a real past paper marked against the published scheme. Read where the marks went. Then decide whether the answer is a year of weekly sessions, a six-week block on two topics, or nothing more than better timing practice. A free trial lesson over live video is available before any payment, and the first conversation is about the diagnosis rather than the package. If the honest answer is that your child needs less support than you expected, that is the answer you will get.

ajman/cambridge-igcse-additional-maths-0.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606 across both papers, with the calculus, circular measure, series and kinematics content that students meet for the first time in this subject. Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time, late enough for an Ajman household where a parent drives back from Sharjah or Dubai.

intro.heading: A report grade is an opinion; a marked 0606 script is data
paragraphs: Most 0606 enquiries from Ajman begin with a number that cannot be acted on. The report says 5, or says 'working below expectation', and that sentence is a professional judgement rather than a measurement. It does not say whether the student cannot differentiate, can differentiate but writes it in a form that forfeits the accuracy mark, or can do both and ran out of time on the second paper. Those are three entirely different problems with three entirely different repairs, and the only document that distinguishes them is a marked script.

So the work here starts with one. A full timed paper at the right level, marked against the published scheme rather than ticked, with each lost mark classified into one of four categories: a knowledge gap, a method gap, a notation forfeit, or a timing loss. That classification is the whole diagnosis. A candidate losing eighteen marks to notation and timing needs a fortnight of discipline work, not a term of re-teaching, and a family that funds the term instead has bought something expensive that will not move the grade.

0606 is unusually well suited to this way of working. There is no coursework, no practical, no tiered entry and no internal mark, which means every single piece of evidence about the student is written mathematics produced under conditions that resemble the examination. Two papers of equal weight, a grade range running from A* to E, and a syllabus of fifteen topic areas that includes the first calculus most of these students have ever met. Confirm the component structure and timings for your child's exam year at cambridgeinternational.org.

The Ajman context shapes the evidence in one specific way worth naming. Many households here have children at campuses in Ajman and across the Sharjah border at the same time, and 0606 is an optional second maths qualification that only some of those campuses enter candidates for. That means the first evidence to gather is not a mark at all: it is whether the entry exists, which paper series it names, and whether the school teaches the subject or expects the student to self-study it alongside Extended 0580. Families discover the third case surprisingly often.

Everything below is built around what can be shown rather than asserted. There is a loss ledger, a reading of how the mark scheme awards method and accuracy credit separately, a ten-week plan with the artefact each week should produce, and a statement of what a monthly progress record ought to contain. Tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in Ajman, because home visiting is a service it runs only in India. Where in-home rates appear here they are the market's published prices, quoted so the comparison is honest.

ajman/cambridge-igcse-additional-maths-0.programmesIntro: 0606 sits beside rather than inside a student's main maths course, and the evidence a family should expect differs at each stage of the route. The notes below describe what each stage produces that can actually be read.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606
programmes.description: A separate qualification examined by two written papers of equal weight, normally taken alongside Extended Mathematics 0580 by stronger candidates. The syllabus covers functions, quadratic functions, equations and inequalities, indices and surds, factors of polynomials, simultaneous equations, logarithmic and exponential functions, straight-line graphs, circular measure, trigonometry, permutations and combinations, series, vectors in two dimensions, differentiation and integration, and kinematics. There is no coursework and no tiered entry.
programmes.countryNote: In Ajman the subject is offered unevenly. Some campuses teach it as a timetabled course, some run it as a lunchtime or after-school class, and some enter candidates who are expected to cover most of it independently. The evidence to gather first is which of those three your child is in, because a self-study candidate needs the content taught and the examination technique built, which is roughly double the work of consolidating a taught course.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, Extended tier
programmes.description: The course 0606 assumes. Extended 0580 algebra, trigonometry and graph work are the floor rather than the target, and a candidate who reached a grade 6 at Extended by leaning on the calculator paper will find 0606 unforgiving. The useful evidence here is the Extended script rather than the Extended grade: a student with strong algebraic manipulation and weak geometry copes with 0606 far better than one with the reverse profile.
programmes.countryNote: An Ajman household running both subjects should expect two separate diagnostics rather than one. The papers reward different things, and a single assessment covering both tends to flatter the student in whichever subject it leans towards. Two diagnostics also make the monthly record readable, because movement in one subject stops being hidden inside an average.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, and A Level Mathematics
programmes.description: What 0606 is a bridge to. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and A Level Mathematics both open with differentiation and integration as assumed language, and a student arriving with genuine 0606 calculus starts the first term reading rather than decoding. The evidence of a genuine 0606 is specific: correct notation, exact answers left in exact form, and derivatives of trigonometric functions handled in radians without prompting.
programmes.countryNote: No IB session or results date is published on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking; confirm any Diploma date with the school's coordinator or on ibo.org. What can be said is that UAE schools sit the May session and that a student who banked 0606 properly in Year 11 needs noticeably fewer paid hours in Year 12 than one who was carried through it.

ajman/cambridge-igcse-additional-maths-0.subjectsIntro: The fifteen topic areas of 0606 do not fail in the same way, and the evidence that a topic is secure differs from topic to topic. The notes below give what secure work looks like on paper and the error that recurs when it is not.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.description: Domain, range, composite and inverse functions, modulus functions and their graphs. Secure work shows the domain written as an inequality rather than described in words, and an inverse found by rearranging with the variable swapped at the correct stage. The recurring error is an inverse quoted with the original variable, which looks like a slip and is marked as one.

subjects.name: Quadratic functions and the discriminant
subjects.description: Completing the square, maximum and minimum points, and conditions on the discriminant for real, equal or no roots. Secure work states the discriminant condition as an inequality before substituting. The commonest loss is solving a discriminant equation when the question asked for a range, which forfeits the whole mark allocation even with correct algebra underneath.

subjects.name: Indices, surds and logarithms
subjects.description: Laws of indices, surd manipulation, exponential and logarithmic functions, and solving equations using logarithms. Secure work rationalises denominators without prompting and leaves exact answers exact. The recurring forfeit is a decimal answer where the scheme wanted a surd or a logarithm, which is an accuracy mark lost on an otherwise perfect method.

subjects.name: Polynomials and simultaneous equations
subjects.description: The factor and remainder theorems, cubic factorisation, and simultaneous equations where one is non-linear. Secure work sets out the substitution explicitly rather than jumping to a quadratic. Students who work mentally lose the method credit and then, having no written line to check, frequently lose the accuracy mark as well.

subjects.name: Straight-line graphs and transformations to linear form
subjects.description: Gradients, intercepts, and converting relationships into a linear form so a graph can be used to find constants. Secure work names what is plotted on each axis before drawing anything. The recurring error is plotting the raw variables and then reading constants off a curve, which earns nothing however neat the graph.

subjects.name: Circular measure and radians
subjects.description: Arc length, sector area and problems set in radians rather than degrees. This is the first place most candidates meet radians as a working unit rather than a curiosity, and it is the single most reliable source of lost marks in the subject. Secure work shows the calculator mode checked and angles substituted in radians; the error is a correct method evaluated in degrees.

subjects.name: Trigonometry: identities and equations
subjects.description: The three reciprocal functions, the Pythagorean identities, and solving trigonometric equations within a stated interval. Secure work lists every solution in the interval rather than the first one found. The usual loss is a candidate who solves correctly and then reports one root where the scheme expected three, which is most of the question gone.

subjects.name: Differentiation
subjects.description: Derivatives of polynomials, exponentials, logarithms and trigonometric functions, the product, quotient and chain rules, tangents and normals, stationary points and rates of change. Secure work states which rule is being used before applying it. The recurring forfeit is a stationary point found and then not classified, because the question asked whether it was a maximum or a minimum and the answer stopped early.

subjects.name: Integration and areas
subjects.description: Integration of the standard functions, definite integrals, and areas under and between curves. Secure work writes the limits into the integral before evaluating and keeps the constant of integration where the question is indefinite. The commonest losses are an omitted constant and a negative area reported as negative rather than interpreted.

subjects.name: Kinematics, series and permutations
subjects.description: Displacement, velocity and acceleration via calculus; binomial expansion and arithmetic and geometric series; permutations and combinations. Kinematics is where calculus becomes a story, and secure work labels which function is being differentiated or integrated and why. Series questions are lost on the term number rather than the method, and the counting topics are lost on whether order matters.

sections.heading: The first diagnostic, and the four categories every lost mark falls into
paragraphs: The first session produces a marked paper rather than a plan. A timed 0606 paper, sat under conditions, then marked against the published scheme with each lost mark assigned to one of four categories. A knowledge gap means the student does not hold the content. A method gap means they hold it but cannot structure a solution. A notation forfeit means the mathematics was right and the presentation cost the mark. A timing loss means the question was never attempted.

The reason this matters is that the four categories have wildly different repair costs. Notation forfeits and timing losses together often account for a fifth of a weak script, and both are discipline rather than teaching: two or three sessions of explicit drill, then consistency. Knowledge gaps are the expensive category, because calculus cannot be installed in a fortnight. A family told only that their child is 'weak at maths' has no way to know which of these they are funding.

The second reason is that it makes progress measurable. Once losses are classified, the monthly record can show that notation forfeits fell from eleven marks to two while knowledge gaps stayed flat, which is a precise statement about what the hours achieved and what they did not. Nobody can promise a grade, and a provider who offers one should be questioned closely; what can be promised is that the evidence will be shown either way. The third reason is that it changes what a family buys. A ledger dominated by forfeits points at a short, cheap block of discipline work and an early review; a ledger dominated by knowledge gaps points at a longer plan that should start now rather than after the next mock. Both are defensible purchases. Guessing between them is not.
