sections.heading: Why English tuition costs what it does
paragraphs: English is priced in the same published AED bands as the sciences, and the work inside the hour is quite different. A maths or physics session can teach and assess inside the session itself. An English session cannot: the piece has to be written, then marked carefully against the criteria, with credited points named and faults counted, before the next session is worth having. That marking is the product, and it happens outside the hour a family is paying for.

So the question to ask any English tutor in this market is not the rate but what happens to the writing between sessions. The published bands put budget and university-student online tuition at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from about AED 33 to 52; at that level, criteria-based marking of a full composition is rarely included. Qualified online subject tutors publish roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE tuition from AED 150, and named IB and IGCSE specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Premium or examiner-led tuition reaches AED 500 to 650 and above, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

In-home visits run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. For English specifically the in-home premium buys very little that matters, because the work that moves the band is annotation on a page and a conversation about it, both of which happen as well over a shared screen. Every figure here was published by the named provider and collected in October 2026; they are market rates rather than an IB Gram price list, and any provider should be asked for the date and source of its own.

sections.heading: Reading at home: what helps and what does not
paragraphs: Every family on this page has been told to make their child read more, and for most of them it has not worked. The advice is not wrong, it is just imprecise. Volume of reading builds vocabulary and sentence rhythm over years, which is valuable and far too slow to help a Year 11 candidate in February. What moves a 0500 mark in weeks is reading of a particular kind, done in small amounts, with a pen.

Three things are worth doing. Read short non-fiction of the type the reading paper uses, and after each piece write two sentences on what the writer did to the reader rather than what the piece was about. Read the openings of published descriptive writing and copy the structure deliberately into a piece of the student's own. And re-read the student's own marked work, which almost nobody does and which is where the faults they keep repeating are most visible.

What does not help is volume alone, or reading chosen for difficulty rather than interest. A student grinding through a book they dislike produces no analysis and no enthusiasm. For households in Ajman where English is one of two or three languages used daily, the useful framing is not quantity of English input but deliberate attention to how a writer achieves an effect, which is a transferable habit and the thing the paper actually credits. There is also a small amount a parent can do without reading anything themselves. Ask the student to explain, out loud, what a writer was trying to make the reader feel in something they have just read. The answer takes ninety seconds, it needs no preparation from the parent, and it rehearses precisely the move the writer's-effect question is built on.

sections.heading: English marks carry into every other subject
paragraphs: Of all the IGCSE subjects, English is the one whose repairs pay back outside their own paper. The explain questions in physics, the six-mark reasoning answers in biology, the directed responses in business studies and the extended answers in history are all marked on whether the point is made clearly enough to be credited. A student who writes in comma-spliced sentences loses marks in those papers too, quietly, and nobody attributes it to English.

That has a budgeting consequence for an Ajman household supporting several subjects at once. Where money is limited and three subjects look weak, the style and accuracy work in English is often the purchase with the widest effect, because it improves the written answers in every other paper the student sits. It is rarely the purchase families choose, because English feels less urgent than a failing science, and it is frequently the one that moves the most marks in total.

The reverse also holds and is worth saying. A student whose English is secure and whose science marks are weak does not have an English problem, and English tuition will not fix it. Separating those cases is the point of marking reading and writing credit independently: it tells a parent whether the writing is the cause of the low marks elsewhere or simply the thing that is easiest to blame. There is a simple way to check which situation a household is in. Take a marked science or humanities answer and read it as a piece of writing: if the point is there but buried, the English work will help the whole timetable. If the point is absent, no amount of English tuition will supply it, and the money belongs in the subject that is actually short of content.

process.title: Confirm the code and the component
process.description: Two facts from the entry documents decide the plan. Whether the entry is 0500 first language or a second-language code, since those are different qualifications with different papers. And whether the second half of the grade comes from the examined writing paper or from a coursework portfolio, since a portfolio route has internal deadlines and a much tighter boundary around permitted help.

process.title: Produce one marked piece in the free 50-minute trial
process.description: The trial is a working session. The student writes a short timed response and attempts a writer's-effect answer, and the tutor marks both against the published criteria, recording reading credit and writing credit separately and counting the accuracy faults by type. That record is the plan, and it usually points at one half of the mark rather than both. No payment is arranged beforehand.

process.title: Target the half that is actually failing
process.description: A student who reads well and writes inaccurately gets sentence-level work. A student who writes fluently and misses the reading marks gets selection, summary and effect work. Both are four to six weeks and both are measurable. What neither gets is general English tuition, which tends to strengthen whichever half was already working.

process.title: Mark between sessions, redraft inside them
process.description: Writing is set, marked against the criteria outside the paid hour with credited points named and faults counted, and the session itself is spent on the redraft. That ordering is what moves the band, and it is the reverse of the usual arrangement where the session is spent writing and the feedback is verbal and forgotten by Thursday.

process.title: Review the bands monthly, not the grade
process.description: Each month the band positions for content and structure and for style and accuracy are compared against the first marked piece, alongside the counted faults. If one band has moved and the other has not, the work shifts to the stuck one. If neither has moved, the feedback was not specific enough and the approach changes rather than the hours increasing.

whyPoints.title: Reading and writing credit are scored apart
whyPoints.description: 0500 awards them separately and so does the diagnosis. A student strong on comprehension and weak on expression needs a different term from one who writes fluently and misses the summary points, and a total mark out of eighty hides exactly that distinction. Separating them usually names one half of the mark rather than both.

whyPoints.title: Marking happens outside the paid hour
whyPoints.description: In English the marking is the product. A piece is written, marked against the published criteria with credited points named and accuracy faults counted, and the session is then spent on the redraft. When comparing rates in this market, what happens to the writing between sessions is a more useful question than the rate itself.

whyPoints.title: Accuracy faults are counted, not discussed
whyPoints.description: Comma splices, repeated sentence openings, overreaching vocabulary and tense drift are countable on a student's own page. A number falls over a fortnight in a way that 'work on your expression' has not in two years, and because those faults recur in every subject's written answers the work pays back beyond English.

whyPoints.title: The portfolio boundary is stated in full
whyPoints.description: Where a school uses the coursework route, a tutor teaches the form, marks drafts against the criteria and names the band and what would move it. No wording is supplied for a piece that will be submitted, because text handed to a student becomes the student's submitted work and that is the thing that must not happen.

whyPoints.title: Capability and timed performance are both measured
whyPoints.description: A redrafted piece shows what a student can produce; a timed piece shows what they can produce in two hours. The examined route rewards the second and the portfolio route rewards something closer to the first, so both are recorded rather than one being used to flatter the other.

whyPoints.title: The limits are published alongside the offer
whyPoints.description: Lessons are online, one-to-one and on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to Ajman addresses, holds no Cambridge or Ministry of Education accreditation, and does not write any part of work a student will submit. In-home figures quoted here are the market's published prices, included for comparison.

faqs.question: My son's English teacher says his work lacks depth. What does that mean in marks?
faqs.answer: Usually one of two quite different things, and the marked script says which. If the reading credit is low, the problem is selection and analysis: the writer's-effect answers explain what a phrase means rather than what it does, and the summary misses points the question asked for. If the reading credit is sound and the writing credit is low, the problem is expression: sentence control, punctuation of complex sentences and vocabulary precision. Those need unrelated terms of work. Ask for the mark broken into reading and writing rather than as a grade, because that single request reframes the whole conversation.

faqs.question: Is 0500 the same qualification as the English my daughter's friend takes?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and this is worth checking before buying anything. 0500 is English as a First Language. The codes 0510 and 0511 are English as a Second Language, with different papers, different mark schemes and a speaking component in one variant. Literature in English 0475 is a third, separate subject examined on set texts. Schools in Ajman commonly enter different students in the same year group for different codes. The statement of entry carries the code, and a student tutored on the wrong specification spends weeks on tasks their paper does not set.

faqs.question: What is the writer's-effect question actually asking for?
faqs.answer: What the language does to the reader, not what it means and not which device it is. A student who writes that a metaphor compares a crowd to a river has named the device and described the comparison; the credit is for what that choice makes the reader see or feel, and why that image rather than another. Three habits fix most of it: quote short, choose words that carry connotation rather than words that are merely dramatic, and avoid the words effective and engaging, which almost always signal an answer with no analysis in it. Marked practice against the criteria is the only route.

faqs.question: Why does my daughter lose marks on the summary when her points are right?
faqs.answer: Because the summary is credited twice and she is probably collecting only one half. There are marks for the points selected and separate marks for concision and control in her own words. A summary that identifies every required point while reproducing the passage's phrasing can score well on selection and lose the writing credit almost entirely. The repair is to separate the two in practice: list the points first, then write the summary without looking at the passage. It is a technique fix rather than a comprehension one, and it typically takes two or three marked attempts.

faqs.question: What is the difference between descriptive and narrative composition?
faqs.answer: A description builds a place or a moment through specific detail with almost no plot; a narrative tells a story. The commonest error is answering a descriptive title with a story that has description attached, which is then marked against the descriptive criteria and loses content and structure credit. For narrative, the usual failure is scope: a plot that needs three thousand words produces an unfinished piece and a collapsed ending however strong the opening was. One incident, deliberately structured, with a controlled ending, is what the time allows.

faqs.question: How do I get the style and accuracy band to move?
faqs.answer: By counting faults on your child's own writing rather than discussing expression in general. Four faults account for most of this band in this market: comma splices, where two complete sentences are joined with a comma; repetitive sentence openings; vocabulary chosen for impressiveness and used slightly wrongly; and tense drift inside a narrative. Mark every instance on one piece and give the number. A student who learns they produced eleven comma splices in six hundred words has something to act on, and the count falls over a fortnight in a way that general advice has not in two years.

faqs.question: My son's school uses coursework for English. What can a tutor do?
faqs.answer: Teach the form, analyse published examples, explain what the criteria reward, mark his own draft against those criteria, and tell him which band the piece sits in and what would move it. What a tutor does not do is supply wording for a piece that will be submitted, rewrite his sentences into his draft, or provide text to be adapted, because anything handed over becomes his submitted work. That boundary is also what makes the evidence worth having: a band position reached on his own writing is one he can reach again, and one improved by somebody else predicts nothing.

faqs.question: When are the portfolio deadlines, and who sets them?
faqs.answer: The school sets them, which is why families on this route are so often caught out. Unlike an examined paper with a published series date, portfolio deadlines are internal and sit inside the school's own calendar, usually spread across the year with drafting built in. Ask the head of English for the schedule in writing in September rather than discovering it when a piece is overdue. For Ajman households with a child at a Sharjah campus, note that the deadlines follow that school's calendar, and that school sits under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves assessment methods in that emirate.

faqs.question: Will reading more books fix my daughter's English grade?
faqs.answer: Over years, yes; over a term, no, and that is why the advice keeps failing. Volume of reading builds vocabulary and sentence rhythm slowly. What moves a 0500 mark in weeks is reading of a specific kind in small amounts with a pen: short non-fiction of the type the reading paper uses, followed by two written sentences on what the writer did to the reader rather than what the piece was about. Re-reading her own marked work is the other high-value habit, because the faults she keeps repeating are most visible there and almost nobody looks.

faqs.question: How many sessions does it take to move a band in English?
faqs.answer: Four to six weeks of weekly work with marking in between, for one band, where the target has been identified. The style and accuracy band moves on counted faults and tends to shift first. Content and structure moves on planning and takes slightly longer, because a student has to learn to shape a piece before writing it rather than discovering the shape halfway through. A plan that aims at both bands at once usually moves neither. Nobody can promise a particular grade, and a provider offering one should be questioned closely.

faqs.question: Does paying more per hour get better English marking?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and the rate is the wrong question. In English the marking is the product: a piece written, marked against the published criteria with credited points named and faults counted, and then redrafted in the session. The useful question is what happens to the writing between sessions. Published bands run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget and university-student online tuition, AED 150 to 300 for qualified online subject tutors, and AED 200 to 450 and above for named specialists, with premium tuition at AED 500 to 650 and above. Those are market figures collected October 2026, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Is an in-home English tutor worth the extra cost in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Less than in most subjects, on the published numbers. In-home visits run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and the work that actually moves an English band is annotation on a page plus a conversation about it. Both of those happen as well over a shared screen as across a table, and screen sharing makes the annotations easier to keep for the monthly record. The in-home premium in this subject mostly buys presence, which some students genuinely need, rather than better marking.

faqs.question: Will English tuition help my son's marks in his other subjects?
faqs.answer: Often more than families expect. Explain questions in physics, reasoning answers in biology, directed responses in business studies and extended answers in history are all credited on whether the point is made clearly enough to be read as the point. A student writing in comma-spliced sentences loses marks in those papers too, and nobody attributes it to English. Where a household is choosing between three weak subjects on a limited budget, the accuracy work in English is frequently the purchase with the widest effect, even though it rarely feels like the urgent one.

faqs.question: How should we handle the timing on a two-hour English paper?
faqs.answer: With a written time budget at the top of the paper, because both 0500 papers put substantial questions at the end and the commonest structural failure is over-writing early. A short-answer question worth two marks receives two points and no context; the long analysis and extended-response questions receive the time their credit justifies. Practising this is examination technique rather than English, which makes it one of the cheapest mark recoveries available, and it shows up immediately in the difference between a student's redrafted work and their timed work.

faqs.question: What if no 0500 specialist is free in the slot we need?
faqs.answer: You will be told before anything is booked. First-language English at this level needs somebody who marks against the published criteria rather than giving general encouragement, which is a narrower group than general English tutoring, and the post-7pm slots most Ajman commuting households need fill first. The options are a different hour, a short wait for one to open, or a named specialist based outside the UAE teaching on Gulf Standard Time, disclosed in advance along with the rate. What you will not be offered is a second-language specialist presented as a 0500 tutor.

ajman/cambridge-igcse-english-first-lang.closingHeading: One marked piece tells you more than a term of reports
ajman/cambridge-igcse-english-first-lang.closingBody: The quickest way to find out what is wrong with a 0500 grade is to have one piece of your child's writing marked properly: against the published criteria, with the reading credit and the writing credit recorded apart, and with the accuracy faults counted by type. Send the most recent marked work and the entry documents showing the code and which component the school uses for the second half of the grade, then take the free 50-minute trial lesson. That session produces one marked piece and names which half of the mark the work should target. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: The honest answer to what 0580 costs is a monthly figure with five variables in it
paragraphs: Ask what a maths tutor costs in Ajman and you will be given an hourly rate, which is the least useful number available. A household does not spend an hour on tuition. It spends roughly four sessions a month, for the nine teaching months of a school year, often across two children on different curricula, and that total is what actually has to fit alongside school fees. The figure worth knowing is therefore monthly, and the published monthly bands for weekly one-hour tuition run around AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, according to Bestimate's Dubai rate table.

Behind each of those monthly bands sits an hourly rate, and the honest way to read them is cheapest first. University-student and budget online tuition is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from about AED 33 to 52. A qualified online subject tutor sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. An in-home visit including travel runs about AED 180 to 500. Named IB and IGCSE specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium or examiner-led tuition reaches AED 500 to 650 and above, with BartyED publishing AED 650. Those are market rates collected in October 2026 from the providers that published them, not an IB Gram price list.

Five things move an Ajman family's position inside those bands. The first is the tier: a Core 0580 entry and an Extended entry are different courses with different hour requirements and different grade ceilings. The second is how many subjects are in trouble, because maths is rarely alone on a weak report. The third is which emirate the school sits in, since a significant share of Ajman households send children across the border to Sharjah or Dubai campuses and inherit that emirate's calendar. The fourth is the hour of the evening the household can realistically protect. The fifth is whether anybody has to drive, which is the variable with the largest price tag attached.

Ajman itself shapes those variables in a specific way. It is the smallest emirate by area, its private schools sit under federal Ministry of Education supervision rather than under an emirate-level authority, and a large proportion of working parents commute south to Sharjah or Dubai. That combination means the local pool of subject specialists is small, the evening starts late, and the nearest tuition centre is often in another emirate. Each of those pushes the realistic cost of in-person help upwards and makes the comparison with a scheduled video session more favourable than the hourly rates alone suggest.

What follows is the arithmetic rather than the advertising. There is a monthly table, a provider-model table ordered cheapest first, a comparison of what the travel premium actually buys, and the component structure of 0580 so you can see which half of the grade your money is aimed at. Tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in Ajman, because home visiting is a service it runs only in India. Where in-home rates appear on this page they are the market's prices, quoted so the comparison can be made properly.

ajman/cambridge-igcse-maths-0580-tutor.programmesIntro: Maths at 0580 is one stage of a route, and each stage carries a different cost profile for an Ajman family. The notes below are about what each stage demands in paid hours rather than about what it looks like in a prospectus.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
programmes.description: A two-year course examined by two written papers, chosen by tier. Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3; Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4. One paper in each pair is sat without a calculator and one with, following the 2025 syllabus revision, and there is no coursework. The nine content areas are number, algebra and graphs, coordinate geometry, geometry, mensuration, trigonometry, transformations and vectors, probability and statistics. Confirm the structure and the provided formulae for your child's exam year at cambridgeinternational.org.
programmes.countryNote: In Ajman the cost pattern is distinctive. Many families start tuition late, in Year 11 rather than Year 10, because the Year 10 report is read as a slow start rather than a warning. Starting late compresses the same syllabus into fewer months, which pushes a household from the mid monthly band towards the exam-year band. The cheapest version of 0580 support is almost always the one that begins in the autumn of Year 10 at one session a week.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606
programmes.description: A separate qualification several Ajman and Sharjah schools run alongside Extended 0580 for stronger candidates, introducing calculus, series, circular measure and kinematics. It is a second examination with its own two papers and its own hours, not an extension of the maths lesson. Families who assume one tutor covers both subjects for one fee are usually surprised, because the teaching is genuinely different work even when the same tutor does it.
programmes.countryNote: The budget question here is simple and rarely asked in time: if the household can fund one subject properly rather than two thinly, Extended 0580 comes first, because it is the grade that appears on every university and sixth-form requirement. Adding 0606 on half the hours it needs tends to cost a household money without moving either certificate.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Mathematics, and A Level Mathematics
programmes.description: Where 0580 leads. Diploma Mathematics splits into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation at Standard or Higher Level; A Level Mathematics assumes Extended 0580 algebra as a starting point rather than as a target. Students who reached a grade B at Extended by relying on the calculator paper meet that gap in the first term of Year 12, and Year 12 catch-up is the most expensive tuition a family ever buys.
programmes.countryNote: No IB session or results date appears on this page. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so confirm any Diploma date with the school's coordinator or on ibo.org. What can be said safely is that UAE schools sit the May session and that internal deadlines inside a school fall months ahead of it, which is why a two-year plan costs less per mark than a three-month rescue.

ajman/cambridge-igcse-maths-0580-tutor.subjectsIntro: The nine content areas of 0580 do not cost the same to repair. The notes below give what each area demands and roughly how many paid hours it typically absorbs, so a household with a fixed monthly figure can spend it where the marks are.

subjects.name: Number
subjects.description: Fractions, decimals, percentages, ratio, standard form, bounds, indices and surds at Extended. Cheap to repair and examined in every paper, which makes it the best first purchase for a household on a tight monthly figure. Reverse percentage and upper and lower bounds are the two reliable losses; both are rule-based and both take about one session each.

subjects.name: Algebra and graphs
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging, solving linear and quadratic equations, inequalities, sequences, functions and graph sketching. This is the largest block in the syllabus and the one that absorbs the most paid hours. Extended candidates also meet algebraic fractions and completing the square, and a student who is shaky here will lose marks in trigonometry and mensuration questions as well.

subjects.name: Coordinate geometry
subjects.description: Gradients, midpoints, the equation of a straight line, parallel and perpendicular lines, and length of a line segment at Extended. Short, formulaic and among the best value per hour in the syllabus. Candidates lose marks by quoting a gradient without signs or by confusing the perpendicular condition, both of which are single-session fixes.

subjects.name: Geometry
subjects.description: Angle facts, polygons, circle theorems at Extended, symmetry, congruence and similarity, and constructions. Circle theorems are the recurring Extended weakness: students name a theorem without stating the reason the examiner wants, and reasons carry marks of their own. Expect two or three sessions for a candidate who has never written a geometric reason properly.

subjects.name: Mensuration
subjects.description: Perimeter, area, surface area and volume, arcs and sectors, and compound solids. The content is not conceptually hard and the losses are almost all unit errors, unconverted dimensions and rounding at the wrong stage. That makes it a technique problem rather than a knowledge problem, which is cheaper to fix than most of the syllabus.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry and Pythagoras at both tiers, with the sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle and three-dimensional problems at Extended. The common failure is choosing the wrong rule rather than mishandling it, so the useful teaching is decision practice on mixed questions rather than more worked examples of each rule in isolation.

subjects.name: Transformations and vectors
subjects.description: Reflection, rotation, translation, enlargement, column vectors and vector geometry at Extended. Marks disappear in the descriptions: a correct rotation drawn without stating the centre and the direction scores partial credit at best. Short block, high return, and usually taught quickly in school because it sits late in the scheme of work.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Probability, tree and Venn diagrams, averages from frequency tables, cumulative frequency and histograms with unequal class widths at Extended. The histogram question is the single most reliable Extended loss in the whole paper because frequency density is forgotten. It is one session, it recurs every series, and it is the clearest example of cheap marks in 0580.

sections.heading: Start with the month, not the hour
paragraphs: An hourly rate answers a question nobody is asking. A family in Al Rawda with a Year 11 maths problem wants to know what the next nine months look like on a bank statement, and the hourly figure has to be multiplied by four and then by nine before it means anything. Doing that multiplication first changes the decision, because a rate that looks reasonable at AED 300 becomes AED 1,200 a month and AED 10,800 across a school year, which is a different conversation from the one the rate alone invites.

The published monthly bands make the comparison easier. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts weekly one-hour tuition at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Alongside those, the packaged offers visible in this market are AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. The gap between those last two figures is the clearest statement of what travel costs that anyone in this market publishes.

The second multiplication most households forget is children. Maths is rarely the only subject in difficulty and rarely the only child in the house. Two children at one session a week each, in the middle band, is AED 1,200 to 2,400 a month, which for many Ajman families sits in the same range as a term of school fees. That number is the reason this page leads with the tier decision and the diagnostic rather than with a tutor list: deciding what not to buy is worth more than negotiating the rate.

sections.heading: Cheapest first: the five provider models an Ajman family can buy
paragraphs: Ordering the market from the bottom up is more honest than the usual premium-first presentation, because most households do not start at the top and work down. They start with what a cousin pays and work up until the teaching looks like it will survive contact with an Extended paper. The lowest band is university-student and budget online tuition, advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from about AED 33 to 52. That band genuinely works for routine, homework supervision and confidence. It does not reliably move circle theorems or histograms.

Above it sits the qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. This is where most 0580 work belongs: somebody who has taught the syllabus, knows which reason the examiner wants in a geometry question and can mark against the published scheme. Above that again, named IB and IGCSE specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium or examiner-led tuition reaches AED 500 to 650 and above, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

The in-home band sits alongside rather than above those, at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. Reading the two columns side by side is the whole argument: the same qualified subject teaching costs AED 150 to 300 online and AED 180 to 500 with someone in the room, and the difference is travel rather than expertise. Every figure here was published by the named provider and collected in October 2026; ask any provider for the date and source of its own rate before treating it as current.

sections.heading: What the travel premium actually buys in Ajman
paragraphs: The gap between the online band and the in-home band is roughly AED 30 to 200 an hour, and it is worth asking precisely what that buys. It buys presence: a person in the room, a parent who can see the session happening, and a student who cannot close a laptop. Those are real benefits and some students need them. What it does not buy is a wider choice of tutor, and in Ajman that is the trade that matters, because the pool of people who can teach Extended 0580 properly and are willing to drive to Al Yasmeen on a Tuesday evening is small.

It also buys travel time that nobody teaches in. A tutor crossing from Sharjah to Ajman in the evening peak is pricing an hour of driving into the fee, and the monthly figures make that explicit: AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits against AED 799 for eight online sessions. The in-home plan delivers eight hours of teaching across four visits; the online plan delivers eight sessions across eight evenings. Which is better teaching depends on the student, but the second spreads contact across more weeks for roughly half the monthly figure.

The third thing the premium buys is scheduling risk. An in-home arrangement has a single point of failure in the evening traffic, and a cancelled visit in a nine-month plan is a lost week that usually gets absorbed rather than rescheduled. A video session survives weather, roadworks and a parent running late from Dubai. None of this makes in-home visiting wrong. It makes the comparison a cost question rather than a quality question, and the table sets both columns out so an Ajman household can decide with the numbers in front of it.

sections.heading: Why an Ajman address moves the number
paragraphs: Three features of this emirate change the arithmetic, and none of them appears on a general UAE tutoring page. The first is cross-border schooling. A large share of Ajman households send children to campuses in Sharjah or along the Emirates Road corridor, and a child at a Sharjah school sits under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods in that emirate. Ajman's own private schools are supervised federally: the Ministry of Education plays the supervising role for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The second is the commute. A meaningful number of Ajman parents work in Dubai or Sharjah and are not home before 7pm, which means the usable tutoring window is late and narrow. A narrow window raises the price of in-person help, because the tutors willing to work it are fewer, and it raises the price of an inflexible arrangement, because a missed early slot is simply lost. It has almost no effect on the cost of a scheduled video session, which is the quiet reason online delivery prices lower here than the national average would suggest.

The third is scarcity. Ajman is the smallest emirate by area and its private-school population is modest, so the number of resident teachers who have taught Extended 0580 and marked against its schemes is genuinely small. Scarcity shows up as a premium on local availability rather than as a premium on quality, which is the single most useful thing an Ajman parent can understand before negotiating. Removing distance from the selection criteria does not buy a cheaper tutor so much as it buys a better-matched one at the same published band.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: a tier decision with a price attached
paragraphs: 0580 is tiered, and the tier is the most consequential financial decision in the subject. Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3 and the certificate is capped: grade C is the ceiling, whatever is spent on tuition. Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4 and the full range is available. A family paying specialist rates for a child entered at Core is buying a better grade C, which may be entirely the right purchase, but it should be a decision rather than a discovery.

The decision belongs to the school, and the timing is the problem. Some Ajman campuses set Core and Extended groups from the start of Year 10, which gives a family eighteen months of warning. Others decide at the Cambridge entry deadline in Year 11, which gives a family weeks. In the second pattern the first many parents hear of it is a mock paper with the tier printed on it, and by then the tuition needed to move a borderline candidate up a tier costs considerably more than the same hours would have cost a year earlier.

There is a budget rule that follows from this and it is worth stating plainly. If your child is borderline between tiers in Year 10, that is the moment to spend, because the hours are buying a ceiling rather than a few marks. If your child is securely Core in Year 11, the honest advice is to spend less rather than more: target the number, algebra and mensuration content that carries most of the Core papers, and stop. Nobody can promise a particular grade at either tier, and a provider who offers to is worth treating with caution.

sections.heading: Four papers, two tiers, and the one sat without a calculator
paragraphs: A 0580 candidate sits two of the syllabus's four papers, decided by tier. Following the 2025 syllabus revision each tier pairs a paper sat without a calculator with a paper sat with one, which changed the preparation materially for students whose arithmetic had been quietly outsourced to a device since Year 7. There is no coursework and nothing banked before the papers, so both mornings carry equal weight. Confirm the component structure, the timings and the list of formulae provided for your child's exam year at cambridgeinternational.org.

The non-calculator paper is where an Ajman tutoring budget most often earns its return, and for an unexpected reason. The content is not harder; the arithmetic is simply unpractised. Fractions without a calculator, surds, standard form by hand and percentage work in the head are skills that a decade of calculator use has eroded, and they can be rebuilt in a handful of sessions because they are drills rather than concepts. A household that funds six well-aimed sessions on exactly this often sees more movement than one funding six months of general support.

The second structural point is that both papers in a tier examine the whole syllabus. There is no topic a candidate can decide not to meet, which is why the marks-lost ordering in the table and in the subject notes above matters more than coverage. Spending on the histogram question, the circle-theorem reasons and the bounds work is spending on content that is certain to appear in some form. Spending on a general revision course is spending on content the student may already hold.

sections.heading: Where 0580 marks go missing, and what each repair costs in hours
paragraphs: Four losses recur in marked Extended scripts from this market, and knowing them converts a vague budget into a short shopping list. Histograms with unequal class widths come first: the frequency-density step is forgotten, the question is worth several marks, it appears reliably, and it takes about one session. Circle theorems come second, and the loss is not the theorem but the reason, because an examiner awards the reasoning mark separately from the answer. Two or three sessions covers a candidate who has never written a geometric reason.

Bounds and reverse percentages are third, and they are the clearest example of cheap marks in the syllabus. Both are rule-following rather than insight, both appear in nearly every series, and both are commonly skipped in school revision because they feel elementary. A session each, with mixed practice afterwards, is usually the whole repair. Fourth is the trigonometry decision: candidates who know the sine rule, the cosine rule and the area formula perfectly still lose marks by choosing the wrong one, so the teaching needed is mixed decision practice rather than further worked examples.

Set against those, the expensive repairs are algebraic fluency and the non-calculator arithmetic, because both are habits built over years rather than topics learned in an evening. A household with a fixed monthly figure should fund the four cheap repairs first, measure the movement on a timed paper, and only then decide whether the expensive work is worth buying. That ordering is the difference between a plan and a standing order, and it is the one piece of advice on this page that costs nothing to follow.

sections.heading: Paying safely under federal oversight
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit, and an Ajman family paying cash to a neighbour's cousin should know what the rules are. The u.ae portal records that the private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, that the permit is granted free of charge for two years, and that eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

No fine amount appears on this page because none is published. Reporting of the ministry's announcement recorded that the amounts and penalties were not specified, and a figure circulating online could not be verified against a ministry source. The official route is MoHRE's own service, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. The permit is free, so a tutor citing permit costs as a reason for a higher rate is citing something that does not exist.

Two further money questions deserve straight answers. The UAE value-added-tax treatment of tuition fees is not stated as fact here, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation; ask any provider directly whether its quoted AED figure includes VAT and get the answer in writing. And whatever a family pays, the data side matters: a lead form about a child collects personal information, and under Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection you are entitled to know what is held, why, and how to have it deleted. Ask that question before the first session, not after the third invoice.

process.title: Establish the tier before discussing money
process.description: The first question is whether your child is entered for Core or Extended, because a Core entry caps the certificate at grade C and changes what any budget can achieve. Ask the school in writing, and if the tier is not yet fixed, ask when it will be. Everything else on this page is a cheaper decision than this one.

process.title: Take the free 50-minute trial as a diagnostic
process.description: The trial is a working session. The tutor sets a short non-calculator sequence, a circle-theorem question and a histogram, marks them live against the published criteria, and names the specific losses. That turns a monthly budget into a list of four or five repairs in order of marks, which is the only way to spend a fixed figure well. No payment is arranged before it happens.

process.title: Agree a monthly total, not an hourly rate
process.description: Sessions a month, months in the plan, and the total that produces. If two children are involved, the total is agreed for both before the first paid session rather than discovered across three invoices. Where the figure exceeds what the household wants to commit, the plan is cut back to the highest-return repairs rather than stretched thin across everything.

process.title: Protect one evening on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Slots are set late enough for a household where a parent drives back from Dubai or Sharjah, and where two subjects are involved they are blocked on the same evening so the rest of the week stays clear. The same hour every week matters more than which hour, because a rescheduled session is the most common form of wasted money in this market.

process.title: Measure at week six and cut if it has not moved
process.description: After six weeks there is a second timed paper and a comparison against the first, broken down by the losses the diagnostic named. If a measure has moved, the plan continues. If it has not, the approach changes rather than the hours increasing, and if a repair is finished the sessions stop. Spending less when less is needed is part of the arrangement.

whyPoints.title: The monthly figure comes first
whyPoints.description: Every rate on this page is published with its source and then converted into what a household actually spends across a month and a school year. An hourly number that has not been multiplied by four and then by nine is not a budget, and the gap between those two framings is where most families in this market are surprised.

whyPoints.title: Rates are attributed, never presented as ours
whyPoints.description: The AED bands here were published by named providers and collected in October 2026. They are market rates, not an IB Gram price list, and where a provider published a specific figure it is named alongside it. Any page quoting a rate without a date and a source is quoting something that may be two years stale.

whyPoints.title: The tier is treated as the main cost decision
whyPoints.description: Most tutoring copy treats Core and Extended as a detail. In 0580 the tier sets the ceiling on the certificate, which means it sets the ceiling on what any amount of tuition can buy. Establishing it before the budget conversation is the single most valuable thing an Ajman parent can do this term.

whyPoints.title: The repairs are ordered by marks per hour
whyPoints.description: Histograms, circle-theorem reasons, bounds, reverse percentages and the trigonometry choice are named specifically, with rough hour costs, so a household with a fixed figure can spend it where the marks are rather than on general revision. Cheap repairs come first and the expensive habits are only bought once the cheap ones are banked.

whyPoints.title: The permit facts are the real ones
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE private tuition work permit is free of charge for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and no fine schedule is published anywhere. That means nobody can justify a premium on permit costs, and nobody should be quoting penalty figures at you. Both are useful things to know while negotiating.

whyPoints.title: What is not on offer is stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are online, one-to-one and on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to Ajman addresses, holds no Ministry of Education or Cambridge accreditation, does not perform equivalency, and does not produce work a student will submit. The in-home figures on this page are the market's prices, quoted for comparison.

faqs.question: What should an Ajman family budget per month for 0580 maths support?
faqs.answer: Published monthly bands for weekly one-hour tuition run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work, according to Bestimate's Dubai rate table. Most Extended candidates with two or three weak content areas sit in the middle band, which is about four sessions a month at the AED 150 to 300 hourly range qualified online subject tutors publish. Two children at one session each a week doubles that. Those are market figures collected in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Is a group class at a centre better value than one-to-one for 0580?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes. Per mark, usually not, and the reason is diagnosis. A group class teaches a syllabus at a pace; it does not find out that your child loses marks on frequency density and on geometric reasons specifically. For a candidate whose losses are not yet identified, a centre class provides structure cheaply and is a reasonable first step. For a candidate who has sat a mock and has four identifiable weaknesses, one-to-one hours pointed at those four will usually move the mark further for the same total spend. Centres in this market also rarely publish a rate, so ask for it in writing.

faqs.question: How much more does an in-home maths tutor cost in Ajman than an online one?
faqs.answer: On published rates, the gap is roughly AED 30 to 200 an hour. Qualified online subject tutors publish about AED 150 to 300; in-home visits including travel run about AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. The monthly packages make it starker: AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. The difference is travel time rather than teaching quality, and in Ajman it also narrows the tutor pool to whoever will drive to your district at your hour.

faqs.question: Does a Core entry change what tutoring can achieve for my son?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the most important thing to establish before spending. A Core 0580 entry caps the certificate at grade C regardless of how many hours are bought, because Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3 and the full grade range is only available on the Extended papers. That does not make tuition pointless; a secure grade C is a real outcome and it may be exactly what the household needs. It does mean that paying specialist rates in the hope of an A is buying something the entry cannot deliver. Ask the school in writing which tier your son is entered for.

faqs.question: When does my child's school in Ajman decide the maths tier?
faqs.answer: It varies, and the variation is what costs families money. Some Ajman campuses set Core and Extended groups from the beginning of Year 10, which gives you eighteen months of warning and the chance to spend when spending changes a ceiling. Others decide at the Cambridge entry deadline in Year 11, and in those schools the first many parents hear of it is a mock paper with the tier printed on it. Ask the head of maths directly, in writing, when the tier is fixed and what evidence it is based on. That question costs nothing and reframes the entire budget.

faqs.question: Why is there a maths paper without a calculator now?
faqs.answer: Because the 2025 syllabus revision paired each tier's papers so that one is sat without a calculator and one with. Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3; Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4. Confirm the arrangement, the timings and the formulae provided for your child's exam year at cambridgeinternational.org. The practical consequence for an Ajman family is that fractions, surds, standard form and percentage work by hand are examined skills again, and for students who have used a calculator since Year 7 those are drills rather than concepts, which makes them unusually cheap to rebuild.

faqs.question: Which single 0580 topic gives the most marks back per hour paid?
faqs.answer: On marked Extended scripts from this market, histograms with unequal class widths. The frequency-density step is forgotten, the question carries several marks, it appears reliably, and the whole repair is usually one session plus mixed practice. Close behind it are upper and lower bounds and reverse percentages, both rule-based and both commonly skipped in school revision for feeling elementary. Circle-theorem reasoning is next and takes two or three sessions, because the reasoning mark is awarded separately from the answer. Fund those four before anything else and measure the movement on a timed paper.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in this market rise closer to the exams?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens rather than the published bands moving, and the effect on a household is the same. In the final term the specialists who can teach Extended technique are already holding weekly slots, so what is left is either an inconvenient hour or a less experienced tutor at the same rate. Bestimate's specialist exam-year monthly band of AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above reflects that intensity rather than a seasonal surcharge. The way to avoid paying it is to start in the autumn of Year 10 at one session a week, which is the cheapest version of this subject per mark.

faqs.question: Does my quoted AED rate include value-added tax?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider directly and get the answer in writing. This page does not state the UAE value-added-tax treatment of tuition fees as fact, because doing so responsibly requires a Federal Tax Authority citation, and several pages in this market state it without one. What a family can reasonably insist on is clarity about the specific figure being quoted to them: whether the number in the message is the amount that will leave the account, and whether any registration number is held. A provider who cannot answer that plainly is telling you something useful.

faqs.question: Who supervises private schools in Ajman, and does that affect tutoring?
faqs.answer: The Ministry of Education plays the supervising role for private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, so Ajman has no emirate-level authority of the kind Dubai and Sharjah have. By contrast, the Sharjah Private Education Authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods in that emirate, which matters to the many Ajman families whose children attend Sharjah campuses. None of those bodies regulates private tutoring itself; that sits with MoHRE through the private tuition work permit. So the regulator question affects which school calendar and fee regime you are inside, not who may teach your child.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Ajman need a permit, and does it cost them money?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it is free. The u.ae portal records that the private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility extending to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no schedule of amounts is published. Because the permit carries no fee, a tutor citing licensing costs as a reason for a higher rate is citing something that does not exist.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover maths and physics to save us money?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the test is whether they have taught and marked both syllabuses rather than whether they are comfortable with both subjects. A genuine dual specialist saves a household a scheduling slot and occasionally a small amount of money. A maths tutor covering physics on general science confidence costs more in the end, because the losses in 0625 are about practical technique and equation recall rather than about algebra. Where two subjects are genuinely needed, scheduling them back to back on one evening protects the rest of the week, which is worth more to most Ajman families than a discount.

faqs.question: My daughter is in Year 11 and the mock was poor. What is the smallest spend that helps?
faqs.answer: A diagnostic timed paper at her entered tier, followed by six to ten sessions aimed only at what that paper exposed. At the published mid band that is roughly AED 900 to 3,000 in total rather than a nine-month commitment, and it is the lowest spend that reliably moves a boundary when the gaps are specific. If the paper shows most of the two years missing rather than four identifiable losses, a short block will not fix it and you should know that before paying. Nobody can promise a particular grade, and a provider offering one should be questioned closely.

faqs.question: What happens to our money if we stop after one or two sessions?
faqs.answer: The free 50-minute trial lesson runs before any payment is arranged, so the first session costs nothing and no card details are taken to book it. After that, sessions are agreed as a monthly total rather than as a long contract, which means stopping is a matter of not renewing rather than of recovering a prepayment. If a repair finishes early, the sessions stop; spending less when less is needed is part of the arrangement rather than an exception to it. Ask any provider in this market what its own cancellation position is in writing before prepaying a package.

faqs.question: What personal data does booking a maths tutor in Ajman involve?
faqs.answer: An enquiry collects a name, a year group, a school, a subject and a contact number, and the sessions themselves generate marked work and progress notes. Under Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection a parent is entitled to know what is held, the purpose it is held for, and how to have it removed, at any point. Nothing about a student is published, and no grades or photograph are needed to book a trial lesson. Ask any provider in this market the same question before the first session rather than after the third invoice.

ajman/cambridge-igcse-maths-0580-tutor.closingBody: Two numbers decide what a 0580 year costs an Ajman household, and both can be settled this week. The first is the tier your child is entered for, because a Core entry caps the certificate at grade C and changes what any budget can buy. The second is the monthly total you are willing to commit, converted from an hourly rate rather than guessed at. Bring the mock script and the entry confirmation to the free 50-minute trial lesson, and the session will name the four or five repairs worth funding and the order to fund them in. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

ajman/cambridge-igcse-physics-0625-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 at both tiers: the Core route through Papers 1 and 3, the Extended route through Papers 2 and 4, with Paper 5 or Paper 6 alongside. Slots run on Gulf Standard Time, late enough for Ajman households where a parent commutes back from Sharjah or Dubai.

intro.heading: Same grade, different problem: what a marked physics script tells you
paragraphs: Physics grades are unusually bad at saying what is wrong. A grade 5 on an Extended paper can come from four or five distinct causes that share nothing in common, and the school report cannot distinguish them because it is a summary rather than a measurement. One student has not committed the equations to recall and loses every calculation. Another recalls them and loses marks on the graph question for an unlabelled axis and a hand-drawn line of best fit. A third knows the physics and answers a four-mark describe question in one sentence because nobody has shown them what the command word is worth.

Those three students need entirely different terms. The first needs a recall programme. The second needs about three sessions on presentation and will recover marks without learning any new physics. The third needs command-word work, which is closer to English teaching than to science. A household that funds general physics revision for any of them is buying something that may not touch the actual loss, and in Ajman, where households often support two or three children at once, that matters financially as well as academically.

So the work starts with the script. A timed paper at the right tier, marked against the published scheme rather than ticked, with the multiple-choice responses read as a pattern rather than as a number. Wrong answers on a multiple-choice paper are better evidence than right ones, because distractors in 0625 are written deliberately to catch specific misconceptions, and a student who chooses the same kind of distractor repeatedly is telling you which misconception they hold.

0625 also has an element the maths subjects do not: a fifth of the grade sits in the practical component, and which route your child is on changes the evidence entirely. Paper 5 is a practical test sat in the school laboratory; Paper 6 is a written paper about experiments. Confirm which one the school entered your child for, along with the component structure and timings for the exam year, at cambridgeinternational.org. Families frequently do not know, and the two routes need different preparation. The tier matters just as much: a Core entry caps the certificate at grade C whatever is spent, so establishing it is a five-minute task that reframes every budget conversation that follows.

Everything below is built on what a marked paper can show. There is a distractor-pattern table, a ledger of the presentation marks that graphs and tables carry, an equation-recall structure, and a plain account of what the practical routes demand. Tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in Ajman, because home visiting is a service it runs only in India. In-home rates quoted here are the market's published prices, included so the comparison is honest.

A practical component, Paper 5 or Paper 6, carries 20% of the grade either way

ajman/cambridge-igcse-physics-0625-tutor.programmesIntro: Physics at 0625 is a stage with a distinctive evidence problem: much of what a student is assessed on is technique rather than content. The notes below describe what each stage demands and what proves it is in place.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
programmes.description: A two-year course assessed by three components. A multiple-choice paper and a theory paper, both set by tier, plus a practical component taken as either a practical test or a written alternative to practical carrying a fifth of the grade. The six topic areas are motion, forces and energy; thermal physics; waves; electricity and magnetism; nuclear physics; and space physics. There is no coursework. Confirm the structure and timings for your child's exam year at cambridgeinternational.org.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman campuses differ in how much laboratory time a physics cohort actually gets, and that is the variable that decides which practical route makes sense. A school with limited laboratory access that nonetheless enters candidates for the practical test is setting up a problem, and a family is entitled to ask which paper the entry names. Several Ajman households discover the answer only when a mock arrives in the wrong format.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences
programmes.description: The combined-science route several Ajman and Sharjah schools run instead of three separate sciences. It covers physics, chemistry and biology to a reduced depth and produces one or two grades rather than three. A student on this route is not sitting 0625 and does not need 0625 past papers, and confusing the two is the commonest reason an Ajman family books tuition that does not fit the examination.
programmes.countryNote: Check the subject line on the statement of entry rather than the timetable. A child described at home as 'doing physics' may be on a co-ordinated route with a shared practical component, and the tuition plan for that is different: less depth, more breadth, and a practical paper covering three sciences rather than one.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Physics, and A Level Physics
programmes.description: Where a strong Extended 0625 grade leads. Both courses assume the mechanics, electricity and waves content of the IGCSE as working knowledge and open with it rather than building to it, and both expect graph and uncertainty handling that 0625 only introduces. A candidate who reached grade 6 without securing the practical skills meets that gap in the first term, and it is more expensive to close at seventeen than at fifteen.
programmes.countryNote: No IB session or results date is published on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking; confirm any Diploma date with the school's coordinator or on ibo.org. UAE schools sit the May session, and the internal assessment deadlines inside a school fall months earlier, which is why securing practical technique in Year 11 is cheaper than repairing it in Year 12.

ajman/cambridge-igcse-physics-0625-tutor.subjectsIntro: The six topic areas of 0625 fail in characteristic ways, and the evidence of security differs across them. The notes below say what secure work looks like and the error that recurs when it is absent.

subjects.name: Motion, forces and energy: kinematics
subjects.description: Speed, velocity, acceleration, distance-time and speed-time graphs. Secure work reads a gradient as a rate with units attached and an area under a speed-time graph as a distance. The recurring error is describing a graph rather than interpreting it: 'the line goes up' where the mark was for constant acceleration with a stated value.

subjects.name: Forces, moments and pressure
subjects.description: Newton's laws, resultant force, moments, equilibrium, density and pressure. Secure work draws the forces before writing anything. The usual loss is a moment calculated with the distance measured from the wrong point, which produces a plausible number and no marks, and it is almost always a diagram habit rather than a physics gap.

subjects.name: Energy, work and power
subjects.description: Energy stores and transfers, work, power, efficiency and energy resources. Secure answers name the store at the start and the store at the end rather than saying energy was lost. Efficiency questions are lost on the ratio direction, and the energy-resources content is largely recall, which makes it the cheapest block in the syllabus to repair.

subjects.name: Thermal physics
subjects.description: Kinetic particle theory, thermal expansion, specific heat capacity, latent heat and the three transfer mechanisms. Secure work distinguishes temperature from internal energy explicitly. The reliable loss is a conduction or convection explanation that describes heat as a substance moving rather than as particle interaction or density change.

subjects.name: Waves: general properties, light and sound
subjects.description: Reflection, refraction, dispersion, lenses, the electromagnetic spectrum and sound. Secure work in ray optics draws construction lines with a ruler and labels the normal. Marks disappear when a ray diagram is sketched freehand, because the angles are measured by the examiner, and that is a presentation loss rather than a knowledge one.

subjects.name: Electricity: circuits and components
subjects.description: Charge, current, potential difference, resistance, series and parallel circuits, and circuit components. Secure work labels every meter and states whether a reading is of current or potential difference. The recurring Extended loss is parallel resistance treated as a sum, and the recurring Core loss is a circuit symbol drawn ambiguously enough to be read as something else.

subjects.name: Electromagnetism and electromagnetic induction
subjects.description: Magnetic fields, the motor effect, induction, transformers and the national grid. Secure answers state the direction rule being used by name. This area sits late in most schemes of work and is therefore thin in a January mock, which makes it one of the highest-return topics for a short block of paid hours in Year 11.

subjects.name: Nuclear and space physics
subjects.description: Atomic structure, radioactivity, half-life, nuclear fission and fusion, the solar system and stellar life cycles. Half-life is the one genuine calculation here and it is lost on the number of halvings rather than the method. Space physics is almost entirely recall and sits at the very end of the course, so it is frequently unexamined in school mocks and entirely examinable in the real paper.

ajman/cambridge-igcse-physics-0625-tutor.regionsIntro: What varies across Ajman for a physics family is laboratory access at school and workable space at home, both of which affect the practical component more than the theory. These notes are about those two things.

regions.name: Al Nuaimiya
regions.note: Central Ajman with the emirate's longest-established campuses, generally the ones with the most settled science departments. A candidate here is more likely to be on a genuine practical-test route, which changes what the preparation has to cover.

regions.name: Al Rashidiya
regions.note: Older Ajman near the commercial strip and the Corniche. Apartment living dominates, so the limiting factor for a physics session is a quiet surface big enough to draw a ray diagram with a ruler, which sounds trivial and is not.

regions.name: Al Jurf
regions.note: Mixed residential near the university area, with several households supporting children across different curricula. Where one child is on separate sciences and another on a co-ordinated route, the two need different past papers and the entry documents are the only way to tell.

regions.name: Al Mowaihat
regions.note: Inland villa communities with long school runs. Students here routinely arrive home late, and a physics session that produces drawn work needs the student alert, so the slot choice affects the quality of the evidence as much as the attendance.

regions.note: Waterfront villas and apartments. Households here often have good study space, which helps with the drawn and graphed work physics demands; the constraint is more often the evening schedule than the room.

ajman/cambridge-igcse-physics-0625-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways of running 0625 support, separated by which component the marked script says is failing. All three run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and each begins with a free 50-minute trial lesson used as a diagnostic.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through Year 11
modes.description: A fixed slot following the school's teaching order, with each session producing a written answer marked against the published scheme. The weekly pattern is what catches the presentation habits early, because an unlabelled axis spotted in October costs one session and the same habit spotted in April costs marks in the examination. Electromagnetism and space physics, which sit late in most schemes, get covered rather than skipped.
bullets: Tracks the school scheme rather than a generic syllabus order
One marked written answer out of every session
Graph and diagram work done with instruments, not freehand
Compared against the first diagnostic at week six

modes.title: A practical-component block
modes.description: A narrow block on the practical paper alone, which carries a fifth of the grade and is almost always the least revised part of the course. The work differs by route: for the written alternative it is method, variables, tables, graphs, sources of error and improvements; for the practical test it is reliable method and write-up habits rather than rehearsing apparatus the student will meet in their own school laboratory.
bullets: Which paper the school entered your child for is established first
Independent, dependent and control variables drilled until automatic
Tables ruled with units in the headings, not in the cells
Error and improvement answers, where most of this paper's marks go

modes.title: A recall and technique block before the series
modes.description: Six to ten sessions after a mock, split between equation recall and command-word discipline according to what the marked script shows. This is the purchase that moves a borderline candidate most reliably, because both of those losses are measured in marks rather than in understanding, and both respond to drill inside a fortnight.
bullets: Opens with a timed paper at the entered tier
Equation recall tested cold rather than with the formula visible
Describe, explain, calculate and suggest practised as distinct tasks
Closes with a second timed paper for a like-for-like comparison

sections.heading: Reading the multiple-choice paper as a pattern rather than a score
paragraphs: A multiple-choice physics paper is the most under-used diagnostic document a family owns. Parents see a mark out of forty and treat it as a measure of how much physics the student knows. Examiners write the alternatives on purpose: the wrong options are not random, they are the answers a student arrives at by holding a specific, well-documented misconception. A student who consistently picks the option that treats heat as a substance, or that adds parallel resistances, has given you a precise piece of information.

That turns thirty-odd wrong answers into a handful of named repairs. The student who selects the distractor corresponding to a gradient read as a value rather than as a rate has a graph-reading problem that will also be costing them marks on the theory paper. The student who picks the option where the moment is taken about the wrong pivot has a diagram habit. In both cases the multiple-choice paper has diagnosed a loss that will appear in the longer paper too, where it is worth far more marks.

The practical method is simple enough for a parent to follow. Group the wrong answers by the misconception each distractor represents, count the groups, and work on the two largest. A score tells you a student is weak; a pattern tells you what to teach on Tuesday. This is also why a diagnostic session asks the student to explain why they chose a wrong option rather than simply marking it wrong: the reasoning is the evidence, and the choice is only the trace of it.

sections.heading: Graphs, tables and the marks that are awarded for presentation
paragraphs: Physics gives marks for things that are not physics, and an evidence-led plan treats those as the cheapest marks on the paper. A graph question awards credit for labelled axes with units, a sensible scale, correctly plotted points and a line of best fit drawn with a ruler where the relationship is linear. A student who understands the experiment perfectly and sketches the line freehand loses credit that has nothing to do with their understanding, and they lose it in every series.

Tables work the same way. Units belong in the column heading rather than beside each value, readings should be given to a consistent number of decimal places, and a repeated reading needs a mean that is calculated rather than estimated. These are rules, not insights. They take one session to teach, a fortnight to become automatic, and they appear on both the theory paper and the practical component, which means the hours spent on them are paid back twice.

The reason this belongs near the front of a plan rather than at the end is psychological as much as practical. A student who has been told for two years that they are weak at physics, and who then recovers eight or nine marks in a fortnight by learning to rule a line and label an axis, starts the content work from a different place. It is also the clearest evidence a parent will see: the same student, the same physics, a visibly different script.

sections.heading: Equation recall, and proving a formula is available under pressure
paragraphs: 0625 expects a candidate to bring equations with them rather than to be handed them, which makes recall a separately testable thing. Confirm for your child's exam year which relationships are provided and which must be remembered, at cambridgeinternational.org, because this is exactly the kind of detail that changes between syllabus versions and that a tutor working from memory gets wrong.

The evidence problem is that recall in a quiet room with a textbook nearby is not the same as recall in the fortieth minute of a paper. So the test used here is cold: a blank sheet, a topic named, and every relationship the student can produce, written out with the quantities defined and the units attached. What comes back is usually revealing. Students often hold the equation and not the units, or hold it in one rearranged form only, which fails the moment a question asks for a different variable.

The repair is retrieval practice rather than copying. Equations grouped by topic, tested cold at the start of each session, with the gaps recorded so the record shows which group is secure and which is not. Rearrangement is drilled separately, because a student who can only use a formula in the form they memorised it in will lose marks on roughly half the calculations that use it. None of this is sophisticated teaching. It is bookkeeping, and it is the single most reliable way to move a physics calculation mark.
