sections.heading: From a tower on the Emirates Road: what each arrangement assumes
paragraphs: This page targets a home-tutor search, so the question deserves answering rather than deflecting. A visiting tutor at an Emirates City apartment is a real option, sold by real providers, and for a young child or a household with no quiet space it can be the better product. The honest objection is not quality, it is the road: the arrangement assumes a predictable drive at the exact hour the Emirates Road is least predictable.

IB Gram delivers to Emirates City as one-to-one online tuition over live video. We do not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists in India only. The argument for it in this district is narrow and strong. The specialist pool stops being people willing to drive to a tower on the Ajman side of the Emirates Road, which is a small group, and becomes people who teach that board at that level, which is a much larger one.

The table lists what each arrangement quietly assumes, because assumptions are where these decisions go wrong. Online tuition assumes a device, a connection and one room that can be quiet for an hour, and if a household cannot supply those then it is the wrong choice, headphones or not. A visiting arrangement assumes a predictable drive. A centre class assumes two spare journeys. Sibling help assumes goodwill, which is usually present, and subject knowledge, which at exam level often is not.

One honest recommendation before any of it. Where the school runs subject-support sessions and has a specialist in that subject, those are already inside the fees and take no travel from anybody. For a commuting household that is the cheapest possible fix, and a provider who never mentions it is selling hours rather than solving a problem.

sections.heading: Coverage and the fallback, stated before you book
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit, which is strange, because every matching service has one. Subject scarcity is real and it is uneven: IGCSE mathematics has the widest pool of anything, and a smaller Diploma subject at Higher Level in a specific term may have nobody free at all. A family that is told this up front can plan. A family that discovers it in week three has lost three weeks.

The pattern is geographic as well as subject-based. The northern emirates have fewer UAE-based specialists than Dubai across almost every subject, which is a straightforward consequence of where the schools and the teachers are. For Emirates City that means the honest answer to some requests is a specialist working from outside the UAE on Gulf Standard Time, and that answer is given at matching rather than buried.

What we will not do is put a generalist into a Higher Level slot and hope the student does not notice. They do notice, usually in the third session, and by then a term has gone. If nobody who teaches that syllabus at that level is available in the window you need, the answer is no, with an estimate of when it changes.

The table is the current shape of that coverage, written to be checked rather than admired. Ask about your own subject and level specifically, because the shape moves between terms and the autumn is tighter than the spring.

sections.heading: The examination year counted backwards from the board's own dates
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes an examination calendar, and a commuting family is the most likely to be caught by one. The deadlines that matter are not the paper dates. They are the entry deadline, the tier confirmation, the forecast-grade submission and the coursework internal dates, and all of them sit months earlier and arrive through a school rather than through a provider.

The dates in the table come from Cambridge's and Pearson's own published pages, and the first correction to make is which Cambridge series applies in Ajman at all. Cambridge offers IGCSE, O Level and International A Level to UAE centres in a June series and a November series; the additional series sat in February and March is an entry route for India, so an Emirates City family should never build a plan on it. For June, final entries close in the spring, months ahead of the first paper, and the centre holds the exact date. Pearson's figures are firmer because the timetable is already published: its International GCSE November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, its June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

That last pair of figures is the one worth understanding before choosing a series. A November entry produces results in late January, which lands after many university application deadlines. A June entry produces results in late August. For a student who needs a grade for an application, the series choice is a strategic decision rather than a scheduling one, and it is made at entry.

No IB dates appear on this page. The IB's own site could not be read directly for this project, so no IB session, upload or results date is published anywhere here. Secondary sources circulate; they are not sources. Ask your child's diploma coordinator for the session calendar and plan against that, and treat any tutoring page that states IB dates without naming ibo.org as a page that guessed.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in a shared-device household
paragraphs: A household where three people share a laptop and an older sibling is doing a degree in the next room is a household where coursework help happens informally and constantly. Nobody is trying to break any rules. The IB's position is still that submitted work must be the student's own, that a supervisor must see drafts, and that the submission is authenticated, and the consequence of drifting across that line falls on the student.

The useful version of the boundary is behavioural rather than legalistic. Help that explains, questions, tests and gives feedback on work the student has already produced is legitimate from anyone. Help that supplies sentences, reorganises the student's draft on their behalf, provides a dataset, or hands back a document containing new material is not, whether it comes from a tutor, a cousin or a paid website.

The test a family can run at the dining table is whether the student can explain, without prompting, why each choice in the piece was made. If they cannot, the work has drifted, and the fix is to go back rather than forward. That is a hard conversation two weeks before a deadline and a much easier one in the first week, which is the argument for front-loading coursework support rather than buying it late.

One market-specific warning. There are providers selling completed Internal Assessments to UAE families at fixed prices. Buying one is malpractice under IB rules and the student carries the consequence, not the seller. A page in this market that does not say so plainly is being commercially careful at a family's expense.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the weekend and the Emirates City evening
paragraphs: The UAE academic year contains Ramadan, and in a commuting household it changes the week more than anywhere else. School days shorten, so children are home earlier. Working hours shift, so a parent may be home earlier too. Energy moves to after Iftar. Taken together, that is the one period of the year when an afternoon slot genuinely works in this district, and plans that ignore it waste the opportunity as well as the risk.

The practical adjustments are small. Shorter sessions more often, because concentration while fasting is a real constraint. Heavier analytical work moved to whatever part of the day a particular household has energy in, which varies more than any general advice can capture. And a revision timetable written in February for a May or June series redrafted around those weeks rather than assuming they behave like ordinary ones.

The weekend is the other scheduling asset families under-use. Friday afternoons and Saturdays are the only times a commuting parent is reliably present and unhurried, which makes them the best slots in the week for anything that needs supervision, for a marked timed paper, or for a coursework session where a decision has to be made rather than a skill practised. The weekday evening is for practice; the weekend is for the work that needs an adult in the room.

On booking mechanics, briefly: slots are held on Gulf Standard Time, the same tutor runs them week to week, and a short written note follows each one. In a household where the person who pays for the lesson is often not the person present at it, that note is not administrative politeness. It is how the arrangement stays accountable.

process.title: Tell us the school direction and the parent's return time
process.description: Not just the subject. Which way the school run goes and when the supervising adult is actually home decides the slot, and the slot decides whether the arrangement lasts past the fourth week. Those two facts are more useful at the start than any description of the child's difficulties.

process.title: Free trial at the real slot, not a convenient one
process.description: If 8pm on a Tuesday is the hour that exists in your week, the trial runs at 8pm on a Tuesday with the tutor who would take the course. Testing a 5pm slot and then discovering nobody is home for it is how families lose a month deciding.

process.title: Board dates into one calendar in the first week
process.description: Entry deadline, zone-specific timetable, forecast grades and coursework internal dates, taken from the exams officer and the board's own pages. A commuting parent cannot rely on a bag note, so the calendar is built once at the start and the weekly plan is derived from it.

process.title: Written note after every session, reviewed at six weeks
process.description: Each session leaves a short note and the annotated work in a shared document. At six weeks the plan is reviewed against a marked component rather than against impressions, and it can conclude that the subject, the tutor or the slot needs changing.

whyPoints.title: A slot built from your actual week
whyPoints.description: Departure times, return times and the supervising parent's arrival, mapped before anything is booked. The commonest failure in Emirates City is a sensible-looking 5.30pm slot in a household where nobody is home until 7.30pm, and it is entirely avoidable.

whyPoints.title: No travel in the price and none in your evening
whyPoints.description: An in-home rate carries the tutor's drive whether or not it is itemised, and the household pays again in setup and overrun. An online hour costs an hour. In a district built on road time, that arithmetic is the whole argument.

whyPoints.title: Board deadlines quoted from the boards
whyPoints.description: Cambridge's June and November series, Pearson's November 2026 timetable window and both boards' published results dates, taken from their own pages. No IB dates appear because the IB's site could not be read for this project, and a guessed date is worse than none.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed, not discovered
whyPoints.description: Higher Level specialists are scarcer in the northern emirates than in Dubai, and in some subjects and some windows the honest answer is no. That is said at matching, with an estimate of when it changes, rather than filled with a generalist.

whyPoints.title: A written note for the parent who was not there
whyPoints.description: In a commuting household the person who books the lesson is frequently not the person home for it. Every session leaves a short note and the annotated work in a shared document, which is how the arrangement stays accountable rather than hopeful.

faqs.question: Can we get a home tutor to come to our tower in Emirates City?
faqs.answer: Visiting tutors do serve Ajman and charge roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the rate, so the option exists. IB Gram does not provide it: lessons for Emirates City families run one-to-one over live video, and home visiting is a service we offer in India only. The objection to a visiting arrangement here is the road rather than the format. A specialist coming from Sharjah budgets thirty to forty-five minutes each way at 5pm and from Dubai an hour or more, and that is paid for in the rate and again in late arrivals.

faqs.question: Both of us commute to Dubai. What time can a lesson realistically happen?
faqs.answer: Either 8pm with an adult present, or earlier with the session running unsupervised. Those are genuinely different products and worth choosing between rather than defaulting into. For a younger child or anyone who needs supervision, take the later slot and accept the compromise on freshness. For a self-directed Diploma student who wants a marked component and a correction session, the earlier slot is better because they are not exhausted. Whichever you choose, the written note after each session is what keeps a parent on the road in the loop.

faqs.question: Our apartment has no spare room. Does online tuition still work?
faqs.answer: Usually, with two cheap fixes. Headphones remove the household's noise from the lesson and the lesson's noise from the household, and they are the highest-return purchase a family on this page can make. Then agree the arrangement once rather than weekly: one hour, one surface, everyone else told in advance. What does not work is a lesson on a phone propped against something, because screen-shared written work is most of why online delivery is useful, and a student cannot write and watch on a six-inch screen.

faqs.question: When does the Cambridge entry deadline fall, and who tells us the date?
faqs.answer: Months before the papers, and the centre tells you rather than the board. Cambridge gives UAE candidates a June series and a November series, and the extra series examined in February and March is an India entry route, so it is not the calendar an Emirates City family should be working to. For June, final entries close in the spring, roughly four months ahead of the first paper, and the exact date arrives on your child's statement of entry. November follows the same pattern on its own dates: entries close well in advance, and the tier is fixed at entry rather than at the exam. Ask your school's exams officer for the zone-specific timetable in September, since Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the wrong version is the candidate's own risk.

faqs.question: Should my daughter sit the November series or wait for June?
faqs.answer: It depends on when she needs the grade. Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August and to students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A November entry therefore produces a grade in late January, which falls after a number of university application deadlines, and a June entry produces one in late August. That makes the series choice strategic rather than administrative, and it is made at entry, months before anybody is revising seriously.

faqs.question: Why does a visiting tutor cost more than an online one for the same subject?
faqs.answer: Because the drive is inside the rate. Market figures read in October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150 to 300 an hour and in-home visits at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's Dubai table at AED 180 to 350. The gap is travel time, and in Emirates City that travel is substantial: fifteen to twenty minutes each way from central Ajman, thirty to forty-five from Sharjah at 5pm, an hour or more from Dubai in the peak. The household pays again in setup time and in the days the tutor arrives late.

faqs.question: Is there a tutor available for Higher Level chemistry in Ajman this term?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and possibly not, which is why the question is answered before money changes hands. Higher Level specialists in the sciences are genuinely scarce across the northern emirates, more so than in Dubai, and availability is tighter in the autumn term than in the spring. If nobody who teaches that syllabus at that level has a slot in your window, the answer is no with an estimate of when it changes. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the alternative may be a specialist working from outside the UAE on Gulf Standard Time, stated at matching.

faqs.question: Which board does my child's Emirates City school actually use?
faqs.answer: Ask the school office for the exam-entry letter or the statement of entry, which carries the board, the syllabus code and the tier. Cambridge codes look like 0580 and 0625; Pearson Edexcel codes look like 4MA1 and 4PH1. Both are taught in Ajman and in Sharjah, and they set different papers with different mark tariffs, so practice material has to come from the right one. A report card gives you the subject name, which is not enough for a tutor to plan from and not enough for you to buy past papers with.

faqs.question: My son studies alone between 5pm and 7.30pm. How do we make that time count?
faqs.answer: Give it a shape rather than a duration. An unsupervised block works when the task is specific and checkable: twenty questions from a past paper, a set of retrieval questions he marks himself, a section of coursework reading with notes to show. It fails when the instruction is to revise, which for most teenagers means re-reading notes and feeling productive. A weekly session that sets and then checks those tasks turns the empty block into the most valuable part of the week, which is better value than filling it with teaching.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take two children in the same Emirates City apartment?
faqs.answer: Not in the same session, usefully. Two children at different levels or on different boards need different papers and different pacing, and a shared hour short-changes both. What works is consecutive slots on the same evening, with the same tutor where the subjects allow, so one quiet hour becomes two and the household rule is set once. Younger children should take the earlier slot while they can still concentrate, and the exam-year student the later one, when the apartment is quietest.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change tuition for a commuting household?
faqs.answer: It makes the week easier rather than harder, if you plan for it. School days shorten so children are home sooner, working hours shift so a parent may be too, and energy moves to after Iftar. That is the one period of the year when an afternoon slot genuinely works in Emirates City. Practically: shorter sessions more often, heavier analytical work placed where your household actually has energy, and a revision timetable written in February redrafted around those weeks rather than left to collapse in the first one.

faqs.question: Are weekend sessions better than weekday evenings here?
faqs.answer: For anything needing an adult in the room, yes. Friday afternoons and Saturdays are the only times a commuting parent is reliably present and unhurried, which makes them the right slots for a marked timed paper, a coursework decision, or a session where the plan is being set rather than practised. Keep the weekday evening for practice and checking, which a student can do with a tutor and without a parent. Splitting the week that way uses the household's real availability instead of fighting it.

faqs.question: My nephew is at university and helps with coursework. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It can become one without anyone intending it. Submitted work must be the student's own, a school supervisor must see drafts, and the submission is authenticated. Explaining content, questioning a research question and giving feedback on something already written are all legitimate from a relative. Supplying sentences, reorganising the draft on the student's behalf, providing a dataset or handing back a document with new material in it are not. The test at home is whether your son could explain every choice in the piece unprompted; if not, the work has drifted and the consequence falls on him.

faqs.question: Which authority regulates schools in Emirates City, and does it change in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Ajman's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, as are those in Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Cross into Sharjah and the regulator becomes the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods in that emirate. Dubai sits with KHDA and Abu Dhabi with ADEK. For an Emirates City family choosing between a campus on the Emirates Road belt and one in Muwaileh, that means a change of route and a change of regulator, including who approves the fee you will be paying.

ajman/emirates-city.closingHeading: Fix the slot before you choose the tutor
ajman/emirates-city.closingBody: In Emirates City the arrangement fails on scheduling far more often than on teaching. So start there: write down when the school bus returns, when the supervising adult gets home, and which of those two numbers the slot has to respect. Then put the board's entry deadline and timetable in the same calendar, because a parent home at 7.30pm will not catch a bag note. Once the hour is real, the tutor can be chosen on subject and level. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no travel at either end.

ajman/ib-diploma-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma subjects to Ajman students over live video, at Higher and Standard Level. Each works from the student's own marked papers and internal assessment drafts, and reports back in the units the Diploma actually uses: criterion letters, mark allocations and points.

intro.heading: Audit the points before buying the hours
paragraphs: Most Diploma enquiries from the northern emirates arrive in one of two states. Either a parent has seen a report with a grade 3 or 4 in a Higher Level subject and wants it fixed, or a student is eight weeks from the exam window and wants everything fixed. Both are treatable, but neither can be planned until somebody writes down where the points currently stand, and that is an audit rather than a conversation.

The audit is simple arithmetic with uncomfortable answers. Six subjects graded one to seven supply forty-two points, and the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge together can add up to three more. Inside each subject, a share of the grade is already sitting in internally assessed work that has been written, submitted or is in draft. That share cannot be revised for. It can only be improved before the deadline, or lived with afterwards.

This is why the first useful question is not which topics are weak but which points are still in play. A student with an unsubmitted exploration and two months before the internal deadline has more recoverable marks available than a student with three weeks to the first paper and everything already uploaded. The two students need entirely different plans, and the second one needs to be told the truth about what is reachable rather than sold an intensive course covering the whole syllabus.

Ajman adds a practical wrinkle that shapes the plan. Diploma candidates living in the emirate are almost always enrolled in schools in Sharjah or Dubai, so their internal deadlines are set by a school regulated by another authority while their study evenings are governed by a commute on the Emirates Road or through the Sharjah crossing. A fixed late slot that survives a bad traffic day is worth more over two years than a better hour that gets cancelled whenever the road does.

The structure of this page follows that audit. It starts with where the forty-five points come from and which of them are already settled, moves to the internally assessed marks banked before any paper is sat, then to what a predicted grade is actually built from and how the evidence behind one can be strengthened. After that come the boundaries on coursework help, the backwards-counted calendar, the market rates in AED by commitment rather than by hour, and the equivalency question a UAE-bound school leaver eventually meets.

Everything below is written on the basis that teaching happens one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we offer only in India. Market AED figures appear with the provider that published them named, and no IB session or results date is published here, because the IB's own pages cannot be reliably verified in this project and a wrong date on an exam page is worse than no date at all.

ajman/ib-diploma-tutor.programmesIntro: Three things sit under the Diploma heading and families often use the words interchangeably. The distinction matters because the assessment model, the points and the university consequences are different in each.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme, full diploma
programmes.description: Six subjects, normally three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, graded one to seven. Alongside them run the three core components: the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and creativity, activity, service. The Extended Essay and TOK are graded A to E and combine on a published matrix to award up to three further points, giving the forty-five point maximum.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman full-diploma candidates are generally enrolled across the border in Sharjah or Dubai schools. The practical consequence is that the internal deadline calendar that governs their coursework is set by a school in another emirate, so any session plan has to start from that school's dates rather than from a generic programme timeline.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme courses taken individually
programmes.description: Students may take Diploma subjects and receive certificates for them without being registered for the full diploma. The subject assessment is identical, including the internally assessed components, but the core points and the overall award conditions do not apply. Universities treat the result differently, so the choice has consequences well beyond the workload.
programmes.countryNote: This route appears in the UAE where a student has moved curriculum late or where a school cannot staff a particular Higher Level subject. For an Ajman family it is worth asking the school directly which registration their child actually holds, since the answer changes what a tutor should prioritise.

programmes.name: The Extended Essay, TOK and CAS
programmes.description: The Extended Essay is an independent research piece of up to four thousand words supervised in school. Theory of Knowledge is assessed by an essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition. Creativity, activity, service carries no points but must be completed for the diploma to be awarded. Together the essay and TOK contribute up to three points through a published matrix.
programmes.countryNote: The core is where Ajman students most often lose points quietly, because supervision quality varies between schools and the deadlines are internal rather than external. A student who treats the Extended Essay as a background task through Year 12 typically meets it as a crisis in Year 13.

ajman/ib-diploma-tutor.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are described by where the marks sit and where they are lost, because a Diploma plan has to be built on question types rather than on topic lists. In each case the first session reads the most recent marked paper and the current state of the internal assessment.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Method marks are available throughout the structured questions and are routinely thrown away by working done in rough and never transferred. At Higher Level, proof and the harder calculus questions separate the top grades; the exploration adds a separate risk where correct mathematics scores poorly against the engagement and reflection criteria.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics dominate, and the marks hinge on interpretation written in context. A regression or a confidence interval computed correctly and left without a sentence explaining what it means in the scenario is a partially answered question, and the pattern repeats across the papers.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Written answers lose marks on precision of language rather than on understanding: a rate explanation without a named collision or energy reason, an equilibrium answer without direction of shift. In the internally assessed investigation, uncertainty handling and a genuine evaluation of the method are what separate bands.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Data analysis and graph questions carry more marks than students expect, and gradient answers without units are a recurring loss. Multi-mark explanation questions need a chain of reasoning; single-sentence answers to four-mark questions are the most avoidable deduction on the papers.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The volume of content disguises the real issue, which is command-term discipline. Outline, explain, distinguish and evaluate each have a fixed expected depth, and a student who writes at one depth throughout a paper scores unevenly without understanding why.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is assessable in itself, and an explanation that never refers back to the diagram it drew loses marks a simpler answer would keep. Evaluation is the standard divider between a four and a six, and at Higher Level the quantitative questions reward shown working in the same way the maths papers do.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The examined skill is analysis of how meaning is constructed, not what a text is about. Competent summary essays stay in the middle bands indefinitely; the shift happens when every paragraph is anchored to a specific choice and its effect on a reader.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the named organisation in the stimulus is what carries the marks. A correct general explanation of a tool with no reference to the case material is most of a wrong answer, and the same discipline governs the internally assessed research work.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies have to be used as evidence rather than recited, and the command terms distinguish between describing research and evaluating it. The internally assessed experimental study is where method, ethics and statistical treatment have to be handled properly rather than narrated.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed through an essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition. The essay is marked on how well knowledge questions are addressed with sustained argument and real examples; essays that explain concepts without answering the prescribed title lose marks no amount of fluency recovers.

ajman/ib-diploma-tutor.regionsTitle: Diploma students across Ajman, and what shapes their week
ajman/ib-diploma-tutor.regionsIntro: Diploma candidates in Ajman share one feature wherever they live: the school setting their deadlines is usually in another emirate. What differs by district is the length of the daily journey and therefore what time serious work can start.

regions.name: Al Nuaimiya
regions.note: Close to the Sharjah boundary and the easiest part of Ajman from which to reach a Sharjah school. Diploma students here tend to be home by 4.30pm, which makes a 6pm session realistic during term and a later one in coursework weeks.

regions.name: Al Jurf
regions.note: Fast access to Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and to Sharjah schools, but a slow return in the evening peak. Students in this cluster usually hold a single late weekday slot rather than trying to fit two sessions into the week.

regions.name: Al Mowaihat
regions.note: Villa sub-districts with long school runs into Sharjah or Dubai. The common pattern here is a weekend morning session for content teaching plus a short weekday review slot during internal deadline weeks.

regions.name: Al Yasmeen and Al Zahya
regions.note: Emirates Road communities with Dubai commutes for parents and sometimes for students. Diploma families here are the ones most likely to be managing an internal deadline set under KHDA from an Ajman address.

regions.name: Ajman Corniche and Al Rumailah
regions.note: Seafront towers with short local journeys but households where parents return late. Final-year students in this cluster often work best in a 9pm review slot in the weeks before an internal upload deadline.

regions.name: Al Helio and Al Rawda
regions.note: Low-rise villa areas with reliable home internet and usually a quiet room available. The practical advantage for a Diploma student is being able to hold a ninety-minute session without interruption, which matters for paper practice.

regions.name: Emirates City and Al Alia
regions.note: High-rise blocks with the longest daily travel in the emirate for students attending school across the border. Adding any journey to that week is the reason families here rule out in-home arrangements before asking the price.

schoolClusters.city: Diploma schools in Sharjah used by Ajman households
schoolClusters.note: The nearest full Diploma provision for most Ajman families, regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods in the emirate. Internal deadline calendars for Ajman students usually come from here.
schools: The International School of Creative Science, Sharjah

schoolClusters.city: Ajman international schools and the local IB continuum
schoolClusters.note: Private schools in Ajman are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than by an emirate-level authority. Students here reach the IB through the continuum school or move across the border for the Diploma years.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Diploma schools reached from the Ajman side

ajman/ib-diploma-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways Diploma work is bought, distinguished by what they are trying to protect: a grade in a taught subject, marks inside an internal assessment, or the final few points before the papers. Most students need two of the three across two years, not all three at once.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one in a Higher Level subject
modes.description: A standing sixty or ninety minute session in the subject where the points are most at risk, running through the taught course. Content is sequenced against the school's scheme of work, with past-paper question types attached to each topic so that practice is examined practice rather than revision in general.

Reviewed at eight weeks against the opening diagnostic
Usually one Higher Level subject at a time, not three

modes.title: Internal assessment review blocks
modes.description: A defined set of sessions timed to the school's own internal deadlines for an exploration, investigation, research project or the Extended Essay. The tutor reads what exists, maps it against the criterion wording and asks questions. The student does the research and the writing and keeps dated drafts.
bullets: Scheduled backwards from the school's upload or submission date
Feedback given by criterion letter and band, with the descriptor quoted
Skills taught on examples other than the assessed piece itself

modes.title: Final-stretch paper discipline
modes.description: A short intensive block in the weeks before the exam window, limited to timed papers and the marking of them. Not content teaching: the aim is question selection, timing, command-term depth and the transfer of working into the answer space, which is where recoverable marks sit at that stage.

sections.heading: Where the forty-five points come from, and which are already decided
paragraphs: The Diploma total is built from two sources. Six subjects graded one to seven supply up to forty-two points. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are each graded A to E and combine on a published matrix to award up to three further points. Creativity, activity, service earns no points at all but has to be completed, which catches out students who assume anything unscored is optional.

Beyond the total there are award conditions, and they are the part families most often discover late. The diploma is awarded on a published set of requirements covering the overall total, minimum performance at Higher and Standard Level, and specific failing conditions attached to low grades and to the core components. A student can reach a numerically adequate total and still not be awarded the diploma because of a single grade or an incomplete core element. Any school's IB coordinator can confirm the current conditions in writing, and that is the right place to get them rather than from a tutoring page.

The audit worth doing is a table of the student's own position: each subject, its current working grade, what proportion of that grade is already fixed in submitted internal work, and where the remaining marks sit. Done honestly, it usually shows that two or three subjects hold almost all the movable points, which is the opposite of the instinct to buy tuition in everything.

It also surfaces the core, which is where quiet point losses happen. The Extended Essay and TOK between them are worth as much as the difference between a strong and a mediocre overall score for many students, and they are supervised internally with deadlines the school sets. A family auditing their child's position in January of the final year and finding the essay unsubmitted has found the most valuable thing on the list.

sections.heading: The marks banked before any paper is sat
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries internally assessed work, and in most subjects it is a substantial slice of the final grade rather than a formality. The mathematics exploration, the scientific investigation, the business research project, the psychology experimental study, the language oral components: all of these are produced during the course, marked by the school and moderated by the IB. Once the school's deadline passes, those marks are settled.

The exact share varies by subject and changes when a syllabus is revised, so the honest instruction is to read the current subject guide your school is teaching to rather than to trust a number on any tutoring site, including this one. What does not vary is the implication. A student whose internal work is strong walks into the exam room needing less from the papers; a student whose internal work was rushed needs more from the papers than is usually available.

This reframes when tuition is worth buying. Money spent on internal assessment work before the deadline buys marks that are then locked in. The same money spent after the deadline cannot touch them. Families in Ajman frequently book in the final term, when the recoverable territory has shrunk to paper technique alone, and then compare the result against what tuition a year earlier would have reached.

The planning habit that follows is unglamorous and effective. Ask the school, in Year 12, for the internal deadline dates for every subject across both years, and write them on one page. Diploma students carry between six and eight internal deadlines, usually clustered, and the clustering is what breaks students rather than any individual piece of work.

sections.heading: What a predicted grade is made of, and how to strengthen one
paragraphs: University offers in the Diploma system run on predicted grades, which are produced by the school and sent with the application. They are not a formality and they are not negotiable in the way a parent might hope, but they are evidential: a teacher predicting a grade is drawing on mock results, classwork, internal assessment quality and their own judgement of trajectory.

That gives a family something concrete to work with. The route to a stronger prediction is to improve the evidence the teacher is looking at, in the weeks before predictions are finalised rather than after. A full past paper completed under timed conditions and marked, a reworked internal assessment draft submitted before the deadline, a sustained improvement across three topic tests: these are things a subject teacher can point to. An assertion that the student has started private tuition is not.

The conversation with the school matters as much as the work. A parents' evening where you can show two marked attempts at the same question type, several weeks apart, and ask whether the teacher sees the same trajectory, is a different meeting from one where you report that your child is trying harder. Several families in Ajman have used precisely that to get a prediction revisited before the application deadline.

What no tutor can do is forecast a grade, and anyone who offers to is selling something they cannot deliver. A tutor's judgement against published criteria is a planning tool. The prediction belongs to the school, the final grade belongs to the IB, and a provider blurring that distinction is a warning sign rather than a selling point.

sections.heading: The evidence file a Diploma student should hold by January of the final year
paragraphs: By the middle of the final year, a Diploma student should be able to produce a small set of documents on request, and most cannot. The file is not bureaucracy. It is the material from which every remaining decision is made, including which subject to prioritise in the last term and whether to approach the school about a prediction.

Six items cover it. A one-page list of current working grades by subject. The internal deadline dates for every remaining component. The most recent full marked paper in each subject taken at Higher Level. The current state of the Extended Essay, with its dated drafts. The TOK essay title and whatever has been written against it. And a short note of the question types that consistently lose marks, which should be three or four specific things rather than a general sense of weakness.

Assembling that file takes an evening and routinely changes the plan. Families discover that the subject they were worried about holds few movable marks while a subject nobody mentioned has an unsubmitted internal assessment worth more. Students discover that what they believed was a content problem is a timing problem visible in three unfinished papers. Neither discovery requires a tutor; both change what a tutor should be asked to do.

It also gives a straightforward basis for judging tuition that is already being paid for. Pick any week from the record and ask what was wrong at the start of that session and what was still wrong at the end. If nothing in the file answers that, the hours were attendance. If the file shows a reworked draft and two improved marked attempts, the money is working and the question is only whether to continue.
bullets: Working grades by subject, on one page
Every remaining internal deadline, with the date the school set
A recent full marked paper in each Higher Level subject
Dated Extended Essay drafts and the TOK title with progress against it
Three or four named question types that consistently lose marks

sections.heading: Academic honesty on the internal assessment, Extended Essay and TOK
paragraphs: The line here is not a matter of taste, and the consequence of crossing it falls on the student rather than on the provider. Internal assessment work, the Extended Essay and the TOK essay must be the student's own. The student selects the research question, gathers or generates the data, writes every sentence and keeps dated drafts showing how the piece developed. A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on what already exists.

Useful help has a recognisable shape. Reading the criterion descriptors with the student until they can state what each band requires. Asking what a given paragraph is doing in the argument. Noting that a conclusion restates findings where the criterion asks for evaluation of method. Teaching uncertainty treatment, a statistical test or a citation convention on a worked example that is not the student's own assessed piece. All of that is teaching.

What sits outside is equally recognisable. Supplying sentences. Rewriting a section into final form. Choosing the research question. Carrying out the analysis on the student's behalf. Providers in this market advertise completed internal assessments at published prices; a student who buys one risks the entire diploma, and the risk does not expire when the work is submitted. We decline that work, and we state it on the page rather than only in a terms document.

The protective habit is record-keeping. Keep every draft dated. Keep a note of the support received and from whom. If the school asks the student to declare help, declare it accurately. Schools are generally far more troubled by polished work that appears from nowhere than by a student who can show six weeks of visible development and name the feedback they acted on.
bullets: The student selects the question, does the work and writes every sentence
Skills are taught on worked examples other than the assessed piece
Feedback is questions and criterion references, never replacement text
Dated drafts and an accurate declaration of support protect the student

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the exam window without inventing dates
paragraphs: Diploma planning is a backwards-counting exercise, and the dates that matter most are set by the school rather than by the IB. Internal assessment deadlines, mock windows, the Extended Essay submission point and the TOK deadlines are all internal. They arrive in clusters, usually in the first half of the final year, and the clustering is what overwhelms students who have planned around the exam window alone.

On IB session and results dates this page deliberately publishes nothing. The IB's own pages could not be verified within this project, and an exam date that turns out to be wrong is worse than no date, so the only sound instruction is to take the session window, the upload deadlines and the results date from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org directly, and to write them down once rather than rely on a figure seen online.

What can be said with confidence is the shape. Entries and registrations are handled by the school months ahead. Internal components close well before any paper. Mocks are typically positioned to feed predicted grades, which means the mock result has a second job beyond diagnosis. Results arrive in the summer for the main session, with a defined window afterwards for enquiries about results, and a student considering a retake needs to understand that window before it opens rather than after.

For a comparison, the externally published Cambridge and Pearson calendars show how far ahead this machinery runs in a system where the dates can be checked. Pearson's International GCSE November 2026 timetable runs to 19 November 2026, with the entry lodged through the centre in the autumn term, and its November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026 while June 2026 results reached them on 20 August 2026. Cambridge's UAE candidates sit a June or a November series, and for June the final entry closes in the spring, months before the first paper. The lead times in the Diploma are no shorter.

sections.heading: What Diploma tuition costs for an Ajman family, in AED
paragraphs: Diploma work sits at the top of this market because the specialist pool is narrow. Published figures from identifiable providers put qualified online subject tuition at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with one provider publishing IB tuition from AED 200, specialist IB and A-Level work at AED 200 to 450 and above, one provider publishing AED 270, and a premium named-tutor rate published at AED 650. In-home visits in this market run roughly AED 180 to 500, with travel inside the price.

Hourly rates are the wrong unit for a Diploma decision, which is why the table below is organised by commitment instead. A year of weekly support in one Higher Level subject, an internal assessment review block timed to a school deadline, and an eight-week paper-discipline intensive are three different purchases with very different totals, and a family comparing them by hourly rate alone will choose badly.

Published monthly estimates give a second reference point. For a single weekly hour, market estimates in this country run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Package offers seen include about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

None of these is an IB Gram price list. Our quote follows the free trial lesson, because what the audit shows changes the work: a student with one unsubmitted internal assessment and eleven weeks of term left is a different job from a student needing a Higher Level subject taught for a year. Quoting one rate for both would be tidier and less honest.

sections.heading: Online delivery, the in-home market and the permit question
paragraphs: A parent wanting someone in the room for a seventeen-year-old facing a Higher Level paper has a reasonable instinct, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a sales reframe. The advantage is real: presence, fewer distractions, and the ability to see a handwritten working-out as it happens. Against it sits a journey of forty minutes to two hours per session from most tutor bases into Ajman, paid for in the rate, in a later start or in cancellations, plus a tutor pool reduced to whoever is willing to make it.

For a Higher Level subject that reduction is usually decisive. The number of people who can teach Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level to a Diploma standard, and who will drive into Ajman on a Tuesday evening, is small enough that a family may be choosing between availability and expertise. Online delivery removes the journey and widens the pool to a national one. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits anywhere in the UAE, since home visits are a service we offer only in India, so that is a stated limit rather than a quiet one.

Alongside format sits legality, which this market discusses less than it should. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit: the private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE and is granted free of charge for two years. The published eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen.

Two consequences worth knowing. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts is published, so any specific figure quoted to a parent should be treated with scepticism. And Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid tutoring of students at their own school, which is worth checking before asking a class teacher for private Diploma lessons.

sections.heading: What a Diploma is worth in the UAE, and the equivalency question
paragraphs: Ajman families planning for universities inside the UAE eventually meet the Ministry of Education equivalency process, which exists so that a school-leaving certificate from an international curriculum can be recognised locally. It is a ministry process. No tutoring provider performs it, guarantees it or speeds it up, and anyone implying otherwise is describing something they do not control.

On the British track the published requirements are specific. A student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects. One ranking provider publishes a six-subject figure for UAE candidates, which does not match that reported rule.

On the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of five in the IELTS academic test, sixty-one in the TOEFL iBT, or four hundred and fifty in the reading and writing section of the SAT, while mathematics requires at least four hundred and fifty in the SAT Math test. For the IB Diploma, no points threshold is published here, because the figure circulating online could not be verified against an official ministry source. Check it on the ministry's own channel before planning subject choices around it.

The practical point for a Diploma student in Ajman is that subject choice in Year 12 has consequences beyond the points. Mathematics route choice in particular, between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, is a prerequisite question for engineering and economics admissions at several institutions, and it is far cheaper to resolve in Year 12 than to work around in Year 13.

process.title: Run the points audit first
process.description: List each subject, its current working grade, what internal work is already submitted and what remains. That page tells you which two or three subjects hold the movable points, which is usually a shorter list than the one a worried family arrives with.

process.title: Collect the internal deadlines
process.description: Ask the school for every remaining internal assessment, Extended Essay and TOK deadline across both years and put them on one sheet. The clustering is what breaks Diploma students, and it only becomes visible when the dates sit next to each other.

process.title: Take the free trial on the real material
process.description: One session at no charge, with no card details taken, working on the most recent marked paper or the current internal assessment draft rather than a generic exercise. A written note follows, naming what the tutor found and what they would prioritise.

process.title: Buy against the points at risk
process.description: A block aimed at the component where marks are still reachable, with an agreed end point: a reworked draft submitted before the school's deadline, or a second marked paper of the same type. The commitment is quoted as a block rather than as a rolling charge.

process.title: Review, then decide about the next term
process.description: Compare the agreed end point against the opening audit. Continue in that subject, switch to another where more points are now movable, change tutor, or stop. All four are reasonable, and the audit rather than a renewal conversation should decide.

whyPoints.title: Planned in points, reported in marks
whyPoints.description: Sessions are aimed at components where points are still reachable, and feedback comes back with the marks available, the marks awarded and the reason in the mark scheme's language. A parent who does not know the subject can still audit that.

whyPoints.title: Specialists for Higher Level, not substitutes
whyPoints.description: Because teaching is online, the pool for a Higher Level subject is national rather than limited to who will travel into Ajman on a weekday evening. Where we cannot staff a combination properly, we say so instead of placing a generalist.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: On internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the TOK essay the student owns the question, the data and every sentence. We teach skills on other examples, read what exists and ask questions. We turn down requests to supply text.

whyPoints.title: Figures with their sources named
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here belongs to a provider that published it, and none is presented as ours. Our quote follows the trial because the audit changes the work, and one hourly rate for a year of teaching and a five-session draft review would be misleading.

whyPoints.title: No invented exam dates
whyPoints.description: This page publishes no IB session or results date, because we could not verify them from the IB directly. Cambridge and Pearson dates appear where they are published and sourced. A wrong date on an exam page costs a family more than a missing one.

whyPoints.title: Slots that hold across two years
whyPoints.description: Evening starts that work after a Sharjah or Dubai commute, post-Iftar timing during Ramadan, and no cancellation when the roads are bad. Across a two-year programme, reliability produces more marked work than any single outstanding session.

faqs.question: How are the forty-five Diploma points actually made up?
faqs.answer: Six subjects graded one to seven give up to forty-two points. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are each graded A to E and combine on a published matrix to award up to three more, giving forty-five. Creativity, activity, service earns no points but must be completed for the diploma to be awarded. Within each subject, part of the grade comes from internally assessed work marked at school and moderated by the IB, and the rest from externally marked papers. That split is why an audit of what is already submitted matters more than a topic list.

faqs.question: Can a student reach enough points and still not be awarded the diploma?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the thing families discover latest. The award rests on a published set of conditions covering the overall total, minimum performance across Higher and Standard Level, specific failing conditions attached to very low grades, and completion of the core including creativity, activity, service. A numerically adequate total with one grade below the threshold, or an incomplete core element, can still fail the award. Ask your school's IB coordinator for the current conditions in writing rather than relying on any tutoring site, including this one.

faqs.question: How much of my child's Diploma grade is already decided before the exams?
faqs.answer: A substantial part of each subject grade sits in internally assessed work produced during the course: the mathematics exploration, the scientific investigation, research projects, oral components. The exact share differs by subject and changes when a syllabus is revised, so read the current subject guide your school teaches to rather than trusting a figure online. The practical consequence is blunt: money spent on that work before the school's deadline buys marks that then lock in, while the same money spent afterwards cannot reach them at all.

faqs.question: Where does a predicted grade come from, and can it be revisited?
faqs.answer: The school produces it from mock results, classwork, the quality of internal assessment work and the teacher's judgement of trajectory. It is not negotiable in the way families hope, but it is evidential, which means the evidence can be improved before predictions are finalised. A timed full paper completed and marked, a reworked draft submitted before the deadline, or three topic tests showing a sustained direction are things a teacher can point to. A statement that private tuition has started is not.

faqs.question: My child has a three in a Higher Level subject in January. What is realistic?
faqs.answer: It depends almost entirely on what is still movable. If an internal assessment in that subject is unsubmitted or reworkable before the school's deadline, there is real recoverable ground. If everything internal is settled, the remaining territory is paper technique: question selection, timing, command-term depth and transferring working into the answer space. That is worth doing and it is not nothing, but it is a narrower job than a family usually expects. An honest provider will tell you which case you are in before quoting.

faqs.question: What does Diploma tuition cost per hour for a family in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Published market figures put qualified online subject tuition at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with one provider publishing IB from AED 200. Specialist IB work runs about AED 200 to 450 and above; one provider published AED 270 and a premium named-tutor rate of AED 650 has been published. In-home visits sit around AED 180 to 500 because travel is inside the price. For a single weekly hour, market monthly estimates run AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are other providers' figures; ours follows the trial lesson.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give feedback on an Extended Essay draft without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can read what the student has written and ask questions about it, point out that a section describes where the criteria ask for analysis, teach referencing conventions and research discipline on examples that are not the assessed essay, and work through the criterion descriptors until the student can state what each band requires. A tutor must not supply sentences, rewrite a section into final form or choose the research question. Keep dated drafts, and declare the support accurately if the school asks what help was received.

faqs.question: How many points can the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge add?
faqs.answer: Up to three between them. Each is graded A to E and the two grades combine on a published matrix to produce the core points. For many students those three points are the difference between a competitive and an ordinary total, which is out of proportion to the attention they usually receive. Both are supervised internally with deadlines the school sets, so they are also the components most often left late. A family auditing a Diploma position in the final year should check the state of both before looking at anything else.

faqs.question: When should an Ajman Diploma student start the internal assessment work?
faqs.answer: Earlier than the school's deadline implies, because the deadlines cluster. A typical Diploma student carries internal components in several subjects plus the Extended Essay and TOK, and most of those dates fall in the first half of the final year. Starting each piece when the school introduces it, rather than when the deadline appears, is the difference between work that can be redrafted and work that is submitted in whatever state it reaches. Ask in Year 12 for every internal date across both years and put them on one page.

faqs.question: Is the November session worth considering if May goes badly?
faqs.answer: It exists as an option and some UAE students use it, but the decision needs the real dates and conditions rather than general advice, and it has to be made with the school. This page publishes no IB session or results dates, because the IB's own pages could not be verified in this project and a wrong exam date is worse than none. Get the session window, the enquiry-upon-results window and the retake entry deadline from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org, and understand the enquiry window before results arrive rather than after.

faqs.question: Does the UAE equivalency process recognise an IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process and the authority's own channel is the only reliable source for its current requirements. The British-track rules are published: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no lower than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at E. The American track specifies IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT 450 in reading and writing, and SAT Math 450. For the IB, no points figure is published here because it could not be verified officially.

faqs.question: How do Diploma sessions fit around a commute from Ajman into Dubai or Sharjah?
faqs.answer: By being held in the evening and by not requiring anyone to travel. Starts at 7pm or 7.30pm hold reliably from Al Nuaimiya and Al Jurf, later from Emirates City where the daily journey is longest, and final-year students in coursework weeks often take a 9pm review slot. During Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar timing for the month and then return. Over two years the slot that survives a bad traffic day and a parent's travel week produces considerably more marked work than a better hour cancelled twice a month.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram arrange a Diploma tutor to teach at an address in Ajman?
faqs.answer: No. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Diploma teaching for Ajman students is delivered one-to-one over live video with a shared screen for working through papers, and marked work returned in writing afterwards. The trade-off is deliberate. You give up having a person in the room, and you gain access to a Higher Level specialist for the exact subject and level rather than choosing from whoever is willing to drive into the emirate on a weekday evening.

faqs.question: What should be in the evidence file by January of the final year?
faqs.answer: Six things. Current working grades by subject on one page. Every remaining internal deadline with the date the school set. A recent full marked paper in each Higher Level subject. The Extended Essay with its dated drafts. The TOK title and whatever has been written against it. And three or four named question types that consistently lose marks, rather than a general sense of weakness. Assembling that takes an evening and regularly changes which subject a family prioritises in the final term.

faqs.question: Can one Ajman IB Diploma tutor cover two Higher Level subjects for the same student?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, where the combination is a natural pairing such as two sciences or mathematics with physics, and where the tutor genuinely examines both at that level. More often the honest answer is two specialists in two slots, because Higher Level depth is subject-specific and a tutor stretched across two unrelated subjects teaches both at Standard Level depth. Ask which subjects a tutor has actually taught at Higher Level rather than which they can cover. Where we cannot staff the second subject properly, we will say so rather than extend the first tutor into it.

ajman/ib-diploma-tutor.closingHeading: Write the audit, then decide what to buy
ajman/ib-diploma-tutor.closingBody: Before looking for an IB diploma tutor in Ajman, spend an evening on the audit: each subject with its current working grade, what internal work is already submitted, every remaining internal deadline, and the three or four question types that keep losing marks. That single page usually shows that two subjects hold almost all the recoverable points, which is a much smaller and cheaper problem than the one most families arrive with. Send it with the most recent marked paper and any internal assessment draft, take the free trial lesson, and the plan that follows will be aimed at points that are genuinely still in play.

ajman/ib-dp-biology-hl-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover IB Biology at Higher Level: the full theme structure, data-based questions, the extended response in Paper 2, and supervision of the student's own scientific investigation. Pick one, book the free trial, and ask for a marked script at the end of it.

intro.heading: What a marked Biology HL script actually tells you
paragraphs: Biology at Higher Level is the subject where the gap between effort and grade is widest. A student can revise for eleven hours, know the content, and still come back with a 4. The reason is almost never the biology. It is that a Higher Level Biology paper does not ask what a student knows; it asks for a precise number of specific points, phrased in the way a command term demands, inside a word count the student is never shown. A script marked 11 out of 20 on an extended response is not a script from a student who does not understand gene expression. It is a script from a student who wrote four correct points where the mark scheme wanted seven, and wrote them as description where the paper asked for explanation.

That is diagnosable, and the diagnosis sits in a document you already have. Before you pay anyone in Ajman, Sharjah or anywhere else, find the last Biology HL script the school returned. Look at where the pen marks stop. If the teacher's ticks cluster in the first half of every long answer and thin out after that, the student is running out of distinct points, not out of knowledge. If ticks are spread evenly but the total is still low, the student is losing marks on command terms and on the data questions. Those are two different problems and they need two different sorts of hour.

This page is organised around that evidence trail rather than around a sales argument. It sets out where the marks sit in the current Biology guide, what each command term actually requires on paper, how the four investigation criteria are worded and what a draft looks like when it is on track, and what a twelve-week run of sessions should leave behind in writing. If a tutor cannot show you those artefacts, the hours are not working, whatever the student says about feeling more confident.

A word on grade movement, because it is the thing every parent asks and almost every tutoring page answers dishonestly. Nobody can promise a Biology HL grade. What can be shown is movement in the components that make the grade up: raw marks on timed Paper 2 Section A questions, the number of distinct mark-scheme points landed in an extended response, the criteria bands a scientific investigation draft is sitting in. Those are countable week by week. A page that promises a 7 is selling you something it cannot deliver; a tutor who hands back a Paper 2 Section B answer with the mark scheme's seven points listed in the margin, three of them circled as present, is giving you something you can act on.

Ajman adds one practical wrinkle to all of this. A large share of Ajman families work in Dubai or Sharjah, which pushes the realistic start of a weekday session past 19:00, and Biology HL students are frequently the same students carrying Chemistry HL and a Maths course. An hour of travel either way is an hour that was going to be revision. Online delivery is what keeps the hour in the house, and it is also what gives an Ajman student access to a Higher Level Biology specialist rather than to whoever teaches science within a twenty-minute drive of Al Nuaimiya.

ajman/ib-dp-biology-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: An Ajman student arriving at Biology HL has usually come through one of three routes, and each route leaves a different hole. The notes below say what that hole normally is and what evidence shows it has been filled.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Biology at Higher Level runs over roughly 240 taught hours across two years, against about 150 at Standard Level. The extra time is not spread evenly: it concentrates in the additional depth attached to each theme and in the volume of data-handling practice the course assumes. Assessment in the guide currently being sat is two written papers plus the student's own scientific investigation, which carries a fifth of the final mark.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman Academy is the emirate's IB continuum school, so a local Diploma cohort is small and a Higher Level Biology set can be smaller still. That has a direct consequence for evidence: with few students in the room, there is little peer benchmarking, and a student can sit at a 4 for a whole term without it looking unusual. Marked past-paper work becomes the only honest yardstick.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Sciences marks against four criteria, and the written feedback a student has lived with for five years is criterion-shaped: a comment on inquiry and designing, a comment on processing and evaluating. It builds good habits of investigation and poor habits of timed writing, because MYP work is rarely produced against a clock with a mark scheme behind it.
programmes.countryNote: An Ajman Academy student moving up from MYP into Biology HL usually arrives with strong practical instincts and no experience of a mark-scheme point as a unit of currency. The evidence of that transition going well is specific: the first timed Paper 2 Section A attempt scores poorly, and the second, after the command-term work, scores noticeably better on the same topic.

programmes.name: IGCSE and Year 11 into Biology HL
programmes.description: Most Higher Level Biology students in the northern emirates come from Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE Biology rather than from MYP, because the UK curriculum is the largest single curriculum in the UAE private sector. An IGCSE A* in Biology is a weak predictor of a 6 at Higher Level: the content overlaps, the assessment style does not.
programmes.countryNote: The usual Ajman pattern is a student who finished IGCSE Biology at a Sharjah or Ajman British-curriculum school in June and started Higher Level in September with no bridging work. The gap that shows up first is statistics and data interpretation, which IGCSE Biology touches lightly and Paper 1B interrogates directly. Six to eight weeks of targeted data work closes it.

ajman/ib-dp-biology-hl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Higher Level Biology is taught through themes and levels of organisation rather than as a list of chapters, which makes it hard for a parent to see which part is broken. The breakdown below names the areas where marked scripts most often show losses, with what the loss looks like on paper.

subjects.name: Water, carbohydrates, lipids and proteins
subjects.description: Molecular structure questions reward precision in language: hydrogen bonding, cohesion, condensation and hydrolysis each have a required phrasing. Scripts lose marks here by describing a property without naming the structural feature that causes it. The fix is vocabulary drilling against mark schemes, not re-teaching.

subjects.name: Cell structure, membranes and transport
subjects.description: Osmosis and active transport questions frequently carry a data stem. Students who know the biology still lose marks by answering the biology rather than the data, ignoring the graph in front of them. Marked scripts show this as a correct paragraph with no reference to any figure in the question.

subjects.name: Cell cycle, mitosis and meiosis
subjects.description: Higher Level adds depth to the control of the cell cycle and the behaviour of chromosomes, and this is a reliable source of extended-response questions. The commonest loss is stage sequencing written loosely, so an examiner cannot award a point for a process the student has described out of order.

subjects.name: DNA replication, transcription and translation
subjects.description: This cluster produces the longest answers and the widest mark spread on the paper. Higher Level expects named enzymes, directionality and the role of specific sequences. Scripts that score poorly are usually complete in content and short on distinct, separately creditable points.

subjects.name: Gene expression and inheritance
subjects.description: Genetics questions reward working shown as a labelled cross with phenotype ratios stated. Answers written as prose lose marks that the same student would gain by drawing. A tutor should be asking for a diagram before a sentence on every inheritance item.

subjects.name: Gas exchange, transport and homeostasis
subjects.description: Physiology questions are marked on causal chains: a change, a receptor, a response, an effect. Students who list facts about the kidney or the lung score well below students who write four linked clauses. This is a writing-structure problem rather than a knowledge problem.

subjects.name: Nerves, muscles and movement
subjects.description: Higher Level content on action potentials and muscle contraction carries heavy terminology and a strong sequencing demand. Scripts lose marks to vague timing language. Practice here is best done as a spoken explanation before it is written, which online screen-sharing suits well.

subjects.name: Ecology, energy flow and climate
subjects.description: Ecology is frequently the last theme taught and the first one forgotten, and it supplies a disproportionate share of data-based questions. Marked scripts from January mocks show ecology losses more often than any other theme, purely because of when it was covered.

subjects.name: Statistics and data-based questions
subjects.description: Paper 1B is nothing but data. Error bars, standard deviation, correlation against causation and reading a scale correctly are each worth marks, and each is a skill rather than a topic. This is the single highest-yield area for a student on a 4 who already knows the content.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: A fifth of the final grade, marked against four criteria worth six marks each. Most losses are in methodology and evaluation rather than in the biology: an unquantified variable, a sample size never justified, a conclusion stated more strongly than the data allows.

sections.heading: Where the marks sit in Higher Level Biology, and where scripts lose them
paragraphs: In the Biology guide currently being assessed, there is no Paper 3. The grade is built from two written papers and the student's own scientific investigation, and the shift away from the older three-paper structure matters for how you read an old mock result: a script marked under the previous arrangement is not directly comparable to one marked now. Confirm with your child's Diploma coordinator which guide the cohort is sitting before buying any revision material, because second-hand books for the superseded course are still circulating widely in the UAE.

Paper 1 splits into two parts that behave like different examinations. Part A is multiple choice across the whole course, and it punishes thin coverage rather than thin understanding: a student who skipped a sub-topic loses those marks outright with nothing to write their way out of. Part B is data-based, built around unseen material, and it rewards a skill set that has almost nothing to do with memorised content. A student can be strong on one part and weak on the other, and a single Paper 1 percentage hides that completely. Ask for the two parts to be scored separately.

Paper 2 is where Higher Level grades are decided. Section A mixes data analysis with short structured questions; Section B is an extended response chosen from options, worth a substantial block of marks in one go. The commonest pattern in a marked Section B answer is a student who has written a page of accurate biology and earned half the available marks, because the mark scheme lists distinct creditable points and the answer repeated three of them in different words. That is the single most fixable thing in the subject.

The scientific investigation carries a fifth of the final grade and is marked against four criteria of six marks each. It is the only component where the student controls the conditions entirely, and the only one where a deadline is set inside the school rather than by the examination board. It is therefore both the easiest component to improve and the easiest to leave until it is too late to improve.
