sections.heading: Equilibrium and acid-base: where Higher Level candidates lose most
paragraphs: Two topics account for a disproportionate share of lost Higher Level marks, and they lose them in opposite ways. Equilibrium loses marks to incomplete reasoning: a student states which way a system shifts and does not say why, and the mark was for the reason. Acid-base loses marks to arithmetic: the logarithms are unforgiving, and a weak acid treated with the strong acid method produces a pH that is wrong by a predictable amount and earns nothing.

Le Chatelier questions are answered badly more often than any other single item in the subject, and the fault is a habit rather than a misunderstanding. Asked what happens when pressure is increased on a gaseous equilibrium, students write that the position shifts to the right. The mark scheme wants the direction and the reason: that there are fewer moles of gas on the right, so the system reduces pressure by favouring that side. Two marks were available and one was taken. Multiply that across a paper and across a mock season and the cost is substantial. The repair is a sentence pattern, drilled: direction, then because, then the specific property that changed.

Acid-base at Higher Level introduces the dissociation constants, pKa and pKb, buffers and titration curves, and it is the most arithmetically demanding area of the course. The most frequent error is applying the strong acid relationship to a weak acid, which skips the equilibrium entirely. The second most frequent is mishandling the logarithm, usually by taking it of the wrong quantity. The third is a buffer calculation in which the ratio of acid to conjugate base is inverted. All three are procedural, all three are visible on a marked script, and all three respond to a worked pattern repeated on varied systems.

Titration curves deserve separate mention because they are highly scoreable and widely feared. The shape is determined by what is being titrated against what, the equivalence point is identified from the steep section, the half-equivalence point gives pKa directly, and the appropriate indicator follows from the pH at equivalence. That is four facts and a procedure, and a student who has them can answer almost any titration curve question on any system.

sections.heading: Organic mechanisms: curly arrows are a mark scheme, not a drawing
paragraphs: Mechanism questions are among the most predictable marks in Higher Level Chemistry and among the most commonly thrown away, because students treat them as pictures rather than as answers. A mechanism mark is allocated to a specific arrow starting at a specific origin and ending at a specific destination. An arrow drawn from the right place to the right place earns the mark. An arrow that looks approximately correct and starts from the wrong atom does not, however well the student understands the chemistry conceptually.

The Higher Level mechanism set is finite: nucleophilic substitution by both routes, electrophilic addition to alkenes, electrophilic substitution on an aromatic ring, and free-radical substitution with its initiation, propagation and termination steps. Each has a fixed sequence of arrows, a fixed set of intermediates, and a fixed set of things that must be labelled. Learning them as sequences rather than as images is what converts them into reliable marks, and it is the kind of thing that takes two or three sessions of deliberate practice.

There is a reasoning layer on top which separates the stronger candidates. The route a substitution takes depends on the substrate, and explaining why one route is favoured over another - steric accessibility, the stability of the intermediate, the nature of the solvent - is where the extended marks sit. Students who can draw both mechanisms and cannot explain which applies to a given substrate score the drawing marks and lose the explanation ones, which is usually the difference between a 5 and a 6.

The practice format matters here. Drawing a mechanism while watching somebody else draw it teaches almost nothing, because the arrows look obvious in retrospect. The format that works is the student drawing from a blank page, on a substrate they have not seen, with the tutor then marking arrow by arrow against the scheme and naming which arrow earned what. That is screen work, and annotating the same page together is better than sitting beside each other with two sheets of paper.

sections.heading: Paper 1A: forty questions, and the pacing problem nobody practises
paragraphs: At Higher Level, Paper 1A is forty multiple-choice questions spanning the whole syllabus, and it is the component students revise for least deliberately. The usual approach is to do some multiple-choice questions from a revision book, untimed, checking the answers as they go. That builds familiarity with question types and does almost nothing about the actual difficulty, which is that forty items in the time available leave no room for working anything out from first principles.

The students who struggle have a recognisable method. They treat each item as a small problem to be solved, derive the answer, and then check it against the options. On a dozen questions that is fine. Across forty it runs out of time, and the last eight are guessed under pressure. The students who do well recognise rather than derive: they see what the question is about, eliminate two options immediately, and commit. That is a trainable behaviour, and it is trained by timed sets, not by untimed practice.

Two measurable things are worth tracking, because they turn a vague worry into evidence. The first is how many questions the student attempts in a fixed period - twenty minutes, say - which measures pace directly. The second is the ratio of changed answers that moved from right to wrong against those that moved from wrong to right. Most students change answers far more often than helps them, and seeing their own ratio usually stops it immediately. Both numbers move within a few weeks and both are recordable, which makes them good evidence for a six-week review.

There is a content dimension too. Because Paper 1A spans the whole syllabus in single items, a topic that was covered thinly shows up as a cluster of wrong answers rather than as one lost question. That makes the paper a useful diagnostic as well as a component to be revised: sorting a student's wrong answers by topic produces a far more honest coverage audit than asking them which topics they feel unsure about.

sections.heading: Paper 2 long answers: marks go to steps, not to conclusions
paragraphs: Paper 2 carries forty-four per cent of a Higher Level Chemistry grade in two and a half hours, and its extended-response questions are where the most recoverable marks sit. The reason is a mismatch between what students think is being assessed and what is. Students write to arrive at a conclusion. The mark scheme allocates marks to the intermediate steps: the quantity calculated, the principle named, the comparison made, the condition stated. A fluent paragraph that reaches the correct end point without showing those steps collects a fraction of what was available.

The symptom on a script is a correct final answer with two marks out of five beside it, and a student who cannot understand why. The explanation is that three of the five marks were for things they did in their head. Chemistry examiners cannot award marks for reasoning that is not on the page, and in a subject where every answer involves a chain of inference, a great deal of reasoning stays in the student's head unless they have been trained to put it down.

The fix is structural and takes about six weeks of marked writing. Before writing anything, list the steps the answer requires, in order, as bullet points in the margin. Then write each one as a sentence containing the quantity or the principle it establishes. Then read the question again and check that the final sentence answers what was asked rather than what was interesting. Students resist the margin step because it feels like wasted time under exam pressure, and it buys back more time than it costs by preventing the rewrite that follows a wandering answer.

The same discipline is what turns an extended question into a reliable score rather than a gamble. It also makes a tutor's work visible: a marked long answer with the mark-scheme points named beside each line is something a parent can read directly, and it is the clearest available evidence of whether the hour was worth paying for. Ask for one at the end of a free trial, and treat general encouragement without a marked script as the answer to a different question.

sections.heading: Spectroscopy: the most method-driven marks in the subject
paragraphs: Structure determination from spectra is the part of Higher Level Chemistry that most rewards following a procedure, and it is consequently the part where a well-drilled average student can outscore a brighter one who improvises. The procedure is fixed. Establish the molecular formula, usually from the mass spectrum or from percentage composition data. Compute the index of hydrogen deficiency to find out how many rings or double bonds must be present. Read the infrared spectrum for functional groups. Then read the nuclear magnetic resonance spectrum for the carbon skeleton: how many environments, how many hydrogens in each, and what the splitting pattern says about neighbours.

The common failure is doing it backwards. A student looks at the spectra, forms a hypothesis about the structure, and then tries to justify it. If the hypothesis is right they score most of the marks and miss the method ones; if it is wrong they lose the question entirely and cannot see where they went astray. Working forwards from the formula is slower by a minute and far more reliable, and it produces partial credit even when the final structure is not reached.

Nuclear magnetic resonance interpretation is the Higher Level element that needs the most practice, and specifically the splitting patterns. The relationship between the number of neighbouring hydrogens and the number of peaks is simple to state and takes repetition to apply quickly, particularly on molecules with several distinct environments. Integration ratios are the other half: a student who reads the ratio before trying to assign anything has narrowed the possibilities enormously before doing any chemistry.

Because the procedure is fixed, this is also one of the easiest areas in which to demonstrate progress. Give a student an unfamiliar set of spectra at the start of a block and an equivalent set four sessions later, and the difference is visible and countable rather than impressionistic. For a family trying to judge whether tutoring is working, that kind of before-and-after evidence is worth more than a report of improved confidence.

sections.heading: What Higher Level Chemistry opens, and how to check it
paragraphs: Chemistry at Higher Level is taken by a large number of students who do not enjoy it, for one reason: it is a prerequisite or a strong preference for medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, veterinary science, biomedical sciences and several engineering routes. That makes the stakes different from most subjects. A student taking it out of interest can drop to Standard Level if it becomes unmanageable; a student taking it for a medical application usually cannot, and the planning has to reflect that.

The requirement itself must be read from the destination rather than inferred. Entry requirements are set by the admitting institution, differ between two courses with the same name at different universities, and are revised between admissions cycles. Some medical programmes specify Chemistry at Higher Level and a second science; some accept Chemistry with Biology at either level; some add a separate admissions test. Reading the published requirements of the specific programmes a student is considering, and writing to the admissions office where the wording is ambiguous, is the only reliable method.

Alongside university admission sits the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency process, which is a separate thing often confused with it. For the British track the published rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. For the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in SAT reading and writing, and mathematics by at least 450 in SAT Math.

No IB points threshold for equivalency has been confirmed from the Ministry's own pages, so a specific figure quoted to a family should be verified on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject IGCSE requirement, which is not what the source says. IB Gram does not perform, expedite or guarantee equivalency, and tutoring is not required for it. paragraphs: Hourly rates are how tutoring is advertised and monthly totals are how families actually decide, so it is more useful to start from the month. A single weekly ninety-minute session is six hours a month; two sessions a week in an examination term is twelve. Those two numbers, multiplied by a rate, are the real decision, and they produce figures that look very different from an hourly quotation.

Published UAE market rates give the range. Budget online tutoring runs roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at about AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An IB specialist runs AED 200 to AED 450 or more, where TutorChase publishes AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table gives AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Converted to months, a weekly ninety-minute session with a subject specialist is a meaningful commitment rather than an incidental cost, and a family should know the number before the first call rather than after the third invoice. For Higher Level Chemistry specifically, two observations are worth making about where that money goes furthest. A calculation fluency block of three or four sessions is a small purchase with an effect across every topic, so it is usually the best first spend. sections.heading: Where an Ajman Chemistry HL student sits, and what a session can and cannot do
paragraphs: Ajman's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than by an emirate authority, the arrangement u.ae sets out for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Diploma provision in the emirate is concentrated in a single continuum school, which means a large proportion of Higher Level Chemistry students living here attend school in Sharjah or Dubai, under the Sharjah Private Education Authority or KHDA. Their investigation deadline, their mock weeks and their covered-topic list all belong to that school, and those are the documents a tutoring plan has to be built on.

Private tutoring is licensed federally. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since the ministry has not published a schedule of amounts, any figure presented as fact should be treated as unverified. The permit's code of conduct also bars a holder from tutoring students affiliated with their own school.

IB Gram delivers tutoring for UAE families one-to-one over live video. It does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. For Chemistry the honest account of what that covers is specific. Calculation work, mechanism drawing, spectroscopy assignment, long-answer structure, data analysis and every piece of past-paper marking are shared-screen activities in which annotating the same page together is better than two people with two sheets of paper. What it does not cover is handling apparatus, which belongs to the school, and fume-cupboard work in particular has no remote equivalent.

The boundary on coursework is equally worth stating plainly. A tutor may teach chemistry, explain what each investigation criterion rewards, advise on whether a chosen reaction will produce measurable and repeatable data, and read a draft the student has written. A tutor may not supply data, produce the analysis, write any part of the report, or hand over a worked solution for submission. Work that is not the candidate's own is a malpractice matter for the IB and the consequence falls on the student. Some operators in this market sell completed internal assessments; that is the thing to walk away from at any price.

whyPoints.title: Calculation treated as the spine, not a sub-topic
whyPoints.description: Most marks on a Chemistry paper route through converting to moles, applying a ratio and converting back. Five minutes of drill at the start of every session makes that operation automatic, and a student whose attention is no longer consumed by it has attention left for the chemistry.

whyPoints.title: Mechanisms marked arrow by arrow
whyPoints.description: A mechanism mark belongs to a specific arrow from a specific origin, which makes mechanisms scheme-driven rather than impressionistic. Practice means the student drawing from a blank page on an unfamiliar substrate, then the arrows marked individually with the scheme point named.

whyPoints.title: Long answers planned before they are written
whyPoints.description: Paper 2 allocates marks to intermediate steps, not to the conclusion, and most students keep their reasoning in their head. A margin plan listing the required steps takes thirty seconds and buys back the time it costs by preventing the wandering answer that has to be rewritten.

faqs.question: My daughter can explain the chemistry but her marks sit in the middle. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly that she has revised by reading and is being examined on doing. Most marks on a Higher Level Chemistry paper require a quantity to be calculated or a reasoning chain to be written down, and both are performances rather than understandings. A student can hold the concepts well and still be slow and inconsistent at the mole operation the paper keeps asking for, or write a fluent answer that keeps three of the five marked steps in her head. Both are visible on a marked script within ten minutes.

faqs.question: Which single skill gives back the most Chemistry marks?
faqs.answer: Automatic mole calculation. Convert what the question gives into moles, apply the reacting ratio, convert back, check units and significant figures. Energetics, titration, equilibrium, electrochemistry and yield questions all route through it. A student who executes it without thinking has attention left for the chemistry; one who works it out each time is spending their concentration on arithmetic. Five minutes of mixed drill at the start of every session makes it automatic in about a month, with no new content learned.

faqs.question: Why does my son lose marks on Le Chatelier questions he says are easy?
faqs.answer: Because he is giving the direction and not the reason, and the second mark was for the reason. Asked what happens when pressure increases on a gaseous equilibrium, the full answer states which way the position shifts and why - that there are fewer moles of gas on that side, so favouring it reduces the pressure. The repair is a sentence pattern drilled until it is automatic: direction, then because, then the specific property that changed. It is the most commonly dropped mark in the whole subject.

faqs.question: What is the most common arithmetic error in Higher Level acid-base questions?
faqs.answer: Applying the strong acid relationship to a weak acid, which skips the dissociation equilibrium entirely and produces a pH wrong by a predictable amount. Second is mishandling the logarithm, usually by taking it of the wrong quantity. Third is inverting the ratio of acid to conjugate base in a buffer calculation. All three are procedural, all three show on a marked script, and all three respond to one worked pattern repeated on several unfamiliar systems rather than to more explanation.

faqs.question: How should a student prepare for forty multiple-choice questions?
faqs.answer: With timed sets, not untimed practice. Forty items at Higher Level leave no room to derive answers from first principles, and the students who struggle are the ones treating each as a small problem to solve rather than a question to recognise and eliminate options on. Two numbers are worth tracking: how many questions get attempted in a fixed twenty minutes, and the ratio of changed answers that moved from right to wrong. Most students change answers far more often than helps them, and seeing their own figure usually stops it.

faqs.question: Why does a correct final answer only score two marks out of five?
faqs.answer: Because three of the five marks were for steps the student did in their head. Paper 2 allocates marks to the intermediate reasoning - the quantity calculated, the principle named, the comparison made, the condition stated - and an examiner cannot credit reasoning that is not on the page. The fix is a thirty-second margin plan listing the steps the answer requires before writing anything, then one sentence per step containing the quantity or principle it establishes. It takes about six weeks of marked writing to become automatic.

faqs.question: Are organic mechanisms worth learning properly or should we focus elsewhere?
faqs.answer: Worth learning properly, because the set is finite and the marks are predictable. Nucleophilic substitution by both routes, electrophilic addition, electrophilic substitution on an aromatic ring and free-radical substitution cover it, and each has a fixed sequence of arrows and intermediates. A mechanism mark belongs to a specific arrow from a specific origin, so an approximately correct drawing earns nothing. Two or three sessions of drawing from a blank page on unfamiliar substrates, then marking arrow by arrow, converts them into reliable marks.

faqs.question: How do students actually answer a spectroscopy question?
faqs.answer: Forwards, not backwards. Establish the molecular formula, compute the index of hydrogen deficiency to find how many rings or double bonds must exist, read the infrared spectrum for functional groups, then read the nuclear magnetic resonance spectrum for environments, integration ratios and splitting. Students who guess the structure first and justify it afterwards score the lucky cases and lose the method marks. Working forwards is a minute slower and earns partial credit even when the final structure is not reached.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level Chemistry essential for medicine from the UAE?
faqs.answer: Frequently specified, but it must be read from the destination rather than assumed. Entry requirements are set by the admitting institution, differ between two courses with the same name at different universities, and are revised between cycles. Some medical programmes specify Chemistry at Higher Level plus a second science, some accept Chemistry with Biology at either level, and many add a separate admissions test. Read the published requirements of the specific programmes under consideration and write to admissions where the wording is ambiguous.

faqs.question: What does a weekly Chemistry session actually come to per month?
faqs.answer: A weekly ninety-minute session is six hours a month. At published UAE market rates that is roughly AED 270 to AED 900 at the budget tier, where EdFlik lists AED 45 to AED 65 an hour and Tutopiya AED 33 to AED 52; AED 900 to AED 1,800 with a qualified subject tutor, where Unitors publishes IB from AED 200; and AED 1,200 to AED 2,700 with an IB specialist, where TutorChase publishes AED 270 and Bestimate gives AED 200 to AED 450 or more. Advertised monthly packages include AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are other providers' figures, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: What is the best first thing to buy for a stuck Higher Level Chemistry student?
faqs.answer: Usually a calculation fluency block of three or four sessions, because it is small, it is finite, and its effect appears in every topic rather than in one. The worst thing to buy is an open-ended weekly hour with no stated purpose, because chemistry homework will expand to fill it and homework supervision does not move a grade. Ask for a written note saying which of calculation fluency, Higher Level reasoning, long-answer structure or investigation supervision is being bought, and what it will leave behind on paper.

faqs.question: Can online lessons cover the practical side of Chemistry HL?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the limit should be stated rather than talked around. Handling apparatus belongs to the school, and fume-cupboard work has no remote equivalent at all. What online lessons cover is everything else: calculation, mechanism drawing, spectroscopy assignment, long-answer structure, data processing, uncertainty and all past-paper marking, each of which is better done annotating one shared page than with two people holding two sheets of paper. Experimental design can also be worked through fully before the student carries it out.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram arrange a Chemistry tutor to teach at an address in Ajman?
faqs.answer: No. Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video, and IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is offered only in India. The market rate for an in-home visit, for comparison, is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour because travel sits inside the price, with Bestimate giving AED 180 to AED 350. In a small emirate the premium usually buys a generalist rather than somebody who teaches Higher Level Chemistry every week.

faqs.question: Should my child take Chemistry and a second Higher Level science together?
faqs.answer: It depends on laboratory provision and deadline coordination more than on ability. Two Higher Level sciences means about 480 taught hours between them and two scientific investigations with overlapping deadlines, both competing for the same scarce practical time. Laboratory and fume-cupboard provision differs between campuses in Ajman and Sharjah, and it is a fair question to ask a school directly. Ask which weeks each investigation falls in and whether the two departments coordinate, before the subject form is signed.

faqs.question: What makes a Chemistry investigation design work or fail?
faqs.answer: Whether the chosen reaction produces a measurable, repeatable change with the equipment actually available, and whether uncertainty was planned before data collection rather than estimated afterwards. A question that yields three data points or a change too small to measure reliably leaves the analysis with nothing to analyse and the evaluation with only the obvious to say. That is a design decision, taken months before submission, and no amount of redrafting repairs it. It is why the design block is the one worth buying first.

faqs.question: Do tutors working with Ajman families need a licence?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is free. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts has been published.

ajman/ib-dp-chemistry-hl-tutor.closingHeading: Audit the calculation before buying the content
ajman/ib-dp-chemistry-hl-tutor.closingBody: The quickest way to find out what is wrong with a Higher Level Chemistry grade is to set a short mixed series of mole calculations and watch how they are done. A student who writes the setup before reaching for a calculator and converts units on the first line has a reasoning or structure problem. A student who hunts for a half-remembered formula and checks whether the answer looks plausible has a fluency problem, and that one is both cheaper and faster to fix than anybody expects. Send a marked paper, take the free lesson, and let the first ten minutes settle which of the two it is before any content is retaught.

ajman/ib-dp-computer-science-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach Diploma Computer Science rather than programming in general: the core topics, the option your child's school actually runs, the computational solution documentation, and the Higher Level case study. Each profile names the levels taken and the option topics covered, which is the first thing worth checking.

intro.heading: Where the marks in Diploma Computer Science really sit
paragraphs: Computer Science is the Diploma subject where a student's self-assessment is least reliable. A sixteen-year-old who builds working programs for pleasure will tell you the course is fine, and may still be heading for a 4, because the majority of the grade is assessed in writing. Under the current subject guide, Standard Level candidates sit Paper 1 at 45 per cent of the grade, Paper 2 at 25 per cent, and submit the computational solution for the remaining 30 per cent. Higher Level sits a longer Paper 1 at 40 per cent, Paper 2 at 20 per cent, Paper 3 on a released case study at 20 per cent, and the same solution at 20 per cent.

Read that split again and the diagnosis becomes easier. At Standard Level, seventy per cent of the grade is earned by writing about computing under time pressure. Pseudocode in an examination hall, trace tables, explanations of how a processor handles an instruction, descriptions of how a protocol behaves when a packet is lost. None of that is practised by writing an app, and none of it is fixed by a tutor who is primarily a developer. Confirm the current weightings against the copy of the guide your child's school holds before planning around them.

The second structural fact that catches Ajman families is the option. Each school teaches one of four option topics — databases, modelling and simulation, web science, or object-oriented programming — and the choice is made by the department, not the student. Paper 2 is entirely on that option. A quarter of a Standard Level grade therefore rests on material your child may have been taught in a handful of lessons by a teacher whose own background is in a different one of the four.

Then there is the computational solution: 34 marks across five criteria, developed over roughly thirty hours. Criterion A covers planning, B the solution overview, C the development, D the functionality shown in a recorded video, and E the evaluation. Criterion C carries twelve of the thirty-four marks, more than any other, and it is awarded for explaining the techniques used and why they were appropriate. Students who write excellent code and poor documentation routinely score below students whose programs are simpler and whose writing is precise.

Ajman adds a supply problem on top of all this. Diploma Computer Science runs in very few schools in the emirate, and a department is often one teacher. If that teacher's option is web science and your child is strong at object-oriented thinking, there is no second opinion available within a short drive. That scarcity, rather than price, is the real argument for taking these lessons online. The sections below work through each component in turn, say where the marks actually leak, and set out what a weekly hour can and cannot repair.

ajman/ib-dp-computer-science-tutor.programmesIntro: Computer Science sits in group four, among the sciences, and most of this page concerns the Diploma. Students arrive from Middle Years design and mathematics, or from an IGCSE Computer Science course, and the two routes leave very different gaps. programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Middle Years design and digital work is assessed on criteria A to D, with inquiry, development of ideas, creating the solution and evaluation. That structure is genuinely good preparation for the computational solution later, because both reward documented reasoning. What it does not build is examination stamina for written theory, since Middle Years assessment carries no comparable timed paper.
programmes.countryNote: Middle Years provision in Ajman is concentrated at Ajman Academy, with alternatives a commute away in Sharjah. Families here usually contact us at option-choice time asking whether a child who enjoys building things will enjoy Diploma Computer Science. The honest answer is that enjoying building is necessary and nowhere near sufficient, and one session with a past Paper 1 settles the question faster than a conversation.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Both levels cover the core topics: system fundamentals, computer organisation, networks, and computational thinking with problem-solving and programming. Higher Level adds abstract data structures, resource management and control, all three of which are examined in the longer Paper 1 and all three of which are typically taught late in the second year. The computational solution runs alongside from the first year.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma candidates are the audience for this page. Very few Ajman schools run Computer Science to Diploma level, so a student here is often one of three or four in a cohort, with no peer group to compare work against. That isolation is the specific thing online one-to-one fixes: a tutor who has read dozens of solutions can tell your child where theirs sits long before the school's moderation does.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Where a school offers it, the Career-related Programme pairs Diploma courses with a career-related study, and Computer Science is a common pairing with an IT or engineering pathway. Candidates sit the same papers for the Diploma courses they take, so the assessment analysis on this page applies without change. The surrounding workload is lighter on core deadlines.
programmes.countryNote: Career-related places in the northern emirates are scarce, and Ajman families asking about it are generally comparing it with a BTEC or A-Level route in Sharjah. We teach the Computer Science component identically. The scheduling benefit is that reflective-project weeks do not collide with the Extended Essay deadlines, which frees January evenings for solution development.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: A computer science Extended Essay is one of the harder choices in the subject list, because a 4,000-word essay needs a question that can be answered with evidence rather than a project that can be built. Students who want to write code should put that energy into the computational solution, which is assessed, instead of into an essay that rewards argument.
programmes.countryNote: For an Ajman Diploma student the core is mostly a scheduling problem. The solution development window, the Extended Essay interim deadline and the first Theory of Knowledge exhibition draft tend to arrive in the same term, in a household that may already be absorbing a daily commute to Sharjah. We book solution supervision as separate, dated hours rather than folding it into a weekly subject slot.

ajman/ib-dp-computer-science-tutor.subjectsIntro: Below are the parts of the course a tutoring plan is actually built against: the four core topics, the three Higher Level extensions, the option paper and the internally assessed solution. Identify which two of these your child is losing marks in before agreeing to anything weekly — the diagnosis changes the plan completely.

subjects.name: Topic 1: System fundamentals
subjects.description: Planning and installing systems, change management, data migration, usability, and the role of stakeholders in a system's design. Low on technical difficulty and high on marks lost, because answers read as common sense rather than as the specific terminology the mark scheme rewards. The fix is vocabulary drill against past questions.

subjects.name: Topic 2: Computer organisation
subjects.description: Architecture, the fetch-execute cycle, primary and secondary memory, logic gates, binary and hexadecimal representation, and the operating system's role. Students who learned to code without ever meeting a register find this topic genuinely foreign, and it rewards diagram practice far more than reading.

subjects.name: Topic 3: Networks
subjects.description: Network types, standards, the OSI layers, protocols, data packets, transmission media, compression, and wireless security. The most memorisable topic in the course and the one where a disciplined student can bank marks quickly. Questions usually ask what happens when something fails, so prepare failure cases rather than definitions.

subjects.name: Topic 4: Computational thinking and programming
subjects.description: Thinking procedurally and abstractly, flowcharts, pseudocode, trace tables, searching and sorting, arrays and collections. This is the topic where handwritten pseudocode under time pressure separates candidates, because an examiner marks what is on the page and not what the student meant to express.

subjects.name: Topic 5: Abstract data structures
subjects.description: Linked lists, stacks, queues, binary trees, recursion and dynamic data structures. Conceptually the hardest content in the Higher Level course and almost always taught late. Students who delay it until April are preparing the longest Paper 1 section in the least time available, which is a predictable and avoidable loss.

subjects.name: Topic 6: Resource management
subjects.description: How an operating system manages memory, processors, storage and peripherals, including scheduling and virtual memory. Short, examinable and frequently skimmed. Higher Level candidates who can describe a specific scheduling decision and its trade-off pick up marks their peers leave on the table.

subjects.name: Topic 7: Control
subjects.description: Control systems, sensors, actuators, feedback loops, distributed control and the role of microprocessors in embedded systems. The smallest Higher Level extension and the one most often examined with an unfamiliar real-world scenario, which rewards students who have practised applying the vocabulary to something they have never seen.

subjects.name: The option topic and Paper 2
subjects.levels: One of four, chosen by the school
subjects.description: Databases, modelling and simulation, web science, or object-oriented programming, with a Higher Level extension on the same option. Paper 2 examines only this. Find out which option your child's school teaches before booking a tutor, because a tutor strong in a different option is of limited use for a quarter of the grade.

subjects.name: The computational solution
subjects.levels: SL and HL, marked in school
subjects.description: A working product plus documentation, assessed on five criteria worth 34 marks in total: planning, solution overview, development, functionality in a recorded video, and evaluation. Supervision is feedback on the student's own product and prose. Our tutors question design decisions and mark documentation against criteria; they write no code and no sentences.

sections.heading: What the Diploma Computer Science grade is actually made of
paragraphs: Most families begin with a vague sense that their child is 'struggling in computer science' and no sense of which component is responsible. The components are not equivalent, and they do not respond to the same teaching. At Standard Level the written theory paper is the single biggest block of marks in the course; at Higher Level it is still the biggest, with a third paper added on an annually released case study. The internally assessed solution, which absorbs the most student hours by a wide margin, is worth less than either paper.

That mismatch between hours spent and marks available explains most of the disappointing grades we are asked about. A student spends four months building an ambitious product, documents it thinly, and sits a theory paper they have practised twice. The solution rewards documentation more than ambition, and the paper rewards practice. Reversing the time allocation is free, and it is often the single most valuable thing a first consultation produces.

Before you buy any hours, get three facts from the Diploma coordinator: which option the school teaches, what the school's internal deadline for the solution is, and whether your child is entered at Standard or Higher Level. Plans built on assumptions about any of those three go wrong expensively. The table below sets the components side by side; confirm the current figures against your school's copy of the subject guide, because the IB revises these outlines and a superseded version is worse than none.

sections.heading: Paper 1: the theory half, and the five places marks disappear
paragraphs: Paper 1 is written, timed and unforgiving about language. The first place marks disappear is pseudocode on paper. Students who have only ever written code in an editor lose marks to missing loop terminators, undeclared variables and logic that an interpreter would have caught. Handwriting pseudocode for twenty minutes a week, without a machine, closes that gap faster than any amount of further programming practice.

The second is trace tables. A trace table is a mechanical exercise with a right answer, and candidates who rush it lose every dependent mark that follows. The third is terminology in system fundamentals: answers that describe a sensible process in ordinary English score far below answers using the terms the mark scheme lists. The fourth is diagram questions in computer organisation, where a labelled sketch earns marks that a paragraph does not.

The fifth, and the most expensive at Higher Level, is the extension content. Abstract data structures, resource management and control are typically taught in the final two terms, compressed, and then examined in the longest paper of the course. A student meeting recursion and binary trees for the first time in March is in trouble that is entirely predictable in the previous September. Where a family comes to us early, pulling those topics forward is the first thing we recommend, and it costs nothing but reordering. Ask the Diploma coordinator in September when each extension topic is scheduled, and judge the risk from the answer rather than from the mock result in March.

sections.heading: Paper 2: the option, and why your child's option was chosen for them
paragraphs: Paper 2 covers a single option topic from four: databases, modelling and simulation, web science, or object-oriented programming. Your child does not choose it. The department does, usually on the basis of the teacher's own background and the resources already in place, and that choice was often made before your child joined the school. A quarter of a Standard Level grade and a fifth of a Higher Level grade rest on it.

This is where a thin department hurts most. In a school with one Computer Science teacher, the option is whichever one that teacher can deliver, and the teaching may be compressed into a term because the core topics ran long. Students arrive at Paper 2 having seen the option content once. The symptom in a mock paper is distinctive: core questions answered competently and option questions answered in generalities.

The repair is a dated block rather than a weekly rate, because the content is finite and the paper is predictable in shape. Ask the school which option is taught, then ask any prospective tutor to teach a past Paper 2 question from that specific option in the free first lesson. A tutor whose own strength is web science can be excellent and still be the wrong purchase for a student sitting the object-oriented programming option. This is the single most common mismatch we see in Computer Science enquiries from the northern emirates, and it costs a family a term before anyone notices.

sections.heading: The computational solution: 34 marks across five criteria
paragraphs: The computational solution is assessed in school and moderated by the IB, and it is marked against five criteria totalling 34 marks. Criterion A covers planning, including the problem definition and the client or adviser consultation. Criterion B is the solution overview: the design, the record of tasks, the test plan. Criterion C is development. Criterion D is functionality and extensibility, demonstrated in a recorded video. Criterion E is the evaluation, including recommendations for further development.

Students consistently misread where the marks are. Criterion C carries twelve of the thirty-four, more than a third of the total, and it is not awarded for how good the program is. It is awarded for explaining the techniques used, justifying why each was appropriate for the problem, and showing algorithmic thinking. A simple product documented precisely outscores an ambitious product documented loosely, every time, and this is the most reliable mark gain available in the whole course.

Criterion D catches students out differently. The video must show the product working, and features not shown cannot be credited no matter how well they are described in the documentation. We watch the video with the student and list what an examiner will not have seen. Criterion A is where plans go wrong earliest: a problem definition without a real client, or an ambition too large for roughly thirty hours of development, produces a project that cannot be finished and cannot be rescued late in the second year.

sections.heading: Coding ability is not the same as Diploma marks
paragraphs: This is the hardest conversation we have with Computer Science families, and it is worth having early. A student who has written games, automated something at home, or taught themselves a framework has a genuine advantage in one criterion of one component. They have no advantage at all in handwritten pseudocode, in describing the fetch-execute cycle, in the option paper, or in justifying technique choices in formal prose. Several of these students arrive believing the subject is easy and discover otherwise in the second mock.

The mirror case is just as common and much more encouraging. A student who finds programming laborious but writes clearly can score very well, because the written components are most of the grade and the solution rewards documentation. We have supported students whose products were modest and whose final grades were not, purely on the strength of precise Criterion C writing and a disciplined evaluation.

The practical consequence for hiring is that a developer and a Diploma specialist are different purchases. A professional programmer can help a student build something and may give advice that actively costs marks, because industry practice and Criterion C requirements are not the same thing. Ask any prospective tutor which criterion carries the most marks on the solution. If the answer is not Criterion C with twelve, you are talking to a developer rather than to someone who has read the mark scheme, and the hour will be priced as though you were not.

sections.heading: Paper 3 and the Higher Level case study released each year
paragraphs: Higher Level candidates sit a third paper based on a case study the IB releases annually, ahead of the examination session. The case describes a scenario with a technical context, and the questions require core and extension topics to be applied to it, along with terminology specific to the scenario that students are expected to have researched in advance. Schools receive the case through the Diploma coordinator.

It is the most neglected component in the Higher Level course, for an understandable reason: it is worth a fifth of the grade, it arrives while the solution is mid-development, and it has no textbook. Students read the case once, intend to come back to it, and then meet it cold in the examination hall. The specific loss is vocabulary. A case study on, say, a distributed system brings its own terms, and candidates who have not built a glossary cannot write precisely about it.

Paper 3 preparation is genuinely front-loadable, which makes it good value as a dated block rather than as part of an open-ended weekly rate. Useful work looks like this: build the glossary, map which core and extension topics the scenario touches, research the technologies named, and answer the extended question under time. Four to six focused hours in the term the case is released are worth considerably more than the same hours in the final fortnight, when every Higher Level subject is competing for the same few evenings in an Ajman household.

sections.heading: When an Ajman school cannot run the course your child wants
paragraphs: Diploma Computer Science is not offered everywhere in this emirate, and families discover that at the worst possible moment: during option selection in the spring of the Middle Years final year. Private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, and a school's subject offer is a staffing decision rather than a regulatory one, so there is no authority to appeal to about a course that is not timetabled.

Families then weigh four realistic paths. The first is taking the course the school does offer in group four and treating computing as an interest, which is the cheapest and often the right answer. The second is a school move, usually to Sharjah or northern Dubai, where the Diploma offer is wider — a significant decision for a family running a northern-emirates commute. The third is sitting the subject as a private candidate, which needs an examination centre that will accept the entry and a plan for the internally assessed solution; schools and centres set their own policies and fees, so ask before assuming.

The fourth is less dramatic and more common: the school runs the course, thinly, and the family supplements it. That is most of our Computer Science work in this emirate. One specialist hour a week against the component that is actually weak, with the school providing the entry, the moderation and the internal deadlines. The table below sets the four paths against what each one actually demands of a family.

sections.heading: How lessons reach an Ajman household, and what support costs
paragraphs: Computer Science is the clearest case on this site for remote delivery, and the reason is supply rather than price. The published UAE market has a visiting tier at AED 180–500 an hour with travel included, against online tiers of AED 150–300 for a qualified subject teacher and AED 200–450 and above for an IB specialist. In most subjects the extra outlay on a visiting tutor buys convenience. In this one it buys a shortlist of perhaps one person in the emirate who has taught the object-oriented programming option to Higher Level.

So the travel premium here is not buying better teaching; it is buying the nearest teaching. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE — visiting tuition is an India-only service — and lessons for Ajman families run one-to-one over live video. The format happens to suit this subject unusually well: both screens are shareable, the student codes on their own machine while the tutor watches, and documentation is marked in the margin of the actual document rather than described over a table.

For reference, the figures above come from EdFlik's published AED 45–65 entry rate, Tutopiya's AED 33–52, Unitors listing IB from AED 200, TutorChase at AED 270, Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table, and BartyED at AED 650, all read in October 2026. They are those companies' numbers, not ours. IB Gram publishes no hourly list; the free first lesson comes first and the figure is agreed in the consultation after it, which is also where we tell you if nobody suitable is free in your slot.

sections.heading: Permits, the regulator and the questions worth asking first
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated rather than informal. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the private tuition work permit, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The MoHRE service is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing, with a two-working-day completion time and no published fee. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so none is quoted here.

One rule bears directly on Computer Science. Because departments are small, families sometimes ask whether their child's own teacher can tutor them privately. The permit's code of conduct bars a permit holder from serving students affiliated with their own school, and Abu Dhabi's regulator has published professional-ethics rules to the same effect for its schools. We decline those requests. The tutor is the person who moderates the solution, and paying them privately puts both the student and the teacher in an indefensible position.

IB Gram holds no accreditation from any education authority or examination board and claims none. We are an independent matching platform with no premises in the UAE, and a page that implies regulator approval is a page to read sceptically — including ours, if it ever did. The useful questions for any provider are narrow: do you hold the MoHRE permit, which option topic do you teach, how many computational solutions have you supervised, and what is the most marks a criterion carries?

faqs.question: My son codes well but his Computer Science grade is a 4. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly the written components. At Standard Level, Paper 1 and Paper 2 together are seventy per cent of the grade, and neither rewards fluency in an editor. The usual culprits are handwritten pseudocode, rushed trace tables, and answers in ordinary English where the mark scheme wants specific terminology. Send a marked mock paper and the pattern is normally visible in ten minutes. The repair is weekly written practice away from a machine, not more programming, and it moves marks faster than almost anything else in this subject.

faqs.question: Which option topic does my child's Ajman school teach, and why does it matter so much?
faqs.answer: Ask the Diploma coordinator, because the school chooses one of databases, modelling and simulation, web science, or object-oriented programming, and Paper 2 examines only that one. It is a quarter of a Standard Level grade and a fifth of a Higher Level grade. The choice usually reflects the teacher's own background and was often made before your child joined. Booking a tutor without knowing the option is the single most common mistake in Computer Science enquiries from this emirate, because a tutor strong in a different option cannot help with that paper.

faqs.question: How many marks is the computational solution worth, and where are they?
faqs.answer: Thirty-four marks across five criteria. Criterion A covers planning at six marks, B the solution overview at six, C development at twelve, D functionality shown in a recorded video at four, and E evaluation at six. Criterion C is the largest single block and is awarded for explaining and justifying the techniques used, not for how impressive the product is. A modest program with precise development documentation reliably outscores an ambitious one with loose documentation, which is the most dependable mark gain available in this course.

faqs.question: Does a feature count if it works but is not shown in the video?
faqs.answer: No, and this costs marks every year. Criterion D assesses functionality and extensibility as demonstrated in the recording, so a feature that exists in the code but never appears on screen cannot be credited, however well the documentation describes it. We watch the video with the student and list what an examiner will not have seen, which usually takes one session. Re-recording to cover the gaps is permitted and is entirely the student's own work, so it is a safe and unusually cheap improvement.

faqs.question: When should a Higher Level student start work on the Paper 3 case study?
faqs.answer: In the term it is released, not in the final fortnight. The case study is published annually ahead of the session and reaches students through the Diploma coordinator. It is worth a fifth of the Higher Level grade and it has no textbook, so the work is building a glossary of the scenario's own terminology, mapping which core and extension topics it touches, and researching the technologies named. Four to six focused hours early are worth far more than the same hours in April, when every Higher Level subject is competing for the same evenings.

faqs.question: Why are abstract data structures such a problem for Higher Level candidates?
faqs.answer: Because the content is the hardest in the course and is almost always taught last. Linked lists, stacks, queues, binary trees and recursion are abstract, they are examined in the longest paper, and a student meeting them in March has no time to let them settle. Where a family comes to us in the first Diploma year, pulling this topic forward is the first recommendation, and it costs nothing but reordering. Where they come to us in spring, we teach it intensively and accept that the result will be narrower than it needed to be.

faqs.question: Is a professional software developer a good Computer Science tutor?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and sometimes actively unhelpful. A developer can help a student build a product and may give advice that costs marks, because industry practice and the Criterion C requirements are not the same thing. What the course rewards is justified technique choice in formal prose, handwritten pseudocode, and precise topic terminology. A simple test in the free first lesson settles it: ask which criterion carries the most marks on the solution. If the answer is not Criterion C with twelve, you are speaking to a developer rather than a reader of the mark scheme.

faqs.question: Our Ajman school does not timetable Diploma Computer Science. What are the real options?
faqs.answer: Four. Take another group four subject and keep computing as an interest, which is the cheapest and often the right answer. Move to a school in Sharjah or northern Dubai with a wider Diploma offer, accepting the fee change and the commute. Sit as a private candidate, which needs a centre willing to accept the entry and a workable plan for the internally assessed solution, with fees set by that centre. Or supplement a thinly taught course where the school does run it. Subject offer is a staffing decision, so there is no regulator to appeal to.

faqs.question: Can my daughter's own school Computer Science teacher tutor her privately for a fee?
faqs.answer: We decline those requests, and you should treat an offer of them carefully. The MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct barring a holder from serving students affiliated with their own school, and Abu Dhabi's regulator has published professional-ethics rules to the same effect. In this subject the conflict is sharper than usual, because that teacher marks and moderates the computational solution. Paying them privately puts the student's own submission in an indefensible position at moderation, which is a far bigger risk than the convenience is worth.

faqs.question: What may a tutor legitimately do with the computational solution?
faqs.answer: Ask questions about design decisions, teach a technique the student then implements themselves, mark documentation against each criterion's wording, point out that an evaluation claims more than its evidence supports, and watch the functionality video for unshown features. What a tutor may not do is write code, write prose, choose the problem, or hand over a design. Our tutors do not write a student's documentation, and we state that plainly because completed assessed work is sold openly in this market and an IB malpractice finding lands on the student.

faqs.question: How many weekly hours does a Computer Science plan in Ajman usually need?
faqs.answer: One hour a week is the common shape, with extra dated blocks at two points: the option paper intensive in the term before the written papers, and solution supervision across the development window. Students who are badly behind on the Higher Level extension topics sometimes need two hours a week for a term, then drop back to one. Buying a standing two-hour weekly slot for two years is almost always more than the subject needs, and it leaves nothing in the budget for the blocks where the marks actually move.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Computer Science tutor to a house in Ajman?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; visiting tuition is a service we run only in India. Every lesson for an Ajman family is delivered one-to-one over live video. For this subject the format is a genuine advantage rather than a compromise: the student codes on their own machine while the tutor watches the screen, and documentation is marked inside the actual file. The local visiting market does exist at a published AED 180–500 an hour if having someone in the room is non-negotiable for your child.

faqs.question: What does Diploma Computer Science support cost in the UAE market?
faqs.answer: Published figures, read in October 2026, run from AED 45–65 an hour at EdFlik's entry tier and AED 33–52 at Tutopiya's, through AED 150–300 for a qualified subject teacher online with Unitors listing IB from AED 200, to AED 200–450 and above for a specialist, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650. Visiting tutors are quoted at AED 180–500 including travel. Those are their numbers. IB Gram publishes no hourly list; the free first lesson comes before any figure is agreed.

faqs.question: What happens if no Computer Science specialist in our option is free?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than substituting a generalist. This is the thinnest specialism we match for in the northern emirates, and the contested slots are weekday evenings after 7pm, which is exactly when Ajman families commuting from Dubai are available. The realistic options are a different evening, a Saturday block, or a wait of a week or two for the right tutor. If the option topic cannot be matched at all, we say so, because a tutor teaching the wrong option is worse than no tutor for Paper 2.

ajman/ib-dp-economics-hl-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach IB Economics at Higher Level: the four units, the nine key concepts, the quantitative content that only Higher Level students sit, and the three-commentary portfolio. Book the free trial and bring a marked Paper 2 to it.

intro.heading: Why able writers lose marks in Higher Level Economics
paragraphs: Economics attracts the students who read the business pages and argue well at dinner. That is exactly why the subject surprises them. A Higher Level Economics paper is not an essay competition. It is a technical examination with a rigid mark allocation, and a candidate who writes four elegant paragraphs about inflation without drawing a single diagram, defining a single term or reaching a judgement has produced something an examiner cannot reward. The marks are there for specific, nameable acts: a definition, a correctly labelled diagram, an explained causal chain, a figure quoted from the extract, and an evaluative conclusion that actually decides something.

At Higher Level there is a third paper that Standard Level candidates never see, and it is where the grade is usually won or lost. The policy paper asks for calculations and a reasoned policy recommendation, drawing on the quantitative content reserved for Higher Level: multipliers, elasticity arithmetic, the Lorenz curve and Gini coefficient, balance-of-payments figures, terms of trade. Students who have treated Economics as a discursive subject for eighteen months arrive at that paper having never practised arithmetic under timing. The repair is mechanical and it is fast, but it has to be deliberate.

This page is organised around the assessment rather than around a pitch. It explains what each component asks for, how long it lasts and what share of the grade it carries; which diagrams examiners expect to see and how they must be labelled; how the three-commentary portfolio works, including the rules about units, sources and key concepts that cause more lost marks than any economics does; what the Higher Level quantitative content actually contains; and how the command-term ladder from define to evaluate maps onto the mark allocations. By the end you should be able to look at your child's last marked paper and see which of those things is missing.

A note for Ajman households specifically. Ajman's own Diploma provision is small, so a substantial number of Higher Level Economics students here are registered at schools in Sharjah or Dubai and cross an emirate border every morning. That has two consequences. The first is scheduling: with a parent commuting and a school run over the border, a realistic weekday session starts after 19:00, and the late-evening slots fill first across the northern emirates. The second is choice of tutor. Economics at Higher Level, with genuine command of the policy paper, is a narrow specialism, and the number of people who teach it well within a short drive of Al Nuaimiya or Al Rawda is small.

Online delivery answers both. The lesson starts when the student is home rather than when a tutor has crossed Ajman, and the family selects from people who teach Higher Level Economics rather than from those who live nearby. For a subject whose core skill is drawing and annotating diagrams, a shared screen with a drawing surface on it is a better teaching instrument than a notebook on a kitchen table, because the diagram can be built, broken and rebuilt in front of the student and saved afterwards.

ajman/ib-dp-economics-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: Higher Level Economics is taken by students arriving from several different directions, and each arrival brings a predictable weakness. The notes below say what that weakness normally is for an Ajman or Sharjah student and what the first weeks should address.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Higher Level Economics covers four units: an introduction to economics, microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy. Higher Level candidates study additional quantitative material inside those units and sit a third paper built on it. Assessment is three written papers plus a portfolio of three commentaries written on published news articles, with the papers carrying the large majority of the grade.
programmes.countryNote: Economics is one of the most commonly chosen Higher Level subjects in UAE schools, partly because so many families here work in trade, logistics, property and finance, and students arrive with real intuition about exchange rates, oil prices and construction cycles. That intuition helps with the portfolio and hinders the papers, where an examiner rewards the textbook mechanism rather than the student's own commercial sense.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme into Economics
programmes.description: MYP Individuals and Societies builds research and argument, marked against criteria rather than against a mark scheme with discrete points. Students come out able to construct a case and unused to the idea that a diagram without axis labels earns nothing, or that a two-mark definition has a required form.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman Academy students moving up from MYP into Higher Level Economics usually need the first half-term spent on technical convention rather than content: how an examiner expects a diagram drawn, what a definition must contain, and how a mark allocation tells you how long an answer should be. That convention work is quick and it changes scores immediately.

programmes.name: IGCSE Economics or Business Studies into Higher Level
programmes.description: Many students enter Higher Level Economics from Cambridge IGCSE Economics, from Business Studies, or from neither. The ones arriving from Business Studies are the most exposed, because they have learned to answer with application to a company rather than with a model, and Higher Level Economics is a modelling subject.
programmes.countryNote: In the northern emirates the common pattern is a student who sat IGCSE at a Sharjah or Ajman British-curriculum school and started the Diploma without having drawn a market diagram since Year 10. Six weeks of diagram drill, done properly against examiner expectations, closes that gap before macroeconomics starts and makes the rest of the course far cheaper to teach.

programmes.name: Where Higher Level Economics leads
programmes.description: Higher Level Economics is a common entry requirement signal for economics, business, finance and public policy degrees, and the quantitative content in the Higher Level papers is the part that university admissions treat as evidence of readiness. Many economics degrees also expect a mathematics course at Higher Level, which is a separate conversation from this one.
programmes.countryNote: Students in the UAE applying to universities in the Emirates, the United Kingdom or North America should check mathematics requirements alongside Economics, because several economics programmes specify a particular mathematics route rather than any Higher Level mathematics. Requirements should be read on each university's own admissions page rather than taken from a tutoring site.

ajman/ib-dp-economics-hl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Below are the parts of the Higher Level Economics course where marked scripts most often show losses, with what the loss looks like on paper. Several are Higher Level only, which is why a Standard Level revision guide is a poor investment for a Higher Level candidate.

subjects.name: Demand, supply and market equilibrium
subjects.description: The foundation diagram set, and the one students draw sloppily because they learned it first. Missing axis labels, unlabelled equilibrium points and curves shifted without a stated cause are the standard losses. Every later diagram inherits these habits, so this is the cheapest thing in the course to fix properly.

subjects.name: Elasticities and the arithmetic behind them
subjects.description: Price, income and cross elasticity involve calculation as well as interpretation, and Higher Level questions ask for the number and its meaning. Students lose marks by computing correctly and then failing to say what the value implies for a firm or a government.

subjects.name: Market failure and government intervention
subjects.description: Externality diagrams carry welfare loss areas that must be identified and shaded, not merely mentioned. Indirect taxes and subsidies at Higher Level require incidence calculations. Scripts commonly describe the policy and never show the welfare effect the diagram exists to demonstrate.

subjects.name: Aggregate demand, aggregate supply and the multiplier
subjects.description: The Keynesian multiplier and marginal propensities are Higher Level content and appear as calculation. The commonest loss is a correct multiplier value used in no further sentence, when the mark scheme wants the resulting change in output stated and interpreted.

subjects.name: Inflation, unemployment and the Phillips curve
subjects.description: Measurement matters here: constructing a price index, reading unemployment data, and the Higher Level treatment of short-run and long-run Phillips curves. Answers lose marks by discussing the trade-off without drawing it or without naming the type of unemployment under discussion.

subjects.name: Inequality, poverty and the Gini coefficient
subjects.description: The Lorenz curve and the Gini coefficient are Higher Level content and are routinely examined as interpretation of a figure. Students who can describe inequality in words but cannot read a Lorenz curve lose a reliable block of marks in Paper 3.

subjects.name: International trade, protectionism and exchange rates
subjects.description: Tariff diagrams have several areas to identify and each one is a separate mark. At Higher Level, calculations on tariff revenue, consumer and producer surplus and the terms of trade appear, as does the Marshall-Lerner condition and the J-curve effect.

subjects.name: Balance of payments and the current account
subjects.description: Higher Level candidates are asked to work with balance-of-payments accounts numerically and to explain the relationship between the current and financial accounts. This is a favourite source of Paper 3 calculation and it is almost never practised enough before a mock.

subjects.name: Economic development and sustainability
subjects.description: The global economy unit rewards specific country evidence and precise indicator names. Generic development discussion scores poorly; a named policy, a named country and a figure score well. Students in the UAE often have strong material here from the region if they are taught to use it as evidence.

subjects.name: The three-commentary portfolio
subjects.description: Three commentaries of up to 800 words each, on three different units, using three different published sources and three different key concepts. The commonest losses are administrative rather than economic: a source that breaks the recency rule, two commentaries on the same unit, or a word count overrun.

sections.heading: What a Higher Level Economics grade is actually made of
paragraphs: Higher Level candidates sit three written papers and submit a portfolio. Standard Level candidates sit two papers and submit the same kind of portfolio with a larger share of the grade attached to it. Knowing the shape matters because it tells you where tutoring hours have the greatest effect, and because a family buying revision material needs to buy for the right level: a Standard Level guide omits a third of what a Higher Level candidate is examined on.

Paper 1 is the extended-response paper. Candidates choose one question from a selection and answer it in two parts, the first asking for explanation and the second for evaluation. It lasts an hour and a quarter, which sounds generous and is not, because a strong answer contains definitions, at least one fully labelled diagram, a developed causal chain and a judgement. Scripts that run out of time almost always do so because the student wrote an introduction of no value for six minutes.

Paper 2 is data response. Candidates work from extracts and a data set, and the marks are distributed across short definitions, a diagram question, explanation questions, and a longer evaluation that must draw on the material provided. The single most common loss on this paper is an answer that would be identical if the extracts had never been printed. Examiners look for figures and phrases lifted from the text and used as evidence.

Paper 3 is sat only by Higher Level candidates and is the policy paper. It contains compulsory questions mixing calculation with explanation and a recommendation, drawing on the quantitative material reserved for Higher Level. It carries a substantial share of the Higher Level grade and it is the component that the weekly content lesson tends to neglect, because arithmetic feels like a mathematics problem rather than an economics one. The portfolio of three commentaries completes the grade and is marked internally against the published rubric before moderation.

sections.heading: Paper 3 is the paper that decides Higher Level Economics
paragraphs: If a Higher Level Economics student is sitting on a 4 or a 5 and writes well, the probability is high that the policy paper is the problem. It is the only component where a student can lose marks to arithmetic, and the only one that asks for a recommendation defended with a number. Students who have spent eighteen months writing about the economy find the format alien, and the alienation shows up as blank space rather than as wrong answers.

The content drawn on is the Higher Level quantitative material: calculating and interpreting elasticities, the Keynesian multiplier and marginal propensities, index numbers, tariff and subsidy effects with welfare areas quantified, consumer and producer surplus, the Lorenz curve and Gini coefficient, balance-of-payments accounts and the terms of trade. None of it is difficult mathematics. All of it is unfamiliar if it has only been met once, in a lesson, a year ago.

Two technical habits account for most of the recoverable marks. The first is setting out working so that method marks survive a slip: a student who writes the formula, substitutes the figures and then miscalculates still collects marks, while a student who writes only a wrong number collects nothing. The second is answering the second half of every question. A calculation is almost always followed by a demand to interpret, explain or recommend, and an unanswered interpretation is the most frequent single omission on the paper.

The recommendation questions are marked like a policy argument rather than like an essay. The examiner wants the policy named, the mechanism explained, the likely magnitude discussed with reference to the data provided, the limitations acknowledged, and a decision reached. A student who lists three policies and never chooses between them has written the structure of a Standard Level answer and will be marked accordingly. Timed practice is what fixes this, and it works quickly: six to eight properly marked papers typically moves a student more than a term of content revision.
bullets: Write the formula and substitution so method marks survive an arithmetic error
Every calculation is followed by an interpretation demand; answer it
Name a policy, give the mechanism, use the data, then decide
