ajman/ib-dp-extended-essay-tutor.modesIntro: Research mentoring is bought in three shapes, and the right one depends on which part of the trail is missing rather than on how much time is left.

modes.title: Research question audit
modes.description: A single session on the question as currently registered, before any substantial reading is committed. The mentor tests whether it is answerable with the sources and equipment actually available in Ajman, whether it is narrow enough for criterion A, and whether it invites analysis or description. The cheapest intervention in the whole project.
bullets: Question tested against available sources and equipment
Scope checked against the 4,000-word ceiling
Written alternatives offered where the question will not hold
Best used in DP1, before the first reflection session

modes.title: Trail review across a term
modes.description: A fortnightly hour that reads whatever the trail currently contains: reflections, notes, partial sections, the running word count. The output each time is a short written note of what the evidence shows and what the next fortnight should add, written so the supervisor can read it too rather than around them.
bullets: Fortnightly rather than weekly, matching research pace
Reads the RPPF reflections as well as the prose
Notes written to be shared with the school supervisor
Pauses through mock fortnights without penalty

modes.title: Criterion audit on a complete draft
modes.description: One or two sessions on a finished draft, scored criterion by criterion with the marks that are reachable identified separately from the marks that are not. A structural fault in criterion C can still be repaired late; a research question problem usually cannot, and saying so plainly is part of the service.
bullets: Each of the five criteria assessed separately
Word count triage against what the count excludes
Reachable marks separated from unreachable ones
The student makes every change; no prose is supplied

sections.heading: The RPPF: the six marks nobody tells you about
paragraphs: Every Extended Essay is accompanied by a Reflections on Planning and Progress Form. The student records reflections after each of three mandated sessions with their supervisor, using about 500 words in total, and the supervisor adds a comment and countersigns it. The form travels to the examiner with the essay. Those reflections are assessed under the engagement criterion, worth six of the 34 marks available, which is more than presentation and the same as focus and method.

Families discover this late, usually after the essay is submitted. The pattern is predictable: a student who has worked hard on the research treats the form as administration, writes three paragraphs describing what they did, and loses four or five marks that required no additional research at all. A reflection that scores well does something different. It records a decision, the reason for it, and what changed as a result. The initial reflection explains why this question rather than the obvious one. The interim reflection records what the evidence did to the plan. The final one evaluates the process, including what failed.

The practical test is whether a reader can see the student's thinking move between the three entries. Three reflections that could have been written on the same afternoon score low however fluent they are. Three that show a question narrowing, a method being abandoned, or a source turning out to be unusable show engagement in exactly the sense the criterion means. None of this requires the mentor to touch the essay itself.

This is also why the reflections are the best diagnostic available to an Ajman parent who cannot judge the subject content. You can read 500 words of your own child's reflection and ask one question: does this describe activity, or does it describe a decision and its consequence? If it describes activity, there are marks sitting on the table, and they are the easiest marks in the entire component to recover.
bullets: Three mandated reflection sessions: initial, interim and the viva voce
About 500 words of student reflection in total on the RPPF
Assessed under engagement, worth six of the 34 marks
Decisions and consequences score; descriptions of activity do not

sections.heading: The research question log, and what each abandoned version costs
paragraphs: A research question rarely survives in its first form, and it should not. What separates a strong project from a weak one is whether the versions are logged or quietly replaced. A log is three columns on one page: the version, what changed, and why the previous one failed. It takes a minute to maintain, it supplies the raw material for the interim reflection, and it is the single clearest piece of evidence that a student is researching rather than assembling.

The log also prices the project honestly. Narrowing a question in week two costs an afternoon. Discovering in week nine that the evidence does not exist costs the essay. An Ajman student who registers a Chemistry question requiring apparatus their school does not hold, or an Economics question requiring firm-level data nobody publishes, has made a mistake that is cheap on day one and nearly unrecoverable by DP2. A mentor reading a log can see the trajectory and say which version to return to.

There is a family of faults the log exposes immediately. Questions that are really topics, recognisable because they have no verb demanding analysis. Questions phrased as yes or no, which push a student towards a conclusion before the research begins. Questions covering a decade when the word count supports a year. Questions that need primary data from an organisation that has not been asked yet. Each of these is visible in the wording alone, without reading a single source.

The log is also the honest answer to the question families ask most often, which is whether a late start is survivable. It depends entirely on which version of the question the student is on. A student in week nine on version one has not tested anything. A student in week four on version four has done the expensive work already and may finish comfortably. Weeks elapsed is the wrong measure; versions tested is the right one.

sections.heading: What the 4,000 words include, and what sits outside the count
paragraphs: The limit is 4,000 words and an examiner is not required to read beyond it. Anything after the limit scores nothing, which means a long essay is not penalised so much as truncated, and the conclusion that carries the critical thinking marks is often what falls off the end. Understanding what counts is therefore worth more than a style guide.

Inside the count are the introduction, the main body, the conclusion and every quotation. Footnotes count too if they contain commentary rather than a bare reference. Outside the count are the title page, the contents page, maps, charts, diagrams, tables, illustrations, equations and calculations, the citations and references themselves, the bibliography and any appendices. That last exclusion gets misused constantly: an appendix that the argument depends on is effectively part of the essay, and an examiner is under no obligation to read it.

The practical consequence for an Ajman student running long is that triage is possible without destroying the argument. Data presentation often moves into properly labelled tables. Extended quotations are usually paraphrased at a quarter of the length with no loss. Descriptive background that restates a textbook can be cut entirely, because criterion B rewards accurate use of subject knowledge rather than a demonstration of having read about it. A 5,900-word draft is commonly a 4,000-word essay with a 1,900-word tour of the field at the front.

Running short is the rarer and more serious problem. An essay at 2,800 words usually signals a question too narrow to sustain analysis, or research that stopped at description. Padding will not fix it and will cost presentation marks. The honest repair is to widen the question by one controlled dimension and re-read, which is why the word count should be checked against the question in week six rather than in the final week.
bullets: Counted: introduction, main body, conclusion, quotations, commentary footnotes
Not counted: title and contents pages, tables, diagrams, equations, references, bibliography, appendices
An examiner may stop at 4,000 words, so the conclusion must sit inside them
An essay well under length usually signals a question that is too narrow

sections.heading: Criterion C: twelve marks, and the sentence pattern that loses them
paragraphs: Critical thinking carries twelve of the 34 marks, more than any other criterion and more than focus and knowledge combined. It is also the criterion most students believe they have satisfied when they have not, because research that is accurate, well-organised and clearly expressed can still contain almost no evaluation. The diagnostic is a sentence-level one and a parent can apply it.

Take any paragraph of the draft and find the sentence that does the work. If it reports what a source says, or what the data shows, the paragraph is description. If it says what the evidence establishes, what it fails to establish, and why one reading is better supported than another, it is analysis. A draft where nine paragraphs out of twelve report and three argue will land in the middle of the band however good the research was. The fix is not more research. It is a reconstruction the student performs on evidence they already hold.

Three patterns recur in essays from small Diploma cohorts, Ajman included. The literature tour, where the first 1,200 words summarise five sources before the question is addressed. The uninterrogated dataset, where numbers are presented and then described rather than questioned for sampling, source or comparability. And the unearned conclusion, where the final section asserts an answer the body never tested. Each has a standard repair, and each repair is a restructuring of material that already exists.

This is why criterion C is where a late intervention is worth most. A mentor cannot un-register a research question in the final fortnight, and should say so. What they can do is read twelve paragraphs, mark each as report or argument, and hand back a map. The student then rebuilds. Twelve marks are in play and the raw material is already on the page, which is a far better position than the family usually believes they are in.
bullets: Twelve of 34 marks, more than any other single criterion
Test each paragraph: does it report, or does it weigh?
The literature tour, the uninterrogated dataset and the unearned conclusion
Late hours reach criterion C and criterion D; they rarely reach criterion A

sections.heading: The three reflection sessions and the viva voce, in the supervisor's words
paragraphs: Supervision is a school responsibility and the IB recommends between three and five hours of it, including the three mandated reflection sessions. The initial session follows the choice of subject and question. The interim session happens once substantial research has been done. The final session is the viva voce, a short concluding interview after submission of the essay, usually ten to fifteen minutes, in which the student discusses what they did and the supervisor forms a view for the engagement criterion.

The viva voce is not an examination and cannot change a mark the essay has earned, but it does feed the supervisor's comment on the form, and a student who cannot explain their own method in conversation has a visible problem. Preparing for it is legitimate and takes one session: rehearse the question's evolution, the two decisions you would defend, the one thing you would do differently, and the limitation you are most aware of. Students who prepare that way tend to produce better final reflections as well, because the conversation forces the thinking into words.

Where mentoring fits is beside the supervisor, not instead of them. The supervisor sets the internal deadlines, holds the three sessions and signs the form; no external mentor can substitute for any of that. A mentor reads more of the draft than three to five hours allows, at a pace that suits an Ajman family whose evenings start after the commute. The arrangement that works is one where the mentor's notes are written to be shown to the supervisor, which also removes any suggestion that outside help is being concealed.

Families should know what is already paid for. Three to five hours of subject supervision, the internal deadline structure, library and database access, and the form itself all come with the school place. Buying a replacement for those is paying twice. Buying a reader for the drafts the supervisor does not have time to read, in the registered subject, is buying something the school is not providing.
bullets: Three to five hours of school supervision is the IB's recommendation
Initial, interim and final reflection sessions are all mandatory
The viva voce runs roughly ten to fifteen minutes and feeds the engagement criterion
Mentor notes should be written so the school supervisor can read them

sections.heading: Primary data an Ajman student can actually get
paragraphs: A research question that needs data nobody will give you is the most common structural failure in this component, and it is a geography problem as much as a method problem. Ajman is small, its institutions are accessible, and a student here can often arrange in a week what a student in a larger city spends a month chasing. The constraint is the opposite of what families expect: the question is rarely limited by what exists locally, but by whether the student asked early enough.

Workable local sources fall into a few groups. Small businesses along the Corniche and in Al Jurf will usually agree to one recorded interview, which supports a Business Management or Economics registration if it is analysed against a framework rather than summarised. Al Zorah's mangrove and lagoon habitat supports field sampling for Biology or Environmental Systems, subject to permission and a method that an examiner will accept. Museum collections and the creek-side dhow yards carry material for History and Visual Arts. The inland districts of Masfout and Manama are agriculturally distinct from the coast, which supports questions about water use and land.

Three rules keep primary data usable. Ask in writing and keep the reply, because a methodology that cannot evidence consent is a presentation problem and an ethics problem. Collect less than you think you need and analyse it harder, since criterion C rewards interrogation rather than volume. And write the limitations section while the data is being collected, when the flaws are obvious, rather than afterwards when the student has become attached to the dataset.

Secondary routes deserve more respect than they get. A narrow question answered rigorously from published statistics or an archive can outscore a weak primary study, and it removes the scheduling risk entirely. For an Ajman student in DP2 with a term gone, the honest recommendation is often to abandon the interview plan and build the essay on sources that already exist, then spend the saved weeks on criterion C.
bullets: Ask for access in writing in DP1, not in DP2
One interview analysed well beats five summarised
Field sampling at Al Zorah needs permission and a defensible method
A rigorous secondary-source essay can outscore a weak primary study

sections.heading: The line a mentor does not cross, and how to check one before you pay
paragraphs: The essay must be the student's own work. A supervisor or mentor may discuss the question, read and give feedback on drafts, and explain what a criterion means. Nobody may supply prose, restructure the argument on the student's behalf, or hand over a model to adapt. IB Gram does not supply assessed coursework, and there is no deadline situation in which that changes. Several providers in this search space advertise finished Internal Assessments and completed research essays; what they are selling the student is a malpractice investigation.

Proofreading sits in a grey band that is worth being clear about. Correcting a student's spelling of a technical term is feedback. Rewriting sentences to a standard the student cannot produce is substitution, and it is detectable because the register will not match the reflections, the viva voce or the student's other work. The safer and more useful approach is to mark a sample paragraph for the error pattern and let the student apply it across the essay, which also teaches something.

Checking a mentor before paying takes three questions. Will you state in writing that you hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit? Private tuition in the UAE is permitted under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, the permit is granted free of charge for two years, and those working without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published, so any specific amount quoted to you is unverified. Second: may I see a redacted example of written feedback? Third: what will you refuse to do?

The third answer is the one that matters. A mentor who names a limit has thought about the rules; a mentor who promises whatever the deadline requires has not. It is also worth knowing that in Abu Dhabi, professional ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct points the same way. A family should never be arranging for a child's own teacher to be privately paid to supervise their essay.
bullets: Discussion, feedback and criterion explanation are permitted
Supplied prose, restructuring and model answers are not
MoHRE private tuition permit: free of charge, two years, Resolution 710 of 2023
No published fine schedule exists, so treat any quoted amount with scepticism

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the internal deadline, not from an exam date
paragraphs: No IB examination or results date appears on this page, because those have to be confirmed against the IB or a school's Diploma coordinator rather than repeated from secondary sources. For the Extended Essay it hardly matters: the deadline that governs the work is the school's internal submission date, which sits months before anything the IB publishes and varies between campuses. An Ajman student at a Sharjah school and a classmate at an Ajman school may be weeks apart.

So the plan is built backwards from that sheet. Final submission and the viva voce at the end. Before them, the complete draft that the single permitted formal comment is given on. Before that, the interim reflection session, which should follow substantial research rather than precede it. Before that, the research question settled and registered, with the log showing which versions were tested. Earliest of all, the subject choice and the supervisor allocation, which in a small cohort can be constrained by who is available rather than by what the student prefers.

Two Ajman-specific pressures distort this. The mandatory UAE subjects, Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies, run alongside the Diploma under federal rules, so a DP1 week here holds less free time than a plan written elsewhere assumes. And Ramadan shifts the working evening: families routinely move sessions to after Iftar, which a remote mentor accommodates without difficulty. A backwards plan that ignores either will be abandoned by October and replaced with panic in February.

The test of the plan is whether the student can name the next artefact and its date. Not the next topic, the next artefact: the revised question, the interim reflection, the methodology section, the complete draft. If the answer is vague, the plan is decorative. If it is specific, the trail the IB requires will build itself, and the engagement marks come almost free.
bullets: The school's internal deadline governs, not an IB-published date
Only one draft receives a formal supervisor comment
Mandatory UAE subjects reduce the free hours a DP1 week contains
Sessions move after Iftar during Ramadan without penalty

process.title: Send the trail, not a summary
process.description: Share the registered research question, the reflection form as it stands, any draft sections, the current word count and the school's internal deadline sheet. Nothing needs tidying. A messy trail is more diagnostic than a clean summary, because the gaps are where the recoverable marks are.

process.title: Take the first session at no charge
process.description: Forty-five minutes on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled after the Ajman school run and the Sharjah or Dubai commute. The mentor reads the question and the reflections live, asks the student to defend two decisions, and names what is reachable. No card details are taken.

process.title: Read the written note
process.description: Within a day you receive a short note: which criteria are secure, which are at risk, which marks a late intervention can still reach and which it cannot. It is written so the school supervisor can read it too. Decide from that note rather than from a conversation.

process.title: Work in fortnights, not weeks
process.description: Research moves at a different pace from revision, so sessions sit a fortnight apart and each one expects a named artefact: a revised question, a methodology section, an interim reflection, a complete draft. The log and the reflection form are updated as the work happens.

process.title: Close out at submission
process.description: After the internal deadline, the final session is a viva voce rehearsal rather than more editing. The record closes with the question log, the reflections and the criterion notes in one place. Nothing renews automatically, and families who continue usually do so for Theory of Knowledge.

whyPoints.title: The evidence already exists
whyPoints.description: This component comes with a mandated reflection trail and a supervisor signature. Reading that trail is cheaper and more honest than inventing a progress report, and it is why an Ajman family can audit this work without understanding the registered subject.

whyPoints.title: Six easy marks are usually unclaimed
whyPoints.description: The engagement criterion rewards documented decisions and most students write descriptions of activity instead. Those marks need no extra research, which makes them the highest-return hour in the entire project and the first thing a first session looks at.

whyPoints.title: A reader in the registered subject
whyPoints.description: In a small Ajman cohort a supervisor may be reading essays well outside their own field. An external mentor who knows the subject adds the reading the recommended three to five hours cannot cover, without displacing anything the school provides.

whyPoints.title: Reachable marks named honestly
whyPoints.description: A research question fault in the final fortnight cannot be undone and a mentor should say so rather than sell hours. Criterion C and criterion D stay reachable very late, and separating the two is more useful to a family than an encouraging estimate.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built for an Ajman evening
whyPoints.description: Sessions start after the commute from Sharjah or Dubai, move after Iftar through Ramadan, and pause for mock fortnights. Delivery is one-to-one over live video, so no travel window has to be found and no travel time is charged.

whyPoints.title: A stated limit, in writing
whyPoints.description: Reading, questioning and explaining criteria are the job. Supplying prose or polishing a submission to completion are not. In a search space where finished coursework is openly advertised, a written limit is the differentiator that matters most.

faqs.question: What is the RPPF and how much of the Extended Essay mark does it carry?
faqs.answer: The Reflections on Planning and Progress Form records the student's reflections after each of the three mandated supervision sessions, in roughly 500 words in total, with a supervisor comment and signature. It travels to the examiner with the essay and is assessed under the engagement criterion, which is worth six of the 34 available marks. That is the same weighting as focus and method and more than presentation, which surprises most families because nobody describes the form as assessed work.

faqs.question: My son wrote his reflections in one sitting the night before. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It costs marks rather than triggering anything. Reflections are assessed on whether they show thinking that moved: a decision taken, the reason, and what changed because of it. Three entries written on the same evening tend to describe activity in the same voice, which reads exactly as it is. If a reflection session is still outstanding, those marks are recoverable. If all three are submitted, the lesson applies to Theory of Knowledge and to the next cohort rather than to this essay.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my daughter's research question will actually work?
faqs.answer: Read it and ask three things. Does it contain a verb that demands analysis rather than description? Can it be evidenced from sources or equipment she can reach in Ajman within a fortnight? And can 4,000 words cover it, which usually means one place, one period and one controlled comparison rather than a decade and a country. A question that fails any of those is cheap to fix in DP1 and close to unrecoverable in the final term, which is why the audit is the first session we suggest.

faqs.question: Why is critical thinking worth twelve marks when the research took all the time?
faqs.answer: Because the IB is assessing what the student did with the evidence, not how much of it they gathered. Twelve of 34 marks sit in criterion C, which rewards analysis, discussion and evaluation. A paragraph that reports what a source says scores in the lower bands however accurate it is; a paragraph that says what the evidence establishes, what it fails to establish, and why one reading is better supported, scores in the upper ones. The repair uses material the student already holds.

faqs.question: Our draft is 5,800 words. What comes out first without wrecking the argument?
faqs.answer: The background tour at the front, which usually accounts for most of the excess and earns almost nothing. Then extended quotations, which paraphrase to a quarter of the length without loss. Then data description, which moves into labelled tables that sit outside the count. What must never be cut is the conclusion, because an examiner may stop reading at 4,000 words and the critical thinking marks are concentrated at the end. A 5,800-word draft is commonly a sound essay with a 1,800-word preamble.

faqs.question: Which parts of the essay do not count towards the 4,000 words?
faqs.answer: The title page, contents page, maps, charts, diagrams, tables, illustrations, equations and calculations, the citations and references themselves, the bibliography and any appendices all sit outside the count. Inside it are the introduction, main body, conclusion, every quotation, and any footnote containing commentary rather than a bare reference. The exclusion most often abused is the appendix: if the argument depends on it, the examiner is under no obligation to read it, so load-bearing material belongs in the body.

faqs.question: What actually happens in the viva voce, and can my child prepare for it?
faqs.answer: It is the third and final reflection session, a short concluding conversation with the supervisor after the essay is handed in, usually ten to fifteen minutes. It is not an examination and cannot change what the essay earned, but it informs the supervisor's comment and feeds the engagement criterion. Preparation is legitimate and takes one session: the question's evolution, two decisions the student would defend, one thing they would do differently, and the limitation they are most conscious of.

faqs.question: How many hours of supervision is an Ajman school required to give?
faqs.answer: The IB recommends three to five hours of supervision in total, including the three mandated reflection sessions, and that comes with the school place. In a small Diploma cohort the supervisor may be reading essays outside their own subject, which is permitted but means subject-specific source evaluation falls to the student. Paying an external mentor to replace those hours is paying twice; paying one to read drafts the supervisor has no time for, in the registered subject, is buying something different.

faqs.question: Can we arrange for my child's own school teacher to be paid to supervise the essay?
faqs.answer: It should be avoided. In Abu Dhabi, professional ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the code of conduct attached to the MoHRE private tuition work permit points in the same direction. Beyond the rules, it confuses the roles: the supervisor signs the reflection form and sets the internal deadlines, and a paid relationship alongside that puts both the teacher and the student in a difficult position.

faqs.question: Is a Biology or Chemistry registration realistic if our Ajman school has limited laboratory time?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the question is designed around what is actually available. Field data from the Al Zorah mangrove and lagoon habitat supports a Biology question, subject to permission and a defensible sampling method. A Chemistry question built on water hardness or chloride content needs simple apparatus and puts the marks where they belong, in the uncertainty discussion. What does not work is registering a question that assumes equipment the school does not hold and discovering it in DP2.

faqs.question: Does the subject the essay is registered in change how hard it is to supervise in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Considerably. Mathematics and Arabic registrations are the hardest to support locally, because a small school may have nobody free to read them in the registered language or at the required level. English and History are the easiest to start late, since they need no equipment or permissions. The sciences are the most dependent on access. Asking the Diploma coordinator who will actually read the drafts, before registration, prevents the commonest avoidable problem in the whole component.

faqs.question: Can a mentor correct the English in the essay before it is submitted?
faqs.answer: Correcting a misspelled technical term is feedback. Rewriting sentences to a standard the student cannot produce is substitution, and it is visible, because the register will not match the reflections, the viva voce or the student's other work. The useful approach is to mark one paragraph for the error pattern and have the student apply it across the essay themselves. That protects the submission and teaches something; a polished document that is not the student's voice does neither.

faqs.question: We are in DP2 with six weeks left. Is anything still worth doing?
faqs.answer: Yes, but it depends on which version of the research question the student is on rather than on how many weeks remain. Criteria C and D stay reachable late: paragraph-level restructuring from report to argument, and presentation, citation and structure, which is the cheapest repair available. Criterion A is structural and usually cannot be fixed in six weeks. An honest first session separates the two and tells you the ceiling before you buy hours, rather than afterwards.

faqs.question: Does an Extended Essay grade count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Equivalency requirements are set by the Ministry of Education and should be verified on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority directly. No IB points threshold is published here, because that figure has not been read on an official UAE source. For the British track the stated requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from the count, plus one A-Level at grade E or two AS-Levels. Tutoring is never a requirement for a regulatory process.

faqs.question: Can mentoring sessions run during Ramadan and the school holidays in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Yes. Most Ajman families move the slot to after Iftar during Ramadan, which a remote mentor can schedule without any travel implication. Research work also suits holidays better than revision does, because reading and data analysis do not depend on term-time lessons. Sessions pause for mock fortnights and school trips without penalty, and a fortnightly rhythm absorbs those interruptions far better than a weekly commitment that quietly stops being kept.

faqs.question: What if nobody is free who reads the subject our essay is registered in?
faqs.answer: You are told rather than matched with the nearest available person. A general essay reader cannot audit a Mathematics or Arabic A registration, and pretending otherwise wastes the family's money and the student's weeks. The options at that point are to wait for a named slot, book a single session on the reflections and the structure, which is subject-independent, or start with Theory of Knowledge where cover is wider and the two core grades combine anyway.

ajman/ib-dp-extended-essay-tutor.closingHeading: Send the form, the question and the deadline sheet
ajman/ib-dp-extended-essay-tutor.closingBody: The quickest way to find out where an Extended Essay stands is to put three documents in front of someone who reads them for a living: the research question as registered, the reflection form as it currently stands, and the school's internal deadline sheet. That takes one 45-minute session on Gulf Standard Time, costs nothing, and produces a written note you keep and can show the supervisor. It will tell you which criteria are secure, which marks are still reachable, and which are not. Many Ajman families need only that session. The rest decide afterwards, with the evidence in front of them.

ajman/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below are the people we would put in front of a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches student in Ajman: graduate mathematicians who teach this course rather than general maths, who mark Paper 3 under timed conditions, and who can explain a lost method mark to a parent whose own calculus is twenty years behind them.

intro.heading: What Analysis and Approaches HL support actually costs an Ajman family
paragraphs: Almost every enquiry about Higher Level maths in Ajman arrives with a number attached. A parent has been quoted AED 200 by one person, AED 450 by another and AED 650 by a third, all for the same Higher Level course, and nobody has explained why. That spread is real and it is not arbitrary. It tracks four things: whether the tutor teaches the Diploma specifically or maths in general, whether marking timed scripts is inside the hour or billed on top, whether someone is driving across the northern emirates to reach you, and how close the May session is when you call.

The honest starting position is that Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the most expensive hour in Diploma tutoring, and there is a reason for that beyond scarcity. The course runs to 240 taught hours against 150 at Standard Level, it carries a Paper 3 that nothing in the student's prior schooling resembles, and a tutor who can teach proof by induction, Maclaurin series and vector geometry to a student who is behind on all three is a narrower pool than one who can get a Year 10 through quadratics. In Ajman that pool is narrower still, because the emirate has a small number of private schools running the full Diploma and almost no local market in Higher Level specialists.

That scarcity is exactly why this page is written around delivery over live video rather than a visit. A family in Al Rawda or Al Mowaihat searching for someone local is choosing from whoever happens to live within a twenty-minute drive and is free at seven in the evening. The same family working online is choosing from Analysis and Approaches specialists outright, and paying for teaching hours rather than for a car on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India, and this page is clear about that before any money is discussed.

What follows is the arithmetic in full. There is a table of what the UAE market publishes by provider model, with each band attributed to the rate card it came from. There is a second table of the six things that move a Higher Level quote in this emirate specifically. There is a breakdown of where the hours actually go inside the course, because a plan built around Paper 3 and the exploration costs differently from a plan built around catching up on Topic 1, and a family that knows which one it needs stops overpaying for the other.

No figure on this page is an IB Gram price list, and no figure is an invention. Where a band is quoted it belongs to the provider that published it, read in October 2026. Our own model is a free trial lesson first, then an agreed plan with a stated number of sessions, so the cost of the next month is a number you can see rather than a range you have to guess at. If the trial shows that tutoring is not what your child needs, the page below also sets out what to try that costs nothing.

ajman/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: A Higher Level maths problem rarely begins in Year 12. It begins two or three years earlier, in a Middle Years or IGCSE classroom where algebraic fluency was good enough to pass and not good enough to build on. Pricing a Higher Level plan honestly means knowing which of these stages the gap belongs to.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
programmes.description: The Higher Level Analysis route is built on 240 taught hours across five topic areas: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. Higher Level adds content that has no Standard Level counterpart at all, including proof by induction, complex numbers in polar and Euler form, Maclaurin series, vector equations of lines and planes, and the harder integration techniques. Assessment is three written papers plus the mathematical exploration, which is marked internally against five criteria and moderated by the IB.
programmes.countryNote: In Ajman the practical constraint is cohort size. A school running one Higher Level Analysis class of a handful of students cannot timetable a second teacher for it, so a student who falls behind in DP1 has nowhere inside the building to go. Families here commonly reach for paid support earlier in DP1 than families in Dubai do, and that earlier start is also the cheapest version of the intervention.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Mathematics, extended strand
programmes.description: MYP mathematics is reported against four criteria rather than a percentage, which makes it hard for a parent to see an algebra problem coming. The extended strand in MYP 4 and 5 is the designated route into Higher Level Analysis, and the criterion that predicts Higher Level survival is Criterion C, communicating, because it is where setting out a full algebraic argument is assessed. A student scoring well on Criterion A knowledge and poorly on Criterion C will meet Paper 1 badly.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman's IB continuum provision is concentrated in a small number of campuses, so many Higher Level candidates in the emirate arrive from a Middle Years programme that was not extended, or from a British or Indian curriculum school in Ajman or Sharjah. Pricing a Higher Level plan for those students means budgeting for a bridging block first, which is cheaper bought in DP1 than repaired in DP2.

programmes.name: IGCSE and Year 11 bridge into Higher Level Analysis
programmes.description: The jump from an IGCSE Extended maths grade into Higher Level Analysis is the single most underestimated transition in the Diploma. IGCSE rewards a correct answer; Higher Level pays for the argument that reaches it. Students who sat Cambridge 0580 without the Additional Mathematics 0606 paper have usually never met formal proof, radian measure as a working unit, or differentiation from first principles, and all three appear in the first term of DP1.
programmes.countryNote: Most Ajman students entering Higher Level Analysis come through Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE at a school in the emirate or across the border in Sharjah. A six to eight week bridge over the summer between Year 11 and DP1 costs a fraction of a full DP2 rescue, and it is the only point in the whole sequence where the work can be done without a deadline pressing on it.

ajman/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Higher Level Analysis is five topic areas, and they do not cost the same to fix. Below is each one with what it assesses and where the marks actually leak, which is how a plan gets priced honestly rather than by the hour in the abstract.

subjects.name: Number and algebra, Higher Level extensions
subjects.description: Binomial expansion with fractional and negative indices, partial fractions, permutations and combinations, proof by induction, contradiction and counterexample, and complex numbers in Cartesian, modulus-argument and Euler form. Proof is where Higher Level candidates lose most of their Paper 1 marks, because the mark scheme pays for structure and students write conclusions without the step that earns them.

subjects.name: Functions and their transformations
subjects.description: Composite and inverse functions, the modulus function, reciprocal and rational functions, odd and even symmetry, and the sketching of transformed graphs without a calculator. Paper 1 asks for a sketch with intercepts, asymptotes and stationary points labelled; a graph drawn without those labels earns almost nothing even when its shape is right.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry, including vectors
subjects.description: Radian measure, compound and double angle identities, inverse trigonometric functions, and the full vector strand: scalar and vector products, equations of lines and planes, angles between planes and intersection problems. Vectors appear in every paper and are the topic Ajman students most often arrive at Higher Level never having seen, because no IGCSE route covers them.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Discrete and continuous random variables, expectation and variance, the binomial and normal distributions, Bayes' theorem, and conditional probability trees. Higher Level adds probability density functions and transformations of random variables. Marks are lost here to arithmetic set up correctly in the wrong order rather than to misunderstanding, which makes it one of the cheaper topics to repair.

subjects.name: Differential calculus
subjects.description: Differentiation from first principles, the chain, product and quotient rules, implicit differentiation, related rates, concavity and points of inflexion, and optimisation in context. The expensive gap is not technique but reading: students differentiate correctly and answer a question the examiner did not ask, because the command term was analyse rather than find.

subjects.name: Integral calculus and differential equations
subjects.description: Integration by substitution and by parts, partial fractions in integration, volumes of revolution, kinematics as a calculus problem, and first-order differential equations by separation of variables, homogeneous substitution and the integrating factor. This is the heaviest Higher Level strand by teaching hours and the one most likely to need a dedicated block of sessions.

subjects.name: Maclaurin series and limits
subjects.description: L'Hôpital's rule, Maclaurin series from standard results and by differentiation, and the use of series in approximation and integration. It sits late in the DP2 scheme of work, which means a student who is behind by February meets it for the first time weeks before the papers. Budgeting a Higher Level plan without allowing for this topic is the most common planning error.

subjects.name: Paper 3 problem solving
subjects.description: Two extended response questions in one hour, worth a fifth of the Higher Level grade between them. Each question builds a small piece of unfamiliar mathematics through scaffolded parts, so the skill assessed is following a mathematical argument the student has never seen before. It cannot be revised by topic, which is why it is the component families most often pay for separately.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: A piece of independent mathematical writing marked out of twenty against five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. The use of mathematics criterion carries six of the twenty marks and is where Higher Level candidates are judged against Higher Level content, not against effort. Support here is supervision and feedback on the student's own work.

subjects.name: Calculator and technology skills
subjects.description: Graphical calculator fluency is examined in Papers 2 and 3 and absent from Paper 1. Solving numerically, finding intersections, evaluating definite integrals and handling statistical distributions on the device are separate skills from the mathematics itself, and a student who learned the maths on paper will lose time rather than marks until they are drilled.

ajman/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-tutor.regionsIntro: Ajman is compact, but the school run and the commute out of the emirate differ enough between communities to change what time a Higher Level session can realistically start. These are the areas Higher Level enquiries most often come from, with what each one means for scheduling.

regions.name: Al Rawda
regions.note: A large established residential district with a mix of villas and low-rise buildings, close to Ajman's main school corridor. Families here can usually start a session at 17:00 because the school bus arrives early, which makes it the cheapest slot to book before evening demand peaks.

regions.name: Al Mowaihat
regions.note: Villa communities spread along the Emirates Road side of the emirate, with many households commuting into Dubai or Sharjah. A parent returning at 19:00 cannot supervise a 17:00 session, so Higher Level students here are usually booked at 19:30 or 20:00 on two weekday evenings.

regions.name: Al Nuaimiya
regions.note: Dense apartment blocks near Ajman City Centre with a large share of the emirate's school-age population. The practical constraint is a quiet room rather than the hour; Higher Level sessions involve a lot of written working, and a shared bedroom with younger siblings is the most common reason a slot gets moved.

regions.name: Ajman Corniche
regions.note: Towers along the waterfront, many of them households working in Dubai on a full commute. Weekend morning sessions are disproportionately popular here, and a Saturday 10:00 slot for Paper 3 practice is both easier to protect and easier to run at full ninety minutes.

regions.note: Mixed industrial and residential area close to Ajman University and the Sheikh Ammar Bin Humaid Street corridor. Shift-working households are common, so Higher Level plans here are often built on a fortnightly ninety-minute session with written marking in between rather than a fixed weekly hour.

regions.name: Al Zorah and Al Yasmeen
regions.note: Newer low-density developments on the northern side of the emirate, with longer drives to school and to the Sharjah border. The distance is why online delivery matters more here than almost anywhere else in Ajman: a visiting Higher Level specialist would bill the travel, and there are very few to visit in the first place.

regions.note: High-rise residential towers towards the Sharjah boundary, heavily occupied by families whose working day ends in Dubai. Internet quality varies between towers and is worth testing in the free trial lesson rather than discovering in week three of a Paper 3 block.

regions.note: Ajman's two inland exclaves, geographically separated from the coastal emirate and an hour or more from an Ajman school campus. Higher Level maths provision within reach is effectively nil, which makes online one-to-one the only realistic specialist option rather than a preference.

schoolClusters.city: Ajman
schoolClusters.note: Ajman's private schools sit under federal Ministry of Education supervision rather than an emirate-level authority, and the number offering the full Diploma is small. Higher Level Analysis candidates in the emirate are therefore concentrated in a handful of cohorts, and several study it in a class of fewer than ten.

schoolClusters.note: A substantial share of Ajman families cross the border for secondary schooling, which is why a Higher Level plan drawn up for an Ajman address often has to fit a Sharjah school's internal deadlines, mock weeks and exploration submission dates rather than Ajman's.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges for Higher Level maths, by provider model
paragraphs: An Analysis and Approaches HL tutor in the UAE is quoted somewhere between AED 150 and AED 450 an hour by qualified specialists, with budget platforms advertising well below that and one premium provider publishing AED 650. Those are published market figures read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list, and the band a family lands in depends far more on what the hour includes than on where they live.

The table below sets out each provider model with the rate its own published material carries. The pattern worth noticing is that the cheap end of the market is cheap because it is selling something narrower: a slot with a university-student tutor, a group of four to ten, or a fixed syllabus pace that does not bend to a student's particular gap. None of that is dishonest, and for a student who is broadly on track and needs company while practising, it is good value. For a Higher Level candidate who cannot start a proof by induction, it is money spent on the wrong thing.

The other pattern is that in-home delivery sits at a premium across every tier, and the premium is travel. A tutor crossing from Dubai or Sharjah into Ajman at six in the evening is giving up an hour of billable time each way, and that hour is inside the rate whether or not the invoice itemises it. That is the single clearest argument for buying Higher Level hours online, and it is an arithmetic argument rather than a marketing one.

Three of the six ranking providers in this market publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars. A UAE family transacting in dirhams should treat an unpublished rate as a signal to ask for the hourly figure, the session length, what marking is included and whether the figure covers a sixty or a ninety-minute slot, before the first session rather than after it.

sections.heading: The six things that move a Higher Level quote in this emirate
paragraphs: Two Ajman families can be quoted AED 180 and AED 420 for the same course in the same week, and both quotes can be fair. The variables are knowable, and a parent who asks about them directly stops being quoted a number and starts being quoted a plan. The table sets out each one with what pushes it to the bottom or the top of its range.

Scarcity is the first and biggest. Higher Level Analysis is the narrowest maths specialism in the Diploma, and the supply of people who can teach Maclaurin series and vector planes to a struggling DP2 student is not a large pool anywhere in the UAE. In Ajman specifically, where the emirate's Diploma cohorts are small, a locally resident Higher Level specialist is close to a statistical accident. That is what an online-first model is actually buying: access to the whole specialist pool rather than to the subset within driving distance.

Timing is the second, and it is the one families control. A plan started in September of DP1 is bought in ordinary weekly hours. The same repair attempted in March of DP2 is bought in intensives, at a point when every specialist's evening slots are already taken and the honest answer to a late enquiry is sometimes that nobody suitable is free. Rates climb close to the session across this market, and availability tightens before the rate does.

The rest is scope. Whether timed marking sits inside the hour, whether exploration supervision is counted separately, whether a ninety-minute slot is priced at one and a half hours or at a block rate, and whether the tutor writes anything down for the parent. None of those are standard across the market, which means an hourly figure on its own tells a family almost nothing.

sections.heading: Paper 3 is the hour you are really paying for
paragraphs: Higher Level Analysis is examined by three papers. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and rewards algebraic control. Paper 2 allows a graphical calculator and rewards knowing when to use it. Paper 3 is one hour, two extended questions, and a fifth of the final grade, and it is unlike anything else in the student's school career.

Each Paper 3 question invents a small piece of mathematics in its stem and then walks the candidate through it in scaffolded parts. A question might define an unfamiliar sequence, ask for a few terms, ask for a conjecture, then ask for a proof of the conjecture by induction. The mathematics required is all on the syllabus; the skill being examined is reading a mathematical argument that the student has never met and keeping hold of the thread for an hour.

This is why Paper 3 cannot be revised by topic and why it is the component families most often buy separately. Practising thirty questions on integration does nothing for it. What works is sitting whole past Paper 3 questions under the real one-hour constraint, then having the script marked line by line against the published mark scheme so that method marks are separated from accuracy marks and the student sees exactly where the argument was abandoned.

For an Ajman student the practical consequence is scheduling. A Paper 3 block needs a protected ninety-minute slot, because an hour-long paper plus review does not fit in an hour. Weekend mornings work better than weekday evenings for this, particularly for families commuting back from Dubai or Sharjah, and a Saturday slot booked in January is a slot that still exists in March.

sections.heading: Online hours against an Ajman doorstep: the arithmetic
paragraphs: The comparison most families actually want is not online versus in-home in the abstract. It is this: for the money available, does my child get more Higher Level maths from a specialist on a screen or from whoever can reach Al Mowaihat by seven? The table answers it with the variables that matter in this emirate.

Travel is the first line of the sum and the one most often left out. A visiting tutor reaching Ajman from Dubai in evening traffic spends between forty and seventy minutes each way, and that time is paid for somewhere. It is either inside the hourly rate, which is why in-home bands sit above online ones across every published tier, or it is absorbed by the tutor, in which case the arrangement does not last a full academic year. Neither outcome favours the family.

The second line is the pool. Ajman's Diploma cohorts are small, and Higher Level Analysis is the narrowest maths specialism the Diploma has. The number of people within a twenty-minute drive of Al Rawda who can teach vector planes and Maclaurin series to a student who is on a grade 3 is very small. The number who can do it, are free at the hour your child is awake and alert, and can mark a Paper 3 script properly, is smaller again.

The honest entry on the other side of the ledger is supervision. A tutor in the room can see a phone being picked up and can read a page of working upside down from across a table. Online, that has to be engineered: the camera on the page, the working photographed and sent, a written note after each session so a parent who was still on the Dubai road knows what happened. That is a real design problem and this page would rather name it than pretend it away.

sections.heading: Pricing the course by where the hours go
paragraphs: An hourly rate is only half a budget. The other half is how many hours, and that depends entirely on which part of Higher Level Analysis has gone wrong. Three families quoted the same AED 250 can end the year having spent very different amounts, because one needed a bridge, one needed a paper and one needed a rescue.

A bridging plan is the cheapest. A student entering DP1 from IGCSE who has never met radians as a working unit, differentiation from first principles or formal proof needs a block of six to eight sessions over a summer, with no deadline pressing and no mock results to react to. Bought at that point, the work is ordinary teaching. Bought in DP2, the same content has to be taught while the class is three topics further on, which doubles the hours and raises the rate because it is now exam-term work.

A component plan is the middle case. A student who is broadly fluent but drops marks on Paper 1 sketching, or who cannot start a Paper 3 question, needs a defined block aimed at that component. This is the easiest thing to price honestly, because the number of sessions can be stated at the start and the evidence of whether it worked is a marked script rather than a feeling.

The rescue is the expensive case and the one to avoid arriving at. A Higher Level student on a grade 3 in February of DP2, with an exploration not yet drafted and three topics unmet, is buying intensives in the weeks when every specialist's diary is already full. Sometimes the honest answer at that point is that a move to Standard Level with the school's agreement is a better purchase than any number of hours, and a tutor who will not say so is not worth the rate.

sections.heading: The exploration: twenty marks, five criteria and what support costs
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration carries a fifth of the Higher Level grade and is marked out of twenty against five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics. The last of those carries six of the twenty marks and is the only criterion where a Higher Level candidate is judged against Higher Level content rather than against process. A competent piece of work built on Standard Level mathematics is capped there, and no amount of polish lifts it.

Most of the money families spend on exploration support is spent at the wrong end. A student who has already written fifteen pages on a topic with no Higher Level mathematics in it is paying for damage repair. The same spend at the topic-selection stage, two or three sessions asking whether the mathematics is reachable, whether the data exists and whether the question can be answered at all, is the highest-value purchase in the whole Higher Level plan.

The limits here are not negotiable and they are not ours. Under IB academic honesty rules the exploration must be the student's own work, and the authenticity declaration your child signs is a real commitment. A tutor may question a topic, teach a technique the student needs, read a draft the student has produced and give feedback against the criteria. A tutor may not supply text, restructure the argument on the student's behalf or produce any part of the finished piece. Any provider offering a finished exploration is offering your child a malpractice investigation.

Practically, exploration supervision is bought as a small number of scheduled sessions rather than as weekly hours, and it has to be timed to the school's internal deadline rather than to the IB's. An Ajman student at a Sharjah school is working to that school's calendar, which is one more reason the plan starts with asking for the school's own dated deadline sheet.

sections.heading: Who may legally charge you for a maths hour in Ajman
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated. The route is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page for it lists no fee and a two working day completion time, applied for through the ministry's app, website and e-services system.

Two consequences follow for a family comparing quotes. First, nobody should be adding a permit fee to your hourly rate, because there is no fee to pass on. Second, individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure for it appears on this page. Asking a tutor directly whether they hold the permit is a reasonable question and a quick one to answer.

There is a separate position for a tutoring operation with premises and staff, which needs an educational services permit as a training institute from the relevant authority rather than an individual tutor permit. The distinction matters when comparing an online one-to-one arrangement with a centre near Ajman City Centre: the centre is a licensed premises with a syllabus pace, while the permit route covers an individual teaching one student at a time.

In Abu Dhabi, press-reported professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's own code of conduct carries a comparable restriction. For an Ajman family the practical reading is simple: a child's own classroom teacher is the wrong person to pay, regardless of emirate, and a tutor who offers that arrangement is telling you something about how they read the rules.

sections.heading: Spending nothing first: what to try before paying anyone
paragraphs: A page written around cost should be honest about the hours that cost nothing, because some Higher Level problems are solved by them and a provider that pretends otherwise is selling rather than advising. Four things are worth doing before a single dirham changes hands, and together they take a weekend.

Ask the school for the subject's dated deadline sheet and the mark breakdown from the last internal assessment, component by component. A Higher Level student losing marks on Paper 1 and holding up on Paper 2 has a non-calculator algebra problem, which is a different purchase from a student who is weak across both. Without that split, any tutoring plan is a guess, and you will pay for the guessing.

Then read the last marked script with your child, not for the total but for where the working stopped. Higher Level mark schemes pay for method, and the commonest pattern in a Higher Level script is a student who knew the technique and never wrote the line that earned the mark. If that is what the script shows, the fix is habit rather than content, and it is cheaper and faster than it feels.

Third, ask the subject teacher directly what they would do with an extra ninety minutes a week. Teachers answer this question well and are not usually asked it. Fourth, use the free trial lesson as a diagnostic rather than as a sample: send the marked script in advance, ask for a written diagnosis afterwards and decide on the basis of that document. One free trial lesson per student, no card details required, and if the diagnosis says tutoring is not the answer, that is a useful free outcome rather than a failed sale.

process.title: Send the evidence, not the worry
process.description: Start with three documents: the most recent marked Higher Level script, the component mark breakdown, and the school's dated deadline sheet for the exploration. Those three tell a specialist more in ten minutes than a conversation does in an hour, and they are what makes the first quote a plan rather than a range.

process.title: Free trial lesson, used as a diagnosis
process.description: One free trial lesson per student, with no card details required. The tutor works a problem with your child, probes where the method breaks and writes a short diagnosis afterwards naming the component at fault. You decide after reading that document, not during the call.

process.title: Agree the plan and the number
process.description: A written plan with the number of sessions, the session length, what marking is included and what the month costs. Higher Level work is usually ninety minutes rather than sixty, and a block aimed at Paper 3 or the exploration is stated separately so you can see what each part of the plan is buying.

process.title: Weekly teaching with marked evidence
process.description: Sessions run on live video on Gulf Standard Time, with written working photographed and marked between them. After each session you get a short note in plain English: what was taught, what was practised, what is still wrong. That note is the thing to read if you are deciding whether to continue.

process.title: Review at four weeks against the script
process.description: Four weeks in, the question is whether the marked scripts have moved, not whether everyone feels better. If the component at fault has not shifted, we change tutor, change approach or say plainly that tutoring is not the lever. A review date fixed at the start is what makes that conversation easy to have.

Three of the providers ranking for this search publish no price at all and two quote in dollars, so a dirham figure with a source attached is the least a UAE family should expect before a first session.

whyPoints.description: Proof by induction, vector planes, Maclaurin series and Paper 3 are Higher Level content with no Standard Level counterpart. whyPoints.description: Timed scripts marked against the published mark scheme, with method marks separated from accuracy marks, and a written note after every session. You are not asked to judge progress by atmosphere; you are given the document the judgement is based on.

whyPoints.description: Slots from 17:00 for families whose school bus arrives early, and late evening or weekend morning slots for households commuting back from Dubai and Sharjah. faqs.question: What does an IB DP math AA HL tutor in Ajman charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates for a qualified online subject tutor run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, and AED 200 to AED 450 for a Diploma specialist, with budget platforms advertising from AED 33 and one premium provider publishing AED 650. Those figures were read from providers' own published material in October 2026 and are market rates rather than an IB Gram price list. Higher Level Analysis sits at the upper half of the specialist band because the course runs to 240 taught hours and carries content, including Paper 3, that no Standard Level course covers. Ask for the hourly figure, the session length and whether marking is included before the first session.

faqs.question: Why is a Higher Level Analysis hour priced above a Standard Level one?
faqs.answer: Three reasons, all structural. The Higher Level course is 240 taught hours against 150 at Standard Level, so there is simply more to teach. It contains material with no Standard Level counterpart at all, including proof by induction, complex numbers in Euler form, Maclaurin series and vector equations of planes. And it carries a third paper worth a fifth of the grade which has to be prepared separately from the topic syllabus. The pool of tutors who can teach all of that confidently is narrower than the pool who can teach Standard Level, and a narrower pool prices higher in every market.

faqs.question: Does a tutor based outside Ajman cost our family more?
faqs.answer: For online lessons, no. Where a tutor sits makes no difference to an hour delivered over live video, and it is why the specialist pool available to an Ajman family online is the same one available to a family in Dubai. For an in-home visit it makes a large difference, because a tutor driving from Dubai or Sharjah into Ajman in evening traffic spends forty to seventy minutes each way and that time is paid for inside the hourly rate. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so the travel question does not arise on our side.

faqs.question: How many Higher Level maths sessions does a term usually come to?
faqs.answer: It depends which problem you are buying against. A summer bridge from IGCSE into DP1 is typically six to eight sessions. A component block aimed at Paper 1 sketching or Paper 3 technique is usually six to ten, which is short enough to state at the outset and judge on marked scripts. Exploration supervision is a handful of scheduled sessions timed to the school's internal deadlines. A DP2 student who is behind on content as well as technique is a different scale of plan, and anyone quoting that without seeing a marked script first is guessing.

faqs.question: Is Paper 3 preparation billed separately from weekly lessons?
faqs.answer: It usually should be, because it is different work. Paper 3 cannot be revised topic by topic: each question invents its own mathematics in the stem and walks the candidate through it in scaffolded parts, so what is being trained is reading an unfamiliar argument under time pressure. That needs whole past questions sat under the real one-hour constraint and then marked line by line, which does not fit inside an ordinary sixty-minute teaching slot. Pricing it as a defined block makes the cost visible and makes it obvious when the block is finished.

faqs.question: What does exploration supervision add to the bill?
faqs.answer: A small number of scheduled sessions rather than a continuing weekly charge, and the cheapest version is bought early. Two or three sessions at the topic-selection stage, spent testing whether the mathematics reaches Higher Level and whether the data exists, prevent the expensive case: a student fifteen pages into a topic with no Higher Level mathematics in it. Feedback is given criterion by criterion against the five criteria and the twenty marks. The student's own work stays their own throughout, which is both an IB requirement and the reason this is supervision rather than production.

faqs.question: Are AA HL tutoring fees in Ajman quoted with VAT included?
faqs.answer: Ask, and ask in writing, because practice varies across this market and we will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition as settled fact without a Federal Tax Authority citation to hand. What matters practically is whether the figure you were quoted is the figure you will pay. A quote should state the amount in dirhams, the session length in minutes, whether marking between sessions is inside that figure, and whether any tax is added on top. A provider that cannot answer those four questions in one message is not ready to take your money.

faqs.question: If we can only spend AED 180 an hour, is Higher Level support still worth starting?
faqs.answer: Yes, but spend it narrowly. At that level the realistic purchase is a diagnosis and a single component rather than a standing weekly arrangement across the whole course. Get the marked script read, identify whether the loss is non-calculator algebra, calculator technique or Paper 3 reading, then buy a short block against that one thing and judge it on the next marked script. Fortnightly ninety-minute sessions with written marking in between often beat weekly hours at the same monthly spend, because the marking is where most of the diagnosis actually happens.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram arrange a Higher Level maths tutor to teach at an address in Ajman?
faqs.answer: No. Every UAE lesson is delivered one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service offered only in India. On the merits, that is also the better arrangement for this particular course: a family in Al Rawda or Al Zorah choosing locally is choosing from whoever is within driving distance, while the same family online is choosing from Analysis and Approaches specialists outright. The honest cost of online delivery is supervision, which we handle with the camera on the page, working photographed for marking and a written note to the parent after each session.

faqs.question: Is a pair of students cheaper per head for Higher Level maths?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes; per outcome, often not. Two Higher Level candidates can share a session productively only if their gaps genuinely overlap, which at Higher Level is less common than at Standard Level because the ways students fail this course diverge sharply. One cannot start a proof; the other knows the content and bleeds accuracy marks. A shared hour then teaches each of them half the time. Where a pair does work well is Paper 3 practice and mark scheme reading, which benefit from two people arguing about the same script.

faqs.question: Do Higher Level maths rates in the northern emirates climb before the May session?
faqs.answer: Rates drift upward across this market as the session approaches, but availability tightens faster than price does. By February the binding constraint for a Higher Level family is usually not the dirham figure but whether any Analysis and Approaches specialist is free at 19:30 on a weekday. The practical implication is that the cheap time to buy Higher Level support and the effective time to buy it are the same time, which is early in DP1 or over the summer before DP2, not after the mock results arrive.

faqs.question: Should we pay for a block of ten lessons up front?
faqs.answer: Only after a free trial and a written diagnosis, and only if the block has a stated purpose. A block aimed at a named component with marked scripts as the evidence is a reasonable thing to commit to, because you can tell at session five whether it is working. A block bought as a general discount on an open-ended arrangement is harder to judge and harder to exit. Ask what happens to unused sessions, whether the slot is held through the school holidays, and what the review point is before paying for any package.

faqs.question: Do we pay for the time a tutor spends marking a Higher Level script?
faqs.answer: Somewhere in the price, yes, and a provider that claims otherwise is either not marking properly or has hidden it in the hourly figure. Marking a full Paper 1 against the published mark scheme, separating method marks from accuracy marks and writing a usable note on it, takes most of an hour. The question to ask is not whether it is paid for but whether it is happening: ask to see a marked script from the first month, with annotations against the mark scheme rather than a tick and a total.

faqs.question: What happens to our plan if no Higher Level Analysis specialist is free in our slot?
faqs.answer: We say so. Higher Level Analysis is the narrowest maths specialism in the Diploma and the diary tightens sharply from January, so there are weeks when the honest answer to a 19:30 weekday request is that nobody suitable is available. The realistic alternatives are a weekend morning slot, a fortnightly ninety-minute session with written marking in between, or a later start date with the work resequenced. Filling the hour with a general maths tutor and charging a specialist rate for it is the one option we will not offer.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest honest first step if our child is on a grade 3 at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Four free things, in this order. Ask the school for the component-by-component mark breakdown, so you know whether Paper 1 or Paper 2 is the problem. Read the last marked script with your child, looking for where the working stopped rather than at the total. Ask the subject teacher what they would do with an extra ninety minutes a week. Then use the free trial lesson as a diagnostic, sending the script in advance and asking for the diagnosis in writing. If that document says a level change is the better answer, that is a useful free outcome.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Higher Level maths and a second Diploma subject for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, because a single tutor covering Higher Level Analysis and Physics HL removes a scheduling problem and a second invoice. The limit is honest competence: the overlap between people who teach Higher Level Analysis well and those who teach a second Higher Level subject well is not large, and a tutor who says yes to every subject on the list is a warning rather than a convenience. Where the double is not available, two specialists on alternating evenings is the better purchase.
