sections.heading: Ajman, the Ministry of Education, and how online lessons actually run here
paragraphs: Ajman's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than by an emirate authority, which is the arrangement u.ae sets out for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. There is no local equivalent of Dubai's KHDA or Abu Dhabi's ADEK here, and the emirate's IB Diploma provision is concentrated in a single continuum school. The practical result is that a large share of Higher Level mathematics students resident in Ajman sit in a Sharjah or Dubai classroom, under the Sharjah Private Education Authority or KHDA respectively, and their internal deadlines belong to that school rather than to this emirate.

Private tutoring itself is licensed federally and the position is clear. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, free of charge, for two years. Eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no schedule of amounts has been published, any figure quoted as fact should be treated as unverified.

IB Gram delivers tutoring for UAE families one-to-one over live video. It does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. For this course the online format is close to ideal, because the two things a Higher Level Applications session needs most are a shared screen and a shared document. A tutor demonstrating a calculator sequence on screen, or annotating a student's Paper 3 attempt line by line while both people look at the same page, is doing the most useful available work, and neither action is improved by being in the same room.

The matching argument is stronger here than in most places. Higher Level Applications is a narrow specialism, the emirate is small, and the pool of people within driving distance who teach graph theory and transition matrices regularly is very limited. A family insisting on physical presence is usually choosing a generalist who will do a competent job on functions and calculus and struggle with the extension content, which is precisely the content costing the marks. Practical checks before committing: test the connection from the room the student will use, confirm sessions leave behind marked work in a shared folder, and fix the slot to one evening for the term.

process.title: Send the last marked paper and the exploration status
process.description: The most recent marked mathematics paper, the level the student is actually taught in, and whether an exploration topic has been chosen. Those three things show whether the problem is coverage, technique, calculator fluency or the twenty per cent sitting in coursework, and they cannot be diagnosed from a conversation.

process.title: Free trial, built around one real question
process.description: One lesson at no cost, with no card details taken, spent on a question from the student's own paper rather than on an introduction. It ends with that question marked, the mark-scheme points named, and a short statement of which of the four failure types is in play.

process.title: A written diagnosis naming the component
process.description: A short note saying which component is losing most marks and why: breadth on Paper 1, lost threads on Paper 2, time and structure on Paper 3, or design on the exploration. The note says what the next six weeks will cover and what they will not, so the hour cannot drift.

process.title: A fixed slot, ninety minutes, one evening
process.description: Set around the Sharjah or Dubai school run rather than around a convenient advertised time, because a 17:30 slot that cannot survive an Al Mowaihat bus schedule will quietly stop. Ninety minutes rather than sixty, so one extension topic and one timed question both fit.

process.title: Review at six weeks on the same evidence
process.description: Compare a marked question from week six against the one from the trial, on the same criteria, plus a timed Paper 3 problem to test whether the extended-reasoning habit has moved. If nothing has changed, the right answer may be a different tutor, and saying so is part of the job.

whyPoints.title: The extension content taught by someone who teaches it
whyPoints.description: Graph theory, transition matrices and numerical differential equations are where Higher Level Applications scripts actually fall apart, and they are the content a generalist is least likely to have taught. Matching online rather than by driving distance is what makes a genuine Applications specialist reachable from this emirate.

whyPoints.title: Calculator fluency treated as syllabus content
whyPoints.description: Every Applications paper permits a graphic display calculator, so keystroke speed is examinable rather than incidental. A few minutes of every session goes on the technology attached to whatever content is being covered, because it is the most reliably measurable improvement available in this course.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 practised whole, under the hour
whyPoints.description: Two extended problems in sixty minutes is a distinct skill, and fragmented practice does not build it. The Paper 3 block sits full papers under real timing and then dismantles them part by part, which is the only format that changes what happens in the examination hall.

whyPoints.title: The exploration treated as a design problem
whyPoints.description: Higher Level explorations usually lose marks under use of mathematics, and that is decided when the topic is chosen rather than when the draft is written. Supervision therefore concentrates on whether the planned mathematics reaches the level, and the student does every piece of the work themselves.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built for the northern emirates
whyPoints.description: Students living in Ajman and schooled in Sharjah or Dubai get home late, and a slot that ignores that will fail by week four. Slots are set once around the actual commute, and ninety minutes is the default because a single transition matrix problem can take twenty minutes to set up properly.

whyPoints.title: Independent of every school named
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform with no affiliation to, endorsement from or formal connection with any school, group or examination board. Schools appear on this page as market context for an emirate whose Diploma provision is small, which is the only honest reason to name them.

faqs.question: People say Applications HL is the soft option. Is that true for my child?
faqs.answer: It is different rather than easier. Analysis is more abstract and more algebraically demanding; Applications is broader, more technological and more dependent on interpreting results in a real context. Applications adds matrices and eigenvalues, graph theory, transition matrices and numerical differential equations, almost none of which a student has met before, so the content is unfamiliar rather than gentle. A student who writes fluent explanations and dislikes proof scores higher in Applications. One who prefers a closed algebraic problem scores higher in Analysis, whatever the syllabus pages suggest.

faqs.question: How is Applications HL assessed and how much does Paper 3 count?
faqs.answer: Four components. Paper 1 is two hours for 110 marks and carries thirty per cent; Paper 2 is two hours for 110 marks and also thirty per cent; Paper 3 is one hour for 55 marks and carries twenty per cent, and only Higher Level candidates sit it; the mathematical exploration is the remaining twenty per cent. Confirm the structure for your child's cohort against the subject guide their coordinator issues, since guides are revised between cycles. The useful consequence is that a fifth of the grade is coursework with no time pressure and help available.

faqs.question: Why does my son get the right number on his calculator and still lose the marks?
faqs.answer: Because in this course the number is rarely the whole answer. A chi-squared result needs both the statistical conclusion and a plain sentence about what it means for the two variables in the question. A correlation coefficient needs a comment on the relationship, not a restatement of its value. A regression equation used for prediction needs a note on whether the prediction sits inside the data range. Each of those is one sentence away from a full mark, and the sentence is the thing being examined. It is a writing habit, drillable in a few weeks.

faqs.question: What is actually in the Higher Level-only part of the Applications course?
faqs.answer: Matrices including determinants, inverses, eigenvalues and eigenvectors; graph theory with adjacency matrices, minimum spanning trees, the Chinese postman and travelling salesman problems; complex numbers in more than one form; vectors with scalar and vector products; non-linear regression; hypothesis testing with chi-squared and t-tests; transition matrices and steady states; and differential equations approached numerically, including Euler's method and phase portraits. Most of it has no school-level precursor, which is why it feels hard. It is new rather than deep, and four careful hours on graph theory usually converts blank space into reliable marks.

faqs.question: How should a student practise for the Higher Level third paper?
faqs.answer: Whole papers under the real hour, then dismantled part by part. Paper 3 sets two extended problems across 55 marks, each scaffolded so that later parts depend on understanding what the middle parts established. The characteristic failure is answering parts a and b, misreading c, and losing d and e entirely. Fragmented practice does not build the skill being tested, which is sustaining one line of reasoning for half an hour. Thirty minutes a problem, enforced, and a written note of what each part established before moving on.

faqs.question: Why is statistics the topic where Applications HL students lose most ground?
faqs.answer: Two reasons. It is the largest topic in the course, and it is the one most often taught thinly, partly because the calculations are short enough that a lesson can look successful when nothing was learned about interpretation. Sampling methods and bias are frequently skipped altogether despite being highly examinable gift marks. Correlation against causation is answered badly more often than any other single point in the subject. The fix is interpretation sentences drilled until automatic, rather than more practice on the calculations themselves.

faqs.question: Our Ajman school teaches Applications HL with one teacher. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, but it is worth knowing which teacher and what they have taught before. In a small cohort one of the two mathematics routes is usually taught better than the other, because the department's experience sits on one side, and a teacher trained in Analysis taking an Applications class will tend to be strongest on functions and calculus and weakest on graph theory and transition matrices. That is exactly where Higher Level marks are lost. A class of four also gets attention a class of twenty does not, which cuts the other way.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the mathematical exploration without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may discuss the topic, explain what each of the five criteria rewards, advise on whether the planned mathematics reaches Higher Level, and read a draft the student has written and give feedback against those criteria. A tutor may not supply the mathematics, produce the data, write any part of the text, or hand over a worked model. Work that is not the candidate's own is a malpractice matter for the IB and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the person who sold the help.

faqs.question: Why do good Higher Level explorations still score in the middle?
faqs.answer: Almost always under criterion E, use of mathematics, which carries six of the twenty marks and requires mathematics commensurate with the level of the course. A student picks a topic they care about, investigates carefully, writes clearly, and uses mathematics that would suit a Standard Level exploration perfectly well. Four criteria score reasonably and the largest one does not. This is a design failure, decided when the topic was chosen, and no draft review can repair it. Test the planned mathematics against the level before any writing begins.

faqs.question: Will Applications HL stop my daughter studying engineering?
faqs.answer: Not generally, but it depends on the programme and this is the part of the decision with real consequences. Some engineering courses specify Analysis and Approaches; many accept either route, particularly in applied disciplines. Requirements are set by the admitting institution, differ between two courses with the same name at different universities, and are revised between admissions cycles. Read the published entry requirements of the specific programmes under consideration, and where the wording is ambiguous write to the admissions office and get the answer in writing before a subject form is signed.

faqs.question: How many Applications HL sessions does a student in Ajman usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends on which of four problems is in play. Repairing one unfamiliar extension topic such as graph theory or transition matrices is typically four to six sessions. Calculator fluency is a short intensive of three or four. A Paper 3 block is four to six, sat as whole papers. Exploration supervision is two short blocks, one at design and one at draft stage. A family buying all four across two years is buying a programme; a family buying one should say which, and should get a written diagnosis naming it.

faqs.question: Should a student move from Applications HL down to Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the reason is usually breadth rather than difficulty. Higher Level adds a great deal of unfamiliar content plus a third paper, and a student managing the shared material but drowning in the extension may do better with a secure Standard Level grade. The decision should be taken early in the second year rather than in the term before examinations, and it should be checked against university requirements first, since some programmes specify a Higher Level mathematics. Ask the school which levels will run as separate classes before assuming a move is available.

faqs.question: Does a student living in Ajman need a tutor based in the UAE for this subject?
faqs.answer: No, and insisting on it narrows the field in a way that usually costs marks. Higher Level Applications is a narrow specialism, Ajman is a small emirate, and the number of people within driving distance who regularly teach graph theory, transition matrices and numerical differential equations is very limited. A family choosing by proximity typically gets a competent generalist who is strongest on exactly the content that is not the problem. Removing distance from the decision is what makes a genuine Applications specialist reachable from this emirate.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram arrange an Applications HL tutor to teach at a house in Ajman?
faqs.answer: No. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, and IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is offered only in India. For this course the format costs very little and gains a great deal. The two things a Higher Level Applications session most needs are a shared screen, for demonstrating calculator sequences, and a shared document, for annotating a Paper 3 attempt line by line. Neither is improved by being in the same room.

faqs.question: Which authority supervises private schools if we live in Ajman?
faqs.answer: The federal Ministry of Education, which u.ae identifies as supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. There is no emirate-level authority here equivalent to Dubai's KHDA or Abu Dhabi's ADEK. In practice many Ajman families enrol across the border, where Sharjah's schools fall under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves curricula, fees and assessment methods as well as inspecting. If your child attends school in another emirate, that emirate's authority and that school's internal calendar are the ones that govern their Diploma.

faqs.question: Do tutors working with Ajman families need a licence, and what does it cost?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it is free. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no schedule of amounts has been published.

ajman/ib-dp-math-ai-hl-tutor.closingBody: A Higher Level Applications grade is four separate things, and families usually buy help for the course rather than for the part that is actually losing marks. Breadth on Paper 1, lost threads on Paper 2, time and structure on Paper 3, and design on the exploration all look the same on a report card and need completely different work. Send the last marked paper and say whether an exploration topic has been chosen. The free trial spends its hour on one real question from that paper, returns it marked with the mark-scheme points named, and says which of the four is in play. That answer is useful whether or not you book anything afterwards.

ajman/ib-dp-math-ai-sl-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below take Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level: the five topics as examined at this level, finance and Voronoi content that carries reliable marks, accuracy and interpretation technique, and supervision of the student's own exploration from topic choice to draft feedback.

intro.heading: Why a capable Standard Level student gets stuck on a 5
paragraphs: Standard Level Applications produces a particular kind of frustrated family. The student is not failing. They understand the lessons, complete the homework, and come out of every paper with a mark in the middle. The report says they are working well. Nothing in that picture suggests a content problem, and nothing in it suggests what to do next either, which is why the search for a tutor usually begins with a parent who cannot name what is wrong.

In this subject the answer is almost always the same, and it is not content. Standard Level Applications is examined with a calculator in both papers, so the arithmetic is not where the marks go. They go in small, repeatable losses spread across every question: a final answer given to the wrong accuracy, a quantity reported without units, a value calculated and never interpreted, a model chosen without a reason stated, a prediction made outside the range of the data, a sentence of explanation not written because the number looked like the answer. Each one costs a single mark. There are forty of them across two papers.

That matters because of how the course is weighted. Each written paper carries forty per cent and the exploration carries twenty. A student losing one mark per question to accuracy and interpretation is losing somewhere between eight and fifteen marks a paper, which is a grade band and sometimes two. Those marks are not hard to recover. They require a set of habits applied consistently, and habits are what a weekly hour with marked work is actually good at building.

The exploration is the other reason a Standard Level grade sits lower than it should. A fifth of this course is coursework, written over months, with no time limit and feedback permitted. It is the most controllable portion of the grade in the subject and it is routinely the part done last, in a rush, on a topic chosen because it sounded interesting rather than because data existed for it. A student who secures strong exploration marks has bought themselves a cushion on the papers that no amount of revision provides.

The Ajman layer is practical rather than academic. The emirate's private schools sit under the federal Ministry of Education, its local Diploma provision is small, and many students here are enrolled in Sharjah or Dubai and get home late. That affects when a session can start and whether the student in it is alert. It also means the number of people nearby who teach this exact course is small, which is the argument for choosing a tutor by what they teach rather than by how far away they live. A household in Al Nuaimiya and a household in Al Zorah face the same constraint for different reasons, and in both cases the fix is the same.

ajman/ib-dp-math-ai-sl-tutor.programmesIntro: Standard Level Applications is chosen at the end of Year 11 and examined two years later, and the useful support looks different at each end of that period. Ajman's Diploma provision is small and many students are enrolled across the emirate border, so the stages below describe where families here actually arrive asking for help.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Standard Level Applications runs for 150 taught hours across five topics: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. Assessment is two written papers of ninety minutes and 80 marks each, both permitting a graphic display calculator, plus a mathematical exploration assessed against five criteria for twenty marks. Confirm the structure for your child's cohort against the subject guide their coordinator issues.
programmes.countryNote: Many Ajman households have a Diploma student enrolled in Sharjah or Dubai, which means the internal deadlines, the mock calendar and the exploration submission date all belong to a school in another emirate. The first thing worth collecting is that school's written deadline list, because a plan built on the wrong calendar loses a term before anybody notices.

programmes.name: First Diploma year
programmes.description: The year when content is new and marks are soft because habits have not formed. The highest-value work here is not content support but accuracy discipline: significant figures, units, context sentences, and reading a question for what it actually asks. Exploration topic selection also belongs in this year, and a topic chosen in the first year with data already in hand is worth several marks over one chosen in the second.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman students arriving from a British or Indian curriculum school typically have strong hand arithmetic and little technology fluency, which is the wrong way round for this course. A short block on the calculator early in the first year prevents a habit that costs time in every paper for two years.

programmes.name: Second Diploma year
programmes.description: Revision, the exploration deadline, mocks and the examination session. By this point the accuracy pattern is established and visible in every marked script, which makes it diagnosable in one session. Work here is past papers under timing, marked against the published scheme, with a running list of the student's own three or four recurring losses rather than a general revision programme.
programmes.countryNote: In the northern emirates the second Diploma year collides with long commutes and a dense internal-assessment calendar. Weekend morning sessions tend to survive better than weekday evening ones in DP2, and timed paper practice is better done in the morning anyway, since it needs ninety minutes of unbroken attention.

programmes.name: Year 11 into Standard Level Applications
programmes.description: The decision year. A Year 11 report says more about which of the four Diploma mathematics routes fits than any conversation does: whether the student can explain a method in words, whether they are comfortable with data, whether they resent open-ended questions. Bridging work is about explanation and technology rather than about algebra, which most students arriving from IGCSE already have.
programmes.countryNote: Where an Ajman or Sharjah school runs only one or two mathematics classes, the available route may be narrower than the four the IB offers. Ask the school which routes will actually run as separate classes next year before building a plan around a level that will not exist on the timetable.

ajman/ib-dp-math-ai-sl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Standard Level Applications is five topics, a technology toolkit and an exploration. The breakdown below is organised by how a marked paper separates them, with what each part is examined on and the kind of mark loss attached to it.

subjects.name: Number, accuracy and percentage error
subjects.description: Standard form, rounding to significant figures and decimal places, upper and lower bounds, and percentage error. Small and heavily examined. Percentage error is the sub-topic where correct method meets the wrong denominator, and accuracy instructions in a question stem are the most commonly ignored words on either paper.

subjects.name: Finance: loans, annuities and amortisation
subjects.description: Compound interest, depreciation, loan repayment, annuities and amortisation schedules, handled with the calculator's finance solver. Mechanical once the solver is fluent, and among the most reliable marks in the course. Students lose them by entering a payment as positive when the convention requires negative, or by misreading compounding frequency.

subjects.name: Sequences and series
subjects.description: Arithmetic and geometric sequences and their sums, applied to growth, decay and repayment contexts. The examinable difficulty is recognising which type a worded situation describes, since the formulae themselves are supplied. A question about a salary rising by a fixed percentage and one rising by a fixed amount look alike and are not.

subjects.name: Functions and model choice
subjects.description: Linear, quadratic, exponential, sinusoidal and piecewise models, with transformations and interpretation of parameters. The mark sits in justifying why a model fits a context or a scatter of data and in saying what each parameter means in that situation, not in producing the equation the calculator already gave.

subjects.name: Voronoi diagrams and the nearest-neighbour problem
subjects.description: Perpendicular bisectors, cells, sites, and the toxic-waste-dump problem of locating a point furthest from all sites. Self-contained, highly scoreable and distinctive to this course. It is often rushed because it appears late in a paper, which is a timing problem rather than a knowledge one.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Volume and surface area of three-dimensional solids, right-angled and non-right-angled trigonometry, the sine and cosine rules, bearings and angles of elevation. Diagram-drawing is the quiet skill: students who sketch the triangle before calculating lose far fewer marks than those who work from the words alone.

subjects.name: Descriptive statistics and data presentation
subjects.description: Sampling methods and bias, measures of central tendency and dispersion, quartiles, box plots, cumulative frequency and outliers. Sampling and bias is the sub-topic most often skipped and most reliably examined, usually as a short question asking why a described method might mislead.

subjects.name: Correlation, regression and Spearman's rank
subjects.description: Scatter diagrams, the product-moment correlation coefficient, least-squares regression and Spearman's rank correlation coefficient. Marks go on interpretation rather than computation: commenting on a relationship, distinguishing correlation from causation, and noticing when a prediction falls outside the range of the data.

subjects.name: Probability and distributions
subjects.description: Sample spaces, Venn and tree diagrams, conditional probability, and the binomial and normal distributions calculated on the calculator. The failure is almost always translation: a worded situation read into the wrong parameters, so a correct calculation answers a question nobody asked.

subjects.name: The chi-squared test at Standard Level
subjects.description: Testing for independence from a contingency table, with degrees of freedom, critical values and a stated conclusion. Entirely procedural once learned, and the conclusion must be given twice: once in statistical terms and once in the plain language of the situation. Half the available marks sit in the second sentence.

subjects.name: Calculus and the trapezoidal rule
subjects.description: Differentiation of simple functions, gradients and tangents, optimisation, definite integrals for area, and numerical approximation by the trapezoidal rule. The calculus here serves modelling rather than proof, so setting the problem up from a described situation carries more marks than executing the technique.

subjects.name: The toolkit and the exploration
subjects.description: Calculator fluency across graphing, regression, distributions, statistical tests and numerical solving, plus the individual exploration assessed for twenty marks against five criteria. At Standard Level the mathematics required is reachable, so explorations here fail on data availability and on communication rather than on ambition.

ajman/ib-dp-math-ai-sl-tutor.regionsTitle: Ajman districts and the practical shape of a Standard Level session
ajman/ib-dp-math-ai-sl-tutor.regionsIntro: Two things decide whether a weekly mathematics hour works in this emirate: what time the student is actually home and awake, and whether their exploration can find data near where they live. The notes below cover both, because the second is a real advantage that almost nobody uses.

regions.name: Al Jurf
regions.note: Mixed residential and industrial, and the district with the most accessible small-business and logistics activity in the emirate. Students here have unusually good exploration options involving queue times, stock turnover or delivery distances, all of which generate the kind of data a Standard Level investigation needs.

regions.name: Ajman Corniche
regions.note: Central and close to the waterfront, with footfall, retail and visitor activity that can be counted. A short, well-designed observational study along the Corniche produces a dataset a student collected themselves, which feeds the personal engagement criterion directly.

regions.name: Al Mowaihat
regions.note: Newer villa housing with long bus routes towards Sharjah. Arrival times after 16:30 are normal, so the sessions that survive a full term start at 19:00 rather than at the earliest advertised slot. Household journey data is also a ready exploration dataset.

regions.name: Al Nuaimiya
regions.note: Dense towers with shared study space and a quick run to the Sharjah border. The practical constraint is a quiet ninety minutes rather than a free ninety minutes, and timed paper practice should be booked for whenever the flat is actually quiet.

regions.name: Al Rawda
regions.note: Villa district where a dedicated desk is easier to arrange and where households often run two Diploma students. Alternating evenings works better than two sessions on the same night, and the second student rarely gets the better hour.

regions.name: Al Yasmeen and Al Zorah
regions.note: Low-density newer developments with many recently arrived families. Mid-course transfers are common here, and a transferring Standard Level student needs two schools' exploration deadlines reconciled before any mathematics is taught.

regions.name: Emirates City
regions.note: High-rise towers where connectivity varies between buildings and sometimes between floors. Test the video link from the actual study room during the free session; a dropped connection during a timed paper costs more than the session did.

regions.name: Al Helio and Al Rashidiya
regions.note: Established residential areas with good access to the Sharjah crossing and short local school runs. Students here are the most able to take an early-evening slot, which is the right time for the ninety-minute unbroken block a full paper needs.

schoolClusters.city: Ajman
schoolClusters.note: Ajman has no emirate-level education authority. Its private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which u.ae names as the supervising body for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Diploma provision in the emirate is concentrated in one continuum school, and the wider local sector is largely British and Indian curriculum, so a Standard Level Applications class here is typically very small.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and the northern emirates, within daily reach
schoolClusters.note: Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah's by its Department of Knowledge; both approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods in addition to inspecting. An Ajman family whose child crosses the border each morning is following that school's calendar and that authority's framework, not this emirate's.

ajman/ib-dp-math-ai-sl-tutor.modesIntro: What a Standard Level family is buying is usually one of three things: an accuracy and interpretation habit, coverage of a topic the school rushed, or the exploration. Each has a natural length and a natural end point, and naming which one is being bought is what stops a weekly hour becoming general homework supervision.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, sixty minutes
modes.description: Sixty minutes is the right length at Standard Level, and the shape matters more than the duration. Twenty minutes on a topic, twenty-five on timed questions from earlier topics, and the last ten on reviewing the marked answers against the scheme. The accuracy habits are built in that final ten minutes, which is why it should never be the part that gets cut when a session overruns.

modes.title: Accuracy and interpretation intensive
modes.description: A short block of three or four sessions aimed only at the small repeated losses: significant figures, units, accuracy instructions in a question stem, the required interpretation sentence, and checking whether a prediction sits inside the data range. This is the highest-return purchase available to a capable Standard Level student and the one families almost never think to ask for.

modes.title: Exploration block
modes.description: Two short blocks: one when the topic is chosen, one when a draft exists. At Standard Level the mathematics needed is reachable, so the design question is whether data exists and whether it can be analysed with something more than a mean and a bar chart. The student collects, calculates and writes; the tutor advises and gives feedback against the criteria.

modes.description: Three or four sessions on the graphic display calculator alone, because both Standard Level papers permit it and a slow candidate does not finish. Regression, distributions, the chi-squared test, the finance solver, numerical solving and graphing, practised until the keystrokes are automatic rather than recalled. Cheap, short and measurable.

sections.heading: Reading a Year 11 report to choose between the four mathematics routes
paragraphs: The IB offers four mathematics routes and most students are told which one they are taking rather than choosing it. Where a choice exists, it is usually made on a predicted grade, which is the least informative evidence available. A far better guide sits in the Year 11 report and in a piece of the student's own written mathematics: whether they can explain a method in words, whether they are comfortable looking at a table of real data, whether they find an open question interesting or merely annoying.

Standard Level Applications suits a specific profile. A student who can write a sentence about what a number means, who does not mind that a question has no single tidy answer, and whose arithmetic is sound but unexciting, will do well here. A student who finds explanation tedious and enjoys the mechanical satisfaction of solving an equation often does better in Analysis even at Standard Level, because Analysis asks for less interpretation and more technique. Neither profile is stronger. They produce different marks in different rooms.

The signals worth reading from a Year 11 report are concrete. Marks lost on worded problems while method marks are earned points towards a comprehension issue rather than a mathematics one, and Applications will expose it because every question has a context. Comments about presentation and showing working point towards the communication criterion in the exploration, which is four of its twenty marks. Strong performance on statistics units and weak performance on algebra units is close to a direct recommendation for Applications over Analysis.

The table below sets the four routes against what a Year 11 report actually shows. Any university requirement should be checked against the institution's own published entry criteria, because those are set by the admitting body, differ between courses of the same name, and are revised between cycles.

sections.heading: Two papers, both with technology, and what that changes about revision
paragraphs: Standard Level Applications is examined in two papers of ninety minutes, each carrying 80 marks and forty per cent of the grade, with a graphic display calculator permitted in both. There is no non-calculator paper at this level in this route, which is the single biggest practical difference from Analysis and the one that most changes how revision should be done. Revising by working through algebra by hand prepares a student for an examination they will not sit.

Paper 1 is built from shorter questions covering the breadth of the syllabus. Its failure mode is coverage: a student who never properly met Voronoi diagrams or the chi-squared test will lose a complete question and cannot make it up elsewhere, because the remaining questions are on other topics. Revision for Paper 1 is therefore audit-driven. Go through the syllabus topic list, mark each one honestly as secure, shaky or unmet, and spend the available time on the unmet ones, however dull that sounds compared with doing more past papers.

Paper 2 is built from longer, multi-part questions in extended contexts. Its failure mode is different: a dropped thread, where a student answers the first two parts and then produces nothing for the later ones because those depend on having understood what the middle established. Revision for Paper 2 is whole-question practice with the clock running, plus the discipline of writing down what each part established before moving on. Doing twenty isolated part-a questions builds none of that.

Both papers reward technology used early. A student uncomfortable with the calculator will try a question by hand that the examiner expected to be solved with the machine, lose four minutes, and then be short of time later in the paper. The pattern compounds: time pressure late in a paper is almost always caused by hesitancy early in it. This is why calculator fluency is worth session time at Standard Level even when the mathematics is understood perfectly well.

sections.heading: Voronoi diagrams and the finance content: the most reliable marks in the course
paragraphs: Two parts of Standard Level Applications behave unlike the rest. Voronoi diagrams and the finance content are both self-contained, both highly procedural once learned, and both reliably examined. Neither depends much on the rest of the syllabus, which means a student can be shaky elsewhere and still collect these marks in full. For a candidate stuck on a 4 or a 5, they are the cheapest available improvement, and they are frequently the two areas a rushed course covered least well.

Voronoi work is a small set of skills: constructing a perpendicular bisector, identifying cells and sites, reading which site a point is nearest to, and solving the largest-empty-circle problem of locating a point as far as possible from every site. The context is usually a map of facilities, and the question asks something a planner would ask. Students lose these marks not through misunderstanding but through rushing, because Voronoi questions tend to appear late in a paper when time is short. That makes it a timing problem with a timing fix.

The finance content is similar in character and larger in scope: compound interest, depreciation, loan repayment, annuities and amortisation schedules, almost all of it executed on the calculator's finance solver. The errors are mechanical and repeatable. A payment entered as a positive number when the convention requires a negative one produces a wrong answer that looks plausible. Compounding frequency misread from the question costs the whole item. Thirty minutes spent establishing the sign convention and the input order properly is worth more than an hour of general revision.

There is a third area with the same character, the chi-squared test. It is procedural: build the contingency table, state degrees of freedom, obtain the statistic, compare with the critical value, and state the conclusion twice - once in statistical terms and once in the plain language of the situation. That second sentence carries marks students routinely forgo because the statistical conclusion feels like the answer. All three of these areas reward exactly the kind of short, concentrated, drillable work that a weekly hour is well suited to.

sections.heading: Where Standard Level candidates actually leak marks, counted by frequency
paragraphs: If you take a stack of marked Standard Level Applications papers from capable students and count the lost marks by cause rather than by topic, the distribution is startling. The great majority are small, repeated and unrelated to understanding. Accuracy errors come first: answers given to two significant figures where three were required, or to three where the question specified otherwise, or rounded mid-calculation so the final figure is slightly wrong. Missing units follow close behind, then missing interpretation, then misread question stems.

Only after those four does anything that looks like a mathematics problem appear, and when it does it is usually one specific topic the school covered in a hurry. That is worth saying plainly to a family who assumed their child needed the whole course retaught. The repair for the first four causes is a habit, applied consistently, verified on marked work every week. The repair for the fifth is teaching one topic. Neither is a two-year programme.

The habit has a shape. Read the question twice and underline the accuracy instruction before touching the calculator. Carry units through the working rather than appending them at the end. After producing any statistical value, write the sentence that says what it means in the situation the question described. Before using a regression equation to predict, check whether the input sits inside the range of the original data. In the final five minutes of a paper, run a pass across every final answer checking accuracy and units only.

Two of those take seconds and recover several marks each. The reason students do not do them is that nobody has ever shown them the arithmetic of their own paper - that they lost eleven marks to things requiring no additional knowledge whatsoever. Once a student sees that count on their own script, the habits tend to install themselves, which is why the first useful session in this subject is a marking session rather than a teaching one.

sections.heading: The exploration at Standard Level: a reachable twenty marks, usually left on the table
paragraphs: A fifth of this grade is written at home over a period of months with feedback permitted, and that is a very unusual thing in an examined subject. At Standard Level the mathematical demand is genuinely reachable: a well-chosen regression with residuals examined, a chi-squared test on data the student collected, a model fitted to a real process and its limitations discussed. None of that is beyond a competent Standard Level student. The marks are lost somewhere else entirely.

They are lost on data. A student chooses a topic because it is interesting, discovers that the data they imagined does not exist in any accessible form, and ends up with a mean, a bar chart and 1,500 words of commentary. Use of mathematics scores low because there was nothing to apply mathematics to. The fix is to invert the order: decide what data can actually be obtained, then choose a question about it. In Ajman that is less restrictive than it sounds, with counted observations available along the Corniche, journey times from any household with a Sharjah commute, and small-business activity throughout Al Jurf.

The second place marks go is mathematical communication, worth four of the twenty. This rewards defined variables, correct notation, labelled axes, stated assumptions and appropriate forms. Students paste calculator output into a document with no notation around it and lose most of the four. It is the easiest criterion to secure and the most commonly neglected, and twenty minutes with somebody who knows what the criterion wants fixes it permanently.

Personal engagement and reflection carry three marks each and both reward honesty about the process. Engagement is evidence of the student doing something themselves: collecting their own data, adapting a method, testing an idea that failed. Reflection is a real discussion of limitations and of what would be done differently, not a closing summary. Both are recorded as the work happens or they are reconstructed unconvincingly at the end, and an examiner can tell which.

The boundary matters here. A tutor may discuss a topic, explain the criteria, advise on whether the planned analysis will work, and read a draft the student has written. A tutor may not supply the mathematics, generate the data, write any part of the text, or hand over a worked analysis. Work that is not the candidate's own is a malpractice matter for the IB, and the consequence falls on the student.

sections.heading: What a Standard Level hour should actually contain
paragraphs: Families paying for a weekly hour rarely know what a good one looks like, which makes it hard to judge whether they are getting one. The honest answer is that a productive Standard Level Applications session has a shape, and the shape is more important than the charm of the person delivering it. An hour that consists of the tutor working through examples on screen while the student watches is comfortable for both parties and changes very little, because the student is never the one doing mathematics under any pressure.

The shape that works puts the student's own writing at the centre. New or shaky content occupies the first portion, taught actively with the student attempting examples rather than observing them. Then timed questions on earlier topics, which keeps revision running continuously instead of being deferred to a revision term that always arrives too late. Then marking, together, against the published scheme, which is where accuracy habits actually install themselves. Then a two-line note of what to practise before next week.

The final segment is the one that gets cut when a session overruns, and it should be the one that never is. Reviewing the marked work is where a student sees the count of marks lost to things requiring no extra knowledge, and that count is what changes behaviour. A session that teaches enthusiastically for sixty minutes and leaves nothing marked has produced a pleasant hour and no evidence. Ask, at the end of a free trial, to be shown the marked work. If there is none, that answers a question.

sections.heading: What Standard Level support costs, taken cheapest first
paragraphs: Most tutoring pages open with premium rates and work downwards. Taken the other way round, the picture is more useful to a family deciding whether to spend anything at all. The cheapest option is nothing: an honest syllabus audit the student does themselves, a checklist of accuracy habits, and a stack of past papers marked against the published scheme by the student with a friend. That costs no money and recovers a genuine number of marks in this particular course, because so many of the losses are habit-based rather than knowledge-based.

Above that sits budget online tutoring, advertised across the UAE from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. For Standard Level content repair on a single rushed topic, that tier can be adequate, and it is honest to say so rather than to insist every Diploma hour needs a specialist. Next is a qualified subject tutor working online at about AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; this is the band where somebody is likely to have taught this exact route before.

An IB specialist sits at AED 200 to AED 450 or more, where TutorChase publishes AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table gives AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and premium named tutoring runs to AED 500 or AED 650, where BartyED publishes AED 650. For a Standard Level student losing marks to accuracy and units, the specialist premium buys less than it does at Higher Level, which is worth knowing before paying it. Monthly comparisons help too: packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle. All of those are other providers' published figures with the source named, not an IB Gram price list.

In-home rates are quoted separately because travel sits inside them: AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with Bestimate giving AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500. IB Gram does not sell that in the UAE in any case. What the premium buys elsewhere is a person in the room, and for a subject examined with a calculator on a shared screen, that is the thing it is hardest to argue is worth a hundred dirhams an hour.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and how online lessons run for an Ajman household
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit and the permit is free. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website or e-services system. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no schedule of amounts is published, treat any quoted figure as unverified.

The permit's code of conduct bars a holder from tutoring students affiliated with their own school, which is the detail that answers a question many families ask quietly. Paying your child's own mathematics teacher for private lessons is not the arrangement to look for, and in Abu Dhabi emirate ADEK's professional-ethics rules place a comparable restriction on private and charter school staff. For an Ajman family whose child attends school in Sharjah or Dubai, the relevant point is simply that the tutor should not be employed by that school.

IB Gram delivers tutoring for UAE families one-to-one over live video. It does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. For Standard Level Applications the format is well matched to the subject, because the work is a shared screen and a shared document: a calculator sequence demonstrated keystroke by keystroke, a student's script annotated line by line while both people look at the same page, a marked answer kept in a folder the parent can open.

Practical points for a household in this emirate. Test the connection from the actual study room during the free session, since building connectivity varies across the towers in Emirates City and the outer districts. Fix the slot to one evening, chosen around the real return time rather than the earliest available, because a 17:30 start that cannot survive an Al Mowaihat bus route will quietly lapse by week four. And make sure the session leaves marked work behind, because in this subject the marked work is the whole evidence of whether the hour was worth paying for.

process.title: Send one marked paper, nothing else
process.description: A single recent marked Standard Level paper tells a tutor more than any conversation: whether the losses are accuracy, units, interpretation, misread stems or one unmet topic. Those five causes need completely different work, and they are indistinguishable from a report card that says the student is doing fine.

process.title: Free trial spent counting the losses
process.description: One session at no cost, with no card details taken, used to go through that paper and count the lost marks by cause rather than by topic. Most capable students discover they lost eight to twelve marks to things requiring no additional knowledge, and seeing that count is usually what changes their behaviour.

process.title: A losses list the student keeps
process.description: A short written list of this student's own three or four recurring errors, kept by the student and updated every session. It is deliberately not a revision plan. It is the thing they read in the last five minutes of a paper, which is when most of these marks are recoverable.

process.title: A fixed sixty-minute slot with a fixed shape
process.description: One evening a week, set around the real commute, divided between content, timed questions and marking together. The marking segment is the one that never gets cut, because it is where the habits install. Weekend mornings are better than weekday evenings during the second Diploma year.

process.title: Exploration settled in the first year
process.description: The topic and the data decided while there is still time to change either, rather than in the term the draft is due. The student collects the data and writes the text; feedback comes by criterion with the band named. A fifth of the grade is the most controllable part of this course and the most commonly wasted.

whyPoints.title: The losses counted before anything is taught
whyPoints.description: In this course most lost marks come from accuracy, units, missing interpretation and misread stems rather than from not knowing the mathematics. Counting them on the student's own script is a diagnostic that takes one session and often reframes what the family thought they were buying.

whyPoints.title: Both papers practised as they are examined
whyPoints.description: Standard Level Applications has no non-calculator paper, so revision done by hand prepares a student for an examination they will not sit. Calculator fluency is attached to whatever content a session covers, because hesitancy early in a paper is what causes time pressure later in it.

whyPoints.title: Marked work left behind every week
whyPoints.description: An hour of enthusiastic demonstration leaves no evidence. A session that returns the student's own writing marked against the published scheme leaves something a parent can read and a student can act on, which is the only reliable way to judge whether the hour was worth its cost.

whyPoints.title: The exploration treated as a data problem
whyPoints.description: At Standard Level the mathematics needed is reachable, so explorations fail on data availability and on communication rather than on ambition. Supervision starts from what data can actually be obtained in this emirate, and the student does every part of the collection, analysis and writing.

whyPoints.title: An honest account of what to buy, including nothing
whyPoints.description: This page sets out the free options first, and says plainly that budget tutoring is adequate for some Standard Level repairs and that the specialist premium buys less here than at Higher Level. A family that knows that is making a decision rather than accepting a recommendation.

Schools appear here as market context for an emirate whose own Diploma provision is small, which is the only honest reason to list them.

faqs.question: My daughter is a solid 5 in Applications SL and nothing moves it. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: Start by counting her lost marks by cause rather than by topic on one recent paper. In this course a capable student typically loses eight to twelve marks per paper to accuracy instructions ignored, units omitted, interpretation sentences not written, and question stems misread. None of that needs more mathematics taught. It needs a short list of habits applied consistently and verified on marked work each week. Only after that count should anyone decide whether a topic actually needs reteaching, and usually one does at most.

faqs.question: Is there a non-calculator paper in Applications at Standard Level?
faqs.answer: No. Both Standard Level Applications papers permit a graphic display calculator, which is the biggest practical difference from the Analysis route and the thing most families get wrong about revision. Revising by working through algebra by hand prepares a student for an examination they will not sit. It also means hesitancy with the calculator is expensive: a student who tries by hand what the examiner expected to be done by machine loses minutes early and runs short of time later. Confirm the structure for your child's cohort with their coordinator.

faqs.question: What are Voronoi diagrams and are they worth revising properly?
faqs.answer: They are among the most reliable marks in the course. The content is small and self-contained: perpendicular bisectors, cells and sites, identifying which site a point is nearest to, and locating a point as far as possible from every site, usually framed as a planning or facility-siting problem. Students lose these marks to rushing rather than to confusion, because Voronoi questions tend to appear late in a paper when time is tight. A couple of focused sessions converts them from a gamble into a near-certainty.

faqs.question: Why does my son keep getting the finance questions wrong when he knows the method?
faqs.answer: Almost always one of two mechanical errors. The calculator's finance solver uses a sign convention, and a payment entered as a positive number where the convention requires a negative one produces a plausible-looking wrong answer. The other is compounding frequency misread from the question stem, which loses the whole item. Both are fixed by establishing the input order and the sign convention properly once, which takes about half an hour, and then using it on five varied questions until it is automatic rather than remembered.

faqs.question: How much of the Standard Level grade is the exploration worth, and when should it start?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, assessed against five criteria for twenty marks in total, written over months with no time limit and feedback permitted. It is the most controllable portion of the grade in this subject. The topic and, more importantly, the data should be settled in the first Diploma year, because the usual failure is choosing an interesting question and then discovering that no accessible data exists for it. Decide what data can actually be obtained first, then choose a question about it. That inversion is worth several marks.

faqs.question: What kind of exploration data can a student in Ajman actually collect?
faqs.answer: More than most assume. Counted observations along the Corniche give footfall or usage data over time. Any household with a Sharjah or Dubai commute has journey-time data worth modelling. Al Jurf has accessible small-business and logistics activity where queue lengths, stock turnover or delivery distances can be recorded. School-based data such as timings, scores or survey responses works where permission is given. The test is whether the student can obtain enough values to do something beyond a mean and a bar chart, because that is where use of mathematics marks live.

faqs.question: What does mathematical communication mean in the exploration marking?
faqs.answer: It is four of the twenty marks and it rewards defined variables, correct notation, labelled axes, stated assumptions and appropriate mathematical forms. Students lose most of those four by pasting calculator output into a document with no notation around it, no definitions and unlabelled graphs. It is the easiest criterion to secure and the most commonly neglected, and about twenty minutes with somebody who knows what the criterion expects fixes it permanently rather than for one draft.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a mathematics session was actually any good?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the marked work. A productive Standard Level hour puts the student's own writing at the centre: content taught with the student attempting examples, then timed questions on earlier topics, then marking together against the published scheme, then two lines of practice set. An hour of the tutor working through examples on screen while the student watches is comfortable and changes little, because the student never did mathematics under any pressure. If nothing was marked, there is no evidence either way.

faqs.question: Does my child need an IB specialist, or will a cheaper tutor do at Standard Level?
faqs.answer: It depends what is being repaired, and it is worth being honest about. For one rushed topic at Standard Level, budget online tutoring advertised from around AED 45 to AED 150 an hour can be adequate. For exploration supervision and criteria-level marking, the specialist band of AED 200 to AED 450 or more buys something real. The specialist premium matters less at Standard Level than at Higher Level, where unfamiliar extension content makes subject experience decisive. Those are published market rates from other providers, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Should a Standard Level student revise by topic or by past paper?
faqs.answer: Both, but for different papers. Paper 1 is shorter questions across the whole syllabus, so its failure mode is coverage and the right revision is an honest topic audit followed by teaching whatever is genuinely unmet, however dull that feels. Paper 2 is longer multi-part questions, so its failure mode is a dropped thread and the right revision is whole questions under timing with a note of what each part established. Doing more past papers on topics already secure is the most common wasted revision in this course.

faqs.question: Can my son move up to Higher Level Applications after starting at Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends far more on the school's timetable than on the student. Higher Level adds a great deal of unfamiliar content - matrices, graph theory, transition matrices, numerical differential equations - plus a third paper, and in a small cohort the two levels may not run as separate classes at all. Ask the school directly which levels will run next year before planning a move. If a degree requires Higher Level mathematics, settle that question against the university's own published entry requirements first.

faqs.question: How many weeks does it take to fix an accuracy habit?
faqs.answer: Four to six weeks of marked weekly work in most cases, which is unusually fast for anything in the Diploma. The reason is that the behaviour is small and specific: underline the accuracy instruction before calculating, carry units through the working, write the context sentence after any statistical value, check the data range before using a regression equation. Those are not understandings to be acquired but actions to be repeated, and repeated actions install quickly once a student has seen the count of marks they cost.

faqs.question: Does the chi-squared test need a written conclusion as well as a number?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is where half the available marks sit. The full answer builds the contingency table, states the degrees of freedom, obtains the statistic, compares it with the critical value, and then gives the conclusion twice: once in statistical terms about the null hypothesis, and once in plain language about the two variables the question described. Students routinely stop after the statistical sentence because it feels like the answer. Writing both, every time, is a habit worth drilling until it is automatic.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram teach Standard Level Applications at an address in Ajman?
faqs.answer: No. Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video, and IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is offered only in India. For this course the format fits the work: a calculator sequence is demonstrated keystroke by keystroke on a shared screen, a student's script is annotated line by line while both people look at the same page, and the marked work stays in a folder a parent can open. The market rate for an in-home visit, for comparison, runs AED 180 to AED 500 an hour.

faqs.question: What time should a weekly session start for a student commuting from Ajman to Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Later than most families first choose. Bus returns after 16:30 are normal from the Mowaihat and Rawda routes, and a session booked for 17:30 is a session with a tired student in it who will be rescheduled by week four. A 19:00 start holds across a full term in most households. During the second Diploma year weekend mornings work better still, because a full ninety-minute paper needs unbroken attention and a weekday evening rarely supplies it.

faqs.question: Which authority regulates my child's school and does it affect tutoring?
faqs.answer: Ajman's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which u.ae names as the supervising body for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah; there is no emirate-level authority here. If your child attends school in Sharjah, that school falls under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves curricula, fees and assessment methods as well as inspecting. For tutoring the practical consequence is the calendar: the internal deadlines and mock dates that matter are the school's, not the emirate of residence.

ajman/ib-dp-math-ai-sl-tutor.closingHeading: Count the lost marks before buying a single hour
ajman/ib-dp-math-ai-sl-tutor.closingBody: The most useful thing a Standard Level Applications family can do costs nothing: take one recent marked paper and sort the lost marks by cause rather than by topic. Accuracy, units, missing interpretation, a misread stem and one unmet topic are five different problems with five different repairs, and a report card saying the student is working well hides all of them. Send that paper and spend the free session on the count. If the losses are habits, you may need four weeks rather than two years. If one topic is genuinely missing, you will know which one. Either answer is worth having before any money changes hands.

ajman/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below take IB Physics at Higher Level: the five themes with their Higher Level extensions, multiple-choice pacing and data-analysis technique, extended response structure on Paper 2, and supervision of the student's own scientific investigation from design through to evaluation.

intro.heading: What the paperwork already in your house will tell you
paragraphs: Physics at Higher Level is the Diploma subject where a parent's impression and the evidence most often disagree. A student who talks confidently about physics, enjoys the lessons and does the reading can be losing a third of the available marks for reasons that have nothing to do with how much physics they know. Conversely, a student who says they do not understand any of it is sometimes losing marks to pacing and arithmetic, which is a much smaller problem than the sentence suggests. Neither situation can be diagnosed from a conversation.

Three documents settle it, and most households already have all three. The first is a marked Paper 2, with the examiner's or teacher's marks on it. The second is the most recent draft of the scientific investigation, ideally with criterion feedback written on it. The third is the sequence of the last two or three reports, read for direction rather than for the grade. Together they distinguish between four quite different problems: content gaps, technique failures, mathematics weakness, and a coursework component being neglected.

That distinction matters because the four need different work and different amounts of money. A content gap in one theme is four to six sessions. A technique failure in extended response is a habit built over about six weeks of marked writing. A mathematics weakness underneath the physics is a separate repair and often the real story. A neglected investigation is twenty per cent of the grade sitting unclaimed, recoverable with two short supervision blocks and no new physics at all.

The marks themselves are distributed in a way that rewards this kind of audit. At Higher Level, Paper 1 carries thirty-six per cent across multiple choice and data analysis, Paper 2 carries forty-four per cent in structured and extended-response questions, and the scientific investigation carries twenty per cent for twenty-four marks across four criteria. Confirm those weightings against the subject guide your child's coordinator issues, since guides change between cycles. The point stands regardless: a fifth of the grade is written at home over months with feedback permitted, and it is the part most often left until last.

The Ajman context is practical. The emirate's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, local Diploma provision is small, and a large share of Higher Level physics students here are enrolled in Sharjah or Dubai and home late. Laboratory access varies between schools and is the one thing online tutoring genuinely cannot substitute for, which is worth stating plainly rather than talking around. Everything else in this subject - scripts, drafts, derivations, graphs - is work on a shared screen, which is why the distance of a tutor is the least useful criterion for choosing one.
