ajman/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: Higher Level Physics is a 240-hour course, and the useful evidence changes as it progresses: early on it is homework and class tests, later it is marked papers and investigation drafts. The stages below describe where Ajman families actually arrive, and what can be read at each point.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The current IB Physics guide is organised into five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level extensions sit inside each theme rather than at the end of the course. Assessment is Paper 1, split into multiple choice and data analysis, Paper 2 of structured and extended-response questions, and the scientific investigation.
programmes.countryNote: Because Ajman's Diploma provision is concentrated in a single continuum school, many Higher Level physics students resident here are enrolled across the border in Sharjah or Dubai. Their internal deadlines, mock calendar and investigation submission date belong to that school, and the first document a tutor should ask for is that school's written deadline list.

programmes.name: First Diploma year
programmes.description: The year when the evidence is thinnest and the most valuable work is preventative. Mechanics and the mathematics underneath it are laid down here, and a student who leaves the first year with weak algebraic rearrangement and poor graph work will meet that gap in every later theme. The investigation design also belongs in this year in most schools, which makes it the cheapest time to get it right.
programmes.countryNote: Students entering a Diploma from British or Indian curriculum schools in Ajman and Sharjah usually arrive with solid factual physics and little experience of being asked to justify a method. That is a technique gap rather than a knowledge one, and it is much cheaper to address in the first year than in the revision term.

programmes.name: Second Diploma year
programmes.description: Where the evidence becomes abundant: mocks, marked past papers, a full investigation draft and the final report. By this point the pattern on a script is stable and readable in one session. Work here is diagnostic and targeted - whole papers under timing, marked against the published scheme, with a running record of the specific failure types rather than a general revision plan.
programmes.countryNote: The second Diploma year in the northern emirates collides with long commutes and a dense internal-assessment calendar across four or five subjects. Weekend mornings hold better than weekday evenings for the ninety-minute blocks that timed physics papers need, and the investigation tends to be the component that slips when everything else is due.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: MYP Sciences builds investigative habits and a different set of criteria from the Diploma's. The transferable parts are experimental design and the practice of evaluating a method rather than reporting a result. The gap that matters later is mathematical: MYP physics rarely demands the algebraic fluency that Higher Level Diploma physics assumes from the first week.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman Academy runs the IB continuum locally, so a student moving from MYP into the Diploma usually stays in one building and one assessment culture. Students arriving from elsewhere at Year 11 face a sharper change, and the usual shortfall is in graph work and rearrangement rather than in physics content.

programmes.name: IGCSE physics into Higher Level Diploma
programmes.description: An IGCSE physics background covers much of the factual content and almost none of the demand for justification, uncertainty treatment or extended written reasoning. Students arrive able to state a law and unable to explain why a graph's gradient means what it means. A short bridge on uncertainties, graph analysis and algebraic rearrangement is worth more than revisiting content they already hold.
programmes.countryNote: This is the most common entry route into Higher Level physics for Ajman families, since the local sector is largely British and Indian curriculum. A summer block on the mathematics underneath the physics prevents the single most expensive problem in the first Diploma year.

ajman/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Higher Level Physics is five themes, a set of experimental and mathematical tools, and the scientific investigation. The list below follows how a marked script separates them, with what each part is examined on and the evidence that it is or is not working.

subjects.name: Kinematics and dynamics
subjects.description: Motion graphs, equations of uniformly accelerated motion, Newton's laws, momentum and impulse. The evidence of trouble is rarely a wrong law; it is a free-body diagram that was never drawn, so forces are omitted and a correct method is applied to an incomplete situation.

subjects.name: Work, energy and power
subjects.description: Energy transfers, conservation arguments, efficiency and power. Scripts show this going wrong as an accounting error: energy appearing or vanishing between lines because the system boundary was never stated. Writing the boundary down converts a guess into a method.

subjects.name: Rotational motion and circular dynamics
subjects.description: Angular quantities, torque, moment of inertia, angular momentum and rolling bodies. A Higher Level extension with no IGCSE precursor, so it is new rather than hard. Marked scripts show it either secure or blank, which makes it a diagnosable and quickly repairable gap.

subjects.name: Thermal physics and the particulate model
subjects.description: Temperature, internal energy, specific heat, latent heat, the gas laws and the kinetic model. Higher Level adds deeper treatment of thermodynamic reasoning. Latent heat questions are where arithmetic slips cluster, usually from mixing units of mass partway through a calculation.

subjects.name: Waves, superposition and interference
subjects.description: Wave characteristics, reflection, refraction, diffraction, standing waves, the Doppler effect and interference. Higher Level deepens interference and diffraction treatment. The recurring loss is an explanation that describes what happens without identifying the path difference or phase relationship that causes it.

subjects.name: Fields: gravitational and electric
subjects.description: Field strength and potential, orbital motion, electric fields, potential difference and capacitance at Higher Level. The hardest conceptual area in the course for most candidates, because field strength and potential are routinely conflated and the sign conventions are unforgiving.

subjects.name: Electricity, circuits and electromagnetism
subjects.description: Current, resistance, circuit analysis, electromotive force and internal resistance, magnetic fields, induction and alternating current at Higher Level. Internal resistance questions separate a Higher Level cohort more reliably than any other single circuit topic.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, binding energy, fission and fusion, the photoelectric effect, wave-particle duality and, at Higher Level, deeper quantum and nuclear treatment. Heavily examined and often taught last, so a thin pass through it is visible in a mock as a cluster of near-misses.

subjects.name: Uncertainties and error propagation
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through calculations, uncertainty in gradients and intercepts. Examined on Paper 1B and assessed in the investigation, and the single most reliable source of recoverable marks in the subject for a student who has never been taught it properly.

subjects.name: Graph work and data analysis
subjects.description: Linearising a relationship, plotting with error bars, drawing maximum and minimum gradient lines, and extracting a physical quantity from a gradient or intercept. Paper 1B is built on this, and it is drillable, which makes it the fastest measurable improvement available in a marked-work programme.

subjects.name: The mathematics underneath the physics
subjects.description: Algebraic rearrangement, indices, logarithms, trigonometry, small-angle approximations and basic calculus reasoning. Not a separate syllabus topic, and frequently the actual cause of a Higher Level physics problem. A student who cannot rearrange confidently loses marks in every theme and appears to have a physics difficulty.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: An individual investigation worth twenty per cent of the grade, assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation for six marks each. The word ceiling is 3,000. Most of the mark is decided by whether the chosen question can actually generate data with a measurable relationship in it.

sections.heading: Reading a marked Paper 2: what the ticks do not tell you
paragraphs: A returned Paper 2 with a mark on the front is the most under-used document in a Diploma physics household. Parents read the total, students read the grade boundary, and nobody reads the distribution of the losses. That distribution is the diagnosis. Four marks lost on a single long question is a different problem from four marks lost one at a time across eight questions, and the two need completely different work, but the front page shows the same number either way.

The patterns are recognisable once you know what to look for. Marks lost at the start of long questions and nowhere else suggests a reading problem: the student is not extracting what the stem supplied. Marks lost at the end of long questions suggests pacing, or a dropped thread where a later part depended on an earlier result. Marks scattered one at a time across the whole paper usually means units, significant figures or a missing explanatory sentence, which is a habit rather than a knowledge gap. A whole question left blank or abandoned is a content gap in one theme, which is the cheapest of all to fix.

There is a fifth pattern which is the most commonly misread. A student loses marks on questions across several unrelated themes, and all of the lost marks sit at the point where the physics turns into algebra. That is not a physics problem. It is a mathematics problem wearing a physics uniform, and buying physics tuition for it produces a term of frustration on both sides. It shows up most clearly in questions requiring rearrangement before substitution, and it is worth checking before anything else is bought.

The table below converts those patterns into actions. It is written from marked scripts rather than from a syllabus, and the final column is the honest answer to the question families ask first, which is how long before anything changes.

sections.heading: Paper 1A and Paper 1B: two different papers in one booklet
paragraphs: Paper 1 at Higher Level contains two components that have almost nothing in common. Paper 1A is multiple choice across the whole syllabus. Paper 1B is a set of data-analysis questions built on experimental material. Together they carry thirty-six per cent of the grade. Students revise for them as one thing and should not, because the skills are unrelated and the failure modes are opposite: 1A punishes thin coverage and slow recall, while 1B punishes never having been taught uncertainty and graph analysis properly.

Paper 1A is a pacing exercise as much as a knowledge test. Forty questions at Higher Level in the allotted time leaves little room for deliberation, and the students who struggle are usually those who treat each item as a problem to be solved from first principles rather than recognised. The evidence of improvement is clean and quick to measure: the number attempted in a fixed period, and the ratio of changed answers that moved from right to wrong. Both are recordable, and both move within a few weeks of deliberate practice.

Paper 1B is the more interesting half, because it is where a large number of recoverable marks sit. Linearising a relationship so that a graph can be drawn, plotting with error bars, drawing maximum and minimum gradient lines, extracting a physical quantity from a gradient or intercept, and propagating uncertainty through a calculation are procedures. They are not insights. A student who has been taught them properly can do them on unfamiliar material; a student who has not will lose nearly all of these marks regardless of how well they understand the physics involved.

This is the strongest argument for an evidence-led programme. Uncertainty and graph work are drillable, heavily examined and assessed again inside the investigation, so a few focused sessions produce measurable movement in two places at once. When a family asks what the first six weeks should buy, this is frequently the honest answer, and the before-and-after evidence is two marked Paper 1B sections rather than an impression.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, criterion by criterion, read from a draft
paragraphs: The investigation is twenty per cent of a Higher Level physics grade and twenty-four marks across four criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each. It is written over months, with feedback permitted, and it is therefore the most controllable part of the grade. It is also the part most often left until the term it is due, by which point the decisions that determined the mark were taken long ago.

Research design carries the most consequence despite being worth the same six marks as the others. A question that cannot generate a measurable relationship - too few data points, a variable that cannot be controlled, a range too narrow for a trend to appear - produces a report in which data analysis has nothing to analyse, the conclusion has nothing to conclude and the evaluation has only the obvious to say. All four criteria suffer from one decision, and no amount of drafting repairs it. This is why the design block is the one worth buying first.

Data analysis is where the uncertainty work from Paper 1B reappears. Raw data processed without uncertainty, graphs plotted without error bars, a gradient taken without maximum and minimum lines: each of those is a visible band reduction. The criterion rewards appropriate processing and a clear presentation of what the data shows, and it is marked on what is actually on the page rather than on what the student understood. Conclusion rewards an interpretation that is justified by the data and related to accepted physics, including a proper comparison with a literature value where one exists.

Evaluation is the criterion most commonly thrown away. It does not reward listing sources of error in a generic paragraph. It rewards identifying the specific weaknesses of this method, judging their impact on the result, and proposing realistic improvements that would address them. A student who writes that human reaction time was a limitation has said something true and generic; a student who estimates its size and shows what it does to the gradient has written the evaluation the criterion is looking for.

On authorship, the boundary is firm and worth stating. A tutor may discuss the question, explain what each criterion rewards, advise on whether a design will produce usable data, and read a draft the student has written. A tutor may not supply data, produce the analysis, write any part of the report, or hand over a worked graph. Work that is not the candidate's own is a malpractice matter for the IB and the consequence falls on the student.

sections.heading: What moving a 4 to a 6 actually requires in Higher Level Physics
paragraphs: Families reasonably want to know what a grade jump costs in hours. The honest answer is that it depends entirely on which of the four problems is in play, and that two of the four are much cheaper than families expect while one is more expensive. Setting that out plainly is more useful than any promise, and no tutor can guarantee a grade in any case.

The cheapest case is a neglected investigation. Twenty per cent of the grade written at home with feedback permitted, currently scoring in the lower bands because the design was weak or the uncertainty work absent. Two supervision blocks and the student's own rewriting can move that substantially, and it requires no new physics at all. A student whose papers are genuinely at a 5 and whose investigation is at a 3 is not a 5 student; they are a student with an unclaimed fifth of a grade.

The second cheapest is the data-analysis and uncertainty cluster, because the same procedures are examined on Paper 1B and assessed inside the investigation. Four to six focused sessions on linearisation, error bars, gradient uncertainty and propagation show up in two components at once. Third is a single-theme content gap, which is four to six sessions and visible on the next paper covering that theme.

The expensive case is the mathematics underneath. A student who cannot rearrange confidently, who is unsure with indices and logarithms, and who does not trust their trigonometry is losing marks in every theme simultaneously. Repairing that is a separate programme of perhaps eight to twelve sessions, it feels like going backwards while it happens, and it improves everything at once when it lands. Families who recognise this early save a great deal; families who buy physics tuition for it spend a term discovering the diagnosis.

What should be refused in all four cases is a promise. No tutor can guarantee a grade or a score improvement, and any provider offering one should be treated with real scepticism. What can reasonably be promised is evidence: a marked script every week, criterion bands on successive drafts, and a six-week review conducted on the same documents as the first diagnosis. If those exist and nothing has moved, the right conclusion may be a different tutor, and a provider worth paying will say so.

sections.heading: The five themes, and where Higher Level scripts fall apart in each
paragraphs: The current Physics guide is organised into five themes rather than a list of topics, with Higher Level extension content embedded in each rather than appended at the end. That structure matters for revision, because a student who is weak in the shared material of a theme will be weak in its Higher Level extension too, and treating the extension as a separate body of work to be learned late is the most common planning error in this subject.

Space, time and motion carries mechanics, and its Higher Level extension includes rotational dynamics and angular momentum, which has no school-level precursor and is consequently either secure or blank on a script. Fields is the theme that separates a Higher Level cohort most sharply, because field strength and potential are conceptually distinct and routinely conflated, and the sign conventions are unforgiving of a casual approach. Capacitance and induction sit here too, and internal resistance questions in the electrical material are a reliable discriminator.

The particulate nature of matter holds thermal physics and the gas laws, where losses are mostly arithmetic rather than conceptual, usually from inconsistent units of mass or temperature partway through a calculation. Wave behaviour rewards explanations that name the mechanism - path difference, phase relationship, superposition - rather than describing the observed outcome, and scripts that describe without naming lose the explanation marks every time. Nuclear and quantum physics is heavily examined, frequently taught last, and a thin pass through it shows in a mock as a cluster of near-misses.

The practical consequence for a programme is that themes should be audited honestly rather than revised evenly. Mark each theme as secure, shaky or unmet, including its Higher Level extension separately, and spend the available sessions on the unmet entries. Students resist this because revising secure material feels productive and revising unmet material feels uncomfortable. The marked scripts, however, keep pointing at the unmet ones.

sections.heading: The mathematics underneath Higher Level Physics
paragraphs: Higher Level Physics assumes a level of mathematical fluency that it never teaches and rarely states. Algebraic rearrangement before substitution, confident work with indices and standard form, logarithms for decay and intensity relationships, trigonometry including component resolution, small-angle approximations, and the ability to read a gradient as a rate are all expected from early in the first year. A student who is shaky on any of them will find physics difficult in a way that looks like not understanding physics.

The diagnostic is straightforward and takes one session. Give the student a handful of questions where the physics is trivial and the algebra is not - rearrange for a quantity buried in a denominator, take logarithms of both sides of a power relationship, resolve a vector at an awkward angle, convert between units with an index change. If the physics questions were being lost at exactly these steps and these isolated exercises are also difficult, the diagnosis is settled and the programme should change.

What follows is uncomfortable for a few weeks. Repairing mathematical fluency means working on material that feels beneath the student, at a moment when a physics examination is approaching, and both student and parent tend to want to get back to physics. Pushing through is almost always right, because the gain is not confined to one theme: every theme contains algebra, so the repair raises marks across the whole paper rather than in one section of it.

There is a useful side effect worth mentioning. A student taking Higher Level physics is almost always taking a mathematics course too, and the repair improves that grade at the same time. For an Ajman family deciding where to spend a limited budget, that is a genuine double return, and it is the opposite of the conclusion most families reach when a physics grade falls, which is to buy more physics.

sections.heading: Laboratory access, practical skills and what online work can honestly evidence
paragraphs: This is the point where an honest page differs from a marketing one. Physics has a practical component embedded in the course and assessed through the scientific investigation, and the actual handling of apparatus cannot be done over a video link. A student who has never set up a circuit, never used a micrometer, never seen a signal generator, is missing something real, and online tutoring does not supply it. Laboratory provision varies between schools in Ajman and Sharjah, and it is a fair question to ask a school directly before a student commits to two Higher Level sciences.

What can be done remotely is a longer list than families expect, and it covers most of where the marks actually are. Experimental design can be worked through completely: variables, control, range, number of trials, how uncertainty will be estimated, whether a trend will be visible. Data analysis is entirely remote work and is where most investigation marks sit. Evaluation is reasoning about a method, not performing it. And the physics itself - derivations, explanations, graph work, past papers - is screen work in which annotating the same page together is better than sitting side by side.

There is also a practical route that families underuse. The investigation does not require exotic apparatus, and a well-designed experiment using everyday equipment at home, planned properly in a session and then carried out by the student, frequently produces better data than a rushed afternoon in a shared laboratory. Timing a pendulum, measuring terminal velocity in a liquid, tracking cooling curves, measuring resistance against length: all have produced strong investigations, and all can be designed remotely and executed by the student alone.

IB Gram delivers tutoring for UAE families one-to-one over live video. It does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. For this subject, the honest framing is that online delivery covers the analysis, the design reasoning and the entire examined physics, and does not cover apparatus handling, which belongs to the school. Stating the limit is more useful than claiming there is not one.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, permits, and the evidence trail that protects a candidate
paragraphs: An evidence-led programme has a second benefit beyond diagnosis. Keeping every draft, every marked script and every piece of feedback in a shared folder produces, as a by-product, a complete record of how the student's own work developed. If a question is ever raised about authorship, that record is the answer. Families do not usually think about this until it matters, and by then the folder either exists or it does not.

The boundary itself is not complicated. A tutor may teach physics, explain what a criterion rewards, discuss whether an investigation design will produce usable data, read a draft the student has written and give feedback against the published criteria. A tutor may not supply data, produce the analysis, write any part of the report, or hand over a worked solution to be submitted. Work that is not the candidate's own is a malpractice matter for the IB and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the person who sold the service. Some operators in this market sell completed internal assessments outright; that is the thing to walk away from at any price.

On licensing, the UAE position is clear and worth knowing. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no schedule of amounts has been published, any figure quoted as fact should be treated as unverified.

The permit's code of conduct bars a holder from tutoring students affiliated with their own school, which answers the question many families ask quietly about paying their child's own physics teacher. In Abu Dhabi emirate, ADEK's professional-ethics rules place a comparable restriction on private and charter school staff. For an Ajman household whose child is schooled in Sharjah or Dubai, the practical rule is simply that the tutor should not be employed by that school, and a provider who offers that arrangement is offering something the rules do not permit.

faqs.question: What should I send a physics tutor before the first session?
faqs.answer: Three documents, and nothing else. A marked Paper 2 with the marks visible on it, the most recent draft of the scientific investigation with any criterion feedback written on it, and the last two or three reports read for direction rather than for the grade. Those three distinguish between a content gap in one theme, a technique failure, a mathematics weakness underneath the physics, and a neglected coursework component worth a fifth of the grade. A conversation cannot distinguish between them, and a report card hides all four.

faqs.question: How much of a Higher Level Physics grade comes from each component?
faqs.answer: Paper 1, which contains multiple choice and data analysis, carries thirty-six per cent at Higher Level. Paper 2, with structured and extended-response questions, carries forty-four per cent. The scientific investigation carries twenty per cent and is marked out of twenty-four across four criteria. Confirm the weightings for your child's cohort against the subject guide their coordinator issues, since guides are revised between cycles. The useful consequence is that a fifth of the grade is written at home over months with feedback permitted.

faqs.question: My son loses marks across every topic but only where the algebra starts. What is that?
faqs.answer: A mathematics problem wearing a physics uniform, and it is the single most commonly misdiagnosed pattern in this subject. The test takes one session: give him questions where the physics is trivial and the algebra is not - rearranging for a quantity in a denominator, taking logarithms of a power relationship, resolving a vector at an awkward angle. If those are also difficult, buying physics tuition will produce a frustrating term. Repairing rearrangement, indices, logarithms and trigonometry takes eight to twelve sessions and raises marks in every theme at once.

faqs.question: Is there still a third paper in IB Physics at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Under the current guide the assessment is Paper 1, split into a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section, Paper 2 of structured and extended-response questions, and the internally assessed scientific investigation. Families who studied under an earlier structure, or who read older revision material, sometimes expect a separate options paper and plan revision around content that is no longer examined separately. Check the structure for your child's cohort with their coordinator, because that is the authoritative source and it changes between cycles.

faqs.question: Which part of Physics HL gives back the most marks for the least time?
faqs.answer: Uncertainty and graph analysis, because they are examined on Paper 1B and assessed again inside the scientific investigation. Linearising a relationship, plotting with error bars, drawing maximum and minimum gradient lines, extracting a quantity from a gradient, and propagating uncertainty through a calculation are procedures rather than insights, which means they are drillable. Four to six focused sessions typically produce visible movement in two components at once, and the before-and-after evidence is two marked Paper 1B sections rather than an impression.

faqs.question: How do we tell whether my daughter's investigation draft is any good?
faqs.answer: Read it against the four criteria rather than as a piece of writing. Research design: does the question have a measurable relationship, a stated range, controlled variables and enough points for a trend to appear? Data analysis: is uncertainty propagated, are there error bars, are maximum and minimum gradients drawn? Conclusion: is the result compared with accepted physics rather than simply stated? Evaluation: are specific weaknesses identified with an estimate of their effect, or is it a generic list of errors? Weak drafts usually fail the first question, which cannot be fixed by rewriting.

faqs.question: Why does the evaluation section lose marks when my son lists all the errors?
faqs.answer: Because listing is not what the criterion rewards. Six marks are available for identifying the specific weaknesses of this method, judging their impact on the result obtained, and proposing realistic improvements that would address them. Writing that human reaction time was a limitation is true and generic. Estimating its size, showing what it does to the gradient, and proposing a light gate as the fix is the evaluation being asked for. It is the criterion most commonly thrown away and one of the easiest to recover.

faqs.question: Which theme separates a Higher Level physics cohort most sharply?
faqs.answer: Fields, consistently. Field strength and potential are conceptually distinct and get used interchangeably, the sign conventions punish a casual approach, and the theme also holds capacitance, induction and alternating current at Higher Level. Internal resistance questions within the electrical material are a particularly reliable discriminator. Rotational dynamics in the motion theme runs it close for a different reason: it has no school-level precursor, so on a marked script it is either entirely secure or entirely blank, with very little in between.

faqs.question: Can online lessons cover the practical side of Physics HL?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the honest answer names the limit. Handling apparatus cannot be done over a video link, and a student who has never set up a circuit or used a micrometer is missing something real that belongs to the school. What can be done remotely is experimental design in full, the whole of data analysis, evaluation reasoning, and all the examined physics. A well-designed experiment using everyday equipment at home, planned in a session and carried out by the student, often produces better data than a rushed laboratory afternoon.

faqs.question: How long before we see evidence that physics tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: It depends which problem is being addressed, and a provider should tell you before you buy. A content gap in one theme shows on the next paper covering that theme. Accuracy and units habits move in three to four weeks of marked work. Pacing and extended-response technique take four to six weeks. A mathematics repair underneath the physics takes about six weeks and then improves every theme simultaneously. An investigation improvement shows in one submission cycle. None of that is a grade promise, and no tutor can give one.

faqs.question: Should my child take two Higher Level sciences in an Ajman or Sharjah school?
faqs.answer: It depends on laboratory provision and timetabling more than on ability, and it is a fair question to ask the school directly. Two Higher Level sciences means two scientific investigations with overlapping deadlines, two sets of practical work, and roughly 480 taught hours between them. Where laboratory access is limited, the investigations compete for the same scarce resource. Ask which weeks each investigation falls in, and whether the two departments coordinate their deadlines, before the subject form is signed.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a physics tutor to a home in Ajman?
faqs.answer: No. Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video, and IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is offered only in India. For this subject the format covers most of where the marks are: annotating a graph together on a shared screen, working a derivation line by line, marking a script with both people looking at the same page. What it does not cover is apparatus handling, which belongs to the school, and this page says so rather than implying otherwise.

faqs.question: Can we pay my son's own physics teacher for private lessons in Ajman?
faqs.answer: You should not, and a provider arranging it is offering something the rules do not permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, carries a code of conduct barring a holder from tutoring students affiliated with their own school. In Abu Dhabi emirate, ADEK's professional-ethics rules place a comparable restriction on private and charter school staff. For an Ajman family whose child is schooled across the border, the rule is simply that the tutor should not be employed by that school.

faqs.question: What if the six-week review shows nothing has changed?
faqs.answer: Then the programme was wrong, and a provider worth paying will say so rather than recommending more of it. The review runs on the same evidence as the first diagnosis: a marked question and a Paper 1B section from week six against those from the trial, plus the current investigation draft against the previous one. If there has been no movement, the usual explanations are a misdiagnosed category, a slot the student is too tired to use, or a mismatch with the tutor. All three are fixable, and continuing unchanged is not.

faqs.question: Who supervises my child's school if we live in Ajman, and does it affect physics?
faqs.answer: The federal Ministry of Education, which u.ae names as the supervising body for private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah; there is no emirate-level authority here. If your child attends school in Sharjah, that school sits under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves curricula, fees and assessment methods as well as inspecting. For physics specifically the practical consequence is laboratory provision and the internal investigation deadline, both of which belong to the school rather than to the emirate of residence.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the scientific investigation without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is firm. A tutor may discuss the research question, explain what each of the four criteria rewards, advise on whether a design will produce usable data, and read a draft the student has written and give feedback with the band named. A tutor may not supply data, produce the analysis, write any part of the report, or hand over a worked graph. Keeping every draft in a shared folder is also the honest record of how the work developed, which matters if authorship is ever questioned.

ajman/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the documents you already have
ajman/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.closingBody: A Higher Level Physics grade can be stuck for four quite different reasons, and all four produce the same sentence on a report card. The marked Paper 2, the investigation draft and the last few reports are already in the house, and together they say which one it is. Send them, and spend the free lesson on the count rather than on introductions: how many marks are in each category, and which of them are the cheap repairs. Two of the four are cheaper than most families expect. One is more expensive and worth knowing about early. Either way, the answer is more useful than a programme bought on an impression.

Each profile names the levels taken and the options covered, so the match can be checked before the free first lesson.

intro.heading: Psychology tuition in Ajman, priced by the month rather than the hour
paragraphs: An hourly rate tells you almost nothing about what Psychology support will cost a household, because the subject is not consumed evenly. Families buy a cluster of sessions before the first mock, a run of fortnightly hours while the experimental study is written, and then very little until February. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session give the clearest picture available: roughly AED 240–600 a month at the budget tier, AED 600–1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000–2,000 and above for specialist support in an examination year. Those are their figures, read in October 2026.

Translate that into a two-year plan and the number stops being frightening. A typical Ajman Psychology plan is twenty to thirty paid hours spread across two Diploma years, not a standing weekly hour for twenty-four months. Where the hours land matters more than how many there are: essay technique is worth most in the term before a mock, study supervision is worth most in the weeks a draft exists, and content revision is worth almost nothing paid for, because a student with a syllabus and a set of flashcards does it as well alone.

Psychology also has an unusual cost profile among Diploma subjects. There is no practical equipment, no field trip and no expensive text. What there is, instead, is a very large volume of named studies and a mark scheme that rewards a specific essay shape. Both of those are teachable, and neither needs a laboratory, which is why the published online bands apply here cleanly: AED 150–300 an hour for a qualified subject teacher, with Unitors listing IB subjects from AED 200, and AED 200–450 and above for an IB specialist, with TutorChase quoting AED 270.

What changes the number in this emirate specifically is scarcity rather than distance. Diploma Psychology runs in a small number of Ajman schools, often as a single-teacher department, and a large share of families here send children into Sharjah or northern Dubai for a school place instead. A visiting tutor therefore prices a short shortlist: published in-home rates run AED 180–500 an hour with travel folded in, against AED 1,599–1,799 a month for four two-hour visits. IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE — that is an India-only service — so none of those travel costs reach your invoice.

The rest of this page is organised around spending decisions. Which component your money should fix first, why a 22-mark essay is the most expensive habit in the course and a nine-mark answer the cheapest, what the experimental study costs stage by stage, and four things an Ajman parent can check in a single evening at no cost at all — including whether the person asking for money may lawfully take it. Lessons themselves run one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

ajman/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.programmesIntro: Psychology is a group three Diploma subject with no Middle Years equivalent, which makes the entry point unusually abrupt. Students arrive from Middle Years individuals and societies, from an IGCSE in a different social science, or from nothing related at all. Each route leaves a different gap, and the gap decides the first month's spending.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: There is no Middle Years Psychology course, so students come from individuals and societies with research and argument skills but no familiarity with studies, ethics or research methods. The transferable part is criterion-based writing, which is genuinely useful. The missing part is the habit of anchoring every claim to a named study with a date and a finding.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman's Middle Years cohort is concentrated at Ajman Academy, with alternatives in Sharjah. Families here contact us at option-selection time to ask whether a child who likes reading about behaviour will enjoy the Diploma course. One session with a past 22-mark essay question and its mark scheme answers that cheaply, and it is the only paid hour we would recommend at this stage.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Both levels study the biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches, choose from four options, and complete an experimental study. Standard Level sits Paper 1 at 50 per cent and Paper 2 at 25 per cent with the study at 25 per cent. Higher Level sits Paper 1 at 40, Paper 2 at 20, Paper 3 on research methods at 20 and the study at 20. Confirm against the school's copy of the guide.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma candidates are the audience here, and nearly all sit the May session. The practical consequence for an Ajman budget is that the experimental study, the Extended Essay interim deadline and the first set of mocks fall in the same winter term. Hours bought in that window are worth two or three times what the same hours buy in April, and the plan should be built around it.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Where a school offers the Career-related Programme, Psychology is a frequent Diploma course choice beside a health or social-care career study. Candidates sit identical papers, so everything on this page about marks and costs applies unchanged. The difference is the reflective project in place of the Extended Essay, which shifts the heaviest deadline weeks.
programmes.countryNote: Career-related places in the northern emirates are limited, and Ajman families asking about it are usually weighing it against an A-Level route in Sharjah. We teach the Psychology course the same way for both. The scheduling advantage is that January evenings are usually free of competing core deadlines, which is a good month to buy study supervision.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: Psychology is a popular Extended Essay subject and a difficult one, because a 4,000-word essay needs a question answerable from published research rather than from a new experiment. Students who want to run a study should put that effort into the assessed experimental study instead. Theory of Knowledge overlaps usefully with the methods content.
programmes.countryNote: The core creates the main budget clash for an Ajman household. A family running a daily commute into Sharjah or Dubai has perhaps five usable weekday evenings, and in the second winter term the Extended Essay, the experimental study and mock revision compete for all five. We quote core and subject support as separate hours so a family can see which one they are actually funding.

ajman/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.subjectsIntro: A Psychology plan is costed against components, not against the course as a whole. Below are the three core approaches, the four options, the research-methods content examined at Higher Level, and the two assessed essay formats. Work out which two of these your child is losing marks in, because that decides whether this term costs AED 300 or AED 1,200.

subjects.name: The biological approach
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with HL extensions
subjects.description: Localisation, neuroplasticity, neurotransmitters, hormones and pheromones, and genetics in behaviour. Content-heavy and comparatively easy to revise alone, because the studies are discrete and memorable. This is the approach parents should not pay for first: a syllabus and a disciplined fortnight closes most of the gap without a tutor.

subjects.name: The cognitive approach
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with HL extensions
subjects.description: Models of memory, schema theory, thinking and decision-making, reliability of cognitive processes, and the effect of emotion on cognition. Where students most often confuse a model with a study, and where essays drift into describing memory rather than evaluating a claim about it. The repair is cheap and specific: one marked essay, then another.

subjects.name: The sociocultural approach
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with HL extensions
subjects.description: Social identity theory, social cognitive theory, stereotypes, culture and cultural dimensions, and the effects of globalisation on behaviour. Students find the content accessible and the evaluation hard, because the obvious criticisms of cultural research repeat across every study. Teaching distinct evaluation points is what the paid hour is for.

subjects.name: Option: abnormal psychology
subjects.levels: One option at SL, two at HL
subjects.description: Classification and diagnosis, aetiology of disorders, and treatment, including the role of culture in diagnosis. The most commonly taught option in this region and the most study-dense. Essays reward precise use of diagnostic terminology, which is the sort of thing a student can lose four marks on without ever being told why.

subjects.name: Option: developmental psychology
subjects.levels: One option at SL, two at HL
subjects.description: Influences on cognitive and social development, developing an identity, and developing as a learner. Often chosen as the second Higher Level option because it shares studies with the cognitive approach, which genuinely reduces the revision load and therefore the number of paid hours needed.

subjects.name: Option: health psychology
subjects.levels: One option at SL, two at HL
subjects.description: Determinants of health, health problems including addiction and obesity, and health promotion. Less commonly taught, so a tutor matched to it is harder to find at short notice. Where your school teaches this option, ask about availability before a mock rather than after it.

subjects.name: Option: psychology of human relationships
subjects.levels: One option at SL, two at HL
subjects.description: Personal relationships, group dynamics, and social responsibility including prosocial behaviour. Popular with students and deceptively difficult in the examination, because everyday intuition about relationships produces answers that read plausibly and score poorly against the command term.

subjects.name: Approaches to research
subjects.description: Research methods, sampling, ethical considerations, and the analysis of a published study extract. Three short-answer questions on an unseen piece of research. It overlaps heavily with the experimental study, so Higher Level students who do the study properly get much of Paper 3 at no extra cost.

subjects.name: The experimental study
subjects.levels: SL and HL, marked in school
subjects.description: A replication of a published simple experiment, reported in up to 2,200 words and marked out of 22 across four criteria: introduction, exploration, analysis and evaluation. Supervision is feedback on the student's own design, data and writing. Our tutors question method and mark against criteria; they supply no data and no sentences.

sections.heading: What Psychology tuition costs an Ajman family by the month
paragraphs: Monthly figures are more honest than hourly ones for this subject, because almost nobody buys a uniform hour every week for two years. The clearest published monthly estimates in this market come from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table: roughly AED 240–600 a month for a weekly one-hour session at the budget tier, AED 600–1,200 at the qualified middle tier, and AED 1,000–2,000 and above for specialist support during an examination year. Competitor packages in the same cluster advertise around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions.

Behind those monthly numbers sit the hourly bands, and it is worth seeing both. EdFlik publishes from AED 45–65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33–52 at the undergraduate end. Unitors lists IB subjects from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270, Bestimate puts the specialist band at AED 200–450 and above, and BartyED sits at AED 650. Every one of those figures belongs to the company that published it and was read in October 2026; none of them is an IB Gram price, because we publish no hourly list.

The useful thing about reading the market monthly is that it exposes the real cost driver, which is duration rather than rate. Eight months of a mid-tier weekly hour costs more than ten specialist hours concentrated where they matter, and buys less. Most Ajman Psychology plans we build come to twenty to thirty paid hours across both Diploma years, clustered in two or three blocks. Set against the monthly bands above, that lands well below a continuous subscription at any tier.

sections.heading: Which component you are actually paying to repair
paragraphs: Psychology splits into components with very different costs per mark gained. The two Paper 1 and Paper 2 essays are worth 22 marks each and respond to coached technique; the short-answer questions are worth nine each and respond to a template; the experimental study is worth 22 marks over four criteria and needs a reader rather than a teacher; and Higher Level's Paper 3 overlaps so heavily with the study that it is nearly free if the study is done properly.

Diagnose before you spend. A student losing marks across every component has a content problem and probably a revision problem, and the cheapest first move is a fortnight of disciplined flashcards at no cost. A student who answers short questions well and essays badly has a technique problem, which is the most expensive to fix and the most reliable to fix. A student whose papers are fine and whose study draft is thin needs six hours of supervision and nothing else at all.

The table below sets each component against the honest answer to the question families ask most: is this worth paying for? Content revision is listed as not worth paying for, and that is deliberate. Any page that tells you every part of a course needs a tutor is selling hours rather than advice, and in this subject the self-study component is unusually large because the content is memorisable and the studies are published and freely discussed in the textbook the school already issued.

sections.heading: The 22-mark essay is the most expensive habit to teach
paragraphs: Almost every Psychology grade below a 6 is an essay grade. The command term at the front of the question — discuss, evaluate, to what extent, contrast — sets the shape the examiner expects, and students treat all four as instructions to write everything they know about a topic. That produces an answer full of accurate content and short of credit, which is the most demoralising kind of script to read as a parent, because the knowledge is visibly there.

Teaching the repair is slow, which is why it is expensive. Each command term has to be separated from the others, practised against a different question, marked honestly, and then practised again. A student needs to learn that a 'discuss' answer carries weight on both sides of a claim, that an 'evaluate' answer needs criteria stated before judgements are made, and that a 'contrast' answer must sustain the comparison rather than describe two things in sequence. None of that is learnable in one session, and it does not generalise quickly.

What makes it the best purchase in the subject anyway is the arithmetic. At Standard Level, one Paper 1 essay plus one Paper 2 essay is a large share of the total marks available, and the same habit serves both. A block of eight to twelve marked essays with proper feedback has moved more students from a 4 to a 6 than any other intervention we sell. Buy that block in the term before the mock, when there is still time for the habit to bed in, rather than in the fortnight before the real papers.

sections.heading: Nine marks, three times: the cheapest improvement available
paragraphs: Paper 1 opens with three short-answer questions worth nine marks each, and they are the most mechanical marks in the course. Each wants a defined concept, a named study with enough procedural detail to be recognisable, a finding, and a link back to the question. There is no requirement for evaluation and no reward for length. A student who writes a page and a half has usually written three times what the mark scheme needs.

This is teachable in one session and drillable for nothing afterwards. The template is short enough to be written on a card, and the practice material is free: past question stems are available through the school, and a student can write two nine-mark answers in twenty minutes and self-mark them against the template. Parents who want something useful to supervise at no cost should supervise this.

The reason it matters for a budget is proportion. Three nine-mark answers are a meaningful block of Paper 1, and they are available to a disciplined student without a tutor. Every mark banked there is a mark that does not need to be chased in the essay, where the teaching is expensive. We teach the template in the free first lesson where that is what a student needs, and then tell the family to drill it at home rather than booking a term of hours against it. A fortnight of two answers a night, self-marked against the card, reaches the ceiling on this component for most students, and an Ajman parent can supervise the whole of it from the kitchen table.

sections.heading: Higher Level means two options and a third paper to fund
paragraphs: The Standard Level and Higher Level courses are not the same purchase. Standard Level students study one option and answer one essay on it in Paper 2. Higher Level students study two options and answer two essays, in a paper twice the length, and additionally sit Paper 3 on approaches to research. The extension content inside each of the three core approaches is also examined at Higher Level, which lengthens Paper 1.

In cost terms, the second option is the real difference. A whole additional body of named studies, evaluation points and terminology has to be learned and then written about under time, and in a small Ajman department the second option is frequently taught late or compressed. Where that has happened, a dated block on the weaker option is the most efficient spend available to a Higher Level family, and it is usually six to eight hours rather than a term.

Paper 3 behaves in the opposite direction and is good news for a budget. It presents an unseen extract of published research and asks three short questions about method, sampling, ethics and analysis. A student who has genuinely designed, run and evaluated their own experimental study already holds most of what Paper 3 asks for. Where the study has been done properly, two to four hours of practice on past extracts is enough; where the study was rushed, Paper 3 becomes a second cost rather than a free one.

sections.heading: The experimental study, priced stage by stage
paragraphs: The experimental study is a replication of a published simple experiment, written up in no more than 2,200 words and marked in school out of 22 across four criteria: introduction, exploration, analysis and evaluation. The marks are not evenly spread, and neither is the work. Confirm the current criterion wording against your school's copy of the subject guide before building a plan around it.

The expensive errors happen at the start, which is why the first two hours are the ones worth buying. A student who picks a published study that cannot realistically be replicated with a class of volunteers has guaranteed a weak exploration and a weak evaluation months before either is written. A student who gathers data before thinking about the statistical test has often collected the wrong kind of data. Both failures are cheap to prevent and extremely expensive to repair.

The boundary on this component is strict and we hold it. A tutor may question a design, point out an ethical problem, explain what a criterion asks for, check that a chosen statistical test matches the design, and read one draft with questions in the margin. A tutor may not design the study, supply or alter data, or write any part of the report. Our tutors do not write a student's report, and we state that because completed assessed work is sold openly in this market. An IB malpractice finding falls on the student, not on the tutor who caused it.

sections.heading: Four things an Ajman parent can verify in one evening, free
paragraphs: Before any money moves, four checks cost nothing and change what you should pay. The first is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced private tuition work permits, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing with a two-working-day completion time and no fee. Ask any prospective tutor whether they hold it. Individuals tutoring without one face fines and penalties under the applicable laws; the schedule is not published, so no figure belongs on this page.

The second is the regulator. Private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, where Dubai schools answer to KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to ADEK, and Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority. That matters because inspection reporting and curriculum approval follow a federal route here, and because any provider claiming emirate-level accreditation for a service in Ajman has made a mistake worth noticing. IB Gram holds no accreditation from any authority or board and claims none.

The third and fourth checks are a phone call to the Diploma coordinator: which Paper 2 option or options is my child studying, and what is the school's internal deadline for the experimental study? Those two answers determine the tutor match and the month in which hours are worth buying. A quote produced without them is a guess. One further question is worth asking of any provider: is the figure you have quoted inclusive of tax? We will tell you for our own quote, and we will not state the UAE tax treatment of tuition fees here, because that is a Federal Tax Authority matter and an unsourced claim would be worse than silence.

sections.heading: Two Diploma years of Psychology, costed end to end
paragraphs: Set against a two-year horizon, the choices on this page become easy to compare. The table below prices three plausible plans for an Ajman family using the published hourly bands: a continuous weekly hour at the mid tier, a targeted block plan, and a late-panic plan bought in the final eight weeks. The hourly figures are the market's, read in October 2026, and the hour counts are our own planning assumptions rather than quotations.

The targeted plan is cheaper and scores better, and the reason is not mysterious. It spends on essay technique in the term before a mock, on study supervision while a draft exists, and on nothing during the months when a student should be making flashcards. The continuous plan spends through those months at the same rate, which is how a family reaches April having paid for forty hours and seeing a grade that has not moved.

The late plan is the most expensive per mark and we still take the booking, because a family that arrives in March is not helped by being told they should have come in October. What we will say honestly is what eight weeks can reach: essay technique and short-answer templates, yes; a rebuilt experimental study, no, because it has been submitted; two options learned from nothing, no. Fees for school places and private-candidate examination entries sit outside this table because they are set by the school or the centre, and inventing a figure would be worse than leaving the row open.

sections.heading: Online delivery, the visiting premium, and the fallback when nobody is free
paragraphs: Parents in Ajman ask about a visiting tutor, so here is the straight comparison. The published in-home band in this market is AED 180–500 an hour with travel folded in, against AED 150–300 online for a qualified subject teacher and AED 200–450 and above online for a specialist. Monthly packages make the gap plainer still: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599–1,799 for four two-hour visits. The premium buys proximity, and in a small emirate proximity means a very short list of candidates.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tuition is a service we run only in India. Psychology lessons for Ajman families run one-to-one over live video, which suits this subject particularly well: essays are marked live in the document, a study draft is annotated where the student can see each comment, and a named-study revision set can be built on a shared screen and kept. None of that produces a drive, and none of it produces a travel line on an invoice.

The last cost worth naming is the one nobody advertises: the cost of a mismatch. Psychology specialists who cover a specific Paper 2 option are not evenly available, and the most contested slot in our week is a weekday evening after 7pm, which is exactly when Ajman households commuting back from Dubai are free. Where no suitable tutor is available we say so and offer a different evening, a Saturday block, or a short wait. We do not fill the hour with a generalist, because an hour that teaches the wrong option is not cheaper than no hour at all.

process.title: Send one marked script and two dates
process.description: A recent marked Psychology paper or essay, the school's internal deadline for the experimental study, and the option or options being taught. From those three we can say which component is losing marks and in which month hours are worth buying, rather than quoting a rate against a guess.

process.title: Get a component diagnosis, not a sales call
process.description: We read the script and name the problem: content, essay technique, option coverage or the study. Where the honest answer is that a disciplined fortnight of revision would do more than paid hours, we say so. That answer has cost us bookings and is the reason some families come back a year later.

process.title: A free first lesson before any payment
process.description: A full session with the proposed tutor at no charge. Ask them to mark one 22-mark essay in front of your child and explain each mark lost against the command term. Fifteen minutes of that reveals whether you are buying a specialist or a generalist.

process.title: Agree the block, the slot and the total
process.description: Psychology is bought in blocks here, so we agree how many hours, over which weeks, at what figure, and whether that figure includes tax. The Gulf Standard Time slot, holiday pauses and post-Iftar timings during Ramadan are fixed at the same point, in writing.

process.title: Mark, return, record
process.description: Every session produces marked work back before the next one and a short written note of what was covered. For experimental study hours that note doubles as the record a school may want when confirming the report is the student's own work.

process.title: Stop when the block is done
process.description: A block ends on its last session rather than rolling into a subscription. We review the next school assessment against the plan and propose a further block only if the evidence supports one. A plan that never ends was a subscription sold as a plan.

whyPoints.title: Priced monthly and by the block, not by an open subscription
whyPoints.description: Psychology support is worth most in two or three concentrated windows, so that is how we quote it. Twenty to thirty hours across two Diploma years, aimed at essay technique and the experimental study, costs less than a continuous weekly hour and moves more marks.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure is sourced and dated
whyPoints.description: Each band on this page names the company that published it and the month we read it. Three of the six competitors ranking for these queries publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars. A family in Ajman transacts in dirhams and should be able to see the working.

whyPoints.title: We name the parts you should not pay for
whyPoints.description: Named studies, terminology and the nine-mark short-answer template are all within reach of a disciplined student with a syllabus. We teach the template once and then tell families to drill it free, because hours spent there are hours not spent on the 22-mark essay.

whyPoints.title: The study boundary is written down and held
whyPoints.description: Tutors question design, flag ethical problems, check the statistical test and mark a draft against the criteria. They do not design the study, supply data or write the report. Completed coursework is sold openly in this market, and the malpractice finding falls on the student.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the option your school actually teaches
whyPoints.description: Paper 2 examines only the option or options the department runs, and in a single-teacher Ajman department that is often taught late. We ask which it is before proposing anyone, because a specialist in a different option cannot help with a fifth to a quarter of the grade.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the limits
whyPoints.description: No grade promise, no tutor sent to a UAE address, no regulator approval claimed, no premises in the UAE, and a direct answer when no Psychology specialist is free in your slot. Where eight weeks is not enough to fix something, we say which things are out of reach.

faqs.question: What does Diploma Psychology tuition cost per month for a family in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's 2026 monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run about AED 240–600 at the budget tier, AED 600–1,200 at the qualified tier, and AED 1,000–2,000 and above for specialist support in an examination year. Packages advertised in this cluster include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those figures belong to the companies that published them and were read in October 2026. Most plans we build for this emirate are blocks rather than subscriptions, which usually lands below the monthly bands across a full two years.

faqs.question: Is Psychology cheaper to tutor than a Diploma science subject?
faqs.answer: The hourly bands are the same, because the market prices by tutor tier rather than by subject. What differs is how many hours the subject genuinely needs. Psychology has no practical equipment, no laboratory work and a large body of content a disciplined student can revise alone, so the paid hours concentrate on essay technique and the experimental study. A sciences plan usually needs more continuous support across the content. In practice a Psychology plan at twenty to thirty hours over two years is at the lower end of what we build.

faqs.question: Why does teaching a 22-mark essay cost more than teaching the content?
faqs.answer: Because content can be prepared once and delivered to anybody, while essay technique has to be built in one student through repeated marking. Each command term — discuss, evaluate, to what extent, contrast — demands a different answer shape, and learning the difference takes eight to twelve marked essays with honest feedback. That is bespoke work with nothing reusable behind it, which is why it sits in the specialist band. It is also the single most reliable way we know to move a Psychology grade from a 4 to a 6.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level Psychology cost more to support than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the difference is concentrated in one place. Higher Level students study two options rather than one and write two Paper 2 essays, so a second body of named studies has to be learned, and in a small department the second option is often taught late. Budget six to eight extra hours for that. Paper 3 on research methods usually costs very little if the experimental study was done properly, since the skills overlap. The study supervision hours themselves are identical at both levels.

faqs.question: How many hours does the experimental study report actually need?
faqs.answer: Six to ten supported hours across two terms, unevenly spread. One or two at the start, choosing a published experiment that can genuinely be replicated and checking the design and the ethics; nothing at all while data is collected; one or two on the statistical choice; and two to four on the write-up inside the 2,200-word ceiling. The early hours are the ones that save money, because a study that cannot be replicated guarantees a weak exploration and evaluation months before either is written.

faqs.question: Can we pay for short-answer technique on its own and nothing else?
faqs.answer: You can, and usually you should not need to pay much for it. The three nine-mark questions that open Paper 1 want a defined concept, a named study with recognisable procedure, a finding and a link to the question. That is a template short enough to write on a card. We teach it in the free first lesson where that is the need, then suggest the student drills it at home against past stems for nothing. Spending a term of paid hours there takes money away from the 22-mark essay, where the teaching is genuinely hard.

faqs.question: Are the AED figures quoted on this page inclusive of tax?
faqs.answer: The competitor rates here are published without a stated tax treatment, so treat them as advertised figures and ask each provider what their number includes. We will not state the UAE tax position on tuition fees on this page, because that is a Federal Tax Authority matter and an unsourced claim would be worse than none at all. What we will do is tell you, before you commit to anything, whether the figure IB Gram quotes you is inclusive. Ask every provider you shortlist the same question and compare the answers.

faqs.question: Does a Psychology tutor living outside Ajman cost us more?
faqs.answer: No. Distance only affects a visiting tutor's rate, where travel time is paid for, which is why the published in-home band of AED 180–500 an hour sits above comparable online bands. For a lesson delivered over live video the tutor's location changes nothing about the hour you buy. What it changes is the shortlist: instead of the handful of people within a short drive of Al Rawda or Al Mowaihat, you choose from Diploma Psychology specialists who cover your child's actual Paper 2 option.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Psychology tutor to a house in Ajman?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; visiting tuition is a service we run only in India. Lessons for Ajman families are delivered one-to-one over live video. The format suits this subject well, because essays are marked inside the document, study drafts are annotated where the student can see each comment, and a revision set of named studies can be built on a shared screen and kept. The local visiting market does exist at a published AED 180–500 an hour if proximity is non-negotiable.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with my daughter's experimental study, and what is off limits?
faqs.answer: A tutor may question the design, warn about a confound, flag an ethical problem before data is collected, explain what each assessment criterion asks for, check that the statistical test matches the design, and read one draft leaving questions in the margin. A tutor may not design the study, collect or alter data, or write any part of the report. Our tutors do not write a student's report. Completed assessed work is sold openly in this market, and an IB malpractice finding falls on your daughter rather than on whoever supplied it.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor may lawfully charge us for lessons in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask directly whether they hold the private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE free of charge for two years, and the service is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing with a two-working-day completion time and no published fee. Teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18 may all apply. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Does it matter for tutoring that Ajman schools report to the federal Ministry of Education?
faqs.answer: Indirectly, and it is worth knowing. Private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, where Dubai answers to KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to ADEK, and Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Inspection reporting and curriculum approval therefore follow a federal route here. For a tutoring plan the practical effect is that internal deadlines and option choices are set by the school rather than the regulator, so the coordinator is the person to ask, not the authority.

faqs.question: Which Paper 2 option is my child studying, and does it change what we pay?
faqs.answer: Ask the Diploma coordinator: schools teach one of abnormal psychology, developmental psychology, health psychology, or the psychology of human relationships, and Higher Level students take two. It does not change the hourly band, but it changes availability. Abnormal and developmental psychology are widely taught and easy to match; health psychology is less common, so a specialist in it may need a week or two of notice. Booking before a mock rather than after it is the practical way to avoid paying for a mismatch.

faqs.question: We can spend about AED 600 a month. What does that realistically buy for Psychology?
faqs.answer: At published mid-tier bands, roughly two to three hours a month with a qualified subject teacher, or fewer hours with a specialist. Our advice at that budget is to spend nothing for several months and then buy a concentrated block: eight to ten specialist hours on 22-mark essay technique in the term before the mock, plus four to six on the experimental study while a draft exists. Spread thinly across two years, AED 600 a month buys company. Concentrated into two blocks, it buys the two things that actually move the grade.

faqs.question: If no Psychology specialist is available in our slot, what do you tell us?
faqs.answer: The truth, with options. Psychology specialists matched to a specific Paper 2 option are not evenly available, and weekday evenings after 7pm are the most contested hours in our week, which is exactly when Ajman families commuting from Dubai are free. We offer a different evening, a Saturday block, or a wait of a week or two. If none of that works we say so rather than putting a generalist in the slot, because an hour on the wrong option is not better value than no hour.

ajman/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.closingHeading: Spend in the right month, not every month
ajman/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.closingBody: An IB DP Psychology tutor in Ajman is worth paying for in two windows: the term before a mock, when 22-mark essay technique can still bed in, and the weeks a draft of the experimental study exists. Outside those windows a syllabus and a disciplined fortnight do more than an hourly rate. Send us one marked script, the option your child is studying and the school's internal deadline, and we will tell you which window you are in and what a block should cost. The first lesson is free, sessions run one-to-one over live video to Gulf Standard Time, and the published figures on this page belong to the companies that published them.
