sections.heading: Reading a quote: per hour, per session, per month, per subject
paragraphs: Four units are in common use in this market and they are not interchangeable, which is how two quotes that look similar turn out to differ by half. Ask which unit you are being quoted in and convert everything to one before you compare anything.

Per hour is the cleanest and the rarest at the premium end. Per session matters because a session is not always sixty minutes: ninety-minute and two-hour sessions are standard for in-home work, so AED 400 a session may be AED 200 an hour or AED 267 an hour depending on length. Per month is the hardest to read, because a monthly figure hides both the session length and the number of sessions. The AED 799 monthly online package seen in this market covers eight sessions, which is roughly AED 100 a session; the AED 1,599 to 1,799 in-home monthly figures cover four two-hour visits, which is AED 200 to 225 an hour. Same market, very different arithmetic.

Per subject is the unit that catches families out at the end. A quote given for a student is not a quote for three subjects, and the assumption that a weekly hour can rotate between Chemistry, Mathematics and English is how a plan ends up delivering a third of a session in each. If you need two subjects, price two arrangements and decide whether you want both, rather than buying one and dividing it.

Two further questions worth asking in writing. Does the figure include the tutor's marking time, and is that marking done before the session or inside it? And what is the position on tax: we will not state the VAT treatment of tuition fees as a matter of fact, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation nobody in this market provides, but any provider quoting you a figure should be able to say plainly whether their own number includes it.
bullets: Convert every quote to AED per teaching hour before comparing
Ask the session length before accepting a per-session figure
Ask how many sessions a monthly package contains, and how long each is
Price per subject, not per child
Ask whether marking is included and whether it happens before the hour

sections.heading: Six things that move the number in Ajman specifically
paragraphs: Generic UAE price pages give you a national band and leave you to guess where your own emirate sits inside it. Six local factors do most of the work here, and five of them push upwards.

Specialist scarcity is the largest. IB provision in Ajman is concentrated rather than widespread, so the local pool of people who can mark a Higher Level Chemistry investigation is small, and a small pool prices like a small pool. The commute is the second: with many households having a parent working in Dubai or Sharjah, the usable evening starts late and the slots between 18:30 and 21:00 are the only ones that reliably work, which concentrates demand into a narrow window. Travel distance is the third, and it varies sharply by district — Al Rashidiya is cheap to reach, Al Jurf is not.

The fourth is the two-hour minimum convention on visits, which doubles the smallest amount you can buy. The fifth is the academic calendar: Ramadan compresses the school day and shifts sessions later, and the months around internally assessed deadlines concentrate demand across every family at once. The sixth factor pushes the other way, and it is the only one that does: because lessons can run over video, an Ajman family is buying from a national pool rather than a local one, which is why online specialist rates in this market sit below in-home rates rather than above them.

One factor that should not move the number, and sometimes does: a provider's claim to regulator approval. No tutoring platform in this market holds an endorsement from the International Baccalaureate, the Ministry of Education or any emirate authority, and a premium charged on the strength of an implied seal of approval is a premium on nothing. IB Gram holds no such accreditation and claims none.

sections.heading: The cheapest intervention in the two years, and when to buy it
paragraphs: The highest-value money in a Diploma, measured by grade movement per dirham, is almost always spent in the summer between the two years, and almost nobody spends it there. The reason is arithmetic rather than pedagogy. A content gap in a Higher Level subject is measured in dozens of teaching hours, and a weekly hour during term is consumed by whatever is urgent that week, so the gap never closes while new content keeps arriving on top of it.

A fortnight of daily hours in a quiet period behaves completely differently. There is no new content arriving, no homework competing, and the tutor can work through a syllabus in sequence rather than triaging. Families who do this typically spend less in total than families who buy a weekly hour for eighteen months, and they start DP2 without the deficit that would otherwise have shaped the whole year.

The second cheapest intervention is earlier still: the year before the Diploma begins. A student entering DP1 secure in algebraic manipulation, able to write a paragraph with a controlling idea and used to working against a criterion rather than for a teacher's approval has access to the whole programme. One who is not may be paying for remedial work in two subjects for two years. Middle Years support is quieter, less urgent and considerably better value than anything purchasable in DP2.

The most expensive intervention is the one bought six weeks before papers for a gap that is two years wide. It is also the one most often sold, because that is when parents are most frightened. A short block repairs technique and cannot install a syllabus, and we will say so at the diagnostic. The honest conversation at that point is about triage — which subjects to protect, and whether a later session is the sensible route for the weakest.
bullets: Best value: a concentrated block in the summer between DP1 and DP2
Second best: skills work in the Middle Years, before the Diploma begins
Reasonable: short component blocks with a named school deadline
Worst value: a long weekly arrangement bought in panic in the final term

sections.heading: What the money does not buy, at any rate
paragraphs: Three things are not purchasable, and a provider who prices them is selling something they cannot deliver. The first is a grade. No tutor can promise a Diploma score or a specific improvement, and any package priced against a predicted total is a claim about an outcome controlled by the student and the examiner. The gate on every page of this site blocks that claim, and it should.

The second is motivation. A tutor can see the work, mark it and tell you honestly when it has not been done. They cannot make a seventeen-year-old open a book at eight o'clock, and where that is the actual problem the sessions become a weekly receipt for the same information. If the diagnostic reaches that conclusion, we will say it rather than invoice around it for a term — which is cheaper for you and more sustainable for us.

The third is authorship, and this is the one with consequences. One operator researched in this market advertises completed internal assessments at a four-figure price. Buying that transfers the risk entirely onto your child: awarding bodies treat authorship breaches as malpractice, the penalty can reach an entire entry rather than one component, and the student confirms the work is their own as part of submitting it. A tutor may teach the skill, read the criteria, question a draft the student has written and mark a timed task. That is the whole of the permitted range, and it is enough.

What the money does buy is specific and checkable: diagnosis of where the marks are going, training in the technique that recovers them, marked work every week, and a written record you can read without the subject guide. Judge any arrangement on whether those four things arrive, not on how reassuring the conversation was.

sections.heading: Why this is delivered over live video, and what that removes from the bill
paragraphs: Every lesson for an Ajman family runs one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. The student needs a device with a camera, a reliable connection, paper and the same desk each week. Work is photographed and sent ahead so the tutor has marked it before the hour begins, which means the billed time is teaching rather than reading.

Three cost lines disappear in that arrangement and it is worth being specific about which. Travel, both the tutor's and the hidden cost of your evening. The two-hour minimum booking, because there is no journey to justify, so a single hour is a purchasable unit. And the scarcity premium, because the pool is no longer whoever can reach your district by 19:00. That third one is the largest in a small emirate, and it is the reason online specialist rates in this market sit below in-home rates rather than above them.

Two things get worse, and they belong in the same paragraph as the savings. A screen cannot supervise a reluctant student into starting, and it cannot handle laboratory apparatus. Where supervision is the real requirement, the honest recommendation is the in-home market option priced earlier on this page, and we would rather say that at the diagnostic than afterwards. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, and pretending otherwise would waste your evening.

For the typical Ajman enquiry — one Higher Level subject, a grade below target, components approaching — the format is not a compromise. It is the reason a household in Al Mowaihat can hold a standing 19:30 slot with a specialist in the subject rather than a weekly appointment with the nearest available generalist.

sections.heading: What a quote from us looks like, and the honest no
paragraphs: You send the subject, the level, the year group, a photograph of a recent marked piece and the two evening windows that genuinely work. We come back with a named tutor, their subject and level coverage, a proposed slot in Gulf Standard Time and a figure for a defined block rather than a tariff. The first lesson is free and is a diagnostic; no payment is taken before it, and there is no obligation to continue afterwards.

The quote names three things explicitly, because those are the three that go wrong elsewhere. How long a session is. Whether marking is included and when it happens. And what the block is for, with an end date, so that it does not quietly become a subscription. If you want two subjects, you get two figures, because a rotating hour is not two arrangements.

The availability answer is given straight, which is rare in this market. Mathematics, the three sciences, English A and B, Economics, Business Management and Psychology are generally coverable within a few days at both levels. Some ab initio languages, the arts at Higher Level and Arabic as a first language take longer or cannot be covered, and when that is the case we say so rather than holding an enquiry open. Telling you where the gap is lets you look in the right place.

And there is a point at which the honest answer is to spend nothing. If the diagnostic says the gap is supervision, or that the student is carrying three Higher Levels they cannot carry, or that six weeks will not close a two-year deficit, you will hear that at the free lesson. The week-six review exists for the same reason: six marked pieces on the table, one question about whether the targeted criterion moved, and a willingness to recommend stopping if it did not.

process.title: Send a marked piece, the subject and the level
process.description: A photograph of recent marked work tells us more than a description does: it shows the level, the command terms being missed and the state of written method under time pressure. Add the year group, the target grade and the two evening windows your household can genuinely hold, since an unkeepable slot is not a plan.

process.title: A free diagnostic lesson, no payment first
process.description: One hour with the script in front of both of them. The output is a written diagnosis: which loss patterns are present, which are weeks of work and which are a term, and what the first three weeks would target. If the honest conclusion is to spend nothing, that is what you will be told, and there is nothing to cancel.

process.title: A quote for a block, not a tariff
process.description: A figure for a defined number of hours with a named target and an end date, stating session length, whether marking is included and when it happens. Two subjects get two figures. Nothing renews automatically, because an undefined block becomes a subscription and nobody notices the moment it happened.

process.title: Weekly marked work, prepared before the hour
process.description: A timed task every week, sat to the real limit, photographed and sent ahead so it is already marked. The session is spent on the marks rather than on reading, and a written note follows naming the criterion targeted and whether it moved. That note is what the week-six review reads.

process.title: Review at week six and decide
process.description: Parent, student and tutor look at six marked pieces and answer one question: has the targeted criterion moved? If it has, pick the next target or stop. If it has not, either the diagnosis or the match changes. A provider unwilling to hold that conversation has told you something useful.

whyPoints.title: Every figure attributed and dated
whyPoints.description: Three of six researched competitors publish no price at all and the two that do quote in US dollars. Each AED band on this page names the provider or survey that published it and is dated to October 2026, so you can test the quote in front of you against the band rather than against a feeling.

whyPoints.title: Priced in blocks with an end date
whyPoints.description: Quotes name the hours, the target and the finish, and nothing renews by default. The most common way a tutoring budget runs away is a block that silently became a subscription in month three, which is a structural problem rather than a question of rate.

whyPoints.title: Marking inside the rate, done before the hour
whyPoints.description: A session spent reading the student's work for the first time is specialist time billed for silent reading. Work is photographed and sent ahead so it arrives marked, which makes the hour teaching and makes the total number of hours smaller.

whyPoints.title: The scarcity premium removed, not disguised
whyPoints.description: In a small emirate the dearest part of an in-home quote is that the pool is whoever can drive to your district by seven. Video delivery replaces that pool with a national one, which is why online specialist rates here sit below in-home rates instead of above them.

whyPoints.title: Nothing claimed about accreditation
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or endorsement from the International Baccalaureate, the Ministry of Education or any emirate education authority, and no page here says otherwise. A premium charged on an implied seal of approval is a premium on nothing.

whyPoints.title: A willingness to say spend nothing
whyPoints.description: If the diagnosis is that the gap is supervision, or that the timeline is too short for the deficit, you hear it at the free lesson rather than after a term of invoices. The week-six review is built to produce the same answer when the evidence supports it.

faqs.question: What does an hour with an IB home tutor in Ajman cost once travel is inside the number?
faqs.answer: Market figures researched in October 2026 put in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 an hour in a 2026 Dubai cost survey, with independent home tutors charging AED 200 to 500 once travel sits inside the rate. A qualified subject tutor working online sits lower, around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200 and TutorChase quoting AED 270 for specialist work. The gap between those bands is travel, a two-hour minimum booking convention and cancellation risk rather than teaching quality. These are market rates, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Why is the hourly rate the least useful number in a tutoring quote?
faqs.answer: Because the cheque is rate multiplied by hours, and providers publish only the first half. A tutor at AED 150 who needs thirty-two hours costs AED 4,800; one at AED 270 who needs twelve costs AED 3,240 and finishes sooner. The number of hours depends on whether the gap is technique or content, whether the work set between sessions gets done, and how early you start. All three are knowable in advance, and the first can be read from one marked script, which is why a diagnosis is worth more than a rate card.

faqs.question: Which months of the two Diploma years cost an Ajman family the most?
faqs.answer: The first term of the second year, by a clear margin. Internally assessed components close while new content is still arriving, mocks follow, and predicted grades are set, so demand for specialist hours concentrates across every family at once. Published monthly estimates for weekly one-hour specialist support in an examination year reach AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above, against AED 600 to 1,200 mid-tier. The quiet months are the first term of the first year and the weeks after the papers, when the right spend is nothing at all.

faqs.question: An Ajman provider quoted us a monthly figure — how do I work out what the hour costs?
faqs.answer: Only once you have converted it. A monthly figure hides both session length and session count, which is where comparisons go wrong. An AED 799 monthly online package seen in this market covers eight sessions, roughly AED 100 each. In-home monthly figures of AED 1,599 to 1,799 cover four two-hour visits, which works out at AED 200 to 225 per teaching hour. Same market, very different arithmetic. Ask how many sessions, how long each one is, whether marking is included, and whether unused sessions carry forward before you compare anything.

faqs.question: Should a tutoring quote in Ajman include VAT, and how do I ask about it?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider directly whether their own quoted figure is inclusive, and ask for it in writing. This page deliberately does not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as a matter of fact, because doing so properly requires a Federal Tax Authority citation that nobody in this market supplies, and an unsourced tax statement on a price page is worse than silence. What is reasonable to expect is that any provider can tell you plainly whether the number they quoted is what leaves your account, and can produce a tax registration number if they hold one.

faqs.question: When in the two Diploma years does money work hardest?
faqs.answer: In the summer between the two years, and almost nobody spends it there. A content gap in a Higher Level subject takes dozens of teaching hours, and a weekly hour during term gets consumed by whatever is urgent that week, so the gap never closes while new material keeps landing on top of it. A fortnight of daily hours in a quiet period works through a syllabus in sequence instead of triaging. Families who do this usually spend less in total than those buying a weekly hour for eighteen months, and start the final year without the deficit.

faqs.question: Do IB tutors charge more than IGCSE tutors, and is that justified?
faqs.answer: They generally do, and the published figures show it: Unitors lists IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Part of that is content depth, since Higher Level subjects reach further than an IGCSE syllabus. Part is scarcity, especially in a small emirate where the pool of people who can mark a Higher Level science investigation against its criteria is thin. And part is the core, because Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay need process coaching that an IGCSE tutor has never had to give. The premium is real rather than invented.

faqs.question: Who pays for the tutor's marking time between sessions?
faqs.answer: Somebody always does, and the question is whether it is named. A tutor who reads the student's work for the first time during the session has been paid a specialist rate for silent reading, which makes their rate look competitive and their hours high. A tutor who marks before the hour has absorbed that preparation into the rate, so the rate looks dearer and the hours are fewer. Over a term the second is usually cheaper and always more useful. Ask whether marking is included and whether it happens before the session or inside it.

faqs.question: What happens to the fee if we cancel a session during exam leave?
faqs.answer: Agree this before the second lesson, because the answer differs sharply by format. A cancelled online session costs a tutor one empty hour, so notice terms are usually looser. A cancelled visit costs them the hour plus the journey, which is why in-home cancellation terms are tighter and why a family that moves sessions around a school calendar pays for the flexibility. Settle three things in writing: the notice period, whether a missed session can be moved rather than forfeited, and what happens to a block during an extended school break.

faqs.question: Is a group class in Ajman worth the saving over one-to-one?
faqs.answer: It buys a different product rather than a cheaper version of the same one. At the AED 33 to 65 per-head band published by Tutopiya and EdFlik in October 2026, a group block delivers broad syllabus coverage and a cohort to pace against, which suits a student behind on content across a whole subject. What it cannot do is diagnose one student's specific loss pattern. If you do not yet know why the grade is stuck, buy the diagnosis first; coverage without diagnosis usually repeats material the student already had.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to our villa in Ajman, and what would that cost instead?
faqs.answer: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Everything for an Ajman family runs one-to-one over live video at times set in Gulf Standard Time. The in-home market genuinely exists and is priced on this page so you can weigh it fairly: AED 180 to 350 an hour in the 2026 survey, AED 200 to 500 for independents once travel is inside the rate, usually with a two-hour minimum. The one thing it buys that a screen cannot is an adult in the room, which matters when supervision is the real need.

faqs.question: How many hours should we budget for one Higher Level subject across both years?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether the gap is technique or content, and the diagnosis is cheap compared with guessing. Technique repairs — command terms, written method, closing an evaluative answer — are typically weeks of marked practice rather than months, so a short block plus maintenance can be enough. A missing third of a Higher Level syllabus is dozens of teaching hours and is best bought concentrated rather than weekly. Ask for the component-level marks behind the current prediction; they convert a vague worry about the subject into a countable list of movable marks.

faqs.question: Does a higher hourly rate mean a stronger IB tutor?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and the market gives you reasons to be careful in both directions. At the top end, BartyED publishes AED 650 for premium named tutoring, and a rate at that level is a claim about scarcity rather than a proof of effectiveness. At the bottom, AED 33 to 52 generally buys group teaching or a university student rather than specialist one-to-one. What correlates with movement is far more mundane: who marks the work, against what, how quickly it comes back, and whether the plan for the next three weeks is specific enough to be proved wrong.

faqs.question: What should an Ajman family refuse to pay for at any price?
faqs.answer: Finished coursework. One operator researched in this market advertises completed internal assessments at a four-figure sum, and buying that moves the entire risk onto your child: awarding bodies treat authorship breaches as malpractice, penalties can reach a whole entry rather than one component, and the student confirms the work is their own at submission. Also refuse to pay a premium for a claimed regulator endorsement. No platform in this market holds approval from the International Baccalaureate, the Ministry of Education or an emirate authority, and IB Gram claims none.

faqs.question: Can we try one lesson before committing to any monthly spend?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is how it is designed to work. The first lesson is a free diagnostic, no payment is taken beforehand, and there is no obligation to continue afterwards. What you receive from it is a written diagnosis: which loss patterns are present in the student's own marked work, which are weeks of work and which are a term, and what the first three weeks would target. If the honest answer is that the school's own support, a different subject or nothing at all is the better purchase, you will be told at that point rather than later.

ajman/ib-home-tutor.closingHeading: Get the diagnosis before you get the quote
ajman/ib-home-tutor.closingBody: The cheapest thing you can do today is find out what is actually wrong, because the hours required follow from the diagnosis and the cost follows from the hours. Send the subject, the level, the year group, a photograph of a recent marked piece and the two evening windows your household can genuinely hold. We will arrange a free diagnostic lesson with a specialist in that subject, and afterwards you will have a written note of the loss patterns, a realistic repair time for each, and a figure for a defined block with an end date on it. If the honest recommendation is to spend nothing this term, that is what you will hear.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-ajman-corniche.tutorsIntro: Tutors matched to Ajman Corniche families work backwards from the student's own school deadlines rather than from a generic scheme of work. The subjects below are the Diploma courses most often requested from this part of the emirate.

intro.heading: Count the two years backwards, then decide what to buy
paragraphs: The Diploma looks like a two-year course and behaves like a series of deadlines, most of which are set inside the school rather than by the board. An Internal Assessment draft date in November, a Theory of Knowledge essay upload, an Extended Essay supervision meeting, a mock window: none of these appears on an examination timetable and all of them determine the final grade. Families who plan from the exam date backwards see them coming. Families who plan forwards from today meet them one at a time, in a hurry.

Ajman Corniche is a dense strip of apartment towers along the seafront of the old city, which has two practical effects on a tuition plan. School runs here are among the shortest in the emirate, often fifteen minutes, so a session can start early. And a flat is a flat: a quiet room for a live video lesson has to be planned around siblings and a kitchen rather than assumed, which is a scheduling detail worth settling in week one rather than week five.

Delivery is stated plainly so nothing below reads the wrong way. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. The phrase in this page's address is what parents type into a search box, and it is answered honestly: what in-home tuition costs in this market, what the premium pays for, and why a Corniche family generally gets more teaching per dirham from a specialist on a screen than from whoever can reach the tower by six.

The second thing a calendar-led page owes a reader is restraint about dates. This project has not been able to verify a single IB exam or results date from the IB itself, because the board's own site returns an error to automated checking. So no IB date appears below. What does appear is the structure of the two years, the internal deadlines that drive it, and sourced Cambridge and Pearson dates where a Corniche household also has an IGCSE candidate.

The third is honesty about what time can do. An eight-week block before a series can change paper technique substantially, because technique responds quickly to timed practice marked against a real scheme. Eight weeks cannot build two years of missing content, and a provider that implies otherwise is selling hope. Knowing which of those two problems you have is the single most valuable output of a first session.

Everything factual is attributed. Market rates are given with the provider that published them and the month they were read, October 2026. Regulatory statements come from federal and emirate sources. Where a figure has no source, it is not here.
bullets: Roughly a fifth to a quarter of each Diploma subject grade is internally assessed, on internal deadlines.
The Extended Essay carries a 4,000-word ceiling and a research question that has to fit inside it.
UAE schools sit the May session; a November session exists as an alternative route.
No IB session or results date in this project is verified from the board, so none is published here.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-ajman-corniche.programmesIntro: Three IB stages reach Ajman Corniche households, and each has a different relationship with the calendar. Only one of them has external deadlines, which is exactly why the other two get left alone too long.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external papers and no fixed deadlines, which makes this the stage with the most forgiving calendar and the most neglected foundations. The work that matters is mechanics: number bonds, written method, reading stamina, explaining an answer in a sentence. None of it is urgent and all of it is expensive to repair later.
programmes.countryNote: The Corniche's short school runs make a 4:00pm primary slot easy to sustain, and the absence of deadlines means the plan can be genuinely light: two half-hour sessions a week, reviewed at the end of each term rather than each month.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8, with internal assessment dates set by the school across the year. The calendar here is real but invisible to most parents, because MYP assessment arrives as projects and tasks rather than as examinations. A strand left unaddressed costs a predictable number of marks every time it recurs.
programmes.countryNote: MYP Year 11 is where the Corniche households most often start looking, because the Diploma or IGCSE decision and the first serious internal assessments arrive in the same term. Starting a term earlier makes that decision an informed one rather than a reaction.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Every subject carries an internally assessed component on a school-set deadline, and those deadlines cluster in the autumn of the final year, which is also when university applications are written. The Diploma is a scheduling problem wearing the costume of an academic one.
programmes.countryNote: There is no large Diploma cohort in Ajman, so a Corniche student may be one of a handful in the emirate taking a particular Higher Level option, and the school's own deadline calendar is the only one they will be given. Getting a copy of it in September is the highest-value administrative act of the year.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-ajman-corniche.subjectsIntro: The Diploma subjects most often requested from Ajman Corniche, each with the calendar pressure point as well as the content one.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The non-calculator paper is where marks go for GDC-fluent students. Calendar pressure comes from the exploration, which needs a viable topic chosen a term before it is written, not a fortnight.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led. HL adds graph theory and matrices, usually taught late in the final year, so a student who is behind in autumn meets new content and revision simultaneously.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the losses. The internal assessment needs a method settled early enough to collect usable data, which is the deadline most often missed in this subject.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Unit errors, gradients read rather than calculated, explanations written as equations. Technique responds quickly to timed practice, which makes Physics a strong candidate for a short pre-series block.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Rewards sequence and precision: naming a process earns a mark, ordering its stages earns the rest. Statistics questions catch students who have never calculated a standard deviation by hand.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries, each needing a genuinely recent article, a labelled diagram and a respected word count. The articles have to be found as they appear rather than hunted for the week before the deadline.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the case stimulus is the whole paper. The Higher Level pre-released case study is published well ahead, which makes early structured reading worth more here than in any other subject.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 rewards argument about how a text works rather than summary. The Individual Oral needs a global issue chosen early and two extracts that genuinely support it, which is a term's decision, not a week's.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Both are bought late more often than any other component. The essay answers a prescribed title with one line of argument; the Extended Essay needs a question answerable inside 4,000 words, which is a narrowing problem.

sections.heading: The Diploma counted backwards
paragraphs: Start at the end and work back, because that is the only order in which the Diploma makes sense. The fixed point for a UAE student is the May examination window. Everything else is derived from it, and almost all of the derived dates are set inside the school rather than by the board, which is why they are invisible until they arrive.

Working backwards from the papers: the final weeks are timed practice and nothing else. Before that, a mock window roughly a term out, which exists to generate information rather than a grade. Before that, the cluster of internal coursework deadlines in the autumn of the final year, when the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and most subject Internal Assessments are due in draft or final form. Before that, the choice of topics and research questions, which should sit in the spring of the first year. Before all of it, the subject and level choices that determine what the two years will feel like.

Seen in that order, the implication for a tuition plan is clear and slightly counterintuitive: the most valuable intervention is early and cheap, and the least valuable is late and expensive. A term of weekly work in the first year, while content is being built, changes more than the same money spent in the final spring. The spring block has its own job, which is converting knowledge into marks, and it cannot do the first job as well.

Dates are deliberately absent from the table below. No IB session or results date in this project has been verified from the board itself, so the table gives the sequence and the span rather than a calendar a parent might act on. Take actual dates from your school's Diploma coordinator or from ibo.org.

sections.heading: What eight weeks can actually achieve
paragraphs: Families almost always arrive with eight weeks or fewer and want to know whether it is worth starting. The answer is yes, with a condition: eight weeks changes technique reliably and content only partially, so the first session has to establish which of the two is the actual problem.

Technique problems respond fast. A student who knows the chemistry and loses marks because they write a trend without a cause, or who runs out of time on the last two questions of a paper, can gain visibly in six to eight weeks of timed practice marked against a real scheme. The mechanism is not motivation, it is specificity: the student starts seeing the marker's wording rather than their own, and the error log stops being a list of topics and becomes a list of habits.

Content problems are different. A Higher Level student missing a term of calculus or a whole organic chemistry sequence needs the content taught, and teaching it properly takes the time it takes. Eight weeks will cover part of it, prioritised by what the paper weights most heavily, and that is a legitimate plan as long as it is described accurately rather than sold as a rescue.

The table maps the block against the term it sits in, because an eight-week block in October is a different purchase from the same block in March, even at the same price. The same tutor, the same hours and the same invoice produce materially different results depending only on which part of the two years they land in, which is the most under-used piece of leverage a family holds.

sections.heading: Internal deadlines are the real deadlines
paragraphs: The examination window is the date everyone knows and the least useful one to plan against, because by the time it arrives every decision has been made. The dates that decide a Diploma grade are set by the school, communicated once, and usually written down in a document the student has and the parent does not.

The reason they matter so much is weighting. Roughly a fifth to a quarter of each subject grade is internally assessed, which means the coursework in six subjects together accounts for a very large share of the total, and all of it is produced under internal deadlines in a single busy autumn. A student who submits five adequate internal assessments and one unfinished one has lost more marks than a weak paper would cost them.

What makes this tractable is that the deadlines are knowable in September. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the internal assessment calendar, the Extended Essay supervision schedule and the Theory of Knowledge essay dates for the whole year, and the plan writes itself: coursework blocks before each cluster, paper technique after they clear. A tutor working from that document plans around the student's real year rather than a generic one.

The table lists the components and what has to exist before each internal deadline. Mark allocations should be confirmed against the subject guide your school issues, because guides are revised and this page does not reproduce them. The pattern across all six subjects is the same: the work that has to be finished first is almost never the writing, it is the decision that makes the writing possible.

sections.heading: Why this page publishes no IB exam date
paragraphs: It would be easy to put a date here. Secondary sources converge, other tutoring pages quote them confidently, and a parent reading a page with a date on it feels better served than one reading a page without.

The problem is verification. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, which means no IB exam or results date in this project has been confirmed from the board itself. A date taken from a secondary source and published to thousands of pages becomes thousands of liabilities the moment it is wrong or revised, and the cost of that falls on a family planning a revision schedule, booking travel, or deciding whether to enter a resit.

This project has already seen the consequence of getting a calendar wrong in this market. An earlier version of its research offered the Cambridge February and March key dates as the worked example, and pages went out quoting a February-March exam window and a late-November entry deadline to UAE parents. Cambridge offers the February and March series to candidates in India; a UAE centre enters June and November. A date a parent acts on has to be right for their country, and a page that cannot verify one should say so.

So the position here is: UAE Diploma schools sit the May session, a November session exists as an alternative route, and every specific date should come from your school's Diploma coordinator or from ibo.org directly. For a Corniche household with an IGCSE candidate as well, the Cambridge and Pearson positions below are sourced from the boards' own pages and can be used with their framing.

sections.heading: The mock window, and what to do with the marked paper
paragraphs: Mocks exist to produce information, and most of that information is thrown away. The grade is read, the household reacts to it, and the papers go into a bag. The marks themselves are nearly worthless as a planning input; the pattern of where they were lost is the most valuable document a student will own that year.

A useful reading of a marked paper answers four questions. Which marks were lost to content the student has never securely learned. Which were lost to method, where the knowledge was present and the working did not earn it. Which were lost to the command term, where the student answered a different question from the one asked. And which were lost to time, in the questions attempted hastily or not at all. Those four causes need four different responses, and only the first one needs teaching.

That reading takes about an hour per paper and should happen within a fortnight, while the student still remembers what they were thinking. In practice it rarely happens at all, which is why a mock-review session is one of the highest-value single purchases available in this market: one hour that redirects the next eight weeks.

The output should be written down. An error log grouped by cause rather than by topic is what turns a disappointing mock into a plan, and it is also the document that tells a family in the spring whether the plan is working, because the same causes either keep recurring or stop.
bullets: Read the marked paper by cause, not by topic.
Content, method, command term, timing: four causes, four different responses.
Do it within a fortnight, while the student remembers their thinking.
Write the error log down; it is the measure of whether the plan is working.

sections.heading: Results week, enquiries and the second window
paragraphs: The calendar does not stop at the papers, and the fortnight after results is where families make the most consequential decisions with the least information. There are three distinct options and they have different deadlines, so knowing which applies matters more than reacting quickly.

The first is an enquiry upon results, where a school asks the board to review a mark. That is a school process with its own deadline and its own criteria, and the right question for the Diploma coordinator is whether the component profile makes a review plausible, not whether the overall grade was disappointing. The second is a resit in the next available session. The third is to accept the result and move on, which is frequently the right answer and is rarely presented as one.

For the IGCSE side of a Corniche household the sourced dates make this concrete. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. So a November entry means waiting until January, which matters if a post-16 place depends on the grade. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026.

For the IB, the same restraint applies as above: UAE schools sit the May session, a November session exists, and dates come from the coordinator rather than from here. The table below gives the decision sequence, which is stable even when the dates are not.

sections.heading: Ramadan, UAE term dates and the Corniche evening
paragraphs: Two calendar features of this market are absent from almost every tutoring page and both reshape a plan. The first is Ramadan. School hours shorten, the useful study window moves to after Iftar, and a month of a two-year course passes in a different rhythm from the rest of it. The second is that UAE term dates and the Diploma's internal deadline cluster do not always sit comfortably together, so a coursework deadline can land immediately after a break during which nothing was done.

The practical answer to Ramadan is to decide before it begins rather than during it. Sessions move to post-Iftar timing, or shorten and keep their frequency, and the choice should be made with the student. An online booking absorbs that change easily; an in-home visit after Iftar is a much harder thing to arrange on the Corniche, where parking and tower access add friction to an already late evening. A month that is quietly abandoned is where more Diploma momentum is lost than in any single bad mock.

Prayer times shift through the year, which has a smaller but recurring effect. A slot that worked in September will collide with Maghrib by November unless it was set to end before the prayer rather than to run up against it. Fifteen minutes of planning in week one removes a term of rescheduling.

The last Corniche-specific point is the room. These are apartments, often with siblings and a shared living space, and a live video lesson needs forty-five uninterrupted minutes somewhere. Families who settle that in week one, by agreeing which room and what the rest of the household does during the session, lose far fewer sessions than those who improvise it weekly.
bullets: Decide the Ramadan arrangement before the month starts, with the student.
Set the session to end before Maghrib, not against it.
Check what sits immediately after each school break; deadlines cluster there.
Agree the room and the household's rules for it in week one.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when a deadline is close
paragraphs: Calendar pressure is what turns a legitimate coursework request into an illegitimate one. Nobody sets out to buy a finished Internal Assessment; they run out of time, a provider offers a solution, and the boundary moves. Stating the boundary in advance is worth more than restating it afterwards.

What a tutor may do: teach the subject content, explain each assessment criterion and what its descriptors demand, help narrow a research question so it fits the word limit, review a method for feasibility and ethics, and give written feedback on a draft the student has already written. What a tutor must never do: write, redraft or complete an Internal Assessment, an exploration, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or any assessed coursework, or supply text for a student to paste in. A page found during research for this project sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, and the consequence of buying one falls on the student rather than on the seller.

There is a materials boundary too. No tutor should reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads; the official source should be referenced and linked instead. That is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure.

And a boundary on claims. No tutor can promise a grade, because boundaries are set after the series on the basis of that series' papers, and any provider offering a promised score or money back against a result is either misunderstanding that or hoping the question is not asked. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none.

process.title: Send the school's deadline calendar
process.description: The internal assessment dates, the Extended Essay supervision schedule and the Theory of Knowledge essay deadlines for the whole year. Ask the Diploma coordinator in September. That single document is what lets a plan be built backwards instead of reactively.

process.title: Take the free diagnostic session
process.description: The first session is a diagnosis, with no card details taken. Its job is to establish whether the problem is content, method, command-term reading or timing, because those four need different responses and only one of them needs teaching. You keep the written summary either way.

process.title: Place the block where it earns most
process.description: A coursework block before the autumn deadline cluster, paper technique after it clears, and the heavy weeks in the final eight to twelve before the papers. Same money, different term, materially different result.

process.title: Fix the slot and the room
process.description: Sessions are set on Gulf Standard Time to end before Maghrib rather than against it, and because lessons run online no part of the slot is travel. On the Corniche the second half of this matters: agree which room and what the household does during the session in week one.

process.title: Review against the error log, not the mood
process.description: Progress is measured by whether the same causes keep recurring in marked work. That makes the review conversation factual rather than anxious, and it is what tells a family when weekly work can step down to fortnightly or stop.

whyPoints.title: Planned backwards, not forwards
whyPoints.description: The plan starts from the exam window and the school's own internal deadlines rather than from the week you enquired. That is the difference between coursework blocks that sit before a deadline cluster and ones that sit on top of it.

whyPoints.title: No unverified dates
whyPoints.description: No IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the board itself, so none is published. An earlier version of this project's research quoted the Cambridge February and March dates, which apply to India rather than the UAE. That mistake is not repeated here.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what eight weeks does
whyPoints.description: Technique responds quickly to timed practice marked against a real scheme. Missing content takes the time it takes. A first session establishes which of those you have, and the plan is described accurately rather than sold as a rescue.

whyPoints.title: The mock paper actually read
whyPoints.description: A marked paper read by cause rather than by topic redirects the next eight weeks for the price of one session. In this market it is the single highest-value hour available and almost nobody offers it as a product.

whyPoints.title: Ramadan and Maghrib built in
whyPoints.description: Sessions are set to end before the prayer and moved to post-Iftar timing for Ramadan rather than being quietly dropped for a month. A quietly abandoned month costs more Diploma momentum than a bad mock does.

whyPoints.title: Stated limits on coursework and claims
whyPoints.description: Teaching, criterion explanation and written feedback on the student's own draft: yes. Producing any part of an assessment: never, at any price or any deadline. No promised grades, and no claim of approval from any regulator or board.

faqs.question: We have eight weeks before the papers. Is it too late to start in Ajman Corniche?
faqs.answer: No, with a condition. Eight weeks changes technique reliably and content only partially, so the first session has to establish which is the real problem. A student who knows the material and loses marks on command terms, working or pacing can gain visibly in that time through timed practice marked against a real scheme. A student missing a whole content sequence will get part of it, prioritised by what the paper weights most, which is a legitimate plan when it is described accurately rather than sold as a rescue.

faqs.question: Which Diploma deadlines should I ask the school about in September?
faqs.answer: Three documents cover almost everything: the internal assessment calendar for all six subjects, the Extended Essay supervision schedule, and the Theory of Knowledge essay dates. Ask the Diploma coordinator for all of them at the start of the year. Roughly a fifth to a quarter of each subject grade is internally assessed and those deadlines cluster in one busy autumn, so having them in writing is what allows coursework blocks to sit before the cluster rather than on top of it.

faqs.question: Why does this page not give an IB exam date?
faqs.answer: Because none has been verified. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB exam or results date in this project is confirmed from the board, and publishing an unverified date that a family plans a revision schedule around would be worse than publishing none. What is safe to say is that UAE schools sit the May session and that a November session exists as an alternative route. Take every specific date from your school's Diploma coordinator or from ibo.org directly.

faqs.question: What should we actually do with a disappointing mock paper?
faqs.answer: Read it by cause rather than by topic, within a fortnight, while the student still remembers their thinking. Four questions: which marks were lost to content never securely learned, which to method where the knowledge was there and the working did not earn it, which to the command term where a different question was answered, and which to time. Those four causes need four different responses and only the first needs teaching. Write the result down as an error log.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest time in the Diploma to buy tuition?
faqs.answer: The autumn of the first year, and almost nobody does it then. Content is being built, the student has capacity, there are no coursework deadlines competing for attention, and rates in this market have not firmed up the way they do as a series approaches. The same money spent in the final spring has a narrower job: converting knowledge already present into marks. Both jobs are real, but only one of them can be done late.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change a Diploma plan on the Corniche?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten and the useful study window moves to after Iftar, so a month of a two-year course runs on a different rhythm. Decide the arrangement before the month begins: move sessions to post-Iftar timing, or shorten them and keep the frequency. An online booking absorbs that easily, whereas an in-home visit after Iftar adds parking and tower access to an already late evening. A quietly abandoned month costs more momentum than a single bad mock.

faqs.question: My child's Extended Essay is at 5,000 words. What now?
faqs.answer: The problem is almost always the research question rather than the writing. A question too broad to answer inside 4,000 words produces an essay that cannot be cut without losing the argument, so the work is narrowing the question and then rebuilding the structure around the narrower version. A tutor may help with that, explain what each named criterion demands, and give written feedback on the student's drafts. A tutor must never rewrite or complete the essay.

faqs.question: Should we enter an enquiry upon results or a resit?
faqs.answer: Ask for the component breakdown before deciding, because the two options suit different shortfalls. A grade that missed narrowly on one component may support an enquiry upon results, which is a school process with its own deadline and criteria; ask the coordinator whether the profile makes a review plausible rather than whether the grade was disappointing. A broad shortfall across every component is a resit question, and a short block can only close it if the diagnosis says the cause is technique.

faqs.question: Can a session start before 5pm for a family on Ajman Corniche?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the few parts of the emirate where it is genuinely easy. School runs from the Corniche are among the shortest in Ajman, often around fifteen minutes, so a 4:00pm start works after food and a short break. Because lessons run online there is no travel to add at either end. The real constraint here is not time but space: a flat needs an agreed quiet room for forty-five uninterrupted minutes.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should a Grade 12 student have?
faqs.answer: It should change through the year rather than being set once. Through the autumn, when coursework deadlines cluster, one weekly session per subject plus a coursework block is usually right, because adding paper technique at the same time produces two half-done jobs. In the final eight to twelve weeks, two or three sessions a week in the subjects that need it earns its cost, since timed practice marked against a real scheme compounds in a way content teaching does not.

faqs.question: Does the IB November session work as a resit route for a UAE student?
faqs.answer: A November session exists as an alternative to the May session, and it is used by students who need a second attempt or whose school calendar suits it. What this page will not do is publish the dates, because none has been verified from the board. The decision itself should rest on the component breakdown and on whether the receiving institution can wait for the later results. Ask your Diploma coordinator about entry deadlines and about how the timing fits any offer held.

faqs.question: What if my child is the only one in the emirate taking their Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: It happens here, because Ajman's Diploma cohort is small. The practical effect is that the subject teacher may be the only person locally who knows the course, so there is no second opinion available and no peer group to calibrate against. That is the strongest argument for an online specialist: not convenience, but access to somebody who has taught the same papers to other cohorts and can say whether a piece of work is where it should be.

faqs.question: Do we need to worry about Cambridge zones if we also have an IGCSE candidate?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth passing on because almost no tuition page does. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask the exams officer which zone your centre sits in, and revise from the centre's own timetable rather than one found online.

faqs.question: Is an in-home tutor on the Corniche worth the premium?
faqs.answer: It buys physical presence, which genuinely matters for a younger or easily distracted student, and the published premium is real: a qualified subject tutor working online is advertised at AED 150 to 300 an hour, while in-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent tutors, read October 2026. For Diploma paper work, where most of a session is a question, a mark scheme and a shared screen, the premium buys very little.

faqs.question: How do we tell whether the tuition is working before the next report?
faqs.answer: By watching the error log rather than the mood. If the same causes keep appearing in marked work, the plan has not landed. If the recurring causes change, it has. That makes the review factual and also tells you when to spend less: once a diagnosed gap closes, weekly work should move to fortnightly or stop until the next pressure point. A provider that never proposes stepping down is managing revenue rather than marks.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-ajman-corniche.closingHeading: Send the deadline calendar, and we will plan backwards
ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-ajman-corniche.closingBody: If your child is in the Diploma and living on Ajman Corniche, the most useful thing you can send is not a subject but a document: the school's internal assessment calendar, the Extended Essay supervision schedule and the Theory of Knowledge dates. With those in hand the plan writes itself, with coursework blocks before each deadline cluster and paper technique after they clear. The first session is a free diagnosis on the real paper, with no card details taken, and the written summary is yours either way. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, set to end before Maghrib.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-helio.tutorsIntro: Tutors matched to Al Helio students are subject specialists who talk in papers and criteria rather than in reassurance: which component the marks are being lost in, which command term is being misread, and what the next twenty questions should be.

intro.heading: The problem is almost always a specific component
paragraphs: A Diploma grade is not a single number produced by general ability. It is the sum of two or three externally marked papers and one internally assessed component, each with its own structure, its own weighting and its own characteristic way of losing marks. When a student is stuck at a 4 or a 5, the useful question is never whether they are working hard enough. It is which component is bleeding, and why.

That question has a small number of answers and they recur. A Mathematics student who is fluent with a graphical calculator and cannot factorise by hand loses on Paper 1. A Chemistry student who states a trend without naming the cause loses on the data questions. A Biology student who names a process without ordering its stages loses the back half of every long answer. An Economics student who draws a diagram without labelling axes, shift and new equilibrium loses marks they had already earned conceptually. None of those is a knowledge gap in the ordinary sense, and none responds to more revision.

Al Helio is a residential district inland in Ajman, with villa housing across Al Helio 1 and 2 and a reasonable drive to the emirate's school belt. What that means practically is that the Diploma cohort around a student here is small, and so is the number of people locally who have taught a particular Higher Level option. Several are contractually unable to tutor students at their own school in any case. The nearest available teacher and the right teacher are usually two different people.

Delivery is stated plainly. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For subject work this is not a compromise: most of a useful Diploma session is a question, a mark scheme and a pen, annotated live on a shared screen and kept afterwards, which is closer to how examiners work than a kitchen table is.

Two cautions about what follows. Weightings and criterion allocations are given because they are what makes the page useful, but IB subject guides are revised and this page does not reproduce them: confirm every figure against the guide your school issues. And no IB exam or results date appears here, because the IB's own site returns an error to automated checking and nothing in this project has been verified from the board itself.

What is not here is any claim about outcomes. No tutor can promise a grade, because boundaries are set after a series on the basis of that series' papers. What a specialist changes is the precision of a student's practice, which is a smaller claim and a verifiable one.
bullets: Mathematics at Higher Level sits three papers; Standard Level sits two, plus the exploration in both.
The internal assessment carries 20 per cent of a Diploma science grade on the current syllabus structure.
The Mathematics exploration is marked across five criteria totalling 20 marks.
Command terms are not stylistic: state, describe, explain and evaluate ask for different amounts of writing.
Confirm every weighting and criterion allocation against your school's own subject guide.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-helio.programmesIntro: Al Helio households reach this page from three stages, but only one of them has external papers. The content work described below is mostly Diploma work, with the earlier stages included because that is where the technique is either built or missed.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8, with strands inside each criterion. The marks reward process: a pattern identified, a justification given, a reflection written. Students who have been rewarded for correct answers lose marks for not showing the reasoning, and the repair is reading the strand wording and writing to it deliberately.
programmes.countryNote: MYP is where Diploma command-term habits are either formed or not. An Al Helio student who learns in Year 9 that 'explain' requires a mechanism and 'state' does not arrives in Grade 11 with an advantage that no amount of Diploma revision substitutes for.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, with each subject assessed through external papers plus an internally assessed component. The component structures differ by subject group, which is why a general study-skills approach helps so little: the thing that moves a Chemistry grade is not the thing that moves an English A grade.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman's Diploma cohort is small, so a student here may be one of very few in the emirate on a particular Higher Level option. That makes an external subject specialist less of a luxury than it would be in Dubai, where a school might have three teachers on the same course.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: The core components are assessed against named criteria and sit outside any subject's teaching time, which is why they are the most frequently neglected part of the Diploma. The Extended Essay has a 4,000-word ceiling and a research question that has to be answerable inside it; the Theory of Knowledge essay responds to a prescribed title and rewards a single line of argument.
programmes.countryNote: Supervision of these is provided by the school, and a tutor's role is narrower: explaining what each criterion demands, helping narrow a question, and giving written feedback on drafts the student has written. Nothing is produced on the student's behalf.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-helio.subjectsIntro: Each entry below names the component where marks are usually lost and what the paper actually rewards. Weightings should be confirmed against the subject guide your school issues.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level sits three papers, Standard Level two, plus the exploration in both. Paper 1 is taken without a calculator, which is where GDC-fluent students lose heavily on surds, factorising and manipulation. HL adds proof by induction, complex numbers and substantially harder calculus.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led, with the calculator central rather than incidental. Marks go on reporting a regression output without interpreting it in context, and on rounding mid-calculation. HL adds graph theory and matrices, usually taught late in Grade 12.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the losses. On data questions students name a trend and stop, where the mark requires the cause. HL extends into transition metals and spectroscopic identification, which rewards pattern recognition over memorised lists.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Unit errors, gradients read off a graph rather than calculated, and explanation questions answered with an equation instead of a sentence. HL content arrives alongside coursework deadlines, so a student already behind meets new material and revision at the same time.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Naming a process earns a mark; ordering its stages earns the rest, and most lost marks sit in that second half. Statistics questions catch students who have never calculated a standard deviation by hand, which is a one-session repair once somebody names it.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram marks are the most reliably available and the most reliably dropped: axes unlabelled, the shift not shown, the new equilibrium not marked. HL adds quantitative questions. The commentaries need recent articles collected as they appear.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A tool described scores little; a tool applied to the case stimulus scores well. HL adds the pre-released case study, published far enough ahead that structured early reading is worth more here than in any other subject on the timetable.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is a guided analysis and is where unprepared students summarise instead of arguing about how the text works. The Individual Oral needs a global issue chosen early and two extracts that genuinely support it. HL adds the essay, which needs an argument rather than a tour.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic A
subjects.description: Language B assesses reading comprehension, writing to a specified text type and a spoken component. Home speakers lose marks on register and text-type convention rather than vocabulary. Arabic A sits alongside the Ministry's own requirements for Arab students.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The essay responds to a prescribed title and is marked against named criteria. Breadth is the standard failure: four knowledge claims gestured at rather than one argument developed, with examples that illustrate nothing in particular.

sections.heading: Mathematics: what each paper actually asks for
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject where the structure itself explains most of the lost marks, and where families are most likely to have been given a diagnosis that is simply wrong. A student described as weak at maths is very often a student who is strong at calculator-supported work and has never been required to manipulate algebra without one.

The structure makes that visible. At Higher Level a student sits three papers; at Standard Level two, with the exploration in both cases. Paper 1 is taken without a calculator. Everything a student has learned to outsource to a graphical calculator has to be done by hand on that paper: surds, factorising a cubic, solving simultaneous equations, differentiating from first principles. A student can lose a grade on Paper 1 while performing perfectly adequately everywhere else.

The choice of route matters as much as the level. Analysis and Approaches rewards algebraic fluency and formal proof; Applications and Interpretation rewards modelling, statistics and interpretation of output, with the calculator central rather than incidental. Students pushed into Analysis and Approaches because it sounds more rigorous, when their strength is interpretation, lose marks for two years on a choice made in an afternoon.

The exploration is the component most often mishandled, because it is marked on five criteria totalling 20 marks and the largest single allocation goes to the use of mathematics. A beautifully written piece about a topic with no mathematical development in it cannot reach the upper bands, and no amount of editing changes that. The viability of the topic is the whole decision, and it belongs a term before the writing.

sections.heading: Where marks actually go in the Diploma sciences
paragraphs: Science papers do not mostly test whether a student knows the content. They test whether a student can produce the specific thing the mark scheme is looking for, in the number of words the question allows, using the vocabulary the syllabus uses. A great deal of apparently inexplicable underperformance is a student who knows the answer and writes a different, correct, unrewarded thing.

Three patterns account for most of it. The first is stating a trend without a cause: the graph goes up, which earns nothing, where the mark required the reason it goes up. The second is answering the topic rather than the command term: an 'explain' question answered with a description, which is a complete answer to a question nobody asked. The third is evaluation written as a list of mistakes rather than as a ranked argument about which source of error mattered most, which is the single most common weakness in internal assessments across all three sciences.

The internal assessment is worth taking seriously on arithmetic grounds alone: on the current structure it carries 20 per cent of the grade, and unlike a paper it can be worked on calmly over weeks. Students who leave the method decision late cannot collect usable data, and no amount of writing rescues a dataset that does not support an analysis.

sections.heading: Command terms decide the mark
paragraphs: This is the cheapest improvement available in the Diploma and almost nobody buys it, because it does not look like teaching. Every question in every subject opens with a command term that specifies what kind of answer earns marks, and the terms are defined by the board rather than used loosely. A student who treats them as synonyms is writing at random.

The practical consequence is that length and type of answer are prescribed. State wants a fact with no reasoning. Describe wants features, in sequence, without explanation. Explain wants a mechanism or a cause. Compare wants both things in the same sentence rather than two separate paragraphs. Evaluate wants a judgement supported by both sides. Discuss wants a balanced review. A student who writes a paragraph for a state question wastes time they will need later; a student who writes a sentence for an explain question loses marks they knew.

Teaching it is quick and the gains show within a few weeks. The method is to take questions the student has already answered, cover the answers, and have them identify what the command term demanded and whether they delivered it. The realisation is usually immediate and slightly painful, which is why it sticks.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level, compared properly
paragraphs: Students and parents in Ajman often make this decision with one sentence of information: Higher Level is harder and looks better. Both halves of that are true and neither is sufficient, because what actually changes between the levels is the content, the number of papers and the depth of reasoning expected, and those changes affect different students very differently.

The content extension is the obvious difference and the least decisive one. The more consequential difference is reasoning depth: Higher Level papers ask more questions where the route to the answer is not given, and reward students who build an approach rather than recognise a method. A student who is excellent at executing known procedures and uncomfortable with unfamiliar problems often performs better at Standard Level in a subject they genuinely enjoy than at Higher Level in the same subject.

The third factor is capacity. Three Higher Levels plus the core is a fixed amount of time, and a student taking a fourth subject at Higher Level because it was available usually pays for it in the coursework term. The honest question is not whether a student could cope with the content, but what the marginal Higher Level costs the other five subjects.

Where a Higher Level is genuinely needed for a university route, it needs to be chosen and then supported properly from the first term rather than defended in the last one. The table sets out the dimensions that differ, so the choice can be made against something.

sections.heading: The internal assessment, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The internal assessment is the only part of the Diploma a student can work on calmly, which makes it the most wasted opportunity in the course. It is marked against named criteria with fixed allocations, and a student who reads those criteria before starting is in a different position from one who writes first and checks afterwards.

The pattern across subjects is the same even though the criteria differ. There is a criterion that rewards the quality of the central decision, whether that is the research question, the method or the mathematical topic. There is one that rewards the technical work itself. There is one that rewards communication and structure. And there is one that rewards reflection or evaluation, which is reliably the weakest section in student work because it is written last and treated as a formality.

The highest-value intervention is therefore early and narrow: checking that the central decision will support the technical criterion. A Mathematics exploration on a topic with no mathematics to develop, a science investigation whose method will not generate analysable data, an Economics commentary built on an article too old or too thin: each of those caps the grade before a word is written, and each is visible in a single session.

sections.heading: Past-paper work done properly
paragraphs: Past papers are the most available resource in the Diploma and the most poorly used. The standard pattern is to attempt a paper, check the answers, feel either relieved or discouraged, and move on. That produces almost no learning, because the answer tells a student what they should have written and not why they wrote something else.

The version that works has four steps and takes longer than the paper itself. Attempt a question group under time, with no notes. Mark it against the published scheme rather than an answer key, reading the scheme's wording closely, because the wording is the specification. Classify every lost mark by cause: content not known, method not shown, command term misread, or time. Then, and only then, choose the next twenty questions on the basis of the classification rather than on the basis of the next topic in the book.

That classification is the whole output. An error log grouped by cause is the single most useful document a Diploma student can own, because it converts a vague sense of weakness into four short lists, only one of which requires teaching. Students are routinely surprised to discover that the majority of their lost marks are method and command term rather than content, which changes what the next eight weeks should contain.

One rule about materials, for completeness. No tutor should supply IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; the official source should be referenced and linked instead, and work should be done against material the student legitimately holds through their school. Reproducing assessment material is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure.
