sections.heading: Group 3, languages and the components nobody drills
paragraphs: Science and mathematics attract most of the tuition in this market, which leaves a set of components that are reliably underprepared and reliably fixable. Economics, Business Management, English A and the languages all contain specific mark-earning techniques that are rarely taught explicitly and respond quickly when they are.

In Economics the diagram is the clearest example. Diagram marks are among the most available on the paper and among the most commonly dropped, because students draw a shape they recognise without labelling the axes, showing the shift or marking the new equilibrium. Fixing that is a mechanical exercise over a few sessions, and it applies across every topic in the course. The same is true of data response, where the mark requires the figure from the extract to be quoted rather than paraphrased.

In Business Management the equivalent is application. A tool reproduced from memory earns almost nothing; the same tool built from the case stimulus earns well. Students who know the syllabus perfectly and score in the middle bands are almost always failing to use the business in front of them, and that habit changes within a handful of timed case questions.

In English A and the languages the failure is structural rather than technical. Paper 1 rewards an argument about how a text constructs meaning, and students write summaries; the Individual Oral rewards a global issue that the chosen extracts genuinely support, and students choose extracts they like. In Arabic B, home speakers lose marks on register and text-type convention rather than on vocabulary, which is a distinction no amount of general fluency work addresses.
bullets: Economics: label the axes, show the shift, mark the new equilibrium, quote the figure.
Business Management: use the business in the stimulus, not the theory in the textbook.
English A Paper 1: argue about how the text works, do not summarise what it says.
Arabic B: register and text-type convention, not vocabulary, is where home speakers lose.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with assessed work, and who may tutor at all
paragraphs: A page this far into coursework detail owes a clear boundary. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain each assessment criterion and what its descriptors demand, help narrow a research question or test whether a topic has enough mathematics in it, review a method for feasibility and ethics, and give written feedback on a draft the student has already written.

A tutor must never write, redraft or complete an Internal Assessment, a Mathematics exploration, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or any assessed coursework, and must not supply text, data or diagrams for a student to submit. A page found during research for this project sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. That is an academic integrity breach and an IB malpractice trigger, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on whoever sold it.

The materials rule applies alongside it. No tutor should reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads. Reference and link the official source instead, which is why this page carries no attachments and asks readers to confirm every weighting against their own school's guide.

Finally, who may teach. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no tutor can promise a grade.

process.title: Name the component, not the subject
process.description: The useful enquiry says which paper or which internal component the marks are going on, and brings a recent marked piece of work. 'Chemistry Paper 2 extended responses' is a request that can be answered properly; 'Chemistry' is a request that takes a session to narrow.

process.title: Take the free diagnostic session
process.description: The first session is a diagnosis with no card details taken. The tutor works through real paper questions and classifies lost marks into content, method, command term and time, then writes it up. Most students are surprised how little of the loss is content, which changes the plan.

process.title: Check the internal assessment decision early
process.description: Before any writing, the central decision is tested: does the exploration topic contain mathematics to develop, will the method generate analysable data, does the article support real analysis. That single check protects the component that carries roughly a fifth of the grade.

process.title: Work in question groups, marked to the scheme
process.description: Sessions are built on timed question groups marked against the published scheme in the same sitting, with the student reading the marker's wording. Full papers come at the weekend, because pacing across a complete paper is itself part of what is assessed.

process.title: Review against the error log
process.description: Progress is measured by whether the recurring causes change, not by how a session felt. That makes the review factual, and it is what tells a family when weekly work can step down to fortnightly or stop until the next pressure point.

whyPoints.title: Mark schemes read as specifications

whyPoints.description: The decision that caps the grade is the topic, the method or the article, and it is visible in a single session. Checking it early protects roughly a fifth of a subject grade; checking it late protects nothing.

faqs.question: My child is stuck at a 5 in Chemistry. Where is the mark actually going?
faqs.answer: Usually in two places. On the data-based questions, where a trend is stated and the cause is not, so the mark the scheme wanted is never offered. And on Paper 2 extended responses, where the command term is misread and a description is given for an explain question, which is a complete answer to a question nobody asked. Both are diagnosable in one session with a recent marked paper, and both respond faster than content teaching does because the knowledge is already there.

faqs.question: Why does my child do well in class and badly on Maths Paper 1?
faqs.answer: Because Paper 1 is taken without a calculator and classwork rarely is. Everything a student has learned to outsource to a graphical calculator has to be done by hand on that paper: surds, factorising, solving simultaneous equations, differentiating from first principles. A student can lose a grade on Paper 1 while performing adequately on Paper 2 and the exploration. The repair is timed non-calculator drilling rather than more theory, and it shows within a few weeks.

faqs.question: For an Al Helio student, is AA or AI the better Maths route?
faqs.answer: It depends on what they are good at rather than on which sounds more rigorous. Analysis and Approaches rewards algebraic fluency and formal proof, with Higher Level adding proof by induction, complex numbers and considerably harder calculus. Applications and Interpretation rewards modelling, statistics and interpretation of calculator output, with Higher Level adding graph theory and matrices. Check the specific university courses being considered, because some require one route, and then choose for fit rather than reputation.

faqs.question: How much does the internal assessment actually count in a DP science?
faqs.answer: On the current structure it carries 20 per cent of the subject grade, which is why it deserves more calm attention than it usually gets. Unlike a paper it can be worked on over weeks, and unlike a paper the decision that caps the grade is taken at the start: whether the method will generate data that can actually be analysed. Confirm the weighting against the subject guide your school issues, because guides are revised and this page does not reproduce them.

faqs.question: What is the single cheapest improvement available in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Command-term work, and almost nobody buys it because it does not look like teaching. Every question opens with a term that specifies what kind of answer earns marks, and the terms are defined by the board rather than used loosely. State wants a fact; describe wants features in order; explain wants a mechanism; evaluate wants a judgement from both sides. The method is to take answers the student has already written and ask whether they delivered what the term demanded.

faqs.question: How should an Al Helio student use past papers?
faqs.answer: Four steps, and the marking takes longer than the paper. Attempt a question group under time with no notes. Mark it against the published scheme rather than an answer key, reading the wording closely, because the wording is the specification. Classify every lost mark by cause: content, method, command term or time. Then choose the next twenty questions from that classification rather than from the next topic in the book. The classification is the output; the score is not.

faqs.question: My child's Mathematics exploration has no maths in it. Can that be fixed?
faqs.answer: Only by changing the topic, and the sooner the better. The exploration is marked across five criteria totalling 20 marks, with use of mathematics carrying the largest single allocation, so a well-written piece about a topic with nothing to develop mathematically cannot reach the upper bands no matter how it is polished. A tutor may test a topic's viability and give feedback on the student's drafts, but the student chooses, writes and develops every part of it themselves.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level worth it if the content is manageable?
faqs.answer: Content is the least decisive difference. What changes most at Higher Level is reasoning demand: more questions where the route to the answer is not given, rewarding students who build an approach rather than recognise a method. The second factor is capacity, because three Higher Levels plus the core is a fixed amount of time and a fourth usually costs the other five subjects in the coursework term. Check whether a university route actually requires it before deciding.

faqs.question: Why do evaluation sections score so poorly in science work?
faqs.answer: Because they are written last and treated as a formality, and because students write a list of mistakes instead of an argument. The marks are available for ranking: which source of error mattered most, why, and what it did to the conclusion. A list of five limitations with no judgement between them earns far less than two limitations argued properly. Rewriting an existing evaluation as a ranked claim with reasons is a single-session exercise and it transfers to every subsequent piece.

faqs.question: What is going wrong if Economics answers feel right but score mid-band?
faqs.answer: Almost always the diagram and the extract. Diagram marks are among the most available on the paper and among the most commonly dropped, because students draw a recognisable shape without labelling the axes, showing the shift or marking the new equilibrium. On data response, the mark usually requires the figure from the extract to be quoted rather than paraphrased. Both are mechanical fixes over a few sessions and both apply across every topic in the course.

faqs.question: Can online sessions really work for a subject like Physics?
faqs.answer: For paper work, yes, and arguably better than a kitchen table. Most of a useful session is a question, a mark scheme and a pen, annotated live on a shared screen and kept afterwards, which is close to how examiners actually work. The laboratory component happens at school with school equipment regardless of who tutors, and a tutor's contribution there is the planning, the tabulation, the uncertainty treatment and the evaluation, all of which are written skills.

faqs.question: How many sessions does it take to change a paper technique?
faqs.answer: Technique usually moves inside six to eight weeks of timed practice marked against a real scheme, because the student starts reading the marker's wording rather than their own. Content is different: a missing topic sequence takes the time it takes, and an honest plan says which part of it will be covered and in what order, prioritised by paper weighting. The first session's job is to establish which of the two problems you actually have.

faqs.question: Is there a Higher Level specialist for my subject in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Often not, and it is better to hear that early. The emirate's Diploma cohort is small, the number of local teachers on a given Higher Level option is smaller, and some of the best-placed ones are barred from tutoring students at their own school. For Higher Level sciences and Economics the practical answer for an Al Helio family is to plan on an online specialist from the start rather than spending a term searching for somebody who is not there.

faqs.question: Can a tutor send us Diploma past papers and mark schemes to keep?
faqs.answer: No, and no tutor should. Reproducing or distributing IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads is a copyright matter, and for unreleased material it is a malpractice exposure. Work is done against material the student legitimately holds through their school, marked against the published scheme in the session, with the official source referenced and linked. That is also why this page asks you to confirm weightings against your own school's guide.

faqs.question: Why does this page quote weightings but no exam dates?
faqs.answer: Because the two have different sourcing. Component structures and criterion allocations come from subject guides that schools issue to students, which is why the page gives them and tells you to confirm them against your own copy. Exam and results dates would have to come from the IB itself, and the board's own site returns an error to automated checking, so nothing in this project has been verified from it. An unverified date a family plans a revision schedule around is worse than no date.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-jurf.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma and Middle Years subjects to students in Ajman and across the Gulf time zone. Each profile names the subject and level, and each works from the student's own school assessment calendar rather than a generic revision plan.

intro.heading: The Diploma is a calendar problem before it is a teaching problem
paragraphs: Al Jurf is one of the more mixed districts in Ajman: residential streets alongside the university and hospital area, the courts, and the industrial zone further out. A notable share of households here work in education or medicine, which means parents who already understand assessment deadlines and are often the first to notice when their child's are converging. It also means households where both parents work late, and where an evening study plan has to survive a fortnight without supervision.

The Diploma punishes drift more than it punishes weakness. A student who is a little behind in September of DP2 is not a little behind in November; they are simultaneously late on an internal assessment draft, an Extended Essay deadline, a Theory of Knowledge exhibition and the first mock papers, because schools place those within weeks of each other. The written examinations in May are the visible deadline, and by the time they arrive most of the damage has already been done or avoided.

So the useful way to buy tutoring is backwards. Fix the session, then the school's internal deadlines, then the mock window, then the weeks that are actually available between them, and only then decide what a weekly hour is for. A plan built forwards from the day a parent happens to start searching tends to spend its first six weeks on whatever topic the student mentioned, which is rarely the topic that the next deadline requires.

The phrase in the search is home tutor, and the honest answer about delivery belongs here rather than at the bottom of the page. IB Gram does not provide in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Lessons for Al Jurf families are live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own draft or past paper on a shared screen. For calendar work this is an advantage rather than a compromise: a draft can be annotated and saved, and a deadline-week session can be moved to the next evening without anybody absorbing a wasted journey.

What this page sets out is the year as a sequence. The DP2 autumn and its four deadlines. What a mock paper is actually for and how to read one. How Ramadan and the UAE academic calendar change the available hours. Why no specific International Baccalaureate examination date appears anywhere on this page. The Cambridge and Pearson series, for the sibling who is sitting IGCSE at the same time. What a given number of remaining weeks can realistically achieve. And the academic-honesty line, which is under most pressure precisely when deadlines bunch.

None of that requires a parent to understand the syllabus. It requires one page of dates, held by the school and rarely consolidated by the family, and a willingness to put the hours where the calendar says they are needed rather than where the student feels most anxious. Those two things are worth more than any extra session.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-jurf.programmesIntro: Each International Baccalaureate programme has its own rhythm, and the rhythm is what determines when tutoring helps. The notes below describe the year rather than the syllabus, because for an Al Jurf family the timing question is the one that decides whether an hour is useful.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry units, portfolios and a final-year exhibition rather than examinations. The calendar is driven by unit boundaries and parent conferences, and the only hard deadline most children meet is the exhibition. That makes the year feel unpressured and allows a gap in number fluency or reading stamina to persist unnoticed for several terms.
programmes.countryNote: For Al Jurf families the useful intervention points are the weeks before each reporting conference, when a specific strand can be targeted with evidence. Short sessions of thirty to forty minutes twice weekly work better than a single long one, particularly for children on longer bus routes out to schools west of the city.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessment runs continuously against four criteria per subject, which means there is no quiet term. Criterion deadlines arrive every few weeks, and the Personal Project in the final year is the first extended independent piece most students attempt. Students who are strong on content lose marks on the process criteria, and those losses accumulate across every subject at once.
programmes.countryNote: The Personal Project timeline is the one worth marking on a family calendar in Al Jurf, because it runs alongside everything else and is easy to defer. A student who sets the project question in the first term rather than the second avoids the compression that otherwise lands in the same weeks as subject criterion deadlines.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years, six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal assessments carry roughly a fifth to a quarter of each subject grade and are marked by the school before external moderation. The decisive period is the autumn of DP2, when coursework deadlines, the first mocks and ordinary teaching all occupy the same weeks.
programmes.countryNote: DP2 students in Al Jurf typically move from two weekly sessions to three in the autumn term, then taper after mocks into targeted paper work. Families who keep the same two-session pattern through the coursework crunch almost always end up buying emergency hours in March instead, which costs more and achieves less.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Diploma courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project and service learning. The academic demand inside the Diploma courses is unchanged; what differs is the core and the breadth. The reflective project has its own deadline, which tends to be the component that slips because it has no examination attached.
programmes.countryNote: No Ajman school is a significant Career-related Programme provider, so students in Al Jurf following it have usually transferred to a Sharjah or Dubai school. Support is almost always for the Diploma courses within the programme, with separate scheduled time for the reflective project rather than hoping it fits around them.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-jurf.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are described by their internal assessment and paper timing, because that is what a backwards-planned schedule needs. Content gaps can be addressed at many points in the year; coursework cannot.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration is the internal component, and it is usually set in DP1 with a draft due early in DP2. Topics chosen late are the ones that produce thin mathematics. Paper work concentrates in the final term, with the HL third paper needing separate practice because it is an extended investigation rather than a question set.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics, with a calculator assumed throughout. The exploration needs real data, so collection has to be planned weeks before writing starts. Students who leave data gathering until the draft deadline end up with a dataset too small to support the statistical claims they then make about it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The internal assessment lives on uncertainty and error analysis, which schools rarely have laboratory time to teach properly. Starting that work before the practical is performed changes the mark considerably. Paper preparation needs separate attention to multiple choice, where loose definitions cost marks that content knowledge had already earned.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics generate most requests, and the internal assessment requires a research question narrow enough to answer in the word count. Data-based paper questions need practice separate from content revision, and that practice is usually the first thing dropped when deadlines bunch.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume makes revision feel endless, and command terms decide the marks. The internal assessment typically fails on statistical choice rather than on biology. Both are best addressed in the autumn of DP2, before the paper-shaped final term leaves no room for coursework repair.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a set of commentaries on published news articles, each with its own deadline, and article choice sets the ceiling before writing begins. Spreading the three commentaries across DP1 and early DP2 is the difference between a controlled process and three rushed pieces in one month.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The Higher Level case study is pre-released, which creates a defined preparation window that most students underuse. The internal assessment requires primary or secondary research planned in advance. Both are calendar items rather than revision items, and both reward early scheduling.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral is an internally assessed component with a recording date, and the Higher Level essay has its own deadline. Neither can be rescued in the final term. Preparation is a matter of choosing a genuinely arguable global issue early and practising the structure repeatedly.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay both carry deadlines that sit inside the same crowded autumn term as subject coursework. Theory of Knowledge is the component students most reliably defer, and the one where a small number of well-timed sessions produces the clearest improvement.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A single extended piece with supervisor checkpoints spread across both years. The research question is the whole battle; an essay with a question too broad to answer cannot be repaired by better writing later. Supervisor meetings are the deadlines that matter, and they are set by the school.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-jurf.regionsTitle: Al Jurf and the surrounding Ajman communities
ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-jurf.regionsIntro: Each part of Ajman runs on a slightly different weekly rhythm, depending on where its children go to school and what their parents' working hours look like. The notes below describe how the academic year actually lands in each.

regions.name: Al Jurf
regions.note: Residential streets beside the university and hospital district, with the courts and the industrial area nearby. Many households have two working parents on shift or academic schedules, so study time needs to be fixed rather than supervised.

regions.name: Al Rashidiya
regions.note: Central and close to the Sharjah approach roads. Students here lose the most time to afternoon traffic, which compresses the usable evening and makes the deadline weeks in the autumn term noticeably tighter.

regions.name: Al Nuaimiya
regions.note: Dense apartment living with a young student population and a busy informal tutoring market. Continuity is the weakness: arrangements change often, which is a problem for coursework that needs the same reader over months.

regions.name: Al Rawda
regions.note: Villa sub-communities popular with families working in Sharjah. School runs are short in the morning and slow in the afternoon, so the practical study block starts late and the Saturday morning slot does the heavy lifting.

regions.name: Al Mowaihat
regions.note: Closest to the schools west of the city, which means earlier arrivals home and the most flexible weekday schedule in the emirate. Families here can realistically run a 5pm session in the autumn deadline period.

regions.name: Al Zorah
regions.note: Low-density waterfront housing with long drives to every school. The time lost to transport is the single biggest constraint on a DP2 schedule here, and the reason an online slot is worth more than a local one.

regions.name: Emirates City
regions.note: Towers near the main highway with a transient population and a wide curriculum mix. Students arrive home earlier than in the older districts, so the autumn crunch is more manageable if the plan is set before it starts.

regions.name: Ajman Corniche
regions.note: Seafront apartments with a high proportion of teaching households. Parents here tend to recognise a converging deadline set early, which is why requests from the Corniche often arrive in September rather than February.

schoolClusters.city: Ajman schools and their assessment calendars
schoolClusters.note: Private schools in Ajman are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, and each school sets its own internal deadline dates within the framework its programme requires. Students we support from Al Jurf attend the schools below, and we work from whichever calendar their school issues.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah IB schools within reach of Al Jurf
schoolClusters.note: Private education in Sharjah is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Several Diploma cohorts sit a short drive across the emirate border.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-jurf.schoolDisclaimer: Schools appear here as context for the area we support; IB Gram has no affiliation with, or endorsement from, any of them.
ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-jurf.modesIntro: The three formats below map onto three different parts of the Diploma year. Choosing the wrong one for the point in the calendar you are at is the commonest planning error families make.

modes.title: Autumn coursework scheduling
modes.description: Through the DP2 autumn, sessions are organised around whichever internal deadline is next rather than around a subject. One week is an Economics commentary, the next a Physics uncertainty analysis, the next a Theory of Knowledge exhibition object. The point is to stop four deadlines arriving as one, and it only works if the school's dates are known at the start.
bullets: Session agenda set by the next school deadline, not by subject rotation
Student's own draft reviewed; the student writes every submitted word
Supervisor meetings respected rather than duplicated
Weekly written note so the parent can see what is outstanding

modes.title: Post-mock diagnostic and repair
modes.description: Mock results are the most useful information a Diploma family gets all year, and most of it is thrown away. This format starts by reading the mock paper question by question against the mark scheme, identifies the three or four recurring failure types, and builds a short sequence of sessions aimed only at those.
bullets: Mock scripts read against the published scheme, not just the total
Failure types named: method, timing, command term, content
A defined block rather than an open-ended commitment
Re-test on the same paper type at the end of the block

modes.title: Final-term paper work
modes.description: From roughly eight weeks out, teaching becomes paper-shaped. Each session takes one paper type under timed conditions, then marks and reworks it. New content is taught only where a gap blocks a whole paper section. This is also the format that fits the changed hours of Ramadan, because a timed paper can be sat at any hour the student is alert.
bullets: Timed papers followed by marking in the same session
Three to five sessions a week during school holidays if needed
Scheduled after Iftar where the block falls in Ramadan
Named gaps accepted rather than pretended away

sections.heading: The Diploma year from Al Jurf, counted backwards
paragraphs: Start at the end and work back. The written papers for UAE Diploma candidates are sat in the May session. Before that comes the final term, which is paper-shaped: timed practice, mark-scheme work, and repair of whatever the mocks exposed. Before that comes the mock window itself, set by the school, usually in the winter. Before that comes the autumn of DP2, which is where the coursework lives. And before all of it comes DP1, which is the only year in the programme with slack in it.

Laid out that way, the planning errors become obvious. A family that starts tutoring in March of DP2 has bought into the final term only, which can sharpen paper technique and cannot repair an internal assessment that has already been submitted. A family that starts in September of DP1 has two years of room and usually does not need three sessions a week to use it. The expensive moment is the one in between: the autumn of DP2, when everything converges and the hours available do not expand to match.

For Al Jurf households in particular, the autumn crunch collides with working patterns. Parents in the hospital and university district often cannot supervise a 6pm study block on a Tuesday, which means the structure has to come from the schedule rather than from an adult in the room. A fixed weekly slot with an agenda set by the next deadline does that job. A flexible arrangement that moves whenever the week is busy does not, because the weeks are all busy in that term.

The practical first step is to get the school's internal deadline dates in writing and put them on one page: subject internal assessments, the Extended Essay checkpoints, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay, and the mock window. Most schools issue this. Few families consolidate it, and the consolidation is where the realisation usually happens that three of them fall in the same fortnight.
bullets: May session, final term, mock window, DP2 autumn, DP1: plan in that order
Starting in March buys paper technique only
The autumn of DP2 is the expensive convergence point
Put every internal deadline on one page before buying any hours

sections.heading: Four internal deadlines in one term
paragraphs: The table below is the shape of a typical DP2 autumn. Exact dates belong to your child's school and vary between Ajman and Sharjah schools and between cohorts, so the table shows sequence and requirement rather than dates. What it demonstrates is the convergence: a student with three Higher Level subjects can face a subject internal assessment draft, an Extended Essay full draft, a Theory of Knowledge exhibition submission and the first mock papers within about six weeks.

Read the right-hand column carefully, because it is the one that decides whether a deadline is survivable. An internal assessment draft due in November needs its research question settled in September and its data collected in October. A student who has the question but no data in late October has effectively missed the deadline already, whatever the calendar says. The same logic applies to the Extended Essay: a full draft requires reading that happened months earlier.

This is why the autumn is where tutoring earns its keep, and why the agenda should follow the deadline sequence rather than a subject rotation. An hour spent on Economics content in the week an Economics commentary is due is an hour wasted; an hour spent on whether the chosen article actually supports the required diagram is not. The work is scheduling as much as teaching, and the scheduling has to come from the school's dates.

One caution about the final row. Feedback returned on a draft is the most valuable document in the process and the least used. A supervisor's comment identifying a weak analysis section is an instruction, and a student who reads it, agrees with it and submits the same analysis has thrown away the one free correction the system offers. Scheduling a session specifically to work through returned feedback, before the final submission window closes, is a small intervention with a disproportionate effect on the mark.

sections.heading: What a mock paper is actually for
paragraphs: Mocks are usually treated as a rehearsal and reported as a grade. Both of those waste them. A mock script is the only document in the Diploma year that shows, question by question, how a particular student fails under timed conditions, and the grade on the front is the least informative thing in it.

Read properly, a mock separates four distinct problems that look identical from the outside. There is content the student does not know. There is content they know and cannot retrieve under pressure. There is a method they can execute but abandon when the numbers get awkward. And there is timing, where the last questions are blank or rushed and the marks lost there have nothing to do with understanding. Each needs a different response, and a general instruction to revise more addresses none of them.

The diagnostic is mechanical. Mark the script against the published scheme, record the marks by question rather than as a total, and tag each loss with one of those four labels. The pattern is usually clear within one paper and unmistakable across two. A student losing eleven marks to timing and four to content should be practising timed sections, not rereading notes, and that distinction is invisible in a reported percentage.

For a family in Al Jurf, the practical value is that the post-mock period is short and the repair block has to be aimed. Four or five sessions spent on the two failure types that cost the most marks will move more than twenty sessions of general revision, and the evidence for which two is sitting in the script the school has already marked.
bullets: Record marks by question, not as a total
Tag each loss: content, retrieval, method, timing
Timing losses are fixed by timed practice, not by revision
Aim the post-mock block at the two most expensive failure types

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the shape of the UAE academic year
paragraphs: Any study plan that ignores Ramadan will be rewritten in the first week of it. School days shorten, the afternoon is low-energy for fasting students, and the productive hours move to the evening after Iftar. For a Diploma student this is a real constraint on a term that may already contain a mock window or a coursework deadline, and it is entirely predictable, which means it can be planned for instead of absorbed.

Two approaches work for Ajman families. The first is to shift sessions to roughly 9pm onwards for the month, which suits timed paper practice and review better than new teaching. The second is to pause for the month entirely and compensate with an intensive block afterwards, which suits a student whose energy drops sharply. What does not work is leaving a 6.30pm slot in place and hoping, which produces a month of poor sessions and a resentful student.

Eid holidays and the school breaks around them are the other side of the same coin: they are the only multi-day blocks in the year where a student can do sustained work on an Extended Essay or an internal assessment without a school timetable interrupting. Families who plan one or two intensive sessions into a holiday week rather than treating it as entirely free time consistently arrive at the following term in better shape.

The summer between DP1 and DP2 is the largest unused asset in the whole programme. Internal assessment research questions settled in July, Extended Essay reading done in August, and the student starts DP2 with the autumn convergence already partly disarmed. It is also the cheapest intervention in the year, because a handful of sessions in a quiet month replaces a crisis block in November.

sections.heading: Why this page publishes no International Baccalaureate examination date
paragraphs: There is a deliberate absence on this page. No specific International Baccalaureate examination or results date appears anywhere on it, and that is a decision rather than an oversight. The organisation's own site blocks automated retrieval, which means no date in our research for this project was confirmed from the source itself. Secondary sites converge on windows and they are not the authority, and a date a parent acts on must be right.

This matters more than it sounds, because the cost of a wrong date is asymmetric. A page that is vague about an examination window costs a reader a phone call to the school. A page that publishes a confident wrong window costs a family a misaligned revision plan, and in the worst case a missed registration. There is a live example of exactly that failure in this market: Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only, and pages written for UAE parents have quoted its entry deadlines and examination windows as though they applied here.

So the position on this page is simple. UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session; that is stable and safe to state. For the exact dates of papers, the internal upload deadlines your school works to, and the day results are released, the authority is your child's International Baccalaureate coordinator and the organisation's own published calendar. Ask the coordinator in September and write the dates on the same page as the school's internal deadlines.

The Cambridge and Pearson dates in the next section are different, because they come from the boards' own published pages and are quoted with the framing those pages use. Where a date is historical it is given with its year, because that is what makes it checkable. Where a series is in the future it is named by its month only, so the page does not quietly become wrong twelve months from now.
bullets: UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session
No specific IB examination or results date is published here
Confirm dates with your school's IB coordinator, in writing, in September
Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only

sections.heading: The sibling sitting IGCSE: Cambridge and Pearson series
paragraphs: Many Al Jurf households are running two calendars at once, because one child is in the Diploma while another is mid-IGCSE. The board calendars are published, unlike the Diploma dates discussed above, and they can be stated with their sources attached.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October windows. Every examination centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge is explicit that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the centre's zone, stating that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. That is a sentence worth reading twice, and it is the reason to work only from the timetable the school's examinations officer issues.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May and June and again in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Results from the June 2026 series reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 series results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series, which is why any session plan should link the live official timetable rather than rely on a restatement that can be revised.

The planning consequence for a two-child household is that the November series is a genuine resit route for an IGCSE grade, with results arriving in January, while the Diploma has no equivalent mid-year repair. A family budgeting tutoring hours across both children should treat the Diploma calendar as fixed and the IGCSE calendar as having one built-in second chance, which changes where the scarce hours should go in the autumn.

sections.heading: What a given number of weeks can actually achieve
paragraphs: Families almost always ask whether it is too late, and the honest answer depends entirely on the number of weeks and on what is being repaired. Content can be taught quickly. Technique takes repetition. Coursework that has been submitted cannot be changed at all. Those three facts produce very different answers to the same question asked in September, January and April.

The table below is a working rule rather than a promise, and it deliberately contains the word no in several places. A plan that claims full syllabus coverage in six weeks is not reading the calendar. A plan that names what it will not attempt is more likely to deliver what it does attempt, and it lets a parent decide whether the spend is worth it with the information in front of them.

What shifts the arithmetic most is the student's own working time between sessions. A weekly hour with four hours of independent work behind it moves several times faster than the same hour with nothing behind it, and in a household where both parents work late that independent time has to be scheduled rather than assumed. For Al Jurf families this is often the real variable, not the number of sessions purchased.

The other variable worth naming is how many subjects the remaining weeks are being asked to carry. Eight weeks aimed at one paper in one subject is a real intervention. The same eight weeks spread across four subjects is two sessions each, which is enough to identify a problem and not enough to fix one. Where several subjects are weak late in the year, the better decision is usually to concentrate on the two where marks move fastest and accept the others as they stand, which is an uncomfortable conversation and a more honest plan.

table.caption: WEEKS REMAINING AND WHAT THEY REALISTICALLY BUY
rows: Content coverage, coursework done properly, technique built
Nothing much is out of reach at this range
Two or three named weak topics plus paper technique
Weekly teaching plus a post-mock repair block
Paper technique, timing, the highest-value topic gaps
Broad content recovery across several subjects
Paper-shaped block, three to five sessions a week
Timing discipline, command terms, one topic
Short intensive on one paper type
Any change to the submitted work
Redirect all hours to the written papers

sections.heading: Deadline pressure and the academic-honesty line
paragraphs: The academic-honesty boundary is tested hardest in exactly the weeks this page is about. A student with three internal deadlines in a fortnight is the student most likely to be offered, and most tempted by, a service that will simply produce the work. That market exists in this search segment, and one site in it sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price.

What is being sold there is a risk, not a shortcut. Submitting work that is not the student's own is an academic-honesty breach under the organisation's rules, and the consequences for a Diploma candidate can extend to losing the Diploma itself. The detection route is also more mundane than families imagine: a supervisor who has read a student's work all year notices when the voice changes, and the supervisor's declaration is part of the process.

Legitimate help under deadline pressure looks narrow and is more effective than it sounds. A tutor can read a draft and ask where the evidence actually supports the claim. They can explain what a criterion descriptor requires in that subject, because terms such as personal engagement and evaluation have specific evidence requirements rather than general ones. They can cut a research question down to something answerable in the word count, which is the single most common cause of a capped mark. They can teach the student to read their own paragraph the way a moderator will.

What a tutor cannot do is write, rewrite to a finished state, or supply text for submission, and a tutor who is asked should decline. For a family under deadline pressure that refusal can feel unhelpful in the moment. It is the part of the service that protects the thing the whole two years was for, and hearing it clearly is a reason to trust the rest.
bullets: Internal assessments are worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of each subject grade
Purchased coursework risks the Diploma, not just the mark
Criterion descriptors are technical and teachable; that is where the marks are
A tutor who refuses to draft is doing the job correctly

process.title: Send the school's deadline dates first
process.description: Before subjects or slots, we want the internal assessment dates, Extended Essay checkpoints, Theory of Knowledge deadlines and the mock window as your child's school has issued them. That single page determines what the first six weeks of tutoring should be about, and most families have never put it together in one view.

process.title: Name the subjects and levels
process.description: Three Higher Levels and three Standard Levels, with the Mathematics route specified. Level changes who can teach the course properly, and the Higher Level option topics your school chose change it again. The school report or the subject teacher will confirm anything you are unsure about.

process.title: Free trial lesson on the next deadline
process.description: One lesson, no charge, no payment details taken beforehand, spent on whatever is actually due next rather than on a general assessment. For a DP2 student in the autumn that is usually a draft or a commentary, and the hour tells you more about the tutor than any introductory conversation would.

process.title: Build the schedule backwards
process.description: We fix the session, then the school deadlines, then the mock window, then count the weeks genuinely available and agree what each one is for. The output is a short plan with named gaps rather than a promise of full coverage, which is the only version of this document that survives contact with a term.

process.title: Re-plan after mocks, not before
process.description: Mock scripts are read question by question against the published scheme and the plan is rewritten around what they show. That is the one scheduled review point in the year where the evidence is good enough to change course, and it is the moment most families instead double down on whatever they were already doing.

whyPoints.title: Planned from the session backwards
whyPoints.description: The schedule starts from the examination and the school's internal deadlines, not from the week a parent began searching. That ordering is what stops the first six weeks being spent on a topic the next deadline does not require, which is the commonest waste in Diploma tutoring.

whyPoints.title: Your school's calendar, not a generic one
whyPoints.description: Deadlines differ between schools and cohorts, and an Ajman school and a Sharjah school may be weeks apart on the same component. We work from the dates your child's school issued, which is why we ask for them before anything is booked.

whyPoints.title: Mock scripts read properly
whyPoints.description: Marks recorded question by question and each loss tagged as content, retrieval, method or timing. Four or five sessions aimed at the two most expensive failure types will move more than a term of general revision, and the evidence is already in the script.

whyPoints.title: Honest about dates we cannot verify
whyPoints.description: No International Baccalaureate examination or results date appears on this page, because none could be confirmed from the organisation's own site. Cambridge and Pearson dates are quoted with their sources and their framing, and future series are named by month so the page does not go stale.

whyPoints.title: Ramadan planned, not absorbed
whyPoints.description: Sessions shift to after Iftar or pause for the month with an intensive block afterwards, decided in advance rather than improvised in week one. A fasting student at a 6.30pm session in that month is not studying, whatever the schedule says.

whyPoints.title: A fixed boundary under pressure
whyPoints.description: Coursework is taught, questioned and reviewed, never written or completed. The weeks when deadlines converge are exactly when that line matters, and a service willing to cross it is selling a certification risk alongside the hour.

faqs.question: When should an Al Jurf family start Diploma tutoring?
faqs.answer: The cheapest effective point is the summer between DP1 and DP2, when internal assessment research questions can be settled and Extended Essay reading done before the autumn convergence. The most common point is the autumn of DP2, which works but costs more because everything is urgent. Starting in the final term buys paper technique only: coursework already submitted cannot be changed. If you are choosing between September and January, choose September and buy fewer hours.

faqs.question: Why do four Diploma deadlines land in the same few weeks?
faqs.answer: Because the components are independent of each other and all have to be complete before external moderation and the examination term. Subject internal assessments, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay, and the school's mocks each have their own logic, and schools place them where they fit rather than where they are comfortable. The result in a typical DP2 autumn is three or four converging within about six weeks. Consolidating the dates onto one page is how a family sees it coming.

faqs.question: What does the mock window actually tell us?
faqs.answer: More than the grade suggests, if the script is read rather than the total. A mock separates four problems that look identical from outside: content not known, content not retrievable under pressure, method abandoned mid-question, and time simply run out. Each needs a different response, and a general instruction to revise addresses none of them. Mark the paper against the published scheme, record marks by question, tag each loss, and the next four sessions become obvious.

faqs.question: Can a Diploma student make up ground in eight weeks?
faqs.answer: On paper technique, timing and two or three named topics, yes, and that can be worth several marks a paper. On reteaching a two-year syllabus, no, and any plan claiming otherwise is not reading the calendar. Eight weeks works best as a paper-shaped block: timed papers, marked against the scheme in the same session, with the highest-value gaps taught where they block a whole section. Named gaps left alone deliberately is part of a plan that works.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to a home in Al Jurf?
faqs.answer: No. In-home visits are a service IB Gram provides only in India, not anywhere in the UAE. Diploma lessons for Al Jurf families run live over video, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own draft or past paper annotated on a shared screen. For deadline work the format helps: the annotated draft is saved, and a session in a crowded week can be moved to the following evening without anybody absorbing a wasted journey across Ajman.

faqs.question: How should we handle Ramadan in a DP2 year?
faqs.answer: Decide in advance rather than in the first week. Two approaches work: shift sessions to roughly 9pm after Iftar, which suits timed paper practice and review better than new teaching, or pause for the month and book an intensive block afterwards. Leaving a 6.30pm slot in place produces a month of tired sessions. Tell us a couple of weeks ahead, because late-evening slots fill quickly across the Gulf during that period and a preferred tutor may not be free.

faqs.question: What should we do with the summer between DP1 and DP2?
faqs.answer: Treat it as the largest unused asset in the programme. Internal assessment research questions settled in July and Extended Essay reading done in August remove a large part of the autumn convergence before it starts. Two or three sessions a month through the summer costs far less than the emergency block in November that it prevents. Students resist this and the arithmetic is not close: a question corrected in July saves a rewrite in week ten of DP2.

faqs.question: Why are there no Diploma examination dates anywhere on this page?
faqs.answer: Because we could not confirm them from the organisation's own source, which blocks automated retrieval, and a date a parent acts on must be right. UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session, which is stable and safe to state. For paper dates, internal upload deadlines and the results release day, ask your child's International Baccalaureate coordinator and the organisation's published calendar, in September, and write them on the same page as the school's internal deadlines. Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page are quoted from the boards' own pages.

faqs.question: Our younger child sits IGCSE. Do the two calendars clash?
faqs.answer: They overlap in the spring, which is where household attention becomes the scarce resource rather than money. The useful difference is that the November series gives an IGCSE candidate a genuine second chance with results in January, while the Diploma has no mid-year repair route. In an autumn where hours are limited, that argues for putting them into the Diploma deadlines and treating the IGCSE as having one built-in retry. Cambridge runs June and November for UAE candidates.

faqs.question: Which internal assessment is most often left too late?
faqs.answer: Theory of Knowledge, because it has no examination attached and therefore no obvious penalty for deferring it, followed by the Extended Essay, where the real deadline is the reading rather than the writing. Subject internal assessments are usually chased by the subject teacher and so get done. The pattern is predictable enough to plan around: schedule the components nobody is chasing first, because the ones with a teacher behind them will happen anyway.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a DP2 student in Ajman need?
faqs.answer: Two through DP1, three during the autumn coursework convergence, then a taper after mocks into a targeted block. More than three weekly sessions usually means the student has no time left to do the independent work that makes sessions stick, and in a household where both parents work late that independent time has to be scheduled rather than assumed. If three sessions are not enough, the problem is more likely study method than teaching volume.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an internal assessment the week it is due?
faqs.answer: They can read the draft, question whether the evidence supports the claims, explain what a criterion actually requires, and help the student prioritise what to fix in the time left. They cannot write it, rewrite it to a finished state, or supply text for submission, and they should decline if asked. Under deadline pressure that refusal feels unhelpful and is the point of the service: submitted work that is not the student's own risks the Diploma itself, not just the mark.

faqs.question: What happens if the school moves a deadline?
faqs.answer: Tell us the same week and the session agenda moves with it. This is the main practical reason we ask for the school's calendar at the start rather than working to a generic plan: a deadline that shifts two weeks changes which component the next three sessions should address. Schools in Ajman and Sharjah do adjust dates, particularly around the mock window and public holidays, and a plan that cannot absorb that is a plan that will be abandoned.

faqs.question: Is there any point starting after the final mocks?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a narrow scope. The remaining weeks are paper weeks: timing discipline, command terms, mark-scheme familiarity and the one or two topics that block whole sections. That is genuinely worth marks. What it cannot do is repair coursework already submitted or build content from scratch across several subjects. Buy it as a defined block with a stated number of hours rather than an open-ended arrangement, and judge it on marked timed papers before and after.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-jurf.closingHeading: Send the dates, then the subjects
ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-jurf.closingBody: The first useful message from an Al Jurf family is not a request for a tutor; it is the school's list of internal assessment deadlines, Extended Essay checkpoints, Theory of Knowledge dates and the mock window, with the subjects and levels alongside. From that we can say what the next six weeks should actually be about, whether a specialist in each subject is free in your evening slot this term, and what a realistic plan looks like counting backwards from the session. The trial lesson then runs on whatever is due next, which is a better test of a tutor than any introduction.

intro.heading: Climb the rate ladder before you pick a rung
paragraphs: The spread of tutoring prices reaching Al Mowaihat is roughly fourteenfold. At the bottom, online tuition is advertised from AED 33 to 52 by Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650 an hour for a premium named tutor. Between them sit a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150 to 300, in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500, and IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 270 per TutorChase and AED 200 to 450 and above per the Bestimate survey. All read in October 2026.

Most pages in this market pick one of those numbers and present it as the price. The useful version is the ladder itself, because each rung buys a genuinely different thing, and a family's job is to work out which rung the problem sits on. Supervision is a bottom-rung job. Diagnosing why a Higher Level Chemistry student loses marks on equilibrium is not, and paying bottom-rung money for it means paying for somebody to learn the course alongside your child.

Al Mowaihat is useful ground for this argument. The villa districts numbered 1 to 3 run along Sheikh Ammar Road, close enough to Ajman's school belt that mid-afternoon sessions are realistic and close enough to the Sharjah boundary that plenty of tutors advertise here. The local supply at the bottom of the ladder is real. The local supply at the top, for a specific Diploma Higher Level option, is close to nonexistent.

Delivery is stated plainly so the rest reads correctly. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. The phrase in this page's address is what parents type, and it is answered honestly: what in-home tuition costs around Al Mowaihat, what the premium consists of, and why a screen usually buys more teaching per dirham here than a car does.

Nothing below is an IB Gram price list, because the right rate depends on subject, level and weeks remaining. What is published is the market, with sources, so that any quote can be checked against something. That is deliberately different from the norm in this cluster: three of the six competitor pages researched for this project publish no price at all, one asks the price in its own list of questions and then declines to answer it, and two quote in US dollars, a currency no household in Al Mowaihat actually banks in. A parent cannot negotiate against a blank, which is most of the reason this page starts with figures rather than with reassurance. The bands below are the floor and the ceiling of what is being asked across the emirate, and knowing both is what makes a single quote legible.

sections.heading: The rate ladder: what each AED band actually buys
paragraphs: Start at the bottom rather than the top, because the bottom rung is where most of the market's volume sits and where most of the disappointment is generated. Online tuition advertised from AED 33 to 65 an hour buys a person, a schedule and a routine. That is genuinely useful for a primary child or for a teenager who will not sit down without supervision. It does not buy a diagnosis, and it will not survive contact with a Higher Level paper.

The middle of the ladder, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, is where the purchase changes character. Here you are buying somebody who knows the syllabus, has seen the mark scheme and can tell you in forty minutes whether marks are going on recall, method, command-term reading or timing. For most Middle Years and Standard Level work this rung is the whole answer, and climbing higher adds reputation rather than effect.

The specialist rung, AED 200 to 450 and above, is paid for scarcity. There are very few teachers in the Northern Emirates covering Higher Level Chemistry, Higher Level Economics with its commentaries, or a minority language, and some of those are contractually unable to tutor their own school's students. Above that sits the premium band at AED 500 to 650, where BartyED's published AED 650 buys a particular named individual. That can be the right purchase and it is rarely the necessary one.

What follows from the ladder is a single discipline: identify the rung the problem is on before shopping for a rate. Nearly all of the avoidable spending in this market comes from buying the wrong rung rather than from being overcharged on the right one.

sections.heading: The extras that catch Al Mowaihat parents off guard
paragraphs: An hourly rate is not a price. The number that matters is what leaves the account over a term, and the gap between the two is made up of things nobody volunteers at the enquiry stage. The commonest is the minimum block: a rate quoted per hour but sold in packs of eight or twelve, with the first invoice three or four times the number discussed.

The second is the cancellation rule. Twenty-four hours' notice is reasonable; a charged session for a child sent home ill at 2pm is not, and a family in Al Mowaihat with a school run that ends at 3:15pm will meet that rule several times a term. The third is the travel supplement, which on an in-home quote may be inside the rate or added separately, and which is worth having stated in writing before a tutor's first journey up Sheikh Ammar Road.

The fourth is the rate review. A number quoted in September is not necessarily the number charged in March, because demand rises towards a series and capacity does not. The fifth is material: whether reports, notes and marked work are included or billed. The sixth is tax treatment, where the only reasonable thing to establish is whether a quoted AED figure is inclusive or exclusive, and whether the provider holds a tax registration number.
None of these is improper. All six are answerable in a short message before any payment, and a provider that will not answer them in writing has told you something useful at no cost.

sections.heading: One session a week or two? The arithmetic of diminishing returns
paragraphs: Frequency is the lever families reach for when a report is disappointing, and it is the wrong lever most of the time. A second weekly session doubles the bill and rarely doubles the effect, because the binding constraint is usually not teaching time but the work done between sessions. A student who does not practise between one lesson a week will not practise between two.

The honest pattern across a Diploma is a curve rather than a flat line. Grade 11 wants one session a week in the subject that is genuinely weak, with the emphasis on building rather than on polishing. The autumn of Grade 12 wants coursework attention, which is often block work rather than weekly hours. The spring before the papers is the only period where two or three sessions a week reliably earns its cost, because timed practice marked against a real scheme compounds in a way that content teaching does not.

There is an exception worth naming. Where a student has missed a block of school, changed curriculum mid-year, or arrived from a system with a different sequence, two sessions a week for a defined number of weeks is catch-up rather than intensity, and it should have an end date written into it from the start. The distinction is not pedantic: catch-up has a finishing line that both the tutor and the student can see, while intensity has none, which is why it quietly becomes the permanent arrangement nobody reviews.

sections.heading: Sharing the cost: siblings, pairs and the Al Mowaihat cluster
paragraphs: Cost sharing is the most under-used lever available to families in this part of Ajman, and the reason is structural rather than financial: it needs two students on the same syllabus code at the same tier with a similar starting point, and in a small emirate that is hard to arrange outside the two or three most widely taught subjects.

Where it works best is siblings. Two children in one household on different subjects cannot share a session, but they can share a tutor relationship, a slot pattern and a reporting rhythm, and that reduces the administrative friction that causes families to drift away from a plan they were paying for. Where it works second best is a pair of classmates from the same Al Mowaihat school sitting the same paper, revising technique rather than content.

What sharing cannot do is follow one student's specific gaps. A group of two to four is an exam-technique format: timed questions, mark-scheme reading, the discipline of showing method. The moment the diagnosis identifies an individual topic sequence that has broken down, the group stops being cheaper and starts being slower.

A tuition centre's group class is a different product again, and a legitimate one. Worth knowing: an operation with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. Asking a centre for its permit number is an ordinary question.

sections.heading: What scarcity does to a price around Al Mowaihat
paragraphs: The single biggest driver of a Diploma quote in Ajman is not the tutor's confidence, it is how many people could plausibly do the job. That number is high for Mathematics and English and very low for several Higher Level options, and the price follows it almost exactly.

There is a second squeeze on local supply that families rarely hear about. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the current policy document and should be verified against it, but the direction is consistent across sources: the nearest qualified teacher is frequently the one person who cannot take the work.

Put those two facts together and the local market for a scarce Higher Level subject around Al Mowaihat is thinner than the advertising suggests. Removing the geographic constraint is what changes the price, because the comparison is no longer between the two people who could reach Sheikh Ammar Road by 5pm. Scarcity that is an artefact of a radius is not real scarcity, and it should not be paid for as though it were.

sections.heading: What you are actually buying when you buy coursework support
paragraphs: Coursework is the most commercially attractive thing in this market and the easiest to buy badly, because the marks are internal and the criteria are published in documents most parents have never opened. Worth knowing: the internal component is roughly a fifth to a quarter of each Diploma subject grade, and it is marked against named criteria with fixed mark allocations, not against a general impression of quality.

That changes what good support looks like. For the Mathematics exploration, the marks are divided across presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, with use of mathematics carrying the largest single allocation. A student who writes beautifully about a topic they have not mathematically developed cannot reach the top bands, and no amount of polishing fixes that. For Middle Years subjects, each of the four criteria is marked out of 8, which means a strand left unaddressed costs a predictable number of marks.

Legitimate support is therefore criterion work: reading the descriptors, identifying which strand is unaddressed, and giving written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor must never write, redraft or complete the exploration, the Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay, a TOK essay or any assessed coursework, and must not supply text for a student to paste. A page found during research for this project sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; the consequence of buying one falls on the student, not on the seller.

Confirm every mark allocation against the subject guide your school issues, because guides are revised and this page does not reproduce them. No tutor should supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads; the correct behaviour is to reference and link the official source.

sections.heading: Is the tutor permitted to teach, and how would you know?
paragraphs: This is a short section because the answer is short, and it belongs on a cost page because the cheapest quotes are where the question matters most. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years.

Eligibility is broad. Teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students may all apply. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with applications made through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here.

The cost logic is uncomfortable for the bottom of the market. Because the permit is free and takes two working days, a low rate cannot be explained by permit costs being avoided, only by the permit not existing. A parent cannot tell from an advertisement, so the question has to be asked, and it is one sentence long.

For completeness: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and nothing on this page should be read as a claim of one. Describing what a regulator does is not the same as claiming its endorsement, and the difference matters.

sections.heading: Spending in the right term
paragraphs: The last cost lever is timing, and it is free. Rates in this market firm up as a series approaches because demand rises and the same teachers cannot teach more hours. A family booking Higher Level support in September is not competing for capacity; the same family booking in spring is. Early planning is a discount that costs nothing to claim.

On the IB side, dates have to be handled honestly. No IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, because the board's own site returns an error to automated checking. What is safe to say is that UAE schools sit the May session and that a November session exists as an alternative route, and that any specific date should come from the school's Diploma coordinator or from ibo.org. A tutoring page is not a timetable.

On the IGCSE side of a household the sourced position is firmer. Cambridge runs June and November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones; the board states that using the correct zone timetable is essential and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. Cambridge's February/March series is offered in India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026.

One more timing note specific to this market: Ramadan shortens school hours and moves the useful study window to after Iftar. Online sessions move with it. An in-home tutor driving to Al Mowaihat after Iftar is a much harder thing to arrange, and that month is frequently where a term's momentum is quietly lost.

process.title: Name the rung, not just the subject
process.description: Say what you think is wrong: not sitting down to work, not understanding a topic, or knowing the content and losing marks anyway. Those three sit on three different rungs of the rate ladder, and naming yours saves a term of paying for the wrong one.

process.title: Take the free diagnostic lesson
process.description: The first session is a diagnosis and no card details are taken for it. The tutor works through real paper questions to establish whether marks are going on recall, method, command-term reading or timing, and you keep the written summary either way.

process.title: Get the six extras answered in writing
process.description: Minimum block, cancellation notice, travel, rate reviews, whether notes are included, and whether the figure is inclusive of tax. Ask every provider the same six questions and the quotes become comparable for the first time.

process.title: Book a slot that uses Al Mowaihat's short school run
process.description: The district's proximity to Ajman's school belt makes a 4:00pm or 4:30pm start genuinely achievable, which is rare in this emirate. Because lessons run online there is no travel to add at either end, so the earliest workable slot is the one straight after the drive home.

process.title: Reduce the frequency on purpose
process.description: The aim is fewer sessions. Once the diagnosed gap closes, weekly work should move to fortnightly or stop until the next pressure point. A provider that never proposes stepping down is managing revenue rather than marks.
