faqs.question: What is the cheapest sensible way to get IB help in Al Mowaihat?
faqs.answer: Identify which rung the problem sits on first. If the issue is that work does not get started, the bottom rung does the job: online tuition is advertised from AED 33 to 52 by Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik, and supervision is a real service worth that price. If the issue is losing marks despite knowing the content, the bottom rung will waste a term. The cheapest route overall is a free diagnostic lesson, then buying only the rung the diagnosis points at.

faqs.question: Why is Higher Level Chemistry quoted so much higher than Standard Level Maths in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Scarcity, not difficulty. Mathematics is taught in every Diploma school in the emirate, so the pool is deep and pricing is competitive. Higher Level Chemistry is taught by a handful of teachers across the Northern Emirates, and in Abu Dhabi the regulator's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid tuition of their own students, with the MoHRE permit code of conduct barring the same. Specialist rates were published at AED 270 by TutorChase and AED 200 to 450 and above in the Bestimate survey.

faqs.question: Will two sessions a week work twice as well as one for my child in Al Mowaihat?
faqs.answer: Rarely, because the binding constraint is usually the work done between sessions rather than teaching time. A student who does not practise between one weekly lesson will not practise between two. The pattern that does earn its cost is a curve: one session a week in Grade 11, block work on coursework in the autumn of Grade 12, then two or three a week for the eight to twelve weeks before the papers, when timed practice marked against a real scheme compounds.

faqs.question: What extras should I ask about before paying an Ajman tutor?
faqs.answer: Six, and all six are answerable in a short message. Minimum block size and whether unused sessions are refundable or transferable. Cancellation notice, including what happens when a child is sent home ill. Whether travel is inside an in-home rate. Whether the rate can change mid-year. Whether written notes and marked work are included. And whether the AED figure quoted is inclusive or exclusive of tax, with a tax registration number if one is held. A provider that will not answer in writing has told you something.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same Al Mowaihat household share one tutor to cut the bill?
faqs.answer: If they are on the same syllabus code at the same tier with a similar starting point, yes, and the saving per student is material. If they are on different subjects, they cannot share a session but they can share a tutor relationship, a slot pattern and a reporting rhythm, which removes the administrative friction that makes families drift away from plans they are paying for. What sharing cannot do is follow one child's individual gaps, so it suits technique work better than repair work.

faqs.question: How much does a two-year IB Diploma tuition plan come to in total?
faqs.answer: For one Higher Level subject taught weekly at mid-market rates it lands in the AED 10,000 to 20,000 range across Grades 11 and 12, derived from Bestimate's monthly bands of AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Two subjects roughly doubles it. The reason to calculate it in Grade 11 rather than Grade 12 is that the shape of the spend, light early and heavy before the papers, is only available to a family that planned it.

faqs.question: Does a tuition centre group class work out cheaper than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: On headline price, usually yes, and for exam technique a group can be effective. The trade is that a group cannot follow one student's specific gaps, and that you travel to a fixed timetable rather than choosing a slot. One thing worth asking a centre: an operation with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. The permit number is a fair question.

faqs.question: How are marks divided inside an IB Mathematics exploration?
faqs.answer: Across five criteria totalling 20 marks, covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, with use of mathematics carrying the largest single allocation. The practical consequence is that a student who writes well about a topic they have not mathematically developed cannot reach the top bands, and polishing the prose will not fix it. Confirm the current allocations against the subject guide your school issues, because guides are revised and this page does not reproduce them.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying a premium named tutor at AED 650 an hour?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and rarely necessarily. BartyED's published AED 650 buys a particular individual's time, which can be the right purchase for a very scarce Higher Level option or for a student who has already worked through the mid rung without progress. For a Standard Level subject it is almost never the efficient choice: the qualified online band of AED 150 to 300 contains people who know the same mark scheme. Ask what the premium is for, specifically, and expect a concrete answer.

faqs.question: Does the price change if we start in September instead of March?
faqs.answer: In this market it generally does, because demand rises towards a series while the same tutors cannot teach more hours. A family booking a scarce Higher Level subject in September is not competing for capacity; the same family booking in spring is. That makes early planning a discount available to anybody prepared to claim it. It also means a quote given in autumn should not be assumed to hold in spring, which is reasonable to ask a provider to confirm in writing.

faqs.question: How much Extended Essay help can an Al Mowaihat student legitimately buy?
faqs.answer: Yes, inside a boundary worth stating precisely. A tutor may help narrow a research question so it can actually be answered within the 4,000-word ceiling, discuss structure, explain what each named criterion demands, and give written feedback on drafts the student has written. A tutor must never write, redraft or complete the essay, nor supply text to paste in. Work sold as a finished piece is academic malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on whoever sold it.

faqs.question: Why is there no IB exam date on this page?
faqs.answer: Because none has been verified. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project is confirmed from the board itself, and publishing an unverified date that a parent plans around would be worse than publishing none. What is safe to say is that UAE schools sit the May session and that a November session exists as an alternative route. Any specific date should come from your school's Diploma coordinator or from ibo.org.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan affect a tuition plan in Al Mowaihat?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten and the useful study window moves to after Iftar, which is precisely when an in-home tutor is least likely to be driving anywhere. Online sessions move with the month: rescheduled to post-Iftar timing, or kept at the same frequency with shorter sessions. The practical advice is to set the arrangement before the month begins rather than cancelling week by week, because a quietly abandoned month is where a term's momentum is most often lost.

faqs.question: Is a cheap tutor without a MoHRE permit actually cheaper?
faqs.answer: The permit is free of charge, valid for two years and listed with a two-working-day completion time on MoHRE's own service page, so a low rate cannot be explained by avoiding a permit cost. It can be explained by the permit not existing. Individuals offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. Private tutoring here is not unregulated and the permit is not optional, so ask to see it.

faqs.question: What is the single most common way Ajman families waste tuition money?
faqs.answer: Buying hours against an undiagnosed problem. A family worried about Chemistry books two sessions a week in September and finds in January that nothing has changed, because nobody established whether the issue was recall, method, command-term reading or timing. One diagnostic session that answers that question is worth more than a term of unfocused ones, and at IB Gram it is free with no card details taken. The second most common is paying a specialist rate for what is really supervision.

intro.heading: Start with the calendar, not the tutor
paragraphs: The useful question is not whether a good IB tutor exists in Al Nuaimiya. It is what the next eight weeks have to achieve. An IB Diploma runs on fixed internal deadlines, and almost every parent who searches for an IB home tutor in Al Nuaimiya is somewhere specific on that timeline: a DP1 student who has just chosen subjects and found Higher Level heavier than expected, a DP1 student whose Internal Assessment proposal is overdue, or a DP2 student whose mock paper came back below the predicted grade with the May examinations ahead.

Those three positions need different teaching. The DP1 subject-choice problem is diagnostic work — finding which topic from the first term was never secured, then rebuilding it before the course moves on. The Internal Assessment problem is process coaching: narrowing a research question until it is answerable, planning data collection that will survive the criteria, and reading the student's own draft against the published descriptors. The DP2 mock problem is almost always exam technique rather than content, and it is fixed with timed past-paper work and a command-term audit.

Al Nuaimiya sits in the dense middle of Ajman city, a short drive from the Sharjah boundary and within reach of three school clusters: the Ajman schools themselves, the large Sharjah international schools, and a handful of Dubai campuses that families commute to along Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road. That geography matters for the calendar rather than for the tutoring. A child who leaves the house before seven and gets home at half past four cannot start a serious Higher Level session at four. The realistic window in this neighbourhood opens later than it does in Abu Dhabi, and it has to be planned.

This page is written around that timing. It counts the Diploma year backwards from the May session, sets out what the Internal Assessment criteria actually reward, explains where a tutor's role stops under IB academic-honesty rules, and publishes what the Ajman tutoring market charges per month rather than per hour, because a month is the unit families budget in. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE — that service exists only in India — so every session described here happens over live video, with the tutor and student sharing a screen and a worked solution.

One practical note before the calendar itself. Because Al Nuaimiya families commute across three emirates, the session slot that survives a full term is almost never the one first agreed in September. Fix the weekly hour against the student's actual return time rather than against the school's published finish, and leave the Internal Assessment weeks deliberately underbooked, so that a draft deadline never has to displace a Higher Level content session. A timetable built with that slack in it holds through the year; one without it collapses by about week four.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nuaimiya.programmesIntro: Al Nuaimiya families reach IB Gram at three different points on the IB continuum, and the teaching changes at each. The notes below say what the stage demands in an Ajman school year and what a weekly online session realistically covers at that age.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The Primary Years Programme is inquiry-led and reports against learner attributes rather than subject marks, which is why parents often cannot tell whether reading or number fluency is actually behind. Online support at this stage is short, frequent and concrete: number bonds, place value, decoding, sentence construction. Twenty-five to thirty minutes of live one-to-one work twice a week does more at this age than a single long session.
programmes.countryNote: In Ajman the PYP cohort is small, so a parent in Al Nuaimiya comparing their child against classmates has a thin sample to judge by. A diagnostic session gives a clearer reading: a tutor works through graded tasks and reports which specific skill is missing, which is a more useful starting point than a termly attribute report.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The Middle Years Programme marks each subject against four criteria on an eight-point scale, and the criterion that sinks most students is the one about applying knowledge in unfamiliar situations. MYP work also carries the Personal Project in the final year. Online sessions here focus on the criteria language, because a student who cannot tell a describe task from an evaluate task loses marks in work they understood perfectly well.
programmes.countryNote: Al Nuaimiya students who move from MYP into the Diploma, or sideways into IGCSE at a Sharjah school, arrive with strong inquiry habits and thin procedural fluency. The gap is usually algebra and lab write-up discipline. A six to eight week bridging block over the summer closes it before DP1 starts, and it is the single most common booking from this part of Ajman.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma Programme is three Higher Levels, three Standard Levels, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, all running at once. The failure mode is not weakness in one subject; it is a collision of deadlines in the same fortnight. Online tutoring at Diploma level is subject teaching plus scheduling triage, deciding what gets attention this week and what can safely wait.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma candidates living in Al Nuaimiya mostly travel to school in Ajman, Sharjah or Dubai, which compresses the study evening. Sessions for this group are commonly booked between seven and nine in the evening Gulf Standard Time, and the tutor keeps the student's own school submission dates, not a generic IB timeline, as the reference points for each block of work.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nuaimiya.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects Ajman families ask for most, with a note on what the assessment actually rewards. Coverage is by subject and level, so a Higher Level request is matched to a tutor who teaches that level rather than to a generalist.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Heavy on algebraic manipulation, calculus and proof. Higher Level adds Maclaurin series, vectors and harder complex numbers. Marks are lost on unjustified steps rather than wrong answers, so the teaching focus is written method and the twenty-mark exploration.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led work, with a graphical display calculator used throughout. Students who chose it to avoid calculus are surprised by the statistical inference at Higher Level. Sessions concentrate on calculator fluency and interpreting output in context.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The syllabus rewards reasoning from first principles, and the scientific investigation is marked out of 24. Most lost marks sit in uncertainty treatment and in extended-response questions where the student states a law but never applies it to the given situation.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium carry the Higher Level load. The common pattern in Ajman classrooms is confident recall paired with weak calculation discipline: moles set up correctly, significant figures and units dropped at the final line.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the problem rather than difficulty. Students who revise by rereading notes stall around a grade 5. Sessions use retrieval practice against the syllabus understandings and drill the data-analysis questions, which carry disproportionate marks for the time spent.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides grades here. A correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagram earns marks a paragraph of prose cannot. Higher Level adds quantitative questions, and the portfolio of commentaries needs real published articles chosen early rather than hunted the week before.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application is what separates a 4 from a 6: using a decision tree or break-even analysis on the case material instead of defining it. Higher Level sits a pre-released case study, which rewards structured preparation across the months before the paper.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the paper on unseen non-literary texts both reward a clear analytical line rather than wide reading. Teaching focuses on building a thesis in the first minute and sustaining it with close textual evidence under timed conditions.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay are both knowledge-question work, not opinion writing. Students lose marks by arguing a position without identifying the knowledge claim underneath it. Sessions coach the structure and return the drafting to the student.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor in Al Nuaimiya can actually be booked for
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Al Nuaimiya, in the sense most parents mean it, is one named teacher who works with one student on one subject at a fixed weekly time and is accountable for that subject's progress. That is exactly what IB Gram provides. The part that differs from the search phrase is the room: the session happens over live video with a shared screen, not at an Ajman address. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs only in India, and no tutor will be sent to a UAE home.

Stating that plainly is better for the parent than a hedge, because the trade is in your favour. In-home tutoring in the northern emirates is constrained by who happens to live within a reasonable drive. For a Diploma subject at Higher Level, that pool is small. A family in Al Nuaimiya looking for Physics Higher Level or Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level may find two or three candidates locally, and the one who is free on Tuesday evening may not be the one who knows the subject best. Online removes the drive from the equation and leaves only the question of who teaches the subject well.

There is a second, quieter benefit. A tutor who does not travel does not price travel into the hour, and does not lose teaching time to the Sharjah-Ajman evening traffic. The published market figures later on this page show what that premium looks like in AED. For a household running two children through separate subjects, removing travel is often what makes a second subject affordable at all.

What a booking looks like in practice: a short conversation about the subject, level and the deadline you are working to, a free trial lesson with the proposed tutor, and then a fixed weekly slot. If the trial does not work, you say so and the slot is rematched. There is no requirement to commit to a term before seeing a lesson.

sections.heading: The Diploma year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Almost nothing in the IB Diploma is decided in the exam hall. By the time a candidate sits a paper, the Internal Assessment is submitted and marked, the Extended Essay is gone, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition is finished, and the predicted grades that drive university offers are already with the universities. Counting the year backwards from the May session is the only honest way to see where a student actually stands.

The table below is a planning skeleton, not a published timetable. IB session and results dates are set by the International Baccalaureate and by your child's school, and the dates that matter to your family are the ones the school's Diploma coordinator issues: internal draft deadlines, upload windows and mock dates vary from school to school. Treat the school's calendar as authoritative and confirm any IB date with the coordinator or on ibo.org before planning around it.

For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications sat alongside or before the Diploma, the dates are published and firm. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and candidates in the UAE sit those two. The February/March series is offered to India only, so no Ajman family should be planning around it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

One administrative detail catches families who moved emirate or school mid-year. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and the zone determines which version of the timetable applies. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Ask the school's examinations officer which zone your centre sits in rather than reading a timetable found through a search.

sections.heading: Eight weeks, planned properly: what a term block actually achieves
paragraphs: Parents in Al Nuaimiya often ask what a fixed block of tutoring can realistically change. Eight weeks of one well-planned session a week, with practice completed between sessions, is enough to repair two or three specific topics and to change how a student answers a question. It is not enough to cover a Higher Level syllabus that was never learned, and any tutor who says otherwise is selling rather than teaching.

Week one is diagnostic and should feel uncomfortable. The tutor works through graded questions from across the course, not from the current unit, to find where the floor is. A DP2 Chemistry student who cannot reliably convert between moles and concentration will fail energetics questions for reasons that look like energetics and are not. Finding that in week one saves six weeks of treating symptoms.

Weeks two to five rebuild those foundation topics while keeping pace with the school. This is the part that requires the tutor to know what the school is teaching that fortnight, which is why the session plan follows the school's scheme of work rather than a fixed curriculum of its own. The student should be doing twenty to forty minutes of set practice between sessions; without it, the hour is spent re-explaining rather than extending.

Weeks six to eight move to timed work and marking. The student attempts questions under time, the tutor marks against the published scheme, and the two of them read the mark allocation together. The habit being built is reading the command term and the mark total before writing. A six-mark evaluate question answered as a describe question loses most of its marks regardless of how much the student knows, and that is the most common and most fixable loss in the whole Diploma.

sections.heading: Internal assessment criteria, letter by letter
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market names a single Internal Assessment criterion, which is strange, because the criteria are published and they are where the marks are. A student who has read the descriptors for their own subject writes a different piece of work from one who has not, and the difference is usually two or three marks.

The sciences share one scientific investigation, marked out of 24 across four criteria. Mathematics uses a different structure, marked out of 20 across five criteria, and the two that students most often leave empty are the ones about personal engagement and reflection. Those two are not decoration; together they carry a meaningful share of the total, and they cannot be retrofitted into a finished exploration the night before. In the sciences the equivalent blind spot is evaluation, where a limitation has to name a specific methodological weakness and state which direction it pushed the result. Read the descriptors for your own subject once, in the IB's own wording, before the first draft rather than after it.

A tutor's work on an Internal Assessment is to make the criteria legible and to ask the questions the descriptors imply. Has the research design actually controlled the variable it claims to control? Does the data analysis carry uncertainty through the calculation? Does the conclusion answer the research question that was asked, or a more convenient one? That is coaching, and the student does every word of the writing. Under IB academic-honesty rules it could not be otherwise.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an IA, EE or TOK essay
paragraphs: This boundary is worth stating in plain terms, because there are operations in this market selling finished Internal Assessments, and a student who submits one risks a malpractice finding and the loss of the Diploma. IB Gram will not supply assessed work, and no tutor working through the platform may write, redraft to completion or ghost-write any part of a student's submission.

What a tutor can do is substantial. They can teach the underlying content, explain the criteria, discuss a proposed research question, warn that a method will not generate usable data, read a draft the student has written and point to where the argument breaks, model a worked example on a different question, and ask the questions a supervisor would ask. All of that is teaching, and all of it is recorded as feedback on the student's own work.

The practical test is simple: after the session, has the document changed because the student changed it? If the tutor's sentences are in it, the line has been crossed. Supervisors notice, and so do the authentication processes schools run. Parents sometimes find this frustrating in the week before a deadline. It is also the reason the reflection criteria can be answered truthfully, and those criteria carry marks a bought essay cannot earn.

The same rule applies to past papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents. IB Gram does not reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson material. Tutors reference the official publications and link to them, and the school or the official site is where the student obtains them.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the Ajman school calendar and when revision actually happens
paragraphs: Revision plans drawn in October tend to assume the second term runs evenly. In the UAE it does not. Ramadan shortens the school day, shifts energy into the evening, and lands in the part of the year when Diploma candidates are finishing Internal Assessments and starting serious examination practice. A plan that ignores it loses several weeks and then compresses them into the fortnight before the papers.

The workable approach is to decide in advance which weeks are for new learning and which are for consolidation. Reduced school hours free the late morning and early afternoon, and a student who normally has a session at eight in the evening may do better at eleven in the morning. Post-Iftar slots work for some families and are a poor choice for others; the honest answer is that a student who is tired at nine at night will not absorb vector resolution, and the session should move rather than be endured.

Eid breaks and the spring school holiday are the other variable. Both are genuine opportunities for a focused block: three or four longer sessions in a week, on one subject, can clear a backlog that weekly sessions would take a term to reach. They are also the right time to do the unglamorous work of writing out a full set of definitions or working a complete past paper under time, because there is no homework competing for the evening.

Practically, this means a tutoring plan for an Ajman family should be set out against the school's published calendar at the start of the term, with the Ramadan weeks marked as consolidation and one holiday week marked as an intensive block. Agreeing that in advance avoids the conversation in which six weeks have passed and nothing on the plan has moved.

sections.heading: Session timing in Al Nuaimiya and the commuter evening
paragraphs: Al Nuaimiya is one of the more densely populated parts of Ajman, and a large share of working parents here travel to Sharjah or Dubai. That has a direct effect on tutoring: the evening is short, it is shared with siblings, and the hour at which a secondary student can concentrate is later than a timetable would suggest.

Children attending school inside Ajman are generally home by mid-afternoon and can take a four or five o'clock session. Children who travel to a Sharjah or Dubai campus are not, and the drive home along the Emirates Road or through the Sharjah boundary in the evening peak can take far longer than the same journey at midday. For those families the realistic slots are between seven and nine in the evening, and all sessions run in Gulf Standard Time so there is no conversion to get wrong.

Apartment living shapes the session as much as the clock does. A student working at the dining table while a younger sibling does homework next to them will not hold a train of reasoning for an hour. Headphones, a fixed surface and a closed door matter more than equipment. A tablet is workable for discussion and poor for mathematics; a laptop with a separate keyboard, or a cheap graphics tablet for writing out working, changes the quality of a Higher Level maths session noticeably.

Weekend mornings are underused and worth considering. Saturday morning sessions are consistently the most productive slot in this neighbourhood: the student is rested, nothing else is scheduled, and a ninety-minute block is possible in a way it never is on a Tuesday evening. Families running an intensive pre-examination block almost always end up there.

sections.heading: What a month of IB support costs in the Ajman market
paragraphs: Most published tutoring prices in this market are hourly, which is the wrong unit for a family deciding whether to start. The decision is monthly, so the figures below are set out that way first. They are market rates gathered from published provider pricing and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table in October 2026, not IB Gram's price list. IB Gram's own position is a free trial lesson and a quoted rate after the subject, level and frequency are known.

Reading the market monthly makes the structure obvious. A budget online tutor, often a university student, advertises from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, which is a weekly session at somewhere between AED 240 and 600 a month on Bestimate's estimates for a weekly one-hour arrangement. A qualified subject specialist online sits in the AED 150 to 300 band hourly: Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An IB or IGCSE specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and Bestimate putting an examination-year specialist at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and more a month. Premium named tutors go further again, with BartyED publishing AED 650 an hour.

The in-home comparison is where the monthly view earns its keep. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour and home tutors generally at AED 200 to 500, and advertised in-home monthly packages of four two-hour sessions run at AED 1,599 to 1,799 against online packages seen at AED 799 a month for eight sessions. That gap is travel, and in the northern emirates the travel is real: a tutor crossing from Sharjah or Dubai into Ajman in the evening peak is paid for the drive as well as the teaching.

What that means for an Al Nuaimiya household is that the online route typically buys either a better-qualified tutor at the same monthly spend, or a second subject at the same total. For a DP2 student needing both Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level and Chemistry Higher Level, that is the difference between covering one weak subject and covering both.

process.title: Tell us the deadline, not just the subject
process.description: The first conversation is about where your child sits on the calendar: the next school assessment, the Internal Assessment date, the mock window. That determines whether the right booking is a term-long weekly session, a short process-coaching block or a pre-examination sprint.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the proposed tutor
process.description: You meet the tutor who would teach, not a sales call. The lesson is real teaching on a real topic, and the tutor reports afterwards on what they found. If the match is wrong, say so and we rematch; there is no commitment to a term before the trial.

process.title: A diagnostic first block
process.description: The opening sessions deliberately test material from earlier in the course rather than the current unit. The output is a written note naming the specific topics that need rebuilding, which becomes the plan for the following weeks and the reference point for the six-week review.

process.title: Fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time
process.description: A set time each week, confirmed in writing, with the school's own scheme of work as the reference. Session notes follow each lesson so a parent commuting back from Dubai can read what happened rather than ask a tired teenager.

process.title: Review at six weeks against school data
process.description: We compare the plan with the student's school assessment results and change what is not working: frequency, subject focus, or the tutor. A review that only reports progress is not a review, so the six-week conversation includes what has not moved and why.

whyPoints.title: Subject specialists, not the nearest available tutor
whyPoints.description: Matching online means a Higher Level request is answered by someone who teaches that level, rather than by whoever can reach Al Nuaimiya on a Tuesday. For narrow combinations such as Physics Higher Level with Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, that is the whole difference.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page carries the provider or research source that published it and the month it was read. Three of the main competitor pages in this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty treated as a hard line
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, review and give feedback on the student's own work. Nothing is written for the student, and no assessed work is supplied. That is an IB requirement and a protection for your child, whose Diploma is at risk if a submission is not authentically theirs.

whyPoints.title: Planned against your school's calendar
whyPoints.description: The reference dates are the ones your child's Diploma coordinator issued, not a generic IB timeline. Draft deadlines, upload windows and mock dates differ between schools, and a plan built on the wrong set of dates runs a fortnight late all year.

whyPoints.title: Coverage stated honestly, including the gaps
whyPoints.description: If no specialist in a niche subject and level is free for your slot, we say so and give you a realistic match time rather than filling the hour with a generalist. A disclosed gap is more useful to a parent than a confident mismatch.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IB home tutor to an Al Nuaimiya address?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Every session for an Al Nuaimiya family is one-to-one teaching delivered live online over video, with a shared screen for working through problems. The practical effect is that your child is matched to a tutor who teaches their exact subject and level rather than to whoever lives within a reasonable drive of Ajman city. It also removes the travel premium that published in-home rates in this market carry, which is usually what makes a second subject affordable.

faqs.question: How late in the evening can an Al Nuaimiya family book an IB session?
faqs.answer: Later than most families expect, and that is deliberate. Many Al Nuaimiya parents work in Sharjah or Dubai and many students travel to school across the emirate boundary, so the usable study window often does not open until seven. Slots between seven and nine in the evening Gulf Standard Time are common for Diploma students from this neighbourhood. Earlier slots at four or five suit children attending school inside Ajman. If a nine o'clock session is only ever going to produce a tired hour, the better answer is to move the subject to a Saturday morning block instead.

faqs.question: My daughter is in DP1 at a school near Al Nuaimiya - when should her Internal Assessment work start?
faqs.answer: Earlier than the school's final deadline suggests. The proposal and the pilot work belong in DP1, because a research question that cannot generate usable data is a problem you want to discover with a term in hand rather than a fortnight. In the sciences the investigation is marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and research design is decided before any data exists. Ask the subject teacher for the school's internal draft dates and work backwards from those, not from the submission window.

faqs.question: What does a month of weekly IB tutoring cost for an Al Nuaimiya family?
faqs.answer: Market rates rather than ours: on Bestimate's October 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour arrangement, a budget online tutor runs roughly AED 240 to 600 a month, a mid-range qualified tutor AED 600 to 1,200, and an examination-year specialist AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. Advertised in-home packages of four two-hour sessions sit at AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month against online packages seen at AED 799 for eight sessions. IB Gram quotes after a free trial, once the subject, level and frequency are settled.

faqs.question: Which exam series do IB and Cambridge students living in Al Nuaimiya sit?
faqs.answer: IB Diploma candidates at UAE schools sit the May session, and your child's school confirms the exact dates through its Diploma coordinator. For Cambridge qualifications, candidates in the UAE sit the June series and the November series; the February/March series is offered to India only, so no Ajman family should plan around it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones, and the zone decides which timetable applies, so ask the school's examinations officer which zone yours is in.

faqs.question: Can my son keep IB lessons going during Ramadan in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the timetable rewritten rather than simply reduced. School hours shorten, which frees the late morning and early afternoon, and for many students those hours are better than a post-Iftar slot for anything demanding. The sensible pattern is to mark the Ramadan weeks as consolidation rather than new content, keep the session but move it to the time the student is actually alert, and use an Eid or holiday week for a concentrated block on one subject. Deciding this at the start of the term avoids losing the weeks altogether.

faqs.question: Who regulates the private schools my child in Al Nuaimiya might attend?
faqs.answer: Private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which u.ae describes as playing a pivotal role in that oversight. Dubai schools answer to KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to ADEK, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge. If your child commutes to a Sharjah or Dubai campus, the regulator that matters is the one for the school's emirate, not the one for your home address, and inspection reports are published by that authority.

faqs.question: Is eight weeks enough time to fix a falling IB Maths grade?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks of one well-planned weekly session, with practice done between sessions, is enough to repair two or three specific topics and to change how questions are answered. It is not enough to cover a Higher Level syllabus that was never learned. The first session should be diagnostic across the whole course rather than the current unit, because a student failing calculus questions often has an algebra problem underneath. What moves fastest is written method and command-term discipline, and those are habits rather than content.

faqs.question: Can an IB tutor help with the Extended Essay without writing any of it?
faqs.answer: That is the only form of help available, and it is more useful than it sounds. A tutor can discuss whether a research question is answerable in four thousand words, warn that a source base will not support the argument, read a draft the student has written and show where the reasoning breaks, and ask the questions a supervisor will ask at the next meeting. What they will not do is supply sentences. If the tutor's writing appears in the essay, the submission is no longer the student's own work and the Diploma itself is at risk.

faqs.question: What happens if no IB Physics HL specialist is free for our Al Nuaimiya slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you, give a realistic match time, and offer the alternatives rather than filling the hour with a generalist. Narrow combinations at Higher Level are the ones where availability genuinely bites, particularly for a fixed evening slot during examination term. Options usually include a slightly different time, a short block with a specialist at lower frequency, or starting with the subject where a specialist is available now. A disclosed gap lets you plan; a confident mismatch costs a term before anyone admits it.

faqs.question: How many marks does the science Internal Assessment carry in the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: The scientific investigation is marked out of 24, split evenly across four criteria at six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Mathematics is structured differently, with the exploration marked out of 20 across presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. The criteria are published, and reading the descriptors for your child's own subject before the work starts is the single cheapest improvement available. Students who have never read them lose marks in evaluation and reflection for reasons they could easily have avoided.

faqs.question: Do we need to live in Dubai to get a strong IB tutor from Al Nuaimiya?
faqs.answer: No, and that is the point of delivering lessons online. The constraint on in-home tutoring in the northern emirates is geographic: the pool is whoever can drive to your address at the time you need. Online, the pool is everyone who teaches that subject at that level and is free at your slot. For a family in Al Nuaimiya needing something narrow, such as Economics Higher Level or Mathematics Applications and Interpretation Higher Level, that difference decides whether the match is a specialist or a compromise.

faqs.question: Will the tutor follow my child's own school deadlines rather than a generic plan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we ask for those dates before the first session. Internal draft deadlines, upload windows and mock examination dates differ between schools, and a plan built on a generic IB timeline tends to run a fortnight behind the one the student is actually judged against. The tutor works from the school's scheme of work and the coordinator's published dates, and the session note after each lesson references them. If the school changes a date, the plan changes with it rather than after it.

faqs.question: How does the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency process treat an IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is run by the Ministry of Education, not by any tutoring provider, and the requirements differ by curriculum. For the British track the published rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. We do not publish an IB points threshold, because no figure for the IB track has been read on a Ministry source. Check moe.gov.ae or the attestation authority directly before relying on any number.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nuaimiya.closingHeading: Work out the deadline first, then book the trial
ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nuaimiya.closingBody: If you are searching for an IB home tutor in Al Nuaimiya, the most useful thing you can do in the next ten minutes is write down three dates: the next school assessment, the next Internal Assessment deadline, and the mock window. Those decide whether your child needs a term-long weekly session, a short process-coaching block or a pre-examination sprint. Bring those dates to the first conversation, take the free trial lesson with the proposed tutor, and judge the match on the teaching rather than on a sales call. Lessons run live online, one-to-one, in Gulf Standard Time, and the slot is yours to change if it stops working.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-rashidiya-ajma.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma and Middle Years subjects to students across Ajman and the Northern Emirates. Each profile names the subject and the level taught, because a Mathematics AA HL teacher and a Mathematics AI SL teacher are not interchangeable, however similar the course titles look on a school report.

intro.heading: The school run decides the lesson, not the other way round
paragraphs: Al Rashidiya sits close to the older centre of Ajman, within a few minutes of Sheikh Rashid Bin Humaid Street and a short run from the Sharjah border. Very few families here send their children to a school inside the neighbourhood itself. The IB students living in Al Rashidiya are generally bussed out: to Ajman Academy in the newer western communities, or south across the emirate line to the International Baccalaureate schools clustered in Sharjah and Muwaileh. That single fact shapes everything about tutoring here.

A bus that leaves school at 2.45pm and threads back through the Sharjah-Ajman corridor does not reach Al Rashidiya at 3.10pm. On an ordinary Tuesday it arrives somewhere between 3.50pm and 4.40pm, and on a day with rain or a closure on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road it can be later still. A student who walks in at 4.30pm needs to eat, change and decompress before anything cognitive happens. The honest earliest start for a Diploma lesson in this neighbourhood is around 5.30pm, and the realistic sweet spot is 6.30pm to 8pm.

That window is exactly where in-home tutoring in the Northern Emirates falls apart. A tutor who lives in Ajman and travels to homes can serve perhaps three students an evening, and they will be the three closest to each other. A tutor who happens to specialise in Biology HL and lives in Al Nuaimiya is not going to drive to Al Rashidiya for a single hour, and a tutor who does drive is charging for the journey whether the invoice says so or not. The pool shrinks to whoever is nearby and free, which is a poor way to choose someone to teach Paper 3.

IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; the in-home service exists only in India. For an Al Rashidiya family the lesson happens on live video, one tutor and one student, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own past paper on screen. The practical effect is that the pool stops being geographic. A Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL teacher who has taught the course for years can take the 6.45pm slot, and the travel time that would have cost AED 60 to AED 120 of somebody's evening goes back into the lesson.

This page is written for the parent doing the arithmetic on a Sunday evening: which night, which subject, how many weeks, and what it costs. It names the schools Al Rashidiya children actually attend, sets out when a session can start without wrecking sleep, gives the Ajman and Northern Emirates rate bands that nobody else publishes, and explains what the Ministry of Education oversight of Ajman private schools does and does not mean for a tutoring plan. It also states plainly what an IB tutor is allowed to do with an Internal Assessment, which is the single most misunderstood part of Diploma support in this market.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-rashidiya-ajma.programmesIntro: Al Rashidiya families reach the Diploma by several routes: through an IB Primary Years and Middle Years school in Ajman, through a British-curriculum primary followed by a move into MYP, or straight from IGCSE into DP1. Each entry point leaves a different gap, and the programme notes below describe what that gap looks like for a student travelling from this part of Ajman.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than discrete subject syllabuses. Children research, document and present, and assessment is largely formative: portfolios, learning journals, an exhibition in the final year. Parents moving in from a textbook-and-test system often read the absence of weekly marks as an absence of rigour, which it is not. What it does mean is that number fluency and written stamina have to be watched deliberately, because nothing in the structure forces them to the surface.
programmes.countryNote: Al Rashidiya children in PYP are usually at Ajman Academy or at a Sharjah IB primary, which means a bus run of thirty to fifty minutes each way. Tutoring at this age works best in short evening blocks of thirty to forty minutes, twice a week, aimed at arithmetic recall and reading fluency. Longer sessions after a long commute produce tears, not progress.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP assessment runs on four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and reported as a 1-7 grade after a published conversion. Criterion A is usually knowledge and understanding; the later criteria reward investigation, communication and reflection. Students who are strong on content and weak on process score worse than their parents expect, because three of the four criteria are about how the work was done. The Personal Project in the final year is the first genuinely independent piece of work most students meet.
programmes.countryNote: For Ajman students the MYP years are where the commute starts to bite. A Year 10 student losing ninety minutes a day to the bus has less time than a classmate living in Muwaileh, and the first thing that gets dropped is the reflective write-up rather than the content. Evening sessions here concentrate on criterion language and on getting investigations planned before they are attempted.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internally assessed component worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of the grade, and the written papers are sat in a single window. The Diploma punishes drift: a student who is behind in October of DP2 is behind on four separate internal deadlines at once, because the IA, the Extended Essay and the TOK exhibition all land within weeks of each other.
programmes.countryNote: Al Rashidiya DP students are typically travelling furthest at the point when they can least afford the time. Two evening sessions a week, each on a different subject, is the pattern that holds through DP1; in DP2 most families here move to three and then taper after the mock window. The schedule is built around the bus, not around a notional 4pm start that never happens.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs two or more Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a service-learning strand. It is far less common in the UAE than the full Diploma, and families often discover it only when a school suggests it as an alternative for a student struggling to carry three Higher Levels. The academic demand in the DP courses taken is identical to the full Diploma; what changes is the breadth and the core.
programmes.countryNote: No Ajman school is a large CP provider, so students here who follow it usually do so at a Sharjah or Dubai school after a late transfer. Support is almost always for the two or three Diploma courses inside the programme, taught exactly as they would be for a full Diploma candidate, with separate time for the reflective project.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-rashidiya-ajma.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones Ajman and Northern Emirates families ask about most for Diploma and upper-MYP support. Each entry says what the course actually assesses and where marks go missing, because the gap between a 5 and a 6 is almost never a gap in effort.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency, calculus and proof. At Higher Level the third paper is an extended investigation and rewards students who can sustain an argument over several pages rather than answer in fragments. Marks are lost in the middle of long questions, where a correct method is abandoned because the numbers look ugly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use. The graphical display calculator is assumed, not optional, and students who treat it as a last resort run out of time. The exploration here usually needs real data, and the commonest failure is a dataset too small to carry any statistical claim the student then makes about it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, fields, thermodynamics and the HL extension into quantum and nuclear topics. Multiple choice rewards precision about definitions; the long papers reward unit discipline and sketch graphs. The internal assessment fails most often on uncertainty treatment, which is the part school practicals rarely have time to teach properly.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, energetics, equilibrium, acids and bases, organic and the HL extensions. Organic mechanisms are where Northern Emirates students most often report feeling lost, usually because curly-arrow notation was learned as decoration rather than as a claim about electron movement. Data-based questions need practice separate from content revision.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cell biology, genetics, ecology, physiology and the HL depth in plant biology and neurobiology. The subject looks memorisable and is not: command terms do the work, and a student who answers 'explain' questions with a description loses marks they genuinely earned the knowledge for. Statistical handling in the IA is a recurring weak point.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, the global economy and the HL quantitative extension. Diagram accuracy carries real marks, and most lost marks sit in unlabelled axes or a shift drawn in the wrong direction. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries on published news articles, and article choice determines the ceiling before any writing happens.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Organisational structure, human resources, finance, marketing and operations. The case-study paper is unseen at SL and pre-released at HL, which changes the preparation entirely. Students lose marks by describing a tool rather than applying it to the stimulus in front of them, and by ignoring the mark allocation on evaluation questions.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Non-literary and literary texts studied together, assessed through a guided analysis paper, a comparative essay, the individual oral and, at HL, a formal essay. The individual oral is where preparation pays most, because the global issue has to be genuinely arguable rather than a theme restated as a question.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Productive and receptive skills across five prescribed themes, with assessment through listening, reading, writing and an individual oral. For residents of Ajman this sits alongside the Ministry's mandatory Arabic requirement at school, and the two are not the same course. Tutoring usually targets writing register and the oral, which carry the most transferable gain.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Systems fundamentals, computational thinking, abstract data structures at HL, and a solution developed as the internal assessment. Students arrive able to code and unable to document, and the IA marks sit heavily in planning and criteria-driven evaluation rather than in the quality of the program itself.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-rashidiya-ajma.regionsTitle: Al Rashidiya and the neighbourhoods around it
ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-rashidiya-ajma.regionsIntro: Al Rashidiya is one of several Ajman communities whose children travel out to school, and each has its own commute arithmetic. The notes below describe what the evening looks like from each, because that is what decides which slot a family should book.

regions.name: Al Rashidiya
regions.note: Close to the old centre and the Corniche approach, with easy access to Sheikh Rashid Bin Humaid Street. Buses to Sharjah IB schools leave early and return between 3.50pm and 4.40pm. Lessons book best from 6pm.

regions.name: Al Nuaimiya
regions.note: Dense, apartment-heavy and the most central of the Ajman residential districts. Shorter school runs for Ajman-based schools, but heavy afternoon traffic around the university area pushes arrivals later than the distance suggests.

regions.name: Al Jurf
regions.note: Industrial and institutional in parts, residential in others, with the Ajman courts and several clinics nearby. Families here are often split between Ajman and Sharjah schools, so sibling slots rarely line up without planning.

regions.name: Al Rawda
regions.note: Villa communities spread across Al Rawda 1, 2 and 3, popular with families working in Sharjah. The run to Muwaileh schools is short in the morning and slow in the afternoon, which is why 6.30pm starts dominate here.

regions.name: Al Zorah
regions.note: Low-density waterfront development on the northern lagoon, with longer drives to every school in the emirate. Students here lose the most time to transport and gain the most from an online slot that starts the minute they are home.

regions.name: Emirates City
regions.note: High-rise towers near Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, with a young resident population and a mix of curricula. Road access is good, so afternoon arrivals are earlier than in the older districts and 5.30pm sessions are workable.

regions.name: Al Mowaihat
regions.note: Three villa sub-communities west of the city centre, closest to Ajman Academy. Short bus runs make this the one part of Ajman where a 5pm Diploma session is genuinely realistic on most weekdays.

regions.name: Ajman Corniche
regions.note: Seafront apartments and hotels along the beach road, popular with teaching and medical families. Parking and congestion around the Corniche in the early evening make a video lesson considerably simpler than a visitor.

schoolClusters.city: Ajman schools serving Al Rashidiya
schoolClusters.note: Ajman's private schools sit under federal Ministry of Education supervision rather than an emirate-level authority, and the International Baccalaureate provision inside the emirate is concentrated in a small number of schools to the west of the city. Students we support from Al Rashidiya attend the schools below.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and Muwaileh schools on the Al Rashidiya bus routes
schoolClusters.note: Because the Sharjah border is a few minutes from Al Rashidiya, a large share of Diploma candidates living here are enrolled in Sharjah, where private education is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Bus runs along the Maliha and University City roads set the family's evening timetable.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-rashidiya-ajma.modesIntro: Three shapes of support cover almost every request that comes from this part of Ajman. The difference between them is not the quality of the teaching but how the week is organised around the bus, the mock window and the internal deadlines.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, built around the bus
modes.description: One subject, one tutor, the same slot each week, scheduled after the realistic arrival time rather than the timetabled one. Most Al Rashidiya families run two subjects on two separate evenings in DP1 and add a third in DP2. The tutor keeps the student's own school assessment calendar, so the lesson before a school test is a test-preparation lesson.
bullets: Sixty or ninety minute sessions, 5.30pm to 9.30pm Gulf Standard Time
Same tutor each week, with a named replacement if illness intervenes
Work set between lessons is marked before the next one

modes.title: Internal assessment and Extended Essay coaching
modes.description: Structured sessions on the student's own draft: research question, method, criterion-by-criterion review and a plan for the next revision. The tutor reads, questions and annotates. The student writes every word that is submitted, which is both an IB academic-honesty requirement and the only version of this support worth buying.

modes.title: Intensive blocks in the run-up to the written papers
modes.description: Short, dense sequences of sessions aimed at one paper or one weak topic, usually booked during the Ajman school holidays or in the weeks after mocks. Each block starts with a diagnostic on a past paper under timed conditions and ends with the same paper type re-sat, so the parent can see what moved and what did not.
bullets: Three to five sessions a week over a defined fortnight

sections.heading: What a search for an IB home tutor in Al Rashidiya actually returns
paragraphs: Type the phrase into Google from an Ajman connection and the first page is mostly Dubai. Agencies list Al Rashidiya in a footer of forty neighbourhood names, quote no rate, and route the enquiry to a sales line. One or two results are genuine independent tutors, and a handful are classified listings of uncertain age. Almost nothing on that first page tells you what an hour costs, who is permitted to teach privately in the UAE, or whether anybody actually covers Higher Level Physics within driving distance of your building.

The underlying difficulty is supply. Ajman is a small emirate with a modest number of International Baccalaureate candidates, and Diploma teaching is subject-and-level specific in a way that general tutoring is not. A teacher who can carry a Year 9 science class confidently is not automatically able to teach the HL options or mark against the IA criteria. The number of people within a twenty-minute drive of Al Rashidiya who can do that for a given subject is small, and in some subjects it is effectively zero.

So the honest answer to the search is a reframing. The thing a parent in Al Rashidiya wants is not a person in a car; it is a specialist in that subject at that level, available at the hour their child is actually home and awake. Removing the travel requirement is what makes the specialist findable. Everything else on this page follows from that: the timings, the rate comparison, and the explanation of what the lesson looks like when it happens over live video with a shared screen rather than across a dining table.

A reasonable way to test the claim is the trial. One lesson, free, on a topic the student is currently stuck on, with no payment details collected first. If the online format does not work for that particular child, an hour has been spent finding out rather than a term's fees.
bullets: Most results for the phrase are Dubai agencies with no published rate
Diploma teaching is level-specific; a general tutor is not a substitute
Removing travel is what makes a Higher Level specialist reachable from Ajman
The trial lesson is the cheapest test of whether the format suits the child

sections.heading: The Al Rashidiya school run, hour by hour
paragraphs: The timings below are the ones families in this part of Ajman report, and they are the reason a tutoring plan built on a 4pm start fails within a fortnight. School end times in the UAE cluster in the early afternoon, but the bus does not arrive when school ends. It loads, it waits, it works through a route, and for Al Rashidiya children attending a Sharjah or western-Ajman school that route is long.

Note what happens to the evening on the longest runs. A student who reaches home at 4.40pm, eats at 5.15pm and starts school homework at 5.45pm has no serious capacity before 7pm. Booking them at 5pm produces a tired hour of poor work and an argument. Booking them at 7pm produces a lesson. The same student in the Al Mowaihat villas, ten minutes from Ajman Academy, can genuinely work at 5pm, which is why two families in the same emirate need different slots.

Friday and Saturday behave differently again. The UAE weekend leaves Saturday morning as the single best block of the week for Extended Essay and Internal Assessment work, because it is the only time a Diploma student is both rested and unhurried. Families who move their coursework session to a 10am Saturday slot usually report that the writing finally starts moving, having tried and failed to do the same work at 8pm on a Wednesday.

During Ramadan the whole structure shifts. School days shorten, the afternoon is low-energy, and the productive hours move to after Iftar. Sessions commonly run from about 9pm, and some families pause entirely for the month and compensate with a fortnight of intensive work afterwards. Either approach works; what does not work is pretending the ordinary schedule still applies.

sections.heading: Why the local tutor pool thins out at Higher Level
paragraphs: There is no shortage of people offering tuition in Ajman. There is a shortage of people who have taught a specific Diploma course at a specific level recently enough to know how it is marked. Those two things are easy to confuse when a listing says only 'IB tutor, all subjects', which is a phrase that should prompt a question rather than a booking.

Consider what a Physics HL student needs. The tutor has to be comfortable with the option topic the school chose, with the uncertainty and error analysis that the internal assessment lives or dies on, and with the multiple-choice paper's habit of punishing a loose definition. Within a short drive of Al Rashidiya, the set of people who meet that description and are free at 7pm on a Thursday is very small. Across the whole set of teachers who teach that course online in this time zone, it is not small at all.

The same logic applies with more force to the thinly taught subjects. Economics HL, Computer Science, Arabic B at Higher Level, Music, Global Politics: a neighbourhood is simply the wrong unit of search for any of them. Families who insist on proximity in these subjects usually end up with a generalist, and the generalist teaches the content well enough while missing the assessment craft that the grade actually turns on.

Where IB Gram cannot match a subject at the level requested, the position is stated rather than filled with whoever is available. A parent is told that the Thursday 7pm slot for that particular Higher Level course is not covered this term, with an estimate of when it will be. That is less satisfying than a quick yes, and considerably less expensive than six weeks of the wrong teaching.
bullets: 'All subjects, all levels' is a claim no single Diploma teacher can support
Option-topic choice varies by school and changes what the tutor must know
Thinly taught subjects are the ones proximity hurts most
An honest 'not available this term' is part of the service

sections.heading: Online lessons against an in-home visit, for a family in this neighbourhood
paragraphs: The comparison below is specific to Al Rashidiya rather than general. The variables that matter here are the distance from the Sharjah border, the congestion on the approach roads in the early evening, and the small local pool of Diploma specialists. In a dense Dubai community with many IB teachers living nearby, some of these rows would read differently.

The travel premium is the row parents underestimate. Market rates for in-home one-to-one visits in the UAE are quoted roughly between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour depending on level and provider, and the upper half of that band is largely the journey. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts in-home sessions at AED 180 to AED 350, with specialist in-home tutors quoted up to AED 500. None of that money reaches the teaching.

The second row parents underestimate is cancellation. A tutor who drives loses an evening if a lesson falls through, so cancellation terms tend to be strict and reschedules are hard. An online slot can be moved to the following evening without anybody absorbing a lost journey, which matters in a household where a school trip or a sibling's fixture can take out a Tuesday without warning.

What an in-home visit genuinely offers is physical presence, which helps a small number of students a great deal: very young children, some students with specific additional needs, and anyone who cannot be kept at a desk without an adult in the room. IB Gram does not provide home visits in the UAE at all, and a family in that position is better served by a local in-home tutor than by a format that will not suit the child.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs in Ajman and the Northern Emirates
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages for these searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not the currency any family here transacts in. The bands below are market rates in dirhams, collected from published competitor pages and from Bestimate's Dubai tutoring rate table. They are not IB Gram's price list; they are what the market charges, so that a quote can be judged against something.

Read the table from the bottom up rather than the top down. The premium band at AED 500 and above exists, and BartyED publishes AED 650 an hour; what it buys is a named individual with an examining or elite-school background, and for most students it is not the constraint on the grade. The band that matters for a Diploma student in Ajman is the AED 150 to AED 300 qualified-subject-tutor range, where the variable is whether the person has taught that course at that level.

Ajman rates generally sit at or slightly below the Dubai bands, for the ordinary reason that local in-home tutors here charge less than those serving Downtown or Emirates Hills. Online rates do not vary by emirate, because the delivery cost does not. That is one of the quieter advantages of the format for a Northern Emirates family: the price of a specialist is the same from Al Rashidiya as it is from Jumeirah.

Monthly arithmetic is more useful than hourly. Packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run from AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. A two-subject Diploma plan is therefore a four-figure monthly commitment, and worth planning as one.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school in Ajman, and what that means for tutoring
paragraphs: Ajman is one of the emirates where private schools are supervised federally rather than by an emirate-level authority. The UAE government's own guidance states that the Ministry of Education 'plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in the emirates of Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah'. Dubai has the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi has the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge.

This matters for an Al Rashidiya family in a practical way, because many children here cross into Sharjah for school. A student at a Sharjah school is in a system where the authority approves 'tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods', while a sibling at an Ajman school sits under federal supervision. Inspection reporting, fee approval and complaint routes differ accordingly, and the right office to contact depends on which side of the border the school stands.

What no regulator does is certify a private tutor's subject competence. The regulatory question about tutoring in the UAE is a labour one: an individual giving private lessons needs a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

So when an advertisement describes tutors as approved by a regulator, treat it as a warning sign rather than a credential. A permit is a work authorisation, not an endorsement of teaching quality, and a Ministry or authority endorsement of a private tutoring business is not a thing that exists in the form these advertisements imply. IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation and does not claim one; what can be asked of any tutor, anywhere, is which course and level they have taught and how recently.
bullets: Ajman private schools: federal Ministry of Education supervision
Sharjah schools: Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves fees and curricula
Private tuition work permit: MoHRE, free for two years, under Resolution No. 710 of 2023
