sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: Every family in Ajman running an international curriculum is also running a second, mandatory curriculum, and it is the part of the week most tutoring conversations skip. Federal rules require private schools to teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies regardless of the international curriculum they are licensed for. The requirement is not a formality; it occupies timetable hours and it generates marks on a report card that a Diploma student still has to carry.

The Dubai regulator's published guidance on mandatory subjects is the clearest statement of how this works in practice anywhere in the UAE, and the principles it describes apply broadly. Schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are explicitly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language.

Instructional time in that guidance is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with schools permitted to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advice that no mandatory-subject lesson should run under 25 minutes. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic need the appropriate subject approval from the regulator in Dubai. The guidance also states that using different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is prohibited, which is a real constraint on what any tutor can legitimately bring to these subjects.

For a Diploma student in Al Rashidiya the implication is narrow and useful. Arabic support is worth buying where the student is at risk of a weak school grade or is taking Arabic B as a Diploma language, and it should work with the school's own material rather than substituting a parallel syllabus. Islamic Education and Social Studies tutoring, where a family wants it, is revision support for the school's prescribed content, not an alternative course.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an Internal Assessment
paragraphs: This is the boundary that decides whether tutoring helps a Diploma student or endangers them. Every Diploma subject has an internally assessed component, worth somewhere between a fifth and a quarter of the subject grade, and all of it must be the student's own work. A tutor who supplies text, rewrites paragraphs to a finished state, or hands over a research question with a method attached has produced a malpractice problem rather than a better mark.

There is an active market in exactly that. One site found in this search segment sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. For the student, submitting purchased work is an academic-honesty breach with consequences up to the loss of the Diploma, and the detection route is mundane: a supervisor who has watched a student work all year can tell when the voice changes. The purchase is also unnecessary, because the parts of the IA where marks are genuinely lost are teachable.

What legitimate support looks like is narrower and more effective. The tutor reads the student's draft and asks where the data supports the claim. They explain what the criterion descriptors mean in that subject, because 'personal engagement' and 'evaluation' are technical terms with specific evidence requirements. They teach uncertainty treatment in a science IA and statistical choice in a biology or economics one. They push a research question down to something answerable in the word count, which is the single most common cause of a capped mark.

The same boundary applies to the Extended Essay and to Theory of Knowledge. A tutor can teach the structure of a knowledge claim, interrogate a weak counterclaim, and show a student how to read their own paragraph as an examiner would. A tutor cannot write it, and should decline if asked. Being told no on this point is a sign the service is worth keeping.
bullets: The internal assessment is worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of each subject grade
Criterion descriptors are technical; most lost marks sit there, not in content
Buying completed coursework risks the Diploma itself
A tutor who declines to draft for a student is doing the job correctly

process.title: Tell us the bus time, not the school time
process.description: The first question is when your child is actually home on each weekday, which school they travel from, and which evenings are already committed. For Al Rashidiya families this is the information that determines whether a slot will survive past the second week, and it is more useful to us than any other detail.

process.title: Name the subject and the level precisely
process.description: Mathematics AA HL, Chemistry SL, Economics HL: the level and the route change which teacher is right. If you are not sure which Mathematics course your child is on, the school report or the subject teacher will say, and it is worth confirming before the first lesson is booked.

process.title: Free trial lesson in the slot you want
process.description: One lesson, at no charge and with no payment details collected, scheduled in the evening slot you intend to keep. The tutor works on something your child is currently stuck on rather than giving a general assessment, so the hour produces an opinion you can act on either way.

process.title: Agree the weekly rhythm and the deadlines
process.description: After the trial you confirm the slot, the frequency and whether the term includes internal-assessment work. We take your child's school assessment calendar so the session before a school test is spent on that test, and so coursework deadlines are not met with a surprise.

process.title: Review at the end of the first half-term
process.description: A short written note on what has moved, what has not, and whether the plan should change. Most Al Rashidiya families adjust something at this point: a different evening, a second subject, or a shift from weekly teaching to a pre-mock intensive block.

whyPoints.title: Timings set by the Northern Emirates commute
whyPoints.description: Slots run to 9.30pm because the bus from Sharjah does not get a child home at 3.15pm. A plan built on honest arrival times survives the term; one built on timetabled end-of-school times collapses in the second fortnight and takes the parent's goodwill with it.

whyPoints.title: Specialists matched by level, not by distance
whyPoints.description: The Higher Level option topic your child's school chose determines who can teach them properly. Searching a time zone rather than a twenty-minute radius is what makes that person findable from Ajman, and it is the whole argument for the online format on this page.

whyPoints.title: Rates you can check against the market
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, so you can compare any quote you receive, including ours, against something external. Three of the best-ranked pages for these searches publish no price at all.

whyPoints.title: A stated boundary on coursework
whyPoints.description: The internal assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay are taught, questioned and reviewed, never drafted. This is a hard rule rather than a preference, and it protects the one thing a Diploma student cannot replace if it goes wrong.

whyPoints.title: Honest answers about coverage
whyPoints.description: If no specialist in your subject and level is free in the slot you need, you are told so with a realistic estimate, rather than matched with a generalist. Availability transparency is the item no competitor page in this segment discloses.

whyPoints.title: No office, no claimed accreditation
whyPoints.description: IB Gram has no UAE premises and holds no regulator approval, and says so. The permit that applies to private tutoring in the UAE is a labour authorisation from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and no authority certifies a tutoring company's teaching quality.

faqs.question: Can a Diploma session start before 5pm if my child studies in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and it is usually a false economy. A bus from a Muwaileh or University City school reaches Al Rashidiya between about 3.50pm and 4.30pm, and a Diploma student needs food and a break before anything demanding. A 4.30pm or 5pm start produces a tired hour. Families who try it almost always move the slot within a fortnight. The exception is a student driven home directly or attending a school in western Ajman, where 5pm works. If an early slot is the only option, make it the shorter homework-support session rather than the Higher Level teaching one.

faqs.question: Which schools do IB students living in Al Rashidiya usually attend?
faqs.answer: Inside Ajman, Ajman Academy is the main International Baccalaureate provider, and families here also use Ajman Modern School, GEMS Cambridge International School, Habitat School Ajman, Al Ameer English School and Ajman Private School in Al Nuaimiya for other curricula. A large share of Diploma candidates living in Al Rashidiya travel into Sharjah, to schools such as Victoria International School of Sharjah, Scholars International Academy, Australian International School and The Millennium School. We name these as context for the neighbourhood, not as an affiliation of any kind.

faqs.question: How late can a weekday lesson run for a DP2 student in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Our latest regular weekday slot starts at 9.30pm Gulf Standard Time, though few DP2 students should be doing new teaching at that hour on a school night. A 9.30pm session works well for a short review or a timed question set; it works badly for a difficult new topic. During Ramadan the picture reverses, and post-Iftar slots from around 9pm become the most productive of the day. Outside Ramadan, our advice to Al Rashidiya families is to keep the demanding subject at 6.30pm or 7pm and use the late slot only for consolidation.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a home tutor to an Al Rashidiya address?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; the home-tutoring service exists only in India. Lessons for Ajman families are delivered live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own papers on screen. The page is titled for the phrase parents search, and the honest answer is that the substance of what you want, a subject specialist teaching your child one-to-one at a convenient hour, is delivered without anybody travelling. If physical presence is essential for your child, a local in-home tutor is the better route.

faqs.question: How long should a one-to-one Diploma lesson be for a Year 12 student?
faqs.answer: Sixty minutes for weekly subject teaching, ninety when the session includes timed past-paper work that has to be attempted and then reviewed in the same sitting. Ninety minutes is too long for a student who has just come off a long bus run, which is another reason the start time matters more than the duration. Internal assessment sessions are usually sixty minutes, because they are discussion and annotation rather than new content. Younger students in the Middle Years Programme do better with forty-five minutes twice a week than ninety minutes once.

faqs.question: What happens to our schedule during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: School days shorten, afternoons are low-energy, and the usable study hours move to after Iftar. Most Ajman families either shift sessions to roughly 9pm onwards or pause for the month and book an intensive block afterwards. Both work. What does not work is leaving a 6.30pm slot in place and hoping. We ask families to tell us their preference a couple of weeks ahead so tutor availability can be arranged, because the late-evening slots fill quickly across the Gulf during that period.

faqs.question: Is two subjects a week too much for a DP1 student in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Two is the usual starting point and it is manageable for most DP1 students, provided they fall on separate evenings and neither sits immediately after a long bus run. The load becomes a problem when a third subject is added without dropping anything else, or when internal assessment work starts and nothing is moved to make room. For a student losing ninety minutes a day to the commute, two subjects plus protected coursework time on Saturday morning is a more realistic plan than three weekday sessions.

faqs.question: Who supervises the private school my child attends in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Private schools in Ajman are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which the UAE government describes as playing a pivotal role in overseeing private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. If your child crosses into Sharjah for school, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education there and also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Dubai schools fall under the Knowledge and Human Development Authority and Abu Dhabi schools under the Department of Education and Knowledge. The route for a fee query or a complaint depends on which of these applies.

faqs.question: What does the Ajman to Sharjah commute do to a 4pm start?
faqs.answer: It usually removes it. The approach roads between Ajman and Sharjah congest from the middle of the afternoon, and a bus route that collects from several communities adds further time. A student whose school day ends at 2.45pm can reach Al Rashidiya at 4.30pm. Any plan whose first lesson is at 4pm is really a plan for a lesson that starts late, ends late and runs on a tired student. The fix is simple: book the slot that matches the arrival time you actually observe over a normal week.

faqs.question: Can a younger sibling in the Middle Years Programme share the same weekly slot?
faqs.answer: Not the same slot, because lessons are one-to-one and the two students need different teaching. What does work is consecutive slots on the same evening with different tutors, which keeps the household to one disrupted evening rather than two. Many Al Rashidiya families run a Middle Years session at 5.30pm and a Diploma session at 7pm on the same night. The younger student also benefits from the shorter format, usually forty-five minutes, which fits neatly before the older one starts.

faqs.question: What should an Al Rashidiya parent send us before the trial?
faqs.answer: Three things are enough: the most recent school report or assessment feedback, the current unit or topic list from the subject teacher, and a piece of the student's own recent work, ideally something that was marked. For a Diploma student also send the school's internal assessment deadline dates if you have them. That gives the tutor the starting point rather than spending the free trial lesson discovering it. No school records, photographs or grade histories are needed beyond this.

faqs.question: Will the tutor follow my child's own school deadlines?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the main reason we ask for the school assessment calendar at the start. The session before a school test is spent on that test; the weeks before an internal assessment deadline are spent on the draft the supervisor is expecting. A tutor working to a generic revision plan while the school runs its own calendar wastes half the value of the lesson. If your child's school changes a deadline, telling us the same week means the plan moves with it.

faqs.question: What if no Higher Level specialist is free in our preferred slot?
faqs.answer: You will be told that directly, with an estimate of when the slot is likely to open and an alternative evening if one exists. For some combinations, a Higher Level option topic in a thinly taught subject at a popular hour, the honest answer in a given term is no. Being matched with a generalist instead would cost you six weeks and teach your child the content without the assessment craft that the grade turns on. No page in this search segment discloses a coverage limit; this one does.

faqs.question: Is the free trial lesson conditional on anything?
faqs.answer: It is one lesson, at no charge, with no card or payment details collected beforehand and no obligation to continue. The conditions are only that it is a single session, that it is used for teaching rather than as a general assessment interview, and that it is booked in a slot where a specialist in your subject is actually available. If no specialist is free, we say so rather than offering a trial with somebody else and hoping the subject question does not come up.

faqs.question: Do Cambridge and Pearson candidates in Ajman sit the same exam series?
faqs.answer: Broadly, yes. Cambridge International runs its IGCSE and A Level examinations in a June series and a November series for candidates in the UAE, and the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Diploma candidates at Ajman and Sharjah IB schools sit the May session. Confirm your child's specific dates with the school's examinations officer and the board's published timetable, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-rawda.tutorsIntro: Each tutor below is listed against the subject and level they teach, because the Diploma is marked at the level of the component rather than the subject. A teacher fluent in Higher Level paper structure and criterion language is a different proposition from one who knows the content well.

intro.heading: The Diploma is a marking system before it is a syllabus
paragraphs: Al Rawda spreads across three villa sub-communities west of the older centre of Ajman, with Sheikh Ammar Bin Humaid Street running past it and a steady traffic of school buses heading towards Sharjah in the morning. Families here are mostly settled rather than transient, and the Diploma students in these streets have generally been in the same school system for years. That produces a particular kind of enquiry: not panic, but a specific question about why a competent student is stuck on a 5.

The answer is almost always the marking system rather than the content. A Diploma student who understands their subject and scores a 5 is usually losing marks in identifiable, repeatable places: an 'explain' question answered as a description, a method abandoned halfway, an internal assessment that was capped by a research question too broad to answer, an Extended Essay that spent 900 of its 4,000 words on context. None of that is a knowledge problem, and none of it is fixed by reading the textbook again.

This page is built from the subject guides outwards. It names which paper carries which weighting, so that a student knows where revision effort converts into marks. It names internal assessment criteria by letter with their mark allocations, because almost no page in this market does, and because a student who knows that reflection carries three marks writes a different paragraph. It sets out the word and page limits across components, since a limit breached is a mark lost without argument. And it describes what past-paper work looks like when it is done properly rather than collected.

On delivery there is no ambiguity. IB Gram does not provide in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring exists only in our India service. Lessons for Al Rawda families are live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own script or draft annotated on a shared screen. For mark-scheme work this is the better surface by some distance: a paragraph can be marked up against the descriptor and the annotated version saved, which a notebook on a kitchen table cannot do.

One caution before the detail. Weightings, criteria and limits are set by the current subject guide for each course, and guides are revised on their own cycles. Everything below reflects the structure of the courses as they are currently taught, and the authority for your child's specific course is the subject guide their school works from. Any tutor worth hiring will know which guide that is and will say so when asked.

What the detail is for is simple. A parent who knows that the internal assessment is a fifth of a science grade, and that half of its criteria reward what happens after the experiment rather than during it, can ask a tutor a question that separates a specialist from a generalist in one answer. That is the practical value of the next few thousand words.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-rawda.programmesIntro: Each International Baccalaureate programme is assessed on a different model, and the model is what a tutor has to be fluent in. The notes below describe the assessment structure rather than the educational philosophy.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, converted to a 1-7 grade through a published boundary table. Criterion A is typically knowing and understanding; the remaining three reward investigation, communication and reflection or critical thinking depending on the subject group. A student strong on content and weak on process loses marks in three of the four criteria simultaneously.
programmes.countryNote: For Al Rawda students in MYP the useful work is criterion language rather than content. A Year 9 student who learns what 'analyse' requires in the MYP descriptors, and writes to it, improves in every subject at once, which makes a single weekly hour unusually good value at this stage compared with Diploma-level support.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, each assessed through written papers plus an internally assessed component usually worth around a fifth to a quarter of the subject grade, alongside Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The core carries up to three additional points on the diploma total through the combined Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma candidates at Ajman and Sharjah schools sit the May session. No specific examination or results date appears on this page: the organisation's own site blocks automated retrieval and no date in our research could be verified, so your child's International Baccalaureate coordinator is the authority for all of them.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry with portfolio and exhibition assessment rather than examinations. There are no criterion letters or weightings to learn here, which is exactly why gaps in arithmetic fluency and written stamina can persist for several years without a report card surfacing them.
programmes.countryNote: Al Rawda families with children in PYP who want a check on progress are better served by a short diagnostic than by ongoing tuition. Two sessions on number fluency and reading comprehension will show whether there is anything to act on, which is a cheaper answer than a term of weekly support bought on a general worry.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Diploma courses taken alongside a career-related study, a reflective project and service learning. The Diploma courses inside it are assessed identically to the full Diploma, including their internal components, so the marking detail on this page applies in full to those subjects.
programmes.countryNote: No Ajman school is a significant provider, so Al Rawda students on this route have generally transferred to a Sharjah or Dubai school. Support concentrates on the Diploma courses within the programme and on the reflective project, which needs its own scheduled time rather than the leftovers of a busy week.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-rawda.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is described by its assessment architecture: what the components are, roughly what they are worth, and the specific place marks go missing. Weightings reflect the current course structure and should be confirmed against the subject guide your child's school uses.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Standard Level two papers carry 40 per cent each with the exploration at 20 per cent. At Higher Level the two main papers carry 30 per cent each, Paper 3 carries 20 per cent and the exploration 20 per cent. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which punishes students who have outsourced arithmetic to the machine all year.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The same component structure as Analysis and Approaches, with modelling and statistics in place of proof and pure analysis. The calculator is assumed throughout, including in Paper 1, and the exploration almost always needs genuine data, which has to be collected weeks before the writing starts.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 combines multiple choice with a data-analysis section and carries around 36 per cent, Paper 2 around 44 per cent, and the internal assessment 20 per cent. Multiple choice punishes imprecise definitions; the internal assessment lives on uncertainty propagation, which school laboratory time rarely covers properly.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The same component split as physics, with the internal assessment at 20 per cent. Marks leak in data-based questions where significant figures and units are treated as presentation rather than content, and in organic mechanisms written as decoration instead of as claims about electron movement.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Component weightings mirror the other sciences. The subject appears memorisable and is not: command terms do the work, and an 'explain' question answered as a description loses marks the student had already earned the knowledge for. Statistical choice is the usual weakness in the internal assessment.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: At Standard Level Paper 1 carries 30 per cent, Paper 2 40 per cent and the internal assessment 30 per cent. At Higher Level the three papers carry 20, 30 and 30 per cent with the internal assessment at 20. The internal assessment is three commentaries on published articles, each with a word limit, and article choice sets the ceiling.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Paper 1 around 35 per cent, Paper 2 around 40 per cent and the internal assessment around 25 per cent, with the Higher Level Paper 1 case study pre-released. Evaluation marks are the ones most often untouched: candidates describe a tool accurately and never reach a judgement supported by the stimulus.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: At Higher Level Paper 1 carries 35 per cent, Paper 2 25 per cent, the individual oral 20 per cent and the Higher Level essay 20 per cent. At Standard Level the two papers carry 35 per cent each with the oral at 30. The oral is assessed against four criteria and the global issue must be genuinely arguable.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed through an exhibition of three objects with written commentary and an essay on a prescribed title with a 1,600-word limit. Both are marked holistically rather than against lettered criteria, and the essay is where most students write about knowledge instead of making a knowledge claim and defending it.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words assessed against five criteria: focus and method, knowledge and understanding, critical thinking, presentation, and engagement, with critical thinking carrying the largest allocation. Essays are most often capped by a research question too broad to answer rather than by weak writing.

sections.heading: Command terms are the marking system in miniature
paragraphs: The most expensive habit in the Diploma is answering the question the student wishes had been asked. A paper asks them to explain and they describe. It asks them to evaluate and they list advantages. It asks them to suggest and they state a fact. Each of those is a complete answer to a different question, and the mark scheme does not award it.

Command terms are published in every subject guide and they are specific. Describe asks for an account without reasons. Explain asks for reasons or mechanisms. Analyse asks the student to break something into parts and show how they relate. Evaluate asks for a judgement supported by evidence and weighed against an alternative. Suggest asks for a plausible answer where no single one is required. Compare asks for similarities and differences, both of them.

What makes this teachable rather than obvious is that the fix is mechanical. A student who, for one term, underlines the command term before writing and names what it requires will stop making the error. The gain is largest in the sciences and in economics, where several marks a paper sit in this one habit, and it is visible within a fortnight because the losses were never about understanding.

This is also the clearest demonstration of what a tutor's marking fluency buys. A parent reading a script sees an answer that looks reasonable. A teacher who marks against the scheme sees that four of the eleven lost marks were command-term failures, two were unit errors, and five were a method abandoned at the second step. Those three findings lead to three different pieces of work, and none of them is 'revise more'.

table.caption: COMMAND TERMS AND WHAT THE SCHEME ACTUALLY REQUIRES
rows: Explaining when no explanation is required
Complete coverage of the features asked for
A causal chain, each step stated
Separation into elements plus their relationship
A list of advantages and disadvantages
A conclusion that chooses, with supporting evidence
A reasoned possibility, consistent with the data

sections.heading: Internal assessment criteria, by letter
paragraphs: Internal assessments are the single largest block of unclaimed marks in the Diploma, and the reason is almost never the subject content. It is that students write to a general idea of quality rather than to the criteria, which are published, specific and weighted unevenly. A student who does not know that reflection carries three marks on a mathematics exploration will write a conclusion that restates the result and claim none of them.

The mathematics exploration is the clearest example, because its five criteria are compact. Presentation carries four marks and rewards a coherent, organised piece rather than neat formatting. Mathematical communication carries four and rewards correct notation, defined variables and consistent symbols. Personal engagement carries three and rewards genuine independent thinking rather than enthusiasm declared in the introduction. Reflection carries three and rewards the student discussing the significance and limitations of what they did. Use of mathematics carries six, the largest single allocation, and rewards work that is relevant, correct and at a level commensurate with the course.

The Extended Essay works the same way with a different distribution. Focus and method, knowledge and understanding, and engagement each carry six marks, presentation four, and critical thinking twelve, which is more than a third of the total. An essay that researches carefully and never argues cannot reach the upper bands however well written it is, and that single fact changes how a student should spend their 4,000 words.

The practical consequence is that criterion work is the highest-yield tutoring available to a Diploma student, and it is available cheaply because it is short. Reading a draft against the descriptors takes an hour. Rewriting a reflection section to actually reflect takes the student an evening. The marks involved are often several per subject, and almost no competitor page in this market names a single criterion letter.

table.caption: CRITERION ALLOCATIONS ON TWO MAJOR COMPONENTS
rows: A coherent, organised and concise piece of work
Correct notation, defined variables, consistent symbols
Significance and limitations discussed, not restated results
Relevant, correct work at the level of the course
Argument and evaluation, not accumulated research
A research question answerable in 4,000 words

sections.heading: Word and page limits are part of the mark scheme
paragraphs: Limits are treated by students as an administrative detail and by examiners as a condition of assessment. An Extended Essay has a 4,000-word limit, and material beyond it is not read. A Theory of Knowledge essay has a 1,600-word limit. Economics commentaries have their own word limit per commentary, and the mathematics exploration has a recommended page range rather than a word count. Breaching any of these costs marks that content cannot recover.

The subtler problem is allocation within the limit. An Extended Essay that spends 900 words establishing context has 3,100 left for the argument that carries twelve of the available marks. A Theory of Knowledge essay that defines its terms for 400 of its 1,600 words has spent a quarter of the paper on the least rewarded part of it. Most students discover this at the final draft, which is the point at which cutting is painful and structural change impossible.

The fix is to plan to the limit from the first outline. A student who allocates word counts per section before writing produces a different first draft: shorter introduction, longer analysis, a conclusion that earns its place. It is a dull intervention and it reliably moves marks, particularly on the Extended Essay where the imbalance is almost universal.

Confirm the current limit for your child's component against the subject guide their school uses, since these are revised on each guide's own cycle. Any tutor working on a long-form component should know the limit without checking and should be planning the draft against it rather than editing towards it at the end.

table.caption: LIMITS AND WHERE THE WORDS SHOULD ACTUALLY GO
rows: Context and literature overwhelm the argument
Majority of the words on analysis and evaluation
Word limit set by the current guide

sections.heading: Where the sciences leak marks
paragraphs: Science papers in the Diploma reward a narrow set of habits, and the losses are consistent enough across cohorts to name. In physics, the first is unit and prefix discipline: an answer correct to three significant figures in the wrong prefix scores nothing. The second is the sketch graph, where candidates draw a shape without labelling axes or marking an intercept the question asked for. The third is multiple choice treated as a quick section, when it rewards precision about definitions more than any other part of the paper.

In chemistry the recurring losses sit in data-based questions. Significant figures carried inconsistently through a calculation, units omitted from a rate, a mole ratio applied in the wrong direction. Organic mechanisms are the other standing weakness, and the diagnostic question is simple: can the student say what the arrow means? A student who treats curly arrows as a drawing convention cannot predict an unfamiliar mechanism, and unfamiliar mechanisms are what the papers ask about.

In biology the losses are command-term failures and statistics. The content is large enough that students default to recall, and the papers reward applying recall to an unfamiliar context. The internal assessment then fails on statistical choice: a test applied because it was the one taught, not because the data meet its assumptions. Both are teachable, and neither is addressed by rereading the chapter.

Across all three, the internal assessment weighting of around a fifth of the subject grade means uncertainty treatment and evaluation are worth more than their share of teaching time. School laboratory sessions are arranged around performing the experiment; the marks are largely in what happens afterwards. That asymmetry is the single best reason for a Diploma science student in Al Rawda to buy a defined block of internal assessment support.
bullets: Unit and prefix errors convert correct physics into no marks
Significant figures and units carry marks in chemistry data questions
Biology rewards applying recall, not reciting it
The internal assessment is worth about a fifth of each science grade

sections.heading: Mathematics: the route, the papers and the calculator
paragraphs: The Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation decision is made early and shapes two years. Analysis and Approaches emphasises algebra, calculus and proof; Applications and Interpretation emphasises modelling, statistics and technology. Neither is the easier course, and the right choice depends on the student's strengths and on what their intended university course expects, which is worth checking with the specific institution rather than assumed.

The component structure differs by level in a way that changes revision strategy. At Standard Level two papers carry 40 per cent each and the exploration 20 per cent. At Higher Level the two main papers carry 30 per cent each, Paper 3 carries 20 per cent and the exploration 20 per cent. Paper 3 at Higher Level is an extended investigation rather than a question set, and it needs separate practice, because a student who has only ever answered short questions will not sustain a multi-page argument under time.

In Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 is sat without a calculator. Students who have used a graphical display calculator as a crutch all year discover this late, and the discovery is expensive. Conversely in Applications and Interpretation the calculator is assumed throughout, and students who treat it as a last resort run out of time. Both failures are habits built over months and corrected over weeks, which is why they need naming early rather than in the final term.

The exploration is 20 per cent of the grade in every configuration, which makes it the most reliably underweighted piece of work in the subject. Twenty marks, five criteria, use of mathematics carrying six of them. A student who chooses a topic that permits mathematics at the level of their course, rather than a topic they find interesting but can only treat trivially, has already claimed most of the available ground.

sections.heading: Past-paper work, done properly
paragraphs: Almost every Diploma student has past papers. Far fewer have practised with them, because collecting and attempting are not the same as practising. A paper attempted without timing, marked by the student against an answer rather than a scheme, and then filed, teaches close to nothing. The same paper under time, marked against the published scheme question by question with each loss tagged, is the best diagnostic available outside a mock.

The protocol matters more than the volume. Sit the paper under proper conditions, with the correct time and no interruptions. Mark it against the scheme, awarding only what the scheme awards, which is uncomfortable and necessary: students routinely give themselves method marks the scheme does not offer. Record the marks by question rather than as a total. Then tag each loss as content not known, content not retrievable under pressure, method abandoned, or time run out.

That tagging is where the value sits, because the four categories need different responses and look identical in a percentage. A student losing eleven marks to timing should be practising timed sections, not rereading notes. A student losing them to abandoned methods should be working deliberately through ugly arithmetic until finishing becomes automatic. A student losing them to content gaps needs teaching, and in most scripts that is the smallest of the four categories.

Three papers treated this way are worth more than fifteen collected. For an Al Rawda student with a fixed weekly hour, the sensible pattern is to sit the paper independently between sessions and use the session for marking and repair, which converts the paid hour into the part that only a teacher can do.
bullets: Timed conditions, correct paper type, no interruptions
Mark against the published scheme, not against an answer
Record marks by question and tag each loss
Sit papers between sessions; use the session for marking and repair

sections.heading: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay as assessed writing
paragraphs: The core components are treated by many students as the parts of the Diploma that are not really marked, which is a misreading with a points cost. The Theory of Knowledge essay and the Extended Essay together contribute up to three additional points to the diploma total through a published matrix, and those points regularly decide whether a conditional university offer is met.

Both are assessed writing rather than general reflection, and both have a specific failure mode. Theory of Knowledge essays fail by writing about knowledge instead of making a knowledge claim and defending it against a counterclaim with worked examples. A paragraph that says knowledge in the natural sciences is often provisional, with no example and no opposing case, has said nothing assessable. The fix is structural: claim, counterclaim, example, implication, in that order, repeatedly.

Extended Essays fail at the research question. A question too broad cannot be answered in 4,000 words, so the essay surveys instead of arguing, and critical thinking, which carries twelve marks, goes largely unclaimed. The repair is cheap if it happens early and impossible if it happens late: narrowing a question in September costs a conversation, and narrowing it after 3,000 words costs the essay.

Legitimate help on both is specific and bounded. A tutor can teach the structure of a knowledge claim, interrogate a weak counterclaim, show a student how to read their own paragraph as a moderator will, and insist on a question that can actually be answered. A tutor cannot write any part of either document, and should decline if asked, because submitted work that is not the student's own is an academic-honesty breach that can reach the Diploma itself.
bullets: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay contribute up to three diploma points
Theory of Knowledge essays need claim, counterclaim, example, implication
Extended Essays are usually capped by the research question, not the writing
Teaching, questioning and feedback only; the student writes every word

process.title: Send one marked script
process.description: A recent marked paper or a returned internal assessment draft tells us more than any description of the problem. From one script we can usually say whether the lost marks are command terms, units, abandoned methods, timing or genuine content gaps, and those five lead to five different plans.

process.title: Name the subject, level and component
process.description: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL with Paper 3 as the weakness is a different request from Mathematics SL with a stalled exploration. Component-level precision is what allows a tutor to be matched on fluency with the thing that is actually wrong rather than with the subject in general.

process.title: Free trial on the weakest component
process.description: One lesson at no charge with no payment details collected, spent marking or teaching the component that carries the most unclaimed marks. You get a short written note naming the component, the marks targeted and the first piece of work. The note is the thing to judge.

process.title: Agree the component sequence
process.description: We set out which components will be worked on in which order and why, using the weightings rather than the student's preferences. A term spent on a component worth 20 per cent, where several marks are unclaimed, beats a term spread thinly across everything.

process.title: Re-test on the same paper type
process.description: At the end of a block the student sits the same paper type under the same conditions, marked the same way. That comparison is the only honest check on whether the work moved anything, and it is also the moment to decide whether to continue, change component or stop.

whyPoints.title: Weightings drive the agenda
whyPoints.description: Sessions are aimed at the component carrying the most unclaimed marks rather than at chapter order or the topic the student mentions. That is a different plan from general revision, and it is the one that converts effort into grade.

whyPoints.title: Criterion letters named, not paraphrased
whyPoints.description: Internal assessment work happens with the descriptor on screen next to the paragraph, and the mark allocation stated. A student who knows that reflection carries three marks writes a different section, and almost no page in this market names a single criterion letter.

whyPoints.title: Limits planned, not edited towards
whyPoints.description: Word and page limits are built into the outline rather than discovered at the final draft. An Extended Essay planned to its limit allocates most of its words to the criterion worth twelve marks instead of to context nobody is paid to read.

whyPoints.title: Marking against the published scheme
whyPoints.description: Papers are marked for what the scheme awards, not for what the answer resembles, and losses are tagged so each one leads to specific work. Students mark themselves generously; that generosity is where the mock surprise comes from.

whyPoints.title: No invented dates or figures
whyPoints.description: No International Baccalaureate examination or results date appears on this page, because none could be verified from the organisation itself. There is no success percentage or average-score claim either, because we could not produce the data behind one.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay are taught, questioned and reviewed, never drafted. A service that offers to produce them is selling an academic-honesty breach that falls on the student rather than the seller.

faqs.question: Why is my child stuck on a 5 when they understand the subject?
faqs.answer: Almost always because of where the marks are lost rather than what is known. The usual pattern in a script is command-term failures, unit or significant-figure errors, methods abandoned at the second step, and questions left unfinished. Those are four separate habits and none of them is fixed by rereading the textbook. One marked paper, read against the published scheme question by question, normally shows which of the four is costing the most, and that becomes the work.

faqs.question: What are the internal assessment criteria worth in a Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: The internal component is typically worth around a fifth to a quarter of the subject grade, and within it the criteria are weighted unevenly. On the mathematics exploration, use of mathematics carries six of the twenty marks, presentation and mathematical communication four each, and personal engagement and reflection three each. Knowing those numbers changes what a student writes: a reflection section worth three marks deserves a proper discussion of limitations, not a restatement of the result.

faqs.question: How much does the Extended Essay actually affect the diploma total?
faqs.answer: The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay together contribute up to three additional points through a published matrix, and those points routinely decide whether a conditional university offer is met. Within the essay itself, critical thinking carries twelve of the available marks, more than a third, which means an essay that researches thoroughly and never argues cannot reach the upper bands however carefully it is written.

faqs.question: Which command terms cost Diploma students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Explain and evaluate, consistently. Explain asks for reasons or a mechanism and is routinely answered with a description, which is a complete answer to a different question. Evaluate asks for a judgement weighed against an alternative and is routinely answered with a list of advantages and disadvantages and no conclusion. Both are mechanical to fix: underline the command term, name what it requires, then write. The gain is visible within a fortnight because the knowledge was never missing.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Diploma tutor to Al Rawda?
faqs.answer: No. In-home visits are a service IB Gram offers only in India, not anywhere in the UAE. Lessons for Al Rawda families are live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own script or draft annotated on a shared screen. For criterion and mark-scheme work that is the better surface: the descriptor sits beside the paragraph, the annotation is saved for revision, and the specialist is chosen for fluency in the component rather than proximity.

faqs.question: Is Mathematics Analysis and Approaches harder than Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Neither is the easier course; they reward different strengths. Analysis and Approaches emphasises algebra, calculus and proof, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator. Applications and Interpretation emphasises modelling and statistics, with the calculator assumed throughout. The right choice depends on the student and on what their intended university course expects, and that expectation should be checked with the specific institution rather than assumed from a general impression.

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 at Higher Level and how should it be prepared?
faqs.answer: In Higher Level mathematics, Paper 3 carries around 20 per cent of the grade and is an extended investigation rather than a set of short questions. It requires sustaining a line of reasoning across several pages, often in an unfamiliar context, which is a different skill from answering well-defined questions. Students who have only practised short-answer papers do badly on it. The preparation is specific: whole investigations attempted under time, then marked and reworked.

faqs.question: How long should a science internal assessment research question be in scope?
faqs.answer: Narrow enough to be answered properly within the word limit set by the current subject guide. The commonest cap comes from a question so broad that the student can only treat it superficially, which limits the analysis and evaluation criteria regardless of how carefully the experiment was performed. Narrowing it is a single conversation if it happens before data collection and a rewrite if it happens afterwards, which is why the first session on an internal assessment should be about the question.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my child's internal assessment?
faqs.answer: A tutor can read it against the published criteria, explain what each descriptor requires as evidence, and show the student where their draft does not yet meet it. That is feedback, and it is legitimate and useful. What a tutor cannot do is award the mark that counts, which is the school's role, or write, rewrite or supply text for submission. If the draft needs restructuring, the student does the restructuring with the criteria in front of them.

faqs.question: Why does the word limit matter if the content is good?
faqs.answer: Because material beyond the limit is not read, and because the allocation within the limit decides which criteria get served. An Extended Essay that spends 900 of its 4,000 words on context has 3,100 left for the argument that carries twelve marks. A Theory of Knowledge essay that defines terms for 400 of its 1,600 words has spent a quarter of the paper on its least rewarded part. Plan the word counts per section before writing, not after.

faqs.question: How many past papers should a Diploma student do?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most students collect and far more carefully. Three papers sat under proper timed conditions, marked against the published scheme question by question with each loss tagged as content, retrieval, method or timing, are worth more than fifteen attempted casually and filed. The sensible pattern with a weekly session is to sit the paper independently between lessons and use the paid hour for marking and repair, which is the part only a teacher can do.

faqs.question: What goes wrong most often in a Theory of Knowledge essay?
faqs.answer: Writing about knowledge instead of making a knowledge claim and defending it. A paragraph stating that scientific knowledge is provisional, with no example and no opposing case, contains nothing assessable. The structural fix is to write claim, counterclaim, worked example, implication, and repeat it. Students find this formulaic and the marks improve anyway, because the assessment rewards argument supported by specific examples rather than general reflection about the nature of knowing.

faqs.question: Are the weightings on this page the ones my child's course uses?
faqs.answer: They reflect the current structure of these courses, and the authority for your child's specific course is the subject guide their school works from, since guides are revised on their own cycles. Any tutor worth hiring will know which guide applies and will say so without being pressed. If a tutor cannot name the components and their approximate weightings for the course they claim to teach, that is the useful piece of information from the conversation.

faqs.question: Is one hour a week enough for a Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: It is enough if the hour is used for the part the student cannot do alone and if there is independent work behind it. An hour spent marking a paper the student sat during the week, naming the failure types and setting the next task, moves more than an hour of teaching with nothing attached to it. An hour a week with no work between sessions moves very little, whatever the subject or the tutor, and that is usually the real variable rather than frequency.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-rawda.closingHeading: Send a script, not a description
ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-rawda.closingBody: The fastest way for an Al Rawda family to get a useful answer is to send one marked paper or one returned internal assessment draft, with the subject and level named. From that we can usually say where the marks are actually going, which component carries the most unclaimed ground, and whether a specialist fluent in that component is free in your evening slot this term. The free trial lesson is then spent on that component rather than on an introduction, and the written note afterwards names the marks targeted and the first piece of work.

intro.heading: Why an IB parent's search ends differently
paragraphs: Al Yasmeen is a villa district set back from the Ajman coast, with wide plots, a settled resident population and a school run that mostly stays inside the emirate. It is a comfortable place to raise a family and a difficult place to find a Diploma Programme tutor. The reason is arithmetic rather than geography: the IB accounts for a small share of students in the UAE compared with the British and Indian curricula, so the pool of tutors who have taught a specific Higher Level subject through to a grade boundary is small everywhere, and smaller again inside one neighbourhood.

That scarcity is why the usual search produces the wrong kind of candidate. Plenty of tutors can teach differentiation. Far fewer can tell you that a mathematical exploration is marked on five criteria lettered A to E, that criterion E carries six of the twenty marks, and that personal engagement is worth three marks a student usually throws away by choosing a topic from a list. Those are different kinds of knowledge, and only the second one moves an IB grade.

The Diploma compounds the problem by assessing things that do not exist in other systems. Theory of Knowledge has an essay capped at 1,600 words and an exhibition of three objects. The Extended Essay runs to 4,000 words and is marked on five criteria worth 34 marks in total. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment with its own criterion letters and its own internal school deadline. A tutor who has never supervised any of it will be learning on your child's time.

This page is built to help you test for the right thing. It sets out what separates an IB tutor from a competent subject teacher, gives you the questions that reveal the difference, publishes the Internal Assessment criteria by letter and mark so you can check an answer, and lists the word limits across the Diploma so nobody in your household is guessing. Competing pages in this market mention Internal Assessments without naming a single criterion; the details are on this page because they are what a parent needs.

There is one more thing worth saying before the detail. Diploma students are busy in a way that other sixteen-year-olds are not, and a plan that ignores that fails whatever its academic merit. Six subjects, three core components and CAS commitments produce weeks where nothing can be added, and the only tuition hour that survives is the one fixed before the term started.

On delivery, the position is simple and stated the same way on every IB Gram country page. There is no office, centre or branch in the UAE. Nobody arrives at a villa in Al Yasmeen, because home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only. UAE tuition is one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with the recording available afterwards and a short written note to the parent after each session.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-yasmeen.programmesIntro: The IB runs as a continuum, and families in Al Yasmeen usually enter it at one of three points. Each stage has a different failure mode and a different tutoring brief.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led learning organised around transdisciplinary themes, with no external examinations and a report format that describes development rather than ranking it. Support at this stage is almost always about literacy or number fluency rather than about the programme itself, and it works best in short, frequent sessions.
programmes.countryNote: For Al Yasmeen families the practical issue at this age is reading stamina in English when it is a second or third language at home. A weekly half-hour of reading aloud with correction does more than a full hour of worksheets, and it costs less. Schools in Ajman also teach Arabic alongside the licensed curriculum, which is a second reading load for a young child.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, scored one to eight and converted to a grade one to seven. The conversion is where parents misread the report: a criterion score of five is not a percentage, and a strong-sounding report can hide a specific weakness in one criterion across every subject.
programmes.countryNote: MYP Year 5 is the cheapest and most effective place to intervene before the Diploma. Students who arrive in Diploma Year 1 without algebraic fluency, lab-report discipline or the habit of citing sources need several times as many paid hours to repair it. One session a week through MYP 4 and 5 is the quietest money a family can spend well.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Three subjects at Higher Level, three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment with its own criteria. The grade is out of 45, with up to three bonus points from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix, and the commonest cause of a disappointing total is not a weak paper but an Internal Assessment left to the last fortnight.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. Exact session and results dates are set by the IB and should be confirmed with your child's Diploma coordinator rather than taken from a tutoring page. The dates that genuinely govern the year are the school's own internal deadlines for the exploration, the Extended Essay drafts and the TOK exhibition, and those sit months before any exam.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route combining Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Offered by far fewer schools in the UAE than the Diploma, so a family exploring it should confirm availability with the school before planning around it.
programmes.countryNote: Where it is offered, the reflective project is the component that most resembles an Extended Essay in the support it needs: structure, sourcing and a defensible argument, with the writing staying entirely the student's own. Families in Ajman considering this route often do so for the subject flexibility rather than the workload.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-yasmeen.subjectsIntro: Diploma requests from this part of Ajman cluster in the sciences, mathematics and economics, with English A and Business Management close behind. Each note names the component where marks go missing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level adds Paper 3, an extended problem-solving paper that rewards students who can sustain an argument over several parts. The exploration carries twenty marks on criteria A to E, and most lost marks sit in reflection and personal engagement rather than in the mathematics itself.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-active throughout, with statistics and modelling at its centre. Students who chose it to avoid proof often underestimate the Higher Level statistical testing content, which is where the grade is decided.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The scientific investigation is assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Uncertainty handling is the single most reliable source of lost marks, and it is rarely taught slowly enough in a full class.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and equilibrium calculations separate a 5 from a 7. The investigation needs a question narrow enough to generate a controlled data set, and a tutor's most useful intervention is refusing a topic that is too broad in week one.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Precision marking rather than volume. Answers that describe a trend without naming the mechanism earn little, and the investigation needs a measurable dependent variable rather than an interesting idea.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The Internal Assessment is three commentaries of 800 words each, marked on criteria A to E for fourteen marks apiece. Diagram accuracy earns marks before analysis begins, and Higher Level adds quantitative work in Paper 3.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the named organisation is what the criteria reward. Students lose marks writing textbook theory with the company's name attached, and the research project needs a focused question rather than a broad company review.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is guided analysis of unseen non-literary text, and the Individual Oral is the component students under-rehearse most. Higher Level adds an essay on a studied text, marked on its own criteria.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An essay of up to 1,600 words on a prescribed title and an exhibition of three objects with a commentary of up to 950 words. Most students write description where the marker wants an argument about how knowledge is produced.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Up to 4,000 words, marked on five criteria worth 34 marks. Supervision is about focus, method and critical engagement; the writing is entirely the student's, and the reflections are assessed alongside it.

sections.heading: What a parent in Al Yasmeen is really asking
paragraphs: The search phrase is about location but the question underneath it is about competence. Is there anybody reachable from here who has actually taught this programme? For the Diploma, in a villa district in Ajman, the honest answer is that the local pool is thin and the few local candidates are mostly British-curriculum tutors who will treat the IB as A Level with different paperwork.

That mistake is costly in a specific way. A Diploma grade is built from external papers and an Internal Assessment, and the Internal Assessment is where a well-taught student gains and a badly supported student quietly loses. A tutor who drills content and ignores the criteria can lift a student's understanding while the grade stays where it was, because the marks being lost were never in the content.

So the question worth asking is narrower than location and narrower than subject. It is whether the tutor has taken a student through this subject at this level, including its Internal Assessment, and can describe the criteria without looking them up. Once you ask that, the catchment stops mattering, because the honest answer in Al Yasmeen, Al Mowaihat or Al Helio is the same: the specialist is unlikely to be the nearest person.

IB Gram answers it by matching on the subject and level rather than the postcode, and by delivering every UAE lesson one-to-one over live video. Nobody travels to a villa in Al Yasmeen; home visits are an India-only service. What a family gains in exchange is a tutor chosen from a national and international pool instead of a neighbourhood one.

sections.heading: An IB tutor and a good subject teacher are not the same hire
paragraphs: A strong subject teacher knows the content. An IB tutor knows the content and the assessment architecture around it, and in this programme the architecture carries a large share of the grade. Each Diploma subject has an Internal Assessment worth a substantial slice of the final mark, and each is assessed on named criteria with published mark allocations rather than on a general impression of quality.

The difference shows up immediately in how the two approach a weak draft. A subject teacher reads it and says the analysis needs more depth. An IB tutor reads it and says that criterion C is capped at three marks here because the personal engagement is asserted rather than demonstrated, and that the fix is a paragraph explaining why this student chose this data set. One comment is encouragement; the other is a mark.

The same gap appears in the external papers. Command terms in the IB have specific meanings, and a question that says evaluate is asking for something the word discuss is not. Students who have been taught in another system frequently answer the question they expected rather than the one printed, and a tutor who has marked IB scripts spots that pattern in a single session.

Theory of Knowledge is the clearest test of all. It is unlike anything in a national curriculum, it carries bonus points on the Diploma matrix with the Extended Essay, and a tutor who cannot explain how an exhibition differs from an essay has not worked with the programme. Ask about it early; the answer sorts candidates faster than any credential list.

sections.heading: Internal Assessment criteria, by letter and mark
paragraphs: This is the table competing pages in this market do not publish. Research across sixty-odd ranking pages found none that names a single Internal Assessment criterion, let alone its mark allocation, even though the Internal Assessment is where most recoverable marks sit. A parent who knows the letters can check a tutor's answer, and a student who knows them can self-mark a draft before anyone else reads it.

The pattern worth noticing is that presentation and communication criteria are small, while the analytical criteria are large. Students instinctively polish the parts worth three or four marks and skimp on the parts worth six or twelve. In an Extended Essay, critical thinking alone carries twelve of the 34 marks, which is more than focus, method and presentation combined.

Use the table as a planning tool rather than a reference. Work out which criterion your child's draft is weakest against, and spend the paid hours there. A session that lifts a six-mark criterion by two marks is worth more than three sessions spent tidying a four-mark presentation criterion that was already fine.

There is a second use for it. When a tutor explains a mark your child received, the letters let you follow the explanation instead of accepting it. A parent who can ask why criterion D scored two rather than three is in a different conversation from a parent told the work needed more depth, and that conversation is where a tutoring relationship becomes accountable.

Criteria and mark allocations are set by the IB and are revised from time to time with syllabus changes. Confirm the current version for your child's subject and cohort with the school's Diploma coordinator or the subject guide the school holds, because the version in force depends on the year of first assessment.

sections.heading: Word limits across the Diploma, in one place
paragraphs: Half the stress in a Diploma household comes from not knowing how long something is supposed to be. Limits exist, they differ by component, and exceeding them has consequences that range from lost marks to work that cannot be assessed. Having them written down removes an argument that otherwise recurs every few weeks.

The Extended Essay is capped at 4,000 words, and examiners are not required to read beyond it. The Theory of Knowledge essay is capped at 1,600 words and the exhibition commentary at 950. Each Economics commentary is 800 words, three times over. The science investigation report sits at 3,000 words. A mathematics exploration has a recommended length rather than a hard cap, usually described as twelve to twenty pages, which trips up students who equate length with quality.

Two practical habits follow. First, write to eighty per cent of the limit and use the remaining space for revision rather than addition, because cutting a finished piece by 600 words destroys structure. Second, check what the limit excludes, since bibliographies, appendices and some figure captions usually sit outside the count, and students either waste words or hide content in the wrong place.

Confirm every figure against the current subject guide for your child's cohort. Limits are set by the IB and change with syllabus revisions, and the version that matters is the one for the year of first assessment your child sits under. The school's coordinator holds it.

sections.heading: Al Yasmeen afternoons and where the hour fits
paragraphs: Scheduling is not an administrative afterthought in a Diploma year; it is most of why a plan fails. Al Yasmeen has an advantage here over the coastal districts. Many children attend schools inside Ajman, so the journey home is short and the afternoon is not consumed by a drive back from Sharjah or Dubai. That makes a 4.30pm or 5pm start realistic, and those are the slots that stay available.

The households that struggle are the ones driving into Sharjah or further, where a 2.45pm finish becomes a 4.15pm arrival and a tired student. For them the honest recommendation is a 6.30pm or 7pm slot with a break and a meal first, or a weekend morning. A session scheduled into the gap where a teenager is actually hungry and flat produces an hour of attendance and very little learning.

Fix the day as well as the time. A slot that moves weekly is the slot that disappears in March, because every competing commitment is negotiable except the one that is already fixed. Diploma students have CAS, internal deadlines and mock weeks landing in clusters, and the only defence is a tuition hour that nobody has to decide about each week.

Build the year backwards from the school's internal deadlines rather than from the exam session. The dates that actually shape a Diploma Year 1 are the exploration deadline, the Extended Essay first-draft date and the TOK exhibition submission, and they sit months before any paper. Ask the coordinator for them in September and put them on one page on the fridge.

sections.heading: What Diploma support costs across this market
paragraphs: Take the cheapest end first, because that is where most families start looking. Budget online providers in this market advertise from AED 45 to 65 an hour, and one platform lists from AED 33 to 52. At that level you are buying a recent graduate or an undergraduate, which is reasonable value for Middle Years catch-up and thin cover for a Higher Level Diploma paper with an Internal Assessment attached.

A step up, Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 an hour against IGCSE from AED 150, and that gap is the market pricing scarcity rather than prestige. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Dubai cost table puts specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 and above, with a premium named tutor at AED 650 published by BartyED. In-home visits anywhere in the UAE are quoted between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour once travel is priced in, and the travel component buys presence rather than teaching.

What a parent can verify matters more than any band. Ask whether the tutor has taught this subject at this level, which Internal Assessment criteria they can name, whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, how many hours the whole plan comes to, and what happens to a prepaid block if the match fails in week two. Those five answers explain almost every price difference you will encounter.

IB Gram does not print an hourly figure on these pages, because the rate depends on the subject, the level and how close the session is to the May series. The free trial lesson comes first, no card details are taken before it, and the number for your child's case is quoted after it.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: The IB treats work submitted for assessment as the student's own, and a breach is not a telling-off. It is a malpractice case that can cost the Diploma. This market contains at least one provider selling completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price, which makes the boundary worth stating on the page rather than in small print.

What legitimate support looks like is specific. A tutor teaches the skill the task assesses. They explain each criterion and what the band descriptors actually describe. They discuss a research question and say honestly when it is too broad to answer. They read a draft the student has written and identify which paragraph fails which criterion. They help build a timetable so an exploration is not written in one weekend. They prepare a student for a reflection conversation without scripting it.

What a tutor never does is write a sentence of the work, rewrite a paragraph into final form, supply a model answer for reshaping, or hand over anything the student then submits. The same applies to the Extended Essay, the TOK essay and exhibition, and every subject Internal Assessment. Supervisors know their students' writing, and the IB's own reflection process exists partly to expose work that is not the candidate's.

IB Gram also does not reproduce or supply IB syllabus documents, subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Those belong to the IB. A tutor references them, works from material the school has already issued, and points parents to the official source, which has the additional advantage of being current.

process.description: Agree a weekday hour that survives the term, on Gulf Standard Time. Then put the school's internal deadlines for the exploration, the Extended Essay and the TOK components into the plan, because those govern the year more than the exam session does.

process.title: Review against criteria at six weeks
process.description: Look at a marked draft or script and ask which criteria have moved. If nothing has shifted, change the approach or the tutor. Criterion-level review is more honest than a general sense of progress and it catches a poor match in weeks rather than terms.
