faqs.question: Is there an IB home tutor in Al Yasmeen who has actually taught the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Within Al Yasmeen itself, unlikely. The IB is a minority curriculum in the UAE compared with the British and Indian systems, so Diploma specialists are scarce nationally and scarcer inside one villa district. Most locally available tutors are British-curriculum teachers who will treat the Diploma as A Level with extra paperwork, and that approach misses the Internal Assessment entirely. IB Gram matches on the subject and level instead, then delivers the lesson one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. No tutor comes to an Ajman address; home visits are offered in India only.

faqs.question: How can I tell in one conversation whether a tutor knows the IB?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions. Which criteria is the Internal Assessment in my child's subject marked on, by letter? Which criterion carries the most marks? How long may the Theory of Knowledge essay be? A tutor who has worked with the programme will name criteria A to E for a mathematics exploration, will tell you that criterion E carries six of twenty marks, and will know the essay cap is 1,600 words. Someone who talks about building confidence and exam technique instead has told you they have not supervised an Internal Assessment.

faqs.question: My son is in MYP Year 4. Is it too early to start tutoring?
faqs.answer: It is the best time, and the cheapest. Middle Years support costs less per hour than Diploma support and prevents the expensive problem: a student arriving in Diploma Year 1 without algebraic fluency, lab-report discipline or the habit of citing sources. One weekly session through MYP 4 and 5 is a smaller total spend than a single panicked Diploma spring. The other reason to start now is reading the report correctly, since criterion scores out of eight are routinely misread as percentages, hiding a specific weakness that shows up across every subject.

faqs.question: What exactly can a tutor do with my daughter's mathematics exploration?
faqs.answer: Teach the mathematics, explain what criteria A to E reward, discuss whether her chosen topic can generate genuine personal engagement, read the draft she has written and say which criterion each section fails, and set a timetable so it is not produced in one weekend. What a tutor cannot do is write any part of it, rewrite a paragraph into final form, or supply a model exploration to reshape. The exploration carries twenty marks and the IB treats it as her own work; buying one is a malpractice case she would carry, not the provider.

faqs.question: Does Ajman have an education regulator like KHDA or ADEK?
faqs.answer: No. Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority and Abu Dhabi's by the Department of Education and Knowledge, but u.ae states that the Ministry of Education plays the supervisory role for private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge. For a parent in Al Yasmeen the practical consequence is that school-level queries go through the federal Ministry rather than an emirate-level authority. IB Gram claims no approval or accreditation from any of them.

faqs.question: Which IB session do schools in Ajman sit, and when should planning start?
faqs.answer: UAE schools sit the May Diploma session. Exact exam and results dates are set by the IB and should be confirmed with your child's Diploma coordinator rather than taken from any tutoring page, including this one. What governs the year in practice are the school's internal deadlines: the exploration submission, Extended Essay draft dates and the TOK exhibition. Those sit months before the papers and are where most lost marks originate. Ask for them in September and build the tuition plan backwards from them.

faqs.question: How much does Higher Level Diploma tutoring cost compared with Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Higher Level sits at the top of the published bands because the specialist pool is smaller. Across this market, budget online providers advertise from AED 33 to 65 an hour, Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 against IGCSE from AED 150, TutorChase quotes AED 270, and Bestimate's table puts specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 and above, with one premium provider at AED 650. Standard Level work usually sits in the mid band. Those are published market figures read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices; ours is quoted after the free trial.

faqs.question: Can one tutor support both a Diploma subject and the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Often yes, if the essay sits in that subject. A chemistry tutor who understands the Extended Essay criteria can work on both, and there is an efficiency in it because the research question and the subject knowledge interact. Where it goes wrong is an essay in a different discipline: a maths tutor supervising a history essay will coach structure competently and miss what criterion B rewards in that subject. Ask whether the tutor has supervised an Extended Essay in the specific subject before combining the two roles.

faqs.question: Does online tuition work for a subject with a practical component?
faqs.answer: The practical work stays at school; the tutor prepares everything around it. For the sciences, the investigation is assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and none of those four need a laboratory to teach. Choosing a measurable variable, controlling the method, handling uncertainties and writing an evaluation that names specific weaknesses are all screen-shareable work, and arguably better taught with the student's own data table open than in a crowded lab. What the school provides is the apparatus and the supervision of the practical itself.

faqs.question: What are the bonus points for TOK and the Extended Essay worth?
faqs.answer: Up to three points on the Diploma total of 45, awarded from a matrix that combines the grades for Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. Those three points decide university offers more often than families expect, and they come from two components students treat as side tasks: an essay of up to 1,600 words on a prescribed title and a 4,000-word research essay marked on five criteria worth 34 marks. Starting both early is the cheapest way to secure them, because neither rewards work compressed into a single term.

faqs.question: My child goes to school in Sharjah. Does that change the session time?
faqs.answer: It changes it by roughly two hours. An Al Yasmeen family with children at an Ajman school can realistically start at 4.30pm or 5pm, because the journey home is short. A family driving back from Sharjah is looking at a 6.30pm or 7pm start with a break and a meal first, or a weekend morning instead. Booking a session into the window when a teenager is tired and hungry buys attendance rather than learning. Lessons run on Gulf Standard Time, so the slot agreed is the slot at home.

faqs.question: How many hours does a Higher Level subject usually need across two years?
faqs.answer: One weekly hour across both Diploma years is roughly seventy sessions of term time, and that is the common pattern for a subject a student intends to continue at university. A single component in trouble needs far less: a focused block of six to ten hours on Paper 3 technique or on an Internal Assessment is often enough. The expensive version is leaving a Higher Level subject until the second half of Diploma Year 2, where the same grade movement needs more hours in fewer weeks at specialist rates.

faqs.question: Will the tutor give us past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider who offers to is distributing material they do not own. IB past papers, mark schemes, subject guides and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, and reproducing or supplying them is a copyright matter. A tutor references them, works from material your child's school has already issued, and points you to the official source. There is a practical advantage in that: the school's version is the one in force for your child's cohort, and syllabus revisions change both content and criteria between years of first assessment.

faqs.question: What should the first month of IB tutoring actually produce?
faqs.answer: Three things you can see. A named list of the components and criteria where marks are currently being lost, based on marked work rather than impressions. A short written plan with the school's internal deadlines on it. And at least one piece of the student's own work improved against a specific criterion, so the difference is visible in a mark and not just in confidence. If after six weeks none of those exist, the plan needs changing or the tutor does, and changing early costs a fortnight rather than a grade.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-yasmeen.closingHeading: Test for the criteria, then book the hour
ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-yasmeen.closingBody: The search for an IB home tutor in Al Yasmeen is really a search for Diploma fluency, and that is testable in ten minutes. Ask which criteria the Internal Assessment is marked on, which one carries the most marks, and how long the Theory of Knowledge essay may be. Send us the subject, the level and the component in trouble, take the free trial, and ask the tutor to mark a page of your child's draft aloud against the criteria. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, at an hour that holds through a crowded term. Nobody arrives at your gate, and nothing here suggests otherwise.

intro.heading: The question nobody answers straight
paragraphs: Al Zorah is the least dense part of Ajman: low-rise waterfront development along the northern lagoon, a nature reserve, a golf course and a small resident population spread across a lot of ground. There is no school inside it. Every child living here travels, often a long way, and the nearest cluster of people who might tutor privately is several kilometres and a traffic-dependent twenty minutes away. If proximity is going to fail anywhere in the emirate, it fails here first.

That makes the real question visible, which is useful. A parent in Al Zorah cannot pretend that the nearest available tutor is probably fine, because there is no nearest available tutor. So the question becomes the right one from the start: does this person actually know my child's course? Not the International Baccalaureate as an idea, not the Diploma in general, but Chemistry at Higher Level with the option content this particular school teaches, assessed against the criteria in the guide the school works from.

Most of the market cannot answer that, and the reason is structural rather than dishonest. A Diploma candidate carries six subjects, three at Higher Level, and several courses allow the school to choose among content options. Two students both studying Higher Level biology at two Ajman schools may have been taught different option material and will sit papers shaped around it. A tutor who has taught one and not the other is not interchangeable, and 'IB tutor, all subjects' is a claim no individual can support.

IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Lessons for Al Zorah families are live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time, which is the only arrangement that makes the verification question answerable at all. Once the pool is everybody teaching that course in this time zone rather than everybody within a twenty-minute drive of the lagoon, there is at least a chance that the specific person exists.

This page is about verification. What 'knows the syllabus' means in Diploma terms. The option-topic problem and why it defeats local search. The three distinct ways a tutor can be wrong about an International Baccalaureate course. How to test a claim in a single message before any money changes hands. What we say when nobody is available, which happens and should be said. What a subject guide contains, since that is the document the whole argument rests on. And the coursework boundary, which is where an unqualified tutor does the most damage.

Nothing here requires a parent to learn the course. It requires two short messages, one to the school and one to whoever you are considering, and a willingness to read the second reply sceptically rather than gratefully.

programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, converted to a 1-7 grade through a published boundary table. A tutor who knows the programme will name the criteria for the subject they teach and describe what evidence each one requires. One who talks about covering the content is describing the smallest part of the mark.

For families here, that makes an MYP trial lesson unusually diagnostic: within twenty minutes it is clear whether the person is teaching to the assessment or to the topic.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, each with written papers and an internally assessed component worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of the grade, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Several courses carry school-selected content, so knowing the course means knowing which version the school teaches.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-zorah.subjectsIntro: For each subject below, the description names the specific thing a tutor must know beyond the content. These are the details that separate someone who has taught the course from someone who has read about it.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Must know which structure the school's guide uses, how the internal assessment is marked, and the arithmetic conventions that cost marks in data questions. A tutor who cannot say what an arrow means in a reaction mechanism, as a claim about electrons rather than a drawing habit, has not taught the course recently.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Must know the command terms that separate a 5 from a 7 and the statistical choices the internal assessment requires. Biology is the subject where content fluency most convincingly imitates course fluency, which makes it the one where verification matters most.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Must be fluent in uncertainty propagation for the internal assessment and in the precision the multiple-choice section demands. A tutor who treats units and prefixes as presentation rather than content will leave a student losing marks on correct physics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Must know that Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, that Higher Level Paper 3 is an extended investigation rather than a question set, and what the exploration criteria reward. Any of those three being news to a tutor answers the question for you.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Must know that the calculator is assumed throughout and that the exploration usually needs genuine collected data. A tutor who conflates this course with Analysis and Approaches is describing a course your child is not sitting.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Must know that the internal assessment is a set of commentaries on published articles, each with a word limit, and that article choice caps the mark before writing begins. Diagram discipline is the other test: axis labelling is where the marks quietly go.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Must know that the Higher Level case study is pre-released and what that changes about preparation, and must be able to describe what an evaluation question requires beyond a list of advantages. Most candidates never make the judgement the marks are for.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Must know the components, including the individual oral with its recording date and its criteria, and at Higher Level the separate essay. A tutor who discusses only literary analysis is describing half the course, since non-literary texts carry equal weight.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Must know which of the two courses the student is on, because the assumptions about fluency differ completely, and must know the five prescribed themes and the assessment structure. Being a fluent Arabic speaker is not the same as knowing this course.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Must know that the internal assessment is a documented solution marked largely on planning and evaluation rather than on the quality of the program. Students arrive able to code and unable to document, and a tutor from a software background often shares that weakness.

sections.heading: What 'knows the syllabus' means in the Diploma
paragraphs: In a national examination system, knowing the syllabus means knowing one document. In the Diploma it means knowing four things, and a tutor can be solid on one or two of them while being useless on the rest, which is why vague claims survive so easily.

The first is content, including which school-selected material applies. Several Diploma courses allow a school to choose among content options or to emphasise particular material, so two candidates in the same subject at the same level can be taught different things and will meet papers shaped around what they were taught. A tutor who has not asked which version your child studies has not begun to answer the question.

The second is assessment architecture: how many papers, how long, what weighting, what each one rewards. A student revising evenly across components that carry 20 and 44 per cent of the grade is misallocating their time, and only a tutor who knows the weightings can correct that. The third is the internal assessment and its criteria, which carry roughly a fifth to a quarter of each subject grade and are marked against published descriptors with uneven allocations.

The fourth is the examiner's habits: where candidates in that specific course reliably lose marks. Unit discipline in physics. Significant figures in chemistry data questions. Command-term failures in biology. Axis labelling in economics diagrams. These are not general study skills; they are course-specific patterns, and a teacher who has marked or taught the course can list them in a sentence. Someone who cannot has not been close enough to the marking to help with it.

Assessment architecture: papers, durations, weightings

sections.heading: The option-topic problem, and why it defeats a local search
paragraphs: School-selected content is the detail that quietly destroys the premise of neighbourhood tutoring in the Diploma. In a national system, every candidate in a subject sits the same paper from the same content list. In the Diploma, the school's choices within a course mean a tutor needs to know not just the subject and level but the particular configuration your child's school teaches.

Multiply that out and the local supply problem becomes arithmetic rather than opinion. Six subjects, two levels, several courses with school-selected elements, and a small emirate. The number of people within reach of Al Zorah who have taught your child's exact configuration recently is, for most subjects, zero, and for the remainder one or two who are probably not free at the hour your child is home.

The same arithmetic explains something parents find puzzling, which is why a tutor who came highly recommended by another family turned out to be a poor fit. The recommendation was honest. The other family's child was at a different school, sitting a different configuration, possibly at a different level. Nothing in a recommendation surfaces that, because the person recommending does not know what to mention.

The practical response is to make the configuration part of the request. Ask the subject teacher which options or content selections the school teaches for each course, write them down, and give them to anybody you are considering. A specialist will react to that information; a generalist will treat it as administrative detail, and that reaction is the answer you were looking for.

sections.heading: Three distinct ways a tutor can be wrong about an IB course
paragraphs: Not all mismatches are the same, and the three kinds fail at different points in the year, which is why some go undetected for months. Knowing the three makes it possible to spot a problem before the mock window rather than after it.

The first is the wrong curriculum entirely. A teacher fluent in A Levels or in a national curriculum, teaching Diploma content with a different assessment model in mind. This is often good teaching producing poor marks: the physics is correct, the student can do the problems, and nobody has worked on the internal assessment's uncertainty requirements or the multiple-choice precision. It surfaces at the first mock and is sometimes blamed on the student.

The second is the right curriculum and the wrong level. Someone comfortable with Standard Level teaching a Higher Level student, which works for two terms and then fails, because the Higher Level extension material and the additional paper arrive late in the course. By then the student is behind in the part of the subject that distinguishes their grade, and the time to fix it has gone.

The third is the right level and the wrong configuration: the correct course, the correct level, and the content options the tutor knows are not the ones the school teaches. This is the hardest to detect because everything looks right for most of the year. It shows up in the final term when paper practice reveals material the student has never met, which is the worst possible moment to discover it.
bullets: Wrong curriculum: good teaching, wrong assessment model, surfaces at mocks
Wrong level: works for two terms, fails on the Higher Level extension
Wrong configuration: invisible until final-term paper practice
All three are prevented by one question asked before booking

sections.heading: How to test the claim in one message
paragraphs: The verification does not require a parent to understand the course, which is the useful part. It requires four questions whose answers are either specific or evasive, and the difference is audible in the first sentence of each.

Ask: which papers does my child sit for this subject at this level, and how long is each one? What proportion of the grade is the internal assessment, and what are its criteria called? Which content selections or options have you taught for this course, and when? And where do candidates in this course most reliably lose marks, in your experience of marking or teaching it?

A specialist answers all four in a few lines, with numbers in them. The weightings come out without hesitation. The criteria are named rather than described. The content answer includes a school or a year. The marks answer is concrete and slightly boring: unit prefixes, significant figures, command terms, a particular topic where the papers are harsher than the textbook suggests. None of it sounds like marketing, because it is not.

A generalist produces warmth and generality. Years of experience. A love of the subject. An emphasis on confidence and building rapport. All of that may be true and none of it answers what was asked. The tell is not the absence of credentials; it is the absence of numbers. Ask the four questions in one message and read the reply once. The decision is usually obvious.
bullets: Which papers, how long each, what weighting
What the internal assessment is worth and what its criteria are called
Which content selections they have taught, and when
Where candidates in that course lose marks

sections.heading: What we say when nobody is available
paragraphs: A page that only explains how to find a specialist is half a page. The other half is what happens when the specialist does not exist in your window, which in a small emirate for a thinly taught Higher Level course is a real outcome rather than a hypothetical.

Our answer is to say so, with a date. No competitor page in this search segment discloses a coverage limit, and several route enquiries to a sales conversation that ends with somebody being offered whoever is free. That produces the first failure mode described above: good teaching, wrong assessment model, discovered at the mock. It is a worse outcome than waiting, and considerably worse than being told the truth in week one.

What we offer instead is a waiting position with a realistic date and a short written interim plan at no charge: what to work on alone, which past papers to attempt and in what order, and what to bring to the first session when a slot opens. For a motivated Diploma student that is often enough to hold ground for a term. It is not as good as teaching and it is honest about being less.

Where the wait would run past a deadline that matters, such as an internal assessment submission, we say that too, and the sensible advice may be to find a local tutor for that specific piece of work or to lean harder on the school's own supervisor, who is paid to support it. That advice costs us the booking, and giving it is the only version of this service worth running at a scale where nobody can be a specialist in everything.

sections.heading: The subject guide is the document everything rests on
paragraphs: Everything on this page depends on one artefact: the subject guide for each course, which sets out content, assessment structure, weightings and the criteria for the internal assessment. A tutor who knows the course knows that document for the version your child's school is teaching, and a parent who knows it exists can ask the one question that settles most doubts.

Guides are revised on their own cycles, which is why a teacher's experience from several years ago can be partly out of date. A course that has been revised may have different assessment weightings, a restructured internal assessment or reorganised content, and a tutor working from memory of the previous version will teach competently towards the wrong target. Asking which version of the guide they work from is not pedantic; it is the single most informative question available.

What a parent should not do is try to obtain and read the guide themselves, or ask a tutor to supply one. These are the organisation's copyright documents, along with past papers and mark schemes, and reproducing or distributing them is not something a legitimate tutor will offer. The school holds the guide for each course and the subject teacher can summarise the relevant parts in a conversation, which is the proper route.

The practical sequence is therefore simple. Ask the subject teacher which guide version applies and which content selections the school teaches. Give that to the tutor. Listen to whether the answer that comes back engages with it. That is the whole verification, and it costs one message to the school and one to the tutor.

sections.heading: Where an unqualified tutor does the most damage
paragraphs: The worst consequences of a mismatched tutor are not in the written papers, where a student can recover with good late teaching. They are in the internal assessment and the core components, because those close permanently and because bad advice there is confidently given.

A tutor who does not know the criteria will approve a research question that cannot be answered within the word limit, and the mark is capped before any data are collected. They will encourage a student to add more content to a piece where the marks sit in reflection and evaluation. They will treat the Extended Essay as a research exercise when critical thinking carries more than a third of the available marks. Each of those is a plausible instruction given in good faith, and each costs marks that no later work recovers.

There is a worse version, and it exists in this market. Services offer to produce coursework outright, with one site in this search segment selling completed Internal Assessments at a published price. For a Diploma candidate, submitting purchased work is an academic-honesty breach whose consequences can extend to the loss of the Diploma, and the detection route is mundane: a supervisor who has read the student's work all year notices when the voice changes.

Legitimate help is narrow and effective. Read the draft, ask where the evidence supports the claim, explain what each criterion requires as evidence, cut the research question to something answerable, teach the student to read their own paragraph as a moderator will. A tutor does not write, rewrite to a finished state or supply text, and should decline if asked. In the weeks when deadlines converge, that refusal is the most valuable thing the arrangement provides.
bullets: Internal assessment errors close permanently; paper weaknesses do not
A capped research question is the commonest avoidable loss
Purchased coursework risks the Diploma itself
The tutor's refusal is part of what you are buying

faqs.question: How do I know whether a tutor really knows my child's IB course?
faqs.answer: Ask four questions in one message: which papers does my child sit at this level and how long is each, what proportion of the grade is the internal assessment and what are its criteria called, which content selections have you taught for this course and when, and where do candidates in this course most reliably lose marks. A specialist answers with numbers in a few lines. A generalist answers with warmth and no figures, which is the tell.

faqs.question: Why does the school's choice of content options matter to a tutor?
faqs.answer: Because several Diploma courses allow the school to choose among content options or emphasise particular material, and the papers a student meets are shaped around what they were taught. Two candidates in the same subject at the same level at two Ajman schools can therefore need different teaching. A tutor who has taught one configuration and not the other looks correct for most of the year and is exposed in final-term paper practice.

faqs.question: Is there anyone in Al Zorah who tutors the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Realistically, no. Al Zorah is low-density waterfront development with a nature reserve and a golf course, no school inside it and a small, spread-out population. The nearest dense residential district is around twenty minutes away in good traffic. A visiting tutor serving one weekly hour here spends more time travelling than teaching, which is why local quotes are high and local specialist supply is effectively nil.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to Al Zorah?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service IB Gram offers only in India, not anywhere in the UAE. Lessons for families here are live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own work on a shared screen. Given where Al Zorah sits, that is also the only arrangement in which the verification question on this page has a positive answer: the pool becomes everybody teaching the course in this time zone rather than nobody within reach.

faqs.question: What are the three ways a tutor can be wrong about an IB subject?
faqs.answer: Wrong curriculum, where someone fluent in A Levels or a national system teaches correct content towards a different assessment model and it surfaces at the first mock. Wrong level, where a Standard Level teacher carries a Higher Level student for two terms and fails on the extension material. And wrong configuration, where the course and level are right but the content selections are not, which stays invisible until the final term. All three are prevented by asking before booking.

faqs.question: Can you give me my child's subject guide or past papers?
faqs.answer: No, and a tutor who offers to is telling you something useful about how they work. Subject guides, past papers and mark schemes are the organisation's copyright documents. Your child's school holds the guide for each course and the subject teacher can summarise the relevant parts, which is the proper route. What we can do is teach to those requirements and explain what each criterion asks for, using the student's own work.

faqs.question: What happens if you have no specialist for our subject?
faqs.answer: You are told in week one, with a realistic date for when a slot may open, plus a short written interim plan at no charge: what to work on alone, which past papers to attempt and in what order, and what to bring to the first session. For a motivated Diploma student that often holds ground for a term. If the wait would run past an internal assessment deadline, we say so and suggest the school supervisor or a local option instead.

faqs.question: Is a recommendation from another Ajman family reliable?
faqs.answer: It is reliable evidence about punctuality, manner and whether the tutor turns up, and no evidence at all about course match. The recommending family's child may be at a different school, on a different level, studying a different configuration. Nothing in the conversation surfaces that, because the person recommending does not know what to mention. Take the recommendation, then ask the four verification questions anyway.

faqs.question: Why should a tutor know the component weightings?
faqs.answer: Because a student revising evenly across components that carry very different shares of the grade is misallocating their time, and only someone who knows the weightings can correct it. Internal assessments typically carry roughly a fifth to a quarter of a subject grade, and the written papers differ from each other substantially. A tutor who cannot state the split for the course they claim to teach cannot build a sensible plan for the term.

faqs.question: Does experience with A Levels transfer to the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the part that does not transfer is the part that decides the grade. Content overlaps substantially in mathematics and the sciences. Assessment does not: the Diploma's internal components, criterion marking, command-term conventions and paper structures are different, and the core components have no A Level equivalent. A teacher moving between the two can become fluent, and the question to ask is whether they have, not whether they could.

faqs.question: How quickly does a wrong match become obvious?
faqs.answer: It depends which of the three mismatches it is. Wrong curriculum usually shows at the first mock, when correct knowledge produces disappointing marks. Wrong level shows late in the first year, when the Higher Level extension arrives. Wrong configuration can stay hidden until the final term, when paper practice turns up material the student has never seen. That last case is the argument for verifying at the start rather than relying on the term to reveal it.

faqs.question: What should a trial lesson actually look like?
faqs.answer: It should start on the topic your child is stuck on this week and get into it within a few minutes. A specialist does that because they recognise the material and know where the difficulty usually sits. A generalist wants to assess first, discuss learning styles, and establish rapport, which is pleasant and uses the hour you were going to judge them on. Ask for the trial to be on a named topic and see what happens.

faqs.question: Can a tutor approve my child's internal assessment research question?
faqs.answer: A tutor can tell you whether it is answerable within the word limit and whether the available data can support the claims, which is the most valuable single piece of advice in the whole process. What they cannot do is approve it formally, which is the supervisor's role, or write any part of the resulting work. A question that is too broad caps the mark before data collection begins, and that is the commonest avoidable loss in the programme.

faqs.question: Is the long commute from Al Zorah a reason to tutor more?
faqs.answer: It is a reason to schedule differently rather than to buy more hours. A student losing ninety minutes a day to travel has less independent study time, and the first casualty is usually the long-form work: the Extended Essay reading, the internal assessment write-up. Protecting a Saturday morning block for that work does more than adding a weekday session, which lands on a student who is already at the end of a long day.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-zorah.closingHeading: Ask the school, then test the claim
ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-al-zorah.closingBody: Two messages are all this needs. Ask your child's subject teacher which content selections the school teaches and which guide version applies. Then send us the subject, the level and that configuration, along with the evening hour that genuinely works in Al Zorah. We will reply with a match statement naming the course, level and content version the proposed tutor has taught, or with a date and a free interim plan if nobody is available. Either reply is checkable, which is more than the search results for this phrase currently offer.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-emirates-city.tutorsIntro: The tutors matched to Emirates City families are subject teachers who will tell you which Diploma syllabus they last taught and what their students lost marks on. What they will not do is quote a round number before hearing the subject, the level and how many weeks are left.

intro.heading: Work out the year first, then the hour
paragraphs: Hourly rates are how tutoring is advertised and monthly totals are how families actually decide. An hour at AED 200 sounds different from AED 800 a month, and different again from roughly AED 7,200 over a nine-month school year for one subject, which is the same number seen from further away. Emirates City is a high-rise community strung along Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, and a large share of households here chose it precisely because the cost of living is lower than the equivalent in Dubai. A tuition bill that creeps is a real problem, not an abstract one.

So this page starts at the other end. The figures below are market rates in AED, attributed to whoever published them and dated October 2026, arranged by what a household actually pays per month and per year rather than by tier. Then it takes the in-home premium apart, because that premium is where most of the avoidable money goes for a family in Ajman: a tutor travelling in from Sharjah or Dubai in the evening is billing the journey whether or not the invoice says so.

Delivery is stated up front so nothing on this page is read the wrong way. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one online, over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. The URL you arrived on uses the phrase parents type, and the phrase is answered honestly: what in-home tuition costs in this market, what it adds, and why a family in a tower off the E311 usually gets more teaching per dirham from a screen.

The second half of the money question is less comfortable: what tuition is worth buying at all. Paying for a generalist to supervise homework in a Diploma Higher Level subject is a slow waste. Paying for four sessions a week in October when the real deadline is a May series is front-loading effort that will not survive the spring. Paying for coursework help that crosses into producing the work is worse than waste, because the risk lands on the student. Each of those has its own section below.

Nothing here is an IB Gram price list. Rates depend on the subject, the level and how many weeks remain, and a single published number would be wrong for most readers. What is published instead is the market, in enough detail that any quote, including this one, can be judged against something real rather than against a competitor's silence. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this project publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars, which no household in Ajman actually banks in.
bullets: Advertised monthly packages in this market: AED 799 for eight online sessions, AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four in-home visits of two hours.
Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session: AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid, AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support.
A qualified subject tutor working online is published at AED 150 to 300 an hour; in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500.
KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, which steadies one half of an education budget but not the other.
The MoHRE private tuition work permit is free and valid for two years, so a cheap rate is not explained by permit costs.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-emirates-city.programmesIntro: Emirates City families on the IB are usually at one of three stages, and the budget behaves differently at each. Primary support is cheap and optional; the Diploma is the expensive year and the one where a wrong choice of tutor costs the most.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external papers, so there is no mark scheme to buy practice against. Tutoring at this stage earns its money on mechanics: number bonds, written methods, reading stamina and the habit of explaining an answer. Two 30-minute sessions a week at the budget end of the market is a reasonable spend; an hour of specialist time is not what this stage needs.
programmes.countryNote: At budget online rates of AED 45 to 150 an hour, two short primary sessions a week sits roughly in Bestimate's AED 240 to 600 monthly band. Emirates City parents commuting to Dubai often prefer 7:00pm for primary sessions, after dinner, which an online slot can absorb and a travelling tutor usually cannot.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP subjects are marked against four criteria, each out of 8, and the criteria reward process. This is the stage where a cheap generalist stops working, because the problem is rarely the content: it is that the student is not writing to the criterion strands. One session a week with somebody who has read the subject guide beats three with somebody who has not.
programmes.countryNote: Mid-market online rates of AED 150 to 300 an hour put a weekly MYP session at roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month, which matches Bestimate's middle band. Most Emirates City families start with one subject here rather than two, and add the second only after a reporting cycle shows whether it is working.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, with an internally assessed component in each subject worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of the grade. This is where specialist rates of AED 200 to 450 and above apply, and where they are usually justified: the Higher Level papers are not teachable by somebody meeting them for the first time.
programmes.countryNote: A two-year Diploma plan is the largest single number in this page's tables, and it is also the one most families never calculate before starting. Running one HL subject weekly across both years at mid-market rates lands in the AED 10,000 to 20,000 range in total, which is worth knowing in Grade 11 rather than in Grade 12.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-emirates-city.subjectsIntro: Subject scarcity is the main thing that moves a Diploma rate, so this grid is written with cost in mind: where the teaching is widely available, where it is not, and what the money is actually fixing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most commonly requested Diploma subject and therefore the most competitively priced. Marks go missing on Paper 1, the non-calculator paper, where students fluent with a GDC cannot factorise by hand. That is a drilling problem, which means progress per dirham is high and sessions can often step down to fortnightly once fluency returns.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led, with the GDC central. Students lose marks reporting a regression output without interpreting it in context. HL AI adds graph theory and matrices, often taught late, which is why AI HL support booked in the spring costs more per unit of benefit than the same support booked in autumn.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms account for most of the losses, with data-based questions catching students who state a trend without a cause. A scarce subject at HL in the Northern Emirates, so expect the upper half of the specialist band rather than the mid-market rate.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Unit errors, gradients read instead of calculated, and explanation questions answered with equations. Scarce at HL locally. The cheapest effective intervention is usually a short paper-focused block rather than a year of weekly sessions, because the failure is technique more often than content.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Looks learnable and punishes imprecision: a process named but not sequenced, a diagram labelled but not explained. Database and statistics questions catch students who have never calculated a standard deviation by hand. Widely available, so mid-market pricing is realistic.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry a large share of the marks and most students draw them unlabelled. HL adds quantitative work. The internal assessment commentaries need genuinely recent articles and a respected word count, which is the part families most often try to buy and should not.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Marks come from applying a tool to the specific case rather than describing the tool. HL adds the pre-released case study, which rewards early structured reading. Because the pre-release is published well ahead, support bought early is materially cheaper per mark than support bought in the last fortnight.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is where unprepared students summarise instead of arguing about how a text works. The Individual Oral needs a global issue chosen early. Widely available and therefore keenly priced, but the quality spread between tutors is wider here than in any science.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: TOK is often bought late and in a panic, which is the most expensive way to buy it. The essay responds to prescribed titles and rewards a clear line of argument over breadth. A small number of sessions early in the cycle does more than a block of them a fortnight before the deadline.

schoolClusters.note: Most Emirates City children are driven inland or into the old city, 15 to 25 minutes depending on the hour. Fees in this cluster sit well below the Dubai equivalent, which is part of why families choose Ajman, and it changes the share of the education budget that tuition can reasonably take.

schoolClusters.note: A significant number of Emirates City parents already drive to Dubai or Sharjah for work and take a child to school on the way. That makes a late online slot far easier to keep than an in-home visit timed to a return journey on the E311.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one across a term
modes.description: One subject, one tutor, the same slot each week. At mid-market online rates this is the AED 600 to 1,200 a month shape, and it is the right spend when a topic sequence has broken down rather than a single test having gone badly. Its value comes from continuity: the tutor does not spend the first ten minutes rebuilding context.
bullets: 60 or 90 minutes, fixed weekly on Gulf Standard Time
Written notes after each session naming the next target
Reviewed against the school's own reporting cycle, not a generic scheme
Can step down to fortnightly once the gap closes, which lowers the bill

modes.title: Short paper-focused block
modes.description: Four to six weeks aimed at one paper, with timed questions marked to the published scheme. This is usually the cheapest effective intervention available, because it converts knowledge the student already has into marks rather than teaching new content. Families who book this instead of a year of weekly sessions often spend a third as much.
bullets: Two or three sessions a week for four to six weeks
Every answer marked against the official mark scheme
An error log grouped by cause, not by topic
Most often used in the run-up to mocks or a series

modes.title: Coursework process coaching
modes.description: For the Internal Assessment or Extended Essay, the work is narrowing a research question, planning a method, reading the criterion descriptors and giving written feedback on drafts the student has written. The student writes every word. Priced by the block rather than the hour because the useful work is spread across weeks of drafting.

Criterion-by-criterion feedback on the student's own draft

sections.heading: What a year of IB tuition actually costs an Emirates City household
paragraphs: Take the hourly rate out of the conversation for a moment. A household budget runs monthly, and a school year runs roughly nine teaching months with two shorter terms around it. One subject, one hour a week, at the middle of the market works out at four or five sessions a month and nine months of them. That is the number worth knowing before the first lesson, because it is the number that gets quietly doubled when a second subject is added in February.

The published monthly estimates make the shape clear. Bestimate's survey puts a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Advertised packages in this market sit at AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four in-home visits of two hours. Note what that second comparison really is: eight hours of teaching against eight hours of teaching, at roughly double the price, with the difference being a car.

Against that, the other half of an Ajman education budget is relatively stable. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package; Ajman fees are set under a different regime but the direction of travel in the sector is public information a parent can look up. Tuition, by contrast, is uncapped and entirely discretionary, which is exactly why it deserves a planned annual figure rather than a monthly drift.

The table below converts the published hourly bands into the monthly and annual numbers a household actually recognises. Every figure is derived from rates read in October 2026 and attributed in the section above; none of it is an IB Gram price.

sections.heading: The five ways Emirates City families overpay
paragraphs: None of these is a scam. They are all ordinary decisions that look sensible at the time and cost a family several thousand dirhams across a Diploma. The first is buying hours instead of buying a diagnosis. A family worried about Chemistry books two sessions a week in September, and in January the student is no better, because nobody ever established whether the problem was recall, method, command-term reading or timing. One diagnostic session that answers that question is worth more than a term of unfocused ones.

The second is paying a specialist rate for supervision. Watching a teenager do homework is a real service and it is worth the budget tier, not the specialist tier. Paying AED 300 an hour for somebody to sit while past papers are attempted silently is the most common invisible waste in this market. The third is the opposite error: paying a budget rate for Higher Level content. A tutor meeting Higher Level Physics for the first time alongside your child is being paid to learn, and the bill arrives twice.

The fourth is front-loading. Four sessions a week in October for a May series burns the student's appetite and the family's budget before the period when practice compounds. Effort should rise towards the series, not peak in the first term. The fifth is buying coursework help that drifts into coursework production, which is both the most expensive thing in this market and the only one that can cost a student their Diploma rather than their money.

The cheapest correction for all five is the same: a free diagnostic lesson, a written statement of what is actually wrong, and a plan with a stated number of sessions and an end date. If a provider cannot give you that in writing before payment, the quote is not comparable to anything.
bullets: Buy a diagnosis before buying a term of hours.
Match the tier to the task: supervision is a budget-tier job, Higher Level is not.
Ask for a stated number of sessions with an end date, not an open subscription.
Let the intensity rise towards the series rather than peaking in October.

sections.heading: How a tuition quote is actually built, line by line
paragraphs: Two quotes for the same subject can differ by a factor of four, and the difference is rarely teaching quality alone. A quote is assembled from the tutor's own rate, the provider's margin, the travel if anybody is travelling, the scarcity of the subject at the level required, and the number of weeks left before the assessment that matters. Asking which of those five is moving the number is a fair question and a revealing one.

Scarcity is the component families underestimate. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches is taught in almost every Diploma school, so the pool is deep and the price is competitive. Chemistry at Higher Level, or Economics with its internal assessment commentaries, is taught by a handful of teachers in the whole emirate, several of whom cannot tutor their own school's students. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid tuition of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that bars the same. The nearest qualified teacher is frequently the one person unavailable.

Timing is the next component. Rates in this market firm up as a series approaches, for the ordinary reason that demand rises and the same tutors cannot teach more hours. A family booking Higher Level support in the spring is competing for capacity; the same family booking in September is not. That is a discount available to anybody willing to plan, and it costs nothing to take.

The last component is what the provider does when the match fails. A replacement at no extra charge is worth real money, and in a geographic model it is frequently impossible: in Ajman, the tutor who does not fit is often the only one who could reach you. The table sets out what to ask for against each line of a quote.

sections.heading: What the in-home premium buys for an Emirates City apartment
paragraphs: In-home tuition has real advantages and a page that denies them is selling rather than advising. A tutor in the room reads body language, can take a book out of a student's hands, and cannot be muted. For a young or easily distracted child, that is worth paying for, and for some families it is the only format that works at all.

What it costs in Emirates City specifically is reach and reliability, and a measurable share of the fee. The towers sit on the E311 corridor, which is fast at 2pm and slow at 6pm. A tutor coming from Sharjah or Dubai is adding an hour or more of round trip to a one-hour lesson, and that time is priced in somewhere. The published gap is the evidence: a qualified tutor working online is advertised at AED 150 to 300 an hour, while in-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 350 in the Bestimate survey and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors.

Then there is fragility. The in-home pool willing to drive to a specific Ajman tower on a weekday evening is small, and it shrinks again once a particular Higher Level subject is required. A cancelled visit is a cancelled week, because there is no second person to call. An online slot has a bench behind it.

IB Gram offers only the online format in the UAE, and no page here will tell an Emirates City parent otherwise. In-home visits are an India-only service. The comparison below is written so that a family choosing in-home anyway can at least see what they are buying and price it properly.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: fees, exam entry and the two-year Diploma
paragraphs: Tuition is the only part of an education budget with no published ceiling, which is why it should be sized against the parts that do have one. Dubai's private sector gives the clearest public picture: 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26, US at 14 and the International Baccalaureate at 7. KHDA then confirmed on 22 May 2026 that fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total.

Ajman sits under a different regime, with private schools supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than by KHDA, and fee levels in the emirate are materially lower than the Dubai equivalent. That is part of the reason Emirates City exists as a community. It also means tuition can swallow a larger proportion of an Ajman education budget than a Dubai family would notice, simply because the base against which it is compared is smaller.

The other costs nobody budgets for are examination and administrative. A private candidate pays entry fees through a centre rather than through a school. A resit entry after results is a second entry fee. Equivalency and attestation have their own official channels and their own charges, set by the authority rather than by anybody selling tuition. None of those is large individually and together they land in the same term as the heaviest tuition month of the Diploma.

The point of the table is sequencing, not alarm. Seen two years out, a Diploma plan is a series of decisions with dates on them. Seen three weeks out, it is an emergency, and emergencies are the most expensive way to buy anything.

sections.heading: Is a cheaper tutor cheaper? The permit question
paragraphs: There is a version of the budget conversation that ends badly, and it starts with the assumption that the cheapest available person is simply a less polished version of the expensive one. Sometimes that is true. Sometimes the difference is that one of them is operating within the rules and the other is not.

Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here.

Read that against the price list and the conclusion is awkward for the cheap end of the market. The permit costs nothing and takes two working days, so a low rate cannot be explained by permit costs being avoided. It can, however, be explained by the permit not existing, and a family cannot tell from an advertisement. The question is one sentence long and worth asking every time.

A separate point for completeness: a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. That is a different thing from an individual's tuition permit, and IB Gram holds neither. Nothing on this page should be read as a claim of approval by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

sections.heading: The most overpriced product in this market is coursework help
paragraphs: The Diploma is roughly a quarter internally assessed, which makes coursework both the most commercially attractive thing to sell and the most dangerous thing to buy. One page found during the research for this project sells completed Internal Assessments outright at AED 3,750. That is a remarkable amount of money for something that, if detected, costs the student the Diploma rather than costing the seller anything at all.

The legitimate version of this service is cheaper and more useful. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain each assessment criterion and what its descriptors actually demand, help narrow a research question, review a method for feasibility and ethics, and give written feedback on a draft the student has already written. A tutor must never write, redraft or complete an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay, a TOK essay or any assessed coursework, and must not supply text for the student to paste in.

There is a related boundary on materials. No tutor may reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads. The correct behaviour is to reference the official source and link to it, which is why there are no attachments on this page. Reproducing assessment material is a copyright matter, and for unreleased material it is a malpractice exposure.

The third boundary is the one that affects price most directly: no tutor can promise a grade, so no tutor can price one. Any provider selling a promised score, a promised improvement or money back against an outcome is either misunderstanding how grade boundaries are set or hoping you will not ask. What tuition reliably changes is the amount and the quality of deliberate practice, and the gap between what a student knows and what reaches the page.
bullets: Teaching criteria, command terms and content: legitimate, and the thing worth paying for.
Written feedback on a draft the student wrote: legitimate.
Producing text, data or diagrams for submission: never, at any price.
A promised score, or money back against a result: not something anybody can honestly sell.

sections.heading: When tuition money is well spent: the Diploma calendar
paragraphs: Spend follows the calendar or it is wasted. The fixed point for most UAE Diploma students is the May session, and everything a family pays for should be sequenced backwards from it: internal coursework deadlines set by the school, the mock window, the final months of timed paper practice. Grade 11 is for building; Grade 12 autumn is for coursework; Grade 12 spring is for papers. A budget that ignores that order buys the right hours at the wrong time.

A note on honesty about dates, because it affects planning. No IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself; the board's own site returns an error to automated checking. What can be said safely is that UAE schools sit the May session and that a November session exists as an alternative route. Any specific IB date should come from your school's Diploma coordinator or from ibo.org directly. A tutoring page is not a timetable.

For the IGCSE side of a household, the sourced position is clearer. Cambridge runs June and November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones; the board states it is essential to use the correct zone timetable and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. Cambridge's February/March series is offered in India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026.

The practical budgeting consequence is simple. Book the diagnosis early, keep the autumn light, and reserve the heavier spend for the eight to twelve weeks before the papers, when timed practice marked against a real scheme produces more marks per dirham than anything else available.

process.title: Say what you want it to cost
process.description: A budget stated up front produces a better plan than a budget discovered later. Tell us the subject, the level, the school and what you are willing to spend across a term, and the answer will be a format that fits it rather than an open-ended subscription that does not.

process.title: Take the free diagnostic lesson first
process.description: The first session is a diagnosis, not a sales call, and no card details are taken for it. The tutor works through real paper questions to establish whether marks are going on recall, method, command-term reading or timing, and you receive a written summary naming the first three targets.

process.title: Agree a session count and an end date
process.description: Open-ended tuition is how a budget drifts. A plan with a stated number of sessions and a review date is comparable to other quotes and easy to stop. For most Emirates City families that is a term at a time, reviewed against the school's own reporting cycle.

process.title: Book a slot that survives the E311
process.description: Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time and are set around the commute rather than against it. In Emirates City that frequently means 7:00pm or 8:00pm, once the second parent is home. Because lessons are online, no travel time is added to either side of the slot.

process.title: Step down when the gap closes
process.description: The aim is fewer sessions, not more. Once the diagnosed gap closes, weekly work can usually move to fortnightly, or stop entirely until the next pressure point. A provider that never proposes reducing the frequency is managing its revenue rather than your child's marks.

whyPoints.title: Prices you can audit, not a range with no source
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page names who published it and the month it was read. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this project publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars, which is not a currency an Ajman family transacts in.

whyPoints.title: No journey inside the fee
whyPoints.description: Lessons run online over live video, so none of what you pay is a tutor's drive up the E311. The published gap between online and in-home rates in this market is the clearest single argument for the format, and it is set out in a table rather than asserted.

whyPoints.title: A diagnosis before a subscription
whyPoints.description: The free first lesson exists to find out what is actually wrong, because the most common waste in this market is buying hours against an undiagnosed problem. The written summary afterwards is yours whether or not you book anything further.

whyPoints.title: A replacement costs nothing
whyPoints.description: If the match is wrong, a different tutor takes over with the notes already written. In a geographic model that is often impossible, because the tutor who does not fit may be the only one who could reach an Emirates City tower on a weekday evening.

whyPoints.title: Stated limits on coursework and on claims
whyPoints.description: Teaching, criterion explanation and feedback on the student's own draft: yes. Producing any part of an Internal Assessment or Extended Essay: never. No promised grades, no self-published ratings, and no claim of approval from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built for an Ajman commute
whyPoints.description: A large share of Ajman households work in Dubai or Sharjah, so useful slots here start later than in Abu Dhabi. Sessions are set accordingly and can move to post-Iftar timing through Ramadan rather than being quietly dropped for a month.

faqs.question: What does a full year of IB tuition cost a family in Emirates City?
faqs.answer: Work it from the monthly figure. Bestimate's survey puts a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Across nine teaching months that is roughly AED 2,200 to 5,400, AED 5,400 to 10,800, or AED 9,000 to 18,000 and above for one subject. Two subjects doubles it. The figure most families never calculate first is the two-year Diploma total for a single Higher Level subject, which lands in the AED 10,000 to 20,000 range.

faqs.question: Is an AED 799 online package better value than an AED 1,699 in-home package?
faqs.answer: Compare hours, not headline prices. The advertised online package is eight sessions a month; the in-home package is four visits of two hours, which is also eight hours. So the same teaching time is being offered at roughly double the price, and the difference is largely the journey. That premium buys a tutor physically in the room, which genuinely matters for a young or easily distracted student. For Diploma paper work, where most of the session is a question, a mark scheme and a shared screen, it buys very little.

faqs.question: Why do quotes for the same IB subject vary so much across Ajman?
faqs.answer: Five things move the number: the tutor's own rate, the provider's margin, travel, how scarce the subject is at that level, and how many weeks are left before the assessment. Scarcity is the one families underestimate. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches is taught in nearly every Diploma school, so the pool is deep and pricing is competitive. Chemistry at Higher Level is taught by a handful of teachers in the emirate, several of whom cannot tutor their own school's students. Ask which of the five is moving your quote.

faqs.question: Is an Ajman tuition rate quoted inclusive of VAT or not?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider directly and get the answer in writing, because it changes what you are comparing. This page deliberately does not state how UAE tax rules treat tuition fees, since that position needs a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than a tutoring company's summary, and a wrong answer here would be worse than no answer. What is reasonable to expect from any provider is a clear statement of whether a quoted AED figure is inclusive or exclusive, and a tax registration number if one is held.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Diploma student in Emirates City really need?
faqs.answer: Most start with one per subject and should. One well-targeted weekly hour, with work done between sessions, beats three unfocused ones and costs a third as much. The sensible pattern is light in Grade 11 and the autumn of Grade 12 while coursework is the priority, rising to two or three sessions a week for the eight to twelve weeks before the papers. Front-loading four sessions a week in October burns both the student's appetite and the budget before the period when practice actually compounds.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two IB subjects to save money?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, but check the level first. A tutor can credibly cover two Standard Level subjects in a related group, or Mathematics and Physics at Standard Level. Two Higher Level subjects from different groups is a much stronger claim and should be tested with specific questions about papers and recent teaching. The saving is usually smaller than expected, because the rate follows the harder subject. Where it genuinely helps is scheduling: one relationship, one slot pattern, one set of notes.

faqs.question: Is a cheap university-student tutor a false economy for Higher Level?
faqs.answer: For Higher Level content, usually yes. A tutor meeting Higher Level Physics for the first time alongside your child is being paid to learn the course, and you pay twice: once for the sessions and again for the term that produced nothing. Where a budget-tier tutor is genuinely the right buy is supervision and routine: sitting with a student through timed practice, keeping the schedule, checking work was done. That is a real service worth the budget rate of AED 45 to 150 an hour, not the specialist rate.

faqs.question: What does an in-home tutor actually add for an apartment in Emirates City?
faqs.answer: Physical presence, and that is not nothing. A tutor in the room reads body language, can take a book out of a student's hands and cannot be muted. What it costs is a measurable share of the fee and a fragile schedule. Emirates City sits on the E311 corridor, fast at 2pm and slow at 6pm, so a tutor from Sharjah or Dubai adds an hour or more of round trip. The published rate gap, AED 150 to 300 online against AED 180 to 500 in-home, is that journey.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in this market rise closer to the exam session?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the ordinary reason that demand rises and the same tutors cannot teach more hours. A family booking Higher Level support in the spring is competing for scarce capacity; the same family booking in September is not. That makes early booking a genuine discount available to anybody willing to plan, and it costs nothing to take. It also means a quote given in October should not be assumed to hold in March, which is a fair thing to ask a provider to confirm in writing.

faqs.question: Would a small group be cheaper for several Emirates City families on the same subject?
faqs.answer: Per student, yes, and for exam technique a group of two to four can work well. The requirement is that the students are on the same syllabus code, the same tier or level and roughly the same starting point, which is harder to arrange in Ajman than in Dubai because the local cohort for any one Higher Level option is small. What a group cannot do is follow one student's specific gaps, so it is a poor fit where the diagnosis has identified an individual topic sequence that has broken down.

faqs.question: What should I send when asking three providers for an IB quote?
faqs.answer: Send the same five things to each, or the quotes will not be comparable: the subject and level, the syllabus or programme, the school, the series the student is working towards, and the number of weeks you want to cover. Then ask each provider the same four questions: which syllabus did the proposed tutor last teach, is travel inside the rate, does the rate change closer to the series, and what happens in week three if the match is wrong. The spread in the answers is more informative than the spread in the prices.

faqs.question: Does a tutor without a MoHRE permit charge less, and does it matter?
faqs.answer: The permit is free of charge and valid for two years, with a two-working-day completion time listed on MoHRE's own service page, so a low rate cannot be explained by avoiding a permit cost. It can be explained by the permit not existing. Individuals offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. Private tutoring in the UAE is not unregulated and a permit is not optional. Asking to see it takes one sentence.

faqs.question: What happens to our money if we stop after one lesson?
faqs.answer: At IB Gram the first diagnostic lesson is free and no card details are taken to book it, so stopping after it costs nothing and you keep the written summary of what the tutor found. For any provider, the question worth asking before payment is whether sessions are bought in blocks, whether unused sessions are refundable or transferable, and how much notice a cancellation needs. Get those three answers in writing. A provider that cannot state them is selling a subscription rather than a plan.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects cost the most to tutor, and why?
faqs.answer: Scarcity sets the price more than difficulty does. Higher Level Chemistry and Physics, Economics with its internal assessment commentaries, and minority languages sit at the top of the band in the Northern Emirates because very few teachers locally cover them, and some of those are barred from tutoring their own school's students. Mathematics and English sit lower because almost every Diploma school teaches them, so the pool is deep. Specialist IB and IGCSE rates were published at AED 270 by TutorChase and AED 200 to 450 and above by Bestimate.

faqs.question: Is Extended Essay or Internal Assessment support priced differently from weekly tuition?
faqs.answer: It usually is, and it should be, because the useful work is spread across weeks of drafting rather than delivered in a fixed hour. Block pricing is normal and reasonable. What is not reasonable is paying for the work itself: a page found during research for this project sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, which is both a large sum and an academic malpractice risk carried entirely by the student. Legitimate support is criterion explanation, research-question narrowing, method review and written feedback on the student's own drafts.

ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-emirates-city.closingHeading: Get the diagnosis free, then decide what to spend
ajman/ib-home-tutor-in-emirates-city.closingBody: If the real question is what this will cost across a year, the cheapest way to answer it is to find out what is actually wrong first. The diagnostic lesson is free, no card details are taken, and the written summary of where the marks are going is yours either way. Tell us the subject, the level, the school, the series being worked towards and the budget you have in mind, and the plan that comes back will have a session count and an end date on it rather than an open subscription. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, timed around the drive back up the E311 to Emirates City.
